content:
0月15号法国各大报头版关注焦点各异。《解放报》关注乌克兰议题，大字标题点出：乌克兰被美国抛弃了。指出，由于美国总统特朗普和俄罗斯总统普京之间的协议，美国情报机构不再向乌克兰提供俄罗斯空袭的信息，因此加剧了乌克兰平民的危险。

《费加罗报》头版关注国内议题：指出退休选民成为总统竞选策略的核心。文章认为，过去一年，50岁以上的法国选民已占多数。退休人员积极参与政治，构成了一个稳固的选民基础，足以左右总统选举的走向。尽管年轻人的积极参与掩盖了老年人的光芒，但由于其在选举中的影响力，老年人在塑造未来政治格局方面仍然至关重要。极右翼国民联盟（RN）正指望这一群体赢得胜利。国民联盟目前在65岁及以上选民中占据多数，并将维护退休人员权益作为其竞选纲领的核心内容。

天主教《十字架报》头版配图关注的是：加沙，废墟中的幸存者。背景是巴勒斯坦权力机构于10月10日宣布推迟原定于近期举行的立法和总统选举。新的选举日期定于2027年9月11日，但这一举措引发了广泛的质疑。这一决定令欧洲国家，特别是法国感到失望，它们一直呼吁巴勒斯坦机构进行民主改革。但十字架报指出，文章战争爆发三年后，这片飞地超过80%的建筑已被摧毁或损坏。对于一个饱受苦难的民族而言，投票意味着什么？这个问题在加沙地带居民即将再次在赤贫中度过寒冬之际凸显出来。

**中国式压路机一路碾压**

这是经济类《回声报》头版头条大标题。这里指的"碾压"是中国出口激增对国际市场的压力。根据北京本周三上午公布的统计数据，中国贸易增速在9月份加快。在全球强劲需求的推动下，尤其是在人工智能爆炸式增长的带动下，中国9月份出口增长超过三分之一，为今年创纪录的贸易顺差铺平了道路。

尽管美国和欧盟采取了应对措施，但中国产品依然毫无阻力，一路碾压。这些数据无疑会让大西洋两岸的一些西方领导人感到不快。就在特朗普与习近平会晤一个月后，两国脆弱的贸易休战协议得以延长，9月份中国对美国的出口增长了39.65%。近期与欧洲达成协议减少中国汽车出口的欧洲，对欧洲的出口也呈现蓬勃发展：增长了25.25%，达到七个月来的最高水平。

至于对东盟国家的出口，其增幅继续领跑，高达52.26%。这主要是因为，除了密切的贸易联系外，包括越南在内的一些东盟国家还是对美出口的门户，从而缓解了华盛顿和北京之间贸易战的影响。自特朗普入主白宫以来，这场贸易战愈演愈烈。随着上个月平陆运河的开通，成为中国商品输出的新通道，这种情况未来可能会进一步恶化。

这种热情导致价格飙升。集成电路的情况尤为明显：尽管9月份中国集成电路的销量仅增长了1%，但销售额却增长了136%。至于受到北京严格管控的稀土元素，其出口也持续增长，9月份增长了6.74%。

文章也指出，这些令人瞩目的业绩仅仅是中国商业活力的最新体现，但这个世界第二大经济体存在诸多脆弱迹象，正因如此，国际货币基金组织刚刚下调了对中国的经济增长预期。

**人类在工厂的工作是否即将机器人完全取代**

这是《费加罗报》一篇文章的主题。文章称，很难想象还有比这更具象征意义的场景。一位海信员工身穿防护服，戴着口罩，弯腰在生产线上，仔细查看眼前缓缓移动的电视面板，似乎完全没有注意到右侧的机器人及其两只机械臂。人与机器依然并肩工作。但这种状态还能持续多久呢？海信集团的一位工程师解释说：“他们的生产线的自动化程度目前在整个电视行业中是最高的：整体流程自动化程度为70%，关键环节则达到了100%。”

这个趋势已经蔓延到诸多行业。小米声称，其位于北京昌平区占地8万平方米的智能手机工厂已达到这一技术里程碑，该工厂平均每秒可生产一部手机。据报道，位于中国东北宁波的汽车制造商Zeekr在其工厂中运行数千台机器人，每天生产800辆电动汽车，自动化程度高达90%。特斯拉也声称其上海超级工厂的自动化程度达到95%，年产100万辆电动汽车。

海信也计划在其位于青岛的电视工厂实现这一目标，目标是在2030年实现，并预期将带来诸多益处。海信发言人介绍，“理论上，我们已经可以完全取代人工。但我们正在遵循一套精确的路线图：优先采用自动化来取代那些对质量或精度要求极高，以及需要进行体力劳动或质量控制的工作岗位。”

这篇文章最后指出，根据国际机器人联合会的数据，到2025年，中国工厂将安装35.4万台机器人，比上一年增长20%。中国占全球新增机器人安装量的60%，而美国仅占不到5%。 洛桑大学经济学家理查德·鲍德温教授在今年夏天发表的一项研究中解释道：“中国目前的工业就业正沿着与几十年前发达经济体相同的轨迹发展：随着生产率的提高，以及劳动密集型生产环节转移到工资水平较低的国家，工业就业正在下降。”他重申，与普遍的看法相反，北京并非从西方窃取工业就业岗位，而是窃取其生产能力。

务实的中国政府深知，自动化及其带来的生产率提升是抵消人口结构崩溃并维持其全球领导地位的唯一途径。中国工人是否会毫无抗拒地接受这一重大变革，还有待观察。

**法国人如何看中国汽车？**

另一篇《费加罗报》上与中国相关的文章继续关注巴黎国际汽车展上的中国车型比以往任何时候都更引起参观者的兴趣，文章标题为：中国汽车是“欧洲车的仿制品，但更好”。这并非是费加罗报的评论，而是引用一名车展参观者的评价。

本周，在总共60家巴黎国际车展参展商中，约有20个品牌来自中国，中国汽车强势亮相巴黎车展，吸引着那些主要追求性价比的法国消费者。许多中国品牌对法国大众来说还很陌生，是因为一些中国制造商首次在法国参展，但魅力攻势似乎对在巴黎车展上接受采访的法国消费者奏效了。一个关键论点反复出现：价格。

咨询公司C-Ways的首席执行官埃里克·尚帕诺（Éric Champarnaud）几天前在《费加罗报》报道中指出：“如今，35%到40%的法国人表示他们愿意购买中国汽车。” 当前油价飙升也间接惠及中国汽车制造商，推动了电动和混合动力汽车的销售，而这正是中国品牌的强项。

但面对中国汽车，一些法国车主仍然心存疑虑。究其原因，有参观者说 “这既是为了维护我的民族自豪感，也是因为我对中国车的可靠性有所怀疑。而且，这些品牌在法国的售后服务网络是否足够完善？还有零配件的供应问题。”

两位现已退休的前同事，58岁的布鲁诺和57岁的迪迪埃告诉《费加罗报》，中国车在外观设计方面也有待提高。“我觉得它们的设计过时了，很平淡。它们没有法国车那种独特的气质。”

也有两位《费加罗报》记者在车展上采访到的汽车行业人员认为中国汽车制造商“取得了长足的进步”，他们指出：“中国的车是欧洲车的仿制品，但更好一些，”

title: 曼谷专栏 - 未来经济2026: 中美科技博弈重塑全球

content:
在当今地缘政治冲突加剧与技术革命交织的背景下，人工智能（AI）和大数据正在成为大国博弈的核心战场。世界银行未来经济论坛专家警告称，中美两国在人工智能和数据领域的激烈竞争正在影响全球经济的发展命运。有人担忧，人工智能和大数据可能沦为地缘政治博弈的工具。

综合东南亚媒体报道，2026年10月14日，在泰国曼谷举行的2026年国际货币基金组织与世界银行集团年会（2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings）系列活动中，一场以“安全资本”（Capital for Security）为主题的专题讨论会吸引了全球金融、银行和外交人士的目光。

这次讨论会由香港金融服务发展局副总裁冯国荣、美国资深外交官罗伯特·弗兰克·戈德克（Robert Frank Godec）、麻省理工学院（MIT）开放学习政府事务主任约翰·拉多万（John Radovan）以及《财富》杂志亚洲编辑总监安德鲁·斯台普斯博士（Dr. Andrew Staples）共同发声。讨论内容反映了全球经济在当前时代面临的关键性挑战，专家们一致认为，传统世界秩序正受到地缘政治冲突、贸易战、金融市场波动以及中美超级大国竞争的强烈冲击。人工智能和数据作为关键因素正在改变全球经济结构和权力平衡。

专家意见指出，乌克兰局势、中东局势以及大国之间的紧张关系，包括在各个地区引发的冲突正在影响全球经济的走向，包括能源价格、债券市场以及全球化的发展趋势。与此同时，科技竞争已经成为影响经济稳定的另一个重要因素，尤其是经处理转换用于训练AI模型的数据，正逐步成为企业创造附加值和提升核心竞争力的关键资源。这一发展趋势正迫使科技公司、金融机构乃至国家安全部门全面转向数据驱动的运营模式。

**寻求摆脱技术垄断焦虑**

专家们认为，目前关键挑战在于数据和数字基础设施的集中化。来自美国和中国的大型科技公司在数据获取和数据中心等基础设施投资方面发挥着重要作用，这可能加剧垄断风险，并导致各国对少数科技服务提供商的依赖。

有人担忧这个问题与国际安全息息相关，原因是数据和技术的获取可以像美元或半导体技术一样，成为经济和地缘政治关系中的关键因素，并且被用作谈判筹码。

关于如何突破技术垄断，避免全面性技术依赖。专家建议构建“数据主权”与推广AI技术。首先争取掌控关键数据资产，每个国家必须建立健全的机制，有效地管理、存储和保护包括能源、环境以及智能终端设备等在内的国家战略数据，确保将其转化为本土技术创新与经济效益。

推广开源人工智能技术是另一种机制，它能增加创新机会，减少对大型服务提供商的依赖，使资源有限的国家能够开发符合自身需求的技术，从而摆脱全面依赖。

**地缘博弈下的东盟机遇**

与会专家对东盟经济前景抱以乐观态度。作为拥有超过 7 亿人口和正向经济增长趋势的地区，东南亚在超级大国之间的激烈竞争与冲突中获得了前所未有的发展机遇。泰国、越南和印度尼西亚正受到制造业基地转移和创新投资商的青睐。

不过，为了适应并且抓住这一转型带来的时代机遇。构建更为紧密的区域联盟、加快人力资源开发、建立数据主权，一切都需要东盟持续付诸努力，通过连接资本、技术、创新和供应链来全面提升成员国的竞争力，增强东盟在多元经济合作中的战略自主性。从而平衡大国关系，避免单一依赖任何超级大国。

**适应AI****重塑全球经济**

对于各国应对全球经济变化以及方兴未艾的人工智能技术，与会专家从政策维度提出了三个关键思路。分别是：

1. 培养适应人工智能经济的劳动力，实现劳动力技能转型。即：加快培养具备人工智能知识和理解能力的人才，同时提升和调整劳动力技能，使其能够适应不断变化的劳动力市场需求，从而有效地运用技术并提高生产力。

2. 改革传统教育体系，注重培养实用技能。即：从传统的课堂学习转向优先发展科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）教育，并推广短期课程，使学习者和劳动者能够立即将所学知识应用于实践工作中。

3. 维护人文与合作价值。强调解决复杂的全球性难题仍须依赖于信任、开放沟通、尊重多样性以及人与人、国与国之间的理性合作。

总而言之，随着人工智能技术的进步，人文关怀、关系构建和协作愈发显得重要。尤其在充满不确定性的全球新秩序中，技术准备、人力资源积累以及跨国合作的力度，将决定一个国家或区域长期经济的发展命运。发言者强调，面对AI技术浪潮，各国政府应超越情绪化的政治反应，转向基于理性的政策制定，共同构建和平稳定与可持续发展框架。对东盟而言，抓住生产基地转移与创新投资爆发的时机，将其高效转化为可持续、高附加值的经济增长，俨然是刻不容缓的时代课题。

title: Labor groups allege contract swaps, low pay for Indonesian workers - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 劳工组织指控印尼工人的合同互换和低工资 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月15日电 劳工组织周四指责一家台湾海上风电设备制造商剥削印度尼西亚技术工人，据称这些技术工人的月薪合同被低薪小时协议取代，并敦促审查​​用于将他们带到台湾的制度。在台北劳动部 (MOL) 外的一次抗议活动中，包括台湾国际工人协会 (TIWA) 在内的团体表示，代表一个更大团体的五名工人对涉及世纪能源有限公司的海上风电项目的工资和工作条件提出了投诉。
content:
中新社台北10月15日电 劳工组织周四指责一家台湾海上风电设备制造商剥削印度尼西亚技术工人，据称这些技术工人的月薪合同被低薪小时协议取代，并敦促审查​​用于将他们带到台湾的制度。

在台北劳工部 (MOL) 外举行的抗议活动中，包括台湾国际工人协会 (TIWA) 在内的团体表示，代表一个更大团体的五名工人对涉及世纪能源有限公司的海上风电项目的工资和工作条件提出了投诉，该项目是台湾一家主要的海上风电海底基础制造商。

TIWA协调员陈容柔表示，这些工人——合格的焊工和装配工——是由新加坡的Sheffield Green和印度尼西亚的PT Kepodang Makmur Sejahtera根据“合同履行”制度带到台湾的，该制度允许海外公司派遣人员从事合同项目。

陈说，一些人最初签订的合同承诺每月 48,000 新台币（1,482 美元），但后来支付的工资约为每小时新台币 100 至 143 元。

## 世纪能源的回应

世纪能源在周四晚些时候发表的一份声明中表示，这些外国技术人员是根据台湾当局批准的安排被带到台湾的，并否认逃避任何法律责任。
它还对有关工人工资的指控提出异议，称这些指控“与事实不符”，但没有提供进一步的细节或工资数字。

该公司表示，雇佣条款受工人与海外承包商之间协议的约束，因此“不合适”直接干预。不过，它承诺将继续监督工人的福利并配合政府检查。

## 工人账户

Eko是一位印度尼西亚装配工的化名，他自称在这些项目上工作了五年，尽管拥有专业资格，但他每小时的收入约为新台币100元。他还培训了菲律宾和越南蓝领移民工人，他说这些人缺乏类似的技术资格。

“为什么我的工资比蓝领农民工低？”他问道，并补充说他每月工作约 260 小时，没有劳工或职业事故保险。

另一名化名 Yat 的印尼工人表示，他签署了一份协议，承诺每月新台币 48,000 元，但在离开印尼前几天，他得到了一份工资较低的小时合同。

陈说，工人们向公司提出了担忧，但被告知，“如果你不想工作，就回家吧。”

## 工资和最低工资
台湾目前的最低工资为每月新台币 29,500 元，或每小时新台币 196 元。陈先生以每月26个工作日加上14小时加班计算，计算出时薪100元的员工，每月收入为新台币28,362元，包括奖金和加班费。

这些团体援引世纪能源的2025年可持续发展报告称，该公司当年有508名合同履行人员，分配到新北八里区和台中的工厂。

他们估计，如果类似的安排适用于约 500 名员工，公司每月可节省超过新台币 1400 万元的工资和与就业相关的缴费。

## 团体需求

抗议者呼吁对涉嫌变相雇佣的行为进行调查，审查工人合同，对工人进行赔偿，并根据适用条款继续雇佣

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Labor groups on Thursday accused a Taiwanese offshore wind equipment manufacturer of exploiting Indonesian technical workers whose monthly salary contracts were allegedly replaced with lower-paying hourly agreements, and urged a review of the system used to bring them to Taiwan.

At a protest outside the Ministry of Labor (MOL) in Taipei, groups including the Taiwan International Workers' Association (TIWA) said five workers, representing a larger group, had complained about pay and working conditions on offshore wind projects involving Century Energy Co., Ltd., a major Taiwanese manufacturer of offshore wind subsea foundations.

TIWA coordinator Betty Chen (陳容柔) said the workers -- qualified welders and fitters -- were brought to Taiwan by Singapore-based Sheffield Green and Indonesia's PT Kepodang Makmur Sejahtera under a "contract performance" system that allows overseas companies to send personnel to work on contracted projects.

Some had initially signed contracts promising NT$48,000 (US$1,482) a month but were later paid about NT$100 to NT$143 per hour, Chen said.

## Century Energy's response

In a statement issued later Thursday, Century Energy said the foreign technical workers had been brought to Taiwan under arrangements approved by Taiwanese authorities, and denied evading any legal responsibilities.

It also disputed the allegations about the workers' wages, saying they "did not match the facts," but did not provide further details or wage figures.

The company said employment terms were governed by agreements between the workers and overseas contractors, making it "inappropriate" for it to intervene directly. However, it pledged to continue monitoring the workers' welfare and to cooperate with government inspections.

## Workers' accounts

Eko, a pseudonym for an Indonesian fitter who said he had worked on the projects for five years, said he earned about NT$100 an hour despite holding professional qualifications. He also trained Filipino and Vietnamese blue-collar migrant workers who, he said, lacked comparable technical qualifications.

"Why am I paid less than blue-collar migrant workers?" he asked, adding that he worked about 260 hours a month and had no labor or occupational accident insurance.

Another Indonesian worker, speaking under the pseudonym Yat, said he signed an agreement promising NT$48,000 a month but was given a lower-paying hourly contract just days before leaving Indonesia.

Chen said workers had raised concerns with the company but were told, "If you don't want to work, go home."

## Pay and minimum wage

Taiwan's minimum wage is currently NT$29,500 per month, or NT$196 per hour, for covered workers. Based on an illustrative calculation of 26 workdays a month plus 14 hours of overtime, Chen estimated that a worker earning NT$100 an hour would receive NT$28,362 a month, including bonuses and overtime pay.

Citing Century Energy's 2025 sustainability report, the groups said the company had 508 contract performance personnel that year, assigned to facilities in New Taipei's Bali District and Taichung.

They estimated that the company could save more than NT$14 million a month in wages and employment-related contributions if similar arrangements applied to approximately 500 workers.

## Groups' demands

The protesters called for investigations into suspected disguised employment, reviews of workers' contracts, compensation for the workers, continued employment under terms applicable to foreign technical workers and a system to help and shelter workers seeking redress.

## Ministry of Labor response

The MOL replied in general terms, saying foreign workers dispatched to Taiwan under commercial contracts must receive the protections for employment terms and occupational injury compensation provided under applicable Taiwanese laws, such as the Labor Standards Act where it applies.

The ministry said it would step up inspections of high-risk cases and "deal strictly under the law" with companies found using contract performance arrangements to "circumvent employment and labor regulations."

(By Sunny Lai)

# AI demand highlights Taiwan's semiconductor capabilities: Lai

10/15/2026 04:00 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

President Lai Ching-te delivers remarks at the inauguration of Micron Technology Inc.’s new facility in Taichung on Thursday. CNA photo Oct. 15, 2026

Taichung, Oct. 15 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said Thursday that as global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) grows, the world will increasingly rely on Taiwan for its comprehensive semiconductor capabilities and trusted supply chain.

Speaking at the inauguration of U.S. memory chipmaker Micron Technology Inc.'s new advanced assembly and testing facility in Taichung, Lai said Taiwan combines the world-leading advanced chip manufacturing and packaging technologies of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) with Micron's continued investment in advanced memory.

The more the world needs AI, the more it needs Taiwan -- a trusted partner with complete industrial capabilities, Lai said.

The new facility, completed in just over a year, demonstrates Micron's commitment to Taiwan and will strengthen both the company's global competitiveness and Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem, he added.

Micron has invested more than NT$1.4 trillion (US$43.18 billion) in Taiwan over the past three decades, reflecting its confidence in the country, Lai said.

He said chips and memory are both indispensable in the AI era, adding that the new facility will enhance advanced packaging and testing capabilities for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to meet rising global AI demand.

Micron Technology Inc.'s new advanced assembly and testing facility in Taichung on Thursday. CNA photo Oct. 15, 2026

Lai noted that the government has extended its three major Taiwan investment incentive programs through 2027, expanding eligibility to overseas Taiwanese businesses and foreign companies while providing financing support and one-stop services to help address land, water and electricity needs.

He added that Micron has also secured funding under the Ministry of Economic Affairs' A+ Industrial Innovation R&D Program to accelerate HBM research and development in Taiwan, boosting investment and production capacity.

Lai also reiterated the government's "dual-engine" strategy of developing both high-tech and traditional industries, saying it aims to help precision manufacturers upgrade technologies and integrate into high-tech supply chains.

He called for closer cooperation between central and local governments, employers and workers to foster a healthy industrial environment, saying harmonious labor-management relations are essential to sustainable business growth.

(By Chao Li-yen and Evelyn Kao)

zh_title: 台北世界邮票展庆祝中华邮政成立130周年 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月15日电 菲律宾2026年世界集邮锦标赛展览将于11月在台北举行，为期六天，活动组织者周四表示，以纪念台湾国有邮政服务中华邮政成立130周年。中华邮政的历史可追溯至 1896 年清光绪年间在中国成立的大清邮政。中华民国取代清朝后，国有邮政于1912年改现名。2026年是邮政成立130周年。免费活动的组织者是
content:
中新社台北10月15日电 菲律宾2026年世界集邮锦标赛展览将于11月在台北举行，为期六天，活动组织者周四表示，以纪念台湾国有邮政服务中华邮政成立130周年。

中华邮政的历史可追溯至 1896 年清光绪年间在中国成立的大清邮政。

中华民国取代清朝后，国营邮政于1912年更名为现名。

2026 年是邮政服务诞生 130 周年。

此次免费活动由中华邮政和台湾中华台北集邮联合会（CTPF）主办。这也标志着该国举办世界集邮锦标赛十周年。

主办方表示，该博览会已获得国际集邮联合会（FIP）的批准，将设有约100个展位，以满足来自世界各地的邮政组织、集邮者、贸易商和出版物的需求。

CTPF名誉主席陈友安表示，展会将聚焦创新和可持续发展。

他表示，此次活动预计将吸引来自全球90多个国家和地区的邮政部门代表参加。

此外，陈先生透露，此次活动将展出约2000幅邮票，涵盖从历史到流行文化等广泛题材。
据中华邮报报道，博览会期间还将举办特别主题日，吸引各年龄段、各界人士参加。

例如，中华邮政宣布，在11月20日展览开幕当天，该活动将设有“邮政日”，与会者将能够看到为庆祝世界集邮锦标赛展览而设计的纪念邮票。

与此同时，参加活动“艺术和文学日”的游客将看到以台湾故宫博物院文物为灵感的邮票，而在“收藏家日”参加活动的人们将看到围绕全球流行的神奇宝贝集换式卡牌游戏设计的邮票。

活动中还将展示历史邮票，以教育参观者。

集邮作家俱乐部主席何辉庆表示，将向参观者介绍旧邮票，例如越南民主共和国（越南北部共产主义国家）在 1945 年至 1976 年期间发行的邮票。

何说，未来的集邮爱好者将有机会看到包含针对美国军方的政治宣传的 DRV 邮票，这为从不同角度看待越南战争提供了难得的机会。

菲律宾2026年世界集邮锦标赛展览将于11月20日至25日举行。

主办方欢迎感兴趣的参观者和热心的集邮爱好者参加免费展览。

（詹姆斯·罗）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) The PHILATAIPEI 2026 World Stamp Championship Exhibition will be held for six days in November in Taipei, marking the 130th anniversary of Chunghwa Post, Taiwan's state-owned postal service, organizers of the event said Thursday.

Chunghwa Post traces its origins to the Great Qing Post, established in China in 1896 during the Qing dynasty under Emperor Guangxu.

After the Qing Dynasty was replaced by the Republic of China, the state-owned postal service was given its current name in 1912.

2026 marks the 130th anniversary of the postal service.

The free event is organized by Chunghwa Post and Taiwan's Chinese Taipei Philatelic Federation (CTPF). It will also mark a decade since the country hosted a World Stamp Championship Exhibition.

Organizers said that the expo has been sanctioned by the International Philatelic Federation (FIP) and will feature around 100 booths to cater to postal organizations, stamp collectors, traders and publications from around the world.

CTPF Honorary chairman Chen Yu-an (陳友安) noted that the exhibition will focus on innovation and sustainability.

He said that the event is expected to attract representatives from postal services in over 90 countries and regions around the world.

In addition, Chen revealed that the event will exhibit about 2,000 frames of stamps, covering a wide range of subjects, from history to pop culture.

According to Chunghwa Post, it will also organize special themed days during the expo to attract attendees of all ages and from all walks of life.

For example, Chunghwa Post announced that on the exhibition's opening day, Nov. 20, the event will feature a "postal day" where attendees will be able to see commemorative stamps designed to celebrate the World Stamp Championship Exhibition.

Meanwhile, visitors to the event's "arts and literature day" will be introduced to stamps inspired by artifacts from Taiwan's National Palace Museum, while people who go to the event during "collectors day" will see stamps designed around the globally popular Pokémon Trading Card Game.

Historical stamps will also be presented at the event to educate visitors.

Ho Huei-ching (何輝慶), President of the Philatelic Writers' Club, said visitors will be introduced to old stamps such as those issued by the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (DRV), the communist state in north Vietnam from 1945-1976.

Ho said prospective philatelists will get the chance to view DRV stamps containing political propaganda directed at the American military, providing a rare opportunity to view the Vietnam War from a different perspective.

The PHILATAIPEI 2026 World Stamp Championship Exhibition will be held from Nov. 20-25.

Organizers welcome interested visitors and avid philatelists to attend the free exhibition.

(By James Lo)

Enditem/AW

title: Smoky Mountain Boots and Roots Hiking, Thu, Oct 22, 2026, 7:00 AM   | Meetup
summary: ## Details **OVERVIEW** Are you into endless views? Old-growth forests? Mist bouncing off a 100-foot waterfall hitting your face? Then spend a long weekend with a small group of women hiking the best trails in the Great Smoky Mountains Nati
content:
## Details

**OVERVIEW**
 Are you into endless views? Old-growth forests? Mist bouncing off a 100-foot waterfall hitting your face? Then spend a long weekend with a small group of women hiking the best trails in the Great Smoky Mountains National Park (including parts of the Appalachian Trail).

Channel your inner goat girl as you stroll through iconic scenery and listen to stories of the women who helped shape the Smokies. Take a brief break from the trail living out your pottery fantasies throwing clay on the wheel and sculpting your very own mug. Then kick back like a queen with nightly glamping near Gatlinburg, TN.

**BOOTS = HIKING**
 Get your blues and greens in on three stunning hikes that don’t even look real. The views from Charlies Bunion and Ramsay Cascades are complete madness. Wind your way through pine trees and over classic creek crossings that make you momentarily consider a coonskin hat. (But not really, because animals ♥️)

**ROOTS = HER-STORY**
 Did you know a woman was the first settler to move to the Smoky Mountains? You didn’t? That’s because Martha Jane Huskey Ogle’s husband called dibs on the fame. Learn about the deliciously woman-heavy history of a wilderness that man tried real hard to claim as his own. Your Explorer Chick guide will drop all the juicy gossip, connecting you to the goosebumpy sisterhood who walked before you.
 Deep dive into Appalachian crafts straddling a wheel and molding a coffee mug with your very own hands. Local artists will guide you through the entire pottery process and only help when needed. After 10 weeks of drying, firing, and glazing, your mug will show up at your doorstep. Surprise! Relive the SHE-nanigans of your Smokies trip.

**YOU FEELING MAX COMFY WHILE GLAMPING**
 Put your feet up in total Insta-worthy digs at our adorable glamping site minutes from Gatlinburg. You will sleep in a tent that has been tastefully decorated and luxuriously appointed with WiFi and temperature control – with meals freshly prepared at camp by your Explorer Chick guides. You only have one task after hiking: RELAX.

**ADVENTURE HIGHLIGHTS:**

*   Hike the Appalachian Trail to the sweeping panaromic views from Charlies Bunion
*   Get up close and personal with the Smokies tallest waterfall, Ramsey Cascades
*   Learn how to work clay on a wheel as you create your one of a kind glazed coffee mug
*   Kick back at camp with breakfasts and dinners cooked by your Explorer Chick guides.
*   Sleep easy at our Glamping site with canvas tents outfitted with all the creature comforts.
*   Relax with a comprehensive itinerary that makes the logistics, transportation, navigation, meal planning, lodging, and everything between easy.
*   Geek out with supportive and encouraging Explorer Chicks on a private, women-only, small group adventure tour.

**See the website for full details and to book.**

Unreal hoodoos? Check. Slot canyons? Majestic overlooks? Check. All this and more (like heated tents with electricity) await you during our Women’s Hiking and Glamping in Zion National Park and Bryce Canyon weekend adventure!

**BRYCE CANYON HIKING AND BEGINNER-FRIENDLY CANYONEERING**
 Escape to prehistoric Utah where you’ll hike stupid-pretty trails in Zion National Park and Bryce Canyon National Park. Wade through the Virgin River below 1,500′ canyon walls in the Narrows. Spend an entire day exploring Bryce Canyon National Park. Ghost the tourists as you wander deep into orange hoodoos. Explore areas of Zion so remote, they can only be reached by rappelling, scrambling, and down-climbing on a beginner-friendly canyoneering route.

**ZION NATIONAL PARK’S SCOUT LOOKOUT**
 Beastmaster up the West Rim Trail to Scout Lookout and enjoy some of the best views in Zion National Park. You’ll hike through Refrigerator Canyon, and shimmy up all 21 of Walters Wiggles to Scout Lookout with panoramic views of Zion Canyon and Virgin River. Afterward, dry your pits as you descend the trail to an easier hike around the scenic streams of Upper and Lower Emerald Pools.

**GLAMPING**
 Every night you’ll rest your head in Insta-worthy glamping tents bordering Zion National Park. Kick it by the campfire under a diamond sky with goddesses who aren’t afraid to get dirty.

title: 初步贸易报告显示，中国向澳大利亚“倾销”铝制门窗。

content: 委员会提议建议产业部长发布针对中国商品的倾销税通知。 (ABC 新闻：Will Hunter) 澳大利亚国际贸易监测机构发现，中国生产的铝门窗被“倾销”至澳大利亚，严重压低当地价格并损害了澳大利亚的铝门窗产业。 从今天起，进口这些商品的企业在货物进入该国时，还必须缴纳一笔财务担保金，这引发了关于建筑成本上升以及中国可能采取报复措施的警告。 在初步报告中，前名为反倾销委员会的澳大利亚贸易救济委员会发现，除一家中国出口商外，所有中国出口商均在 2024 年 7 月 1 日至去年 6 月 30 日期间倾销了这些商品。 委员会发现，这些商品的销售倾销幅度在 5.3% 到 70.4% 之间，具体取决于出口商，占其正常价格的百分比。 委员会还发现，部分出口商从中国各级政府部门获得了适度的补贴。 委员会发现，中国进口商品对澳大利亚产业造成了“实质性损害”。 委员会估计，在调查期间，当地铝门窗市场的价值约为 28 亿美元。 中国进口商品占总销售额的 19%，澳大利亚占约 79%，其余 2% 来自其他国家。 委员会估计，中国进口商品使该产业损失了 3.5 亿美元。 (ABC 新闻：Yiying Li) 根据报告，从 2021 年 7 月到 2025 年 6 月，当地制造商的销量下降了约 19%。 同时，根据报告，其销售额价值从 2023 财年的峰值下降了约 14%。 委员会发现，他们审查的投标和报价中有一半低于预期价格 30%，而超过四分之一则被压低 40% 以上。 委员会估计，由于受到中国“倾销和/或受补贴进口”的低价冲击，澳大利亚产业损失了约 3.5 亿美元。 委员会提议建议产业和创新部长 Tim Ayres 发布针对中国商品的倾销税通知，这将导致对这些进口商品征收关税。 目前，中国制造的铝门窗在中国 – 澳大利亚自由贸易协定下没有面临任何关税。 Ayres 先生的发言人表示，阿尔巴尼斯政府支持公平自由的贸易。 “澳大利亚贸易救济委员会根据行业申请启动其严谨、基于证据的调查，”他们表示。 “任何实施的贸易救济措施均完全符合澳大利亚在贸易协定下的义务。” 证券可能“有效导致价格上涨” 在调查进行的同时，委员会表示，需要金融证券来“防止对澳大利亚产业造成实质性损害”。 从今天起，进口商必须提供价值在其产品价值 5.3% 到 73.3% 之间的金融证券。具体百分比将取决于出口公司。 这些证券是可能随后需缴纳的关税的财务担保。产业部长将最终决定是否征收任何关税。 专家表示，政府宣布的措施可能导致价格上涨。 (ABC 新闻：Lily Nothling) UNSW 国际经济法教授周伟欢表示，很可能将征收关税，因为很难改变委员会初步报告中的发现。 他表示，证券可能“有效导致价格上涨”，因为进口商会在定价中考虑这些费用。 “价格影响将涉及进口铝门窗和门的上涨，进而推高商业和住宅建筑的建造成本，”周教授表示。 “保护竞争免受不公平贸易侵害” 调查于 11 月 25 日开始，由 Ventora Group 和澳大利亚玻璃门窗协会 (AGWA) 提出申请。 申请称，当地产业因销售损失和价格抑制而“遭受实质性损害”。 “我们并非要求政府保护澳大利亚企业免受竞争，”AGWA 首席执行官 Clinton Skeoch 在接受 ABC 采访时说。 “我们要求政府保护竞争免受不公平贸易的侵害。” AGWA 欢迎这一证券措施，并表示这对一个面临倾销进口严重压力的行业来说“是一项重要且积极的发展”。 ABC 已联系中国商务部和中国大使馆寻求评论。 周教授表示，中国采取报复行动的可能性不大，因为中国历史上针对澳大利亚的反倾销和反补贴行动远少于澳大利亚针对中国的行动。 “但这并非不可能，如果中国决定采取行动，那么农业出口可能会成为目标，”他表示。 在调查期间，媒体报道引发了对中国铝门窗质量的担忧。 (ABC 中央西区：Luke Wong) Ventora 委托对进口中国窗户进行测试，AGWA 公开了测试结果。 委员会表示，在初步发现中，它并未考虑测试结果或其他关于产品质量或合规性的指控。 建筑商提出成本担忧 Master Builders Australia 代理首席执行官 Melissa Byrne 表示，该组织将“仔细审查委员会的发现”。 “与此同时，任何增加建造成本的措施都出现在住房可负担性和项目可行性面临巨大压力的时期，”她说。 她说，澳大利亚“必须不限制高质量、合规建筑产品和材料的流通”。 最终建议将于 12 月 16 日之前提交。部长预计将在收到建议后 30 天内做出决定。 最终报告将在部长做出决定后发布。

## 香港街頭被偷拍？正妹怒查陌生男手機卻找嘸證據 網揭她驚人身分

2026-10-15 19:55 香港01／ 撰文／布萊恩  香港  偷拍  手機
關閉

「偷拍」公審以及證據問題常惹爭議。示意圖／Ingimage

「[**偷拍**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%81%B7%E6%8B%8D)」公審以及證據問題常惹爭議。有[**香港**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF)女子於[Threads](https://www.threads.com/@rachelywww/post/DeZGyJKAlxN?xmt=AQG0jSVbfig9lgkqP-8fjHIsyW2mfsW9Xq5_DYknM8tIrFT4ptzvSx83XV1D6VyQJzCvDAiB&slof=1)發布影片，公審在[**中環**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E7%92%B0)卑利街被2名男子偷拍。雖然她最終未能在2名男子[**手機**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%89%8B%E6%A9%9F)中發現任何偷拍她的相片，但她認為只是對方在其不知情下刪除了相片，揚言「不知道他是怎麼把照片弄走（刪除）的，但他很明顯就是拍了我們啊」，並將男子樣貌放到網路公審，批評「就算被我當場抓到，他也會厚著臉皮否認。這些人能不能有點男子氣概啊！」

事件引起網友爭議，認為女子沒有證據證明男子偷拍，卻放到網路「公審」對方做法不妥當，「真的太扯了」、「那個男人到底要怎麼做，才能證明自己沒有偷拍？難道要靠發文者的主觀認定嗎？」、「沒有證據、毫無根據，就說人家偷拍」。還有網友發現，**女子身份為以18歲之齡參加《香港小姐2026》的KOL李欣穎（Rachel Li）**。

面對網友圍攻，李欣穎留言反駁「不要把猥瑣的偷拍行為包裝成合情合理的藉口」，又表示：「如果把手機轉交給別人，事後檢查不到就叫作沒做過，那這個世界上所有小偷偷完東西再把贓物丟掉，是不是就變清白了？」結果再觸發罵戰。

## 港姐參選人李欣穎拍片公審中環遭2男子偷拍

影片長約2分鐘，看到李欣穎追著2名被她指控「偷拍」的男人拍攝，並要求對方展示手機相簿。對方起初拒絕展示手機，重覆「I didn't take a picture（我沒有拍照）」，惟李欣穎追著拍攝對方相貌，爆粗罵「FXXK YOU」，男子則明言「I will sue you if you do that（如果妳那樣做，我會控告妳）」，再次強調「I didn't take a picture（我沒有拍照）」。

## 未發現男子偷拍證據 李欣穎：不知道他怎麼把照片刪除的，但很明顯就是偷拍

畫面一轉，男子向李欣穎展示手機相簿，未有發現任何拍攝她的照片，惟李欣穎形容對方是「已刪」照片，並非沒有拍攝，聲言「不知道他是怎麼把照片弄走（刪除）的，但他很明顯就是拍了我們啊」。

李欣穎又問男子如果沒有偷拍，為何要躲藏，對方否認躲藏，但李欣穎不接受解釋，表示會放上網路公審，明言「thank you for the reel content（感謝您提供影片題材）」。

## 男子多次否認偷伯 李欣穎：感謝提供影片題材

李欣穎事後補充，「他（男子）把手機交給他的朋友了，接著他的朋友就離開了，然後我們要追上去問他。那個時候我們顧不上其他事，他就說沒有（偷拍），手機裡全都是他家人的照片」。

## 李欣穎批男子羞恥無賴：香港真系太多偷拍狂

雖然找不到偷拍證據，但李欣穎批評男子「可恥」、「無賴」，「他（有家庭）還要出去這樣偷拍別人，真的很可恥啊，有損市容啊。可以當面問我要不要合照，但不要偷拍」，又聲稱不只1次被人偷拍，「香港真的有太多偷拍狂了。全部被我抓到的話，全部都會厚著臉皮否認。這些男人能不能有點男子氣概啊！」

## 網友圍攻李欣穎：沒有證據、毫無根據就說人家偷拍，難道妳的眼睛就是證據嗎？

不過李欣穎「公審」不成，反被大批網友圍攻，指摘她沒有證據就指控男子偷拍並「公審」，做法離譜，「妳拍不到他偷拍妳，妳就把影片放上網，不是大家就一定要支持妳。整段影片只看到妳追著別人、一直騷擾人家，人家都說沒有拍妳的照片了，妳卻硬說人家把照片刪掉了」、「妳真的太過分了，明明就是在誣賴人啊，想博取流量也不用這樣吧？現在是妳偷拍別人、妳騷擾別人，還誣賴人家，看到整段影片真的很生氣！」、「1. 妳沒有證據；2. 法例明文規定的是私密部位；3. 無罪推定原則」、「只知道妳在偷拍別人，不要整天覺得自己被人偷拍，好不好？」、「那個被拍的男人到底要怎麼做，才能證明自己沒有偷拍？難道要靠發文者的主觀認定嗎？」

## 李欣穎反擊網友：查不出來就代表沒做過嗎？

面對網友圍攻，李欣穎再強調男子有偷拍，「如果把手機轉交給別人，事後檢查不到就叫作沒做過，那這個世界上所有小偷偷完東西再把贓物丟掉，是不是就變清白了？」李欣穎又搬出香港法例中的「非法拍攝私密部位」及「窺淫罪」，強調「一般街拍和『偷拍』是兩回事，不要把猥瑣的偷拍行為包裝成合情合理的藉口」，結果網友罵聲更多。「不如妳先定義一下什麼是『私密部位』吧！」、「其實妳有沒有想過，妳這樣做會連真正需要幫助的女性也一起害了？」

## 非法拍攝私密部位、窺淫罪可監禁5年

根據《刑事罪行條例》（第200章）第159AA 條，「私密部位」定義為個人的生殖器官、臀部、肛門範圍或胸部（不論是露出或僅有內衣遮蔽），或個人所穿的、遮蔽著生殖器官、臀部、肛門範圍或胸部的內衣，明顯與一般「街拍」不同。

而根據香港法例第200章《刑事罪行條例》第159AAC條「非法拍攝或觀察私密部位」，任何人拍攝某名個人的私密部位，而拍攝情況是若非遭拍攝，該部位本來不是可讓人看到的，即屬犯罪，可處監禁5年。

另根據香港法例第200章《刑事罪行條例》第159AAB條「窺淫」，任何人拍攝某名個人的私密部位，或某名個人進行私密作為，即屬犯罪，同樣可處監禁5年。

content:
【大紀元2026年10月15日訊】今年5月、9月，美國總統川普和中共黨魁習近平實現了互訪。兩次「川習會」後，國際上對美台關係議論紛紛。儘管兩次「川習會」上，習近平都跟川普談了台灣問題，但是，並沒有改變美國政府對台灣的立場。相反，美台關係持續全面升級，至少有六大進展。

## **一、美台關係全面升級的六大進展**

### **第一，台灣對美國5000****億美元的投資承諾在兌現中。**

川普總統第二任期開始後，據美國官方數據，台灣對美國承諾的投資總額已達5000億美元。

7月16日，美國商務部宣布：台積電將在美國亞利桑那州追加1,000億美元投資，用於生產先進半導體及封裝設備。加上此前的投資承諾，台積電在美投資總額將達到2,650億美元，規劃廠區增至12座，成為美國歷史上規模最大的外來直接投資。

美國商務部的聲明稱，台積電的新增投資將給美國帶來數以萬計的就業機會，將先進半導體的製造帶回美國，並帶動數十億美元的間接經濟產出。

美國在台協會（AIT）處長谷立言（Raymond F. Greene）說，這項投資「充分展現美國與台灣對彼此的信任與信心，而這正是美台夥伴關係的核心」。

### **第二，台灣購買美國液化天然氣被稱為「史上最大的交易之一」。**

川普在阿拉斯加瓦西拉的集會上宣布：台灣已同意在未來20年內購買阿拉斯加液化天然氣管道項目約30%的產量。據路透社報導，川普稱這直接保證了該項目的徹底成功，也是史上最大的交易之一。

10月14日，台灣經濟部證實，台灣「中油股份有限公司」已於2025年3月簽署買賣暨投資意向書，歷經近一年半協商後取得重大進展。規劃內容包括項目投產後每年採購600萬噸液化天然氣，並參與項目開發，投資金額最高44億美元，最快2032年起供氣。

台灣經濟部強調，該項目可經太平洋航線直達台灣，有助於分散運輸路線與地緣供應風險。

### **第三，美國企業加大對台灣的投資力度。**

10月8日，美國總統川普在華盛頓舉行的「科學：新黃金時代」峰會上，向6位科技界領袖頒發了美國科學與技術領域的最高國家榮譽。

其中，兩位出生於台灣的美國科技巨頭——英偉達創始人兼首席執行官黃仁勳，超微半導體董事長兼首席執行官蘇姿丰，獲頒「國家科學獎章」。

黃仁勳的英偉達、蘇姿丰的超微，與台灣AI產業有千絲萬縷的聯繫。

英偉達絕大部分的高端圖形處理器與人工智能芯片，都交由台灣的台積電進行獨家或主要代工生產。英偉達在台灣的合作夥伴還包括鴻海、廣達、緯創、華碩、微星、技嘉等。

5月27日，黃仁勳在台北宣布：英偉達將在台灣建立總部並擴大投資，每年預估投入約1500億美元。

超微半導體在台灣的合作夥伴包括台積電、日月光、矽品、力成、欣興、景碩、緯創、緯穎、英業達、台達電、營邦等。

5月21日，蘇姿丰宣布：超微將在台灣AI產業投資超過100億美元，用於加速建置AI基礎設施與提升先進封裝產能。

10月6日，蘇姿丰再度訪台時表示，由於AI市場需求暴增，相關投資計劃進展順利並決定繼續調高投資金額。

谷歌、蘋果、微軟等美國的科技巨頭，都在台灣供應鏈中深度布局。

比如，谷歌在台灣設立了美國總部以外全球最大的硬件與AI基礎建設研發中心。蘋果在台灣設有研發中心和技術實驗室，且其全球有四分之一的供應鏈廠商位於台灣。微軟在台灣設有數據中心與亞洲首座AI研發中心。這些美國科技巨頭都在台灣持續投資。

### **第四，台美在無人機方面的合作取得新突破。**

俄烏戰爭使無人機在現代戰爭中的作用變得異常關鍵。受烏克蘭的啟發，台灣在無人機方面也迅速趕上。

台灣從2022年起啟動無人機計劃。台灣無人機的產量從2024年的約1萬架增加到2025年的超過12萬架，並計劃到2028年年產18萬架。

美國國防科技公司安杜里爾（Anduril）創辦人拉奇（Palmer Luckey）在一個國際論壇上說，面對地緣政治挑戰，台灣建構不對稱作戰能力的進展速度，「比我們合作的絕大多數國家都快得多，其中也包括美國」。

台積電被稱為台灣的「護國神山」。台灣正在迅速崛起的無人機產業群，有望成為台灣的又一座「護國神山」。

美台在無人機方面的合作，從天空到水面，從短程到遠程，從「美國設計，台灣製造」到「共同設計，台灣製造」，正全方位展開。

10月13日，《華爾街日報》報導，在與台灣合作開發海空無人機的美國業者中，安杜里爾對台無人機合約已逾10億美元。

同日，美國國防科技公司Shield AI正式宣布：已與台灣合作夥伴漢翔航空工業共同完成首架V-BAT垂直起降監偵無人機的設計、生產、組裝、測試；該無人機已運抵台灣海巡署。未來數月內，將陸續交付12架V-BAT給台灣海巡署。

V-BAT屬於第三級（Group 3）無人飛行系統，採用涵道風扇設計，並搭載重油引擎，主要用於情報、監視與偵察，以及目標鎖定等任務。

10月2日，美國國防科技企業AEVEX的成長策略資深副總裁安德斯（Craig Anders）宣布：將與台灣中光電智能機器人公司合作生產VANDAL與ONYX兩款無人機。不久前這兩款無人機已在台東太麻里進行過實際飛行展示。另外，由AEVEX生產的LYNX無人船已由美方交給台灣的海軍陸戰隊操作。

9月中旬，台灣最大造船企業「台灣國際造船股份有限公司」宣布：與美國國防科技公司Havoc AI建立合作夥伴關係，共同推動自主無人水面載具在台灣的生產、技術合作與維護保養。

據美國軍事媒體Defense News報導，傳統上是美國出口武器給台灣，但在無人機領域，未來可能出現相反方向。

### **第五，台灣對美國的出口大幅增長。**

至2026年9月，台灣出口連續35個月正成長，寫下史上最長成長週期。據台灣財政部的數據，台灣9月出口872.2億美元，年增60.9%，創歷年單月新高；累計前9月出口達6615.5億美元，年增46.2%；全年出口值有望達到9000億美元。

1—9月，台灣對美國出口總額達到2077.8億美元，史上首次在同期突破2000億美元大關，提前刷新了全年的歷史紀錄。台灣對美國的出超（順差）達1005.9億美元，首次超越對中國大陸及香港的出超。

去年，美國就成為台灣最大的貿易出口國。今年美國更是台灣出口的第一大客戶。

### **第六，美籍華裔女子張婉瑩因涉監視台灣總統之子被FBI****抓捕。**

10月4日，居住在美國加州爾灣的34歲房產經紀人張婉瑩，準備搭乘前往上海的航班時，在洛杉磯機場被美國聯邦調查局（FBI）探員逮捕。她被指控充當未註冊的中共代理人，涉嫌監控在西雅圖工作的台灣總統賴清德之子賴廷與。

FBI局長帕特爾（Kash Patel）在社交平台X上表示：「外國對手請注意，美國不再是你們可以安全從事間諜活動的地方。有人在美國領土上為中共監視外國領導人的家人，然後試圖搭乘航班返回上海。調查局將追查任何威脅美國國家安全的目標，無論其藏身何處，都將繩之以法。」

## **二、為什麼美台關係會有上述六大進展？**

主要原因可能有三：

### **第一，共享的價值觀是連結台美最關鍵的基石。**

10月7日晚，美國國務卿盧比奧在希臘雅典的帕特農神廟前發表了長達26分鐘的演講。這是一個對西方文明「尋根」的演講，也是一篇在西方文明的源頭試圖復興西方文明的檄文。

那麼，西方文明的根本是什麼呢？就是對上帝的信仰，以及在此基礎上形成的自由、民主、法治、人權等價值觀。

盧比奧演講的核心是，呼籲美國及其盟友共同復興這些在漫長歲月中被塵封、被遺忘、被扭曲、甚至被一些人拋棄了的核心價值觀，回歸常識、理性與傳統。

10月10日，台灣總統賴清德在中華民國115周年國慶大典上，以「台灣山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」為題發表演講。

「山巔之城，地上的鹽，世上的光」，出自《聖經‧新約‧馬太福音》，是耶穌對門徒的教導。其核心涵義是：人應以善行實踐信仰，堅守良善，並以自身的言行為他人帶來正面影響。

賴清德的演講，與盧比奧的演講相呼應，講的都是回歸對神的信仰，守護自由、民主、法治、人權的價值觀。

美國是自由世界的領袖，台灣是以美國為首的自由世界的重要組成部分。共享的傳統價值與普世價值，是把美台連結起來的最重要的基石。

### **第二，共同面臨中共的挑戰是美台攜手合作的動力。**

現在，美國面臨的最大對手，就是中共；台灣面臨的最大威脅，也是中共。

蘇共解散、蘇聯解體後，中共成了全世界唯一的最大的共產主義政黨、中共國成了全世界唯一的最大的共產主義國家。

上世紀90年代以來，中共利用以美國為首的西方國家對中共採取的綏靖政策，利用加入世界貿易組織的機會，利用西方的市場、資本、技術、金融、服務等，迅速成為世界第二大經濟體。

美國是世界第一大經濟體，中共是世界第二大經濟體。習近平上台後，認為中共的「底氣」足了，「東升西降」了，「時與勢」在中共一邊，「當今世界最大的亂源在美國」，「美國是我國發展和安全最大的威脅」，於是，開始在全球範圍內跟美國爭奪霸主地位。

2020年大瘟疫大爆發後，中共發起對美國的新冷戰。標誌性的事件有五：第一，1—2月，中共軍艦挺進太平洋中部的中途島軍演。第二，3月，宣布南海戰略核潛艇的「堡壘海區」建成。第三，6月，宣布對美國太空戰部署完成。第四，7月開始，從渤海到黃海到東海到南海到內地，發起40多年來最密集的軍演。第五，8月25日，《人民日報》發表批判美國的長文，中心思想是：美國最壞，「中共國」最好。

同一年，中共在暴力鎮壓香港反送中運動後，在香港強推「港版國安法」，提前27年終結了香港的「一國兩制」，以中共「一黨專政」取而代之。

同一年，中共在拿下資本主義的香港之後，立即將目標瞄準資本主義的台灣，在渤海、黃海、台海、南海發動了有史以來最密集的軍演，開始對台灣極限施壓，企圖以中共的一黨專政取代台灣的自由民主。

中共若拿下台灣，決不會止步。接下來，就是以台灣為據點，近處威脅日本、韓國、菲律賓等，更大範圍將突破美國在二戰後設立的防衛共產主義擴張的第一島鏈，進而直接威脅資本主義的美國，建立一個以中共為主導的「人類命運共同體」。

中共所謂的「人類命運共同體」是什麼？就是中共老祖宗馬克思講的「解放全人類」的另一種說法。

中共為什麼在拿下資本主義的香港之後，要拿下資本主義的台灣，並與資本主義的美國爭奪世界霸權呢？

因為中共的老祖宗馬克思仇恨資本主義、反對資本主義、必欲戰勝資本主義，最後要取代資本主義，建立社會主義、共產主義的一統天下。

台灣處在西方的自由民主與中共的專制極權對峙的最前沿。美國則在全球範圍內，從雅典，到羅馬，到美洲大陸，面對著中共無孔不入的滲透與顛覆。

守護台灣，就是守護美國，守護自由民主。

如何守護？

在投資、能源、無人機生產、科技、經貿、打擊中共間諜上，全面合作，深度融合，你中有我，我中有你，共同築起對抗共產主義的銅牆鐵壁，乃必然之道。

### **第三，世界第一強國與世界最強勁經濟增長體的強強聯手。**

美國是當今世界上的第一強國。美國強在哪裡？首先，美國人民享有信仰自由、言論自由、免於恐懼的自由、免於匱乏的自由；其次，美國的國父們給美國留下了一個防止專制獨裁極權的有效的分權與制衡的民主政治制度；再次，在自由民主的基礎上，美國有世界上最發達的科技，最強大的軍事實力，最具影響力的金融，最優秀的人才資源，最有消費能力的龐大的市場等。

台灣是當今世界上經濟增長最強勁的地區之一。

據國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）2026年10月發布的《世界經濟展望》報告，台灣2026年的實質GDP增長率預測被大幅上調至10.7%，這一增長率不僅在亞太地區高居榜首，也使台灣成為全球範圍內極為罕見的實現雙位數增長的經濟體。

這一增長速度遠超全球絕大多數主要經濟體。美國預測增長為2.3%，中國預測增長為4.5%，歐元區預測增長為1.1%，印度預測增長為7.0%。

台灣作為全球經濟增長最強勁的經濟體，自然願意與世界第一強國，實現強強聯手了。

## **結語**

現在總有人從川普與習近平關於台灣問題的談話中揣摩美台關係的走向。其實，美台關係不在於川普怎麼說，而在於美國政府與台灣政府實際怎麼做。

現在有一個說法，台灣產業角色正從單純的「Made in Taiwan」代工，轉向以戰略夥伴身分深度嵌入美方核心供應鏈，即「Made with Taiwan」。這個說法很有道理。

如今，美台正在投資、能源、貿易、科技、無人機、安全等各方面相互融合，形成一個共生共成、互利互惠、彼此守護的整體。

綜上，儘管仍有各種挑戰，美台合作的前景仍讓外界看好。

资料照片：来自密歇根州的共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)在众议院中国问题特设委员会举行的听证会上向证人提问。(2023年2月28日)

美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。

穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-calls-for-pentagon-to-update-its-list-of-pla-linked-institutions-and-talent-recruitment-programs)。他建议战争部在“第1286条清单”(Section 1286 List)中增加14家被特设委员会认定为中共“核心国防合作伙伴”的中国科学院下属研究所、62家实验室和国防实验室、58所大学、22项外国恶意人才引进计划，以及中国国家留学基金管理委员会(CSC)和获得该机构资助的研究人员。

穆勒纳尔说，扩大清单的目的是加强美国的研究安全，防止中国及其他外国对手利用战争部资助的科研成果。

**清单直接影响战争部研究经费**

“第1286条清单”依据2019财政年度《国防授权法》第1286条设立，用于识别美国政府认定对国家安全构成风险的外国科研机构、企业、个人和人才引进计划。

从2026财政年度开始，战争部不得为涉及清单内实体的基础研究项目提供资金。这项限制适用于研究拨款、合同及其他形式的资助，并禁止受资助机构与清单内实体共同开展研究或使用对方设备。研究人员如果与清单内机构的人员合作，也可能影响其获得联邦科研经费的资格。

战争部今年7月更新了清单，目前列有中国、俄罗斯和伊朗的130所高校和科研机构。战争部8月还要求30所美国高校审查其与外国机构的学术、资金和科研联系，并采取整改措施。

穆勒纳尔赞扬战争部近年来强化科研安全评估，并限制接受战争部资助的研究人员与美国政府管控清单上的机构合作。

“在这些努力中，战争部的‘第1286条清单’发挥着核心作用，”穆勒纳尔在信中说。“一个实体是否被列入清单，可能直接决定接受战争部资助的研究人员能否与该实体保持科研合作关系。”

他表示，随着列入清单产生的实际后果日益扩大，清单是否完整、准确也变得更加重要。

“这一框架能否发挥作用，不仅取决于对清单内实体施加的限制，也取决于战争部能否识别并认定符合相关标准的外国机构，”穆勒纳尔说。他警告，清单存在的覆盖缺口可能为接受战争部资助的研究人员和机构留下继续与中国相关组织合作的渠道。

**涉及军工、半导体、量子和人工智能**

穆勒纳尔说，特设委员会发现，一些尚未被列入清单的中国科研机构，与中国的国防科研和工业体系存在有记录的隶属、监管、协议或其他重要联系。

他要求战争部审查的机构包括中国科学院下属研究所，以及从事武器、航空航天、高超音速技术、半导体、水下系统、电子战等军事相关研究的实验室。名单还包括由中国国家国防科技工业局(SASTIND)共同管理或支持的高校。

人才引进计划部分则主要涉及量子技术和人工智能等关键及新兴技术领域。

穆勒纳尔说：“以下列出的几类机构尤其值得关注，因为它们与国防体系的关联已经得到美国政府或其他研究安全机构的记录和证实。”

据路透社报道，穆勒纳尔建议增加的58所高校包括清华大学。战争部目前尚未宣布是否接受他的建议；信中提到的机构也并未因为特设委员会的提名而自动受到限制。是否列入清单仍须由战争部依据相关法定标准进行认定。

近年来，美国国会和行政部门不断加强对外国政府参与美国科研项目的审查，重点包括隐瞒外国资金来源、参加外国人才计划、知识产权转移，以及敏感或军民两用技术可能流向外国军方等问题。

中国驻美使馆此前在回应战争部要求美国高校审查外国合作关系时，指责美方将国家安全概念泛化，并把正常的科学、教育和学术交流政治化。北京呼吁美国为两国学术与科研合作提供开放、公平和非歧视性的环境。这一表态并非针对穆勒纳尔最新信函作出。

**要求限制国家留学基金委受资助人员**

除了扩大机构名单，穆勒纳尔还要求战争部禁止任何接受中国国家留学基金管理委员会资助或其他经济支持的研究人员、研究生和博士后参与战争部资助的科研项目。

他主张，这项限制应在有关人员接受中方资助期间持续有效，无论他们是否被正式列为项目负责人、共同研究人员或其他具名参与者。

穆勒纳尔说，中国国家留学基金管理委员会不同于一般国际学生资助项目。该机构近年来因涉及学术自由、对留学生的监控、意识形态要求和潜在间谍活动等指控，在美国受到越来越严格的审查。

 穆勒纳尔促战争部扩大“1286清单”，限制与更多中国高校及实验室合作

title: Hong Kong Customs youth visit Macau for exchange, WCO meeting
zh_title: 香港海关青年访澳交流及世界海关组织会议
summary: 香港海关旗下海关YES青年计划到访澳门进行文化教育交流，包括与澳门海关青年举办烘焙工作坊、参观海事指挥部、参加第36届WCO亚太区域会议等。此行旨在扩大参与者的全球视野 [![图1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026年10月15日17:40 HKT·2分钟读香港海关带领一批海关YES青年计划成员
content:
香港
香港海关海关YES青少年计划到访澳门进行文化教育交流，包括与澳门海关青少年举办烘焙工作坊、参观海事指挥部，以及参加第36届世界海关组织亚太区域会议。此行旨在拓宽参与者的全球视野

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 15 日 17:40 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

香港海关周四宣布，香港海关率领一批海关YES青年计划成员前往澳门进行国际交流之旅，旨在加深两地年轻人之间的互动。

代表团首先与澳门海关“诚信守护者”青年计划成员一起参加葡式蛋挞烘焙工作坊，体验澳门独特的饮食文化，建立友谊。随后，他们参观了澳门海关海事司令部，并参观了海关船队，了解海关在维护海上安全、海上巡逻、打击走私等方面的执法工作。
为加深对澳门“一中心、一平台、一基地”的发展定位的了解，考察团参观了中国与葡语国家商贸合作服务平台展厅，了解中国与葡语国家的经贸合作以及澳门在促进交流中的桥梁作用。

在庆祝中华人民共和国成立77周年之际，代表团还参观了叶挺将军故居，学习革命先辈的英雄事迹和中国近代史，弘扬爱国主义精神。他们游览大三巴牌坊、大炮台、官也街等文化地标，体验澳门中西文化的交融。

香港海关以世界海关组织亚太区副主席身份，安排代表团参加在澳门举行的第36届世界海关组织亚太区联络会议。欢迎酒会上，海关YES成员接待了外宾，并首次与澳门青年代表共同举办活动，在区内海关代表面前展现了自信和责任。
特区政府表示，海关YES将继续配合国家“十五五”规划和香港第一个五年发展规划，举办丰富多彩的内地及国际交流活动，帮助年轻人拓宽全球视野，更好地融入国家发展。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Hong Kong Customs' Customs YES youth programme visited Macau for cultural and educational exchanges, including a baking workshop with Macau customs youth, a tour of the maritime command, and participation in the 36th WCO Asia-Pacific regional meeting. The trip aimed to broaden participants' global视野

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 17:40 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Customs led a group of Customs YES youth programme members on an international exchange trip to Macau, aimed at deepening interaction between young people in the two cities, the government announced on Thursday.

The delegation first joined members of Macau Customs' youth scheme, "Keepers of Integrity", in a Portuguese egg tart baking workshop, experiencing Macau's unique food culture and building friendships. They then visited the Macau Customs Marine Command and toured the customs fleet to learn about its law enforcement work in safeguarding maritime security, conducting sea patrols and combating smuggling.

To enhance understanding of Macau's development positioning as "one centre, one platform, one base", the group visited the China and Portuguese-speaking Countries Commercial and Trade Cooperation Service Platform exhibition hall, learning about economic and trade cooperation between China and Portuguese-speaking nations, and Macau's bridging role in promoting such exchanges.

Marking the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the delegation also visited the former residence of General Ye Ting, studying the heroic deeds of revolutionary forebears and modern Chinese history to foster patriotism. They toured cultural landmarks including the Ruins of St Paul's, the Mount Fortress and Rua do Cunha to experience Macau's blend of Chinese and Western cultures.

Hong Kong Customs, in its capacity as vice-chair of the Asia-Pacific region of the World Customs Organization, arranged for the delegation to participate in the 36th WCO Asia-Pacific Regional Contact Meeting held in Macau. During the welcome reception, Customs YES members received foreign guests and, for the first time, co-hosted the event with Macau youth representatives, showcasing confidence and responsibility before customs representatives from across the region.

Customs YES will continue to organise diverse mainland and international exchange activities in line with the national 15th Five-Year Plan and Hong Kong's first five-year development plan, helping young people broaden their global horizons and better integrate into national development, the government said.

title: HSBC to double Hong Kong AI team to 300 in two to three years
zh_title: 汇丰银行将在两到三年内将香港人工智能团队增加一倍至300人
summary: 汇丰银行亚洲和中东联席首席执行官表示，该行将在两到三年内将其 150 人的香港人工智能团队增加一倍，并将于 2027 年初在香港设立全球人工智能研究所。该银行已在香港监管沙箱下测试了两个生成式人工智能用例[！[图 1： Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 19:13 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 汇丰银行将把人工智能的规模扩大一倍H 中的（AI）团队
content:
商务
汇丰银行亚洲和中东联席首席执行官表示，该行将在两到三年内将其 150 人的香港人工智能团队增加一倍，并将于 2027 年初在香港设立全球人工智能研究所。该银行已在香港监管沙箱下测试了两个生成式人工智能用例

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 19:13 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

汇丰银行一位高级管理人员周四表示，未来两到三年内，汇丰银行将把其香港人工智能 (AI) 团队的规模从 150 名专家扩大一倍至约 300 名。

汇丰银行亚洲及中东地区联席首席执行官廖亦坚表示，该行的技术和人工智能专家分布在香港、英国和其他主要市场。该团队开发了工具来帮助客户经理与客户互动并提高客户服务中心的案件处理质量。

廖还援引集团首席执行官Georges Elhedery的话说，汇丰银行将在香港设立全球人工智能研究院，预计于2027年初开始运营。该研究院初期将专注于人工智能应用案例、后量子密码学和区块链技术。
廖在接受记者采访时表示，香港是集团的本土市场，自然也是高管的基地。该集团运营委员会的四名成员、区域运营委员会成员和各级高管均驻扎在这座城市，他将其描述为集团的中央决策引擎和未来的全球人工智能发展中心。

他补充说，香港资本和财富管理市场充满活力，集团拥有庞大的客户基础和业务增长，有信心在香港部署更多技术和前线员工。

针对有媒体报道香港金管局质疑汇丰为何将人工智能中心设在新加坡而不是香港，廖重申香港是汇丰亚太和中东地区的决策中心，也是科技和人工智能人才的大本营。他表示，该行继续在香港投资，虽然在中国大陆和伦敦设有人工智能团队，但应用程序的整体领导地位位于香港。他指出，该集团与监管机构有着积极、频繁的沟通。

廖表示，汇丰银行在香港金融管理局第二阶段生成式人工智能沙箱下成功测试了两个用例：一个使用生成式人工智能将文本转换为手语，另一个用于预防欺诈，在 eKYC 流程中检测与深度伪造相关的金融诈骗。
他还表示，相信分别在香港和深圳举行的亚太经合组织财长会议和领导人非正式会议将鼓励更多对话和透明度，该组织将积极参与。

Business
HSBC's Asia and Middle East co-CEO says the bank will double its 150-strong Hong Kong artificial intelligence team within two to three years, and will set up a global AI research institute in the city in early 2027. The bank has tested two generative AI use cases under Hong Kong's regulatory sandbox

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 19:13 HKT · 2 min read

HSBC will double the size of its artificial intelligence (AI) team in Hong Kong from 150 specialists to about 300 within the next two to three years, a senior executive said on Thursday.

Liao Yi-kin, co-chief executive of HSBC for Asia and the Middle East, said the bank's technology and AI specialists are based in Hong Kong, Britain and other major markets. The team has developed tools to help relationship managers interact with clients and to improve the quality of case handling at customer service centres.

Liao also cited group chief executive Georges Elhedery as saying that HSBC will establish a global AI research institute in Hong Kong, expected to begin operations in early 2027. The institute will initially focus on AI application cases, post-quantum cryptography and blockchain technology.

Speaking to reporters, Liao said Hong Kong is the group's home market and naturally serves as the base for senior executives. Four members of the group's operating committee, members of the regional operating committee and executives at various levels are based in the city, which he described as the group's central decision-making engine and a future global hub for AI development.

He added that Hong Kong has a vibrant capital and wealth management market, and the group has a large client base and business growth, giving it confidence to deploy more technology and frontline staff in the city.

Responding to media reports that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority had questioned why HSBC placed its AI centre in Singapore rather than Hong Kong, Liao reiterated that Hong Kong is the group's decision-making hub for Asia Pacific and the Middle East and a stronghold for technology and AI personnel. He said the bank continues to invest in Hong Kong, and while it has AI teams in mainland China and London, the overall leadership of applications is based in Hong Kong. He noted the group has positive and frequent communication with regulators.

Liao said HSBC successfully tested two use cases under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's second phase generative AI sandbox: one using generative AI to convert text into sign language, and another on fraud prevention that detects deepfake-related financial scams in the eKYC process.

He also said he believed the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation finance ministers' meeting and leaders' informal meeting, to be held in Hong Kong and Shenzhen respectively, would encourage more dialogue and transparency, and that the group would participate actively.

# BOCHK to issue onshore NCDs, first offshore yuan clearing bank

Bank of China (Hong Kong), the sole yuan clearing bank in the city, plans to issue up to 22.2 billion yuan in onshore interbank certificates of deposit this year, becoming the first offshore clearing bank granted such a quota. The move aims to boost Hong Kong's status as a leading offshore yuan hub.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 19:32 HKT · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=BOCHK%20to%20issue%20onshore%20NCDs%2C%20first%20offshore%20yuan%20clearing%20bank%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/BOCHK-to-issue-onshore-NCDs-first-offshore-yuan-clearing-ban-c58941 "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/BOCHK-to-issue-onshore-NCDs-first-offshore-yuan-clearing-ban-c58941&text=BOCHK%20to%20issue%20onshore%20NCDs%2C%20first%20offshore%20yuan%20clearing%20bank "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/BOCHK-to-issue-onshore-NCDs-first-offshore-yuan-clearing-ban-c58941 "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/BOCHK-to-issue-onshore-NCDs-first-offshore-yuan-clearing-ban-c58941&text=BOCHK%20to%20issue%20onshore%20NCDs%2C%20first%20offshore%20yuan%20clearing%20bank "X")[](mailto:?subject=BOCHK%20to%20issue%20onshore%20NCDs%2C%20first%20offshore%20yuan%20clearing%20bank&body=BOCHK%20to%20issue%20onshore%20NCDs%2C%20first%20offshore%20yuan%20clearing%20bank%0Ahttps%3A//clb.org.hk/en/business/BOCHK-to-issue-onshore-NCDs-first-offshore-yuan-clearing-ban-c58941 "Email")

Bank of China (Hong Kong) (2388), the sole yuan-clearing bank in the city, plans to issue interbank negotiable certificates of deposit (NCDs) in mainland China's onshore market, a move aimed at further strengthening Hong Kong's position as the leading offshore yuan centre.

The lender has become "the first offshore yuan-clearing bank granted an issuance quota for onshore NCDs," according to a statement from the Interest Rate Self-Regulatory Mechanism, which is overseen by the People's Bank of China.

The bank said it plans to issue up to 22.2 billion yuan (HK$26.04 billion) worth of NCDs in 2026, according to a separate statement this week. NCDs are popular short-term debt instruments issued between banks for their financing needs.

"All issuance will be denominated in yuan and the bank will determine the size and tenor of each NCD at its discretion based on market conditions and the bank's circumstances," it said.

The move comes after authorities from Beijing and Hong Kong in July unveiled a range of measures to bolster currency, bond and gold trading in the city, stepping up efforts to establish Hong Kong as a leading offshore yuan centre amid heightened geopolitical tensions.

The yield on one-year NCDs stood at about 1.44 per cent, while the offshore yuan HIBOR, a gauge that measures the interbank borrowing cost in Hong Kong, was at about 1.78 per cent this week.

title: China’s Trade Surplus Goes Vertical
summary: _Thank you for subscribing to my posts. If you’re not yet a paying supporter, please consider becoming one. That’ll allow you to DM me with questions and comments. Your contribution will help cover the cost of the data I use in my posts, wh
content:
_Thank you for subscribing to my posts. If you’re not yet a paying supporter, please consider becoming one. That’ll allow you to DM me with questions and comments. Your contribution will help cover the cost of the data I use in my posts, which I fund out of my own pocket. Thanks so much for your support and feedback!_

Back in my Goldman days, I wrote a report on currency manipulation in Asia. For obvious reasons, I had to be careful in how I wrote things up - many countries in the region were also clients - and the report was published only after careful review. For example, the final draft eschewed words like _“intervention”_ or _“manipulation,”_ so there was lots of self-censoring before the report ever saw the light of day. I got in trouble anyway. The Chinese government complained loudly to senior management and the upshot was that I had to do a conference call with various government officials who yelled at me for an hour about how awful my report was.

I learned a lot about China on that conference call. After all, if a country puts so much energy into intimidating a nerd like me, that’s in my mind a sign of profound fragility. China depends desperately on its export sector for growth, which makes US tariffs an existential threat. Beneath its calm demeanor, China is working furiously to reduce its exports to the US in case the trade war flares up again. I showed the massive ramp-up in China’s exports to emerging markets (EM) that’s a symptom of this in yesterday’s [post](https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/how-china-is-reinventing-its-export). Today’s post looks at how this shows up in China’s overall trade balance.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!zGnl!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe598c90d-5341-4485-a52f-6a9bdc10e8b8_460x432.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!zGnl!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe598c90d-5341-4485-a52f-6a9bdc10e8b8_460x432.png)

China publishes seasonally adjusted export and import data for its biggest trading partners. I use those to construct China’s bilateral trade surplus with the US, which is the black line in the chart above, and its trade surplus with fourteen other countries, which is the blue line. China’s trade surplus with the US is back to pre-2025 levels, but it’s the surplus with the fourteen other countries that looks like it’s going vertical. As the fourteen countries are mostly advanced economies and a few of the bigger EMs, this doesn’t even cover what I talked about in yesterday’s [post](https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/how-china-is-reinventing-its-export), which was about the massive rise in China’s exports across all of EM.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!_vP3!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fec69ac89-bc4e-403c-bac3-e4ade759a2d6_477x432.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!_vP3!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fec69ac89-bc4e-403c-bac3-e4ade759a2d6_477x432.png)

The chart above looks at China’s trade surplus with all countries around the world (not just the countries in the top chart, which are China’s principal trading partners). Since these data aren’t seasonally adjusted, I show January through September totals for every year, which you can think of as a crude seasonal adjustment. It’s clear that something very unusual is going on in the last two years. The chart below shows that the ramp-up in exports is even bigger than meets the eye. That’s because imports are also growing, so the rise in the trade surplus isn’t about import compression. Instead, China’s export sector is firing on all cylinders.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!CUyK!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0a91de5b-aa6d-498b-aa1b-662dac0dffbf_477x432.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!CUyK!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0a91de5b-aa6d-498b-aa1b-662dac0dffbf_477x432.png)

As the chart below shows, the rise in exports is very recent and about a furious orientation away from the US. In China’s recent history, there’s nothing remotely similar, so this feels like state intervention to cut its US export dependence. This isn’t a freebie for China. If you want to export to new markets, you have to discount what you’re selling, so it’s likely this export shift is hitting margins and profitability among China’s exporters. It’s therefore a [deflationary](https://robinjbrooks.substack.com/p/why-us-tariffs-are-deflationary-for) shock. But unlike Western countries, China’s leadership is playing the long game and has clearly decided it’s worth taking a short-term hit to reduce vulnerability to US tariffs over the medium term.

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Yjtp!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F63df0b4a-ee73-45b7-acf0-9fe1696310f5_476x427.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Yjtp!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F63df0b4a-ee73-45b7-acf0-9fe1696310f5_476x427.png)

All of this is massively destabilizing for the global economy. It obviously snuffs out much of the growth potential for US and European goods in EM. It also means that all the EMs being targeted in this export surge are getting roped into a dependence on China that’s bad for them and bad for the West. There’s an urgent need for the US and Europe to get on the same page with respect to all of this.

title: “Secure and controllable”: How Beijing is writing Europe out of its systems
summary: In June 2025, a Chinese state-owned utility put out a tender covering the replacement of the control systems for 67 wind turbines at the Kangbao wind farm in Hebei. The turbines were not broken or outdated. The problem was their controllers
content:
In June 2025, a Chinese state-owned utility put out a tender covering the replacement of the control systems for 67 wind turbines at the Kangbao wind farm in Hebei. The turbines were not broken or outdated. The problem was their controllers, which were imported from Europe. The tender warned not only of high costs and long procurement cycles, but also of a risk of being “controlled by foreign forces”. The prescribed solution was replacement with domestically produced technology.

The Kangbao case is not unusual. A [new study](https://www.osw.waw.pl/designed-out/) by the Centre for Eastern Studies (OSW) of the Chinese wind sector analysed more than 1,600 publicly available procurement documents and found nearly 300 calling for foreign equipment to be replaced. European manufacturers and component suppliers are among those named in the notices as risks to be removed.

The analysis shows that Beijing’s drive to make its energy infrastructure “self-reliant, safe and controllable” is security-focused and discriminates against foreign suppliers, including European ones. And while European suppliers are written out of Chinese critical energy infrastructure, Chinese companies push for expansion in Europe.

It is widely known that China’s leadership under Xi Jinping strives for China to be less reliant on technology imports, especially in critical infrastructure. OSW’s findings describe how this is being done and how European firms are affected. They show a coordinated effort, more than a decade in the making, to identify foreign technological dependencies that could become vulnerabilities, build domestic alternatives and gradually remove the foreign technology itself.

The findings should reassure Europeans already moving towards a more restrictive approach. Reciprocity used to mean asking Beijing to open its market, follow rules and stop discriminating. This notion no longer fits the reality. Europeans need to re-evaluate their understanding of security in critical infrastructure, and to shift what they mean by “reciprocity”: not waiting for China to match Europe’s openness, but matching China’s protective measures.

## China’s path to technological self-reliance and control

The OSW research shows that as early as 2012 Chinese State Council documents warned that core information technologies depended on other countries. The 2015 National Security Law made the development of “self-reliant and controllable” critical technologies a national-security objective. In 2016, Xi Jinping described having core technologies controlled by others as China’s “greatest hidden danger”.

What followed was a three-stage process: creating alternatives, ensuring demand and replacing vulnerabilities. The 14th Five-Year Plan called for manufacturing to become “self-reliant and controllable, safe and efficient”. The 15th Five-Year Plan extended this into industrial-control software, precision bearings, motors, control systems and energy equipment—all areas where European companies retain important capabilities.

At the same time, Beijing has understood that diversification away from non-Chinese inputs could not just be ordered. Someone had to buy the alternatives to ensure the investments were worthwhile. Regulation securing that demand followed: operators were required to prioritise “secure and trustworthy” products; acceptable technologies for electricity systems were set out in official whitelists; and state-owned enterprises were obliged to support indigenous technological innovation.

The last stage is across-the-board substitution, and the OSW study shows the concrete manifestation of this in the energy sector. Since 2022, major state-owned energy utilities have translated the policy approach into their own procurement requirements. Their objections to imported systems are partly practical—poor reliability, slow spare-part delivery—and partly political: not “secure and controllable” and vulnerable to control by “foreign forces”.

In the wind sector, the campaign focuses on systems used to operate and control power assets. The technologies being targeted point to perceived risks of remote disruption and loss of control over power generation stemming from foreign presence in software, databases and other connected elements of critical infrastructure.

## Use China’s risk map to identify Europe’s vulnerabilities

The EU should treat China’s localisation agenda as a guide to how Beijing assesses strategic risk. China does not seek to localise every technology at once. Instead, it sets short- and long-term localisation objectives, and concentrates resources on selected capabilities and parts of the technological stack. Those choices therefore offer a window into which dependencies Beijing considers most dangerous. It is a playbook from which the EU can take inspiration as it weighs its [own trade-offs](https://ecfr.eu/publication/trust-and-trade-offs-how-to-manage-europes-green-technology-dependence-on-china/?amp)—which dependencies are worth the cost of removing and which are not.

The useful lesson is in the prioritisation: where Beijing is prepared to accept foreign dependence, where it seeks to reduce it and where it is willing to spend heavily to eliminate it. The Chinese leadership’s focus on the threat of remote disruption and loss of control to foreign actors over power generation points, in reverse, at the strategic vulnerability that Chinese technologies with remote access create in Europe.

When Beijing judges a technology sensitive enough to demand domestic control, European authorities should ask themselves what vulnerability it is seeking to close and whether Europe faces an equivalent exposure through Chinese suppliers. Europe should pay as much attention to what Chinese companies are eliminating from their own critical systems as to what Beijing wants to sell abroad.

## Decide on high-risk suppliers at EU level

Designating high-risk suppliers and third countries, and imposing mitigation measures, should sit at the EU level. Information and communications technology (ICT) risks cross national borders. In energy, disruption to grid infrastructure or generation assets can have cascading effects beyond the country where it originates, as the [2025 Iberian blackout](https://ecfr.eu/article/a-brighter-future-why-upgrading-the-grid-is-vital-for-europes-competitiveness/?amp) demonstrated. EU-level mitigation measures close the loophole that fragmented implementation creates: a supplier judged to pose an unacceptable security risk in one member state must not be able to simply shift its business to another.

EU-level designations also take the political pressure off individual member states. The [5G Toolbox](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/eu-toolbox-5g-security), the European Commission’s non-binding framework for mitigating cyber-security risks in telecommunications infrastructure, is the lesson in what happens otherwise. Five years after its adoption, only [13 of the EU’s 27 member states](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:52026SC0156) had imposed restrictions on high-risk suppliers, though 22 had the legal powers to do so. Parts of Europe’s 5G infrastructure remain dependent on high-risk vendors, with Germany the most prominent example. Eight years after the debate about these vulnerabilities started, about [60%](https://www.lightreading.com/6g/huawei-5g-deal-defended-by-deutsche-telekom-boss-as-6g-ban-looms) of its radio access network is still provided by Chinese vendors. The share of European vendors present in China’s critical advanced communication systems has since fallen to [less than 3%](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/324592/20260815/nokia-closes-china-rd-hub-5g-world-splits-rival-supply-chains.htm).

## Radically rethink reciprocity

> **“**Beijing criticises the revised Cybersecurity Act as unfairly targeting Chinese companies, while its own procurement notices explicitly name European companies as supply-chain risks to be removed from critical infrastructure.”

Beijing’s [complaints](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/14578-The-EU-Cybersecurity-Act/F33393498_en) about Europe’s risk mitigation actions should be met with a plain and pragmatic observation: China does the same, more extensively and less transparently. Beijing [criticises](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202604/20/WS69e619c4a310d6866eb44785.html) the revised Cybersecurity Act as unfairly targeting Chinese companies, while its own procurement notices explicitly name European companies as supply-chain risks to be removed from critical infrastructure. Its grounds go well beyond technical faults or security incidents: a supplier’s foreign origin is itself disqualifying under a top-down localisation drive.

Under the revised Cybersecurity Act, whether a third country itself excludes EU-origin products from critical infrastructure should be considered when the EU assesses non-technical cyber risks. The EU should stress its own “[legitimate right](https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/News/SpokesmansRemarks/art/2026/art_6ba67ba24946452099098f1c83e3f408.html)”, in Beijing’s own phrase, to protect critical infrastructure, and use the evidence of China’s localisation drive to address asymmetric procurement conditions through the [International Procurement Instrument](https://ecfr.eu/publication/brussels-holdem-european-cards-against-trumpian-coercion/?amp). Trust cannot be a one-way street. Chinese companies should not compete freely for EU public contracts while European firms face systematic exclusion or replacement in China.

Europe is facing a less integrated world: supply chains are already concentrated in a few places, while global technology and energy systems are fragmenting. Openness itself is no longer a virtue, but increasingly a vulnerability. Those trends are not going to reverse any time soon. By eliminating European exposure in its own energy infrastructure, the Chinese leadership has set the tone. It is on Europe to take the message.

_The European Council on Foreign Relations does not take collective positions. ECFR publications only represent the views of their individual authors._

title: China and India Want Much the Same Things From South Asia
summary: La revista de prensa "Tribuna Libre" es una hemeroteca virtual, con acceso gratuito, que ofrece el texto completo de los principales artículos de opinión publicados en diversos medios de comunicación. Forma parte del [proyecto educativo y d
content:
La revista de prensa "Tribuna Libre" es una hemeroteca virtual, con acceso gratuito, que ofrece el texto completo de los principales artículos de opinión publicados en diversos medios de comunicación. Forma parte del [proyecto educativo y de investigación](https://www.almendron.com/asociacion.php) de la Asociación Cultural sin ánimo de lucro «Almendrón».

In this pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi (right) shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a welcome ceremony before the start of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept. 12. Alexander Kazakov/Pool/AFP via Getty

Last month’s BRICS summit marked the pinnacle of an ongoing reset in China-India relations. Chinese President Xi Jinping made his first visit to India in almost seven years for the summit. That visit followed Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to China last year—also his first in seven years—to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Tianjin.

The partial renormalization of relations comes after the two countries’ border conflagration in 2020, which was the worst flare-up of hostilities between both countries in more than four decades. Steps taken to revive relations have included the resumption of direct flights and a relaxation of visa and investment restrictions. Even the intractable border issue has seen substantive progress, as noted by the meeting between Indian National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in August, which produced an eight-point [consensus](https://x.com/EOIBeijing/status/2092626800711225488) as part of their Special Representatives framework. The same month, trade along three border passes [resumed](https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-china-cross-border-trade-resumes-after-6-years-101785637096016.html) after a gap of six years.

On a global level, too, China’s and India’s leaders have had something of a meeting of minds on many issues to do with the international order. At the BRICS summit in India, the 140-point [New Delhi Declaration](https://www.mea.gov.in/bilateral-documents?dtl/41776/BRICS_New_Delhi_Declaration_Building_for_Resilience_Innovation_Cooperation_and_Sustainability_September_12_2026) made several references to the Trump administration’s disruptive foreign policies. These included the need for strengthening a “predictable and rules-based multilateral trading system”, condemning the “imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law”, and expressing “concern about ongoing conflicts in many parts of the world and the current state of polarization and fragmentation in the international order”.

Yet while engagement at the bilateral and global level continues to gain momentum, an overlooked area of engagement is the need for greater cooperation at the regional level. The recent flash floods in Nepal triggered by a glacial collapse near the Chinese border, for example, highlighted the need for a shared Himalayan water diplomacy framework.

After initial apprehension from Kathmandu to accepting foreign aid, China and India have emerged as key sources of humanitarian assistance following that disaster. However, this is being done in [parallel](https://foreignpolicy.com/2026/09/01/nepal-tibet-floods-china-india-disaster-response-border-dispute/) rather than in coordination.

Speaking at the U.N. General Assembly in late September, Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah [called](https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/09/25/balendra-shah-un-speech-full-transcript-of-nepal-prime-minister-s-address-to-the-81st-un-general-assembly) for a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism, led by Nepal, China, and India, to share satellite data and expertise to monitor glacial lakes and strengthen joint early-warning systems. Forums such as the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development—[based](https://www.icimod.org/) in Nepal and comprising eight member states, including China and India—are well positioned to play such a role. Given the long-standing climate of mistrust in the bilateral relationship, projects will need to be assessed on a case-by-case basis and avoid disputed or sensitive territories. But this approach offers a “win-win” solution. It helps prevent India becoming further marginalized in its own neighborhood while facilitating a greater degree of transparency and accountability for an expanded roster of Chinese initiatives in the region.

Over the last decade, China has emerged as a leading trade, investment, and defense partner for most countries in South Asia. Beijing’s keen interest in the region is fueled by a combination of the need to maintain a stable periphery, seeking markets for its exports and investments, and securing alternative trade routes to overcome what then-Chinese President Hu Jintao referred to as a “[Malacca Dilemma](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14799850802006555)”. From New Delhi’s perspective, Beijing’s interests in South Asia are also driven by latent efforts to challenge India’s position in the region, once referred to as a “[String of Pearls](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09700160801886314)” strategy of strategic encirclement. To its credit, New Delhi has moved away from the era of viewing South Asia as its exclusive sphere of influence while demonstrating a growing willingness to partner with like-minded countries on development and infrastructure initiatives in South Asia. For example, it is working with [Japan](https://www.business-standard.com/economy/news/japan-pm-s-india-visit-northeast-high-on-agenda-during-modi-takaichi-talks-126063001011_1.html) through the Act East Forum on infrastructure projects in India’s geopolitically sensitive northeast. But New Delhi still maintains an aversion to an expanded Chinese role in South Asia, given the history of bad blood in the Sino-Indian relationship.

New Delhi’s futile attempts to keep China out of the region have prompted Beijing to develop its own regional initiatives that exclude India. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, established in 2015, was an early example of this, forming a key pillar of its Belt and Road Initiative. This has now been supplemented by newer initiatives, such as [trilateral](https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/inaugural-meeting-of-bangladesh-china-pakistan-trilateral-mechanism-held-on-19-june-2025?mission=chengdu) dialogues with Bangladesh and Pakistan as well as with Afghanistan and Pakistan.

China’s engagement with South Asia has also served to strengthen regional connectivity through infrastructure projects. An example is the [Colombo International Container Terminal](https://www.cict.lk/) in Sri Lanka, which is financed and operated through a joint venture between China Merchants Holdings and the Sri Lanka Ports Authority. In Bangladesh, China is also overseeing the modernization of [Mongla Port](https://today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd/public/print/china-backed-project-to-develop-mongla-port-as-regional-hub-experts-1746558248), the country’s second-largest seaport.

This engagement extends to a people-to-people level. When visiting Kathmandu recently, I was surprised to find a dedicated immigration line at the airport for Chinese nationals (alongside separate lines for Indian and Nepali nationals). China has been convening the [China-South Asia Expo](https://www.csa-expo.com/en/) trade fair in Kunming since 2013, and several Chinese academic institutions also maintain South Asia [institutes](https://www.siis.org.cn/researchEn/17.jspx). Beijing is even playing an increasingly active mediation role, as noted in the case of recent hostilities between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Beijing also claims to have played such a role during the brief India-Pakistan conflict in 2025 (although New Delhi has [disputed](https://www.timesnownews.com/india/had-no-role-government-sources-reject-chinas-mediation-claim-on-india-pakistan-ceasefire-article-153374297) this).

South Asia’s hub-and-spokes political geography—with India being the only country that shares a border with every other state in the region—makes India central to South Asia’s regional architecture. However, New Delhi’s often strained relations with its neighbors and China’s expanded role in the region have prompted some to [ponder a South Asian regional architecture without India](https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/10/20/india-region-bangladesh-pakistan/). Such views have been fueled by the fact that South Asia’s primary regional forum—the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)—has not held a summit since 2014, following a breakdown in India-Pakistan relations. India’s resistance to working with Pakistan has been the primary obstacle to SAARC’s revival (although New Delhi argues that Islamabad’s support for terrorism is the original sin).

In reality, most countries in the region seek to maintain cordial relations with both China and India. Much is said about India’s commitment to [strategic autonomy](https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/11/26/india-end-strategic-autonomy/) in its foreign policy. However, other South Asian countries also have a long-standing tradition of pursuing a multialigned foreign policy. While a handful of countries are in the “China camp” (Pakistan) or “India camp” (Bhutan), most seek to engage both as a means of meeting their development needs while preserving their autonomy. In this context, regimes in the region remain averse to any push to choose between major powers or, worse, carve the region (or for that matter the world) into competing spheres of influence.

Indeed, historically, the smaller states of South Asia have sought to leverage the Sino-Indian rivalry to extract concessions from both countries. This has not always worked in practice, amid concerns about Beijing’s opaque lending practices; Sri Lanka’s Hambantota project, for instance, became synonymous with China’s “[debt trap](https://www.ft.com/content/e150ef0c-de37-11e7-a8a4-0a1e63a52f9c)” diplomacy. Greater China-India alignment in South Asia offers a means to alleviate these concerns.

When considering specific projects the two countries could work on together, water is one area of particular need.

As an upper riparian state, China should be included in discussions about shared river systems in South Asia. So far, these efforts have been largely bilateral: the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan and Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh, for example. Both of these happen to be in limbo, with New Delhi putting the former in abeyance following last year’s India-Pakistan hostilities, while the latter is due to expire in December. Still, a multilateral approach that includes China is required—particularly given the fact that most of the major river systems of South Asia originate in China.

India has direct interests in this given China’s construction of the world’s largest hydroelectric power project across a river (the Brahmaputra/Yarlung Tsangpo) that traverses both countries. And a recent agreement to resume sharing hydrological data between both countries, alongside reviving an expert-level mechanism on trans-border rivers, is a step in the right direction.

Another area of alignment is development. As with the response to the Nepal floods, both countries are often pursuing development initiatives in parallel. An example of this is the Koshi Corridor, a highway and power transmission project in eastern Nepal, with India’s Export-Import Bank providing a [line of credit](https://www.indembkathmandu.gov.in/commerce-wing-brief) to finance the electricity transmission line and China pledging to finance portions of the road project. Ideally, this should be an area of cooperation, especially given that the road project aims to [connect](https://peoplesreview.com.np/2026/05/19/nepals-shortest-india-china-route-biratnagar-kimathanka-track-opens/) India and China through Nepal.
