title: Strategic Implications of the US-China Summit - International Institute for Iranian Studies
summary: 12:14 pm - 15 Oct 2026 The recent bilateral [summit](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/09/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-advances-a-fair-and-reciprocal-relationship-with-china-while-hosting-historic-state-visit/) between US P
content:
12:14 pm - 15 Oct 2026

The recent bilateral [summit](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/09/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-advances-a-fair-and-reciprocal-relationship-with-china-while-hosting-historic-state-visit/) between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington highlighted the complex, transactional state of global superpower relations. While the meeting was framed as an effort to restore strategic stability, it primarily underscored deep structural divergence across technology policy, trade sanctions and regional security conflicts. High-stakes negotiations over artificial intelligence (AI) governance remains stalled beneath intense commercial competition. Meanwhile, the economic fallout from the escalating conflict with Iran has exposed limits in Washington’s tariff enforcement and sanctions posture. These realities demonstrate a dynamic where both nations pursue tactical economic flexibility while advancing aggressive strategic rivalry, mirroring the multifront economic statecraft of Cold War strategic balancing.

This strategic divergence is most acute in the AI race, where the competition over AI is rapidly accelerating across hardware infrastructure and model deployment. US technological dominance relies on massive capital expenditure. According to the [Stanford AI Index Report](https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf), private US investment in AI reached $285.9 billion in 2025, far outpacing China’s direct private spending of $12.4 billion. Individual US cloud technology providers are committing upwards of $150 billion in annual infrastructure spend to maintain compute dominance. The US economy has become heavily tied to this infrastructure buildout, with equity markets and national growth increasingly dependent on sustained corporate spending.

China is countering this capital disparity through an aggressive [open-source model ecosystem](https://www.uscc.gov/sites/default/files/2026-03/Two_Loops--How_Chinas_Open_AI_Strategy_Reinforces_Its_Industrial_Dominance.pdf). By distributing high-performing open-source weights globally, Chinese tech developers compress inference pricing and put severe commercial pressure on proprietary US AI firms. US companies must justify hundreds of billions in capital expenditures while competing against comparable open-source alternatives that reduce deployment costs globally. This structural split carries profound economic and geopolitical consequences for the trajectory of the technology race, resembling historical Cold War efforts to build sphere-of-influence technology networks. As US firms shoulder the immense cost of training proprietary frontier models, Chinese open-source releases lower token costs, directly undercutting US enterprise margins and lowering long-term returns on capital. Furthermore, by making open-source models the default choice for cost-conscious foreign enterprises and Global South economies, Beijing embeds its technological ecosystem globally and builds systemic dependency without violating Western hardware controls. This architectural gap ultimately paralyzes regulatory progress, as Washington focuses on frontier safety risks and intellectual property protections, while Beijing leverages open distribution to counter Western containment, rendering joint oversight improbable.

Efforts toward bilateral AI regulation face severe structural challenges amidst these divergent strategies. Both governments remain intentionally vague on governance standards, preferring strategic ambiguity over binding limits that might restrict native development. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [noted](https://es.tradingview.com/news/benzinga:e3d5d00f2094b:0-scott-bessent-says-us-china-to-meet-in-2-months-on-ai-threats-we-want-to-start-discussing-protocols/) that follow-up bilateral talks might occur in Shenzhen in two months, yet no formal agenda or firm date has been set. With neither state willing to risk technological subordination, effective joint oversight remains improbable.

Beyond technological friction, broader economic vulnerabilities stemming from the Middle East crisis have severely constrained Washington’s capacity to execute its trade strategy against Beijing. China’s primary exposure in the conflict stems from its energy import structure, as maritime blockades and shipping threats around Iranian ports and the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted Beijing’s direct purchases of Iranian crude, forcing Chinese state refiners to rely more heavily on Russian and Gulf-based alternatives. At the same time, surging global energy costs driven by these Middle Eastern disruptions forced pragmatic tactical adjustments in US foreign policy. The US decision to strike a supply deal with Moscow alongside the US Treasury Department’s OFAC license [authorizing](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261009_33) Russian-origin diesel fuel imports, aimed at delivering massive volumes of diesel to global and domestic markets, demonstrates how energy inflation overrides broader economic pressure campaigns.

This shift directly weakens the credibility of enforcement under legislative frameworks such as the [Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefings-statements/2026/09/congressional-bill-h-r-5334-signed-into-law/), which mandates targeted secondary tariff penalties of up to 100% on major importers of Russian energy assets. China remains the premier buyer of Russian crude oil and secondary energy products. Expecting Beijing to comply with US tariff demands or secondary sanctions becomes unenforceable when Washington grants itself policy carve-outs to stabilize domestic fuel supplies. When domestic macroeconomic conditions threaten consumer stability, primary sanctions mechanisms lose deterrence power. Beijing recognizes that the United States cannot simultaneously manage severe Middle Eastern energy disruptions and enforce aggressive tariff schedules against its largest trade partner without inducing economic self-harm.

During summit discussions, the escalation in Iran reflected a shared tactical desire to contain broader regional spillover rather than a sign of strategic alignment. Xi emphasized preserving freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz to safeguard global maritime trade and secure critical energy transit for Chinese industrial needs. For Washington, keeping critical shipping lanes open is essential to preventing secondary oil shocks from further worsening domestic fuel inflation. While both leaders voiced support for de-escalation frameworks and protecting international shipping, Beijing stopped short of offering concrete commitments to reduce its economic ties with Tehran or join Western pressure campaigns. This posture preserves China’s flexibility across the Middle East while leaving US diplomatic and financial bandwidth tied down in regional crisis management.

Ultimately, the latest summit confirms that US-China relations are governed by transactional balancing rather than comprehensive reconciliation. In technology, heavy US capital investment faces persistent pressure from Chinese open-source innovation, while structured AI regulation remains stalled. In trade, US energy vulnerabilities arising from the Middle East conflict have undermined tariff policy consistency. As long as global energy shocks and technological competition persist, bilateral engagement will produce tactical pauses rather than long-term strategic alignment.

title: Anatomy of a lie: how misinformation is spreading through US midterm campaigns
summary: W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardia
content:
W here is James Talarico? The question ricocheted around rightwing echo chambers before metastasising into a conspiracy theory – and a reminder of the persistent danger of disinformation in the [US midterm elections.](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026)

The smear campaign began when Talarico, [the Democratic candidate](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/04/texas-primaries-democrats-texas) for the US Senate in Texas, was not seen in public for nine days. His campaign was slow to explain why. While nature abhors a vacuum, Donald Trump and social media seize on one and weaponise it.

On 30 September, Talarico spoke at a Hispanic Business Council event by video. He had been diagnosed with the flu at an urgent care facility in Dallas after “starting to feel kind of under the weather a few days ago”, he said, and would not appear in person because he had a fever and was still contagious.

On 7 October, the president held a rally in San Antonio, Texas, and claimed without evidence that “Tala-freako”, as he nicknames the Democrat, is vegan. [Trump asserted](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/08/donald-trumps-texas-rally-rocked-by-repeated-protests): “He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”

On the same day, an X account with the username “Dan The Man, Always with a Plan” and a photo of “Trump 2028” cap tweeted without evidence: “He had a mental health crisis. That is what I heard from someone who would know inside information.”

On 8 October, Steve Bannon, a former White House chief strategist, stirred the pot further on his influential War Room podcast in an interview with former Trump fundraiser Caroline Wren, [who baselessly claimed](https://x.com/RealAmVoice/status/2108313243382952207?s=20): “I’m hearing that he checked himself into a mental institution – that he had a full-blown, like, mental breakdown.”

On the same day, Ken Paxton, the Republican running against Talarico, weighed in with [a social media post](https://x.com/KenPaxtonTX/status/2108250407277588546?s=20) that showed Talarico on a “Wanted” poster and said: “Jimmy appears to be having a full-blown mental Tala-freak-out on the national stage. My campaign has a simple request: proof of life.”

On 9 October, Spencer Pratt, a former candidate for mayor of Los Angeles, [offered his take](https://x.com/spencerpratt/status/2108553958696399249?s=20): “My sources are telling me Talarico is in a mental health facility. His campaign has stopped actively planning events in the vital homestretch of the campaign.”

Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux theater on 31 August. Photograph: Brandon Bell/Getty Images

Right media sites swung into action. RedState, the Daily Wire, the Right Scoop, Twitchy and PJ Media all amplified the false claims. Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, put more toxins in the bloodstream with posts such as: “The Talarico campaign is hiding something big that voters ought to know about.”

Then, on 11 October, came the supposed coup de grâce. Conservative social media influencer Nick Sortor posted a 47-second audio clip on X that he said proved that Talarico had been discharged earlier in the week from [Lindner Center of Hope](https://lindnercenterofhope.org/), a mental health treatment centre in Mason, Ohio.

The call was placed by Rhein Amacher, a self-described “right-wing provocateur”. In the clip, a woman whom Sorter claimed was an employee there says it looked like Talarico “was just discharged this evening”. The online Maga faithful were jubilant.

But not for long. The Bulwark obtained the full phone call showing the purported employee had repeatedly denied any record of Talarico being at the centre. The timeline also did not add up. Amacher said he made the call to the mental health centre on Saturday evening, but Talarico was seen at the Austin City Limits music festival on Friday. On Saturday, he made an appearance at a Kacey Musgraves concert in Dallas.

The Lindner Center of Hope [wrote in an X post](https://x.com/LindnerCtrHope/status/2109430626562785517?s=20) on Sunday that Talarico “has never received treatment” from the facility. Talarico replied to the post, saying, “I’ve never even been to Ohio.” He included a tears of joy emoji.

JT Ennis, a spokesperson for Talarico, called Sorter’s claim “a lie designed to promote a pathetic conspiracy theory” in an X post and wrote that Talarico had been recovering from the flu at his home in Austin. Talarico has type 1 diabetes, placing him at higher risk for flu-related complications.

Even Maga followers began to acknowledge that the claim had collapsed. But if the episode appeared absurd, its implications for the midterms were serious.

[Reed Galen](https://x.com/reedgalen), a former Republican strategist and cofounder of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group, said: “It was a bit wild but a good reminder to all of us how sophisticated, effective and efficient the rightwing/ bot/ Russian generated misinformation-disinformation machine is.

“This story came from some weirdos in Ohio or whatever but the point is that someone or something picked it up and amplified it to a point where – despite no evidence of reality – it became something that was an issue in the [Texas](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/texas) Senate campaign.”

Galen added: “Even if Talarico wins, that in and of itself was a win for the tactic. If you have the ability and the willingness to do this stuff, it’s not gonna work every time, but if you do it a lot, sometimes you’re gonna have success, and sometimes those successes might be strategic in nature, not just tactical.”

Disinformation has been rampant in elections for at least a decade and 2026 is no different. NewsGuard, a company that tracks online misinformation, says it has identified and debunked [25 false claims](https://www.newsguardtech.com/special-reports/2026-elections-misinformation-tracker/) about the midterms that have gone viral on social media platforms.

Its list of false claims includes [Abdul El-Sayed](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/abdul-el-sayed), the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan, having called for sharia law in the US during a 2022 speech; a Dominion Voting Systems whistleblower accusing US politicians of taking millions of dollars in bribes to rig the 2026 midterm elections; and Ken Paxton’s Senate campaign paying for a Texas billboard that says “Pedos Ain’t That Bad”.

Another example related to an image that purportedly showed Rob Sand, a centrist Democratic candidate for governor of Iowa, campaigning with the progressives Ilhan Omar and Tim Walz. NewsGuard found it was generated by artificial intelligence (AI).

Even as AI gives new tools to nefarious actors, defences have been weakened. Last year, US secretary Marco Rubio [shut down](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/us-state-department-closing-office-aimed-countering-foreign-disinformation-2025-04-16/) the state department’s Counter Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference office, accusing it of censorship and wasting US taxpayer money.

Major tech platforms – notably Musk’s X and Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta – have gutted trust, safety and factchecking teams, turning online spaces into a lawless wild west. Musk has [spent a record $366m](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/13/elon-musk-political-donor-midterm-elections) in ⁠the election cycle so far to help Republicans retain control of Congress.

[Richard Hasen](https://law.ucla.edu/faculty/faculty-profiles/richard-l-hasen), a professor at UCLA School of Law and election law expert, said: “When you’ve got Elon Musk owning one of the important social media platforms and being a vector for spreading the misinformation, and also when you’ve got the companies like Meta no longer doing the same kind of trust and safety work, it’s just an atmosphere where this kind of stuff can spread.”

But there is another, more optimistic perspective. While the Talarico rumours spread like wildfire in corners of the internet, they did not penetrate the mainstream media, and fizzled out once the reality became clear.

Hasen added: “The Talarico case shows the limits of being able to do this. This was something that was easily disproven and could have potentially even backfired, showing that the anti-Talarico forces are so desperate that they have to make up a false claim to try to boost a weak candidate.

“Every election now we’re hearing it’s going to be ‘the AI election’ and voters are going to be tricked. What I think is happening in part is that everyone’s on their guard. We all know that we can’t necessarily believe our eyes or our ears and things that a politician might appear to say or do might not necessarily be true, so that’s a little bit of a natural check.”

Hasen points out that candidates are better equipped to dismantle digital lies. To debunk the rumour, Talarico shared home security camera footage with the New York Times, establishing his presence at home. “Because we’re leaving digital footprints everywhere, that sometimes could be another way to debunk a rumour.”

[Tara Setmayer](https://www.tarasetmayer.com/), a former Republican communications director on Capitol Hill, also believes that the conspiracy theories have lost their novelty value. “The voters have become hip to this game,” she said. “There are too many other negative things going on in everyday American lives, so I don’t think these types of cheap attacks are going to resonate at this point.

“The difference between this election cycle and past election cycles is that, because it seems like we’ve been here before and we know how batshit crazy Maga can be, that mainstream media isn’t platforming the crazy as often,” said Setmayer._“_ They’re actually reporting it in a way with the healthy amount of scepticism that it deserves, so it’s dismissed off the top whereas in the past it was so novel.”

Setmayer added: “At this point now it feels like [Donald Trump](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump) and Maga’s greatest hits: we’re really in the fat Elvis period of the Maga election campaign tactics and it’s obvious to everyone. The absurdity is finally breaking through even with some Republican voters, evidenced by how terrible Donald Trump’s numbers are and Republicans writ large.”

title: What’s Going On With China’s Military Exercises This Week? - Domino Theory
summary: Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they ar
content:
Many in Taiwan have treated Chinese military exercises this week as significant, following President Lai Ching-te’s (賴清德) National Day speech. But analysis of the location and timing of the drills suggests they are more routine than they are extraordinary.

“China launches 5-day military exercises after Taiwan’s National Day,” read one typical [headline](https://www.rti.org.tw/en/news?uid=3&pid=237144), from Radio Taiwan International. Reuters [described](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-says-it-is-closely-monitoring-series-chinese-live-fire-drills-2026-10-12/) “a series of Chinese live-fire drills,” based on navigation restriction notices published by the China Maritime Safety Administration for five zones in different regions. These areas are all close to China’s coast and range from the Bohai Sea in the north to the South China Sea in the south.

The Chinese Communist Party’s decision to conduct live-fire drills immediately after the National Day address “does nothing to advance regional peace and will only heighten regional tensions,” said Chuang Jui-hsiung (莊瑞雄), head of the Democratic Progressive Party caucus, speaking at a [press conference](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eYyNoOU-StY) on Monday about a different National Day speech by opposition leader Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜).

In [previous years](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgd4yn45qlo), China has launched major military exercises around Taiwan after National Day, framing them as a response to perceived provocations in the president’s speech.

But is that actually what is happening here?

There are some problems with this theory.

As all the coverage acknowledges, these drills are neither around nor close to Taiwan. China has not publicly commented on the exercises this week, nor tied them to Lai’s speech.

The five drill areas described appear to be a partial snapshot of scheduled Chinese military activity at sea this week. A comprehensive review of the Maritime Safety Administration’s website by Domino Theory revealed a total of 12 relevant notices published before Monday. Four of them were for live-fire exercises, the remaining eight were for non-specified military training. The drills are of varying lengths of time, some even extending longer than seven days.

In September, 28 navigation restriction notices were published for live-fire exercises alone. It doesn’t appear that any of these were reported on as being unusual, despite there being broad crossover in the locations involved with the “five” this week.

“I don’t see anything in these notices that strikes me as particularly unusual or significant,” Ethan Connell for Taiwan Security Monitor, a group at George Mason University, told Domino Theory.

The Maritime Safety Administration regularly issues navigation warnings for live-fire exercises and military training, Connell said in a written response, adding “there isn’t much evidence that these five exercises are part of any larger, coordinated training or operation.”

Taiwan’s defense minister, Wellington Koo (顧立雄), told the legislature on Monday that the drills appear to be a “not particularly large,” routine exercise, adding that Taiwan must be cautious and will continue to monitor the situation, adding, “You can see that the timing was deliberately chosen to follow the October 10th National Day address.”

The drills “are likely a response to Lai’s speech, which is to be expected,” said Lyle Morris, a senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis. “But nothing to panic about.”

The number of exercises is noteworthy, Morris said, but doesn’t rise to the level of something like the “[Joint Sword](https://dominotheory.com/china-announces-military-exercises-around-taiwan/)” drills from previous years. Those were among the exercises that took place around Taiwan.

Other analysts disagree about the timing.

“I would not interpret these as exercises targeting President Lai Ching-te,” said Chieh Chung (揭仲), a fellow at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research think tank in Taipei.

Chieh wrote to Domino Theory that [Lai’s speech](https://dominotheory.com/taiwan-intent-on-increasing-defense-spending/) had been uncontroversial this year, but pointed out: “Leaving observers to speculate whether the drills were triggered by Beijing’s displeasure with President Lai’s speech is enough for Beijing to achieve its objective.”

Lai’s only significant mention of China was to say it was engaged in authoritarian expansion, applying pressure “through military and gray-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.”

“Most notices were issued before Lai’s speech, so the drills look routine,” said Ben Lewis, who runs the website [PLATracker](https://www.platracker.com/), which records Chinese military activity around Taiwan. Lewis doesn’t think that the drills are any more significant than they look. But he warned that a closure moving into the Strait or near Taiwan would change this view.

“The CCP disguises its intrusive actions under the pretexts of law enforcement and scientific research, attempting to expand its operational scope during non-conflict periods and create the illusion of de facto jurisdiction,” the Defense Ministry told Domino Theory, answering a question on whether the five drill areas were different in some way. “These moves severely undermine the international order and challenge our law enforcement authority within our waters.”

The Chinese military near Taiwan had been relatively quiet earlier this week, according to [data](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2109811367033143387?s=20) published by the Ministry of National Defense, although its data for [yesterday](https://x.com/MoNDefense/status/2110536140809719853?s=20) showed more activity, including a circumnavigation of Taiwan by an [uncrewed aerial vehicle](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110355583971053644?s=20), or UAV.

China has also this week deployed a carrier battle group into the Western Pacific, centered around the Liaoning aircraft carrier. Based on [information](https://x.com/jointstaffpa/status/2110317371932205415?s=20) published by the Japanese military, the battle group passed through the Okinawa archipelago and was located approximately 370 kilometers to the east of Taiwan on Wednesday.

Taiwan’s data for Chinese activity do not routinely show information about ship type and location, unlike the data for aircraft. Wednesday’s data do not appear to show any flights by Chinese naval aviation east of but close to Taiwan. Taiwan’s Defense Ministry said today that it wouldn’t comment on specifics of the carrier’s activity.

Jason Wang, the chief operating officer of geointelligence firm ingeniSPACE, said it was wrong to associate the drills with the National Day speech and that tying the two together helped with United Front narratives. “These drills were planned and should be seen in the context of raising overall readiness,” Wang said.

Experts contacted for this story did not think the five drill areas reported on this week are different or more significant than the other announced drills that have received less attention. Nor is there any obvious reason that attention should be placed on these when similar exercises last month were largely ignored.

Nonetheless, even if this week is not unusual, that may be its own problem. This high tempo of training is cause for concern in itself. China, said Wang from ingeniSPACE, is exercising more than it is resting.

title: Nutrition experts call for big food ban at biennial congress
summary: Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event. From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for
content:
Nutrition experts have called for a ban of “big food” from future SA Nutrition Congresses following an alleged conflict of interest at this year’s event.

From 7-9 October the Nutrition Society of South Africa (NSSA) and the Association for Dietetics in South Africa (Adsa) hosted their biennial Nutrition Congress, a platform for researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, practitioners and other stakeholders to share and discuss current evidence and developments in nutrition.

This year companies Danone Southern Africa (Danone SA), Unilever South Africa and PepsiCo were exhibitors at the event, which nutrition experts said was a conflict of interest.

According to Tamryn Frank, a nutrition expert and senior lecturer at the University of the Western Cape’s School of Public Health, it is a conflict of interest for an event that aims to improve nutrition in South Africa to have companies like Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo, which produce and sell ultra-processed foods, sponsor it and exhibit at it. Frank added that there was increasing evidence that ultra-processed foods were linked to poor health outcomes like obesity and non-communicable diseases.

PepsiCo’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

If the ultra-processed food industry was allowed to sponsor and exhibit at the Nutrition Congress, to the layman it created the impression that the congress endorsed these companies as part of a solution to SA’s nutrition crisis, Frank said.

Nutrition expert and consultant researcher at the South African Medical Research Council, Catherine Pereira-Kotze, noted that since South Africa was characterised by undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies, together with overweight and obesity, and high levels of poverty, inequality, unemployment and various other social problems, families should not be spending the little they had on ultra-processed foods. Rather, families should be prioritising fruit, vegetables and whole foods in accordance with [national food-based dietary guidelines](https://www.fao.org/nutrition/education/food-dietary-guidelines/regions/countries/south-africa/en/).

“The term ‘healthwashing’ comes to mind where by being aligned with this event it indicates that they are part of the solution. Because if you see the Nutrition Congress’ logo alongside the sponsors or the logos of these ultra-processed food companies I think it gives the impression that they are healthy options,” said Frank.

To protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank, Pereira-Kotze and other nutrition experts shared protest slides during their presentations and created a petition.

### Nutrition experts take a stand

Concerned about the alleged conflict of interest, Frank created a slide to use in her presentation condemning the ultra-processed food industry’s involvement in the congress.The slide stated:

“I DO NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Frank saw it fit to make this the third slide of her presentation as the second slide was a mandatory funding disclosure slide, she said. Frank shared the slide with other concerned speakers who also incorporated it into their presentations.

Zandile Kubeka, the Department of Health Deputy Director of Dietetics in the Child and Youth Health Directorate, shared a similar slide inspired by Frank’s during her presentation. The slide stated:

“THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH DOES NOT SUPPORT THE ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD INDUSTRY EXHIBITING AT THE CONGRESS

THIS IS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST”

Kubeka also noted the presence of ultra-processed food industry sponsors and exhibitors at the Nutrition Congress, and raised concerns regarding potential conflicts of interest in relation to their participation, according to Department of Health spokesperson Foster Mohale.

To further protest against the alleged conflict of interest, Frank had created a [petition](https://awethu.amandla.mobi/petitions/ban-big-food-from-the-nutrition-congress)with the help of Amandla.mobi, she said.

The petition first called on the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA to announce that no companies connected with ultra-processed foods would be allowed to sponsor or exhibit at future congresses or events. Second, they must issue an apology for allowing the ultra-processed food industry to participate in the congress.

### Safeguarding integrity

The Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA shared a collective written response by NSSA representative Elize Symington and Adsa president Maria van der Merwe in response to questions sent by Daily Maverick.

According to the Nutrition Society of SA, Danone, Unilever and PepsiCo complied with NSSA and Adsa’s criteria to participate.

All applications for participation as sponsors or exhibitors at the congress were accompanied by the information entities wanted to share and products to be exhibited, and an illustration of the exhibition stand, all of which had to be approved prior to the congress, it said.

It added that the congress organising committee also reviewed exhibition applications against healthy eating guidelines, compliance with applicable regulations, and alignment with the values and principles of the congress as guided by international consensus.

All congress exhibitors were allocated a stand in one of the exhibition areas to display the brands and products at a fee, and exhibition and sponsorship income was paid into pooled congress funds, according to the organisers.

Danone's exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Danone SA)

Although the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA recognised that commercial sponsorship of nutrition-related scientific and professional activities may create actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest, they did not agree that participation under the safeguards described compromised the independence or integrity of the congress, they said.

For this congress, exhibitors and sponsors were screened and had no role in determining the programme or in the selection of abstracts or speakers, according to the organisers. Private sector participation did not constitute or imply endorsement of any exhibitor’s products or practices, and all speakers declared their affiliations and funding during presentations, they added. The congress’ commitment to open debate on this topic was demonstrated by the inclusion of two sessions specifically addressing conflicts of interest in the programme.

Feedback received this year, including differing perspectives from across the nutrition community, would form part of the host organisations’ ongoing review. Any future policy decisions would be guided by the best available evidence and made through the governance structures of the Nutrition Society of SA and the Association for Dietetics in SA, they said when asked if companies connected to the ultra-processed food industry would be excluded from future congresses as demanded in the petition.

### Exhibitors respond

According to Dudu Mthuli, Nutrition and Health Lead at Unilever Southern Africa, there was no conflict of interest. Unilever was involved only in hosting an exhibition stand and in no other elements of the congress, she said.

Unilever’s stand communicated how their brands fitted into healthy eating. Unilever applied to exhibit at the event, because they were committed to partnering with like-minded stakeholders in educational and sponsorship activities that supported their view of making nutritious, balanced diets accessible, affordable, and enjoyable through science and expertise, Mthuli said.

She added that Unilever’s registered dietitians and food scientists also used the opportunity to keep up to date with science as presented at the sessions.

Unilever’s exhibition stand at the 2026 Nutrition Congress. (Photo: Supplied / Catherine Pereira-Kotze)

Danone saw its participation in the congress “not as a conflict of interest, but as a confluence of interest”, according to Head of Corporate and Regulatory Affairs at Danone SA, Leanne Kiezer.

Danone SA participated in the Nutrition Congress as a presenter in the scientific programme and as an exhibitor, she said. The FoodSAMSA Project published the report [Inside our Food Environments South Africa 2025](https://foodsamsa.samrc.ac.za/FOODSAMSA%20Report%20WP2.pdf) that assessed the commitments and practices of 29 food companies in South Africa for supporting healthier food environments and improving population nutrition. The independent report ranked Danone SA as the leading food company assessed, with a score of 83/100 for its commitments and practices for supporting food environments and improving population nutrition, according to Kiezer.

She added that the Association for Dietetics in South Africa had invited Danone SA to submit an abstract to the Nutrition Congress scientific committee, to share the study results and to provide further detail on the commitments and practices that contributed to Danone SA’s score. Danone SA submitted an abstract that was independently reviewed by the congress’s scientific committee and accepted for an oral presentation as part of the scientific programme.

Danone SA also participated as an exhibitor, with a stand focused on sharing evidence on the health and nutritional benefits of yoghurt. The educational content was not brand or product specific and focused on yoghurt and its benefits from a category perspective, Kiezer said.

Danone SA believed that describing a food company or its portfolio through the single lens of “ultra-processed food” oversimplified the broader picture of nutritional quality, according to Kiezer. The overall nutritional profile of individual foods, and their contribution to dietary patterns, were also important considerations, she said.

Based on Danone SA’s assessment of total volumes sold in 2025, 74% passed the nutrient profiling calculator defined in draft Regulation 3337, while 71% would not carry warning labels under the current draft Regulation 3337 criteria, Kiezer claimed. These benchmarks provided important context on the nutritional quality of their portfolio, she said.

Daily Maverick contacted PepsiCo for comment, but had not received a response by the time of publication.**DM**

## Mauritius Imposes Curfew After Violent Protests

[FreeWorldMaps](https://www.freeworldmaps.net/africa/mauritius/mauritius-location-globe.jpg "https://www.freeworldmaps.net/africa/mauritius/mauritius-location-globe.jpg")

Where is Mauritius?

15 October 2026

Mauritius has[imposed](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo "https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm4g1rnj5qweo")an overnight curfew following violent protests over water shortages and the rising cost of living, marking the island's worst unrest in decades.

Demonstrations escalated after a woman was shot and injured by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting were not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody.

Protesters burned tyres, blocked roads and vandalised police stations and public infrastructure, prompting school and public transport closures.

The British embassy in Mauritius cautioned its citizens about the possibility of further demonstrations, advising them to steer clear of protests and large gatherings. The French embassy also urged French nationals in the country to remain vigilant.

Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam warned that those responsible would face consequences.

Analysts warn that unrest could return if water shortages persist until the rainy season in December.

title: North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
zh_title: 朝鲜和中国延迟12年后开通新桥
summary: 6 小时前 埃维岛和朱莉安娜·汗 新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州 据中国官方媒体报道，随着邻国之间贸易关系的改善，一座拖延已久的连接中国和朝鲜的公路大桥已经开通。中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是应对国际社会因平壤核武器计划而实施严厉制裁的生命线。新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州，将成为朝鲜的主要陆路通道。
content:
6 小时前

埃威岛和

朱莉安娜·汗

新鸭绿江大桥全长 3 公里（1.9 英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州

据中国官方媒体报道，随着邻国之间的贸易关系改善，一座拖延已久的连接中国和朝鲜的公路大桥已经开通。

中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是应对国际社会因平壤核武器计划而实施严厉制裁的生命线。

新鸭绿江大桥全长3公里（1.9英里），从中国边境城市丹东到朝鲜新义州，将成为两国之间贸易的主要陆路通道。

该项目最初定于 2014 年启动，但由于与北京的关系变得冷淡，朝鲜停止了道路和海关设施的建设，因此被无限期推迟。

中国国务院总理李强在周四的视频讲话中表示，这座大桥是“象征中朝传统友谊的新地标”，两国关系正在“翻开新的篇章”。

新鸭绿江大桥是具有数十年历史的中朝友谊大桥的替代方案，该大桥建于 1937 年至 1943 年日本帝国占领该地区期间。

中国外交部发言人毛宁周三表示，这座新大桥是两国之间“互联互通的重要设施”，并补充说这条路线将“进一步便利贸易和人员往来”。
去年，双边贸易额达到 27 亿美元，标志着恢复到大流行前的水平，这主要是由中国对朝鲜的出口推动的。

韩国外国语大学中国研究教授康俊英告诉英国广播公司，由于联合国对朝鲜的制裁仍然有效，跨境贸易“不太可能”突然增加。

“平壤还对突然涌入的中国进口产品保持警惕，这将大大扩大中国对其国内市场的影响力，”他补充道。

“中国很清楚这些担忧，因此贸易更有可能逐步增长。”

北京和平壤是长期盟友，双方签署了共同防御条约，这是中国与任何国家签署的唯一条约。这种关系经常被形容为“唇齿相依”，这是中国前领导人毛泽东首先提出的一句话。

但联盟并非没有紧张。

2010年代的大部分时间里，由于北京对平壤核武器计划的耐心逐渐减弱，两国关系一直处于冷淡状态。金正恩于 2017 年进行了核试验，此后加大了对被禁弹道导弹的试验力度，所有这些都增加了美国的警惕性，并加强了其与韩国和日本的军事联盟。

中国的态度最近发生了转变。
牛津大学讲师爱德华·豪厄尔（Edward Howell）告诉英国广播公司（BBC）：“虽然仅仅十年前，北京还公开批评朝鲜核化，甚至呼吁平壤无核化，但现在中国对此几乎没有说什么。”

观察人士称，原因之一是朝鲜因乌克兰战争而与俄罗斯走得更近。

至少 2,300 名朝鲜士兵[据信已死亡](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypr5985ejo) 在乌克兰为俄罗斯作战。作为回报，俄罗斯向朝鲜提供石油，这违反了联合国的制裁。据估计，2024 年俄罗斯已向平壤输送了[超过 10 亿桶石油](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjr4pr0gyyzo) 作为平壤武器和战略物资的付款。

【原文 English Original】
6 hours ago

Koh Ewe and

Julianna Khan

The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea

A long-delayed road bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, Chinese state media report, as trade ties improve between the neighbours.

China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a lifeline against heavy international sanctions over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme.

The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea, and is set to become the main land route for trade between them.

Its launch, initially slated for 2014, had been indefinitely postponed after North Korea halted construction of its roads and customs facilities, as relations with Beijing turned frosty.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang, in a video address on Thursday, said the bridge was a "new landmark symbolising the traditional friendship between China and North Korea", and that the two countries were "opening a new chapter" in bilateral ties.

The New Yalu River Bridge is an alternative to the decades-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which was built between 1937 and 1943 during Imperial Japan's occupation of the region.

The new bridge is an "important facility for connectivity" between the two countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday, adding that the route would "further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges".

Last year, bilateral trade reached $2.7bn, marking a recovery to pre-pandemic levels, mostly fuelled by Chinese exports to North Korea.

A sharp and sudden increase in trade across the border is "unlikely" as the UN sanctions on North Korea remain in effect, Kang Jun-young, a professor of Chinese studies at the Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, tells the BBC.

"Pyongyang is also wary of a sudden flood of Chinese imports that would greatly expand China's influence over its domestic market," he adds.

"China is well aware of these concerns, so trade is more likely to grow gradually."

Beijing and Pyongyang are long-standing allies with a mutual defence treaty, the only one that China has with any country. The relationship is often described "as close as lips and teeth", a remark first made by China's former leader Mao Zedong.

But the alliance is not without tension.

Ties were frosty for much of the 2010s as Beijing's patience over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme wore thin. Kim Jong Un conducted a nuclear test in 2017 and has since ramped up tests of banned ballistic missiles - all of which increased US wariness, and strengthened its military alliances with South Korea and Japan.

China's attitude has shifted more recently.

"Whilst only a decade ago, Beijing was overtly critical of North Korea's nuclearisation - and indeed calling for Pyongyang's denuclearisation - China is now saying little, if anything, to this effect," Edward Howell, a lecturer at the University of Oxford, tells the BBC.

Observers say one reason is that North Korea has grown closer to Russia because of the Ukraine war.

At least 2,300 North Korean soldiers are [believed to have died](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clypr5985ejo) fighting for Russia in Ukraine. In return, Russia supplies North Korea with oil, in violation of UN sanctions. In 2024, Russia was estimated to have sent [more than a billion barrels of oil](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjr4pr0gyyzo) as payment for Pyongyang's weapons and troops.

Last month, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge, which Russian state media said would allow the movement of up to 300 vehicles and more than 2,000 people every day.

So Beijing is believed to be trying to reassert its sway over Pyongyang by rekindling ties.

Air China resumed direct flights between Beijing and Pyongyang in March after a six-year hiatus triggered by the pandemic. The two countries [reopened passenger train services](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cdxz8v58xvyo) the same month.

Chinese President Xi Jinping's first state visit of this year, in June, was to Pyongyang, where he met North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

"The opening of the New Yalu River Bridge demonstrates bilateral relations are improving and that Xi Jinping's June visit to North Korea was more than symbolic," says Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul.

"But the long delay, including North Korea's pandemic self-isolation and domestic socioeconomic crackdowns, shows what a difficult partner Pyongyang can be for Beijing."

# 专利巴士申请加票价近两成 官员议员竟帮口 评论指是没抗衡力量的新香港宿命

香港四家专利巴士公司申请大幅加价，加幅由17.7%至8.1%不等，加幅之大，引起市民叫苦已是必然，但相关政策局在向立法会提交的文件则更多是为巴士公司解释，由爱国者垄断的立法会，其议员亦没有代市民叫屈，被报章社评形容官员和议员都是在「为加价保驾护航」；更有评论形容议员是， 巴士公司的「另类发言人」，预料小市民继续默默承受这种在没有民间社会抗衡力量下的「宿命」。

发表时间： 15/10/2026 - 10:39 更改时间： 15/10/2026 - 11:51

 14 分钟 浏览时间

 每天接送三百多萬人次的四家專利巴士公司申請大幅加價，市民叫苦，但負責審批的官員和立法會議員，卻對巴士持「理解」的立場。 © （麥燕庭提供）

 作者： [香港特约记者 麦燕庭](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF%E7%89%B9%E7%BA%A6%E8%AE%B0%E8%80%85-%E9%BA%A6%E7%87%95%E5%BA%AD/ "香港特约记者 麦燕庭")

广告

继续浏览后续

在2019年社会运动被打压之前，公用事业的加价申请幅度不单未见有被传媒形容为「狮子开大口」，更会引起立法会内尚有民主派的议员狠批，以及惹来民间的「民间监管公共事业联委会」代市民提出质疑和建议，但在爱国者治港和《港区国安法》实施後，立法会内民主派议员「清零」，不少民间组织亦已解散或偃旗息鼓，以致在运输及物流局各立法会提交四大巴士公司加价申请後，传媒只能街访个别市民表达心声，基本上都是指加幅过巨。

运输及物流局昨(14日)早向立法会提交的文件显示，巴士公司在4月时已提出加价申请，行走港九新界的城巴和九龙巴士公司(九巴)分别申请加价17.7%和16%；主要营运新界往返机场及北大屿山的龙运巴士有限公司(龙运)申请加幅是8.1%；而只在大屿山行驶的新大屿山巴士公司(屿巴)，申请加幅是9.8%。文件解释，巴士公司面对地下铁等交通工具的竞争丶油价持续高企丶营运和人工成本持续上升等挑战，需进一步提升财务状况以继续提供服务。

**「赚少了」便申请加价**

以油价为例，局方指出，受中东战事影响，车用柴油价格急升，3月燃油开支较1月急升85%至逾1.32倍，而8月的油价仍较1月增加近一倍；影响之下，巴士公司首季盈利普遍按年减少两至三成，加上乘客人数仍低於疫情前水平，在过去两年平均每日只录得逾370万乘客人次，仍较2010至2019年平均每日392万人次为低，反映乘客出行习惯出现结构改变，巴士公司面对挑战。

不过，大部分巴士公司并非因为亏蚀而申请加价，而是盈利下跌。文件指出，各巴士公司截至今年6月，临时估算税後盈利均较去年同期大跌55%至31%，当中只有屿巴是录得亏损。时间上，今次巴士公司申请加价亦只是与上次获准加价後不足一年半提出。资料显示，除了龙运巴士公司是在2023年6月加价4.2%之後丶事隔近三年再次申请加价，其馀三间巴士公司均在2025年1月起获准加价4.3%至7,5%後丶事隔一年零四个月後再提出加价降议。

立法会交通事务委员会明(16日)早将举行会议，讨论加价事宜，但传媒采访委员会主席陈恒镔等个别议员所得，议员对巴士公司的经营困难均抱「理解」和「无奈」的态度；个别议员更建议当局协助巴士公司增加非票务收入或提供短期补助来减轻加价压力。至於运输及物流局局长陈美宝亦只是说，会平衡巴士公司财务及市民负担能力，强调政府会做好把关工作。

**四报社评谈加价 半数显体谅 「谁为市民发声？」**

事关民生，香港十馀家报章中，有七家以巴士申请加价为头条新闻，但只有少部分在标题中已提出批评；当中，有四份报章以巴士申请加价为主题，批评的只占半数，但都只能望政府真的把好关，因为专利巴士公司加价须由特首会同行政会议批准。

《明报》社评以《巴士又加价折射困局 高油价时代急需对策》为题指出，政府须顾及加价对民生的影响，而在预见石油库存到明年下半年才有机会恢复而令油价回落，预料电力公司亦会随巴士後尘提出加价，呼吁政府拟定对策，协助市民应付燃料价格持续高企的危机。

《星岛日报》社论则以《专营巴士岂能动辄「嗌加价」 改革票价机制刻不容缓》为题指出，公众对巴士公司「开天杀价」无反制之力，唯一可倚仗的是政府，若港府过度侧重巴士公司的立场，将会引起民怨和消费信心下降，不利经济复苏。长远而言，当局除了帮助公司开源之外，还可考虑引入「可加可减」的票价调整机制，防止突然大幅加价的情况发生。

在社评中提出批评的，分别是《东方日报》和已停止发行实体报章的《成报》。《东方》以《巴士狼死(按：极狠的意思)加价 政府必须把关》为题指出，巴士公司的申请加幅可说是「飞擒大咬」，但「官员和议员则口径一致，松口为加价保驾护航。可怜小市民生活百上加斤，谁为我们发声？」社论续称，「人人化身巴士公司发言人」，估计巴士公司加价必然获批，以去年1月三间巴士公司获批加幅大约较申请加幅少两个百分点为例，预料今年两大巴士公司很大机会加价逾一成。

《东方》又说，巴士公司去年仍有盈利，但脱班丶削班等情况反而加剧，「蚀了一些即喊穷加价，还有官员议员替他们缓颊，商民待遇差距实在太大。」但以现在的情况，只能望声称重视市民负担能力的官员「不要得个讲字，必须做好把关，不能任由巴士公司开天杀价！」

由实体转为网上发表的《成报》，其社评以《4间巴士公司申加价幅度惊人 从没正视开源 只向市民伸手》为题，猛批巴士公司不思进取，经营思维落後，「习惯把自己的无能，变成乘客的帐单」，赚少了便以最省事的方式申请加价，而申靖亦沦为讨价还价的姿态，「彷佛(加幅)报高一点无妨，反正最後总有人替它修饰」，而市民亦被视作最终必须接受结果的一方。

资深新闻工作者李锦洪今早在网上节目中，对巴士加价及小市民反对无从的情况大加批评。他指出，高油价并非今日才出现的问题，但港府缺乏长远策略推动，议员亦没超前建议，反应更是与民生脱节丶对事件了解不足以致回应沦为笑话，慨叹「如此议政质素！」；再加上香港再没有民间社会的抗衡力量，令问题一直原地踏步。

# Taipei hospital highlights long-term medical work in Eswatini

10/15/2026 05:10 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

King Mswati III (center) poses for a photo during his visit to Taipei Medical University Hospital on Thursday. photo courtesy of the Taipei Medical University Hospital Oct. 15, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) The Taipei Medical University Hospital (TMUH) said Thursday it has been providing medical services in Eswatini since 2009, following a visit by King Mswati III to the hospital on Oct. 12.

In a news release, TMUH said Mswati was received by hospital superintendent Shih Chun-ming (施俊明).

Eswatini's absolute monarch arrived in Taiwan last week to attend the Republic of China's National Day celebrations.

Shih said the partnership has expanded from clinical care to medical personnel training and healthcare system development over the past 17 years, helping strengthen Eswatini's medical system.

Shih said TMUH had provided more than 50,000 person-visits of teaching and training services in Eswatini. Through long-term on-site services and the sharing of professional expertise, the hospital has also helped strengthen the country's healthcare capacity.

TMUH Vice Superintendent Wang Wei (王偉) said the hospital's TAIP-X smart healthcare platform has been introduced at Manzini Government Hospital in Eswatini, helping the hospital transition from paper-based operations to digital outpatient services and improve efficiency.

Wang said TMUH and the medical teams there have also established telemedicine services in pediatrics, hematology and oncology, endocrinology, rheumatology and immunology, nephrology, and dermatology.

Taiwanese specialists work with Eswatini resident physicians to provide real-time remote consultations, helping strengthen local specialist care and clinical skills, he added.

Looking ahead, Shih said TMUH will continue to expand medical cooperation with Eswatini by drawing on its clinical expertise and smart healthcare technologies, as well as through professional exchanges and personnel training, to help strengthen local healthcare capacity and raise the international profile of Taiwan's medical expertise.

(By Shen Pei-yao and Ko Lin)

## Details

AI connectivity is the backbone of your governance strategy, but the ecosystem underneath it won't stop moving. New models, new agents, new attack surfaces, every quarter. A governance plan built for today's stack breaks by next quarter's.
 So how do you build one that holds?

Join this live, interactive session and bring your real questions. Submit the governance challenges you're actually facing: budget overruns, policy sprawl, agent access control, compliance across teams, whatever's keeping you up at night. Walk away with a curated roadmap for planning and implementing your AI governance program. Not a generic framework. A plan built around where you are right now and where the market is headed next.

You'll leave with:

*   A framework for governance that adapts as models, agents, and tooling change, instead of one you have to rebuild every quarter
*   Answers to your specific governance questions, submitted live and addressed in the session
*   A curated roadmap for planning and implementing your AI governance program, built around where your organization stands today

## Details

Volunteer to distribute food with Park Circle Cares. SHL will be supporting [Park Circle Cares](https://parkcirclecares.org/)’ monthly food distribution.

Park Circle Cares is a non-faith based, non-profit organization created in 2016 to assist people in the lowcountry who struggle with food insecurity. Park Circle Cares is a member agency with the Lowcountry Food Bank, and distributes 120-150 thousand pounds of food each year. What makes them unique among the many organizations working on the widespread problem of food insecurity in our community is that they only distribute healthy and nutritious foods, 75% of which is produce. Healthy dry goods and proteins make up the remainder.

Park Circle Cares is operated by an all-volunteer working board, and an enthusiastic group of volunteers who set up a farmers’ market style distribution at North Charleston High School on the third Saturday of each month.

## Details

#### **6:00 - 7:00 pm (EST), every 1st and 3rd Thursday at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd, The Mezzanine Suite 228 in Mt. Pleasant.**

#### When bliss connections & experiences nourish your soul, please consider making a donation at[ [givetobliss.com](http://givetobliss.com/)](http://givetobliss.com). Thank-you for your continued friendship & support.

#### After a brief round of introductions, we will begin each class with a fun warm-up exercise to get our creative juices flowing.

#### Next, we will explore utilizing a fresh writing prompt for each class to delve a bit deeper during a 20-minute timed stream of consciousness writing exercise designed to quiet the inner critic.

#### Then we will have the opportunity to share what we have put on paper in its pure unedited form.

#### All levels are welcomed and encouraged to enter our circle. Sharing your work is optional and helps us discover more about you.

#### We may offer further growth opportunities to share your poems through open poetry reading events at bliss and other local venues.

#### **Facilitator: Tish Voit, [[tish@blissspiritualco-op.org](mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org)]([mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org](http://mailto:tish@blissspiritualco-op.org/))**

#### From early childhood I have experienced an intimate connection with spirit. This ever loving, encouraging and persistent guide from within has directed me to become a dedicated leader for causes that help others by building community. I am a playful and intuitive visionary, artist, singer, author, cook, and friend. My favorite place to be is home which I co-create wherever I am.

#### I write to explore my soul self, which is eternal, expansive, and uniquely creative. I enjoy sharing my poems and hearing what others create. To be known is a blessing. Please join us for this inward journey whenever you feel called.

title: ONSITE Beginner Belly Dancing w/ Karen Inella, Mon, Oct 19, 2026, 6:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: **6:00 – 7:00 pm (EST), on the 1st & 3rd Monday at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd in Mt. Pleasant, in the Mat Class Mezzanine.** Explore exotic, sacred Belly dance at bliss, embrace the beauty of your unique shape, have fun, and meet other
content:
**6:00 – 7:00 pm (EST), on the 1st & 3rd Monday at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd in Mt. Pleasant, in the Mat Class Mezzanine.**

Explore exotic, sacred Belly dance at bliss, embrace the beauty of your unique shape, have fun, and meet other adventurous Participants who aren’t afraid to let it roll. Wear comfy clothes. We have plenty of hip shawls to share.

The first five minutes is generally a stretch and warm up of the muscles. Then we explore the way that the different parts of the body express itself with movement… the head, chest, arms, midsection, stomach, hips and of course the legs. Then we will combine these movements with mini combinations and practice simple choreography that everyone can do using authentic music from Egypt, Turkey and other middle eastern countries.

Many styles of Middle Eastern dance will be highlighted including Egyptian, Turkish, Folkloric and Moroccan. We will also introduce many props used in Middle Eastern dance including: the veil, zil, sword, cane and silk fans. This class is facilitated by a seasoned dancer and performer who lives to share her art.

**Facilitator: Karen Inella, [shaktiselenebd@icloud.com**](http://shaktiselenebd@icloud.com**/)

Shakti Selene Shakti started belly dancing at the local YMCA in the South side of Chicago at the age of 16. Her teacher was Jasmine who was a muse of Eddie Kocheck. When she turned 18, she studied Egyptian Cabaret. Performances were made in the Chicago Art Institute where she attended college. She performed at private parties in Chicago Phoenix and Denver. She taught her skills wherever she danced. Her textile business led her to Turkey. Shakti fell in love with Istanbul. She eventually had a house and a dance studio close to the Blue Mosque. Her contacts led to many teaching opportunities, performances and development of a belly dance certification program from Istanbul Dreams. Through them she danced at corporate events, restaurants and taught different styles of belly dance.

Performances: Orient house Istanbul, Hilton Nile Cairo Egypt, Nile. Cruise ship On the Nile, Riads in Morocco, Singapore, taught a Tribal fusion seminar with Hafla, Samras Middle Eastern Dance event, Aegean Odessey Cruise Ship in the Greek islands, Eilot Israel evening local entertainment, Camel contracts, Cafe Paradiso, Taste of India

Dance companies: Ancient Echoes Belly Dance, Charleston Hula dancers, Allegro dance company, Charleston Black Sea dancers, Founding member of Palmetto Oasis

Teaching: Habibi Dance studio, Creative Spark, bliss Spiritual Co-op, Summerville YMCA

Productions: Moon over Morocco 13 years
 Styles of dance: Turkish Cabaret, Roman Havarsi Skirt, American Tribal, Fusion styles, Roman Havarsi, Bollywood, Khaligi, Saidi

Proficient in: Veil, Zil, Tambourine, Egyptian Wings, Silk and Feather Fans, Cane and Sticks.

Added interests: Celebrity chef specializing in Vegan Indian Food,
 Tarot card reader.

MANIFEST ABUNDANCE with the Integration of Reiki and Sacred Lifeforce Energy which will be transferred and shared with all in the circle throughout the entirety of the experience. First, participants will be led to set intentions to worked on. Then sound will be conducted for a deep embodiment of divine vibrations over each participant's body. Feel freedom as you sink deep into relaxation and into the present moment with ocean waves sounds from energies with the wave drum, nostalgic earth energies with Native American flute and Celtic Drone flute, the didgeridoo, primal drumbeats with Shamanic medicine drums and chimes for a much-needed upgrade and restoration.

Reiki is an ancient sacred technique used to integrate universal lifeforce energy into all aspects of our lives. Reiki promotes energies and feelings such as relaxation, stress relief, restoration, balancing, abundance, contentment, euphoria, happiness, and universal love. The list of benefits is infinite. Reiki energy is conducted through the palms of the hands (no hands if preferred), to the Participant to alleviate emotional, mental, physical, and spiritual discomfort and replaced with infinite love, abundance, and wellness. Reiki integration may be personalized, as time permits, for each participant. You will feel uplifted, free, and really awesome when you leave!!

**Facilitator: Chris Wampler, 843 830 7047, [[irlhaggard@gmail.com](mailto:irlhaggard@gmail.com)]([mailto:irlhaggard@gmail.com](http://mailto:irlhaggard@gmail.com/))**

**Leave refreshed and remembering the peace, wisdom, and wholeness that have always lived within you...**
 If you’ve found your way here, welcome.
 Life has a way of asking us to carry more than we were ever meant to hold. Stress, loss, uncertainty, and the pace of everyday living can leave us feeling disconnected—from ourselves, from our bodies, and from the quiet wisdom within.
 This is a space to come back home to yourself.
 A space to breathe deeply…
 to soften…
 to rest…
 and to remember the peace and wholeness that have always lived within you.
 Through immersive sound journeys, Reiki, breath, and intuitive presence, I gently support the body in entering deep states of relaxation, where restoration, emotional release, clarity, and inner connection can naturally unfold.
 Every experience is unique.
 I work with Native American flutes, medicine drums, wave drum, didgeridoo, Celtic drone flute, chimes, voice, and silence itself—woven into soundscapes designed to invite the nervous system to settle and the heart to open.
 I do not believe healing is something I give you.

I believe your body already carries an innate intelligence and profound capacity to heal.

My role is to create a compassionate, grounded space where that natural process can unfold safely and without effort.
 People often share that they leave feeling lighter, calmer, more grounded, and more like themselves again. Some experience renewed clarity or purpose. Others are surprised by how deeply they were able to relax, release, and reconnect with their inner world.
 Whether you are seeking rest, emotional renewal, clarity, or simply a place where nothing is required of you—you are welcome exactly as you are.
 Come as you are.
 Leave remembering who you have always been.
 It would be an honor to share this journey and experience with you.
 With love,
 Rainbow Bridge

title: Chinese V American Views On WAR With Taiwan | Armstrong Economics
summary: [![Image 1: China v Taiwan 3](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg) The Center for Strategic and Intern
content:
[![Image 1: China v Taiwan 3](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/China-v-Taiwan-3.jpg)

The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some [**84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification**](https://chinapower.csis.org/survey-experts-china-approach-to-taiwan/ "84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification") but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.

This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.

The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.

[![Image 2: TaiwanMagnified](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/TaiwanMagnified.jpg)

Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.

Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.

A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.

A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA [**blockade**](https://chinapower.csis.org/data/survey-results-chinas-approach-to-taiwan/ "blockade"), while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.

[![Image 3: Taiwan ECM 2](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg?w=300)](https://www.armstrongeconomics.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Taiwan-ECM-2.jpg)

This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.

Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.

What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.

This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.

If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

# 台湾民团和跨党派立委促行政院送出社会救助法修正草案 卫福部说继续沟通

专注阅读 宽屏☾

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月15日 17:08

台湾劳工阵线、社会救助法修法联盟等民间团体10月14日和跨党派立委开记者会，赶在10月17日“世界消除贫穷日”以前，呼吁行政院尽快送出《社会救助法》修正草案的行政院版本，让立法院实质审查。民间版修正草案1281天前就送进立法院，行政院也多次宣示把这部法列为优先法案，院版却一拖再拖。

受影响的是收入低、却因为资格门槛拿不到救助的人：台湾劳工阵线说，过时的《社会救助法》用虚拟收入的算法和僵硬的门槛，让弱势者不符合资格、拿不到救助。劳阵还引述主计总处的数据说，台湾有126万名低薪劳工，年薪低于39万元新台币；主计总处国势普查处副处长谭文玲9月说明，这是2024年本国籍全时工作者里全年总薪资低于39万元的人数，约占16.8%。台北市康复之友协会的林建宇说，低收入户资格连着身障、医疗、居住等支持，工作多赚的薪水如果抵不过失去的福利，努力工作的人全家反而更穷，这是制度失灵。

民进党立委林月琴说，上一个会期担任社福及卫环委员会召委时，曾为这部法多次深夜打电话给行政院长卓荣泰和副院长、秘书长等人，催促送出草案，但没有结果。林月琴说，草案只有进了立法院，民间、地方政府、行政部门和各党立委才能把资格认定、地方财政和服务量能摊开讨论。

卫福部社工司司长杨雅岚说，会继续朝扩大照顾弱势、促进就业自立和协助分阶段脱贫的方向推动修法；对外界关心的所得设算、家户列计、街友保障等问题，会按简政便民、公平客观和财政可负担的原则继续沟通。

## 茉莉花观察

这一节是茉莉花的看法，依据是上文的事实。

我们的分析 眼下卡住的一环是行政院版还没有送出：民间版三年多前就送进立法院，民进党立委范云说立委都已经准备好了；卫福部这次的回应讲了修法方向和原则，没有说院版什么时候送出。

不同看法 卫福部强调修法要守住财政可负担的原则。我们同意放宽门槛要多花钱；但院版不送进立法院，政府的具体条文和经费方案就进不了立法院的正式审议。

前瞻 行政院年底以前会不会送出院版。我们判断，到2026年12月31日（含当天），行政院不会把《社会救助法》修正草案的院版送进立法院。行政院多次宣示把这部法列为优先法案，院版仍一拖再拖，卫福部这次也没有给出时间。院版没有送出，现行规定就照旧：低收入户多赚的薪水如果抵不过失去的身障、医疗和居住支持，努力工作

## 第十八章 毛澤東陰施借刀計 彭德懷派兵斬袁王

話說朱德、毛澤東會師井岡山後，彼此產生諸多矛盾。由於周恩來的介入，毛澤東重新當選為第四軍前委書記，兩人爭執暫時平息。但中共本是個以鬥爭立黨的組織，它不會停止鬥爭的。

前文講到，因中共中央關於土匪的極端政策，毛澤東提議讓袁文才任第四軍副參謀長，跟隨紅四軍南下，暫時沒有對袁文才採取「極端手段」。

有一天，袁文才來到前委祕書長劉輝霄處。見門敞開著，沒通報就進去了。他四處觀看，突然桌子上一份文件，一行醒目的標題──「與土匪的關係」吸引了他。他屏住呼吸，飛快地讀了下去。這一讀不要緊，袁倒吸一口涼氣，頓覺寒徹肌骨，彷彿掉進了冰窖，一屁股跌坐在地上。聽到響聲的劉輝霄急忙出來，看到袁文才的表情，即刻明白了。

不知此刻袁文才是啥心情：為了毛澤東，為了共產黨，他把什麼都豁出去了，到頭來還是不被信任。其實袁文才沒有真正認清共產黨是什麼東西，不知道共產革命是多麼殘酷：像他這樣的土匪，是中共認定的階級異己分子，不管你曾經為其做過什麼，中共遲早要翻臉，要算賬的。

袁、劉默坐一陣，袁文才怏怏告退。此後，那份文件像噩夢一樣在他腦海中揮之不去。終於有一天，他以「到哪裡革命都一樣」為由，決心再回到自己的部隊去，遂將一張「告假條」放在軍部，拉上劉輝霄、謝桂標等人，趁著黑夜悄悄離開部隊，趕往井岡山。

聞聽袁文才不告而別，毛澤東迅即召開前委會，並嚴肅道：「此例不可開。這是臨陣逃跑、目無軍法的表現，這也表明像袁文才這樣的土匪最終還是靠不住的，必須嚴肅處理。」

朱德緩緩說道：「袁文才所犯錯誤是嚴重的。但考慮到他身後還有隊伍，處理方式要得當，防止出現不可控的狀況。」

毛澤東也陷入沉思。從他內心來講，是支持「六大」決議的：共產黨、紅軍確實需要純潔自己的隊伍，這也是毛澤東從事農運工作時的一貫主張。他從內心也看不起土匪出身的袁、王。尤其是袁文才，身上確實有一些「匪氣」。從純潔黨的隊伍出發，應除掉為宜。

離開井岡山之前，毛澤東專門給彭德懷安排：「袁文才這個人很狡猾，很有心計，你要多注意他的舉動。雖然前委沒有立即執行中央決議，但要見機行事，關鍵時刻要果斷。」實際是給了彭德懷尚方寶劍。毛還囑咐：「井岡山土籍、客籍矛盾極深，但土籍代表更多、更貧苦的農民，關鍵時刻還是更放心一些。」

毛澤東提出的井岡山土籍、客籍之事，是指井岡山土籍人與客籍人的矛盾之爭。土籍是指井岡山原居民，人數眾多，但經濟條件較差，中共黨員也比較多。而客籍人數相對較少，但經濟條件較好，且有不少富商，掌握一定地方權力。故黨內有種說法：「土籍的黨，客籍的槍」。客家、土家矛盾淵源極深，為了化解他們之間的矛盾，毛澤東曾嚴厲批評龍超清、袁文才：「共產黨不分國界省界，不分籍貫地界，群眾不懂，難道你們也不懂？虧你們都是黨的負責幹部！……消除土、客籍矛盾，應當首先從黨內開始，道理已經說得夠明白了。哪個以後還要搞土、客籍爭端，組織上對他不客氣！」

但從中共的觀念看，土籍是更可靠的革命力量，而客籍則是可以聯合的力量，關鍵時候就可以過河拆橋、卸磨殺驢，以免給中共革命造成危害。

經過深思熟慮之後，毛澤東提議：袁文才逃跑之事交給湘贛特委處理。

這是個令人費解的安排。毛澤東十分清楚：湘贛特委由土家族把持，和袁文才之間的矛盾很深。連續三屆特委書記楊開明、鄧乾元、朱昌偕都跟袁勢同水火：楊開明因毛、賀結婚之事遷怒於袁文才；鄧乾元臨走之時，向中央寫信匯報：「袁、王現在對我們處處懷疑，有另找出路脫離我們的徵兆。王在袁的影響下，亦與我們的關係日益惡化」；而朱昌偕亦對袁文才成見極深：「要是不能肅清土匪，則土匪必將與我們為敵，國民黨若因其有益而利導之，以夾攻我們，則我們危矣」。唯特委成員宛希先與袁文才走得比較近，打得火熱。

在宛希先調停下，湘贛特委只給予袁文才黨內警告處分，這可讓朱昌偕、永新縣委書記劉真、寧岡縣委書記王懷懷恨在心，竟對宛希先起了殺心。

宛希先曾處理過一起投敵案。因下屬處理不當，竟把劉真結婚僅三個月的妻子龍家衡處決。劉真把這「殺妻之仇」算在宛希先身上，一直氣憤難平，更是必欲除之而後快。

1930年2月，宛希先接到湘贛特委的緊急通知，讓他速回永新參加重要的軍事行動。誰料去永新的路上，宛遇到了政府軍的包圍。在衝出包圍到達永新後，已耽誤了軍事行動計劃。朱昌偕不問青紅皂白，竟以「貽誤戰機」之名把宛希先處決。這共產黨真是沒人性：對自己革命的同志竟然是說殺就殺。當然，也只有共產黨的組織才會這樣幹。不是說了嗎！中共的內部鬥爭有時就是你死我活的。

宛希先一死，雙方更加對立。

恰逢此時，又發生一件事情，使湘贛特委有了置袁、王於死地的藉口。

一日，袁文才、王佐商議：茶陵、酃縣、寧岡三縣聯防團團總羅克紹有個兵工廠，何不把他抓來，把兵工廠收為己用。說幹就幹，結果就把羅抓到山上，跟他談兵工廠之事。當然，談判自然是先禮後兵，那就好吃好喝的伺候著羅克紹。哪知此事被朱昌偕知道，認定袁文才、王佐與羅克紹私通。立即聯繫劉真、龍超清等人，商定對付袁文才之計。

無巧不成書，此時中共中央特派員彭清泉來到井岡山。背景是中央收到了兩任湘贛特委書記楊開明、鄧乾元事關袁、王的報告。要知道，中央本來就戴著「有色眼鏡」看待袁文才、王佐。對於毛澤東遲遲沒有按照中央政策處理袁、王，中央也很不滿。彭清泉正是帶著解決袁文才、王佐的任務來到井岡山。這與邊界特委朱、龍的想法不謀而合。

可是，一個非常現實的問題卻令他們深感頭痛。袁、王兩部合編的紅四軍三十二團，擁有一千多兵員，七百多枝槍，還有一座兵工廠。加之該部官兵大多獵戶出身，對井岡山地形特別熟悉，戰鬥經驗豐富，其戰鬥力絕不在留守的紅五軍之下。

古語道：「害人之心不可有，防人之心不可無。」而在中共黨內，處處都是害人之輩。若沒有「防人之心」，稍有不慎，就可能落入別人的圈套。

一日，袁文才突然收到毛澤東來信。來信稱：紅四軍前委決定，邊界六縣的赤衛隊合編為紅六軍第三縱隊，任命袁文才為司令，王佐副之，定於2月22日在永新縣城合編，隨後配合紅五軍共同攻打吉安。

看到毛的來信，袁、王自是喜不自勝：老毛還真夠意思，關鍵時刻還想著我們。當即決定，立即趕往永新任職。

與此同時，紅五軍軍長彭德懷在睡夢中被驚醒，說是地方黨委負責人深夜求見。彭急忙迎出內室。還未開口，朱昌偕便趕緊走上前，急急拉住他的手，焦急地說：「彭軍長，出大事了。袁文才、王佐要叛變。」彭德懷驀地一驚，忙扶來人坐定，安慰道：「不要急，慢慢講。」

朱昌偕說：「袁文才、王佐勾結羅克紹叛變了革命。他們在特委聯席會議上，強迫會議改編地方武裝，統歸他們指揮。王佐講話時手拿駁殼槍，囂張得很。看樣子如果不通過他們提出的要求，出席會議的同志有被一網打盡的危險。」話說到此，朱昌偕請求道：「情況已到萬分危急的地步，我們特委務請紅五軍即刻出動，挽救這場危機。」

「情況有這麼嚴重？」彭德懷有些將信將疑：「去年五六月間，王佐率領特務營和五軍共同行動打酃縣、桂東、城口、南雄等地表現還不壞，怎麼變化得這麼快呢？」

朱昌偕忙解釋道：「這完全是袁文才挑撥起來的。他在紅四軍政治部看了六大決議案關於土匪那一段原話，回到井岡山後對王佐說，我們怎樣忠心，也不會被信任。」

鑒於事態如此嚴重緊急，又見朱昌偕等人這般焦急，彭德懷未作深層次的思考。同時，彭也想起毛澤東離開井岡山時的再三囑咐：對袁文才要有足夠的防範，必要時要堅決出手。想到此，彭德懷立即安排張純清率紅五軍第四縱隊隨朱昌偕趕往永新縣城，並聽從朱昌偕指揮。

1930年2月22日下午，袁文才、王佐率紅四軍三十二團七百餘人槍，進駐永新縣城禾川鎮。特委組織了上千民眾，在城東浮橋頭舉行歡迎儀式，紛紛祝賀「袁、王二人榮升新職」。一時間，袁、王二人與特委間出現了罕有的融洽。

當晚，酒足飯飽後，袁文才被安排到了永新縣城尹家巷22號。那是一所乾淨寬敞的宅院。王佐則住進了尹家祠堂，其餘官兵散居在附近早被騰空出來的店鋪與百姓家。

王佐回到住地，感到周圍環境有些不對頭，立刻拉上袁文才就要回去，並不停地說：「快離開這個是非之地，切莫老虎上了狗的當。」但袁文才阻止了王佐，認為王佐多心了。

23日午夜，特委向五縣赤衛隊傳達了軍事部署：「袁、王二人勾結茶陵團總羅克紹已經叛變革命，明日借成立大會之際，務必除掉二位叛徒。各部牢記口令，左臂纏繞白毛巾，一定完成鋤奸任務。」24日凌晨5時左右，朱昌偕帶著十餘名荷槍實彈的赤衛隊員衝進了袁文才住所。他徑直趕往袁文才門口，敲門喊道：「袁司令，老袁，我是朱昌偕，有事找你。」與袁文才同住一室的李筱甫遲疑了一下，還是輕輕拉開了門。袁文才剛從睡夢中睜開眼，朱昌偕抬手就是一槍，子彈正中袁文才眉心。隨即，另外幾支槍同時響起，李筱甫與袁文才倒在了血泊中。

尹家巷22號的槍聲驟然響過後，一直心懷警覺並在住處內打好了地洞的王佐，彷彿天人感應一般從床上一躍而起。嘴上連連叫道：「不好，出事了。」然後，帶上刁輝林等人沿著地洞鑽出了祠堂，跨上幾匹未卸鞍的戰馬，飛馳而去。逃跑的路上，王佐等人遭到紅五軍第四縱隊伏擊，當場斃命。

與此同時，城中的三十二團除部分人逃脫之外，大部被繳械控制起來。特委清點現場，找到了袁文才、李筱甫、王佐等人的十七具屍體。

這樣，袁文才、王佐這兩個結拜兄弟，做到了「不求同年同月同日生，但求同年同月同日死」，也算不枉兄弟一場。

尤其讓人不齒的是：袁文才妻子謝梅香幾天後給袁文才收屍，那屍首已腐爛。要知道，中國人最忌諱的就是暴屍，就算後來的日本人在戰場上遇到中國死亡的士兵，有時都要掩埋的。而那些中共黨徒竟然任憑袁文才暴屍荒郊，真是邪惡他娘給邪惡開門——邪惡到家了！有這麼大的仇恨嗎？

3月初，袁文才的部下謝角銘、謝益謀、陳次謀、曾李生牽頭，聯名客籍黨員幹部劉克猶、朱開卷等十六人，寫信給彭德懷並轉贛西南特委和紅四軍軍委，希望上級能主持公道。但發出的信猶如石沉大海，上級沒有任何回信。不僅如此，特委繼續搜捕袁文才、王佐的同謀者。部分袁、王下屬逃進深山，特委令紅六軍第三縱隊派出部隊上山「搜索圍剿」。

3月下旬，得不到中共反饋的謝角銘等聯絡王佐部下王雲隆，給湘贛兩省國民政府「電告反赤」。兩省政府分別於第三天派出「撫慰大員」來到寧岡龍市，策劃袁王舊部的「反共大業」。

寧岡、遂川兩縣的國民黨政府也派人來井岡山，給農民免費送來了糧食、食鹽等物資，其中還有耕牛，尤其對袁、王舊部排長以上的家庭給予更為優厚的撫慰。當然，對仍然留在紅軍隊伍中的成員，其家庭也受到政府軍的懲治。

4月上旬，寧（岡）遂（川）邊防保衛團在茅坪成立，謝角銘為團總，王雲隆為團副。保衛團以袁、王舊部為主，又招收了兩百多名團丁，加上國民黨吉安駐軍撥來的一批槍彈，使保衛團擴充到七百多人槍。之後，中共軍隊幾次試圖奪回井岡山，但井岡山的一切都變了：老百姓不再給他們提供情報了，不再給他們提供糧食了，甚至出現對紅軍投石塊、打黑槍的情況。失去了老百姓的紅軍，再也沒能收回井岡山。

按照現在中共的說法，袁文才收到的毛澤東來信是偽造的。如此大的事，朱昌偕敢偽造嗎？跟毛澤東朝夕相處的袁文才看不出毛的筆跡嗎？為什麼事後沒有對此進行處理？中央特派員彭清泉來到井岡山的任務，就是對袁文才採取非常手段，難道毛澤東不知道？彭德懷動用軍隊捕殺袁文才，會不跟毛澤東匯報？謝角銘等人的上訪信為什麼沒有回應？

其實，毛澤東自始至終參與了對袁文才、王佐的謀殺。就在開始行動之前，彭清泉親自派人去見毛澤東專門匯報，並得到了老毛寄給袁文才的親筆信。據說，毛澤東曾對袁文才被殺事件痛心疾首，曾後悔地說道：「殺錯了，殺錯了！」典型的「貓哭耗子假慈悲」。既然說殺錯了，那就說明此前一直認為「殺得對」。這跟「還我盧德銘」是一樣的醜惡嘴臉。有的看官說了，毛澤東有那麼惡毒嗎？看看他以後的作為就知道了，這點事對他來說只不過是初試牛刀，小事一樁！

中共內部的相互殘殺，會愈演愈烈。

正是
中共本是一邪黨 過河拆橋自應當
老毛遙指井岡山 自有老彭斬袁王

如是曰：在中共的文獻中，都說是王明的左傾主義害了袁文才。其實，中共六大決定對土匪採取「極端手段」，正是中共對待階級異己分子所應該採取的措施，共產黨面對土匪時就是要採取這樣的革命手段。這和毛澤東在《中國社會各階級的分析》、《湖南農民運動考察報告》中所寫論調完全是一致的。所以袁文才、王佐之死也是必然的。

title: Chinese startup DexForce uses virtual training to cut humanoid robot costs
zh_title: 中国初创公司 DexForce 使用虚拟训练来降低人形机器人成本
summary: 人工智能 中国初创公司 DexForce 使用模拟或合成数据训练人形机器人，以降低成本并提高效率。这家总部位于深圳的公司表示，这种方法可以加速“物理通用人工智能”的进展，并得到了大型企业集团和国家基金的支持。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 16:19 HKT · 2 分钟阅读中国初创公司DexForce 正在使用模拟训练来教学
content:
人工智能
中国初创公司 DexForce 使用模拟或合成数据来训练人形机器人，以降低成本并提高效率。这家总部位于深圳的公司表示，这种方法可以加速“物理通用人工智能”的进展，并得到了大型企业集团和国家基金的支持。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 16:19 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

中国初创公司 DexForce 正在使用模拟训练来教人形机器人执行广泛的现实世界任务，该公司表示，这种方法比从人类工人那里收集数据更快、更便宜。这家总部位于深圳的公司展示了一个屏幕，显示一个虚拟机器人反复将物体放在桌子上，同时其手臂的角度、桌子的颜色和物体本身都发生了变化。
首席执行官贾奎告诉路透社，依靠虚拟环境中生成的合成数据可以更快地推动机器人能力的突破，类似于 ChatGPT 在 2022 年发布后引发的突破，帮助推动生成式人工智能进入主流。 “试图纯粹通过现实世界的数据收集来实现‘物理通用人工智能’将需要 10 万亿个样本……对无限的人类任务进行手动（数据）收集从根本上来说是低效的，”他说，指的是类人机器人可以在不熟悉的环境中按照命令完成新任务的里程碑。

中国已经开发出能够在跑步和跳跃方面超越人类的类人机器人，但更严峻的商业考验在于它们是否能够在工厂、办公室和家庭中可靠地执行有用的工作。许多中国机器人制造商正试图通过从现实世界中重复执行任务的人类工人那里收集大量数据来应对这一挑战。然而，DexForce 开发的人工智能软件旨在模拟物理环境和模型，旨在预测物体如何移动和交互。它创建工作场所或任务的数字版本，在模拟中训练机器人，然后将学习成果转移到物理机器上。
该公司表示，这个过程比从人类训练师那里收集数据更快、更便宜，人类训练师可能需要重复一个动作 100 多次才能生成精确的示例。目前，全国范围内耗巨资建设了数十个仿人机器人数据培训中心，而且往往严重依赖政府补贴。大多数中国机器人制造商都结合使用模拟数据和真实数据，许多人表示获取高质量训练数据仍然是一个关键瓶颈。

贾跃亭是香港中文大学（深圳）的机器学习教授，于 2021 年创立了 DexForce。这家约有 500 名员工的初创公司得到了联想旗下投资部门联想创投、蓝思科技以及多家国有基金的支持。它在最近的 B 轮融资中筹集了 10 亿元人民币（1.47 亿美元），估值超过 100 亿元人民币。彭博社报道称，该公司正在考虑在香港首次公开募股，但贾拒绝发表评论。

该公司的软件被丰田、三星、松下、富士康、海尔和海信等国内外制造商用于工业环境，其仿人机器人则在全国超过 15 个城市的商场和旅游景点制作咖啡并为顾客提供服务。
