title: Former US official praises Taiwan’s drills transformation
summary: ## ENGAGING PARTNERS: Dennis Blair called for greater international cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for partners to maintain maritime presence Dennis Blair, former US director of national intelligence and a retired US
content:
## ENGAGING PARTNERS: Dennis Blair called for greater international cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for partners to maintain maritime presence

Dennis Blair, former US director of national intelligence and a retired US Navy admiral, yesterday praised Taiwan’s decision to transform its large-scale annual military exercises into a whole-of-society defense effort in the past few years.

Speaking virtually at a security conference in Taipei, Blair said that Taiwan’s decision to transform the Han Kuang exercises from “a purely military one” into what he described as a “nation-defensive exercise” was a great decision.

By doing so, Taiwan would be “making sure that all of the capabilities of Taiwan are mobilized and brought to bear,” said Blair, a former commander in chief of the US Pacific Command before retiring in 2002.

## Former US director of national intelligence and retired US Navy admiral Dennis Blair, on the screen, speaks virtually at the International Conference on Sea Lane Security held by the Ocean Affairs Council in Taipei yesterday.

Photo: Wang Kuan-jen, Taipei Times

He said that Taiwan’s all-out effort to demonstrate its determination to defend itself would help convince like-minded countries and regional partners to come to its aid in an emergency.

“And of course, helping Taiwan is very much in the interests of all seafaring nations,” he said.

“After all, if Taiwan can be bullied into giving up parts of its sovereignty, then Japan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Korea, all of the countries of the world have to wonder, the region has to wonder about whether they are next,” he added.

The annual Han Kuang exercises have served as Taiwan’s primary war games since 1984, testing the country’s combat readiness in the event of a possible Chinese invasion.

Originally involving only military personnel from all branches of the armed forces, the exercises have over the past few years been expanded to incorporate whole-of-society defense resilience drills to promote active civil-military operations.

Blair also suggested in his address that Taipei should continue its efforts to monitor maritime activities and enforce laws in waters under its jurisdiction, as China continues to send civilian and government vessels into Taiwan’s waters.

Beyond these monitoring and enforcement efforts, he said Taiwan needs an active campaign of diplomacy and public outreach, similar to what the Philippines has undertaken in its disputes and confrontations with Beijing in the South China Sea.

“The objective is to convey the message that Chinese claims and operations are both illegal and inept. In order to win and retain world attention, Taiwanese public diplomacy needs to be inventive and fresh. Taiwan cannot allow China to establish a new normal in the international public perception,” he said.

Blair made the remarks remotely during the International Conference on Sea Lane Security, organized by the Ocean Affairs Council.

At the opening of the one-day conference, National Security Council Deputy Secretary-General Lii Wen (李問) thanked like-minded partners for jointly voicing opposition to China’s destabilizing actions in the East China Sea, the Taiwan Strait and the South China Sea.

He called for greater international and regional cooperation to enhance early-warning capabilities and for international partners to maintain their maritime presence through measures such as freedom of navigation operations and regional cooperation to combat maritime crime.

title: White House defends new press secretary Katie Zacharia amid questions about her legal credentials
zh_title: 白宫为新任新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚辩护，因为她的法律资格受到质疑

content:
3小时前

萨琳·哈贝希安

](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/7c7f/live/f7333c90-c838-11f1-b2e8-93da8301514e.jpg.webp)盖蒂图片社

白宫正在为其新任新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚辩护，因为她面临着对其法律资历的审查。

唐纳德·特朗普总统上周宣布任命扎卡里亚为律师时，她将自己描述为律师。

但周二，当一名记者问她在哪个州通过了成为美国律师所需的律师考试时，她站在总统身边说：“当我搬到中国时。”

她似乎没有在她居住过的任何州的律师协会注册。白宫通讯主管史蒂文·张 (Steven Cheung) 表示，扎卡里亚“具有独特的资格和聪明才智，可以帮助向美国人民通报情况”。

在回答有关她的资质的问题时，扎卡里亚在本周的一份声明中表示：“我从事国际交易法工作，拥有所有适当的资质。”

周三，监督组织“问责运动”向加州律师协会提出投诉。

他们正在寻求调查扎卡里亚是否“一再向公众声称自己有权在没有执照的情况下执业，加州法律将这种行为视为犯罪”。

加州佩珀代因大学证实，这位 42 岁的政治战略家 2011 年毕业于该大学法学院。
法律学位并不是在美国执业的许可证。

这位新任白宫新闻秘书周三告诉《纽约时报》，当她第一次开始出现在有线电视新闻中时，她曾问佩珀代因应该如何表明自己的身份。

她说，大学校长建议她可以称自己为律师，但不能称自己为律师。

据《华尔街日报》报道，扎卡里亚从法学院毕业后在加州参加了律师资格考试，但没有通过。加州的律师考试被广泛认为是美国最难通过的律师考试之一。

一位直接了解此事的人士告诉媒体，扎卡里亚参加考试的时间大约是在她计划婚礼并准备与未婚夫搬到中国的同时。

由于丈夫在一家美国私募股权公司工作，她搬到了北京。扎卡里亚表示，她在那里研究“国际交易法”。

她的 LinkedIn 个人资料显示，她于 2011-13 年间在北京中伦律师事务所担任律师。

在中国，只有中国公民才有资格获得律师执业资格。外籍雇员可以在律师事务所担任其他职务。

去年2月，扎卡里亚在保守派广播节目《克莱·特拉维斯和巴克·塞克斯顿秀》中表示，她在中国期间曾担任国际金融公司（IFC）和世界银行的外部顾问。

BBC 已联系世界银行和国际金融公司征求意见。
据了解，世界银行集团有时会聘请外部律师事务所，由这些律师事务所决定将哪些律师分配到任何工作的哪些部分。

根据扎卡里亚的 LinkedIn 个人资料，她还担任 Fix California 的总法律顾问，这是一个由特朗普盟友里克·格雷内尔 (Ric Grenell) 创办的保守派非营利组织。

【原文 English Original】
3 hours ago

Sareen Habeshian

](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/7c7f/live/f7333c90-c838-11f1-b2e8-93da8301514e.jpg.webp)Getty Images

The White House is defending its new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, as she faces scrutiny over her legal credentials.

President Donald Trump described Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week and she has referred to herself as a lawyer.

But when she was asked on Tuesday by a reporter in which state she had passed the bar exam required to be an attorney in the US, she said standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China."

She does not appear to be registered to the bar in any state where she has lived. White House communications director Steven Cheung said Zacharia is "uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people".

Responding to questions about her credentials, Zacharia said in a statement this week: "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials."

On Wednesday, a watchdog group, Campaign for Accountability, filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association.

They are seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia "repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practise law without a licence to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime".

The 42-year-old political strategist graduated from law school at Pepperdine University in California in 2011, the university confirmed.

A law degree is not a licence to practise law in the US.

The new White House press secretary told the New York Times on Wednesday that when she first began appearing on cable news, she had asked Pepperdine how she should identify herself.

She said she was advised by the university president that she could call herself a lawyer, but not an attorney.

Zacharia took the bar exam in California after graduating from law school but did not pass, according to the Wall Street Journal. California's bar exam is widely regarded as one of the hardest in the US to pass.

A person with direct knowledge of the matter told the outlet that Zacharia took the exam around the same time that she was planning a wedding and preparing to move to China with her husband-to-be.

She moved to Beijing because of her husband's job at an American private equity firm. Zacharia has said she worked on "international transaction law" there.

Her LinkedIn profile states that she worked as an associate at Zhong Lun Law Firm in Beijing from 2011-13.

In China, only Chinese citizens are eligible to obtain a licence to practise law. Foreign employees may work at law firms in other roles.

In February last year, Zacharia said on conservative radio programme The Clay Travis and Buck Sexton Show that she had worked as outside counsel for the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the World Bank during her time in China.

The BBC has contacted the World Bank and IFC for comment.

It is understood the World Bank Group sometimes retains outside law firms, and that those firms decide which of their lawyers are assigned to which parts of any work.

Zacharia has also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally Ric Grenell, according to her LinkedIn profile.

title: Special Forces in China’s Nuclear and Missile Operations
zh_title: 中国核与导弹行动中的特种部队
source: 亚利桑那州立大学的《小战争杂志》
summary: 摘要 人们对特种部队在管理核行动中的作用知之甚少，尤其是在国外。文章探讨了中国人民解放军火箭军特种作战部队的组织结构和任务。研究中国核行动和导弹行动中的特种部队如何帮助情报专业人员和政策制定者更清楚地了解中国的导弹生存能力以及使其导弹部队面临风险的选择。简介：从苏联手提箱核装置到美国陆军特种部队“绿灯队”
content:
摘要 人们对特种部队在管理核行动中的作用知之甚少，尤其是在国外。文章探讨了中国人民解放军火箭军特种作战部队的组织结构和任务。研究中国核行动和导弹行动中的特种部队如何帮助情报专业人员和政策制定者更清楚地了解中国的导弹生存能力以及使其导弹部队面临风险的选择。简介 从苏联手提箱核装置到冷战期间美国陆军特种部队“绿灯小组”，特种作战在核战略中的作用有着悠久且未被充分认识的历史。研究美国对手如何计划在核行动中使用特种部队的文章就更少了。然而，研究中国人民解放军火箭军（PLARF）如何运用特种作战揭示了党的优先事项、中国的核生存方法以及了解中国弹头管理实践的窗口。最后一个见解尤其重要，因为它可以表明准备情况、警戒状态以及从中央军事委员会（中国共产党的最高军事指挥部）授权使用核到在运载工具上放置弹头的时间表。外界对 PLARF 特种部队知之甚少。以下大多数评估必然是暂时的。
然而，来自中国的足够多的媒体报道、期刊文章和社交媒体帖子让分析人士能够拼凑出一幅关于解放军特种部队如何将特种部队融入其核行动的图景（尽管并不完整）。与冷战期间对核渗透的担忧不同，解放军特种部队构成的威胁并不那么引人注目。尽管未来可能会发生变化，但解放军特种部队的主要任务是反渗透、保卫弹头和“蓝队”（解放军中的敌方部队通常被称为蓝队或蓝军）。 PLARF特种作战部队的组织和任务 PLARF特种部队的总体目标是对中国导弹旅的生存能力和作战能力进行压力测试，反击对手的渗透和破坏，以及保护弹头和导弹阵地。用解放军一名旅长的话说，解放军训练和维持特种作战部队的主要原因之一是纠正“防御行动中的某些缺陷”和“拥有足够可信的自卫能力来防止敌人的渗透”。中国军队喉舌《解放军报》的另一篇文章指出，“尖刀”部队的任务之一是导弹发射支援和反击敌方特种作战攻击。
更广泛地说，2012年《中国战略导弹部队百科全书》指出，火箭军的前身第二炮兵需要为精确制导攻击、特种部队突袭以及攻击后的修复和恢复做好准备。事实上，用于训练解放军军官的2004年《第二炮兵作战科学》中有几段专门介绍敌方特种作战的破坏威胁和防御方法他们。尽管 22 年来，解放军的作战理念、生存能力和技术取得了长足进步，但最近的演习仍然表明，重点是使用特种部队进行反渗透

【原文 English Original】
Abstract Little is known about the role special forces have in managing nuclear operations, especially in foreign countries. The article examines the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force’s special operations units, their organizational structure, and missions. Studying how special forces in China’s nuclear and missile operations helps intelligence professionals and policymakers develop a clearer picture of China’s missile survivability and options to hold at risk its missile forces. Introduction From Soviet suitcase nuclear devices to U.S. Army Special Forces “ Green Light teams ” during the Cold War, the role of special operations in nuclear strategy has a long and underappreciated history. Even fewer pieces have examined how U.S. adversaries plan to employ special forces in nuclear operations. However, studying how the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force (PLARF) employs special operations reveals Party priorities, China’s approach to nuclear survivability, and windows into China’s warhead management practices. The last insight is especially important, since it can indicate readiness, alert status, and timelines from when the Central Military Commission—the Chinese Communist Party’s supreme military command—authorizes nuclear use to the placement of warheads on delivery vehicles. Little is known about the PLARF’s special forces from the outside. Most of the following assessments are necessarily tentative. Yet, enough media reporting, journal articles, and social media posts from China exist for analysts to cobble together a picture–albeit incomplete–of how the PLARF integrates special forces in its nuclear operations. Unlike worries over nuclear infiltration during the Cold War, the threats posed by PLARF’s special forces are less dramatic. Although this may evolve in the future, PLARF special forces primarily focus on counter-infiltration, guarding warheads, and “blue-teaming” (an opposing force in the PLA is generally referred to as blue team or blue force). PLARF Special Operations Forces Organization and Missions PLARF special forces are generally oriented toward stress testing the survivability and operations of China’s missile brigades, countering infiltration and sabotage from adversaries, and protecting warheads and missile sites. In the words of one PLARF brigade commander, one of the main reasons for training and maintaining special operations forces (SOF) units in the PLARF is to rectify “certain shortcomings in defensive operations” and “have sufficient credible self-defense capabilities to prevent enemy infiltration.” Another article from the PLA Daily—the mouthpiece of the Chinese military— posits that one of the missions of the “Sharp Knife” unit is for missile launch support and countering enemy special operations attacks. More broadly, the 2012 China Strategic Missile Force Encyclopedia states that the Second Artillery Forces, the predecessor to the Rocket Force, need to be prepared for precision-guided attacks, special forces raids, and to conduct repairs and recover in the aftermath of an attack. Indeed, the 2004 Science of Second Artillery Campaigns, an operational manual used to train PLA officers, has several passages dedicated to threats of sabotage from enemy special operations and ways to defend against them. Although the PLA’s operational concepts, survivability, and technology have come a long way in 22 years, more recent exercises still suggest an emphasis on the use of special forces for counter-infiltration missions and the protection of launch sites and warheads. Within the PLARF, several special forces units are assigned to different bases and serve different missions. There are at least seven special operations units in some capacity within the PLARF with different yet overlapping missions. Each unit is normally subordinated to a corps-level base that corresponds with a particular geographic area within China, often hosting delivery vehicles or nuclear warheads. There is no unified special operations command in China, and different services and levels of command may have dedicated special forces units. Consequently, the PLARF’s special forces vary in size. Drawing upon Ma Xiu’s research from the China Aerospace Studies Institute and Chinese media reporting, the following table captures known PLARF SOF units, their key characteristics, and command structure. Table 1 : Known PLARF SOF Units PLARF Special Operations Forces Unit Name Chinese Name Key Characteristics Known Location Immediate Parent Unit Special Operations Security Training Team 特种警卫集训队 (Tèzhǒng jǐngwèi jíxùn duì) Approximately 200 personnel focused on anti-reconnaissance, anti-infiltration, and anti-raiding missions Base 61 Directly subordinate to Base 61 Sharp Knife Special Operations Team 利刃特战队 (Lìrèn tè zhànduì) 38-man unit referred to as “missile guardians” and potentially dedicated to counter-SOF and missile launch support One in Base 64; one in Base 67 Security Battalion (Base 67) Knife’s Edge Special Operations Team 刀锋特战队 (Dāofēng tè zhànduì) Base 67 headquarters site security Base 67 Security and Service Battalion Blue Team SOF Unit Unknown[BG3.1][AR3.2][BG3.3] Opposing force unit with a special operations capability focused on technical reconnaissance, electronic warfare, and sabotage to help the PLARF find weaknesses Base 69 Blue Team Unit in the 3rd Test and Training District Special Operations Squadron 特战中对 (Tè zhàn zhōng duì) Opposing force unit at the company level in a remote mountain environment with reconnaissance and surveillance, frequency jamming, SOF, and electronic countermeasure capabilities to help the PLARF find weaknesses Base 69 Blue Team Opposing Force Regiment in the 2nd Test and Training District Special Operations Reconnaissance Team 特种侦察队 (Tèzhǒng zhēnchá duì) Damage assessment and target reconnaissance Staff Department Operations Support Group Reconnaissance Regiment Base 67 is where the PLARF stockpiles its warheads. Within Base 67 is the “Knife’s Edge” Special Operations Team, a 38-man unit primarily focused on site security. The Knife’s Edge is part of the Security and Service Battalion, which itself is subordinated to Base 67 Operations Support Regiment. This team is responsible for physical security around Base 67’s headquarters. Established around 2004, the Sharp Knife Special Operations Team is subordinate to Base 67’s Security Battalion. It primarily focuses on protecting PLA Unit 96038, a unit responsible for warhead management and transportation of warhead stockpiles. Exercises in 2014 suggest that the Sharp Knife team contains snipers and has a role in escorting mobile missiles. Ma Xiu additionally notes that the Sharp Knife personnel are reportedly referred to as “missile guardians” within Base 64, consisting of intermediate-range and intercontinental ballistic missiles. Still, Ma Xiu points out that it’s unknown whether Sharp Knife teams are unique to specific units or if every single PLARF base possesses such a unit. The Sharp Knife team’s command level in Base 64 is also unclear. Located in Anhui province, Base 61 is a command unit that carries several missile brigades, consisting of short-range and medium-range ballistic missiles. Base 61 directly maintains a Special Operations Security Training Team, consisting of approximately 200 personnel for counter-reconnaissance, counter-infiltration, and counter-raiding missions. A 2024 social media post from China Youth Daily showcased approximately 100 trainees for this team, though it is unclear from this post alone how often this team takes in recruits or how many of these trainees become part of the Special Security Training Team. The post further notes that this team guards a “national treasure,” which is often a euphemism for warheads or important delivery vehicles. Within Beijing, the PLARF Headquarters comprises four major components: the staff, political work, logistics, and equipment departments. The PLARF Staff Department Operations Support Group has a reconnaissance regiment in charge of battlefield reconnaissance and intelligence support and a subordinate Special Operations Reconnaissance Team for target reconnaissance and damage assessment. The reconnaissance regiment is based in Beijing with two secondary garrisons in Qinghai and Fujian. The location of the Special Operations Reconnaissance Team is unknown. Stress Testing Missile Survivability The PLARF special operations community has an important role in red-blue exercises and stress testing missile survivability, especially during transit. These exercises pit missile brigades as the red side against a dedicated blue force. In fact, this emphasis on red-blue exercises comes from the top down. China’s 2013 defense white paper, for instance, directs the former Second Artillery Force to conduct red-blue exercises for reconnaissance and counter-reconnaissance, jamming and anti-jamming, and strengthening protection against nuclear, biological, and chemical threats. David C. Logan highlights that the PLARF established the creation of a Blue Army Teaching and Research Section, championed by Colonel Diao Guangming, to develop more difficult and complex training exercises. Within Base 69’s 3rd Test Training District is a PLARF blue force unit and a subordinate special operations unit. Little is known about its special operations capability, though the blue force unit does host PLARF units for exercises and training in plateau operations near the Gobi Desert region. Established in early 2018 as an experimental unit, Base 69’s 2nd Test and Training District also maintains a blue force regiment and a subordinate special operations squadron or company led by Zheng Yihang (some analysts refer to this unit as a squadron while other sources describe Zheng Yihang as a special operations company commander). A PLA Daily article traces the force from a 2004 tactical-confrontation team, through a Blue Force assembled from multiple units in 2012, to formal establishment in 2018, casting it as the missile force’s “first opponent.” From special operations raids to jamming, these exercises involve a variety of capabilities and are focused on preventing red team PLARF missile brigades from “arriving on time, launching on time, or launching accurately” to reveal potential weaknesses. The special operations element infiltrates and reconnoiters launch positions, command posts, and encampments, then raids launchers, transporter-erector-launchers on the move, convoys, and key personnel, often in severe cold, at night, or on the plateau. According to one account from Xinhua News, a PLARF special forces commander stressed non-contact play where “being discovered means failure.” Another PLA Daily article describes several blue force personnel conducting multi-means air reconnaissance while special troops raid from the ground, with blown bridges, ambushed launch vehicles, and jamming that leaves a battalion an “information island.” Red side missile brigades often will respond with camouflage, dispersal, light discipline against satellite passes, counter-reconnaissance, anti-infiltration, and rapid relocation and launch under harassment. After being discovered, red team missile brigades often must search for and apprehend blue force personnel to avoid failure in the exercise. The characteristics of these exercises underscore the PLA’s emphasis and heightened threat perceptions around the survivability of missile brigades. Conclusion and Policy Implications Although the role of special forces in managing nuclear operations is often underappreciated in the literature coming out of Western policy research institutions, the PLA invests significant resources in yearly exercises that test the survivability of missile brigades. Whether founded or unfounded, these exercises could also indicate that the PLARF and senior leadership see a variety of exquisite and unconventional ways in which the United States or other adversaries seek to disrupt the operation of China’s nuclear and conventional missile brigades. As U.S.-China military competition and nuclear competition intensify, the PLARF’s emphasis on protecting missile brigades from a variety of novel threats is unlikely to wane. Though their purview could evolve, the role of special forces in China’s nuclear strategy likely reflect a concern over protecting warheads and delivery vehicles rather than infiltrating an enemy’s forces. While the PLARF’s special forces generally stress-test the survivability of missile launch platforms, there are still many unknowns about the size, location, and number of PLARF SOF units. Future research should also examine in greater detail the organizational structure and command level of these units, the extent of sympathetic bureaucratic support within the PLA, and how they integrate with other components of the PLA. Do PLARF SOF have their own redundant reconnaissance systems, or are they primarily relying on intelligence from other services or organizations to inform their planning? For U.S. policymakers seeking damage limitation or left-of-launch options, researchers can attempt to track their specific routes, gaps in protecting delivery vehicles and warheads, and vulnerabilities in command and control. Ideally, policy entrepreneurs or military planners should find ways to disrupt PLARF mobile missile launcher operations and induce greater spending on internal security forces within the PLARF. This might involve credible and visible investment in long-range reconnaissance, special operations reach, and left-of-launch capabilities to reinforce existing fears over missile survivability and induce countermeasures to rectify perceived gaps. The PLARF has already shown that it takes the raids on its missile brigades seriously; in such a measure-countermeasure competition, every guard battalion, Blue Force detachment, and counter-reconnaissance drill draws money, personnel, and training time away from investing in increased offensive strike capabilities for a Taiwan campaign. Still, this course of action should be pursued only if the defensive burden on China exceeds the offensive investment by the United States, and forecasts of likely PLA countermeasures should be used to verify the soundness of the policy option. The post Special Forces in China’s Nuclear and Missile Operations appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

The core concept is "People's City, Better Life," with focus on topics such as modernizing digital and intelligent technologies in cities and strengthening urban governance. How are different cities exploring more timely and efficient ways to respond to resident's everyday concerns? Recently, CGTN collected a wide range of questions from people around the world about China's "Swift Response to Public Complaints" system and invited foreigners who have lived in China for a long time to share thoughts and experiences.

Daniel, a Russian vlogger who has lived in China for over a decade, shared his real experience of using the Zhejiang provincial government service "Zheliban". For a period of time, there were often construction noises and garbage truck sounds near Daniel's home in the early morning, which disturbed his rest. He submitted a complaint and a video in "Zheliban". A few days later, the staff coordinated the construction time and the community returned to quiet. The complaints system works – and fast – because of digitalization, Daniel says. “It has broken down the information silos between various departments”, making public services more efficient and giving foreigners a greater sense of belonging. He is confident that this system will continue to improve, making life easier for more people. #MyCityMySay | CGTN

content:
Istiqlal English on Instagram: "East Turkistan Occupation Protested Worldwide on October 1

On October 1, the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Uyghurs in many countries took to the streets to protest China's occupation and repressive policies in East Turkistan. Tibetans, Hong Kongers, Southern Mongolians, Chinese dissidents, and human rights groups joined them, and the World Uyghur Congress (WUC) reported joint protests in different countries. Protesters said that while Beijing treats the date as a "day of celebration," for Uyghurs it marks the loss of freedom and the right to self-determination.

Protests by city.
Istanbul: Uyghurs gathered outside the Chinese Consulate General in Sarıyer, in a demonstration called by East Turkistan organisations. Reuters filmed it. Participants cited "occupation," "genocide," and "assimilation."
Berlin: The WUC and other groups organised a protest at the Chinese Embassy with Uyghurs, Tibetans, Hong Kongers, Chinese dissidents, and German supporters. They called for the release of political prisoners and an end to transnational repression.
London: Uyghur, Tibetan, and Hong Kong activists protested at the Chinese Embassy, calling for an end to Chinese Communist Party rule. Former Hong Kong district councillor Clara Cheung called for freedom for all three groups.
Washington, D.C.: The Uyghur American Association and Uyghur Human Rights Project supported a protest at the Chinese Embassy. UHRP said October 1 is not a celebration for Uyghurs and urged stronger international action.
Los Angeles and San Francisco: A protest was held at the consulate in Los Angeles. In San Francisco, Chinese, Hong Kong, Tibetan, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolian, Vietnamese, and Filipino communities protested together and called October 1 a "National Day of Mourning."
Toronto and Vancouver: Uyghur, Tibetan, and Hong Kong communities and Chinese democracy activists protested at the consulates. East Turkistan representatives asked Canada and other democracies to monitor China's rights record and counter its repression of Uyghurs abroad."

## 中國浙大清華發現石墨烯膜新結構並發表 標榜高強度輕量化

2026-10-15 13:36 中央社／ 上海15日電  清華大學

中國媒體今天報導，中國[**浙江大學**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%B5%99%E6%B1%9F%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8)與北京[**清華大學**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%B8%85%E8%8F%AF%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8)研究團隊發現石墨烯膜新結構，昨天深夜艸並在國際學術期刊「自然」（Nature）線上發表研究成果，號稱高強度、高韌性與高彈性，可望為航空航太結構輕量化、增強衝擊防護裝備提供材料基礎。

新浪科技報導，這項研究是在石墨烯膜中發現「層間折疊卡扣」的新結構與新機制，首次實現石墨烯膜的高強度、高韌性與高彈性三合一的性能突破。

[Video 14](https://content1.avplayer.com/5b59760c073ef46a2e6b8f13/videos/69d8bed5fc5b3e8a960d2c4e/hls/video.m3u8?AV_TAGID=6814930766b0cc5c3d0ead4d&pid=615ac1a77d20d4235b6a596a&cid=68149208c94d744b4a057116&AV_TEMPID=681494bbf2ab4be52e0614da&AV_PUBLISHERID=615ac1a77d20d4235b6a596a&av_qd1=6818a0d1ee249970a60232b2&videoId=69d8bed5fc5b3e8a960d2c4e)![Image 1: Udn_Video_2_100426](https://content1.avplayer.com/5b59760c073ef46a2e6b8f13/videos/69d8bed5fc5b3e8a960d2c4e/6dc70f9c-b20f-46a4-8d31-74fe6890d6f8.webp)

新華社報導，石墨烯膜的力學性能提升長期以來面臨強度與韌性難以兼顧的瓶頸。傳統方法有的是透過提高石墨烯片層排列的規整程度，或是增強片層之間的結合力以改善性能。

新研究突破傳統「平面堆疊」設計思路，構築出層間相互咬合的「折疊卡扣結構」石墨烯膜。

新浪科技報導，與傳統平直堆疊不同，折疊結構能夠在層間形成軟的「機械卡扣」，使材料在受力時能夠發生可逆的彈性形變，且有效阻止層間滑移失效，實現強度、韌性和彈性的協同提升，打破傳統層狀材料力學性能的紀錄。

這項研究成果是浙江大學長聘副教授許震、教授高超和[**北京清華大學**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%8C%97%E4%BA%AC%E6%B8%85%E8%8F%AF%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8)教授徐志平團隊合作，浙江大學博士後王利丹、清華大學博士後廖楊超為論文共同第一作者。

高超表示，這項研究有望為航空航太輕量化結構、抗衝擊防護裝備等領域的發展提供材料基礎。

【大紀元2026年10月15日訊】美國網路雜誌Tablet（Tablet Magazine）週日（10月11日）發表了一篇題為「中國十億美元器官移植產業背後的駭人真相」的專題報告，探討了已在中國存在多年並被中共極力掩蓋的器官移植產業。

## 北京閱兵場上的意外對話

該報告從2025年在北京舉行的紀念戰勝日本80周年閱兵期間，中共黨魁習近平與俄羅斯總統普京（Vladimir Putin）之間的一段對話開始。

當時，習近平與普京並肩而行，兩人談論了器官移植與長壽的問題，對話被現場未關閉的媒體直播麥克風錄下。

習近平在翻譯的協助下說道：「以前，人們很少能活到70歲，但如今，70歲仍然是個孩子。」當時，習近平與普京都已是72歲。

普京則回答說，隨著生物技術進步，「人體器官可以不斷移植」，「這會讓我們變得越來越年輕，甚至可能實現永生」。

隨後，直播畫面切換至天安門廣場。兩位領導人稍後出現在觀禮台上。此時，習近平已不在鏡頭之中，但他又就此話題補充說：「有人預測，本世紀有可能活到150歲。」

報告指出，當時各大媒體多把這段習普對話解讀為兩位獨裁領導人對權力的渴望，但長期關注中共的人士則認為，它與兩件事有關：一是大規模強摘良心犯器官，二是為中共高層服務的保健計劃「981工程」。

## 器官移植量激增與迫害法輪功同步

據報告介紹，在中國民眾受傳統觀念影響，自願捐獻器官的意願非常低的背景下，中國的器官移植產業卻在2000年代初期迅速擴張。

值得注意的是，該器官移植產業爆發式增長的時間段，與中共開始全面打壓法輪功的時間段重合。

法輪功是一種佛家修煉功法，因為有益身心健康且效果顯著，在1990年代迅速傳播。在1999年迫害開始前夕，其修煉人數估計有7000萬至1億人。

1999年，時任中共黨魁江澤民因懼怕法輪功的影響力可能超過共產黨，下令實施鎮壓，並透過國家宣傳機器將法輪功污衊為「邪教」。

2006年，《大紀元時報》（The Epoch Times）率先披露，中共開始有系統地摘取被關押的法輪功修煉者的器官。多名證人挺身而出。

一名逃亡海外、化名安妮的護士作證說，其前夫是瀋陽蘇家屯一家醫院的神經外科醫生，他曾被迫從仍有生命跡象的法輪功修煉者身上摘取眼角膜。

## 醫生、法庭的說法

報告說，當年中國的醫院曾公開刊登英文器官移植廣告，並宣傳其器官等待時間短的優點。在有獨立調查人員打電話就此諮詢時，醫生承認會提供「新鮮」器官進行移植，並承諾只要付得起高價，就能迅速安排手術。

以色列心臟外科醫生雅各布·拉維（Jacob Lavee）透露，2005年，他的一名病人告訴他，自己已不想再等了，並已獲得安排，在兩週後前往中國接受心臟移植。當這名病人真的移植了一顆新心臟回來時，拉維博士大為震驚。

拉維後來在倫敦的中國問題獨立法庭（China Tribunal）作證說，在正常醫療體系中，沒有人能夠提前兩週安排心臟移植手術，因為必須有捐獻者死亡才行。

該法庭由曾起訴前南斯拉夫總統米洛舍維奇（Slobodan Milošević）的英國大律師傑弗里·尼斯爵士（Sir Geoffrey Nice）主持。

該法庭在收集證據一年後得出結論，強摘器官在中國「相當大規模」地發生著，而無需任何法律手續即可抓捕和關押的法輪功修煉者，成為了器官移植的主要來源。強摘器官規模之大，已超越了所有可能的理由及所有的合理解釋。

## 為何短時間內能配到器官

報告分析說，在正常移植體系中，器官來自意外事故中的逝者，而且還需要匹配血型、組織和尺寸等，病人往往要等數月甚至數年，才能獲得器官移植的機會。

但中國國內的權貴和付費的外國病人，卻常常能在幾天或幾週內完成器官移植手術，有時甚至能夠提前定好日期。

報告認為，只有存在已配型的龐大活體「器官供體庫」才可能做到這一點。

報告指出，在中共器官移植產業「蓬勃發展」的時間段裡，數以十萬計的法輪功修煉者遭到逮捕。許多人拒絕透露自己的姓名，以保護家人。

一項不成文的規定將法輪功修煉者在羈押期間的死亡一律視為自殺。

外界看到的只是失蹤和酷刑，但在體制內，被關押者卻接受血型檢測、組織配型，並被納入資料庫。

當高級官員或付費客戶需要器官時，便能找到配型合適的人，並專門為這次移植殺死該名囚犯。由於殺人可以按需進行，手術也就能預先安排。

2000年至2005年間，隨著這個活體器官來源庫形成，中國的移植能力呈爆炸式增長。新醫院、新團隊和新手術室以驚人的速度出現，無法以自願捐獻或死刑犯器官來源作出合理解釋。

這個器官庫成為中共政權迫害法輪功修煉者的核心部分。

報告引述的被關押法輪功修煉者的回憶，佐證了這一點。

很多法輪功學員在被關押期間，都曾被抽血、做體檢。這些都是器官移植手術配型的關鍵步驟。

此前，海外獨立中文媒體《大紀元時報》已經披露了多位此類倖存者講述的親身經歷。

[延伸閱讀：前日本黑幫幹部親見遭中共活摘器官的法輪功學員](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/22/6/25/n13767360.htm)

## 981工程與軍方醫院

報告還指出，中共於2005年推出了所謂的「981工程」。這是一個專為黨內高層及權貴階層設立的頂級醫療保健計劃（又稱「首長健康工程」）。該計劃以追求人類長壽（目標直指150歲）及「器官功能再生」為核心。

前解放軍總後勤部衛生部部長白書忠（於2004年退休）被指與該項目的籌備及早期推動密切相關。

追查迫害法輪功國際組織（WOIPFG）的調查人員此前曾匿名致電白書忠，他當時在電話中承認，摘取法輪功修煉者器官是上級下達的命令。

報告說，該保健計劃的合作醫院網絡包括北京的中國人民解放軍總醫院，以及上海長征醫院。

據「追查迫害法輪功國際組織」此前發布的、對中國大陸各大醫院器官移植數據的梳理與研究報告，長征醫院曾做過等待時間短至四小時的緊急肝移植。

報告認為，這在醫學上只有在隨時有活體捐獻者時才可能做到。

報告中還提到了2023年去世的中共文化部前副部長高占祥。其訃告稱，他生前曾「更換了體內許多器官」。

據撰寫訃告的官員說，高占祥生前曾開玩笑表示，「許多零部件已經不是自己的了」。

報告指出，這是中共高層黨員能優先取得器官按需進行移植的跡象。

[延伸閱讀：揭中共「981工程」追求延壽背後的黑幕](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/25/11/14/n14635756.htm)

## 官方否認 數據受質疑

報告指出，長期以來，中共始終否認相關指控。在早期，中共官方解釋說，這些器官來自死刑犯。自2015年起則改稱，只使用了捐獻器官。

但在2019年11月發表於《BMC醫學倫理》（BMC Medical Ethics）的一項研究發現，中共當局公布的器官移植手術數量，帶有明顯人為操縱的痕跡，「年復一年完美貼合特定計算公式」。

2016年，加拿大前官員大衛·喬高（David Kilgour）、人權律師大衛·麥塔斯（David Matas）和調查記者伊森·葛特曼（Ethan Gutmann）聯合報告估計，中國每年實際移植手術數量高達6萬至10萬例，遠高於官方公布的數字，並認為實際數字更接近較高的估值。

為得出這個數字——最高可達官方數據的10倍——三人考慮了中國器官移植醫院的數量（超過700家）、國家級移植中心進行大量移植手術的能力（其中一家每年超過8,000例）、醫院公布的床位數，以及這些醫院對移植手術的高度重視。

葛特曼在2016年向美國國會表示，他認為這一估計數字仍然相當保守。

喬高和麥塔斯在2006年的一份報告中記錄了一名病人的案例：他在上海一家醫院先後被移植了八顆腎臟，直到最後一顆才配型成功。

報告說，2020年，該報告作者曾報導過一名女子飛往中國接受心臟移植手術的案例。醫生在10天內為她找到了四顆配型成功的心臟。

反對強摘器官醫生組織（Doctors Against Forced Organ Harvesting）歐洲區副主任安德烈亞斯·韋伯（Andreas Weber）博士，在2025年「終止強摘器官扶輪衛星社」（EFOH Rotary）的一個活動中分享了一名德國病人的故事：

「這名女子是AB型血，這是一種罕見血型，使尋找配型器官更加困難。她也是一名酗酒者，因此不符合在德國列入等待名單的資格。所以，她在數年內三次飛往中國。她接受了三次肝臟移植，每次支付約40萬歐元。」

## 呼籲美國立法

報告強調，大規模強摘器官體系不會一夜之間形成。正如楊傑凱（Jan Jekielek）近期著作《按需殺害》（Killed to Order）所詳述的，這一體系的基本要素包括多年的蓄意政策、協調一致的行動，以及對特定群體進行有系統的非人化，類似於納粹德國針對猶太人的仇恨運動。

報告還指出，以色列已在2008年立法，將器官販運和器官移植旅遊定為犯罪。隨後，臺灣、意大利、挪威、比利時、韓國、英國和加拿大也已跟進。

目前，美國只有德克薩斯州、亞利桑那州等六個州禁止醫療保險承保來自中國的器官移植手術。

報告呼籲美國參議院通過《2025年制止強摘器官法案》（H.R. 1503）和《法輪功及強摘器官受害者保護法案》（S. 4009），對涉事人員實施制裁、限制簽證，並要求定期公布相關報告。

報告最後強調，習近平與普京之間關於器官移植的討論，雖然是被偶然曝光，但絕非偶然。各國不應再對此保持沉默，以免變相默許中共繼續運作其慘無人道的器官移植體系。

# Hong Kong Space Museum launches new 3D dome film 'Explore the Stars 3D'

The Hong Kong Space Museum has launched a new 3D dome film, 'Explore the Stars 3D', tracing astronomy's past and future. The 28-minute show runs until 14 July 2027, with tickets priced at HK$30 and HK$40.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 12:52 HKT · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=Hong%20Kong%20Space%20Museum%20launches%20new%203D%20dome%20film%20%27Explore%20the%20Stars%203D%27%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-Space-Museum-launches-new-3D-dome-film-Explore-the-196572 "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-Space-Museum-launches-new-3D-dome-film-Explore-the-196572&text=Hong%20Kong%20Space%20Museum%20launches%20new%203D%20dome%20film%20%27Explore%20the%20Stars%203D%27 "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-Space-Museum-launches-new-3D-dome-film-Explore-the-196572 "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-Space-Museum-launches-new-3D-dome-film-Explore-the-196572&text=Hong%20Kong%20Space%20Museum%20launches%20new%203D%20dome%20film%20%27Explore%20the%20Stars%203D%27 "X")[](mailto:?subject=Hong%20Kong%20Space%20Museum%20launches%20new%203D%20dome%20film%20%27Explore%20the%20Stars%203D%27&body=Hong%20Kong%20Space%20Museum%20launches%20new%203D%20dome%20film%20%27Explore%20the%20Stars%203D%27%0Ahttps%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Hong-Kong-Space-Museum-launches-new-3D-dome-film-Explore-the-196572 "Email")

The Hong Kong Space Museum has launched a new stereoscopic dome film, Explore the Stars 3D, which takes audiences on a journey through the past and future of astronomy with vivid, detailed imagery, the government announced on Thursday.

The film showcases how pioneering scientists reshaped humanity's understanding of the universe, gradually unravelling the mysteries of celestial motion. It covers the tracking of the relative positions of the Sun and the Moon along the ecliptic to predict solar and lunar eclipses, the shift from a geocentric to a heliocentric model, and the development of physical laws that help calculate spacecraft orbits.

These discoveries laid the foundation for modern space exploration and paved the way for humanity's ambition to land on Mars, according to the museum.

The programme runs for 28 minutes and will be screened until 14 July 2027. Weekday screenings are scheduled for 2pm and 6.30pm, while weekend and public holiday screenings take place at 12.30pm and 5pm.

Tickets are priced at HK$30 for front seats and HK$40 for rear seats. They are available at the Hong Kong Space Museum box office and through Urbtix (www.urbtix.hk). Details of the show can be found on the museum's website.

The Hong Kong Space Museum is located at 10 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon. It is closed on Tuesdays except public holidays.

人工智能
HKIC 表示，其超过 70% 的资本都针对早期和成长阶段的公司，250 家投资组合公司中有 11 家在香港上市，今年还有 30 多家计划上市。其首席执行官概述了人工智能应用和开源创新的重点。中银投资计划跨境产业化

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:17 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港投资公司（HKIC）行政总裁陈嘉敏表示，公司70%以上的资金投放于早期和成长期的企业，目前投资已初见成效。她在活动上表示，在250个投资项目中，已有11家公司已在香港上市，超过30家公司计划今年上市或提交上市申请。

陈表示，未来的技术应该满足不同人群的需求，易于获取且价格实惠。以人工智能为例，她表示HKIC正在逐步将投资重点转向人工智能价值链的中下游部分，包括实际应用场景。她强调了对开源人工智能的特别关注，她说开源人工智能可以显着降低创新成本，让年轻一代和小型初创企业能够快速创新、蓬勃发展和竞争。
中银集团投资副总裁王军在同场活动中表示，公司正在实施以早期投资、小额投资和硬技术投资为重点的转型战略，以支持香港的研究成果商业化。他表示，该公司已投资超过10只科技基金和9个香港科技项目，重点关注人工智能、生物材料制造和新材料等领域。

王先生表示，中银投资将优先选择香港特区政府支持的项目，并积极探索香港科研与大湾区转型相结合的跨境产业化路径。他主张推广香港研发、内地验证的模式。

王毅表示，中银投作为立足香港的全球投资平台，将发挥国家风险资本、耐心资本和长期资本的作用。他表示，公司在能源、航空、半导体、先进制造等领域投资了一批行业影响力大、金额大、回报丰厚的重大项目。三年来，大湾区科技贷款已突破7000亿元。
王强调，公司将利用全球机构网络和跨境金融服务，助力科技走出去，推动科技创新链与制造产业链无缝对接。

HKIC says over 70 per cent of its capital targets early and growth-stage firms, with 11 of 250 portfolio companies listed in Hong Kong and over 30 planning listings this year. Its CEO outlined a pivot to AI applications and open-source innovation. BOC Investment plans cross-border industrialisation

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 13:17 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Investment Corporation (HKIC) Chief Executive Clara Chan said more than 70 per cent of the company's capital is placed in enterprises at early and growth stages, and the investments are already showing results. Speaking at an event, she said that among 250 portfolio projects, 11 companies have listed in Hong Kong, and over 30 plan to list or submit listing applications this year.

Chan said future technology should serve the needs of different groups of people, be easy to access and affordable. Taking artificial intelligence as an example, she said HKIC is gradually shifting its investment focus to the middle and downstream parts of the AI value chain, including practical application scenarios. She highlighted particular attention to open-source AI, which she said can significantly lower innovation costs and allow younger generations and small startups to innovate quickly, thrive and compete.

Wang Jun, deputy chief executive of BOC Group Investment, said at the same event that the company is implementing a transformation strategy focused on investing early, investing small and investing in hard technology, to support the commercialisation of research in Hong Kong. He said the firm has invested in more than 10 technology funds and nine Hong Kong technology projects, focusing on sectors including artificial intelligence, biomaterials manufacturing and new materials.

Wang said BOC Investment will give priority to projects supported by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government and is actively exploring a cross-border industrialisation pathway that combines Hong Kong research with Greater Bay Area conversion. He argued for promoting a model of Hong Kong research and development with mainland verification.

As a global investment platform based in Hong Kong, Wang said BOC Investment will play the role of national risk capital, patient capital and long-term capital. He said the firm has invested in a number of major projects with significant industry influence, large amounts and attractive returns in energy, aviation, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing. Over the past three years, technology loans in the Greater Bay Area have exceeded 700 billion yuan.

Wang stressed that the company will use its global institutional network and cross-border financial services to help technology go global, and promote seamless connection between the technology innovation chain and the manufacturing industry chain.

content:
A Book about Anti-Communist Movies

We are on the eve of the announcement of the lineup at the first annual Anti-Communist Film Festival. Our headline film is **The Lives of Others.**

I’ve spent over a year talking to Hollywood studios about licensing, visiting movie theaters to make my case (as you might expect, some were not thrilled with the idea), and finally getting a sponsor with the great folks at the Victims of Communism Foundation.

**There’s one more thing I’d like to do. I have a 20,000-word essay about my favorite anti-communist movies, and I'd like to publish it next year as a book and companion to the film festival.** Excerpts from the essay have been published on Hot Air, Chronicles, and on the Victims of Communism website. I’d like to publish the entire essay in paper format, something that people can hold. A samizdat, which during the Cold War was a book or pamphlet that was forbidden in communist countries and was passed around from hand to hand by dissidents.

**Most importantly, what I am calling Freedom’s Fury: A Guide to Anti-Communist Movies would be something that cannot be digitally erased.**

In his forthcoming book Reds: A Global History of Communism, journalist Paul Mason explores how communists want us to forget the past:

I do not want to “take control” of the memory of Marx, any more than the memory of the Russian Revolution or the Spanish Civil War. But I do want to prevent the Communist Party of China from taking control of them. Because, as [philosopher Walter] Benjamin reminds us: “not even the dead are safe from the enemy.” Just as postwar fascism fought to expunge the facts about the Holocaust, we are now seeing—in Putin’s Russia, Xi’s China, and political movements aligned to them in the global south—systematic distortions of the events described here. And it will get worse. In occupied Ukraine, new statues of Lenin are being erected. In Russia, plaques commemorating victims of the Great Purge are being torn down, and the last museum of the Gulag has been closed. In China, all critical writing about Mao is dismissed as “historical nihilism.”

Mason then notes how his own book may be censored:

As you read each chapter, I want you to imagine how it might be written in a future dominated by the brain-frozen clichés of Chinese communism. The Beijing propaganda machine has been busy eradicating the truth about the Tiananmen Square Massacre for nearly forty years. What might it achieve if given the unchallenged right to curate the facts about 1848, 1917, or indeed 1789? Far from being yesterday’s problem, the struggle for the truth about the history of communism may have only just begun. If so, Benjamin’s words on the eve of its darkest and finest hours bear repeating: Every line we succeed in publishing today—no matter how uncertain the future to which we entrust it—is a victory wrested from the powers of darkness.

**American communists would like nothing more than to censor the Anti-Communist Film Festival and forget it ever existed, even before it begins.**

# Fighting for legal fairness

# Support Uyghur film & tell the story together

Hello dear friends:  We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.  If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group  The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:  $100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter. $200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter. $500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film. $5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer. Ï Summary  Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.  Our team  We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.

# Help our local Uyghur restaurant!

In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville.  The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare. Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region. Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.' But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia. Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! title: Donate to Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology, organized by Uyghur Anthology
summary: The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. The
content:
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.

<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>

We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.

All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.

Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.

**Our Story**

There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.

To sum up, the issues were:

*   No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
*   A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
*   Lack of awareness of opportunities
*   No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature

So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.

<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>

The blurb from our first volume:

_"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience._

_By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."_

We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.

Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.

Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:

"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."

Our stats:

*   44 pieces in total by 36 contributors
*   Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
*   All work translated into English
*   11 translators
*   Contributors based in over 10 countries

<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>

**Volume 3**

Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.

**How we'd like to proceed**

*   **Supporting the editors -** all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
*   **Supporting our contributors -** we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
*   **Recruiting more people -** paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
*   **Enhance our level of expertise -**we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
*   **Expand our network -**we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.

<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>

**Who we are**

**Munawwar Abdulla** is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.

**Sonya Imin** is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.

**Maidina Kadeer**is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

**Gulnisa Nazarova**

Donation protected

My name is Gulnisa Nazarova, and I have been an Uyghur language instructor for over 20 years. This year, as I turn 60, instead of gifts I am asking for something much closer to my heart.

My dear mother taught me how to cook. Through her hands, I learned patience, generosity, and how food carries memory. Many of the dishes she passed on come from the Uyghur tradition, a cuisine rich in history, flavor, and storytelling, yet still too little known and increasingly at risk of being forgotten.

This fundraiser supports a lifelong dream of mine: creating a cookbook dedicated to Uyghur cuisine and cultural heritage.

My connection to Uyghur culture begins with my family and upbringing. My parents and ancestors came from the Uyghur Autonomous Region, known as Eastern Turkistan to Soviet Central Asia in the mid-20th century, carrying with them their traditions, food, language, history, and stories. I grew up learning not only recipes, but also their deeper meaning — meals that bring families together, celebrations filled with memory, and dishes that carry history from one generation to the next.

Over the years, I have worked professionally to support Uyghur language and culture through teaching, writing, and sharing my knowledge with others around the world. This cookbook, however, is different. It comes directly from the heart — from meals shared with my family and from a deep desire to preserve the taste of home for future generations.

This is a personal initiative, and the funds raised will help cover:

*   Research and documentation of recipes and food stories
*   Photography and image use for the book
*   Writing and editing
*   Professional design
*   Initial publication costs

Whether you give a little or a lot, you are helping keep a culinary heritage alive.

Thank you for celebrating my 60th birthday by honoring my mother’s legacy with me.

Hi, I'm Mehmet Utku ÖZTÜRK, and I'm reaching out to you to support the vital work of the Uyghur Human Rights Project (UHRP).

As many of you may know, the Uyghurs in East Turkistan face severe human rights challenges, torture, forced labor, child labor and cultural repression (I linked some articles and publications upon this matter at the end, you can check)

UHRP is dedicated to advocating for their civil, political, social, cultural, and economic rights through extensive research and reports.

Your donations will directly impact this important mission by:

*   Funding vital research and publications that raise awareness about the plight of the Uyghurs.
*   Supporting advocacy efforts that push for international accountability and protection of human rights in East Turkistan.

Together, we can help amplify the voices of those who need it most. Please consider donating to support UHRP's ongoing efforts. Every contribution makes a difference. Thank you!

title: Donate to Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children, organized by Yangkey Gangshar
summary: Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Taman
content:
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.

Who We Are & Our Connection

We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.

“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.

A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family

At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.

Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.

He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.

The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.

Our Family’s Connection to This Community

Our connection to this region goes back generations.

Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.

Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.

The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.

Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.

The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.

Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.

What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.

We Are Grieving Many Losses

Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.

His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.

We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.

Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.

How the Funds Will Be Used

We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.

The funds will be used specifically for:

*   Food and daily necessities
*   Shelter, rent, and household expenses
*   Clothing and essential supplies
*   School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
*   Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
*   Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives

100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.

Bringing the Help Directly to Nepal

Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.

We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.

Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.

If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.

Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.

From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.

With gratitude,

Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

— His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama

KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.

Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.

Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:

• Namgyal Higher Secondary School

• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School

• Namgyal Middle Boarding School

• Marshyangdi Boarding High School

• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School

We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.

We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.

For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.

Funds raised will help provide:

• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities

• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses

• Ongoing living and caregiving support

• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers

Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.

You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.

Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.

# Hong Kong releases kindergarten profiles for 2026/27 school year

The Education Bureau has published the online version of the 2026/27 Kindergarten Profile, listing basic information for about 930 kindergartens in Hong Kong to help parents choose schools.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 12:03 HKT · 1 min read

The Education Bureau on 15 October released the online version of the 2026/27 school year “Profile of Kindergartens and Kindergarten-cum-Child Care Centres” (www.chsc.hk/kindergarten), providing basic information on all kindergartens and kindergarten-cum-child care centres in Hong Kong. The bureau said the profile aims to enhance school transparency and help parents obtain more relevant information when choosing schools for their children.

The profile lists basic information on about 930 kindergartens across Hong Kong, including the list of schools participating in the 2026/27 kindergarten education scheme, approved school fees, the number of principals and teachers and their qualifications, student numbers, teacher-to-student ratios, curriculum information, reference prices for major educational supplies, application fees, registration fees and admission application details.

The profile also includes sections on “support for non-Chinese speaking students” and “support for students with special educational needs” for parents’ reference, the bureau said.

For kindergartens participating in the scheme, the profile shows the approved school fees after deducting government subsidies. Parents can also refer to the school’s fee certificate to check approved charges, including details of tuition and meal fees, the bureau said. All participating kindergartens are required to publicly disclose the proportion of expenditure in major spending areas in the profile.

All kindergartens in the scheme must undergo quality reviews to ensure standards. The profile indicates whether kindergartens that have completed quality reviews have met specified standards and provides links to the most recent quality review reports, according to the bureau.

Taipei, Oct. 15 (CNA) Shares in Taiwan tumbled more than 1,500 points at one point Thursday morning, as heavy losses on other major Asian markets and Wall Street triggered a sell-off amid renewed inflation concerns, dealers said.

As of 11:14 a.m., the Taiex, the Taiwan Stock Exchange's benchmark index, had dropped 1,612.82 points, or 3.32 percent, to 47,013.01, dealers said.

The plunge was led by large-cap technology stocks after higher-than-expected U.S. inflation data led investors to anticipate a more hawkish monetary policy from the U.S. Federal Reserve, dealers said.

On Wednesday, the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data for September showed that inflation rose 3.7 percent, higher than the market forecast of 3.6 percent, fueling expectations of a Fed rate hike, dealers said.

Following the release of the CPI data, sell-off occurred on U.S. markets Wednesday, and Asian markets followed suit Thursday morning, with tech stocks in focus, as concerns mounted that AI-related developers would face higher financing costs if interest rates continued to rise, dealers said.

In Taipei, the electronics index had fallen 3.63 percent as of 11:14 a.m., pulling the Taiex sharply lower.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), which accounts for more than 40 percent of the market's total capitalization, was down 2.01 percent at NT$2,440.00 (US$75.54).

Memory chip supplier Nanya Technology Corp. plunged 9.16 percent to NT$436.50, while smartphone IC designer MediaTek Inc. dropped 5.92 percent to NT$4,210.00.

Among other tech stocks, iPhone assembler and AI server maker Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. was down 1.85 percent at NT$238.50, while power-management solutions provider Delta Electronics Inc. fell 8.40 percent to NT$1,635.00.

(By Pan Chih-yi and Frances Huang)

title: Alaska LNG deal may boost Taiwan's energy resilience: U.S. scholar - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 美国学者：阿拉斯加液化天然气交易可能会增强台湾的能源弹性 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社华盛顿10月14日电 一位美国学者周三表示，台湾拟从阿拉斯加管道项目购买液化天然气(LNG)的协议可能会增强台湾的能源弹性，并缩小与美国的贸易顺差。史汀生中心高级研究员迈克尔·坎宁安（Michael Cunningham）对中央社表示，该协议可能会提高台湾作为美国出口市场的重要性，让华盛顿更有动力确保台湾的安全。他表示：“到 2050 年代，台湾仍将至关重要。”他补充说，预计该项目的出口不会开始
content:
中新社华盛顿10月14日电 一位美国学者周三表示，台湾拟从阿拉斯加管道项目购买液化天然气(LNG)的协议可能会增强台湾的能源弹性，并缩小与美国的贸易顺差。

史汀生中心高级研究员迈克尔·坎宁安（Michael Cunningham）对中央社表示，该协议可能会提高台湾作为美国出口市场的重要性，让华盛顿更有动力确保台湾的安全。

他表示：“到 2050 年代，台湾仍将至关重要。”他补充说，预计该项目的出口要到 2031 年才会开始。

坎宁安在回复中央社询问其对此问题看法的电子邮件时表示，“如果这项协议得以实现，将有助于增强台湾的能源弹性”并减少对美国的贸易顺差——这是华盛顿的优先事项。

据财政部统计，2025年，台湾对美国的贸易顺差约为1501亿美元。

周二，美国总统特朗普在阿拉斯加的一次集会上表示，台湾已同意在20年内购买计划中的阿拉斯加液化天然气管道项目30%的天然气产量，并为该项目额外投资44亿美元。他后来在其真相社交平台上的一篇帖子中重申了这一说法。
继他宣布这一消息后，台湾经济部周三证实，台湾国有企业中油集团将在阿拉斯加项目上投资至多44亿美元，并在投产后每年采购600万吨液化天然气。

经济部表示，长期购买和投资计划将使台湾的天然气供应多元化，并增强其能源弹性。

该部门表示，阿拉斯加液化天然气项目还将通过直接跨太平洋向台湾运送货物来减少运输和地缘政治风险。

经济部表示，如果该项目按计划进行，最早可能在 2032 年开始为台湾国内天然气供应做出贡献。

华盛顿哈德逊研究所高级研究员赖利·沃尔特斯表示，台湾对阿拉斯加液化天然气项目的承诺将有助于确保该管道的盈利能力。

沃尔特斯表示，该协议还将有助于台湾对美国做出更广泛的投资承诺，并指出台湾仍需要获得2000亿美元的信贷才能完成与华盛顿的战略投资协议。

（侯绮琳、柯琳）

成品/件

【原文 English Original】
Washington, Oct. 14 (CNA) A proposed deal for Taiwan to purchase liquefied natural gas (LNG) from an Alaska pipeline project could strengthen Taiwan's energy resilience and narrow its trade surplus with the United States, an American scholar said Wednesday.

Michael Cunningham, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center, told CNA that the deal could increase Taiwan's importance as a market for U.S. exports, giving Washington greater incentive to ensure Taiwan's security.

"Taiwan will remain critically important into the 2050s," he said, adding that exports from the project are not expected to begin until 2031.

"If this deal materializes, it will help strengthen Taiwan's energy resilience" and reduce its trade surplus with the U.S. -- a priority for Washington, Cunningham said in an email response to CNA's request for his views on the issue.

In 2025, Taiwan recorded a trade surplus of approximately US$150.1 billion with the U.S., according to Ministry of Finance statistics.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump said at a rally in Alaska that Taiwan had agreed to purchase 30 percent of the natural gas output from the planned Alaska LNG pipeline project over 20 years and invest an additional US$4.4 billion in the project. He later reiterated the claim in a post on his Truth Social platform.

Following his announcement, Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) on Wednesday confirmed that the state-owned CPC Corp., Taiwan will invest up to US$4.4 billion in the Alaska project and purchase 6 million metric tons of LNG annually once production begins.

The long-term purchase and investment plan will diversify Taiwan's natural gas supplies and strengthen its energy resilience, the MOEA said.

The Alaska LNG project would also reduce transportation and geopolitical risks by sending shipments to Taiwan directly across the Pacific, the ministry said.

If the project proceeds as planned, it could begin contributing to Taiwan's domestic natural gas supply as early as 2032, according to the MOEA.

Riley Walters, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute in Washington, said that Taiwan's commitment to the Alaska LNG project would help to ensure the pipeline's profitability.

The deal would also contribute to Taiwan's broader investment commitments to the U.S., Walters said, noting that Taiwan still needs to secure US$200 billion in credit to complete its strategic investment agreement with Washington.

(By Elaine Hou and Ko Lin)

## Details

Most of us know exactly where our comfort zones end. Fewer of us talk about what it costs, or gives us, to step past them. This is a space to explore that.
 Join us over Zoom for an honest conversation about willingness to risk: where you stretch yourself, where you choose discomfort on purpose, and what’s on the line when you stand at the edge of what you know and look over into what you don’t. Guided by a life coach, this isn’t a lecture or a pep talk. It’s a circle where people show up, share, and actually listen to one another.

**We’ll explore questions like:**

*   Where in your life are you stretching yourself right now, and where are you playing it safe?
*   How or when do you choose to be uncomfortable, and what makes it worth it?
*   What’s at risk when you stand at the line between knowing and not knowing?

**What to expect:**

*   A grounding opening to arrive and settle in
*   Guided reflection from our life coach on risk, courage, and the edge of the known
*   Open sharing: say as much or as little as feels right
*   A closing moment to carry something forward, whether that’s a next step or a question to sit with

**Good to know:**

*   Cameras welcome, not required
*   No experience needed, just openness
*   Zoom link sent to confirmed RSVPs ahead of time

content:
Join us for a **free** demo in the LilyPalooza series, hosted by Lily Wang, the last Sunday of each month! Demoed games are 10% off on the day that they are demoed, AFTER the demo is over.

Game: **Cosmoctopus**
 Duration: 60-90 minute playthroughs
 Players: 1-4

Description:
_Welcome, devotees! The celestial gaze of the Great Inky One falls upon you; do you have what it takes to be the most dedicated follower?_

**Cosmoctopus** is an engine-building, tentacle-gathering board game for 1 to 4 devotees. Guide Cosmoctopus through the Inky Realm, a flexible configuration of tiles, to gather resources and obtain powerful cards that represent relics, scripture, hallucinations and constellations. Harness the power of these bizarre objects and experiences, craft potent card combinations and be the first to gain 8 tentacles to win!

Your turns are simple; the game’s excitement and depth lie in working out how best to use an ever-powerful hand of cards. Unlike some other engine-builders, you’ll be straight into the fun, upgrading your engine from turn one. With variable setup, easy ways to alter difficulty and optional solo and co-operative modes, Cosmoctopus offers a versatile tabletop experience, whatever your gaming tastes.

_—description from the publisher_
