content:
## **Key Takeaways:**

*   Under India’s chairmanship the New Delhi BRICS summit adopted a declaration promoting local-currency trade, payment-system interoperability and reforms at the UN, IMF and World Bank, while Modi stressed that the expanded group of eleven members (nearly half the world’s population and 40 percent of global GDP) is non-Western rather than anti-Western.
*   The New Development Bank, now with over $32 billion in approved projects, and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement form the core of an alternative financial architecture that African members such as South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia are using to pursue development while retaining ties with Western partners.
*   Rising Chinese trade and defence links with Central Asia illustrate the region’s diversification, yet the article notes that BRICS’s collective economic weight still outstrips its ability to act as a unified political bloc.

Perhaps, BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa), with the new members and partner states, summit in New Delhi, on September 11 to13, produced a new round of significant declarations, adapting its collective policy towards an increasingly emerging architecture, while distinctively building an ‘Asian model’ of economic alliance. Under the chairmanship of India, the summit centered on creating a genuine reputation that has accumulated for nearly two decades. The timing was, particularly, notable. The most important strategic message was coined: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.”

Addressing the BRICS summit of leading developing nations in New Delhi, Indian Prime Minister, Narendra Modi, warned rising geopolitical tensions, could increasingly affect people worldwide, and called for deepening cooperation and strengthening support across the Global South. “The number of conflicts and tensions in the world is continuously increasing, and this is having an increasingly negative and far-reaching impact on the lives of ordinary people,” Modi said, alongside with leaders including Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. That was one of the main messages sent across the world. Founded in 2006 by Brazil, Russia, India and China, BRICS has expanded to 11 members representing about half the world’s population and a significant share of global economic output. It has sought greater representation for developing countries in global institutions and promoted alternative actions to Western-dominated financial systems.

## **Geopolitics: Is BRICS Challenging the West?**

BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration, expressing indispensable concern relating to forging consensus over many strategic questions, backed greater use of local currencies in trade and stronger cross-border payment systems, while calling for cooperation on food security, energy, digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and climate action. The declaration was a significant breakthrough, which holds competing positions on key regional and geopolitical issues–posed a complex diplomatic challenge amid ongoing conflicts and heightened geopolitical tensions. It emphasizes collective support for a multipolar world order and operational and structural reforms, at the United Nations, including its Security Council, as well as global financial institutions such as the World Bank (WB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The declaration demonstrated BRICS can move together and act on multilateral economic cooperation, and its sustainability in Global South. That makes the question whether India has used its presidency to drum home for BRICS grouping to become more capable of taking economic action, with reports indicating that India entered a particular moment with more than just diplomatic presence. For instance, during the financial year 2024-25, its total exports amounted, approximately, $825 billion, with services accounting for an estimated $387 billion. Few developing countries can match New Delhi’s economic leverage, which stems from its large domestic market, expansion of digital economy, and sustainable growth. Despite national preferences and differences between BRICS members, it is worthy to note that India is a major provider of digital public infrastructure, and its demography plays an increasingly important role in global consumption, production, and services. It therefore exemplifies BRICS members have to build economic prosperity by opening doors. This new phase must strategically focus on a broader economic leverage. And appropriately, India’s geography provides an additional layer of economic leverage, which serves as a classical example for other Asian countries.

## **Сorporate Economic Weight, Limited Collective Power**

While BRICS’s economic weight is enormous–its ability to wield it collectively is not, some analysts argued. However, experts’ arguments closely connected to BRICS operational successes and achievements should not only be measured by whether it can pose an alternative to multinational institutions, but also whether it could make any noticeable difference, in terms of using its natural resources to increase regional trade, raise economic production and improve distribution across the Global South. Several experts position portrays BRICS has offered its member countries alternative pathways for channeling trade and investment that serve the collective interests of member countries–largely national development and poverty alleviation.

Meanwhile, scholars have reminded that BRICS emerged after the 2008 financial collapse and the failures of the World Trade Organization’s (WTO) Doha Round–trade negotiations aimed at reforming the international trading system in favour of Global South countries. Why would the BRICS want to take on the global governance responsibilities of the G7 members? This has been the basic question among scholars until today. It is, however, believed that reforms and greater autonomy would be a greater concern for BRICS rather than overthrowing the unravelling liberal international order.

## **BRICS+ Financial Architecture**

The group is noticeably dominated by China, which has the largest share of the group’s GDP, accounting to about 70% of the organization total. The financial architecture of BRICS is made of the New Development Bank (NDB) and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA). These components were signed into a treaty in 2014 and became active in 2015. The New Development Bank (NDB), formally referred to as the BRICS Development Bank, is a multilateral development bank operated by the five BRICS states. It has non-members as contributors to the NDB.

The bank’s primary focus of lending is infrastructure projects with authorized lending of up to $34 billion annually. South Africa hosts the African headquarters of the bank. The bank has a starting capital of $50 billion, with wealth increased to $100 billion over time. Records show Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa initially contributed $10 billion each to bring the total to $50 billion. As of 2020, it had 53 projects underway worth around $15 billion. By 2025, the bank had approved more than $32 billion for 96 projects.

In 2021, Bangladesh, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates and Uruguay joined the NDB. With India’s presidency in 2026, which was estimated to be a comprehensive and promising for BRICS, as India has outlined its framework of priorities, as it did during its G20 presidency several years ago. In close-coordination with members and partner-states within the BRICS, India has ensured the balance of multifaceted interests, and established mutual-trust in the multipolar world system. The goal of transforming into a full-fledged international organization must go beyond addressing current geopolitical challenges, the necessity to develop effective ways of engaging in global development to reflect multipolarity. Today, collectively, BRICS comprises more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world’s population.

## **BRICS Advocates for Reforms at Financial Institutions**

Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors of BRICS countries have called for reform of global developmental financial institutions ‌such as the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, seeking a ‌stronger voice for emerging market economies. “We will continue to strengthen coordination among BRICS members to make international financial ‌institutions more representative, transparent and accountable. With the growing share of emerging market and developing economies in ​global output and growth, reform of global economic governance remains a consistent BRICS priority,” Finance Chiefs of BRICS countries underlined in an official joint statement.

“We continue to have serious concerns with the unilateral imposition of trade and finance-related actions, including the raising of tariffs and non-tariff measures, which distort trade and are inconsistent with World Trade Organisation rules,” the statement said. “We ‌encourage the BRICS Payment Task Force to ​continue discussions, building ​on the ongoing work, to facilitate practical solutions for cross-border payments among BRICS countries, which are fast, low-cost, more accessible, efficient, transparent, and ​safe,” the statement said. While acknowledging the work done ​by the BRICS payment task force, the ​finance chiefs pushed for progress ​in ensuring greater interoperability of payment systems across member nations. It further noted India will ‌push for progress on linking digital currencies across BRICS countries.

## **BRICS-Africa Transiting from Diplomacy to Strategic Economy**

South Africa (2010), Ethiopia and Egypt (2024), as fully-fledged BRICS members, are seemingly changing policy which has always been strategic ambiguity, to a kind of assertive flexibility. South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt are positioning also as leading African voices for the Global South while, at the same time, maintaining relationships with competing Western powers. In principles, Africa generally collaborates with the United States and Asian-Pacific partners while striking, to a certain degree, multifaceted ties with Russia, and operates within framework of BRICS domain.

South African Cyril Ramaphosa, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, and President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi of Arab Republic of Egypt held separate conversations on the current status and future prospects for their relations, and further discussed ways of strengthening BRICS strategic partnership in politics and security, economics and finance, and cultural and humanitarian ties, while exchanging divergent views on current international and regional issues that are of common significance to the global development. South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt, however, plan to take new initiatives to improve and strengthen relations within BRICS.

The Asian economic architect is, strongly, being advocated for as BRICS new direction, and subsequently as non-Western dominated attention, according to the common statement by leaders of South Africa, Ethiopia and Egypt, while noting the significance of India’s role in hosting the 18th summit, and congratulated India for directing BRICS in shaping South-South alliance and the new economic order. As BRICS-African members, South Africa, Egypt and Ethiopia indicated high aspirations to build an alternative order to the West, wielding power to challenge Western hegemony. Now experiencing ‘reawakening’ from colonial yoke, Africa began throttling alternative pathways, and consistently signaling trade and investment that would serve the interests of the African member countries–largely focused on continental economic development, economic improvement and poverty alleviation.

## Zimbabwe: Cabinet Approves U.S.$650 Million Kariba Floating Solar Project As Gwanda Plant Remains Stalled

14 October 2026

[New Zimbabwe (London)](http://newzimbabwe.com/ "Visit New Zimbabwe (London)")

CABINET has approved the implementation of a US$650 million floating solar power project on Lake Kariba, despite lingering concerns over the stalled Gwanda Solar Project, which was awarded to late businessman Wicknell Chivayo's company, Intratrek Zimbabwe.

The latest initiative comes amid questions over the lack of progress on the Gwanda project, which was approved in 2015 as a 100-megawatt solar power plant intended to help ease Zimbabwe's electricity shortages.

The tender was awarded to Chivayo and his engineering firm, Intratrek Zimbabwe. In April 2016, the Zimbabwe Power Company paid the company US$5 million upfront, but more than a decade after the project was approved, no meaningful progress has been made at the site.

With no clear steps to recover the upfront payment or compel Intratek to deliver, cabinet has now announced plans to implement another major solar power project.

Details of the Lake Kariba initiative were presented by Agriculture, Mechanisation and Water Resources Minister Dr Anxious Masuka during a post-Cabinet briefing.

"The Nation is informed that in December 2023, His Excellency the President Cde E.D. Mnangagwa, directed relevant Government Ministries to facilitate private sector investment for a 600 MW Floating Solar Power Plant on Lake Kariba.

"The Project was intended to augment hydropower generation in the country, stabilize power output, preserve water during the day through solar generation, and to enhance climate resilience and long-term sustainability of the Kariba power generation system," he said.

Masuka said the project is valued at US$650 million and will be implemented through a partnership between the Zimbabwe Electricity Transmission and Distribution Company (ZETDC), which will be the sole off-taker of the electricity generated, and GreenGrid Energy Private Limited, formerly known as Sunspire, as the developer.

"At full capacity, the plant is expected to provide power for 3 million people and create 1,000 direct jobs in Kariba. Progress recorded to date includes the completion of grid and technical studies; land survey and environmental impact assessment processes; regulatory licensing; and the negotiation of the Project's commercial agreements," he said.

According to Masuka, the Power Purchase Agreement and Transmission Connection Agreements were signed in 2025, while technical, regulatory and preparatory work was completed in July 2026.

### 中共：一个自称文化自信的政权，为什么如此害怕几部电影？

[![Image 2](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhziMk8_sLWInAhvKjh8xJMyJOIB-etCotIXPLkTvglH-W2Bw9Y3QdfAcmIvFideZryXEuirXqWq0Ed4VZngohyD4zUTQ6HDFx4FeLTlOHC3UtUKPew43rAHTENcM8CIkMtGr7Vauf_hzayKM7wKrdti-NW2wKvlVnxdK9H1XWIR-P77ilFhLXxy024iSGU/w640-h591/image.png)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhziMk8_sLWInAhvKjh8xJMyJOIB-etCotIXPLkTvglH-W2Bw9Y3QdfAcmIvFideZryXEuirXqWq0Ed4VZngohyD4zUTQ6HDFx4FeLTlOHC3UtUKPew43rAHTENcM8CIkMtGr7Vauf_hzayKM7wKrdti-NW2wKvlVnxdK9H1XWIR-P77ilFhLXxy024iSGU/s1600/image.png)

🎬 **中共：一个自称文化自信的政权，为什么如此害怕几部电影？**

《活着》不让你看，《蓝风筝》不让你看，《天注定》不让你看，《颐和园》不让你看……

从历史创伤到社会现实，从底层苦难到个人命运，凡是可能让人产生疑问、重新思考历史的作品，都成为封禁的对象。

中共集团总说自己代表人民，却害怕人民了解真实的历史；总说制度充满优越性，却连一部电影、一段记忆、一种声音都容不下。

如果历史经得起检验，为什么害怕电影？如果制度经得起比较，为什么害怕真相？

最讽刺的是：电影可以被禁，导演可以被封杀，银幕可以被关闭，人们的记忆不会因为一道禁令就消失。

中共习惯把银幕当成敌人，把镜头当成威胁，把审查当成自信。

#电影审查 #言论自由 #历史不容遗忘 #中共审查

## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AI

China’s state-run refiners are set for a months-long effort to replenish oil stockpiles, according to Eurasia Group, after tapping reserves to cushion the impact of elevated prices stemming from the [US-Iran](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-12/saudi-airport-carnage-pressures-trump-to-boost-us-role-in-yemen) war.

Processors are expected to add 400,000 barrels a day to their oil inventories between November and April, according to an Oct. 13 note from the consultancy. Since April, Beijing has centralized crude inventory management and extended the mandatory period required for refiners to replenish stockpiles to three to five months from one to two months, Eurasia said.

content: 作者臉書  2026-10-13 我们究竟应该怎样纪念老万？ 10月13日是万润南先生逝世一周年，海外的民运同仁们都在追思万润南先生，缅怀他的历史功绩，颂扬他为中国民主事业做出的伟大贡献。 为此我在想一个问题：我们究竟应该怎样纪念老万？我们纪念老万的目的究竟是为了什么？就像我们究竟应该怎样纪念六四？我们纪念六四的目的究竟是为了什么一样，难道仅仅是为了缅怀？为了追思？为了永远不能忘记？！ 本人没有见过老万，只是在媒体上看到过老万的事迹，知道老万是一位杰出的民营企业家，在六四学生运动中公开支持爱国学生，被迫流亡海外后，投入中国民主运动，是民主中国阵线的主要创始人。 我看过老万写的一些文章，特别是他对中共历史的经典概括： “以革命的名义殺人；以共产的名义抢劫；以改革的名义分赃；以维稳的名义封口。”及“从党天下到民天下起码还要一百年” 的论断，都给我留下了深刻的印象。 老万是一位成功的民营企业家，是一代民运领袖，也是一位民主思想家，晚年老万在接受媒体采访时所表达的： “纵然海外民运暗淡，回国亦是自取其辱“ ，这句话不仅反映出老万的个人风骨，也折射出老万晚年内心对现实的心境。 如今老万离开了我们，九泉之下老万的在天之灵希望看到的究竟是什么？究竟期盼的是什么？难道是我们年复一年的对他的追思？还是在他每年逝世的日子一群白发苍苍的民运大佬对他的深情缅怀？！ 以我在网上看到和了解到的老万，我敢断言这绝对不是老万在天之灵所希望看到的，我相信老万的在天之灵最想看到、最期盼的的是：中国民主事业的蓬勃发展、是中共政权的早日垮台、是中国大陆早日向台湾的中华民国一样成为一个现代民主社会，是中国民主运动实实在在的努力和奋斗，而不是年复一年泛泛的追思和缅怀。 看看目前的海外民运乱象丛生，搞了近半个世纪，即制定不出明确的政治路线，也无法形成主流团队，映入社会眼帘的都是万年主席、政庇党、反共表演闹剧、是社会公众对此表现出的不屑，是国内同仁的深深的痛惜；海外民运的这种现状如果不能得到彻底改变、民运的乱象不能彻底根除，任何对先烈的追思都失去了实际的意义，都无法真正告慰逝者的亡灵！ 海外民运伴随着这种乱像已经走过了快半个世纪，伴随着这种乱象纪念了37年六四英烈，难道今后还要这样继续下去，再伴随这种乱象纪念老万37年？呜呼哀哉！ 本人真心希望大家能够将今天对老万的追思和缅怀，转化为动力和力量，改变民运现状，让世人在我们身上重新看到未来中国的希望！ 愿老万的在天之灵能够安息！ 吕洪来 2026年10月13日星期二

title: 从两岸权贵后代的择业轨迹看制度的本质

content: 2026-10-14   历程历程的博客 一次在台北乘坐出租车的经历，让我产生了一连串联想。 司机是一位体型丰满心宽口快的女性，当得知我来自大陆，便热情地聊起家常。聊到兴高之处，她半开玩笑地表达了对大陆 “ 红色家族 ” 权力继承与利益代代相传的 “ 羡慕 ” 。她说，她的父亲是台湾国民政府国防部的退休将军，按常理也属高官门第，可他的官位和人脉却没能对后代有所荫庇。 “ 你看我， ” 她拍了拍方向盘，笑着说， “ 都快当奶奶了，天天还得出来拉客，一天不出车，一天就没进项。好累好烦呐。 ” 她说，在台湾，像她这样的 “ 官二代 ” 随处可见，境况都与她类似。如果没有在社会上立足的一技之长，无论父辈官阶多高，家人和后代就只能像普通人一样，不介意从事最底层的工作去挣生活。 我当时顺口恭维了一句： “ 好啊，这恰恰说明你们的体制清廉、公平；你们的官员在职务上是“为人民服务”的，公私分明，所以后代沾不上光。 ” 这几句对话虽然简单，现在回想起来，却如同一把精细的手术刀，切开了海峡两岸看似同源同种、实则方向截然不同的文明走向和社会运行肌理。 两岸共用同样的汉字、同享儒家传统，然而在面对 “ 权贵的后代如何生存 ” 这一经典而世俗的命题时，两岸的 “ 二代 ” 们却演绎出了截然相反的人生剧本。而这一张张个人职业选择的清单，恰恰是各自社会制度本质的最清晰注脚和表达。 在大陆，人们不难发现一个极显著的现象：在那些需要漫长的时间沉淀、踏实的知识积累以及回报高度不确定的专业领域 —— 比如甘于清苦的基础科学研究、需数十年临床实践的内外科大夫、扎根各类现场的工程技术专家、辛勤耕耘的教师职业等等 —— 红色家族的后代几乎集体 “ 缺席 ” 了。 尽管他们中的绝大多数，从小就占有全社会最顶级的教育资源，拥有随时前往欧美名校留学的通道，但他们在面对人生职业选择时，却展现出一种高度一致的 “ 无师自通 ” 、“家族共识”、“所见略同”、“心有灵犀”、“都不能少”的殊途同归现象：他们极少选择去当科学家、工程师、医生、教师，而是争先恐后扎堆地挤进政界、国有金融运作、资本市场、能源专营以及大型国企的重组与并购环节的领导高层。 这并非因为他们天生缺乏做科学教育工作的智力和能力、天生具有各路领袖人物的资质、天生是资本运作和敛财的高手，而是一种在不受监督的特权体制下，通过理性决策、优化关系、精心算计后的选择。 在一个政治权力高度集中、公有制与行政许可主导核心经济要素的系统里，权力就是最高效的 “ 万能钥匙 ” 。在这片土地上，一纸批文、一次政策风向的透露、一个专营牌照的颁发，其所能创造的财富溢价，远远超过了实验室里几十年的枯坐、工厂流水线上的技术革新、学校里的教书育人、医院里的救死扶伤。对于拥有天然政治信任与血缘人脉的阶层而言，将政治资本转化为金融资本，是最轻松、回报率最高、成本和风险最低的捷径。 结果，那些真正支撑国家科技进步、医疗健康、工业基础、教育等高付出职业，都留给了没有背景、只能靠卷学历和埋头拼搏的普通人子弟；而整个国家经济领域最快捷、利润最丰厚的 “ 咽喉要道 ” 与利益红利，被特权阶层及其代理人牢牢把持，一手遮天，肥水不流外人田。 这就构成了当代中国社会最荒谬的悖论： 官方的宣传上，高悬着 “ 为人民服务 ” 的宏大誓言，高唱着 “ 我党除了工人阶级和最广大人民群众的利益，没有自己特殊的利益 ” 、“我将无我，不负人民”、“不忘初心，牢记使命”；然而在现实的利益图谱中，红色后代们却用他们的脚和银行账户，对这些誓言和承诺作出了最辛辣最彻底的反讽。他们非但没有成为 “ 为人民服务 ” 的公仆，反而借由父辈打下的 “ 江山 ” ，把国家资源与公共红利私有化、家族化、圈子化。在 “ 守江山 ” 的旗号下，他们顺理成章地将权力的延续等同于国家民族利益的需要，将本属于全社会的公有制资产，变相转化为特权阶层 “ 内部循环 ” 的世袭领地。曾经承诺要 “ 消灭阶级压迫 ” 的革命前辈和他们的继承者，最终在制度缺乏有效监督的温床里，演变成了社会阶层固化最坚硬最顽固的绊脚石，成了凌驾于普通劳动者之上的特权阶层。 海峡另一端的台湾，则呈现了另一幅景象。 国民党在 1949 年前的大陆时期，也曾有过 “ 四大家族 ” 与官僚资本垄断的丑态。但随着台湾经历了解严、竞争性民主的洗礼以及军队国家化与法治建设的推进，曾经的 “ 外省权贵 ” 与 “ 蓝二代 ” 们，被强行剥离了依附于政权的特殊照顾。在公开透明的选举政治与舆论的 “ 放大镜 ” 下，父辈的光环不仅不再是后代的避风港，反而成为了被反对党和选民严厉审视的 “ 政治负债 ” 。当国家资源无法再被私人家族随意划拨，当公权力的寻租空间被严密的法治与监管死死封堵，昔日高官的后代们便失去了 “ 不劳而获 ” 的制度土壤。 于是，我们看到了 “ 蓝二代 ” 们的集体正常化：他们必须通过自身的努力去打拼，大量转化为留美博士、大学教授、工程师、医师、律师、跨国公司高管，乃至像那位女司机一样，在缺乏专业技能时，坦然退回普通劳动者的队列，靠双手诚实地换取生活。这种 “ 正常化 ” ，是文明社会的标志。它意味着，权力只是一时的职务，而非可以世代承袭的封地；财富必须来源于市场上的服务与创造，而非血统带来的寄生特权。 两岸权贵后代的择业取向，是一面照出体制清浊的镜子，也预示着两种制度不同的未来。 一个健康的社会，不需要“血脉”和 “ 基因 ” 神话（无论是“红”还是“蓝”），人民也不可能永远忍受“血脉”和 “ 基因 ” 所赋予权贵后代的理所当然的“天然占有者”身份和由此产生的社会政治生态环境。 顺应现代文明，将权力关进法治与民主的笼子，让权贵家族剥离特权和利益、回归为靠本事和劳动吃饭的普通人，才是海峡两岸乃至整个中华民族走出阶层固化、实现长治久安与真正自由繁荣的唯一出路。 这方面，台湾，已经走到前面了。 而大陆，对自己的历史欠账，应该感到羞愧。

# Taiwanese, Korean firms eye Japan grid storage market with China locked out

Chinese battery suppliers' lack of cybersecurity certification creates opening

Taiwan's Cold Electric looks to expand production capacity ninefold for making power storage system. (Cold Electric)

MAO KAWANO

October 15, 2026 04:45 JST

Listen

English (Original)

[](https://twitter.com/share?text=Taiwanese%2C+Korean+firms+eye+Japan+grid+storage+market+with+China+locked+out&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fenergy%2Ftaiwanese-korean-firms-eye-japan-grid-storage-market-with-china-locked-out&via=NikkeiAsia)[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fenergy%2Ftaiwanese-korean-firms-eye-japan-grid-storage-market-with-china-locked-out)[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Taiwanese%2C+Korean+firms+eye+Japan+grid+storage+market+with+China+locked+out+https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fenergy%2Ftaiwanese-korean-firms-eye-japan-grid-storage-market-with-china-locked-out)[](https://t.me/share/url?text=Taiwanese%2C+Korean+firms+eye+Japan+grid+storage+market+with+China+locked+out&url=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fenergy%2Ftaiwanese-korean-firms-eye-japan-grid-storage-market-with-china-locked-out)[](mailto:?subject=Taiwanese%2C%20Korean%20firms%20eye%20Japan%20grid%20storage%20market%20with%20China%20locked%20out&body=https%3A%2F%2Fasia.nikkei.com%2Fbusiness%2Fenergy%2Ftaiwanese-korean-firms-eye-japan-grid-storage-market-with-china-locked-out)

TOKYO -- Taiwanese and South Korean battery suppliers look to make inroads in Japan's grid-scale energy storage market as Chinese rivals' lack of local certification provides an opening.

Cold Electric, a Taiwanese battery storage system manufacturer, plans to expand production capacity at its factories in Taiwan ninefold to 3 gigawatt-hours by 2028. The company is looking to expand sales in Japan, among other markets.

Cold Electric has not been able to compete with Chinese companies on price, so the fact that Chinese manufacturers have not obtained certification in Japan is one reason the company is focusing on the market, said CEO Phil Chen.

Advertisement

Starting next April, the Japanese government will require equipment connected to the power grid to obtain JC-STAR cybersecurity certification. For power storage facilities, this mandate will apply to equipment with communication functions, such as battery control systems and power conditioners.

JC-STAR reviews are conducted by the Innovation Platform Agency (IPA), an organization under Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry. For power storage system products, roughly 50 companies have obtained JC-STAR certifications, according to an IPA list. They include companies from Japan, the U.S., Germany, South Korea and Taiwan.

However, Chinese companies that have significant penetration in the Japanese market, such as Huawei Technologies, Sungrow and BYD, are not on the list.

The government has not said why Chinese companies appear locked out of certification, but national security concerns are believed to be an underlying factor. If Chinese suppliers are unable to receive certification, they will likely be forced to scale back in Japan.

Cold Electric obtained JC-STAR certification in August. There are plans to launch Japan's first energy storage facility using Cold Electric products by the end of the year. The company is partnering with Yuasa M&B, an Osaka-based battery distributor, to expand sales.

Samsung SDI obtained JC-STAR certification last year. The South Korean company plans to increase sales in Japan to 2 GWh by 2030. This marks a tenfold increase from the 2026 forecast. Samsung SDI looks to capture demand from customers switching from Chinese manufacturers.

Formosa Plastics Group, a Taiwanese conglomerate, plans to sell 3 GWh of battery storage annually in Japan by 2029. The group has applied for JC-STAR certification from the IPA and expects to be approved by the end of the year.

Formosa Plastics has petrochemical and materials operations within the group, enabling it to manufacture 70% of battery components, such as electrolytes and separators, in-house. The company is able to respond flexibly to customers' cost requirements.

Storage system users in the U.S. and Southeast Asia are shifting to avoid over relying on Chinese-made equipment, and Formosa Plastics plans to capitalize on that demand, said Clayton Lien, head of the group's Japanese subsidiary.

The company will expand facilities in Taiwan to quintuple production capacity to 10 GWh by 2029.

South Korean and Taiwanese suppliers believe their larger scales give them a price advantage over Japanese companies. While they cannot match prices of Chinese players, they can more easily offer lower prices than Japanese rivals, such as PowerX and GS Yuasa.

Samsung SDI batteries are "20-30% more expensive than Chinese manufacturers, but 20-30% less costly than Japanese manufacturers," said a company executive. The lower costs would be paired with cybersecurity certification, the executive added.

Home to the world's fifth-largest demand for electricity, Japan is rushing to install renewable energy capacity. The country is expected to have 100 GWh worth of operational capacity at power storage facilities by 2040, according to the Tokyo-based consultancy RTS, which would be nine times more than this year.

The scale would be equivalent to bringing online one or two nuclear power plants a year. Power demand is expected to expand further due to the buildup of artificial intelligence data centers.

JC-STAR certification does not apply to battery cells or other components that do not have communication functions. According to a construction company and a specialized trading house that do business with Chinese suppliers such as Huawei, Chinese manufacturers are exploring ways to sell battery storage systems in Japan without telecommunication components. The parts for communications would be outsourced to Japanese companies.

# Memory breakthrough by China's CXMT puts chip rivals on back foot

Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron trail Chinese rival on next-generation advance

Chinese company CXMT said it was "close to the leading edge of global memory production" when it unveiled a new high-capacity LPDDR5X chip in September. © Getty Images

KIM JAEWON, CISSY ZHOU, CHENG TING-FANG and YIFAN YU

SEOUL/HONG KONG/TAIPEI/SUNNYVALE, U.S. -- A breakthrough in next-generation memory chip design, announced by China's CXMT at the weekend, has sent shockwaves through markets and the semiconductor industry, although analysts and industry executives say its rivals have other ways to maintain their competitive edge.

ChangXin Memory Technologies' President Cao Kanyu told an industry conference that a key advance had been made in a next-generation memory cell architecture called 4F-squared, which would allow more cells on a same-sized chip than the existing 6F-squared structure.

The news that CXMT was achieving the next level of miniaturization and density ahead of the three leading players, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, sent their stocks sharply lower on Monday and Tuesday, as well as hitting shares of other tech companies and markets around the world.

Advertisement

It was another example of a Chinese company claiming a technological leap despite being denied access to the latest Western equipment and components by U.S. trade restrictions. In May, Huawei unveiled semiconductor and system design principles, dubbed the Tau Scaling Law, that use techniques beyond the traditional shrinking of transistor sizes to improve performance.

CXMT staged a blockbuster IPO on Shanghai's Star market in July, briefly becoming China's most valuable company. It is the fourth-largest DRAM chipmaker globally, growing to a 10% market share at the end of the second quarter, according to research firm Counterpoint. Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron had 38%, 25%, and 24% shares, respectively.

Some analysts said CXMT's advance was not a threat to its South Korean rivals as there were still more ways to improve productivity per wafer in memory chips rather than changing the structure.

"Korean companies have some easy methods they can use, and once those are exhausted, they'll have to start tackling the more difficult ones. But with CXMT, the U.S. has imposed restrictions preventing the sale of equipment, so there are no easy solutions," said CW Chung, a senior analyst at Nomura based in Hong Kong.

"Since there's no easy solution, the company is now resorting to stopgap measures, either multi-patterning or trying to adopt this 4F-squared technology a bit sooner."

A South Korean chip executive told Nikkei Asia that controlling how much heat a chip generates and how to dissipate it in a densely packed structure was one of the toughest challenges memory chipmakers need to solve for new architectures like 4F-squared and 3D DRAM.

"It is yet to be seen if CXMT can successfully ramp up production and solve the thermal issue in mass production," said the executive.

Dynamic random access memory chips, or DRAM, are critical components used in all kinds of electronic devices, from computers and smartphones to data center servers and cars. DRAM stores data in units called cells, and the area occupied by a single cell is denoted as F-squared. Most memory chips today use a 6F-squared structure, the terminology referring to how much space each cell occupies on a chip. The smaller the number, the more tightly packed the cells, allowing more memory storage.

Moving to 4F-squared would be the first such transition since the mid-2000s when the industry shifted from 8F-squared to adopt 6F-squared.

Both SK Hynix and Samsung have been working on 4F-squared chips, with the former revealing last year plans to transition to a 4F-squared vertical gate (VG) platform for its more advanced chips. Samsung has not officially revealed its strategy, but an industry source familiar with the matter said that the company was also developing 4F-squared. Local media reported that it was working on a 4F-squared structure paired with vertical channel transistors (VCT).

"If you think about how memory technology works, where ultimately you can get more bits per wafer area or more bits per dollar, accelerating those next generations of technologies is also very valuable," Tristan Holtam, group vice president and head of corporate strategy at Applied Materials, told Nikkei Asia.

He was speaking at the U.S. chip equipment supplier's unveiling on Monday of the $5 billion EPIC Center for research and development in Silicon Valley, where Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron will work with it to develop next-generation semiconductors.

"If we can pull forward 4F-squared, if we can pull forward 3D DRAM, that is also going to fulfill a lot of the market requirement," he said, adding that the EPIC Center would help chipmakers cut in half a 10-to-15-year chip design timeline.

Cao at CXMT told the industry conference that the core of CXMT's 4F-squared design was a proprietary transistor called vertical surrounded gate (VSG), which stands upright and wraps the electrical gate around the channel on all sides, giving the chip far greater control over the electrical current to prevent leakage.

The company also plans to launch a new high-performance server-grade RAM module, called DDR5 RDIMM, based on the technology before the end of this year. DDR5 RDIMM is designed for data centers and AI servers.

In September, CXMT also said it had achieved mass production of its fifth-generation DRAM technology platform, putting it "close to the leading edge of global memory production." The company also unveiled a new high-capacity LPDDR5X chip, designed primarily for mobile devices and laptops, built on the same platform.

LPDDR5 is now widely used in high-end smartphones, while DDR5 is commonly found in desktops, laptops and servers. # 薄熙來前搭檔受查：重慶政壇「不倒翁」黃奇帆是誰？

音頻加註文字，

**薄熙來前搭檔受查：重慶政壇「不倒翁」黃奇帆是誰？**

Published 2026年10月14日

中共中紀委在10月13日宣佈，74歲的黃奇帆涉嫌「嚴重違紀違法」，正接受紀律審查和監察調查。

黃奇帆的政途從上海走至重慶市，獲朱鎔基提攜參展浦東新區，大力提振重慶經濟，經濟政績亮眼。黃奇帆在薄熙來主政重慶期間任職市長，成為其緊密搭檔，然而歷經王立軍事件、薄熙來及孫政才兩任市委書記相繼落馬﹐惟他未受波及，被外界稱為重慶政壇「不倒翁」。

黃奇帆已退休九年，淡出政壇仍以學者身份高調評論經濟政策。他突然受查的消息，正值中共五中全會前夕，引發外界關注。

# 1,336 people officially recognized as Siraya since July: CIP

10/14/2026 04:04 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.

Siraya community members dancing at a ceremony, which marked the tribe's official recognition at the Executive Yuan in Taipei in July. CNA photo July 30, 2026

Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) A total of 1,336 people had completed registration as Indigenous Siraya people by the end of September, following the government's official recognition of the Siraya as Taiwan's 17th Indigenous group in July, the Council of Indigenous Peoples (CIP) said Wednesday.

Since the Plains Indigenous Peoples Status Act took effect in October 2025, the CIP has received applications for recognition from nine groups: the Siraya, Taivoan, Makatao, Taokas, Kaxabu, Pazeh, Papora, Babuza and Ketagalan.

The law, which was passed by the Legislature on Oct. 17, 2025, aims to give Plains Indigenous groups' the right to receive official recognition and maintain their collective identity.

According to the CIP's report to the Legislature on Wednesday, applications to be listed on the Siraya membership register and to register Indigenous status opened on Aug. 13.

By the end of September, 12,178 people had applied to be listed on the membership register, of whom 1,336 had completed registration and obtained officially recognized Plains Indigenous status as Siraya people, the CIP said.

Applications from the Pazeh, Kaxabu and Taokas are expected to proceed to review by a panel of experts and scholars, while a draft set of eligibility requirements for membership in the Taivoan group is expected to be released, the council said.

Premier Cho Jung-tai (back, center) and other officials poses for a group photo at the Executive Yuan in Taipei in July. CNA photo July 30, 2026

To qualify for Plains Indigenous status, applicants must provide supporting documentation. One important source is population census records from the Japanese colonial period, which identified their communities and defined the areas where they lived.

The Plains Indigenous people's movement for official recognition began in the 1990s. Before then, they were considered to have largely assimilated into the majority population under the Kuomintang government after it took power in 1945.

Before the Siraya's recognition, Taiwan officially recognized 16 Indigenous groups, generally classified as Mountain Indigenous.

(By Chang Hsiung-feng and Lee Hsin-Yin)

China’s producer [inflation](https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202610/t20261014_1965476.html "Link") swung higher last month, as escalating hostilities in the Middle East sent oil prices surging past $100 a barrel and goods related to AI became more expensive.

Prices at the factory gate exceeded most estimates and jumped 5% from a year earlier, reaching their fastest since 2022, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Wednesday.

title: Analysis: How long will China's top military body remain hollowed out?
zh_title: 分析：中国最高军事机构空心化还要持续多久？
source: 日本经济新闻（Google新闻聚合）
summary: _Katsuji Nakazawa 是日经新闻驻东京的高级职员和社论作家。他在中国担任记者七年，后来担任中国分社社长，并于 2014 年获得沃恩-上田国际记者奖。 中国人民解放军的神经中枢——对中国军事部署做出最终决定的地方——仍然是空心的。在军队内部进行了一系列大清洗后，监督解放军的最高军事机关中央军委已经没有可以指挥地面部队的军装军官了。形势象征
content:
_Katsuji Nakazawa 是日经新闻驻东京的高级职员和社论作家。他在中国担任记者七年，后来担任中国分社社长，并于 2014 年获得沃恩-上田国际记者奖。_

中国人民解放军的神经中枢——对中国军事部署做出最终决定的地方——仍然是空心的。

在军队内部进行了一系列大清洗后，监督解放军的最高军事机关中央军委已经没有可以指挥地面部队的军装军官了。

这种情况象征着中国国家主席习近平及其政府在准备本月晚些时候举行的一次重要党内会议时所面临的矛盾。

习近平还是中国共产党总书记、中央军委主席。中共二十届中央委员会第五次全体会议将于10月26日至29日在北京召开，会议的主题是“全面从严治党”。

2022年10月中国共产党第20次全国代表大会选举产生第20届中央委员会后，与解放军有关的矛盾逐渐暴露出来。自今年年初达到顶峰以来，这种情况没有改变。

9月21日，就在习近平访问美国并在白宫与唐纳德·特朗普总统举行会谈之前不久，宣布了一项重大决定。
公告称，中共中央政治局在当天的会议上决定，以“严重违纪违法”为由，给予张又侠、刘振立开除党籍和军籍处分。

张是中国人民解放军最高军官和中央军委副主席，刘是中央军委委员和中央军委联合参谋部参谋长。自共产党 2022 年全国代表大会以来，他们一直在习近平领导下监督解放军的行动，并自 1 月以来一直受到调查

罢免张和刘的决定预计将在即将举行的五中全会上正式批准。

最近的清洗使得中央军委只剩下两名委员，即习主席和去年升任的副主席张生民。 2022年共产党最后一次全国代表大会结束后，中央军委由七名委员组成。除张又侠和刘振里外，其他三名委员已被罢免。

张胜民是中央军委目前仅存的唯一一名军装军官，他的大部分职业生涯都在解放军的纪律检查和政治工作中度过。他不是军事行动专家。

中央军委现在没有人能够从专业角度为习近平的军事部署和其他行动决策提供建议。

那么，中央军委为何名存实亡呢？
究其原因，与解放军是共产党的军队，而不是担负保卫国家任务的国家军队有密切关系；解放军的首要任务是保护政党。

自2012年成为中国最高领导人以来，习近平多次强调“军队听党指挥”的口号。

解放军是共产党的军队，受党领导。事实上，解放军内部存在党委，这对于国家军队来说是不可想象的。

在中国，国家是党治国，而不是政府治国。

重要的是“坚持全面从严治党”的问题，这是这次全会的重要议题。

当习近平倡导“全面从严治党”

【原文 English Original】
_Katsuji Nakazawa is a Tokyo-based senior staff and editorial writer at Nikkei. He spent seven years in China as a correspondent and later as China bureau chief and was the 2014 recipient of the Vaughn-Ueda International Journalist prize._

The nerve center of the People's Liberation Army -- where final decisions on Chinese military deployments are made -- remains hollowed out.

After a sweeping series of purges within the military, the Central Military Commission, the top military organ that supervises the PLA, has no uniformed officer who can command troops on the ground.

The situation symbolizes the contradictions that face Chinese President Xi Jinping and his administration as they prepare for a key party meeting later this month.

Xi is also general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and chairman of the CMC. The Communist Party's 20th Central Committee will hold its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Oct. 26-29 under the theme of "full and rigorous Party self-governance."

The PLA-related contradictions have gradually come to light after the Communist Party's 20th national congress in October 2022, which elected the 20th Central Committee. The situation has not changed since peaking early this year.

On Sept. 21, shortly before Xi visited the U.S. for talks with President Donald Trump at the White House, a momentous decision was announced.

The Communist Party's elite Politburo decided at that day's meeting to expel Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the party and military for "serious discipline and law violations," according to the announcement.

Zhang was the PLA's top uniformed officer and CMC vice chairman, while Liu was a CMC member and chief of staff of the CMC's Joint Staff Department. They had overseen the PLA's operations under Xi since the Communist Party's 2022 national congress and had been under investigation since January

The decision to oust Zhang and Liu is expected to be formally approved at the upcoming fifth plenum.

The latest purges have left the CMC with only two members, Chairman Xi and Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin, who was promoted to the post last year. The CMC consisted of seven members immediately after the Communist Party's last national congress, in 2022. Besides Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, three others have since been ousted.

Zhang Shengmin, now the only remaining uniformed officer in the CMC, has spent much of his career in discipline inspection and political work within the PLA; he is not a military operations expert.

The CMC now has no one who can advise supreme leader Xi from a professional standpoint when he makes decisions on military deployments and other moves.

So how has the CMC come to exist in name only?

The reason is closely related to the PLA being the Communist Party's military, not a national army tasked with defending the state; the PLA's primary mission is to protect the political party.

Since becoming China's top leader in 2012, Xi has repeatedly stressed the slogan of "a military that follows the command of the Communist Party."

As the PLA is the military wing of the Communist Party, it is governed by the party. In fact, a party committee exists within the PLA, something unthinkable for a national army.

In China, the country is party-run, not government-run.

What is important here is the issue of "persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance," which is high on the agenda at the upcoming plenum.

When Xi advocates "full and rigorous Party self-governance," he also has the PLA, the party's military, in his sights.

While China has seen an unusual concentration of power in Xi's hands, a different logic also operates within the vast Communist Party.

The logic is that, no matter what, one-party rule must be maintained; the system should remain unshaken even when Xi is no longer in power.

The PLA shares this commitment to preserving one-party rule. In this regard, the PLA does not merely protect the top CMC official at the time but the party as a whole.

Since the Communist Party's 20th national congress in 2022, numerous senior military officials have been purged, falling to the Xi administration's signature anti-corruption campaign.

The purges reveal a major contradiction between Xi's policies and the mindset mainstream uniformed officers have maintained for many years.

The military purges, carried out under the banner of fighting corruption, are also testing the political loyalty of generals and other senior military officers: Are they loyal not only to the Communist Party but also to Xi himself?

In Beijing in March, Xi delivered a speech at a plenary meeting of delegates from the PLA and the People's Armed Police Force. It came during the annual session of the National People's Congress, China's parliament.

The keyword in that speech was _er xin_, a term meaning disloyalty but which literally translates as "two hearts." By using the term, Xi implied disloyal generals and other military officers remained in the PLA.

"There must be no place in the military for those who are disloyal to the Party," Xi warned, "and there must be no hiding place for corrupt elements."

Xi's remarks meant that those disloyal to the party -- to Xi himself, really -- are "corrupt elements" and subject to his fierce anti-corruption campaign.

This issue also relates to the interpretation of the CMC's "chairman responsibility system," designed to concentrate final authority on military actions in Xi's hands.

Numerous senior military officials, including those close to Xi, have been ensnared in the supreme leader's anti-corruption campaign and punished. The purges have also dealt Xi a political blow.

In August, China announced that senior military officer Zhong Shaojun had been stripped of his status as a deputy to the NPC. Zhong had long served as director of the CMC's General Office, managing practical work at the commission under Xi.

Xi had sent Zhong into the PLA's nerve center to gather information about the situation there, then had no choice but to discard his prized pawn.

The massive military purges are not merely part of Xi's corruption crackdown; they are key to his efforts to control the PLA. Their outcome could affect the atmosphere at the Communist Party's 21st national congress in 2027.

Xi is poised to bid for a fourth five-year term as party chief at the party event next autumn, and taking full control of the powerful military is crucial to this.

On Sept. 21, the Politburo decided to revise and submit to the fifth plenum a draft decision on strengthening the party's internal governance, according to state-run Xinhua News Agency.

The question now is how much longer the CMC will remain hollowed out. Will the fifth plenum make any personnel changes to resolve the contradiction regarding the military structure, including the CMC?

The purges have left few PLA officers who hold the highest rank of _shangjiang_, general or admiral, whom Xi trusts.

To return the CMC to its 2022 seven-member structure, five new appointments are needed. Defense minister Dong Jun is supposed to be a candidate. His disgraced predecessor, Li Shangfu, was also a CMC member.

Dong, an admiral, assumed the defense portfolio at the end of 2023 and is in charge of China's military diplomacy. He was not promoted to the CMC at the fourth plenum of the Communist Party's 20th Central Committee last October.

If the current military structure is largely functioning, with Xi wielding firm command authority and, in effect, issuing orders directly to the PLA's lower echelons, he has the option to leave the CMC as is until the party's national congress next year. Whether Xi chooses to rebuild the CMC or leave it hollowed out could reveal how thoroughly he has consolidated his personal control.

title: China September new bank loans jump more than expected on stimulus, seasonal boost
summary: BEIJING, Oct 14 (Reuters) - New bank lending in China rose more than expected in September, rebounding sharply from a weak August as policymakers stepped up targeted monetary support for the slowing economy. Chinese banks extended 1.08 tril
content:
BEIJING, Oct 14 (Reuters) - New bank lending in China rose more than expected in September, rebounding sharply from a weak August as policymakers stepped up targeted monetary support for the slowing economy.

Chinese banks extended 1.08 trillion yuan ($161.37 billion) in new loans in September, beating expectations and rising sharply from August's 60 billion yuan, according to Reuters calculations based on data from the People's Bank of China (PBOC) on Wednesday.

Analysts polled by Reuters had expected September new yuan loans would reach 975 billion yuan, compared with 1.29 trillion yuan a year earlier. Chinese lenders typically accelerate credit issuance toward quarter-end to meet internal targets.

The pickup in lending suggests Beijing's latest stimulus push may be gaining traction, but weak overall credit growth points to still-sluggish demand from households and businesses.

Investors are now looking to third-quarter GDP data for signs that the economy, weighed down by the property slump and weak consumer confidence, is beginning to stabilise.

"The improvement likely reflects the rollout of new policy financial instruments in September, which supported project investment and corporate funding demand," said Zhou Hao, chief economist at Guotai Junan International.

"Together with stronger trade data, the latest figures suggest that existing policy measures are having a positive effect on economic activity."

China's trade surplus widened more than expected in September as exports surged, keeping the country on track to surpass last year's record surplus and likely intensifying trade tensions with major partners.

Household loans, including mortgages, were flat in September after a contraction of 202.9 billion yuan in August, according to Reuters calculations. Corporate loans surged to 1.29 trillion yuan last month from 260 billion yuan in August.

The central bank does not provide monthly breakdowns. Reuters calculated the September figures based on the bank's January-September data, compared with the January-August figure.

Outstanding yuan loans rose 4.8% from a year earlier, a record low, and down from 4.9% in August, against analysts' expectations of 4.8%.

New loans issued by Chinese banks totalled 11.52 trillion yuan in the first nine months of this year, down from 14.75 trillion yuan in the same period last year.

PBOC OPTS FOR TARGETED EASING

In late September, the government unveiled measures to spur growth, including targeted rate cuts and mortgage subsidies. Fitch Ratings said the policy package should modestly improve credit transmission, but it is unlikely to materially lift broader credit demand or alter the property sector's weak trajectory.

Policymakers have pledged to step up policy support to help meet an annual target of 4.5% to 5%. GDP growth slowed in the second quarter to a 3-1/2-year low, as weak investment and household consumption overshadowed strength in manufacturing and exports.

China is set to release third-quarter GDP data on October 19.

Still, few analysts expect imminent cuts to policy rates or banks' reserve requirement ratios, as the PBOC appears to favour targeted easing measures over broad-based monetary stimulus.

"We doubt the weakness in broad credit will prompt further monetary easing, not least because the PBOC views much of it as structural," Capital Economics said in a note.

"But given the economy's high debt burden and growing financial strains in the corporate sector, we expect the PBOC to come under pressure to resume monetary easing next year, with 20bp of rate cuts in our forecast."

Broad M2 money supply in September expanded 7.2% from a year earlier, according to the central bank data, an 18-month low, and below analysts' forecast of 7.4% in a Reuters poll. M2 expanded 7.5% in August.

The narrower M1 money supply grew 3.2% year-on-year, compared with 4.1% in August.

Outstanding total social financing - a broad measure of credit and liquidity - rose 7.1% in September from a year earlier, down from 7.2% in August. Any acceleration in government bond issuance could boost such financing.

(Reporting by Kevin Yao and Shi Bu. Editing by Jacqueline Wong, Mark Potter, Alexandra Hudson)

_Copyright Reuters or USA Today via Reuters Connect_

# England launches campaign to create 10,000 foster care places — The Guardian

[Fedir Kryshtovskyi](https://ua.news/en/%D0%A4%D0%B5%D0%B4%D1%96%D1%80%20%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B8%D1%88%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%B2%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9) 14 October 2026 02:22

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fv-angliyi-zapuskaiut-kampaniiu-zi-stvorennia-10-tisiach-mists-u-priiomnikh-simiakh-the-guardian)

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fv-angliyi-zapuskaiut-kampaniiu-zi-stvorennia-10-tisiach-mists-u-priiomnikh-simiakh-the-guardian)

[](https://telegram.me/share/url?url=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fv-angliyi-zapuskaiut-kampaniiu-zi-stvorennia-10-tisiach-mists-u-priiomnikh-simiakh-the-guardian)

[](https://www.threads.net/intent/post?text=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fv-angliyi-zapuskaiut-kampaniiu-zi-stvorennia-10-tisiach-mists-u-priiomnikh-simiakh-the-guardian)

In England, the government is launching its first nationwide campaign to find foster carers, aiming to create 10,000 new foster care places by the end of the parliamentary term. The initiative is primarily aimed at people aged 30 to 49 and is intended to involve them in caring for children who need care.

As [The Guardian reports](https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/14/fostering-in-crisis-can-flexible-care-models-fix-englands-child-placement-shortfall), the number of households taking in children has fallen by 10% since 2021. More than a third of current foster carers are aged over 60.

## Flexible care formats

At the same time, the government will trial new models of foster care, including short-term placements and weekend fostering. Children’s Minister Josh MacAlister said such formats should make fostering more accessible to a wider range of people, including through intergenerational or part-time care.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel [Telegram](https://telegram.me/uanewsstream).

According to him, without a rapid and substantial expansion of the system, children who could live in a family environment will remain in residential care facilities or live far from the places where they grew up.

## Carer shortage and financial pressure

Foster care is the main form of care for children in state care in England. Of the 81,770 such children, around 56,400 are living with foster families at any one time.

Research by the Coram Institute for Children found that more than half a million adults want to become foster carers, while around 3.4 million are interested in the possibility. At the same time, care-sector organisations stress not only the recruitment of new people but also the retention of current carers. Reasons cited for their departure include feeling undervalued, problems in interactions with social workers and financial pressure. According to the Fostering Network, only 33% of carers believe that payments fully cover the costs of raising a child.

# China and Pakistan launch first-ever joint army drills — Anadolu Agency

[UA.NEWS](https://ua.news/en/UA.NEWS) 14 October 2026 22:08

[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fkitai-i-pakistan-upershe-pochali-spilni-armiiski-navchannia-anadolu-agency)

[](https://telegram.me/share/url?url=https%3A%2F%2Fua.news%2Fen%2Fworld%2Fkitai-i-pakistan-upershe-pochali-spilni-armiiski-navchannia-anadolu-agency)

China and Pakistan on October 14 launched their first-ever joint ground forces exercise, Karakoram 2026, in the northwest of China's Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. The opening ceremony was held at a training base in the city of Korla.

## Karakoram 2026 exercise

As [Anadolu Agency reports](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/china-pakistan-begin-first-ever-joint-army-training-exercise/4088986), China Military Bugle, the official media outlet of China's armed forces, announced the start of the exercise. During the event, representatives of the two sides exchanged experience in counterterrorism.

Pakistani military personnel also inspected some examples of Chinese weapons and equipment, the outlet noted.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel [Telegram](https://telegram.me/uanewsstream).

## Training in high-altitude terrain

The exercise focuses on joint counterterrorism operations in high-altitude areas. The program includes training in drone operation, searching for and engaging moving targets, as well as long-range sniper shooting.

In addition, participants will conduct joint command training and exercises involving personnel in practical scenarios. According to China Military Bugle, Karakoram 2026 is intended to deepen cooperation between the sides and enhance their interoperability in counterterrorism.

_This week’s edition of the briefing is a joint effort by our new Iran reporter Tara Rad, who is writing under a pseudonym, and me._

_Here’s what you need to know: Iran’s security chief has warned that U.S.-linked technology sites across the region would be destroyed if war resumes. More than 30 countries, led by the U.S. and U.K., condemned Iran’s covert plots abroad. At home, the execution of musician and mountaineer Ali Sina Mostafavi and the arrest of human-rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi show no easing of the post-protest crackdown. Police in southeast Iran face a run of deadly attacks, and economic strain is showing. Some doctors now earn more driving passengers than treating patients, and the government is widening food aid to about 40 million people._

_Find out more below, and share your thoughts, analysis and predictions with me at [ailves@mbn-news.com](mailto:ailves@mbn-news.com). If you were forwarded the MBN Iran Briefing, please_[_subscribe_](https://alhurra.com/en/newsletter)_._

**QUOTE OF THE WEEK**

> The pulse of the American economy in this region runs through our part of the world … If war breaks out, many of these cables, data centers, artificial intelligence facilities, and numerous other sites will be destroyed.

_—_ _Supreme National Security Council secretary_[_Mohsen Rezaei_](https://www.presstv.co.uk/Detail/2026/10/11/778085/Exclusive--Rezaei-says-%E2%80%98Powers-greater-than-US-tried-to-conquer-Iran,-but-ended-up-in-dustbin-of-history%E2%80%99)

**TOP OF THE NEWS**

**Iran’s Security Chief Puts $2 Trillion of U.S.-Linked Tech Assets on its Target List**

Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei [said](https://www.presstv.co.uk/Detail/2026/10/11/778085/Exclusive--Rezaei-says-%E2%80%98Powers-greater-than-US-tried-to-conquer-Iran,-but-ended-up-in-dustbin-of-history%E2%80%99) in a Press TV interview that if war resumes, Iran is ready to destroy what he said was more than $2 trillion in U.S.-linked technology assets in the region.

“Many of these cables, data centers, artificial intelligence facilities, and numerous other sites will be destroyed,” he said.

He also said that more than “30 million Iranians have registered in [the] ‘Janfada’ (Sacrifice for Iran) Campaign to take up arms in the event of U.S. aggression.” Iran has a population of over 90 million.

Speaking of Iranian threats on foreign targets, over 30 countries, including the U.S. and the U.K., signed a “[Joint Statement on Iran](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/joint-statement-on-iran-12-october)” that “condemn[s] in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners.” The statement notes “the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors” and mentions “the recent campaign of attacks across Europe targeting Jewish communities, Iranian journalists, and U.S. interests, claimed by Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI).”

This came after an alleged terrorist plot against an RAF base at the end of September, [previously covered](https://alhurra.com/en/42956) in this newsletter. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has [said](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjwyz59k5y75o): “There are strong indications that Iran played a part.”

The U.K. also [sanctioned](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/foreign-secretary-statement-on-iran-12-october) two Iranian nationals: the IRGC’s head of counterespionage operations and a man it calls the “facilitator” of a criminal network involved in several plots against Iranian dissidents.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry [rejected](https://fararu.com/fa/news/1009341/%D8%A8%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C%D9%87-%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA-%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AC%D9%87-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D9%88%D8%A7%DA%A9%D9%86%D8%B4-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D8%A7%D9%86%DA%AF%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%B3-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%D9%87-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%BE%D8%B1%DA%86%D9%85-%D8%AF%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%BA%DB%8C%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA) the allegations as an “ugly conspiracy to advance the anti-Iran campaign and evade accountability for Britain’s participation in the American-Zionist military aggression against the Iranian nation.”

_Executed Wednesday: Ali Sina Mostafavi, Photo:_[_Iran Human Rights_](https://iranhr.net/fa/articles/9114/)_._

**More Executions and Arrests**

On Wednesday, Iran [executed](https://www.radiofarda.com/a/iran-judiciary-alisina-mostafavi-protester-executed/33876276.html) Ali Sina Mostafavi, a 38-year-old musician and mountaineer who had climbed Mt. Everest. He’d been detained after the protests in January of this year. The [judiciary’s website](https://www.mizanonline.ir/fa/news/4923653/%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%AD-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%DA%A9%D8%B1%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%87-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%A2%D9%88%DB%8C%D8%AE%D8%AA%D9%87-%D8%B4%D8%AF-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C-%D8%B3%DB%8C%D9%86%D8%A7-%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B7%D9%81%D9%88%DB%8C-%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%D9%87-%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%86%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%B1%D8%B6%D8%A7-%D9%BE%D9%87%D9%84%D9%88%DB%8C-%D9%88-%D8%B1%DA%98%DB%8C%D9%85-%D8%B5%D9%87%DB%8C%D9%88%D9%86%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%AC%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%AC%D9%86%DA%AF-%D8%B1%D9%85%D8%B6%D8%A7%D9%86) called him “one of the armed elements of the American-Zionist enemy affiliated with the hated monarchist movement” and accused him of “communication with hostile media affiliated with the Zionist regime.”

The office of Reza Pahlavi, the exiled former crown prince of Iran, [posted](https://x.com/PahlaviComms/status/2110350868943880201) on X about his execution, describing Mostafavi as “a man full of life, with achievements, ambitions, and a future.”

In a separate development, a lawyer who went to court on Sunday to represent a client was himself [arrested](https://www.hra-news.org/2026/hranews/a-6dd984b1/).

Amirsalar Davoudi, a prominent Iranian human rights lawyer, was detained at the Revolutionary Court in Isfahan while representing Mahshad Kashani, who was imprisoned after the January protests. According to the head of the Isfahan judiciary, Davoudi was [charged](https://www.irna.ir/news/86291394/%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%88%D8%AF%DB%8C-%D9%88%DA%A9%DB%8C%D9%84-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%DA%AF%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%81%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%B1) with publishing false information online, incitement to violence intended to undermine national security, and propaganda against the system. The charges relate partly to [material](https://iranwire.com/en/news/158829-defense-lawyer-arrested-in-iran-after-publishing-wedding-audio-of-executed-prisoner/) he posted on Instagram.

One of those posts concerned his defendant Kashani and another detainee from the January protests named Alireza Sepahi. Davoudi had published an audio recording that he said documented the marriage of the two political prisoners shortly before Sepahi’s execution. Judicial authorities now dispute that account and describe the claim about the marriage ceremony as false. The [judiciary’s website](https://www.mizanonline.ir/fa/news/4923415/%D8%B9%D9%84%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B2%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%85%DB%8C%D8%B1%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%88%D8%AF%DB%8C-%D9%88%DA%A9%DB%8C%D9%84-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%DA%AF%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B1%DB%8C-%D8%AF%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%81%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86-%DA%86%D9%87-%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%AF) said that publishing the audio file “led to propaganda abuse by hostile media outlets.”

Sepahi was sentenced to death and later [executed](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/latest/iran-five-protesters-executed-in-one-week-after-torture-tainted-trials/) on Oct. 5.

Davoudi himself is no stranger to prison. He was arrested in 2018 after representing political prisoners and other defendants in sensitive cases and was originally sentenced to 30 years in prison and 111 lashes. His case has since gone through repeated reviews, retrials and appeals.

His latest arrest is not an isolated case.

On Oct. 8, the Human Rights Activists News Agency [reported](https://www.hra-news.org/2026/hranews/a-6eeb37ba/) that Bahareh Aghaei, another lawyer, had been sentenced to 20 years in prison by a Tehran revolutionary court. She was arrested following the January protests and remains in Qarchak Prison. Other human rights groups have said her case is linked to her support for the protests and families of people killed during them.

**Unrest on Iran’s Eastern Border**

A string of shootings, roadside bombs and security operations has put renewed focus on Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran’s southeastern province bordering Pakistan and Afghanistan.

On Oct. 5, gunmen attacked a police patrol on the road between Bampur and Iranshahr, [killing two officers](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/13/3714902) and wounding another, according to Iranian media. Three days later, another police officer was killed when armed men attacked a patrol near Nosratabad. The following day a police vehicle struck a roadside bomb near Zahedan, killing Nosrat Eftekhari, a deputy provincial police commander responsible for social and cultural affairs.

[Jaish al-Adl](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/13/3715187/%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D9%86%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%AC%DB%8C%D8%B4-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B8%D9%84%D9%85-%DA%86%DA%AF%D9%88%D9%86%D9%87-%D8%AE%D8%B4%D9%88%D9%86%D8%AA-%D8%B1%D8%A7-%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%AA-%D9%85%DB%8C-%DA%A9%D9%86%D8%AF), a Sunni Baluch militant group active in southeastern Iran, claimed responsibility for the first attack, according to Iranian media. Iranian authorities routinely describe it as a terrorist group. But the Iranian reporting does not establish that the same group carried out all three attacks.

The state’s response has been swift. The day after the first attack, the Intelligence Ministry’s provincial office said security forces had [dismantled](https://www.mehrnews.com/news/6952673/%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%B3%D9%87-%DA%A9%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%84%DB%8C%D8%A7%D8%AA%DB%8C-%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87-%D8%A8%D9%87-%DA%AF%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%87%DA%A9-%D9%87%D8%A7%DB%8C-%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B1%DB%8C%D8%B3%D8%AA-%D9%85%D9%86%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85) three armed cells, killing two people and arresting ten. The ministry alleged those detained had received military, bomb-making and assassination training outside Iran before entering the country.

On Sunday, authorities announced the arrest of three people in Chabahar and Dashtiari whom they linked to Jaish al-Adl. Officials said they had identified a safe house and seized weapons and ammunition.

A day later, the regime [executed Omar Dorostaran](https://www.tasnimnews.ir/fa/news/1405/07/20/3720921). Authorities described him as a key Jaish al-Adl operative who supplied weapons, safe houses and logistical support to attack teams. His case, however, was based on earlier attacks in Rask and Chabahar and predates this month’s violence.

by [Diego Almada Lopez](https://cryptobriefing.com/team/diego-almada-lopez/)

10 hours ago

Russia, Iran and China are using generative AI to push disinformation at American voters ahead of the US midterm elections, Bloomberg reported on October 14, 2026.

The midterms are scheduled for November 3, 2026. That leaves less than three weeks for platforms, AI companies and US officials to figure out how much of this content is out there, and who it is aimed at.

## Who is doing what

According to the research findings, all three governments’ affiliated networks have turned to mainstream generative AI products, including [OpenAI](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/openai/)’s ChatGPT and [Anthropic](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/anthropic/)’s Claude.

Intelligence assessments from US agencies and independent analysts indicate the goal is not a single knockout blow. Instead, the operations aim to widen political divides, chip away at public trust in the election process and inflame tensions that already exist.

**Russia** is the most visible actor. A Russian-linked network known as Matryoshka, also tracked as Operation Overload and Storm-1679, has been spreading AI-manipulated videos since early September 2026.

Its output includes deepfakes of celebrities criticizing Democratic figures. It has also produced fabricated news clips styled to look like they came from established outlets such as CNN.

**Iran** has taken a different partisan angle. Iran-associated networks have used AI-generated material to push anti-Republican messaging, and some of them have posed as US activists.

[Meta](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/meta/) took down some of those Iranian networks earlier in 2026.

**China** is working at volume. Chinese operations tracked under the names Spamouflage and Green Cicada consist of thousands of artificial accounts, with AI used to manage those accounts and amplify their narratives.

## The AI companies push back

OpenAI banned accounts tied to Russian and Iranian influence operations on October 8, 2026.

According to the research findings, OpenAI disrupted several Russian and Iranian campaigns that month. Those efforts involved inventing fake journalists and fake organizations, which were then used to spread misleading narratives.

Still, there are important limits on what is known. Investigators are still assessing the full scale of these operations and how directly they target the midterms specifically.

There is also a notable absence of evidence that any of these groups are trying to disrupt voting infrastructure directly. The threat, as currently understood, is to what voters believe, not to the machines that count their ballots.

## How we got here

The Kremlin has run social media disinformation campaigns since 2016 to sow chaos in American elections, the New York Times reported on September 18, 2026.

What has changed is the toolkit. In 2016, influence operations mostly relied on amplifying messages through social media. A decade later, generative AI lets operators produce content cheaply and run campaigns at a scale that would have been hard to staff before.

## What this means

OpenAI’s October bans show these companies can detect and remove bad actors. But detection after the fact means some content has already escaped into the wild.

Meta’s takedowns earlier in 2026 show enforcement is happening, yet the Chinese networks alone reportedly involve thousands of fake accounts.

According to the research findings, Washington has struggled to put comprehensive countermeasures in place against AI-enhanced tactics, and faces growing questions over whether it can keep pace with a threat that changes this quickly.

When a network fabricates clips designed to look like CNN, it borrows that outlet’s credibility.

What to watch next: whether more AI companies publish takedown reports, whether platforms announce additional network removals and whether US agencies release updated assessments before Election Day.

The other open question is whether investigators find any evidence of efforts aimed at election infrastructure itself. For now, the record points to a battle over perception rather than over polling places.

Stocks in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index were on course to lose more than $1 trillion in market value after a six-session decline of about 10%, Bloomberg reported on October 14.

The index fell 3.1% in Wednesday trading, putting it on track for its longest losing streak since May 2025. Higher interest-rate expectations, elevated valuations and the financing demands of AI infrastructure weighed on the sector.

More than half of the index’s members had fallen at least 10% over the six sessions. Arm dropped almost 20%, Applied Materials about 15% and Intel 11%. GlobalFoundries was the only constituent to gain during that period.
