title: What is the SIRA Act, and why does the US want to strengthen research security?
summary: The US House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has called on Congress to pass legislation aimed at preventing the alleged theft and misuse of American taxpayer-funded research by entities linked to [China.](https://www.f
content:
The US House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has called on Congress to pass legislation aimed at preventing the alleged theft and misuse of American taxpayer-funded research by entities linked to [China.](https://www.financialexpress.com/policy/economy/indias-exports-to-china-jump-40-yet-trade-deficit-widens-to-105-93-bn-in-january-sept/4361369/?ref=articlehyperlinking)

In a report titled ‘How to Stop China’s Theft of America’s Taxpayer-Funded Research’, committee chairman John Moolenaar, a Republican from Michigan, claims that the US needs stronger safeguards to protect research funded by the federal government.

The report calls for the passage of the Securing Innovation and Research from Adversaries (SIRA) Act, which seeks to establish consistent restrictions on federally funded research collaborations involving entities on US government restricted lists.

The report draws on congressional investigations, federal enforcement actions and inspector general findings. It also addresses concerns that stricter research security rules could affect academic freedom, slow scientific progress and increase the administrative burden on universities. Here is what the proposed legislation seeks to do and why it matters.

ALSO READ

## What is the SIRA Act?

The Securing Innovation and Research from Adversaries (SIRA) Act is proposed legislation aimed at protecting US-funded research from potential security risks linked to foreign entities.

The legislation would establish government-wide restrictions on federally funded research collaborations involving entities listed on [US government](https://www.financialexpress.com/market/global-markets/us-treasury-yields-could-stay-high-for-the-rest-of-the-decade-heres-what-economists-say/4359783/?ref=articlehyperlinking)restricted lists. These lists identify organisations or other entities that face restrictions because of concerns such as national security risks.

The main objective is to ensure that money provided by American taxpayers for scientific research does not support collaborations with entities that the US government has identified as security risks.

Federal funding supports research in areas such as science, [technology,](https://www.financialexpress.com/life/technology/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-claims-ai-is-insanely-profitable-as-he-courts-billionaire-families/4258255/?ref=articlehyperlinking)engineering and medicine. The proposed legislation seeks to ensure that such funding is used in ways that protect American research interests and national security.

The report argues that research security rules should be consistent across federal agencies rather than vary significantly depending on which agency provides the funding.

## Why has the US raised concerns about research security?

The committee’s report focuses on cases in which researchers allegedly failed to disclose foreign appointments, financial arrangements or participation in overseas talent recruitment programmes.

According to the committee, records examined by federal investigators include cases involving researchers who received compensation from institutions in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) without making the required disclosures to US research funding agencies.

The records also describe alleged conflicts of commitment. These arise when a researcher has obligations to multiple institutions that could affect the time, responsibilities or resources available for their federally funded work.

Another concern is the failure to disclose information about foreign employment and research affiliations. Federal funding agencies rely on such disclosures to assess potential conflicts of interest, overlapping commitments and national security risks.

ALSO READ

The committee argues that these issues require stronger oversight because some of the reported disclosure failures continued across several years, research grants and institutions.

The allegations in individual cases do not, by themselves, establish that every researcher with a foreign affiliation engaged in wrongdoing. The report uses the investigated cases to argue for more consistent disclosure requirements and safeguards.

## What does the committee want the law to change?

The report recommends several measures to strengthen the protection of federally funded research.

**Restrictions on certain research collaborations:**The SIRA Act would introduce consistent restrictions across the federal government on research collaborations involving entities on US government restricted lists. This would provide agencies with a common framework for determining which collaborations should not receive federal research funding.

**Stronger monitoring after grants are awarded:**The committee wants federal agencies to monitor research projects more closely even after funding has been approved. This could help identify changes in researchers’ affiliations, undisclosed financial arrangements or other concerns that emerge during a project’s duration.

**Consistent security standards across agencies:**The report calls for common research security standards across federal agencies. The aim is to reduce differences in how agencies handle disclosures, assess risks and oversee research grants.

**Incentives for universities:**The committee recommends incentives for universities that voluntarily introduce strong research security measures. These could encourage institutions to improve their disclosure procedures and internal checks.

**Stronger enforcement:** The report also calls for greater use of suspension and debarment powers when supported by investigative findings. These measures can restrict an individual or organisation from receiving federal funding or participating in government-funded programmes. Their use would depend on the relevant findings and applicable procedures.

## Why has the committee released more than 700 pages of records?

Alongside the report, the committee released more than 700 pages of previously non-public, unclassified investigative records related to cases examined by the National Science Foundation Office of Inspector General (NSF OIG).

The documents include investigative reports, recommendations on suspension and debarment, official correspondence, financial records, federal grant disclosures and material related to foreign employment and talent recruitment programmes.

According to the committee, the records show cases involving undisclosed foreign appointments, payments from Chinese institutions and failures to report information required by federal funding agencies.

The committee said making the documents public would allow researchers, universities, policymakers and taxpayers to examine the evidence behind its recommendations.

It also argued that repeated failures to disclose foreign affiliations or financial arrangements should not automatically be treated as minor paperwork mistakes. The committee believes such cases require closer scrutiny, particularly when they involve federally funded research.

The release of these records is intended to support the committee’s argument that existing oversight measures need to be strengthened.

How could the SIRA Act affect universities and researchers?

If enacted, the proposed legislation could require universities and researchers receiving federal funding to pay closer attention to their research partnerships and institutional affiliations.

Universities may need to strengthen procedures for checking whether research partners appear on government restricted lists. Researchers could also face closer scrutiny of their foreign appointments, financial support and other professional commitments.

Federal agencies would have a more consistent framework for determining which research collaborations are eligible for government funding. The proposed changes could also increase the responsibility of universities to identify and report potential risks.

The precise impact would depend on the final legislation, its implementation and the rules adopted by federal agencies.

The proposal does not mean that every research collaboration with a Chinese institution would automatically be prohibited. Its stated focus is on collaborations involving entities identified on US government restricted lists.

One of the concerns examined in the report is that tighter research security measures could restrict academic freedom and make international scientific cooperation more difficult.

Universities and researchers rely on international partnerships to exchange knowledge, conduct experiments and develop new technologies. Additional checks could increase administrative work and make some collaborations harder to establish or maintain.

The committee argues that these concerns do not outweigh the need to protect taxpayer-funded research. It maintains that universities should not be left solely responsible for addressing risks involving restricted entities.

The report also challenges the argument that existing university oversight is sufficient. It points to investigative records as evidence that disclosure failures can continue across multiple grants and institutions.

The debate, therefore, centres on how the US can protect sensitive research without unnecessarily limiting legitimate academic cooperation. The report presents the case for stronger safeguards, while the practical effects would depend on how the proposed rules are framed and enforced.

The report is a call for Congress to pass the SIRA Act. Its release does not mean that the proposed legislation has automatically become law.

Congress would need to take the necessary legislative steps before the proposal could establish binding requirements. Federal agencies would then need to implement any enacted provisions through their funding and oversight processes.

The committee has also recommended measures that extend beyond the proposed legislation, including closer monitoring of grants, common security standards and stronger enforcement when investigations support action.

The release of the investigative records is another part of the committee’s effort to build support for these changes by making the evidence behind its recommendations available for public examination.

title: South Korea Expands its Defense Ties Amid Great Power Competition and Uncertain Inter-Korean Relations
summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is seeking a greater role in international security and defense supply chains while also pursuing a more self-reliant defense posture. South Korea's expanding defense partnerships reflect a broader effor
content:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung is seeking a greater role in international security and defense supply chains while also pursuing a more self-reliant defense posture. South Korea's expanding defense partnerships reflect a broader effort to translate its growing defense-industrial capacity into political influence and reduce strategic vulnerabilities amid intensifying US-China competition. Yet as Lee advocates for “peaceful coexistence” with North Korea, Pyongyang's continued military development and deepening cooperation with Russia underscore the potential limits of this approach. Together, these trends create new opportunities for defense-industrial and security cooperation in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, but raise uncertainty about the Korean peninsula’s longer-term security environment.

#### **Seoul Navigates a Contested Security Environment**

Since taking office in June 2025, the Lee administration has sought to balance its relations with the US and China while deepening ties with middle powers to reduce its dependence on either country for security or economic stability. Although the US-South Korea alliance remains strong, with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth praising Seoul’s efforts to increase defense spending, the Trump administration’s more transactional approach to foreign policy has encouraged Seoul to diversify its strategic partnerships. That perception has been strengthened by Washington’s position that South Korea assumes primary responsibility for deterring North Korea, articulated in the 2026 National Defense Strategy, as well as President Trump's decision to scale back the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise in August.

Lee has also notably departed from the hardline approach to North Korea taken by his predecessor, Yoon Suk Yeol. At the UN General Assembly last month, Lee proposed a three-pillar policy to facilitate a “peaceful coexistence” with Pyongyang, advocating for renewed US-North Korea talks and suggesting sanctions relief in exchange for a freeze on Pyongyang's nuclear and ballistic missile programs.

So far, Seoul’s calls for renewed dialogue and engagement have had minimal impact on Pyongyang’s missile tests and military development. North Korea removed all references to reunification in its constitution and continues to reject calls for denuclearization, conducting ballistic missile tests and advancing its sea-based nuclear deterrent. Shaping Pyongyang's calculus are lingering tensions stemming from the Yoon administration, deteriorating relations with Japan, and expanding technical and military cooperation with Russia. The Kim regime likely views its partnership with Moscow as a major strategic advantage, reducing its incentive to participate in talks with the US or South Korea.

With engagement efforts toward North Korea yielding few tangible results and uncertainty surrounding US policy persisting, Seoul is building up its domestic capabilities. South Korea tested its first domestically produced hypersonic glide vehicles this month, marking a notable advancement in its missile capabilities. Seoul has also sought to accelerate the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the US-led Combined Forces Command to the South Korean military, a process that has spanned multiple presidencies, but the Lee administration has especially pushed for. However, US military officials, including the former commander of US Forces Korea, have cautioned that Seoul has not yet attained all military capabilities necessary to assume OPCON, particularly in missile defense and critical C5ISR capabilities (Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance).

#### **Deepening Defense Cooperation with Middle Powers**

In its pursuit of greater strategic autonomy and deterrence, the Lee administration has leveraged defense-industrial development to advance diplomatic objectives and strengthen global influence. Prior to Lee’s tenure, South Korea saw a substantial increase in arms exports along with initiatives aimed at strengthening defense-industrial capacity. These initiatives began following the Russia-Ukraine war and substantially deepened Seoul’s defense ties with Europe, which needed alternative suppliers to quickly replenish depleted stockpiles and to rapidly boost military capabilities. Amid intensifying US-China strategic competition, however, the Lee administration has increasingly framed these efforts as part of a broader hedging strategy. Pursuant to this strategy, the Lee administration has deepened ties with Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian middle powers to diversify its defense and economic relationships without diminishing its defense alliance with the US. Moreover, the Lee administration has expressed willingness to aid partners in building their domestic defense industries, presenting another avenue for Seoul to expand its influence.

Following a years-long trend of South Korean governments advancing security partnerships with Indo-Pacific nations, the Lee administration upgraded its special strategic partnership with Indonesia to a special comprehensive strategic partnership in April, South Korea’s highest level of bilateral ties short of a formal alliance. As part of this partnership, the two countries agreed to proceed with joint production of the KF-21 fighter jet, a program more than a decade in development, while expanding defense-industrial cooperation to include anti-tank guided missile systems and ammunition. The deal helps secure Seoul’s interests in Indonesia, including access to critical minerals and LNG, as South Korea's traditional energy suppliers in the Gulf have faced significant disruptions. More broadly, the move reflects Seoul's effort to strengthen partnerships with members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Seoul has also extended its footprint outside the Indo-Pacific. In the Middle East and North Africa, Seoul has expanded partnerships traditionally centered on energy to include arms exports, localized manufacturing, cybersecurity cooperation and other aspects of defense. In October 2026, South Korea upgraded its bilateral ties with Egypt to a strategic partnership, signing a memorandum of understanding on shipbuilding and broadening joint defense production beyond the manufacture of K-9 self-propelled howitzers, which began earlier this year. Egyptian officials also confirmed discussions over the potential sale of 36 FA-50 aircraft to Cairo. The Lee administration has pursued similar defense-industrial arrangements with the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

For Seoul, strategic defense partnerships with other middle powers enhance its credibility as a reliable defense cooperation partner and support its broader effort to reduce dependence on any single security partner. For its partners, particularly in the MENA region, acquiring South Korean systems that are compatible with Western platforms improves interoperability during joint exercises while reducing exposure to the political sensitivities and potential restrictions that can accompany purchases of Chinese defense equipment (although defense cooperation with Beijing is likely to continue).

#### **Implications for Businesses**

South Korea's push for joint defense production presents opportunities for firms involved in manufacturing, systems integration, logistics, workforce development, and lifecycle sustainment. Across partnerships with Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, Seoul has increasingly paired defense exports with technology-transfer arrangements, training, and long-term maintenance support. This approach aligns with regional efforts to develop indigenous defense industries and could generate demand for industrial infrastructure, engineering services, supply-chain integration, and advanced manufacturing capabilities. However, commercial opportunities will depend on whether political agreements and memorandums of understanding translate into funded procurement programs.

As South Korea's strategic partnership with Egypt expands to include shipbuilding and maritime cooperation, the security of the Suez Canal and Red Sea shipping routes will be of even greater importance for Seoul. Building on the Cheonghae Unit's long-standing anti-piracy mission in the Gulf of Aden, future cooperative frameworks with Cairo could focus on maritime domain awareness, technology transfers in unmanned systems, and the protection of critical infrastructure. Such initiatives would advance Seoul's interest in safeguarding the maritime corridors through which much of its trade and imported energy flow. Recent disruptions to regional shipping and energy markets have only heightened the importance of these routes for South Korea's economic security. Greater South Korean support in preserving freedom of navigation and regional capacity-building could help reduce insecurity and uncertainty for commercial vessels transiting the Bab el-Mandeb or Strait of Hormuz.

In addition to its growing security interests abroad, Seoul must also contend with evolving security challenges on the Korean peninsula. Obstacles to Lee’s peaceful coexistence policy could increase pressure on Seoul to demonstrate that its military can independently execute critical military capabilities as it works toward assuming OPCON. This, in turn, could shape South Korea’s procurement priorities, generating demand for technologies integral to enhancing C5ISR capabilities, including secure communications, command-and-control systems, AI, and unmanned platforms. However, specific procurement contracts will depend on military modernization priorities and the US and South Korea’s assessments of progress toward OPCON transfer requirements.

title: Promising outlook for Sino-Indian tech collaboration
summary: By Arunava Das in Kolkata and Xu Weiwei in Hong Kong | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-10-14 19:59 [![Image 1](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/image_e/2020/facebook.png)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?title=Promising%20outlook%20for%2
content:
By Arunava Das in Kolkata and Xu Weiwei in Hong Kong | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-10-14 19:59 [![Image 1](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/image_e/2020/facebook.png)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?title=Promising%20outlook%20for%20Sino-Indian%20tech%20collaboration&u=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/14/WS6acf6eb4e4b06d4aa0562d18.html "facebook")[![Image 2](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/image_e/2024/twitter.png)](https://twitter.com/share?text=Promising%20outlook%20for%20Sino-Indian%20tech%20collaboration&url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/14/WS6acf6eb4e4b06d4aa0562d18.html "twitter")[![Image 3](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/image_e/2020/linkedin.png)](http://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&title=Promising%20outlook%20for%20Sino-Indian%20tech%20collaboration&url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/14/WS6acf6eb4e4b06d4aa0562d18.html "linkedin")[![Image 4](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/image_e/2017/more_art.gif)](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/14/WS6acf6eb4e4b06d4aa0562d18.html "More")

Following the conclusion of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, observers see significant opportunity and potential in India-China technology collaboration, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI).

Even though competition remains in the technology area, both China and India have their respective advantages so there is also a powerful complementarity, the experts said.

"While India can contribute the software, talent, services and global application layer, China could contribute manufacturing, hardware, industrial deployment and AI engineering at scale," said Dipankar Chakrabarti, founder and managing director, BDSCube Technology Private Limited.

"The BRICS New Delhi Declaration explicitly supports AI cooperation," said Swaran Singh, a former professor of international relations at Jawaharlal Nehru University in Delhi, India.

AI, climate modelling, public health, disaster forecasting, agricultural innovation and affordable digital public infrastructure offer practical entry points for the two countries to work together in technology, the expert said.

Chakrabarti, who formerly was executive director and India leader for data control office at PwC, told China Daily that the most interesting signal from the BRICS Summit in New Delhi is that AI has moved from being a technology issue to being part of the geopolitical architecture of the Global South.

"The BRICS declaration explicitly calls for international cooperation on AI accessibility, safety, innovation and governance," he said. "India and China could cooperate on AI safety and governance. This is particularly plausible because both countries want greater representation for developing countries in global AI governance."

Debashis Sen, a former senior bureaucrat, told China Daily that the BRICS Summit serves as an invitation for countries to look beyond competition toward areas where cooperation could benefit all.

"AI and robotics are among the most promising. The New Delhi Declaration commits members to implementing the BRICS statement on the global governance of AI, and backs cooperation on Industry 4.0 and smart factories," Sen, former additional chief secretary of IT & E in West Bengal, said.

He added that China has become a major force in humanoid robots, while India offers scale, technical talent and a vast laboratory of real-world challenges such as elder care, traffic management, pedestrian safety and sanitation.

Sen, the founder of New Bengal Consulting Pvt Ltd (NBC), which works on AI adoption in the public sector, sees how much these matter for governance.

Chakrabarti said India and China possess capabilities across the entire stack, but they "don't necessarily need to share their most sensitive technologies to cooperate".

Sen also believed the two neighbors can have promising collaboration. "A focused dialogue on civilian AI and robotics among researchers, startups, industry and policymakers would be a sensible beginning. This would allow two neighbors to compete where necessary and cooperate where possible, so technology becomes a bridge rather than another arena of rivalry," he said.

title: Trade Compliance China: What To Know 2026
summary: ## How to Build a China Trade Compliance Program in 2026: Practical Steps for Foreign Manufacturers and Tech Companies Trade compliance china has moved from a back-office formality to a board-level priority for every foreign manufacturer an
content:
## How to Build a China Trade Compliance Program in 2026: Practical Steps for Foreign Manufacturers and Tech Companies

Trade compliance china has moved from a back-office formality to a board-level priority for every foreign manufacturer and technology company operating in or exporting from the People’s Republic. In 2026, intensified enforcement by customs and export-control authorities, alongside a maturing body of legislation covering export controls, sanctions countermeasures and foreign trade, means that an informal, ad hoc approach is no longer defensible. This guide sets out a jurisdiction-specific, executable playbook: governance, risk mapping, written policies, transactional controls, supplier due diligence, monitoring, audit readiness and incident response. It is written for in-house counsel, compliance officers and regional general managers who need concrete steps, checklists and templates rather than high-level commentary.

## Why trade compliance in China matters in 2026

The regulatory centre of gravity has shifted decisively. Since the Export Control Law took effect on 1 December 2020, China has built a national-security-driven export regime with broad triggers, a growing list of controlled items and a licensing structure that reaches dual-use goods, technologies and software. The Regulations on the Export Control of Dual-Use Items, which took effect on 1 December 2024, consolidated and clarified the licensing framework for dual-use items. The Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law, adopted in June 2021, added a countermeasures dimension that can place multinationals in the uncomfortable position of complying with one jurisdiction’s rules while risking exposure under another’s.

At the same time, the General Administration of Customs (GACC) has sharpened its anti-smuggling, valuation and classification enforcement, with audits becoming more data-driven and more frequent.

For boards and senior management, the consequences of weak trade compliance china controls are tangible: administrative fines, seizure of goods, revocation of licences, criminal exposure for serious violations, and reputational damage that can jeopardise market access and banking relationships. Multinationals are responding by formally documenting their trade compliance programs as part of corporate governance and enterprise risk management. A written, tested program is increasingly the baseline expectation of regulators, auditors, insurers and counterparties.

### Who must care, manufacturers, component suppliers and tech exporters

The obligation is not confined to defence contractors or large exporters. Foreign manufacturers assembling finished goods, suppliers of electronic components and semiconductors, SaaS and hardware companies transferring software or technical data across borders, and R&D operations sharing controlled know-how all fall within scope. The transfer of controlled technology to foreign nationals inside China, a concept comparable to the “deemed export” issue familiar from other regimes, is a particular blind spot for technology companies. Any enterprise that imports, exports, re-exports or handles controlled items, or that engages third parties who do, needs a structured approach to trade compliance china.

## Legal framework and regulators to monitor for trade compliance china

Building an effective program begins with an accurate map of the principal laws, the regulators that enforce them and the typical triggers that bring a transaction within scope. China’s framework is administered by several bodies whose remits overlap, and effective export control compliance china depends on understanding how they interact.

### Export Control Law and implementing measures

The Export Control Law is the cornerstone statute, establishing a unified system for controlling dual-use items, military items and other goods, technologies and services relevant to national security and interests. It introduces control lists, end-user and end-use certification, licensing requirements and a control-list and restricted-end-user mechanism. The practical triggers include the export of items on a control list, re-export of controlled items, and transfers of controlled technology, including intangible transfers by email, cloud access or in-person demonstration. Companies should treat the primary statutory text, available through the National People’s Congress portal, as the authoritative reference point and build their internal classification process around it. The administering authority for dual-use export licensing is the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM).

### Customs and GACC, classification, valuation and audits

GACC administers import and export declarations, tariff classification, customs valuation, origin determination and anti-smuggling enforcement. China customs compliance turns on the accuracy of declared classification codes, declared values and stated country of origin, together with the supporting documentation retained to substantiate each declaration. GACC conducts post-clearance audits that reconcile declarations against commercial, logistics and accounting records, and publishes guidance and notices through its official portal. Misclassification, undervaluation and incorrect origin claims are common audit findings and can trigger duty recovery, penalties and, in serious cases, smuggling liability.

### Sanctions and foreign countermeasures

The sanctions dimension of trade compliance china is twofold. First, companies must assess their exposure to extraterritorial sanctions imposed by other jurisdictions, which can affect banking, shipping and counterparty relationships. Second, the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law and related measures create a countermeasures regime under which Chinese authorities may list foreign entities and restrict dealings with them. MOFCOM maintains the Unreliable Entity List, while other relevant lists and guidance are published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MOFCOM. Sanctions compliance china therefore requires a dual lens: screening against foreign restricted-party lists while monitoring Chinese countermeasure lists, and documenting the rationale for any decision that sits between competing legal demands.

### Enforcement bodies and penalties

Enforcement is shared among customs authorities, public security organs and the administrative agencies that issue licences. Penalties range from administrative fines and confiscation of goods and illegal gains to suspension or revocation of export qualifications. For serious violations, particularly smuggling or unauthorised export of controlled items, criminal liability can attach to the enterprise and to responsible individuals, with cases heard through the courts and guided by judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People’s Court. A documented, good-faith compliance program can be a material factor in demonstrating that a violation was neither deliberate nor systemic.

### Regulatory watchlist

| Who to watch | What they publish | Suggested review cadence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GACC (Customs) | Classification rulings, valuation guidance, audit notices, anti-smuggling announcements | Weekly |
| MOFCOM | Export licensing notices, foreign trade measures, unreliable entity list updates | Weekly |
| NPC | Statutory amendments and new legislation | Monthly |
| MFA | Countermeasure lists and foreign-policy measures | Monthly |
| SPC | Guiding cases and judicial interpretations on trade offences | Quarterly |

## Step 1, Governance and program scope for an internal compliance program china

A credible program starts with ownership. Designate an executive sponsor, ideally at board or CEO level, who is accountable for the program’s existence and funding, and appoint a trade compliance officer with the authority and independence to halt non-compliant transactions. Define reporting lines so that the compliance officer can escalate directly to senior management without being filtered through the commercial teams whose transactions they review. An internal compliance program china should also articulate the organisation’s risk appetite in writing, so that decisions about marginal transactions are made against an agreed standard rather than case by case.

### Policy documents to adopt

*   **Trade compliance policy.** The overarching statement of commitment, scope and responsibilities.
*   **Export control procedure.** Classification, licensing and technology-transfer controls.
*   **Import and customs procedure.** Classification, valuation, origin and documentation retention.
*   **Sanctions and restricted-party screening policy.** Screening obligations and escalation of hits.
*   **Recordkeeping and data-transfer policy.** Retention periods and controls on cross-border data.
*   **Incident reporting and investigation policy.** Intake, escalation and self-reporting criteria.

### Resourcing and budget

Effective trade compliance china cannot be staffed on goodwill alone. Budget for a blend of internal legal and operations resource, a reliable licensed customs broker, screening-tool subscriptions and external counsel for complex licensing, enforcement response and periodic legal updates. The following RACI illustrates a workable allocation of responsibilities between central and local teams.

| Activity | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Classification of goods/technology | Trade compliance officer | Executive sponsor | R&D, external counsel | Commercial |
| Restricted-party screening | Compliance analyst | Trade compliance officer | Supply chain | Finance |
| Customs declarations | Customs broker | Logistics manager | Compliance officer | Finance |
| Incident escalation | Compliance officer | Executive sponsor | External counsel | Board |

## Step 2, Risk assessment and mapping

Before writing detailed procedures, map the transactions and business functions that actually trigger controls. The objective is to identify where export, re-export, controlled-technology-transfer, customs classification and import-from-restricted-party risks arise across the organisation, and to prioritise them by likelihood and impact. A risk assessment grounded in the company’s real transaction flows is far more useful than a generic template, and it directs limited resources to the exposures that matter.

### Workshop checklist and stakeholders

Run a structured risk workshop with cross-functional participation. The compliance function cannot see every exposure on its own; the detail lives with the teams that execute transactions.

*   **Commercial and sales.** Customer base, destination countries, end-use representations.
*   **Supply chain and procurement.** Supplier footprint, ownership structures, sourced components.
*   **R&D and engineering.** Controlled technology, foreign-national access, intangible transfers.
*   **IT and data.** Cloud access, cross-border data transfers, repository permissions.
*   **HR.** Nationality data relevant to controlled-technology-access analysis.

### Risk scoring matrix

Score each identified risk on probability and impact, then prioritise. A simple matrix keeps the exercise objective and defensible.

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Misclassification of exported items | High | High | Critical |
| Transfer of controlled technology to foreign nationals | Medium | High | High |
| Dealing with a listed counterparty | Low | High | High |
| Customs undervaluation | Medium | Medium | Medium |
| Incomplete record retention | High | Medium | High |

The deliverable from this step is a prioritised remediation plan, a top-ten list of near-term fixes with owners and deadlines. This plan becomes the engine of the first ninety days of program implementation.

## Step 3, Policies and procedures: the written program with a compliance checklist china

Policies translate risk assessment into repeatable action. A complete written progra

title: Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma reported to IEC for xenophobic smear on Rise candidate Aziz Ally
summary: March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, as well as Operation Dudula, the anti-migrant party contesting the local government election, have attacked Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg Ward 58 councillor candidate Aziz Ally because they thought
content:
March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, as well as Operation Dudula, the anti-migrant party contesting the local government election, have attacked Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg Ward 58 councillor candidate Aziz Ally because they thought he was Somali.

Ally is South African.

“We have submitted a complaint to the IEC as of today. We have not laid a criminal charge,” said Rise Mzansi’s Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni on Wednesday, 14 October.

March and March social media influencers and office-bearers have said that her arrest for “Islamophobia” is imminent, but it may relate to the IEC complaint by Rise instead.

Operation Dudula also earlier attacked a Somali community activist, who is documented and legally in South Africa, when they saw a photograph and a video of him putting up posters in the area, which is South Africa’s most migrant-rich, with 23 communities from different parts of the world calling it home. He was helping Ally.

An Operation Dudula social media post of a documented Somali community activist supporting Aziz Ally’s campaign. (Photo: Supplied / Facebook)

Both anti-migrant organisations unleashed a volley of lies about both men.Ngobese-Zuma said that foreigners were actively running for office and voting for each other to take over South Africa.

On 7 October, Operation Dudula entered this post on Facebook. It reads: “A Somali national is campaigning for the Rise Mzansi party. He says people must vote for Aziz Ally in Ward 58 to get a better life.”

Then Ngobese-Zuma followed, mistaking Ally for a Somali national too.

 Community activist Aziz Ally, right, on an inspection in Ward 58. (Photo: Supplied / Aziz Ally)

He is, in fact, South African and was born in KwaZulu-Natal. Ally is part of a group of dedicated Ward 58 community activists who are up night and day dealing with daily water and power cuts as well as regular fires, like [the one reported here](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-08-mayfair-fire/) by Jamie Ho.

Mayfair has regular fires and no water and electricity on most days. For years, Ally has documented and reported overcrowding, which leads to unsafe living conditions, as [Daily Maverick reported here](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-05-19-we-warned-you-joburg-ignored-years-of-alerts-before-four-mayfair-toddlers-died-in-fire/).

Ally decided to contest the election on 4 November to attempt to bring better governance to a ward long recognised as one of Johannesburg’s most troubled. People from across the African continent, as well as India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, have settled in Ward 58, in which, like Yeoville, Berea and Hillbrow, among other nodes, infrastructure has largely collapsed due to overcrowding.

March and March and Operation Dudula have tried to protest in the area, [but the tight-knit community](https://groundup.org.za/article/mayfair-immigrants-put-their-faith-in-south-africas-police-to-protect-them/) has kept a lid on violence and often sent agents provocateurs scurrying away.

Community activist Aziz Ally in action in Ward 58, Johannesburg. The councillor candidate does everything from reporting illegal scrap dealers to helping people to register complaints with the City about illegal planning and development. (Photo: Supplied / Aziz Ally)

Rise Mzansi has filed a complaint with the IEC over active disinformation and breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

It has brought a complaint against both Ngobese-Zuma and Thomas Mabaso, the host of “The 360 Experience with Thomas Mabaso” podcast, whom the party says amplified the disinformation.

The prohibited conduct included the reckless disregard for verifiable facts (Ally is South African; his Somalian activist aide is documented); fuelling hostility and xenophobia; and undermining electoral integrity by falsely claiming that the electoral system is allowing non-citizens to run as candidates.

Rise Mzansi has implored the IEC to investigate the posts and videos by Ngobese-Zuma and Mabaso; to direct their immediate takedown and correction; and to refer the matter for sanction under its Disinformation Code and the Municipal Electoral Act.

“She said ‘Aziz’ is not a South African name and that I must be Ethiopian or Somalian,” Ally told Daily Maverick.

He was scared after the attacks.

“I didn’t leave the house. It’s a diverse ward; you must unite people,” he said, explaining that he worked with all communities and regularly with the documented Somali migrant who was also attacked.

He said his friend was often part of community clean-ups and patrols.The Ward 58 community has its ups and downs, but it is largely united and offers a way of co-existing and partnership.

“I started campaigning in September, and all was going well. It really broke me. I don’t have motivation any more,” said Ally. **DM**

content:
**第四十篇：从初信者到成熟的神人——为着新耶路撒冷**

**——经历神完整的救恩，在神圣生命里长大、变化、模成并得荣，成为基督的身体、新妇，终极完成新耶路撒冷**

**壹、神拯救我们的最终目的，是完成祂永远的经纶**

以弗所书一章九至十节：「照着祂的喜悦，使我们知道祂意愿的奥秘；这喜悦是祂在自己里面预先定下的，为着时期满足时的经纶，要将万有，无论是在诸天之上的，或是在地上的，都在基督里归一于一个元首之下。」

以弗所书三章九节：「并将那历世历代隐藏在创造万有之神里的奥秘有何等的经纶，向众人照明。」

这两处经文告诉我们，神作事不是没有目的的。在创世以前，神已经有一个永远的心意，就是要把祂自己分赐到祂所拣选、所救赎的人里面，使他们得着祂的生命，成为祂团体的彰显。

因此，我们需要认识：神的救恩不是终点，乃是神永远经纶在我们身上实行的开始。

我们得救以后，不应当只满足于罪得赦免、将来得着永远的福分，更需要认识神今天要在我们里面作什么。祂要把基督作到我们里面，使我们在生命里长大，并与众圣徒同被建造，成为基督的身体。

**生活中的例子**

一个孩子出生以后，父母不会只满足于孩子已经出生，更盼望他健康长大，逐渐成熟。照样，神使我们重生，不是要我们永远停留在属灵婴孩的阶段，乃是要我们在祂的生命里长大成熟。

属灵应用：

我们每天都需要向主祷告：「主啊，不要让我只停留在得救的经历里，求你使我天天在你的生命里长大。」

**贰、神完整的救恩，包括法理的救赎与生机的拯救**

罗马书三章二十四节：「但因神的恩典，借着在基督耶稣里的救赎，就白白地得称义。」

罗马书五章十节：「因为我们作仇敌的时候，且借着神儿子的死得与神和好，既已和好，就更要在祂的生命里得救了。」

这两处经文给我们看见，神完整的救恩包含两个彼此相关的方面。

**一、法理的一面——解决我们在神面前的罪案**

因着人的堕落，我们有罪，亏缺神的荣耀，也落在神公义的审判之下。但主耶稣在十字架上，为我们的罪受死，满足神公义的要求。

借着祂的救赎，我们得蒙赦罪、称义，并与神和好。这是神救恩法理的一面。

**二、生机的一面——使我们在神圣生命里得救**

罗马书五章十节进一步告诉我们：「……就更要在祂的生命里得救了。」这说明，神不仅借着基督的死解决我们的罪，也要借着基督复活的生命，在我们里面继续作拯救的工作。

这生机的拯救，包括重生、圣别、更新、变化、模成与得荣等方面。

法理的救赎，使我们在神面前蒙悦纳；生机的拯救，使我们在神的生命里逐渐变化，成为祂所要得着的人。

**生活中的例子**

一个人原本背负债务，后来有人替他清偿了全部债务。这解决了他的法律责任。但他还需要学习新的生活方式，才能真正过一种不同的生活。这个例子只能帮助我们有限地理解：基督的救赎解决了我们在神面前的罪案，而神生命的工作还要继续改变我们这个人。

属灵应用：

我们不仅要感谢主赦免了我们的罪，也要天天向祂敞开，让祂的生命在我们里面运行。

**叁、重生是神圣生命的开始，使我们成为神的儿女**

约翰福音三章六节：「从肉体生的，就是肉体；从那灵生的，就是灵。」

彼得前书一章三节：「……借耶稣基督从死人中复活，重生了我们，使我们有活的盼望。」

这两处经文告诉我们，我们相信主耶稣以后，不仅罪得赦免，更是从神而生，得着神圣的生命。重生不是改善旧生命，乃是接受一个新的生命，就是神自己的生命。

从前，我们只有受造之人的生命。如今，我们因着相信基督，得着了神圣、永远的生命，成为神的儿女。这就是基督徒生命经历的起点。

**生活中的例子**

一位初信者得救以后，发现自己开始喜欢读圣经，也愿意祷告、亲近主。这不是因为他突然变得完全，乃是因为神圣生命已经在他里面开始运行。

属灵应用：

我们需要认识，自己里面已经有神圣的生命，并学习天天照着这个生命的感觉生活。

**肆、生命长大的秘诀，是天天吃主、喝主、享受主**

约翰福音六章五十七节：「活的父怎样差我来，我又因父活着，照样，那吃我的人，也要因我活着。」

约翰福音七章三十七至三十八节：「……人若渴了，可以到我这里来喝。信入我的人，就如经上所说，从他腹中要流出活水的江河来。」

这两处经文告诉我们，基督不仅是我们的救主，也是我们生命的粮和生命的水。

一个婴孩要长大，必须天天吃喝。照样，我们在神圣生命里长大，也需要天天接受基督作生命的供应。我们怎样吃主、喝主、享受主呢？

主要是借着呼求主名、祷告、读经、祷读主话，并在日常生活中与主交通。我们不应当把读经只当作增加知识，也不应当把祷告只当作向神求东西。读经和祷告最宝贵的意义，是使我们接触这位活的基督，接受祂作生命的供应。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄每天早晨用十分钟读经。读到「主是我的牧者」时，他就简单祷告：「主耶稣，你是我的牧者。今天求你牧养我、引导我，使我在工作和家庭生活中经历你。」这样，他不仅明白经文，也借着主的话享受基督。

属灵应用：

每天建立简单、稳定的晨兴生活，借着祷告和主的话接受生命供应。

**伍、生命的长大，带进圣别、更新与变化**

帖撒罗尼迦前书五章二十三节：「且愿和平的神，亲自全然圣别你们，又愿你们的灵、与魂、与身子得蒙保守，在我们主耶稣基督来临的时候，得以完全，无可指摘。」

罗马书十二章二节：「不要模仿这世代，反要借着心思的更新而变化……」

哥林多后书三章十八节：「但我们众人既然以没有帕子遮蔽的脸，好像镜子观看并返照主的荣光，就渐渐变化成为与祂同样的形像，从荣耀到荣耀，乃是从主灵变化成的。」

这三处经文给我们看见，神圣生命在我们里面运行，会带进圣别、更新和变化。

**一、圣别——使我们在性质上归神并被神浸透**

圣别不仅是外面分别出来，更是神圣别的性情在我们里面作工，使我们的生活逐渐符合神的性情。

**二、更新——使我们的心思逐渐被神改变**

从前，我们习惯凭天然的观念、喜好和判断生活。但神要借着祂的话和那灵的工作，更新我们的心思，使我们学习照着祂的心意生活。

**三、变化——使我们里面的所是逐渐改变**

变化不是外面的修饰，也不是单靠意志改善行为。变化乃是神圣生命在我们里面运行，使我们逐渐彰显基督的形像。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄过去遇到不顺心的事，很容易发脾气。信主以后，他学习在情绪激动时呼求主名，向主祷告。经过一段时间，他发现自己不再像从前那样急躁，而是逐渐有了忍耐和温柔。这就是神圣生命在他里面变化的实际经历。

属灵应用：

当我们发现自己的天然脾气、观念或习惯显露出来时，不只努力改正，更要转向主，让祂的生命在我们里面运行。

**陆、生命成熟，就是基督成形在我们里面**

加拉太书四章十九节：「我的孩子们，我为你们再受生产之苦，直等到基督成形在你们里面。」

歌罗西书一章二十八节：「我们宣扬祂，是用全般的智慧警戒各人，教导各人，好将各人在基督里成熟地献上。」

这两处经文告诉我们，神所要得着的，不只是已经得救的人，更是在基督里成熟的人。生命成熟，不是指一个人懂得许多圣经知识，也不是指他在召会中服事多年。真正的成熟，乃是基督在我们里面逐渐成形，使我们的思想、感情、意志和生活越来越受基督支配。一个生命成熟的人，不再凡事只顾自己的喜好，乃是学习让基督作生命、作人位。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄从前遇到意见不同的人，总想证明自己正确。经过多年的生命经历，他逐渐学习先来到主面前祷告，愿意听取别人的意见，也愿意放下自己的坚持。这不是因为他失去了判断能力，乃是因为他学习让基督在里面掌权。

属灵应用：

我们需要天天向主祷告：「主啊，求你在我里面更多成形，使我不再单凭自己活着，乃是让你在我里面活着。」

**柒、神生机救恩的目标，是使我们模成神长子的形像**

罗马书八章二十九节：「因为神所预知的人，祂也预定他们模成神儿子的形像，使祂儿子在许多弟兄中作长子。」

罗马书八章三十节：「祂所预定的人，又召他们来；所召来的人，又称他们为义；所称为义的人，又叫他们得荣耀。」

这两处经文告诉我们，神拯救我们的目标，是使我们模成祂儿子的形像。基督是神的独生子，也是复活里神的长子。神借着重生，使我们成为祂的众子。

然后，祂继续在我们里面作工，使我们在生命和性情上越来越像基督。最终，在主回来时，神要使我们的身体得赎、改变形状，与基督荣耀的身体同形。这就是得荣。

因此，神完整的救恩，从重生开始，经过生命的长大、圣别、更新、变化和模成，最终达到得荣。神要得着的，不只是蒙赦罪的人，乃是一班在生命和性情上彰显基督的众子。

**生活中的例子**

一个孩子随着生命长大，逐渐显出父亲某些相似的特征。照样，我们既从神而生，神也要借着祂生命的工作，使我们越来越彰显基督。当然，这并不是说我们会成为神格中的神，乃是说我们在神圣生命和性情上有分于神。

属灵应用：

不要只追求外面的成功或属灵表现，更要追求让基督在我们里面长大，使我们逐渐模成祂的形像。

**捌、神圣生命的长大，不是为着个人属灵，乃是为着基督身体的建造**

以弗所书四章十五至十六节：「惟在爱里持守着真实，我们就得以在一切事上长到祂，就是元首基督里面；本于祂，全身借着每一丰富供应的节，并借着每一部分依其度量而有的功用，得以联络在一起，并结合在一起，便叫身体渐渐长大，以致在爱里把自己建造起来。」

这两节经文告诉我们，生命的长大与基督身体的建造有直接关系。我们不是单独追求属灵的人，乃是基督身体上的肢体。一个肢体生命长大，就应当更能够供应其他肢体。

因此，正常的基督徒生活，需要有召会生活。我们需要参加聚会、彼此交通、彼此代祷，并学习传福音、牧养新人、成全圣徒和申言。这就是前面所认识的神命定之路——生、养、教、建。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄刚得救时，只愿意接受别人的帮助。后来，他逐渐在生命里长大，开始关心新人，并学习在聚会中分享主的话。这样，他不仅自己得着供应，也开始成为供应别人的肢体。

属灵应用：

衡量生命长大，不应当只看自己明白多少真理，也要看我们是否越来越爱弟兄姊妹，并愿意供应基督、建造身体。

**玖、神完整救恩的终极完成，就是我们成为新耶路撒冷**

启示录二十一章二节：「我又看见圣城新耶路撒冷由神那里从天而降，预备好了，就如新妇妆饰整齐，等候丈夫。」

启示录二十一章九至十节：

天使对约翰说：「你来，我要将新妇，就是羔羊的妻，指给你看。」

随后，天使将约翰带到高大的山上，把圣城耶路撒冷指给他看。这里给我们看见一个极其重要的启示：新耶路撒冷不仅被称为一座城，也被称为羔羊的妻，就是基督的新妇。

因此，新耶路撒冷不能仅仅按照物质建筑来理解。按照这异象的属灵意义，新耶路撒冷是经过过程并终极完成的三一神，与祂所救赎、重生、变化并荣化之人的永远联结与团体彰显。

**一、精金——表征父神神圣的性情**

启示录二十一章十八节说：「城是纯金的，如同明净的玻璃。」精金表征神圣的性情，说明这座城完全与神的性情相符。

**二、珍珠——表征基督借着死与复活所产生的生命结果**

启示录二十一章二十一节告诉我们，十二个门是十二颗珍珠。从属灵预表的角度看，珍珠指向基督借着死与复活，使我们得以进入神圣建造的经历。

**三、宝石——表征那灵变化的工作**

启示录二十一章十九节告诉我们，城墙的根基是用各样宝石装饰的。宝石表征蒙救赎的人经过神圣生命变化的工作，成为适合神建造的材料。

**四、生命水的河与生命树——表征三一神永远作生命供应**

启示录二十二章一至二节：约翰看见一道生命水的河，从神和羔羊的宝座流出来；河的两边有生命树，供应生命。

这给我们看见，新耶路撒冷不是一个缺少生命的外在建筑。整座城充满神圣生命的供应与流通。神自己是这座城的生命、内容、供应和荣耀。

因此，我们需要清楚认识：新耶路撒冷不是仅仅一个将来供我们进入的物质天堂，乃是神永远经纶的终极完成，是三一神与祂所救赎、变化并荣化之人的团体构成。我们今天在基督里重生、长大、变化，并在身体里被建造，就是有分于这个终极完成的过程。最终，我们要成为新耶路撒冷，作神与羔羊永远的团体彰显。

**拾、从初信者到成熟的神人，需要天天过神人的生活**

加拉太书二章二十节：「我已经与基督同钉十字架；现在活着的，不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着……」

腓立比书一章二十一节：「因为在我，活着就是基督，死了就有益处。」

这两处经文告诉我们，正常基督徒生活的中心，就是基督在我们里面活着。

神人生活不是指我们成为具有神格、可以接受敬拜的神。乃是指我们这些蒙神重生的人，借着神圣生命和那灵的供应，学习否认己、凭基督而活，在日常生活中彰显神的性情。

我们需要在家庭、工作、召会和人际关系中学习活基督。当我们面对困难时，学习祷告。当我们受到冒犯时，学习转向主。当我们遇到软弱的圣徒时，学习用基督的爱顾惜他们。当我们参加聚会时，学习供应基督，建造身体。这就是神人生活的实际实行。

**生活中的例子**

一位弟兄在家庭中遇到意见冲突。从前，他习惯坚持自己的想法。现在，他学习先向主祷告，求主使自己安静下来，并愿意听取家人的意见。这样的经历虽然平常，却是学习凭基督而活的实际操练。

属灵应用：

每天早晨向主祷告：「主耶稣，今天不要让我单凭自己活着，求你在我里面活，使我在一切事上彰显你。」

**拾壹、简短应用祷告**

「哦，主耶稣！感谢你拯救我、重生我，使我得着你的生命。主啊，不要让我停留在属灵婴孩的阶段，求你使我天天享受你，在生命里长大，经历圣别、更新、变化，并模成你的形像。也求你使我与众圣徒一同被建造，成为你的身体和新妇，最终成为新耶路撒冷，作你永远的彰显。阿们！」

title: IPAC报告促英国重整对华政策，建议效法美国国务院设立中国组

content:
伦敦 —

由全球多国议会跨党派议员组成的“对华政策跨国议会联盟”(IPAC)星期三(10月14日)公布报告，批评英国政府对中国欠缺了解，对华政策长期缺乏协调，建议仿照美国国务院设立跨部门“中国事务协调办公室”(Office of China Coordination)，简称“中国组”(China House)，并为涉及国家安全、人权及关键技术的对华交往划定明确红线。

这份报告获得来自英国多个政党的议员支持。作者埃文·福勒(Evan Fowler)接受美国之音采访时强调，报告中提到如何协调政策、提升对中国的知识理解以及明确与中国交往的界限，都是他所接触的英国对华交往人士的广泛诉求。

报告同时承认，英国无法与中国完全脱离接触。重点应在于，如何在交往的同时，避免让短期经济收益削弱长期安全和政策选择。

**报告获得英国跨党派支持**

报告列出的支持者包括工党财政委员会主席梅格·希利尔(Meg Hillier)、保守党影子外交大臣汤姆·图根哈特(Tom Tugendhat)、自由民主党外交事务发言人卡勒姆·米勒(Calum Miller)，以及改革党和苏格兰民族党的议员。值得注意的是，这些议员的背书并不等于英国议会通过报告内容，也不代表政府接受报告建议。

福勒对美国之音说，报告的一个重要意义，是其支持基础超出IPAC联盟本身。他提到的共同诉求包括设立“中国事务协调办公室”、提升对华政策能力，以及建立适用于不同层级英中交往的清晰战略和红线。

“我认为，这些观点获得了相当广泛的共识支持。”他说。

**借鉴美国“中国组”**

IPAC报告警告，在预算削减的情况下，英国正在流失中国问题专家，而政府各部门在对中国政策的执行也相互矛盾。

报告建议设立英国版“中国事务协调办公室”，协调并推动跨部门行动。它还主张将对中国的知识能力，扩展至政府、企业、大学和社会机构，而不只是增加中文培训。

美国的机构安排因此成为此次讨论的一个参照，但英国应当借鉴哪些经验、又应如何适应自身制度，仍是需要回答的问题。

曾任英国安全事务大臣的图根哈特在回答美国之音关于美国国务院“中国组”的提问时说：“我认为，我们在许多不同方面都可以相互学习。但事实上，这是双向的。”

他强调相互学习，而非单方面照搬美国做法。

报告提出的政策协调，也直接关系到英国与美国及欧洲伙伴如何应对中国带来的挑战。不过，设立协调机构本身能否改变决策，受访学者提出了保留意见。

**傅洛达：不是缺乏对华知识，是缺乏勇气**

诺丁汉大学中国问题学者傅洛达(Andreas Fulda)在报告发布前接受美国之音书面采访时说，历届英国政府已经多次听取有关北京所带来挑战的简报。

“问题不是缺乏关于中国的知识。问题是有知识，却没有勇气。”他说。他所指的是，即使采取更强硬立场会带来短期或中期代价，政府是否仍愿意维护民主价值和国家利益。

对于设立“中国组”，傅洛达认为，关键在于政治权力和领导责任，而非机构名称。在英国，这意味着首相府和财政部必须有高级政治领导人将中国事务作为重点，并推动政策落实。

“没有这种果断的政治领导，我担心‘中国事务协调办公室’不会带来很大改变。”他说。

伦敦国王学院治国方略与国家安全研究中心高级研究员索菲娅·加斯顿(Sophia Gaston)在回复美国之音采访问询时表示，英国过去十年的对华政策已从“深度天真”转向更加重视安全，但不同部门对中国挑战的理解仍不一致，妨碍形成有效战略。

她欢迎设立“中国事务协调办公室”，但警告，不应因此进一步把中国风险隔离成少数专家才处理的事务。

“英国真正需要的是，在政府最高层理解并落实对中国威胁的认识，让整个政府体系都在维护我们利益的共同目标下运作。”她说。

**交往的界限**

IPAC报告建议，在关键基础设施、军民两用及前沿技术、跨国镇压和研究合作等领域设立红线，同时继续在符合英国利益的领域开展有选择的接触。

加斯顿认为，判断合作是否安全，不能只看眼前收益，还应考虑一项服务、能力或投资是否会限制英国未来的地缘政治选择，以及英国能否承受合作中断。

英国政府也曾就对华关系进行审视。2025年6月，时任外相戴维·拉米（David Lammy）向议会表示，大部分细节涉及机密，无法在不损害国家利益的情况下公开。政府当时提出，在能够合作的领域合作，在必须应对挑战时采取行动，并加强公务员的中国知识和语言能力。

美国之音就报告涉及的批评向英国外交、联邦与发展事务部(FCDO)请求置评。截至发稿，尚未收到回复。

中新社台北10月14日电 台电董事长曾文生周三表示，台电计划在未来15年内建设43座变电站，以满足不断增长的电力需求。

Tseng 在台北能源台湾期间的一个论坛上表示，扩建还包括约 1,922 公里的新电线。他表示，半导体制造和人工智能 (AI) 不断增长的需求使得及时供电成为公用事业公司面临的主要挑战。

“我们需要在15年内建设43座变电站，平均每年约3座。这是前所未有的，”他说。

曾先生以台北松湖变电站项目为例，说明电网建设面临的困难。台电表示，经过26年的规划和行政程序，该项目于上个月破土动工，预计于2029年竣工。

他说，土地有限意味着传输距离更短，但基础设施也密集，使得新线路建设变得困难。

曾以南台湾科学园区不断增长的电力需求为例，说明了为什么需要额外的变电站。

电网规划还需要考虑人工智能设备从大型数据中心扩展到企业甚至家庭的情况。

他表示，此类设备可能会将晚间高峰需求转移到晚上 8 点至 10 点，促使台电调整负荷预测并评估旧城市电网的升级。
曾补充说，对于规划新设施的公司来说，按时获得电力已成为早期投资考虑因素，因为电力基础设施的建设时间可能比工厂更长。

他敦促大型数据中心建在发电厂附近，并表示较短的专用电力线可以减少建设时间、工程难度和成本。

曾先生随后对记者表示，台电正在与主要用户协调地点和投资时间表，并希望与致力于投资计算基础设施的公司直接合作。

他说，在确定实际投资者之前将供应能力分配给场地开发商可能会导致其他项目的可用能力减少。台电正在考虑制定公平规则来解决这个问题。

曾表示，该公用事业公司增长最快的人工智能相关电力需求目前来自制造业，包括芯片制造、存储芯片生产、包装和服务器生产，而不是计算服务提供商。

他补充说，这些行业的规划正在更早开始，包括在工业园区开发期间，以使电力基础设施与其扩张计划保持一致。

（赵彦祥摄）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) State-run Taiwan Power Co. (Taipower) plans to build 43 substations over the next 15 years to meet growing electricity demand, Chairman Tseng Wen-sheng (曾文生) said Wednesday.

The expansion also includes about 1,922 kilometers of new power lines, Tseng said at a forum during Energy Taiwan in Taipei. Growing demand from semiconductor manufacturing and artificial intelligence (AI) is making the timely delivery of electricity a key challenge for the utility, he said.

"We need to build 43 substations in 15 years, averaging about three a year. This is unprecedented," he said.

Tseng cited the Songhu substation project in Taipei as an example of the difficulties facing grid construction. According to Taipower, the project broke ground last month after 26 years of planning and administrative procedures and is scheduled for completion in 2029.

The limited availability of land means shorter transmission distances but also densely packed infrastructure that makes new lines difficult to build, he said.

Tseng cited growing power demand at the Southern Taiwan Science Park as an example of why additional substations were needed.

Grid planning will also need to take account of AI equipment spreading beyond large data centers to businesses and potentially homes.

Such equipment could shift evening peak demand toward 8-10 p.m., prompting Taipower to adjust its load forecasts and assess upgrades to older urban grids, he said.

For companies planning new facilities, access to electricity on schedule has become an early investment consideration because power infrastructure could take longer to build than factories, Tseng added.

He urged large data centers to locate near power plants, saying shorter dedicated power lines could reduce construction time, engineering difficulties and costs.

Speaking to reporters afterward, Tseng said Taipower is coordinating locations and investment schedules with major users and hopes to work directly with companies committed to investing in computing infrastructure.

Allocating supply capacity to a site developer before an actual investor is secured could leave less capacity available for other projects, he said. Taipower is considering fair rules to address that issue.

The utility's fastest-growing AI-related electricity demand currently comes from manufacturing, including chip fabrication, memory-chip production, packaging and server production, rather than computing service providers, Tseng said.

Planning with those industries is beginning earlier, including during industrial park development, to align electricity infrastructure with their expansion schedules, he added.

(By Chao Yen-hsiang)

Enditem/AW

# DEFENSE/Ex-U.S. national intelligence director praises Han Kuang reforms

10/14/2026 01:27 PM

Dennis Blair, director of national intelligence under former U.S. President Barack Obama. CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) Dennis Blair, director of national intelligence under former U.S. President Barack Obama, on Wednesday praised Taiwan's decision in recent years to transform its large-scale annual military exercises into a whole-of-society defense effort.

Speaking virtually at a security conference in Taipei, Blair told the audience that Taiwan's decision to transform the Han Kuang exercises from "a purely military one" into what he described as a "nation-defensive exercise" was a great decision.

By doing so, Taiwan would be "making sure that all of the capabilities of Taiwan are mobilized and brought to bear," said Blair, a former U.S. Navy admiral who commanded U.S. forces in the Pacific before retiring in 2002.

He argued that Taiwan's all-out effort to demonstrate its determination to defend itself would help convince like-minded countries and regional partners to come to its aid in an emergency.

"And of course, helping Taiwan is very much in the interests of all seafaring nations."

"After all, if Taiwan can be bullied into giving up parts of its sovereignty, then Japan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Korea, all of the countries of the world have to wonder, the region has to wonder about whether they are next," he said.

Two Clouded Leopard armored vehicles advance through the streets during a military exercise in the annual Han Kuang exercises. CNA photo Aug. 13, 2026

The annual Han Kuang exercises have served as Taiwan's primary war games since 1984, testing the country's combat readiness in the event of a possible Chinese invasion.

Originally involving only military personnel from all branches of the armed forces, the exercises have in recent years been expanded to incorporate whole-of-society defense resilience drills to promote active civil-military operations.

Blair also suggested in his address that Taipei should continue its efforts to monitor maritime activities and enforce laws in waters under its jurisdiction, as China continues to send civilian and government vessels into Taiwan's waters.

Beyond these monitoring and enforcement efforts, he argued that Taiwan needs an active campaign of diplomacy and public outreach, similar to what the Philippines has undertaken in its disputes and confrontations with China in the South China Sea.

"The objective is to convey the message that Chinese claims and operations are both illegal and inept. In order to win and retain world attention, Taiwanese public diplomacy needs to be inventive and fresh. Taiwan cannot allow China to establish a new normal in the international public perception."

Blair made the remarks remotely during the 2026 International Conference on Sea Lane Security, organized by Taiwan's Ocean Affairs Council.

At the opening of the one-day conference, Lii Wen (李問), deputy secretary-general of Taiwan's National Security Council, thanked like-minded partners for jointly voicing opposition to China's destabilizing actions in the East China Sea, Taiwan Strait and South China Sea.

He called for greater international and regional cooperation to strengthen early-warning capabilities and for international partners to maintain their maritime presence through measures such as freedom of navigation operations and regional cooperation to combat maritime crime.

(By Joseph Yeh)

title: Loaded for Bear: Why Minister Mantashe’s affection for coal is rooted in BEE, transformation
summary: Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe proudly wears his label, “Old King Coal”, and he boosts the fossil fuel every chance he gets. That has provoked a lot of understandable criticism from environmentalists, as the flames
content:
Mineral and Petroleum Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe proudly wears his label, “Old King Coal”, and he boosts the fossil fuel every chance he gets.

That has provoked a lot of understandable criticism from environmentalists, as the flames of climate change linked to the use of coal, oil and gas threaten to engulf our burning planet.

But what is often overlooked is that Mantashe’s affection for coal is in large part explained by one of his trademark political and policy priorities: transformation and raising the levels of Black ownership and management in the mining industry and the wider economy.

As such, it provides a revealing lens into African and non-African views of the green energy transition, economic development and the use of natural resources.

“Everybody in coal is a Black company, owned and managed by Black South Africans,” Mantashe said last week during his address to the Joburg Mining Indaba. “Today you find Exxaro, Seriti, Thungela and so forth. The old is dying and the new is emerging.”

That is indeed the case, with some caveats.

### Into the weeds

For example, Exxaro, which has coal as its core commodity but is diversifying into manganese, bauxite and copper, is 31.47% “Black empowered”, according to its latest annual report. And its C-suite is predominantly Black, with Ben Magara as its CEO.

Thungela is 67.55% Black owned, according to its latest compliance report to the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Commission and its executive team under CEO Moses Madondo is mostly Black. Unlisted Seriti is overwhelmingly Black owned and managed.

Viewing this transformed landscape, it is useful to recall that Thungela was demerged from Anglo American in 2021 against the backdrop of growing foreign investor aversion to coal because of the unfolding climate crisis.

Anglo’s removal of thermal coal from its portfolio was in response to investor pressure, including from the likes of the pension board for the Church of England.

The bottom line is that foreign capital has been ditching South African coal, and mostly Black, domestic investors have moved into this abandoned space.

This is surely a reflection of conflicting perceptions of the green energy transition, but the issue is seldom framed that way.

On one hand, the urgency of the climate crisis clearly calls for immediate action. The science is gin clear: the CO 2 emissions unleashed by the Industrial Revolution are accelerating climate change and warming our planet at an unprecedented pace.

In the latest flashing red light, this past September was the second-warmest on record and was the second consecutive month in 2026 that saw global temperatures exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

But historically, the majority of CO 2 that has been pumped into the atmosphere has been from the “Global North” or the industrialised economies of Europe and North America. China, India and Indonesia have become big-league members of this club in recent decades.

By contrast, Africa – the world’s poorest continent and the one where climate change will probably have its worst impacts – currently accounts for only about 4% of global emissions.

Viewed through this prism, the “case for coal” in Africa boils down to the perceived unfairness of the region being constrained from using its resource endowment in the same manner that gave rise to industrialisation and high-income levels in advanced economies.

### Rich vein

Mantashe is tapping a rich vein on this front and, politically, it speaks to a wide swathe of his base including the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM), which is staunchly opposed to shuttering South African coal operations for environmental reasons – a stance that is also clearly linked to its membership numbers.

South Africa’s ranking among global CO 2 emitters is 15th – largely because of Eskom and Sasol – but it is dwarfed by the big guys, and Africa as a whole is hardly responsible for our warming world.

Many investors up North may not want coal in their portfolios, but the backlash against the commodity is more muted here for historical reasons. The reluctance to invest in or provide financing for coal projects has been melting like a polar ice cap up North as well.

In 2021, when Anglo was answering the Church of England’s prayers and spinning off Thungela, the UN convened the Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA) – a move that captured the prevailing zeitgeist as a growing number of banks and fund managers were turning their backs on coal.

The NZBA ceased to function a year ago after a tsunami of banks left its shores, including heavyweights such as JPMorgan and Citigroup – and global coal demand reached a record high last year.

There is still a lot of hostility to coal from the finance sector outside Africa. Major European banks such as ING and BNP Paribas remain committed to rapidly reducing their exposure to coal. In South Africa, Nedbank is a leader in this regard.

But in the developing world, Mantashe is not an outlier, and his critics on this issue have often failed to grasp this point. In South Africa, the sector is clearly more “transformed” than most, which surely helps to explain Mantashe’s enthusiasm for it.

This does not mean that it should not be subjected to scrutiny and criticism. But context is important.

South Africa’s BBBEE policies are also widely seen as a deterrent to the foreign investment the economy desperately needs, given our low domestic savings rates, and that is a fair point. But with coal, foreign capital flowed out, and domestic Black investment flowed in.

It’s also the case that South Africa’s coal producers have embraced renewable energy projects. Seriti Green, for example, is focused on this sector.

Global distribution of coal exports in 2025.

For the record, I think the sooner we can dispense with coal, the better. But then, I still own and drive vehicles powered by internal combustion engines and don’t plan to trade them in for a horse and wagon anytime soon. My own lifestyle and standard of living are largely rooted in fossil fuels.

More broadly, this contested terrain over Africa’s resource wealth can be seen in other areas such as debates around the sustainable use and consumption of wildlife products and trophy hunting.

For example, the opposition to reopening the global trade in sustainably harvested rhino horn and trophy hunting in Africa is almost exclusively driven by affluent members of the middle and upper classes in the Global North.

But the scientific spoor of most peer-reviewed studies highlights the positive conservation and economic outcomes of regulated trophy hunting, which is pointedly sanctioned by democratically elected African governments such as Botswana’s and South Africa’s, and supported by rural Black communities that bear the brunt of living [alongside dangerous wildlife](https://conbio.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/con4.70080).

Like Mantashe’s stance on coal, this does not mean that such policies should not be subjected to scrutiny and criticism. But it’s important to keep in mind that what makes greens see red in the Global North does not always press African buttons the same way. **DM**

title: 穆勒纳尔促战争部扩大“1286清单”，限制与更多中国高校及实验室合作
summary: 美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。 穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-
content:
美国国会众议院美国与中共战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)呼吁美国战争部扩大一份涉及研究安全的管控清单，将更多被指与中国国防科研体系存在关联的高校、实验室、科研机构及人才引进计划纳入其中，以防止美国纳税人资助的科研成果被中国政府或军方利用。

穆勒纳尔星期三(10月14日)公布了写给战争部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)的[信函](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-calls-for-pentagon-to-update-its-list-of-pla-linked-institutions-and-talent-recruitment-programs)。他建议战争部在“第1286条清单”(Section 1286 List)中增加14家被特设委员会认定为中共“核心国防合作伙伴”的中国科学院下属研究所、62家实验室和国防实验室、58所大学、22项外国恶意人才引进计划，以及中国国家留学基金管理委员会(CSC)和获得该机构资助的研究人员。

穆勒纳尔说，扩大清单的目的是加强美国的研究安全，防止中国及其他外国对手利用战争部资助的科研成果。

**清单直接影响战争部研究经费**

“第1286条清单”依据2019财政年度《国防授权法》第1286条设立，用于识别美国政府认定对国家安全构成风险的外国科研机构、企业、个人和人才引进计划。

从2026财政年度开始，战争部不得为涉及清单内实体的基础研究项目提供资金。这项限制适用于研究拨款、合同及其他形式的资助，并禁止受资助机构与清单内实体共同开展研究或使用对方设备。研究人员如果与清单内机构的人员合作，也可能影响其获得联邦科研经费的资格。

战争部今年7月更新了清单，目前列有中国、俄罗斯和伊朗的130所高校和科研机构。战争部8月还要求30所美国高校审查其与外国机构的学术、资金和科研联系，并采取整改措施。

穆勒纳尔赞扬战争部近年来强化科研安全评估，并限制接受战争部资助的研究人员与美国政府管控清单上的机构合作。

“在这些努力中，战争部的‘第1286条清单’发挥着核心作用，”穆勒纳尔在信中说。“一个实体是否被列入清单，可能直接决定接受战争部资助的研究人员能否与该实体保持科研合作关系。”

他表示，随着列入清单产生的实际后果日益扩大，清单是否完整、准确也变得更加重要。

“这一框架能否发挥作用，不仅取决于对清单内实体施加的限制，也取决于战争部能否识别并认定符合相关标准的外国机构，”穆勒纳尔说。他警告，清单存在的覆盖缺口可能为接受战争部资助的研究人员和机构留下继续与中国相关组织合作的渠道。

**涉及军工、半导体、量子和人工智能**

穆勒纳尔说，特设委员会发现，一些尚未被列入清单的中国科研机构，与中国的国防科研和工业体系存在有记录的隶属、监管、协议或其他重要联系。

他要求战争部审查的机构包括中国科学院下属研究所，以及从事武器、航空航天、高超音速技术、半导体、水下系统、电子战等军事相关研究的实验室。名单还包括由中国国家国防科技工业局(SASTIND)共同管理或支持的高校。

人才引进计划部分则主要涉及量子技术和人工智能等关键及新兴技术领域。

穆勒纳尔说：“以下列出的几类机构尤其值得关注，因为它们与国防体系的关联已经得到美国政府或其他研究安全机构的记录和证实。”

据路透社报道，穆勒纳尔建议增加的58所高校包括清华大学。战争部目前尚未宣布是否接受他的建议；信中提到的机构也并未因为特设委员会的提名而自动受到限制。是否列入清单仍须由战争部依据相关法定标准进行认定。

近年来，美国国会和行政部门不断加强对外国政府参与美国科研项目的审查，重点包括隐瞒外国资金来源、参加外国人才计划、知识产权转移，以及敏感或军民两用技术可能流向外国军方等问题。

中国驻美使馆此前在回应战争部要求美国高校审查外国合作关系时，指责美方将国家安全概念泛化，并把正常的科学、教育和学术交流政治化。北京呼吁美国为两国学术与科研合作提供开放、公平和非歧视性的环境。这一表态并非针对穆勒纳尔最新信函作出。

**要求限制国家留学基金委受资助人员**

除了扩大机构名单，穆勒纳尔还要求战争部禁止任何接受中国国家留学基金管理委员会资助或其他经济支持的研究人员、研究生和博士后参与战争部资助的科研项目。

他主张，这项限制应在有关人员接受中方资助期间持续有效，无论他们是否被正式列为项目负责人、共同研究人员或其他具名参与者。

穆勒纳尔说，中国国家留学基金管理委员会不同于一般国际学生资助项目。该机构近年来因涉及学术自由、对留学生的监控、意识形态要求和潜在间谍活动等指控，在美国受到越来越严格的审查。

content:
中新社台北10月14日电 一位资深半导体分析师周三表示，埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)计划在德克萨斯州建造大型半导体制造厂，在中短期内不会对台积电产生影响，因为该项目需要五到十年才能实现。

柯克兰资本有限责任公司董事长兼首席执行官、前外国券商分析师杨应超在台北的一个论坛间隙向记者表示，建立领先的芯片代工厂非常复杂。

杨指出，即使对于全球最大的合约芯片制造商台积电来说，建设和扩建新工厂也需要数年时间。

杨说，如果领导特斯拉和SpaceX等公司的马斯克成功建造一座芯片工厂，可能需要五到十年的时间才能投入运营，并补充说该项目在中短期内对台积电“绝对没有影响”。

据最近媒体报道，马斯克计划在德克萨斯州格莱姆斯县建造“Terafab”，这是一个大型垂直一体化半导体制造和人工智能计算综合体。

杨表示，过去许多跨国公司曾尝试进入半导体制造领域，但由于该行业技术壁垒高、资金需求大而失败。

他以他之前工作过的 IBM 半导体业务为例，并指出该业务最终被出售给了 GlobalFoundries。
尽管如此，杨表示，他仍然对马斯克执行该项目的长期能力充满信心，并引用了这位亿万富翁企业家在特斯拉和 SpaceX 的强劲执行记录，后者的业务涵盖电动汽车、自动驾驶、机器人、能源存储、人工智能、卫星通信和太空探索。

他表示，COVID-19大流行期间全球芯片短缺，加上中美贸易紧张局势，增强了美国公司垂直整合其供应链（涵盖芯片设计、制造和先进封装）的愿望。

杨表示，马斯克最初计划投资约30亿美元建设试点工厂，很可能会涉及英特尔等美国合作伙伴，因为华盛顿仍然希望国内企业在半导体制造领域发挥主导作用。

展望未来，杨表示，如果马斯克遵循他提议的转租模式，并允许该公司提供技术咨询服务或租赁该设施的空间，台积电可能会受益。

“英特尔迟早会成为台积电的竞争对手。短期内这不太可能，但五年或十年后，就很难说了，”杨说。 “对于台积电来说，与英特尔走得更近并不是一件坏事，因为双方可以更好地了解彼此。”

（吴家豪、高伊芙琳摄）

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) Elon Musk's reported plan to build a massive semiconductor fabrication complex in Texas will have no impact on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) in the short to medium term, as such a project would take five to 10 years to materialize, a veteran semiconductor analyst said on Wednesday.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a forum in Taipei, Kirk Yang (楊應超), chairman and CEO of Kirkland Capital LLC and a former foreign brokerage analyst, said building a leading-edge chip foundry is highly complex.

Even for TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, constructing and ramping up a new fab takes several years, Yang noted.

If Musk, who leads companies including Tesla Inc. and SpaceX, succeeds in building a chip fab, it will likely be five to 10 years before it becomes operational, Yang said, adding that the project poses "absolutely no impact" on TSMC in the short or medium term.

According to recent media reports, Musk plans to build "Terafab," a massive vertically integrated semiconductor manufacturing and artificial intelligence computing complex in Grimes County, Texas.

Yang noted that many multinational companies have attempted to enter semiconductor manufacturing in the past, but failed because of the industry's high technological barriers and enormous capital requirements.

He cited IBM's semiconductor business, where he previously worked, as an example, noting that it was ultimately sold to GlobalFoundries.

Still, Yang said he remains confident in Musk's long-term ability to execute the project, citing the billionaire entrepreneur's strong execution record at Tesla and SpaceX, whose businesses span electric vehicles, autonomous driving, robotics, energy storage, artificial intelligence, satellite communications and space exploration.

He said the global chip shortage during the COVID-19 pandemic, coupled with U.S.-China trade tensions, has strengthened U.S. companies' desire to vertically integrate their supply chains, covering chip design, manufacturing and advanced packaging.

Yang said Musk's initial plan to invest about US$3 billion in a pilot fab is likely to involve U.S. partners such as Intel, as Washington still hopes domestic companies will play a leading role in semiconductor manufacturing.

Looking further ahead, Yang said TSMC could benefit if Musk follows through on his proposed sublease model and allows the company to provide technical consulting services or lease space at the facility.

"Intel will sooner or later become a competitor to TSMC. That's unlikely in the short term, but five or 10 years from now, it's hard to say," Yang said. "It wouldn't be a bad thing for TSMC to get closer to Intel, as the two sides could gain a better understanding of each other."

(By Wu Chia-hao and Evelyn Kao)

content: 中国是全球最大的玩具制造商，生产美国市场上销售的绝大多数玩具 在美国销售的绝大多数儿童玩具底部，你都会发现同样的三个词——“中国制造”。 根据美国政府数据，2024年进口到该国的玩具中，近八分之七（78.3%）来自中国。 去年，从中国进口的玩具价值98亿美元（74亿英镑），贸易数据显示。 随着圣诞节临近，美国和世界各地的玩具行业即将迎来一年中最繁忙的时刻。 随着零售商为节日旺季准备库存，无论是网络巨头还是“妈妈和爸爸”式的实体商店，BBC世界服务的《追踪金钱》系列追踪了一个玩具如何从中国的一家工厂运送到美国，以及钱去了哪里。 工厂 位于中国南部的广东省，毗邻香港，是中国玩具制造工业的心脏。 在东莞的Mihox工厂，工人们从钢模具中生产塑料玩具，并将它们堆入箱子，准备进行喷漆。 该公司表示，它雇佣了800多人，每年为美国市场生产约5500万个玩具，这占其业务的一半。 每个玩具都始于客户的设计，例如一家美国玩具公司。工厂随后制作原型，并制造模具，从中形成塑料部件和其他组件。 从第一个想法到成品玩具需要一到两年时间，Mihox销售团队的梅兰妮·王（Melanie Wang）表示。其中很大一部分是客户反复回到设计台前。“他们一次又一次地修改设计，以改进它。” 一旦设计获批，事情就会更快地推进。制作一个模具大约需要一个月的时间，生产周期大约持续三个月。 东莞的Mihox工厂雇佣了800多人 那么，工厂能获得美国零售价的多少？“大约20%，”王说。 对于一个30美元的玩具，那就是6美元，必须覆盖塑料和其他材料的价格、包括工资在内的生产成本，以及工厂的利润。 根据美国玩具公司Basic Fun首席执行官Jay Foreman的说法，中国工厂的利润通常在3%到10%之间。因此，对于一个30美元的玩具，工厂收取的6美元中，利润在60到18美分之间。 香港玩具制造商协会总裁Samson Ko表示，他的许多成员在20世纪80年代将工厂迁到了中国内地，被更便宜的土地和劳动力所吸引。 他说，玩具的制造方式自那时起几乎没有改变。“自动化现在主要发生在模具和包装过程中。但对于毛绒玩具，甚至是一些现在的电子产品，仍然非常劳动密集型。” 他补充说，中国劳动力也不再便宜了，因为最近有所上涨。 梅兰妮·王解释说，Mihox能获得玩具零售价的20% 一份今年年初的报告称，越南的平均工资大约是中国的50%。 然而，Ko的会员中不到10%将任何生产迁出了中国，在这些情况下，主要是因为客户要求他们这样做。 他说，中国工厂仍然很忙，因为一个玩具可以经过多种制造过程，从模具成型部件，到添加电子元件、缝制材料，再到最终组装。这通常需要它前往不同的工厂。 Ko补充说，在广东，这些独立的设施彼此靠近，过去一直“和谐工作”。他说，这使得整个制造过程比其他国家运行得更顺畅。 船只 从工厂出来后，玩具通过卡车运送到港口，如深圳，这是广东省最大的港口。 Ivy Tse是FreightAmigo的联合创始人，这是一家香港物流公司，为香港和中国内地出口商运营一个在线平台。这些企业可以预订集装箱、海运至海外目的地、安排保险覆盖，并获取融资。 Tse表示，货船从深圳到美国西海岸大约需要15天，到东海岸需要25到30天。今年的圣诞玩具于8月和9月从中国出发。 Freight从工厂到美国通常增加玩具制造成本的10%，Tse补充道。因此，如果我们坚持一个在美国零售价为30美元的玩具，因此在中国制造成本为6美元，那么将其运送到美国的成本是60美分。 美国边境 一旦玩具到达美国，目前必须向美国海关和边境保护局（CBP）支付针对中国玩具的关税。 上个月，在特朗普总统和中国领导人习近平之间的会谈后，两国政府建议对玩具征收较低的关税。但尚未设定新税率或开始日期，美国必须首先进行公众咨询。目前基本税率为12.5%，一些玩具的税率更高。 这是对玩具的制造价格征收的，而不是对其零售价格征收。因此，对于一个30美元的玩具，基本税率是6美元的12.5%，即75美分。 这项关税由进口玩具的美国公司支付。其中一家这样的公司是Learning Resources，这是一家位于芝加哥附近的家族企业，销售教育玩具。其中一半是从中国进口的。 “我们支付100%的关税，这一点毫无疑问，”该公司的首席执行官Rick Woldenberg说。 美国玩具公司 Jay Foreman表示，美国玩具花费的大部分钱不会离开该国 制造30美元玩具的成本、将其运送到美国以及支付进口关税，总计为7.35美元。因此，剩下22.65美元，占总数的75.5%。 这笔钱永远不会离开美国，Foreman解释说，他来自佛罗里达的Basic Fun公司。他的公司生产Tonka卡车和Care Bears毛绒玩具。 “这笔钱由我的公司、[美国]运输公司、零售商保留，”他说。 如果我们允许2.65美元给美国运输公司，玩具公司和零售商通常将剩余收入五五分成。因此，这将使它们各自获得10美元。 虽然利润率是商业机密，因此通常不会透露，但行业研究表明，玩具公司和零售商通常会获得高达25%或2.50美元的利润。 将一个玩具上架到美国货架需要大量的工作和漫长的旅程。

# 美国无人机新创到台湾找厂商合作生产 美台去年9月以来签至少13项协议

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月15日 06:21

美国无人机和防务新创公司HavocAI、安杜里尔（Anduril Industries）、AEVEX等，正在美国政府牵线下到台湾，寻找能把设计做成产品的台湾厂商；它们仿照台积电的做法，由客户设计、台湾制造，目标是建立同时服务台湾和五角大楼、避开中国的“非红”供应链。2025年9月以来，美台双方已签了至少13项合作协议。

受影响的是台湾的造船、无人机和零部件厂商。台湾政府8月编列了超过70亿美元、为期6年的无人机预算；海军要求6年拨款9.3亿美元，采购国防部去年12月说需要的1320艘单向水面无人艇，这种无人攻击艇到达目标时会爆炸。安杜里尔和台北签的无人机合同已超过10亿美元。

这几组合作里，美方大多提供设计、软件或技术，台湾厂商负责造船、制造和在地采购。台船董事长陈政宏和同事花了半年多评估美欧十多家公司，最后选定HavocAI，9月飞到罗德岛签约，准备共同竞标海军的无人艇合同；双方签的是合作意向书，HavocAI提供自主航行技术，台船负责造船、生产和维修保养。中科院去年和安杜里尔签了共同生产协议，在台湾制造安杜里尔的Barracuda 500巡航导弹和水下无人装备。

AEVEX和中光电智能机器人（CIRC）将合作生产VANDAL和ONYX两款无人机，9月下旬在台湾东南沿海做了现场展示：AEVEX提供用3D打印制作的机身设计，中光电设计飞行控制器、运算板和酬载系统，并在台湾采购马达和电池。按AEVEX公布的资料，VANDAL的飞行距离是486公里、酬载4.5公斤，ONYX是270公里、13.6公斤。另一家美国无人机公司Shield AI的共同创办人曾国光10月2日说，Shield AI一年前在台湾只有1名员工，现在有11人，预计一年内增加到20人。

对美国来说，在本土制造无人机是政策重点：国防部长赫格塞斯去年推出11亿美元的“无人机主导”（Drone Dominance）计划时说，明确偏好采购美国货。曾负责五角

# 也门政府就胡塞武装疑用中国技术制造武器向中方表示关切

也门外交部长周三（10月14日）表示，也门政府已就亲伊朗的胡塞武装可能试图利用中国技术和零部件制造武器、用于也门冲突一事，向中国提出关切。

发表时间： 14/10/2026 - 23:33

 4 分钟 浏览时间

 Elderly man carries a weapon as he joins Houthi supporters gathering to show support to the movement in Sanaa REUTERS - Mohammed al-Mahdi

 作者： [安娜](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%AE%89%E5%A8%9C/ "安娜")

广告

继续浏览后续

法新社报道，也门外长祖巴周三在有关也门冲突升级的线上记者会上，回答法新社记者关于胡塞武装可能采购中国零部件制造武器的提问时表示：“中国是我们的伙伴，我们已同他们讨论了军民两用产品的使用问题。”

也门外长表示：“中方非常希望获取各方面的信息，以便展开调查。中方对也门政府的支持是明确的。”

研究机构“冲突武器研究组织”（CAR）最近发布的一份报告称，胡塞武装正试图生产先进的中程弹道导弹。

报告指出，这支得到德黑兰支持的武装“已将供应链扩展至与伊朗有关的网络之外”。报告还称：“发现了数个专门设计的导弹零部件，同时发现的运输文件提及一家中国供应商。”

法新社无法独立核实这份报告的内容。

胡塞武装与也门政府之间的冲突始于2014年。2015年，沙特领导的军事联盟介入，支援也门政府。经过数年的相对平静后，冲突于今年7月再度爆发。

此后，胡塞武装动用弹道导弹、巡航导弹和无人机，袭击也门政府军，以及沙特境内的民用设施和石油基础设施。

胡塞武装声称，周二夜间至周三凌晨再次袭击了沙特石油巨头阿美公司的一处设施。此前，自10月7日以来，针对利雅得机场的袭击已造成至少18人死亡。

胡塞武装还袭击了红海上的油轮。自阿拉伯半岛另一侧的霍尔木兹海峡关闭以来，红海已成为沙特石油出口的替代通道。

中国长期以来一直是沙特原油的主要买家之一。

# Help James Create a Carbon-Negative Haven

My name is James Alan Smith. I’m an avid outdoorsman, fisherman and traveller. I raised four sons through construction and after my divorce, I got my Teaching credentials for Earth Science and Biology at the High School level. Teaching there three years I became frustrated by Teaching at this level. I then applied for a position Teaching English in Taiwan, at the Elementary level.I had a blast. Four of the best years in my life! Make no mistake, I took it seriously, studying Mandarin and taking in as much of their culture which amazed me daily. Forward many years, and my knees are gone with my mind increasingly fogged by a thyroid deficiency. Also, I have my fourth son living with me who, even as an adult has autism and other issues preventing him from being independent. Now, having worked outdoors as a fisherman and builder, I can say unequivocally that our environment IS changing rapidly. My education and observations made me ponder what solutions we must pursue to mitigate or repair damages to our precious gift; planet Earth! Having built many structures personally and designed more, I have drawn up a modest, and humble structure to help in neutralizing CO2 gain in our VERY thin and vulnerable atmosphere! It’s seemingly huge, but in reality only as thick as the skin on an onion, scaled down. Know that this structure will be inhabited by my son and I, though having done years of research I know by using the wood on my property, solar gain and utilizing prevailing westerly winds that I can achieve energy and corporate independence and hopefully share my successes with the public in the pursuit of carbon negativity. I have the land, am planting fruit and nut trees, with Nitrogen fixing trees and shrubs. I have worked very hard, running a contracting business and know the value of a dollar putting myself through College scalloping way off NY, salmon fishing off CA and mating of Montauk and Captree Island during summers when school was off. I plan on starting a YouTube channel to none other than get the word out, being a Teacher at heart. ANY donation will be greatly appreciated and know that as a believer in miracles, NO money will be wasted or spent irresponsibly. I also plan on writing a book to share my/our progress, initiatives, inventions, observations, mistakes, joys and frustrations. There are 61 acres, half of which are free, more or less for planting (via Permaculture methods) and raising livestock for food gaining complete self sufficiency, selling surplus for cash, maybe jams, JimJam. lol
