content:
中国政府一位发言人星期三(10月14日)表示，台湾海巡部门必须为在南中国海某环礁附近水域向一艘中国渔船使用高压水炮“承担后果”。台湾则表示，台湾海巡署只是履行“正常执法”任务，台湾国安官员指出，中国在这些区域采取了“侵略性行动”。

与此同时，台湾国防部报告说，中国军方星期三在台湾周边进行了又一次所谓的“联合战备警巡”。

本月早些时候，一艘台湾海巡船对滞留在台湾控制的南中国海东沙群岛，西方称普拉塔斯群岛(Pratas Islands)附近限制水域并拒绝离开的中国大陆渔船使用了高压水炮。这艘渔船随后发动机故障，由另一艘中国渔船将其拖离。

中国国务院台湾事务办公室发言人陈斌华在星期三举行的记者会上被问及此事时声称，中国对东沙及其邻近水域拥有“无可争辩的主权”，而且中国大陆船只在相关海域的活动“完全合法正当”。

陈斌华指责台湾的民进党当局“顽固坚持台独分裂立场”，“以危险方式粗暴对待大陆船舶”，“必须承担由此引发的一切后果。”

但是他并没有透露或说明所谓的“一切后果”到底是什么。

东沙群岛位于台湾南部和香港之间，长期以来一直由台湾控制。岛上没有常住平民，但建有简易跑道和国家公园。负责东沙岛安全守卫的是台湾的海巡署而不是军方。由于东沙群岛距离台湾本岛超过400公里，因此安全专家担心这里很容易遭到中国的攻击。

中国不仅声称拥有几乎整个南中国海及其所有岛礁的主权，而且坚称实行民主治理的台湾也是其“不可分割”的领土，即使诉诸武力也要实现台海两岸的统一。

此次东沙群岛海域发生的摩擦之所以引入注目，另一个重要的原因是中国海警在南中国海的争议海域经常对菲律宾的公务船或渔船使用高压水炮，导致菲方船只受损，甚至人员受伤。

台湾行政院院长卓荣泰10月5日对台湾海巡船对大陆渔船使用水炮一事对外做出以下说明。

“发射水炮是不得不为。如果侵犯我国主权，执法人员要保卫国家安全，”卓荣泰说。

路透社援引一位了解东沙群岛周边局势的台湾官员的话说，台湾海巡部门在事件中执行了“正常执法”任务，并以“非常谨慎且适度”的方式进行了应对。

最近几年，随着北京针对台湾的军事威胁愈演愈烈，中方也逐渐扩大使用“灰色地带”战术，就是在不直接诉诸军事行动的情况下使用准军事的海警船、伪装成渔船的民兵船、甚至科考船向台湾施压。

台湾国家安全会议副秘书长李问星期三在台北出席一场论坛时表示，数十年来，中国的扩张野心在区域内采取侵略性行动。

“这些处于冲突门槛之下的‘灰色地带’活动引发了严重关切，因为它们可能扰乱交通运输或破坏关键基础设施，”李问说。

路透社上周四援引台湾民营航空业者安捷航空(Apex Aviation)的监控报告，指今年8月中旬，该公司自营的侦察机在距离台湾东部花莲海岸约50公里处，发现中国民兵船“闵福鼎渔07902”与一艘中国海警船和一艘中国科研船共同航行。

这是首次在该海域发现中国此类型的船只。

美国国务院一位发言人上周五在回答美国之音(VOA)电邮置评请求时表示，“美国对中国在台湾以东的活动持续感到关切。”

“中国的行动深度破坏稳定。中国对台湾已和平管理70余年的海域宣示权威，这只会加剧紧张局势，并破坏其声称寻求的和平解决问题的努力，”这位发言人指出。

发言人还说，“我们敦促北京停止对台湾的压力，转而与台湾民选当局进行有意义的对话。”

与此同时，台湾国防部星期三指出，中国军方当天在台湾周边进行了又一次“联合战备警巡”，出动了包括歼-16战斗机在内的13架军机以及数量不详的海军舰艇。

中国国防部当天稍早表示，辽宁舰及其编队正在西太平洋进行演练，但未透露具体细节。

title: Twins skipper sings praise of relievers, outfielder in KBO postseason victory
zh_title: 双胞胎队长赞扬 KBO 季后赛胜利的中继员和外野手
summary: 作者：Yoo Jee-ho 首尔 10 月 14 日（韩联社）——周三，在他的 LG Twins 击败斗山熊队赢得季后赛胜利后，主教练 Youm Kyoung-youb 对他的替补投手给予了高度赞扬。在韩国棒球组织外卡赛中，双城队以 4-1 获胜，先发球员卡洛斯·卡拉斯科 (Carlos Carrasco) 被指控在六局中仅得一分，但尤姆注意到了他的两名左手投手乔恩·肯尼迪 (Jon Kennedy) 和李宇灿 (Lee Woo-chan) 的工作，他们都在堵塞中努力阻止熊队在首尔蚕室棒球场进行最后的集会。 LG Twins 球员在俱乐部庆祝 4-1 战胜 Doosan Bears
content:
作者：柳智浩

首尔，10 月 14 日（韩联社）——周三，在他的 LG Twins 击败斗山熊队赢得季后赛胜利后，主教练 Youm Kyoung-youb 对他的替补投手给予了高度赞扬。

在韩国棒球组织外卡赛中，双城队以 4-1 获胜，先发球员卡洛斯·卡拉斯科 (Carlos Carrasco) 被指控在六局中仅得一分，但尤姆注意到了他的两名左手投手乔恩·肯尼迪 (Jon Kennedy) 和李宇灿 (Lee Woo-chan) 的工作，他们都在堵塞中努力阻止熊队在首尔蚕室棒球场进行最后的集会。

2026 年 10 月 14 日，LG Twins 球员在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织季后赛俱乐部外卡赛中庆祝以 4-1 战胜斗山熊队。（韩联社）

肯尼迪在第七局上场，卡拉斯科允许一垒安打和二垒安打开始比赛，并将伤害限制在仅一分。随后，当熊队有两名跑垒员时，李连续三振了两名击球手，结束了第八局的威胁。

双胞胎队在奥斯汀·迪恩的两分全垒打中在第一局的底部登上了董事会，但在接下来的六局中打出了零分。他们需要肯尼迪和李的每一点工作才能生存。

“虽然我们早早取得了进球，但我们仍然处于困境，因为我们有一段时间未能获得附加分，”尤姆说。 “然后肯尼迪和小宇就摆脱了麻烦，做得很好。”
中外野手朴海民也发挥了关键作用，他跑下来接替补击球手杨锡焕打出的远距离飞球，并在第七局上垒。本来很容易就能逆转领先优势的一击最终却变成了牺牲飞球，这也是熊队本场比赛唯一的得分。

“那场比赛帮助我们在最后几局建立了一些势头，”尤姆指出。

帕克说，在接球之前，他已经把自己摆在了正确的位置。

“球一离开球棒，我就觉得我可以去接球，”长期以来被认为是 KBO 中最好的防守外野手的帕克说。 “当然，肯尼迪做得非常出色，让下一个人结束了威胁。”

2026 年 10 月 14 日，在首尔蚕室棒球场举行的韩国棒球组织季后赛俱乐部外卡赛中，斗山 Bears 球员以 4-1 输给 LG Twins 后离场。（韩联社）

朴接球后，杨沮丧地扔下了头盔，尽管中外野手说他从未看到过这一情况，因为他正在为下一个击球手做准备。

顺便说一句，这两名球员是高中队友，帕克在这场比赛中并没有想到这一点。

“当我在球场上时，对方的任何人都是我必须击败的敌人，无论是我的高中队友，甚至是我的家人，”帕克说。 “这就是职业运动员应该做的事情。”
落败的主帅金元亨对熊队缺乏进攻性表示遗憾，这让他们整个赛季都深受困扰，而且球员们也未能注意防守细节。

第八局下半，比赛仍悬而未决，熊队凭借挤压短打和狂野的投球失了两分，最终锁定了他们的命运。

金说：“我们重复了一些小错误，在本来可以毫发无伤的情况下我们放弃了跑动。”他同时补充说，他不想点名任何特定球员的失误。 “作为一名主教练，这是一场令人尴尬的比赛。”

jeeho@yna.co.kr
（完）

【原文 English Original】
By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 14 (Yonhap) -- After his LG Twins held off the Doosan Bears for a postseason win Wednesday, manager Youm Kyoung-youb reserved high praise for his relief pitchers.

Starter Carlos Carrasco was charged with just one run in six innings in the Twins' 4-1 victory in the Korea Baseball Organization wild card game, but Youm noted the work of his two left-handers, Jon Kennedy and Lee Woo-chan, who both worked out of jams to prevent the Bears from mounting late rallies at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul.

LG Twins players celebrate their 4-1 win over the Doosan Bears in the clubs' wild card game in the Korea Baseball Organization postseason at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 14, 2026. (Yonhap)

Kennedy came on in the seventh inning after Carrasco allowed a single and a double to start the frame, and limited the damage to just one run. Lee then struck out two straight batters to end an eighth-inning threat when the Bears had two runners aboard.

The Twins got on the board in the bottom of the first on Austin Dean's two-run homer but put up zeroes over the next six innings. They needed every bit of the work by Kennedy and Lee to survive.

"Though we scored early, we were still in a tough spot because we failed to score add-on runs for a while," Youm said. "Then Kennedy and Woo-chan did a great job getting out of trouble."

Center fielder Park Hae-min also played a key role, as he ran down to catch a deep fly hit by pinch hitter Yang Suk-hwan with the bases loaded in the seventh. What could easily have been a lead-flipping hit ended up being a sacrifice fly that scored what turned out to be the Bears' only run of the game.

"That play helped us build some momentum in late innings," Youm noted.

Park said he had positioned himself in just the right spot before making that running catch.

"As soon as the ball left the bat, I felt like I could go get it," said Park, long considered the best defensive outfielder in the KBO. "And of course, Kennedy did an excellent job getting the next out to end the threat."

Doosan Bears players walk off the field after losing to the LG Twins 4-1 in the clubs' wild card game in the Korea Baseball Organization postseason at Jamsil Baseball Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 14, 2026. (Yonhap)

Yang threw down his helmet in frustration after Park made the catch, though the center fielder said he never saw it because he was getting ready for the next batter.

Incidentally, the two players were high school teammates, not that Park had that on his mind during this game.

"When I am on the field, anyone on the other side is the enemy I have to beat, whether it's my high school teammate or even my family member," Park said. "That is what professional athletes are supposed to do."

Kim Won-hyong, the losing manager, lamented the Bears' lack of offensive punch, something that ailed them all season, and also players' failure to pay attention to details on defense.

With the game still hanging in the balance in the bottom of the eighth, the Bears allowed two runs on a squeeze bunt and a wild pitch that sealed their fate.

"We repeated some small mistakes, and we gave up runs in situations that we could have escaped unscathed," Kim said, while adding he did not want to name any particular players for their miscues. "As a manager, this was an embarrassing game."

jeeho@yna.co.kr
(END)

title: March with SHL in the Charleston Pride Parade, Sat, Oct 17, 2026, 8:00 AM   | Meetup
summary: SHL is returning to the Charleston Pride Parade! Years ago, our organization regularly participated in the parade, and we're excited to be back. This year, we're marching alongside our friends in **The Queer Agenda**, a coalition of local o
content:
SHL is returning to the Charleston Pride Parade! Years ago, our organization regularly participated in the parade, and we're excited to be back. This year, we're marching alongside our friends in **The Queer Agenda**, a coalition of local organizations like We Are Family and QT Camp, working together to support and defend the LGBTQIA+ community.

**This is an all ages event**, and this year's theme for our group is "Pride Gives Us Wings." Wear rainbow colors, wings, your favorite LGBTQIA+ flag, or whatever makes you feel festive. Bring your SHL shirt if you have one, and let's show Charleston that our humanist community stands proudly with our LGBTQIA+ neighbors!

**Where and when to meet**

*   **8:00 am**: Check-in at Wragg Mall, 20 Ann St, directly beside the Charleston Museum. Check-in begins at 7:30. We recommend arriving by 8 am to give yourself plenty of time to find our group and get situated.
*   **Finding our group**: Tell Charleston Pride organizers or volunteers in orange shirts that you're with "**The Queer Agenda**," Group B. They can direct you to our staging area.
*   **Finding SHL**: Bonnie Cleaveland, who will be leading our contingent.
*   **8:25 am**: Everyone must be present and assembled with the group by this time. Please don't be late!
*   **9:00 am**: The parade begins, heading south on King Street from Ann Street to Market Street.
*   **Duration**: Approximately 45 minutes. The parade ends at King and Market Streets.

**Parking**
 The closest recommended parking is the Visitors Center Parking Garage at 63 Mary Street, across Ann Street from the Charleston Visitor Center. According to Charleston Pride, parking costs $2 for the first hour and $1 for each additional hour, with a $16 daily maximum.

**Other parking options include**:

*   St. Philip Street Garage — 89 St. Philip Street
*   George Street Lot — 31 George Street
*   Cumberland Street Garage — 90 Cumberland Street
*   65 Hasell Street Parking — 65 Hasell Street

Expect road closures and traffic delays around the parade route. Carpooling is encouraged.

**Get ready for Pride on Friday night!**
 Afraid of showing up but not knowing anyone? We Are Family (WAF) is hosting a Pride preparation gathering on Friday, October 16, 5:30-7:30 pm at the WAF Community Center. You can meet some of the people we'll be marching with and make something fun to wear or carry! Queer Agenda friends can get together to make posters, decorate shirts, create wings, and get ready for the parade.
 It's a great opportunity to meet our fellow marchers before Saturday morning and get into the Pride spirit!

**A few reminders**
 Wear comfortable walking shoes, bring water and sunscreen, and dress for the weather. The parade will proceed rain or shine. Signs and banners celebrating equality and inclusion are welcome. Please don't throw items into the crowd or engage with protesters along the route.

content: 据称的中国间谍网络利用 LinkedIn 针对超过 100 名与澳大利亚有关联的人员。 (ABC 新闻) ABC 的一项调查发现，两个疑似中国间谍的 LinkedIn 账号在全球积累了数千个联系人，并向数十名在政府、警务和贸易领域工作的澳大利亚人提供有偿咨询服务的要约。 据称的间谍伪装成智库员工，以提供“宝贵建议”为交换条件，向目标提供具有竞争力的薪酬。 在 2016 年至 2025 年间，据称的间谍针对了超过 100 名与澳大利亚有关联的个人，包括前昆士兰州州长兼现任反对党领袖史蒂文·迈尔斯（Steven Miles）、一名澳大利亚联邦警察指挥官以及几名高级联邦政府官员。 他们的 LinkedIn 个人资料出现在两个自称代表智库的 LinkedIn 账号的连接记录中。被指控的外国代理人联系了其中 58 个联系人，一些接收者分享了他们的个人联系方式。 ABC 透露，这些澳大利亚人受到了与亚历山大·切尔戈（Alexander Csergo）相同的据称中国间谍网络的针对，而切尔戈已被判为首位因鲁莽外国干涉罪入狱的人。 亚历山大·切尔戈上月因鲁莽外国干涉罪被判监禁三年六个月。 (ABC 新闻：亚当·格里菲斯) 澳大利亚联邦警察（AFP）在调查切尔戈案件期间获得的 LinkedIn 记录显示，这些账号还联系了其他澳大利亚人，包括在政府机构和州贸易与投资机构工作的人。 AFP 指控该行动由中国国家情报机构——国家安全部（MSS）实施。据称，MSS 使用虚假的 LinkedIn 个人资料联系并培养潜在的外国情报来源，随后向他们索取信息。 中国驻堪培拉大使馆拒绝了 AFP 的指控，称其“完全毫无根据”。 “我们坚决拒绝对中国毫无根据的指控和诽谤，并希望澳大利亚媒体遵守职业道德，以公平客观的方式报道，”一名发言人通过电子邮件告诉 ABC。 AFP 指控中国国家国家安全部负责这些在线账号。 (提供) 今年 6 月，五眼联盟（Five Eyes alliance）——由美国、英国、澳大利亚、加拿大和新西兰组成的情报共享合作伙伴关系——发布了一份罕见的联合警告，指出中国情报机构利用在线招聘平台进行招募“可能使中国相对于五眼联盟获得战略和战术优势”。 ABC 询问澳大利亚国内间谍机构 ASIO 的发言人是否了解或正在调查这起据称的间谍行动时，ASIO 发言人表示：“与一贯做法一致，ASIO 不对——也不确认——调查发表评论。” 招聘攻势内幕 2021 年 11 月，当时切尔戈居住在上海，一个名为 Vera Su 的 LinkedIn 账号向他提供了兼职工作。 发送者自称来自 Nesa Consulting，并表示该组织希望专家就中澳贸易提供建议。 根据检方指控，切尔戈随后与两名他认识的人——肯（Ken）和伊芙琳（Evelyn）会面，准备了报告并收到了现金付款。 他于 3 月被定罪，罪名是鲁莽外国干涉，这是根据澳大利亚 2018 年国家安全法引入的罪行。 检方指控称，他的行为涉及保密或欺骗，并且他对于是否支持外国主子的情报活动是鲁莽的。 2021 年 11 月，当亚历山大·切尔戈居住在上海时，一个名为 Vera Su 的 LinkedIn 账号首次联系了他。 (ABC 新闻) 但 ABC 对 Vera Su 通信记录的分析——这些记录最初由 AFP 在调查切尔戈案件时获得——揭示了相同的 LinkedIn 账号如何寻找其他拥有有用专业知识和联系的人。 其中一些直接联系的人的个人资料列出了在 Austrade（联邦贸易与投资促进机构）、外交贸易部、投资 NSW、投资维多利亚州和澳大利亚旅游局工作的经历。 这些账号的推销活动还试图接触政府内部人员。 “我想知道您是否有特殊的信息来源……例如：来自政府重要人物，”一条消息问道。 一些接收者拒绝了。 一名 Austrade 员工表示，他不能接受金钱，因为他受雇于澳大利亚政府，尽管他愿意在其专业网络中介绍他人。 前昆士兰州州长史蒂文·迈尔斯也在 2021 年 4 月与他担任副州长期间与同一个 Vera Su 账号建立了联系。 史蒂文·迈尔斯在担任昆士兰州副州长期间受到了疑似间谍网络的针对。 (ABC 新闻：马克·莱昂纳迪) ABC 未看到迈尔斯先生与该账号之间的任何消息，仅凭连接本身并不能证明他收到了咨询要约或提供了信息。据 ABC 了解，迈尔斯先生没有回应苏女士的任何消息。 ‘蜜罐’ ABC 审查的数据显示，一些与澳大利亚有关联的目标分享了联系方式，或在 LinkedIn 之外继续交换，包括通过微信、电话或会议。 商业顾问尼克·科伊尔（Nick Coyle）在因间谍罪在中国被捕的前任伴侣陈雷（Cheng Lei）被逮捕时，受到了据称中国间谍的接触。 尼克·科伊尔与他的前任伴侣陈雷。 (提供：尼克·科伊尔) “在那段时间，我收到了许多奇怪的接触，”他说。其中一些是“蜜罐”，即试图在网上和现实中成为“朋友”的人。 “我只是采取接触——如果我不认识他们——我会避开，”他说。 澳大利亚生活教练阿德里安·卡希尔（Adrian Cahill）也在 2021 年与 Vera 交换了联系方式。他怀疑他前士兵的背景使他成为了更有吸引力的目标。 “我会收到相当多的，”他说。“人们写信给我说，‘我们有工作，我们有钱，我们有预算。’” 他说他的训练帮助他识别了这些战术，但没有安全经验的人可能会被逐渐引导提供“越来越多信息”。 情报技术的‘根本转变’ 中国情报专家尼古拉斯·埃夫蒂米亚德斯（Nicholas Eftimiades）将这种国家资助的钓鱼行动描述为“根本转变”。 埃夫蒂米亚德斯教授称，中国日益增长的 AI 能力可能正在发挥作用，使大规模接触对中国的更有效和安全。 “他们一次可以接触数十万人，试图让人为你工作是一个成本更低的选择，”他说。 “我们无法跟上这种攻势。” 尼古拉斯·埃夫蒂米亚德斯表示，中国情报人员利用技术低成本、安全地接触大量潜在目标。 (提供) 前美国联邦检察官维卡斯·迪德万（Vikas Didwania），他曾为美国政府处理涉及中国情报行动的案件，称 LinkedIn 是情报收集方面的“金矿”。 “我们在 LinkedIn 上看到，人们发布关于他们能接触到的机密信息类型以及他们拥有的许可类型，”他说。 迪德万表示，从 LinkedIn 招募人员获得的信息可能不是机密，甚至没有用，但可能是培养来源过程的一部分。 “随着这段关系的进展，你可以开始稍微推进一步。” 与中国人合作的澳大利亚人面临的微妙平衡 近年来，ASIO 局长迈克·伯吉斯（Mike Burgess）警告称，澳大利亚面临的外国干涉威胁已达到“极端水平”，并可能加剧。 切尔戈是首位在新威胁环境下因鲁莽外国干涉罪被定罪的人。 在切尔戈的审判期间，法院听到他未披露任何机密信息。他的报告是根据公开材料编制的。 上月在量刑听证会上，地区法院法官克雷格·史密斯（Craig Smith）将切尔戈描述为“一个否则相当不错的人”，但他犯下了“最严重的罪行”。 他判处其监禁三年六个月。 史密斯法官表示，威慑人们参与可能损害澳大利亚国家安全的活动是“根本且重要的”。 然而，对于与中国人合作的澳大利亚人来说，这一判决也重新划定了合法与外国实体合作和国家资助干涉之间的危险界限。 一些专家指出，一个复杂因素是，中国约有 2000 个智库，与共产党和政府有着不同且往往不透明的联系。 中国 2017 年国家安全法要求组织和公民支持国家情报工作。一些专家认为其实际影响也可能影响在中国运营的外国公司。 科伊尔先生说，在与中国工作的澳大利亚人必须变得擅长“一边走路一边嚼口香糖”。 维卡斯·迪德万曾为美国政府起诉中国情报案件。 (提供) 迪德万先生说，应对中国间谍行动的努力需要与造成寒蝉效应的风险相平衡。 “我们如何区分伟大的合作与真正属于 MSS 招募的合作，”他问道。 “这变成了一个真正的挑战。”

内容提要：中国对日本的压力已升级为外交孤立该国的努力。这些努力正在国家以下各级、联合国内进行，并试图离间美国和日本之间的关系。在日本，中华人民共和国（PRC）的孤立运动涉及培养反对派以在两国之间建立更友好的关系。在联合国，中华人民共和国正在利用第二次世界大战后的语言来限制日本的影响力。习近平总书记访问华盛顿也是试图探查美日关系的弱点。这些努力未能像去年其他国家那样孤立日本。日本首相高市仍然拥有民众支持，第二次世界大战的叙述在联合国其他成员国中的影响力不如在中国，唐纳德·特朗普总统与高市的关系仍然牢固。与日本发生外交争端近一年后，中华人民共和国（中华人民共和国）已从向日本施加经济压力转向多方面的行动，旨在在国内、联合国以及美日关系中孤立首相高市早苗的亲台立场。北京在避开高市政府的同时，接待了亲中国的日本政界人士和商界人士代表团，试图在联合国安理会抹黑日本，并敦促美国限制对东京的支持。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Chinese pressure on Japan has escalated to efforts to diplomatically isolate the country. These efforts are ongoing at a subnational level, in the United Nations, and through attempts to drive a wedge between the United States and Japan. In Japan, the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) isolation campaign involves cultivating the opposition to establish friendlier relations between the two countries. In the United Nations, the PRC is drawing on post-World War Two language to limit Japanese influence. General Secretary Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington was also an attempt to probe weaknesses in U.S.–Japan ties. These efforts are failing to isolate Japan, as others have in the past year. Japanese prime minister Takaichi still holds popular support, World War Two narratives are less potent among other UN member states than in the PRC, and President Donald Trump’s relationship with Takaichi remains strong. Nearly a year into its diplomatic spat with Japan, the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has shifted from pressuring Japan economically to a multi-faceted campaign that aims to isolate Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for her pro-Taiwan stance, at home, in the United Nations, and within the U.S.–Japan relationship. While shunning Takaichi’s government, Beijing has hosted delegations of pro-PRC Japanese politicians and businesspeople, attempted to discredit Japan in the UN Security Council, and pressed the United States to limit support for Tokyo. Despite its relentlessness, these PRC efforts are unlikely to succeed. Beijing’s preferred diplomatic partners in Tokyo lack political clout, the UN scheme is far-fetched, and the U.S.–Japan alliance has structural staying power reinforced by the warm relationship between President Donald Trump and Takaichi. PRC Attempts to Cultivat e Japanese Opposition The PRC used the occasion of the 54th anniversary of the normalization of its diplomatic ties with Japan to admonish Takaichi. The PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) said on September 29 that Takaichi had “gravely undermined” the political foundation of bilateral relations with a “blatant challenge to China’s national sovereignty” (公然挑战中国国家主权) ( Embassy of the PRC in the United States , September 29). On the same day, PRC Foreign Minister Wang Yi (王毅) met with former Japanese Foreign Minister Takeshi Iwaya, who opposes Takaichi, in Beijing. Wang told Iwaya that Japan must “correct the erroneous words and deeds” of Takaichi on Taiwan (尽快纠正本国领导人在台湾问题上的错误言行) ( PRC MFA , September 29). For his part, Iwaya echoed PRC talking points when he called for “a return to the original spirit” (中四个政治文件的初心) of the four political documents between the PRC and Japan ( People’s Daily , September 29). The PRC views Iwaya as friendly to its interests. Though a member of Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), he is not close to Takaichi and stepped down after she was elected last year. Sima Nan (司马南), a prominent Chinese political commentator, compared Iwaya favorably to Takaichi, writing on Guangcha that Takaichi “is constantly creating conflict and closing the door to dialogue abroad, while her party rivals are braving pressure to come to China to break the ice and seek cooperation opportunities” (不断制造矛盾、关闭对话大门，党内对手却顶着压力来华破冰、寻求合作机会) ( Guangcha/司马平邦 , September 30). Since July, Iwaya has served as the head of the Beijing-friendly Japan Association for the Promotion of International Trade (JAPIT). He succeeded the late Yohei Kono, a former Speaker of Japan’s House of Representatives with close ties to the PRC. Wang told Iwaya that Kono was “ a politician of conscience who dared to confront Japan’s dark past and bravely reflected on the aggressive crimes of militarism” (一个有良知的政治家，敢于直面日本过去的黑暗历史，勇于反省军国主义的侵略罪责) ( PRC MFA , September 29).  The JAPIT delegation is the third such group that has visited the PRC since August. In mid-September, a delegation from the Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union met with Assistant Foreign Minister Liu Bin (刘彬) in Beijing. They were preceded by a cross-party group of Japanese lawmakers ( Global Times , September 27). None of these delegations have included any prominent Japanese officials in Takaichi’s administration or lawmakers with close ties to the prime minister. Stoking the ‘Enemy State’ Debate The PRC is using its UN Security Council seat to resist Takaichi’s calls to remove archaic clauses in the UN charter that imply Japan is an “enemy state.” The language appears in Articles 53, 77, and 107 of the charter. Article 53 explains that the term “enemy state … applies to any state which during the Second World War has been an enemy of any signatory of the present Charter” ( United Nations, accessed October 6). By this definition, Japan, Germany, Italy, Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, and Finland are “enemy states.” Crucially, Article 53 allows the UN Security Council to take enforcement actions against these “enemy states.” The PRC well knows that three permanent Security Council members—the United States, the United Kingdom, and France—would never agree to that and, without unanimity, the Security Council cannot take any formal action against Japan. Yet the very existence of these clauses serves Beijing’s anti-Japan propaganda purposes. On September 2, MFA spokesman Guo Jiakun (郭嘉昆) said at a press conference that the clauses are designed to prevent countries defeated in World War II from posing any threat in the future. He repeated accusations that Japan has embraced a “new-type militarism” (新型军国主义) and emphasized the need for “full compliance” (全面遵守) with the UN Charter need for “enemy state clauses” (China Brief, April 28 [ 1 ], [ 2 ]; Embassy of the PRC in the United States , September 2). During Takaichi’s first address to the UN General Assembly on September 22, she described Japan as a peace-loving nation and called for the removal of the “enemy state” label in the charter. She noted that the United Nations recognized this language as obsolete in both 1995 and 2005, but that it was never formally removed ( Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan , September 22). PRC media responded indignantly. The People’s Daily-owned tabloid Global Times accused Takaichi of putting on a “diplomatic performance” (外交表演) and “openly challenging the post-war international order” (公然挑战了战后国际秩序) ( Global Times , September 23). Trying to Drive a Wedge in U.S.–Japan Relations The third prong of the PRC’s campaign to isolate Takaichi aims to drive a wedge between Japan and the United States, its chief security partner. Beijing sees an opportunity because of President Trump’s focus on building his personal relationship with Xi Jinping. Xi has used both of his face-to-face meetings with Trump this year to probe potential weak points in the U.S.–Japan relationship. Trump reportedly pushed back in May ( Asahi Shimbun , May 28). Yet during the September summit in Washington, the White House released a fact sheet that said, “[t]he two leaders recalled that United States and China were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war” ( The White House , September 25). Though the readout did not name Japan, the PRC still seized the propaganda opportunity, including for international audiences. In an English translation of the readout, state run-Xinhua News Agency said that the two leaders honored the history of a “China-U.S. joint fight against Japanese aggression in WWII” ( Xinhua , September 25).  Takaichi has handled the issue well. She told reporters that Trump called her after his summit with Xi and explained the meeting in detail. She said that she told Trump that “Japan and the United States have now become each other’s most trusted allies” ( Prime Minister’s Office of Japan , September 26). Suggesting promise for Takaichi, she has aligned Japan with key Trump administration priorities—higher defense spending by allies, large investments in the United States, and critical mineral supply chain diversification—while avoiding conflict with the U.S. president. As a result, the U.S.–Japan alliance has deepened operationally and technologically despite Tokyo’s concerns about U.S. unpredictability. Conclusion Almost one year on from the outbreak of its diplomatic dispute with Japan, the PRC shows no interest in pursuing an off-ramp. Instead, it is trying to undermine Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi by wooing her domestic political opponents and depicting her within the United Nations and to the United States as the leader of a revanchist militarist movement. The PRC’s campaign no longer appears to be focused on inducing any change in Takaichi’s stance on Taiwan or more broadly towards Beijing. Instead, it looks like an attempt to punish her for challenging a PRC “red line” and make an example out of her to other countries. The pressure is unlikely to relent as the PRC prepares for the 21st Party Congress in the fall of 2027, when Xi Jinping is widely expected to seek a fourth term. Yet Beijing will also be wary of going too far, with the degree of U.S. support for Japan a crucial factor in the PRC’s calculations in the months ahead. content:
下载全文 PDF 台湾积体电路制造公司 (TSMC，台湾积体电路制造公司) 生产 90% 以上的先进芯片，为人工智能开发提供动力，显着提升了台湾在全球事务中的战略重要性。近年来，认知影响力行动仍然加剧了许多台湾老年人的担忧，担心台积电的海外扩张可能会损害台湾的经济利益、战略影响力和才华横溢的工程师。然而，像我这样的台湾年轻人可能会认为这些担忧被夸大了。台积电一再强调，其最先进的研发能力将留在台湾，台湾将继续作为公司技术开发和全球生产网络的核心。台湾人不应该担心台积电在美国扩大生产，主要有以下三个原因。首先，此次扩张使台积电能够更好地服务美国领先客户并增加其商机。其次，将生产从台湾转移出去有助于减少环境压力和地缘政治风险，并增强半导体供应链的稳定性。最后，台积电的国际发展计划增强了台湾的全球影响力，并加强了与世界各地合作伙伴的联系。
市场准入、政府补贴和下游供应链效益尽管人们对台积电在美国工厂建造和生产半导体的高成本存在合理的担忧，但值得承认这项活动的长期好处：使台积电能够更快地接触全球客户。尽管在海外建立业务需要更高的成本，但这种扩张在财务上已被证明是可行的，正如台积电亚利桑那州所证明的那样。仅 2025 年，亚利桑那州晶圆厂的净利润就达到新台币 42.​​32 亿元（1.358 亿美元），乍一看似乎是全年数据，但实际上仅在一个季度内就实现了这一收入。台积电亚利桑那州取得成功的关键原因之一是全球芯片市场的变化。美国主要依赖台湾制造尖端逻辑芯片。通过在美国建设更多晶圆厂，台积电能够更好地满足其主要客户的产能需求，其中包括AMD、苹果、英伟达和高通等美国公司。这可以实现更快、更个性化的客户服务，从而与大公司建立信任和亲和力，并鼓励他们将来从台积电购买产品。除了贴近客户之外，美国政府还积极利用立法来鼓励半导体公司在国内建设。
美国商务部根据 CHIPS 和科学法案向台积电提供 66 亿美元的直接拨款资金，并获得 50 亿美元的低息联邦贷款。这笔资金有助于抵消美国比台湾更高的建设和运营成本。此外，台积电在美国的扩张不仅建立了跨行业联系，还为长春集团和三立化学等台湾重要供应商在美国运营铺平了道路，从而推动了广泛的芯片生态系统。当这些主力晶圆厂搬迁到新的土地时，整个材料供应网络也随之移动，从而带来更多的商机。通过授权这些供应商扩展到全球市场，此类行动最终会改变

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Producing more than 90 percent of the advanced chips powering AI development, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC, 台灣積體電路製造公司) has significantly elevated Taiwan’s strategic importance in global affairs. In recent years, cognitive influence operations have nonetheless fueled fears among many older Taiwanese that TSMC’s overseas expansion could cost Taiwan economic benefits, strategic leverage, and talented engineers. Younger Taiwanese like myself, however, may see these concerns as overstated. TSMC has repeatedly emphasized that its most advanced research and development (R&D) capabilities will remain in Taiwan, and that the island will continue to serve as the heart of the company’s technology development and global production network. Taiwanese should not be concerned about TSMC expanding its production in the United States for three main reasons. Firstly, this expansion allows TSMC to better serve leading-edge US customers and grow its business opportunities. Secondly, diversifying production away from Taiwan helps reduce environmental strains and geopolitical risks, and strengthens the stability of the semiconductor supply chain. Finally, TSMC’s international development plans enhance Taiwan’s global presence and strengthen connections with partners around the world. Market Access, Government Subsidies, and Downstream Supply Chain Benefits Although there are valid concerns about the high cost of building and producing semiconductors at TSMC facilities in the United States, it is worth acknowledging the long-term benefit of this activity: providing TSMC with quicker access to customers worldwide. Even though establishing operations abroad entails higher costs, this expansion has proven financially viable, as demonstrated by TSMC Arizona. In 2025 alone, the Arizona fab recorded a net income of NTD 4.232 billion (USD 135.8 million) —income that, at first glance, may appear to have been full-year data, but was actually made in just one quarter. One key reason why TSMC Arizona has been successful has been changes in the global market for chips. The United States relies primarily on Taiwan for the fabrication of leading-edge logic chips. By building more fabs in the United States, TSMC is better able to satisfy the capacity demands of its key customers, including American companies such as AMD, Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm, among others. This enables faster, more personalized customer service, which builds trust and affinity with large companies and encourages them to buy from TSMC in the future. Beyond customer proximity, the United States government has actively employed legislation to encourage semiconductor companies to build domestically. The US Department of Commerce has awarded TSMC USD 6.6 billion in direct grant funding under the CHIPS and Science Act , along with access to USD 5 billion in low-interest federal loans. This funding helps offset the higher costs of construction and operation in the US compared to Taiwan. Furthermore, TSMC’s American expansion not only builds cross-industry connections, but it also drives a broad chip ecosystem by paving the way for critical Taiwanese suppliers such as the Chang Chun Group and Sunlit Chemical to operate in the United States. When these anchor fabs move to new land, the entire material supply network also moves with them, leading to more business opportunities. By empowering these suppliers to expand into global markets, such actions ultimately transfer international investment back into Taiwan’s domestic economy. Therefore, continued expansion in the United States represents a strategic investment in TSMC’s long-term financial future. Image: TSMC Fab 21 under construction in Phoenix, Arizona (November 2023). (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) Environmental Risks and Geopolitics In order to maintain satisfying relationships with customers, TSMC must operate a stable and unbroken semiconductor production line. Some Taiwanese believe that this stability can be maintained at home, yet growing environmental risks and geopolitical realities indicate that relying on production in Taiwan alone is increasingly fragile. Within this context, TSMC’s expansion to the United States can help maintain a stable semiconductor production line. As TSMC continues to expand its production capacity, Taiwan is gradually reaching the limits of its environmental carrying capacity. Semiconductor fabs consume vast amounts of water and electricity. Building more and more fabs in Taiwan will put too much pressure on the power grid. Increasing load will risk energy shortages and infrastructure strain, thus destabilizing production lines not only for TSMC but also for other businesses in Taiwan. By contrast, locations for TSMC’s expansion, such as Arizona, possess far more abundant resources. Arizona has one of the biggest energy grids in the United States, operating over 6,551 megawatts (MW) of installed solar capacity alongside nearly 3,900 megawatts (MW) of battery energy storage systems. Beyond electricity, water is also essential for the semiconductor industry; a single advanced chip factory can consume up to 38 million liters of water per day (an amount approximately equivalent to the daily water usage of a medium-sized city). As a small island with finite resources, Taiwan simply lacks the physical capacity to sustain such immense environmental pressure. Crowding the nation with dozens of new factories would push its fragile water supply to a dangerous breaking point, placing a burden on the everyday lives of Taiwanese citizens. Moreover, an earthquake that hit eastern Taiwan in 2024 caused TSMC factories in Tainan to shut down temporarily, as chip fabs are designed to automatically cease production when any tremors occur. For instance, EUV chipmaking machines possess sensors that detect infinitesimal movements that cannot be noticed by humans; if the EUV machine senses the floor moving, it will shut down completely. Indeed, continuing to print during tremors can blur the circuit lines and potentially result in significant financial losses as wafers must be discarded. Hence, moving factories to locations like Arizona helps mitigate natural disaster risks such as earthquakes and provides a more controllable environment, rendering chip production lines more efficient. Given the relative availability of land, water, and electrical resources in North America, building factories in the United States may ultimately be beneficial for maintaining the stability of the Taiwanese production lines. By expanding its manufacturing capacity overseas, TSMC can reduce its exposure to geopolitical risks – and, in the event of war, help sustain the industrial capacity of the “arsenal of democracy.” For more than seven decades , Taiwan has faced persistent tensions across the Taiwan Strait, which have intensified in recent years and created significant geopolitical uncertainty. A war in the Taiwan Strait could severely disrupt global semiconductor supply chains, triggering shortages of advanced chips and inflicting trillions of dollars in economic losses worldwide. If key fabs in Taiwan are damaged or destroyed, rebuilding the lost production capacity could take years. By expanding its manufacturing capacity into the United States, TSMC can help key geopolitical partners like America maintain access to chips during wartime situations. Soft Power and Continuity Many Taiwanese argue that TSMC is the “ silicon shield ” protecting Taiwan against China. Therefore, they claim that the protection of this shield would be forfeited should TSMC build more factories in the United States. However, I believe TSMC’s global expansion can also help Taiwan garner greater international recognition by building stronger connections with local communities overseas. One example is the collaboration between Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing (JASM) and the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation, which brought Taiwan’s OneSong Orchestra to Kumamoto for a cultural concert . When locals connect with Taiwanese culture through these activities, it transforms Taiwan from an unfamiliar chip supplier into a culturally rich nation that bonds with local communities on a personal level. Such community bonds naturally encourage local communities to support strong diplomatic ties between their government and that of Taiwan. Additionally, these community investments extend into classrooms, where local universities partner with TSMC to build a new generation of semiconductor professionals who have been trained through Taiwanese resources. In the context of Japan, cultural exchanges between TSMC and the local community not only strengthen the company’s ties with Kumamoto residents, but also help build public support for its overseas expansion. In this sense, TSMC’s overseas expansion does more than diversify production—it can also expand Taiwan’s international presence and strengthen its ties with key partners around the world. Many Taiwanese refer to TSMC as the nation’s “Guardian Mountain” (護國神山) because of its crucial role in safeguarding Taiwan’s economic prosperity and national security. TSMC’s global expansion can strengthen the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain, bring production closer to its customers, expand its business opportunities, create new possibilities for young Taiwanese, and enhance Taiwan’s international presence. Some Taiwanese elders may worry that sending engineers to the United States represents a loss of human resources for Taiwan. However, these Taiwanese engineers are not abandoning Taiwan. Instead, they are stepping into global leadership roles and establishing important cross-border industry networks. When these professionals eventually return to Taiwan, they will be able to train the next generation of engineers preparing to go overseas and advance Taiwan’s economic prosperity. Expanding into the United States, therefore, does not mark the end of TSMC’s role as Taiwan’s “Guardian Mountain.” Rather, it is a pragmatic step toward ensuring that TSMC can continue to fulfill that role in a rapidly changing world. One Youth’s Perspective As a junior in the International Bilingual School at Hsinchu-Science-Park, many of my classmates’ parents are employed at TSMC. Drawing inspiration from their parents, some have also decided to pursue a career at TSMC. The establishment of TSMC Arizona has encouraged even more of them to pursue this track, and many of my peers are excited about the new job opportunities abroad that have been created. Indeed, these new job opportunities appeal to Taiwanese teenagers who had never yet been able to imagine their part in the “American Dream.” Ironically, according to a 2024 ABC News/Ipsos survey of US adults, public confidence in the American Dream has significantly eroded. Yet, new TSMC subsidiaries in the United States not only stabilize the production chain but also help revive the long-faded “American Dream” for Taiwanese youth. The main point: While many commentators in Taiwan suggest that TSMC’s expansion to the United States weakens Taiwan’s economic and national security, the business decisions may actually prove more economically viable, and relieve pressure on Taiwan’s grid and water supply. Meanwhile, the opportunities to work in the United States revive the long-faded “American Dream” among Taiwanese youth. title: Fruit at the Forefront of a Trade and Diplomatic Push
zh_title: 处于贸易和外交推动前沿的水果
source: 华盛顿全球台湾研究中心
summary: 下载全文 PDF 今年，来自台湾的新鲜水果首次出现在英国和法国的超市货架上，这让英国和法国的购物者大饱眼福。第一批来自台南的优质欧文芒果和来自台中的黑叶荔枝混合装运，已于六月初在英国曼彻斯特清关。此后不久，台湾芒果也抵达法国，尽管每颗芒果的售价高达29美元，但仍深受法国消费者的欢迎。不到一个月的时间，超过四吨的水果被运走。
content:
下载全文 PDF 今年，来自台湾的新鲜水果首次出现在英国和法国的超市货架上，这让英国和法国的购物者大饱眼福。第一批来自台南的优质欧文芒果和来自台中的黑叶荔枝混合装运，已于六月初在英国曼彻斯特清关。此后不久，台湾芒果也抵达法国，尽管每颗芒果的售价高达29美元，但仍深受法国消费者的欢迎。不到一个月的时间，四吨多的水果就被卖光了。获得将台湾产品运送到欧洲高度保护的关税区的官方许可是一个复杂的过程。该地区与农产品相关的进口法规具有严格的限制性，因为它们涵盖了从标签和农药暴露到农产品如何销售的方方面面。因此，经过“多年的谈判和技术准备”，台北驻欧盟和比利时代表处于2025年宣布获得芒果和番石榴进口清关，这是一项伟大的成就。八个月后，荔枝和火龙果获得批准。欧洲并不是台湾水果出口唯一面临挑战的目的地。台湾农业部门的官员也寻求向新西兰出口菠萝。
这一努力始于2013年新西兰与台澎金马单独关税区经济合作协定（ANZTEC，纽西兰与台澎金马关税领域经济合作定）的签署。经过八年的ANZTEC修正案双边谈判，新西兰终于打开了优质台湾菠萝的大门。 2025年5月，即ANZTEC修订案获得批准两年后，第一批台湾菠萝抵达新西兰市场。减少对单一市场的依赖 2010 年，台湾加入世界贸易组织 (WTO) 前后，台湾的水果开始在许多传统市场失去竞争力，其中包括日本和菲律宾。随着台湾农业面临新的国际竞争，海峡两岸经济合作框架协议（ECFA，海峡两岸经济合作架构协议）为台湾水果创造了机会，导致对单一市场中国的出口大幅增长。 ECFA是送给台湾农民的一份礼物。颁布两年后，台湾农产品出口总额增长了百分之八以上。其中，对中国的水果出口增长了42%；香蕉、哈密瓜、柠檬、红火龙果等早期收获清单上的农产品比2007年猛增42%。然而，受ECFA保护的农产品贸易并没有持续太久。
2021 年 2 月和 9 月，中国突然停止从台湾进口——首先是菠萝，然后是糖苹果和莲雾——声称检查中在多批货物中发现了柑橘粉蚧。 ECFA 批评者表示，中国本来就不是一个可行的长期市场。中国开始种植和培育曾经是台湾标志性水果的水果，侵蚀了对台湾出口的需求。此外，北京开始利用进口水果作为象征性的大棒来迫使台湾就范。中华经济研究院颜慧欣曾警告台湾有必要减少对中国市场的依赖，她写道：“

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Shoppers in the United Kingdom and France got a treat when supplies of fresh fruit from Taiwan found their way onto their supermarket shelves for the first time this year . The first batch, a mixed shipment of premium Irwin mangoes from Tainan and black-leaf lychees from Taichung, cleared customs in the British city of Manchester in early June. Taiwan’s mangoes also arrived in France shortly thereafter , enjoying overwhelming popularity among French consumers despite the astonishing price tag of $29 USD per fruit. In less than a month, more than four tons of the fruit were sold out. Getting an official permit to send Taiwan produce into Europe’s highly protected customs area is a complicated process. The region’s produce-related import regulations are highly restrictive, as they cover everything ranging from labelling and pesticide exposure, to how the produce can be marketed . Therefore, it marked a great achievement when the Taipei Representative Office in the European Union (EU) and Belgium announced in 2025 that it had received clearance for mango and guava imports , after “years of negotiations and technical preparations.” Approvals for lychees and dragon fruit followed eight months later. Europe was not the only challenging destination for Taiwan’s fruit exports. Taiwan’s officials in agricultural sectors also sought to export pineapples to New Zealand. The endeavor began with the signing of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, and Matsu on Economic Cooperation (ANZTEC, 紐西蘭與臺澎金馬個別關稅領域經濟合作協 定) in 2013. Eight years of bilateral negotiations on the amendments to ANZTEC finally opened New Zealand’s doors to premium Taiwan pineapples. In May of 2025—two years after the ANZTEC revisions were approved—the first batch of Taiwan’s pineapples arrived in the New Zealand market. Reducing Dependence on a Single Market In 2010, around the time of Taiwan’s accession into the World Trade Organization (WTO), the island’s fruit began losing competitiveness in many of its traditional markets, which included Japan and the Philippines . As Taiwan’s agricultural industry scrambled in the face of new international competition, the Cross Straits Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA, 海峽兩岸經濟合作架構協 議) created an opportunity for Taiwan’s fruit, resulting in a huge jump in exports into a single market : China. ECFA was a gift for Taiwanese farmers. Two years after it was promulgated, Taiwan’s total agricultural exports increased more than eight percent. Particularly, fruit exports to China grew 42 percent; and produce on the early harvest list, such as bananas, hami melons, lemons, and red dragon fruits, surged 42 percent compared to 2007. Nevertheless, the agricultural trade protected by ECFA did not last. In February and September 2021, China abruptly ended its imports from Taiwan—first pineapples, then sugar apples and wax apples—claiming that inspections had discovered citrus mealybugs in a number of shipments. ECFA critics say China was not a viable long-term market to begin with. China started growing and cultivating what used to be Taiwan’s signature fruits, eroding demand for Taiwan’s exports. Additionally, Beijing began to use fruit imports as a figurative stick to bring Taiwan to heel. Huai-Shing Yen (顏慧 欣 ) of the Chung Hua Institution for Economic Research (中華經濟研究 院 ) had warned of the need to reduce Taiwan’s reliance on the Chinese market, writing that: “The high concentration structure (of exports to China) makes it certain that the import restrictions will have a commercial impact on relevant farmers in Taiwan. As such, China’s actions to restrict imports are loud reminders of the vulnerability that this ‘export dependence’ causes for these agricultural products.” Yen also warned that even if Taiwan had sought to seek redress for China’s actions through the WTO, China “would not be obliged to enter consultations or negotiations with Taiwan.” Instead, Taiwan should seek alternatives, more reliable markets for its products. Weeks after China’s sugar apple and wax apple ban, the then-Council of Agriculture (COA, 行政院農業委員會 ) announced a strategy that sought to capitalize on existing and potential demand for Taiwanese fruit both inside and outside the country. Image: Local officials in Pingtung County (southeastern Taiwan) pose with a shipment of various fruits— mangoes, lychees, and dragon fruit—bound for shipment to Europe under the terms of new trade agreements with the European Union (June 2026). (Image source: Central News Agency ) Cold Chain Logistics: The Unsung Hero Today, Taiwanese fruit is sold at a premium in supermarkets and specialty retailers in numerous countries, such as Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Brunei and Palau—but the produce would not have made it beyond its shores without advancements in Taiwan’s cold chain logistics industry. The Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI, 工業技術研究 院) , a non-government R&D organization that incubated Taiwan’s semiconductor industry , has been dedicated to the development of cold chain logistics since the 1990s . Janet Chen (陳慧 娟) , General Director of ITRI’s Service Systems Technology Center, told this author that there are similarities to transporting fruit and semiconductors, as they both have strict requirements in temperature, humidity, and cleanliness: “Agricultural products must be kept within appropriate temperature and humidity ranges to slow deterioration and preserve freshness and nutritional value. Semiconductor components may also be sensitive to temperature and humidity. Clean storage and transportation environments help prevent cross-contamination and microbial growth in agricultural cold chains. Semiconductor manufacturing requires exceptionally clean environments because even microscopic particles can cause defects.” Chen adds: “Freshness is a major source of value for agricultural products, making timely delivery essential. Semiconductor supply chains also require fast and reliable transportation because delays may lead to missed business opportunities, inventory shortages, or production disruptions. Agricultural cold chains require traceability from farm to table to support food safety and quality control.” [1] Government Ensures Taiwan’s Fruit is Compliant The Ministry of Agriculture (MOA, 農業部) has also ensured that fruit exports comply with regulations that differ from territory to territory. For instance, mangoes heading to Europe must be subjected to heat treatment to kill off any pests or microbial hitchhikers, while pineapples bound for New Zealand must be harvested at a specific life stage . This is not to mention the various pesticide standards set in overseas markets. To support Taiwan’s farmers, the MOA and local governments in 2024 inaugurated a processing park in Yujing District in Tainan , which can process mango and pineapple to meet international standards. Its Produce Processing and Cold Chain Logistics Center ( 玉井農產加工及冷鏈物流中心) is equipped with pre-cooling, processing, refrigeration, and freezer zones capable of processing as much as 800 tons of mangoes a year. External uncertainties highlight the significance of transport quality control. Kris Tang, General Manager of fruit exporter Sunray Fresh ( 昇睿鮮 農) , revealed to this author that during their first commercial shipment, fruit travelled via Frankfurt in the midst of a staffing shortage and a heat wave. “The mango and lychee could not be placed on the same onward flight to the UK and had to arrive separately. (By then), our priority was not simply to preserve the original schedule, but to protect the quality and integrity of the products.” [2] Gaining entry into Europe’s market is a good start—but more needs to be done if Taiwanese farmers are to cut their reliance on the Chinese market entirely. Focus Taiwan has reported that the Taiwan still sold USD 370 million worth of fresh fruit to Hong Kong and China from 2020 to May 2026, while exports to Japan totaled USD 199.4 million during the same period. But exporters know that getting a foothold is just the first, albeit critical step. Tang told this author: “The first shipment was important, but it was only the beginning. What matters is whether we can create a repeatable and commercially sustainable route that allows more Taiwanese fruit and agricultural products to enter the UK and, eventually, the wider European market.” [3] The main point: Taiwan’s move away from relying on a handful of traditional export markets like China has opened new doors for its fruit exports. That pivot, which also resulted in new technological innovation within Taiwan’s cold-chain logistics system, opened new markets in Europe for Taiwan’s mangoes and lychees. Developing its fruit market has also paved the way for Taiwan’s exports beyond high-tech products. [1] Author’s interview, summer 2026. [2] Author’s interview, summer 2026. [3] Ibid. title: “Last Year We Needed Volunteers, This Year We Need Tourists”: Reviving Post-Disaster Tourism in Eastern Taiwan

下载整期 PDF 城镇重建很久之后，它的形象可能仍停留在过去。潜在的游客可能会通过过时的图像和以前的灾难头条新闻来查看这个地方。如果没有足够的保证或激励，他们会比必要的时间更长时间地避开，忘记这个地方曾经是，而且仍然可以是一个度假胜地。这种现象给依赖旅游业为生的居民和企业带来了一场延迟的、不太明显的灾难。花莲县横跨台湾东北海岸和山谷。该地区的经济依赖旅游业，但由于历史上的自然灾害而遭受重挫。对于花莲来说，该行业约占全县就业和产值的40%。该县的光福镇经历了 2024 年地区性地震对旅游业的影响和 2025 年洪水造成的自然破坏，目前正在努力应对游客量长期低迷的问题。本文通过对当地人的采访和第一手研究，探讨了居民在灾后努力重建城镇吸引力的经历，并探讨了政府迄今为止为支持旅游业恢复所做的努力。它还详细说明了政府应采取哪些进一步措施来真正重振经济。本案例研究揭示了灾后重建的长期现实以及重振当地经济所需的政府干预规模。
这也对台湾在国际舞台上的韧性提出了更广泛的问题：当自然灾害和更广泛的危险认知威胁到旅游业时，目的地如何保持游客的信心？由头条新闻定义的小镇光复镇坐落在台湾花莲县花东裂谷，长期以来以其田园风光、自行车路线和原住民文化而闻名。花莲北部该地区的主要旅游景点太鲁阁峡谷吸引的国际游客会顺着峡谷而下，在光复寺停留欣赏风景并在附近的温泉休息。但近两年来，该地区的旅游业经受了严峻考验。 2024年4月，花莲地震给我们带来了第一波打击。太鲁阁峡谷在地震中受损严重，连接台北和花莲的高速公路暂时被封锁。花莲市一栋倒塌建筑物的图片出现在全球主要新闻媒体的头版上。来台国际游客数量锐减，国内游客将假期从花莲转移到其他地方。峡谷以南的所有乡镇都受到旅游业下降的影响。尽管如此，光复并不是受灾最严重的地区之一，它位于花莲市以南一小时车程的地方。居民经历了强烈的震动，建筑物遭受了结构性影响，但受损程度并不像北部城市地区那么严重。
花莲县的大部分地区都是低层房屋，周围环绕着连绵起伏的农田和山脉。该地区很幸运，基本上避免了新闻报道中花莲市的破坏场景。然而，广泛传播的这座城市的图像让人感觉整个县都遭到了破坏，因此参观不安全。在高速公路再次向游客开放后，这个观点仍然存在很长一段时间。图片：X 上危险倾斜的天王星大厦附近的救援人员和设备

DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Long after a town rebuilds itself, its image can remain stuck in the past. Potential visitors may view the place through outdated images and previous disaster headlines. Without enough reassurance or incentives, they steer clear for longer than necessary, forgetting that the place was, and still can be, a holiday destination. This phenomenon results in a delayed, less visible disaster for residents and businesses whose livelihoods depend on tourism. Hualien County stretches over the northeastern coast and valleys of Taiwan. The area’s economy relies on the tourism industry, which has been set back due to a history of natural disasters. For Hualien, that sector accounts for around 40 percent of the county’s employment and output value. A township within this county, Guangfu, is grappling with a particularly prolonged downturn in visitors, having weathered both the tourism fallout of a regional earthquake in 2024 and the physical devastation of floods in 2025. Through interviews with locals and first-hand research, this piece explores the experiences of residents struggling to rebuild a town’s appeal post-disaster, and examines the government’s efforts to support tourism recovery to date. It also details what further steps the government should take to genuinely revive the economy. This case study reveals the long-term realities of post-disaster reconstruction and the scale of government intervention needed to re-energize a local economy. It also raises wider questions for Taiwan’s resilience on the international stage: how can a destination maintain visitor confidence when natural disasters—and broader perceptions of danger—threaten tourism? A Township Defined by Headlines Guangfu Township, nestled in the East Rift Valley of Hualien County, Taiwan, was long known for its rural scenery, cycling routes, and indigenous culture. International tourists drawn in by Taroko Gorge, the region’s main tourist attraction in north Hualien, would make their way down the valley, stopping by Guangfu to enjoy the view and rest in the nearby hot springs. But in the last two years, the area’s tourism industry has been severely tested. In April 2024, the Hualien earthquake dealt the first blow. Taroko Gorge was considerably damaged by the earthquake, and the highway connecting Taipei and Hualien was temporarily blocked. Images of a collapsed building in Hualien City were displayed on front pages of major global news outlets . The number of international visitors to Taiwan plummeted and domestic visitors redirected their holidays away from Hualien. No township south of the gorge was spared the impact of the drop in tourism. This said, Guangfu was not amongst the most severely damaged areas, being situated one hour south of Hualien City by car. Residents experienced strong tremors and buildings sustained structural impacts, although the extent of the damage was not as severe as in the urban areas to the north. Much of this part of Hualien County is made up of low-rise houses surrounded by rolling farmland and mountains. The region was fortunate to largely avoid the scenes of destruction in Hualien City that dominated the news. Nevertheless, the widely broadcasted images of the city contributed to a perception that the whole county was devastated and therefore unsafe to visit. This viewpoint remained long after the highway was opened to visitors again. Image: Rescue workers and equipment near the dangerously-leaning Uranus Building on Xuanyuan Road in Hualien City, in the immediate aftermath of the April 3, 2024 Hualien earthquake. (Image source: ROC Presidential Office / Wikimedia Commons ) In 2024, the National Tourism Administration (交通部觀光署) offered subsidies for six months following the earthquake , in order to stimulate tourism recovery in Hualien. This included the “Hualien Independent Travel Accommodation Subsidy” (花蓮自由行住宿補助) , featuring an NTD 1000 (around USD 30) rebate on the first night, with an additional NTD 1500 (around USD 47) provided on the second. This was combined with discounts on charter flights , shuttles , amusement parks and local products. With Taroko Gorge still shut, the county government diversified regional branding, releasing the video, “ On the Way to Eastern Taiwan: Travel Freely with Peace of Mind , ” and hosting international marketing shows alongside local spotlight events such as the 2024 World Bicycle Day. These initiatives reportedly helped tourism activities in Hualien reach pre-earthquake rates from 2025 , though it is unclear what proportion of these numbers trickled down to townships in the south, such as Guangfu. However, in September 2025, just as tourists were returning to the region, Guangfu Township faced a second blow which left a more devastating impact to the community. The overflowing of a nearby barrier lake caused flash floods, which sent mud and debris into homes and businesses. The floods also left many stranded after a lack of comprehensive evacuation notices caught locals off guard. Fellow citizens arrived in extraordinary numbers to aid in cleanup efforts, with an estimated 30,000 volunteers appearing on September 27, and tens of thousands more in the following weeks. Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿) in Guangfu, recalls their arrival after his shop’s cooking equipment had been washed away: “It brings tears to my eyes to remember. The warmth of Taiwanese people, you never forget that.” [1] The government emergency response was swift. The Legislative Yuan (立法院) passed a NTD 27 billion (USD 859 million) special budget to rebuild parts of the township damaged by the floods, and offered temporary housing, reconstruction loans, and cleanup subsidies to victims. The county government dispatched 790 mud removal trucks and cooperated with the bike rental company YouBike to temporarily install bike stations . When I visited a year later, the relief efforts of both government and private charities had significantly reduced the physical damage of the floods. Many businesses have reopened and locals await the return of visitors. But now, a less visible crisis is unfolding in Guangfu. Many tourists still skip the township, deterred by the lingering perception that conditions there are wet and muddy at best, or dangerous at worst. Ongoing disaster-related reporting continues to dominate the media, re-enforcing the perception of Guangfu as a township still in devastation. Locals are therefore struggling to keep their businesses afloat. Rebuilding public confidence in the township as a tourist destination is a challenge residents cannot shoulder alone. It will require a different kind of targeted, strategic support from the government. Image: Volunteer EMT workers treat wounds in Guangfu Township (Hualien County) in the wake of massive flooding that caused extensive damage throughout the area. (Image source: Central News Agency / YouTube ) Tourist Restoration Policies Beyond Physical Recovery Two challenges remain when it comes to sustainably revitalizing Guangfu’s economy. First, government funding in Guangfu has so far prioritized the concrete efforts of physical restoration over the more abstract needs of tourism recovery. The initial response to the floods by both the central and county governments was remarkable in both speed and scale, with much of Guangfu’s physical infrastructure restored in under a year. Now, government support should extend beyond emergency relief and employ a strategic approach to sustaining the long-term survival of local industries. “People might have their homes again, but what can they do with no livelihood? We need further government support to promote the township and help our businesses get back on their feet,” says “Uncle Tien” ( 田克靚 ), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse ( 見青小築民宿) , whose monthly revenue has been down by 50-80 percent since the autumn of 2025. [2] Second, Guangfu has received limited visibility within Hualien’s wider tourism promotion efforts. The county government has continued since 2024 to launch tourism marketing campaigns to attract international and domestic visitors to the region. However, initiatives tend to be concentrated on north Hualien County and Hualien City. A staff member managing tourism affairs at the Guangfu Township Office (光復鄉公所) confirmed to me that while the office is keen to promote Guangfu’s tourism assets, there are currently no county-level initiatives aimed at helping Guangfu boost the industry. Local officials are committed to revitalizing tourism but seemingly lack the resources and funding required to conduct sustained, large-scale promotional efforts. [3] It is understandable that Hualien’s tourism efforts were focused elsewhere while Guangfu was still undergoing extensive physical restoration. With the township now largely cleared, though, there is a stronger case for requesting additional funding from the county or central governments for campaigns that put Guangfu at the center of tourism promotion. A Focused Strategy for Restoring Tourist Confidence With the help of county and central government, a tailored tourism-recovery framework could be coordinated for the township. This could include: More accurate, balanced information on conditions and daily life on the ground. Coordinated travel campaigns and incentives. Investment in tourism infrastructure. First, more widely publicized information on the township’s recovery and travel conditions will help accelerate the shift in perceptions. Clear, sustained, and positive communication about regional safety and accessibility, as well as regular local government broadcasting of daily life and cultural events will rebuild the public’s trust. This includes both earthquake-related safety assurances and post-flood recovery stories. “Many people worry that it is unsafe here. But the government has done a great deal to ensure our buildings are secure. Clearer public information on this would help reassure visitors,” says breakfast shop owner Li Jen-i. [4] “Guangfu has recovered quickly from the floods, and life has largely returned to normal for many residents. We hope that coverage of the township can better reflect that reality,” say Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), guesthouse owners of Breadfruit B&B (麵包樹舍). They add: “People forget how accessible and peaceful this part of Taiwan is as a holiday destination.” [5] Indeed, despite media coverage focusing primarily on areas under construction, a notable portion of the township was not touched by the floods. The main tourist attractions remain open here, such as the Matai’an Xinlü Farm (馬太鞍欣綠農園 ), where visitors can learn about the indigenous ecological knowledge of the Amis indigenous people (阿美族) ; and the Guangfu Sugar Factory (光復糖廠 ), which dates back to the Japanese period . Without this information to counter negative news coverage, many continue to assume Guangfu is a no-go zone. Second, to effectively promote the township nation-wide and beyond, Guangfu needs the resources of a coordinated government-backed tourism promotion program. Eye-catching marketing campaigns showcasing the area’s rural charm and scenery could be rolled out on social media and displayed in trains, underground (MRT) stations in cities nationwide, and international airports in both Taiwn and abroad. To provide additional financial incentives for people to visit, subsidized travel packages and discounted transport tickets, akin to Hualien County’s post-earthquake discounts, could be reintroduced and adapted for Guangfu. Image: “Laoye” (盧政惠) and “Juju” (陳慧秋), the proprietors of “Breadfruit B&B” (麵包樹舍) in the town of Guangfu (Hualien County) (July 2026). (Image source: Author’s photograph) If the county’s existing tourism campaigns elsewhere in Hualien County are indeed proving effective, the wheel does not need to be reinvented. Government officials can build on existing initiatives and direct them where the region requires further support. Policy lessons can also be taken from abroad. Following the 2019-2020 bushfires in Australia, tourism hotspots across New South Wales struggled with avalanches of cancellations for months . Similarly, f ollowing the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes , towns in Japan experienced protracted slumps in tourism. In both cases, government-funded campaigns and incentives helped boost the recovery of the tourism industry, which encouraged people to travel in an ordinary fashion, rather than to see residents solely as victims needing support . Third, travel promotion and incentives in Guangfu could be matched with continued investment in tourism infrastructure. While the township is easy to reach by direct train and car hire is convenient, the government can pursue further investment in a number of transit methods to enhance the township’s accessibility. These include expanding bike hire options, improving bus services, and introducing shuttle buses between local attractions. Taiwan already boasts 84 shuttle bus routes country-wide. Until Guangfu enjoys better transport services, reliance on car travel will create barriers for those who cannot drive or who do not hold driving licenses. Taiwan has a strong track record of strategic tourism promotion and infrastructure development. A clear tourism roadmap would build on the government’s existing strengths, putting its tools to work for a township in need of greater support. Lessons in Post-Disaster Recovery for Taiwan and the World Cases of natural disasters in Guangfu have shown that while physical restoration can take place remarkably quickly, the harder task is ensuring that local industries recover long-term. This experience can offer lessons that extend well beyond Taiwan. As climate change intensifies the frequency and severity of extreme weather worldwide, governments will increasingly be required to consider the protracted effects of these occurrences on local communities. Building strong strategies to ensure long-term recovery is crucial. Taiwan, meanwhile, has particular reasons to strengthen its capacity for resilience. Its exposure to natural disasters, as well as ongoing concerns over geopolitical tensions in the Taiwan Strait, means that the government is constantly contending with international perceptions of a nation in danger. Taiwan needs to be able not only to rebuild industries after crises, but also to continuously reassure visitors that the country remains a safe and appealing destination. Guangfu offers a smaller-scale opportunity to test how strategic information sharing, combined with promotional tourism campaigns and incentives, can help reshape perceptions of a disaster-affected destination. The main point: Effectively reviving a local economy post-disaster and rebuilding its appeal to tourists requires a long-term, targeted approach from government. This includes strategic information sharing, promotional tourism campaigns and incentives, and infrastructure building. This case study of Guangfu, Hualien County—one year after devastating floods—sheds light on the necessary scale of government intervention and the pertinence of strengthening Taiwan’s tourism resilience both regionally and nationally. [1] Author’s interview with Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿), July 25, 2026. [2] Author’s interview with Uncle Tien ( 田克靚 ), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse ( 見青小築民宿) , July 26, 2026. [3] Author’s informal interview with Guangfu Township local official, July 24, 2026. [4] Author’s with Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿), July 25, 2026. [5] Author’s interview with Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), guesthouse owners of Breadfruit B&B (麵包樹舍), July 25, 2026. Acknowledgments: The author thanks Uncle Tien (田克靚), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse見青小築民宿; Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), owners of 麵包樹舍 Breadfruit B&B; and Li Jen-i (李仁義), owner of a breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿) for their time and insights during interviews for this article. The post “Last Year We Needed Volunteers, This Year We Need Tourists”: Reviving Post-Disaster Tourism in Eastern Taiwan appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

title: Before the Blockade: Marine Insurance’s Relevance to Taiwan’s Energy Lifeline
zh_title: 封锁前：海上保险与台湾能源生命线的关系
source: 华盛顿全球台湾研究中心
summary: 下载整期 PDF 如果发生台湾海峡危机，运往台中或台湾其他主要港口之一的液化天然气 (LNG) 货物的命运可能会变成一个商业问题：它还能获得战争险吗？由于海军规划受到与潜在封锁相关的大部分关注，因此北约的海事战略或欧盟的经济安全议程几乎没有涵盖海上保险。然而，保险公司的决定可能会像海军部署一样影响台湾。 2026 年发生的事件已经证明了这一点：2 月 28 日罢工之后

下载整期 PDF 如果发生台湾海峡危机，运往台中或台湾其他主要港口之一的液化天然气 (LNG) 货物的命运可能会变成一个商业问题：它还能获得战争险吗？由于海军规划受到与潜在封锁相关的大部分关注，因此北约的海事战略或欧盟的经济安全议程几乎没有涵盖海上保险。然而，保险公司的决定可能会像海军部署一样影响台湾。 2026 年发生的事件已经证明了这一点：2 月 28 日对伊朗发动袭击后，霍尔木兹海峡的航运停止了。没有宣布封锁，但保险公司取消了战争险保险、重新报价或大幅重新定价，流量在一周内下降了 80% 以上。劳合社的数据显示，3 月份仅有 181 艘船只过境，其中大部分与伊朗有关，而冲突前一天有 138 艘船只过境。六个月过去了，交通仍然没有恢复。劳合社情报机构统计，9 月 14 日至 20 日这一周内，有 117 起与伊朗无关的过境事件，比冲突前一天的数量还要少。其后果也影响到了台湾，因为台湾三分之​​一以上的天然气要经过霍尔木兹海峡，而大约 96% 的能源是进口的。虽然台湾一半以上的电力由燃气发电厂提供，但其液化天然气库存只能维持 11 天。
目前，政府要求安全库存为11天，并将在2027年增加到14天。同期存储容量预计将从20天增加到24天。所有三个接收站均位于西海岸，面向中华人民共和国（PRC）。这使得台湾的时间非常短：如果液化天然气输送停止，减载（即计划轮流停电）将在几天内开始，并且还需要电网来支持该岛的防御。图片：台湾高雄永安液化天然气接收站（资料照片日期不详）。 （图片来源：Wikimedia Commons） 海上保险如何关闭台湾海峡 商船通常为船舶投保船体险和战争险，并为船员受伤、污染、残骸清除和第三方损害等责任提供保护和赔偿 (P&I)。银行不会为未投保的船舶提供融资，承租人也不会租用一艘船舶。联合战争委员会 (JWC) 是一家总部位于伦敦的组织，由来自劳合社市场协会和国际承保协会的代表组成，汇集了承保海洋船体战争险的承保人。该委员会公布了一份被认为船只遭受战争相关危险风险增加的地理区域清单。因此，船东必须在进入该区域之前通知其保险公司，而保险公司可能会收取额外的风险保费。
此外，租船合同中的战争风险条款允许船东拒绝航行到所列区域，即使有保险。市场可能会在危机完全发生之前发生变化：2022年2月，在俄罗斯入侵乌克兰之前，JWC将黑海和亚速海添加到其所列区域中，以应对随后确实发生的预期情况。 2023年底红海列入名单后，运营商绕行南非好望角，而不是支付附加费。然而，标准的战争风险措辞会带来更大的后果：如果五个永久性国家中的任何两个之间爆发宣战或未宣战的战争，

DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF In the event of a Taiwan Strait crisis, the fate of a liquid natural gas (LNG) cargo bound for Taichung, or one of Taiwan’s other major ports, could turn into a commercial question: can it still obtain war-risk cover? As naval planning receives most of the attention in relation to a potential blockade, marine insurance is barely covered in either NATO’s maritime strategy or the European Union’s economic security agenda . However, an insurer’s decision could affect Taiwan as much as a naval deployment. Events in 2026 have demonstrated this: After the February 28 strikes against Iran, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz halted. No blockade was declared, but insurers canceled, requoted or sharply repriced war-risk cover, and traffic fell by more than 80 percent in a week. Lloyd’s List data showed just 181 vessel transits in March, mostly Iranian-linked, compared with 138 vessel transits a day before the conflict. Six months later, traffic has still not recovered. Lloyd’s List Intelligence counted 117 non-Iranian-linked transits in the week of September 14–20, fewer than on a single day before the conflict. The consequences also affected Taiwan, since more than a third of its gas goes through Hormuz, and about 96 percent of its energy resources are imported. While gas-fired plants generate more than half of Taiwan’s electricity, its working LNG stocks can only last for 11 days . Currently, the government requires a security s tockpile of 11 days, and will raise it to 14 in 2027 . Storage capacity is expected to rise from 20 to 24 days over the same period. All three receiving terminals are on the west coast, facing the People’s Republic of China (PRC). This leaves Taiwan with a very short clock: If LNG deliveries stop, load shedding (i.e., planned rolling blackouts) would begin within days, and the grid would also be needed to support the island’s defense. Image: The Yongan LNG Terminal in Kaohsiung, Taiwan (undated file photo). (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) How Marine Insurance Could Close the Taiwan Strait A merchant vessel normally has hull and war-risk insurance for the ship, and protection and indemnity (P&I) for liabilities, such as crew injuries, pollution, wreck removal and damage to third parties. Banks will not finance an uninsured ship, and charterers will not hire one. The Joint War Committee (JWC), a London-based organization with representatives from the Lloyd’s Market Association and the International Underwriting Association, brings together the underwriters who write marine hull war risk. This Committee publishes a list of geographical areas where vessels are considered at increased risk of war-related perils. Thus, shipowners must notify their insurers before entering the zone, and underwriters may charge an extra risk premium. Moreover, war-risk clauses in charter parties allow owners to refuse a voyage into a listed area, even when cover is available. The market can move before a crisis fully materializes: in February 2022, before the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the JWC added the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov to its Listed Areas in response to an anticipated situation that subsequently did materialize. When the Red Sea was listed at the end of 2023, operators diverted around the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa, instead of paying the surcharge. However, standard war-risk wording carries a larger consequence: If war, declared or undeclared, breaks out between any two of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council , insurance cover ends automatically. Therefore, a conflict between the People’s Republic of China and the United States over Taiwan would fall within the automatic termination clause of the standard Institute War and Strikes Clauses. France and the United Kingdom could also act as contractual triggers rather than distant observers. Lessons from the Hormuz Strait The Hormuz conflict shows how quickly this can happen. War-risk rates for Gulf transits were at 0.25 percent of hull value pre-conflict, but rose sharply within days. Marine insurers Gard, Skuld, NorthStandard, the London P&I Club, and the American Club issued cancellation notices on March 1. Two days later, the JWC extended the Listed Areas across the Gulf littoral, and maritime traffic collapsed. Underwriters in London pushed back against the claim that insurance had closed the Strait, claiming that insurance cover remained available. Instead, cancellation notices were deemed a contractual way to renegotiate terms. Owners kept ships in port because they feared for the safety of their crews and vessels, not because insurance could not be bought. However, insurance contracts had a political impact on shipping decisions around the world within 48 hours, even though no closure orders were issued. Changing the price and terms of risk was enough to halt maritime traffic without a naval blockade. Washington tried to fill the gap: On March 11, the US International Development Finance Corporation named Chubb as lead underwriter for a USD 20 billion maritime reinsurance facility, expanded to USD 40 billion on April 3. Despite this, the measure had limited effect s: It covered the Strait but not the surrounding waters, and excluded loss of life and environmental damage, liabilities of greatest concern to P&I clubs and shipowners. Image: An interior shot of the Lloyd’s Building in London, headquarters of the maritime insurance conglomerate Lloyd’s of London (Sep. 2014). (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) Inserting Taiwan into the Marine Insurance Ecosystem Taiwan lacks institutional channels with key decisionmakers. The JWC works with security advisers, officials and shipping companies, but Taiwan has no standing in the process because it is not formally recognized by most European institutions. Despite this, Taiwanese companies Evergreen, Yang Ming, and Wan Hai rank among the world’s larger carriers . However, in the first week of a crisis, private entities acting in their own commercial interests would decide whether LNG carriers keep sailing, as their choice would be based on Beijing’s capacity to exert influence and coercion. This gap does not necessarily imply bad faith from insurers. Governments have used insurance as a tool of coercion for more than a decade: In 2012, the European Union banned P&I cover for Iranian oil cargoes ; and Security Council Resolution 2321 (2016) prohibited insurance for North Korean vessels. Thus, the PRC knows how these mechanisms work. A permanent forum could close the gap. It should bring American, Taiwanese, British, French and Nordic officials together with the JWC, the International Group, and the main war-risk underwriters. The purpose is to ensure that the committee knows what escort plans, port measures and public guarantees are actually available in the Taiwan Strait, rather than relying on signals Beijing sends. It could be based on the example of c ounter-piracy coordination off Somalia , where governments and industry representatives met and the London market adjusted its Listed Areas as conditions changed. Opportunities for US-Taiwan Collaboration The US government also needs a public backstop before a crisis. Senator Pete Ricketts’s Taiwan Energy Security and Anti-Embargo Act , reported out of committee in January 2026, and Representative Pat Harrigan’s companion House bill would authorize the US Maritime Administration to insure foreign-flagged vessels carrying critical goods to Taiwan if commercial cover were withdrawn. Nevertheless, a Taiwan facility would have to cover the approaches, adjacent waters, crew liability, and environmental damage from day one—and not two weeks later, as it happened in Hormuz. This facility would also have to state in advance how public insurance operates when the five-powers clause ends commercial cover, as this cannot be improvised during a quarantine. Taiwan should be part of those preparations, whether or not it is formally recognized: information about terminal resilience, escort plans, and grid capacity would affect an underwriter’s assessment. Taipei could also negotiate in advance with LNG suppliers and their European insurers on the conditions under which deliveries would continue, which is more cost-effective before a crisis. Marine insurance should be part of Taiwan’s agenda when engaging with Europe, alongside semiconductors. Even though insurers and shipowners did not formally acknowledge the closure of Hormuz in 2026, the events that followed made the Strait unusable for most commercial traffic. Taiwan should start coordinating with the committee in London now to establish a strategy ahead of any future contingency. The main point: Decisions by war-risk underwriters in London could halt LNG deliveries to Taiwan before any naval blockade, as the 2026 Hormuz crisis has showed. Taiwan has no channel to the committee that lists high-risk areas, and a war between the United States and the PRC would end commercial cover automatically. Taipei and Washington should open a standing dialogue with the London market now, and define in advance the public insurance that would take over. The post Before the Blockade: Marine Insurance’s Relevance to Taiwan’s Energy Lifeline appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Hong Kong customs have arrested 10 people and seized about 120,000 suspected duty-not-paid cigarettes in a territory-wide operation targeting retail outlets including newsstands and grocery stores, the department said on Wednesday.

The contraband, estimated to have a market value of about HK$540,000 and a duty value of about HK$400,000, was confiscated in an operation that began last Wednesday, according to a customs statement.

Officers posed as customers in test purchases and found some outlets selling cigarettes at prices below the statutory duty level. Those arrested, three men and seven women aged 26 to 73, included shop owners and staff.

Customs said that since the Smoking (Amendment) Ordinance 2025 was gazetted in mid-September last year, it has conducted frequent inspections of cigarette retail points and launched multiple enforcement operations, including decoy purchases.

In total, 38 cigarette retail outlets have been shut down, about 450,000 duty-not-paid cigarettes seized and 39 people arrested under the enforcement drive, the department said. Eleven cases have completed judicial proceedings, with sentences ranging from four weeks to six months in jail, while the remaining cases are pending court action.
