The complainants alleged that the respondents watched the house burn from beside a white vehicle nearby. Emil said he later found gasoline containers on the property.

The allegations have yet to be established in court.

The couple said Aquino had been claiming about 260 square meters of the property since 2023 while Lucas attended barangay meetings as his attorney-in-fact.

*   ![Image 1: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

A June 9, 2025 letter signed by Lucas as UPACC chairperson asked the barangay captain to investigate and remove the fence and a hut on the disputed property.

The complaint also cited an alleged statement by Aquino days before the fire: "Si Ma'am Pyra na lang ang bahala sa inyo" (Ma'am Pyra will take care of you).

It further referenced a neighbor's account that Aquino allegedly said the group had agreed only to scare the family. The neighbor was not identified as a firsthand witness to the fire.

The BFP, meanwhile, classified the fire as intentional, citing clean burn patterns, substantial material loss in the middle of the structure and the absence of an accidental heat source.

*   ![Image 2: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Fire responders arrived at 5:37 p.m., when the blaze had already been extinguished. The BFP estimated the damage at P200,000 and said evidence had been submitted for forensic analysis.

In a letter to The Manila Times, Lucas denied committing or intending to commit destructive arson, saying her involvement in the dispute was limited to asking barangay officials to address the fence and nipa hut on land belonging to Aquino.

Lucas said she had written to barangay officials in Bueno, Capas, Tarlac, requesting an investigation into the structures, which she described as illegally built on Aquino’s property. She said she had asked officials to resolve the matter through lawful and peaceful means.

“We did not commit any illegal acts,” Lucas said.

*   ![Image 3: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

She maintained that her presence in the area did not establish criminal liability and rejected the allegations against her.

“My mere presence in the area cannot be considered a crime,” she said, adding that she believed the accusations were politically motivated and intended to harass her and malign her reputation.

Lucas also alleged that, months before the complaint was filed, she had received information that the Cadiangs would be used to bring a fabricated case against her.

She offered a counter-account of the fire, saying passersby had seen Emil inside the nipa hut while it was burning. She described the structure as having been illegally built on Aquino’s property.

title: Lawyer Sherily Cua makes memorable debut in Cagayan de Oro chess
summary: Cagayan de Oro City —‎The first time Woman Fide Master Sherily Cua set foot in the City of Gold for competitive chess, she made it personally memorable as the ‎three-time representative of the Philippines at the World Chess Olympiad emerged
content:
Cagayan de Oro City —‎The first time Woman Fide Master Sherily Cua set foot in the City of Gold for competitive chess, she made it personally memorable as the ‎three-time representative of the Philippines at the World Chess Olympiad emerged champion in the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) National Games 2026 Chess Tournament.

‎The Cagayan de Oro hosting of the prestigious IBF chessfest was held Oct. 9 at SM Uptown which saw the Central Luzon pawnpushers sharing the spotlight with Cua by lording it over in the team event.

‎"It's really fun to be here for the first time in Cagayan de Oro, playing on top of the pre-male dominated individual category. The many places for tourist spots, the good vibes, the food culture and peaceful environment to enjoy,"said Cua, a lawyer who wants to be an inspiration for the chess-playing youths that aspire to become legal professionals someday.

*   [WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

"Since chess involves strategic plans and thinking ahead in a smart way, it definitely gives an edge for a chess player to pursue law in college," she added.

‎‎The 39-year-old Cua, who represented‎ Southern Luzon Region, ruled the individual rapid category with a dominant 6.5 points performance in the 7-round Swiss System tournament.

‎Cua actually had a shaky start escaping from a losing position against Dabawenyo lawyer Roland Reyes in the first round before scoring three straight wins. She pulled off another nightmarish escape opposite lawyer Adrian Alain Llanos of Antique Chapter in the fifth round before settling for a draw with Lawrence Earl Roy Gersalia of Bicolandia in the sixth round.

‎Llanos settled for solo second place with 6 points, while defending champion Jason Maxino Bandal of Negros Oriental finished third after prevailing in the tie-break against Judylito Ulanday of Central Luzon.

‎Local bet Robert Manto of the Misamis Oriental Chapter put up a good fight for the home turf after a good start in the first four rounds with a win against Orlando Ba-alan of Palawan, Paulino Cangayo III of Bicolandia Region and Clifford Enoc of Central Visayas Chapter.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

‎Manto narrowly missed a win against Israel Colmo of Antique Chapter in the third round when he failed to convert his two-pawn advantage in the rook-and-pawn endgame.

‎Nonetheless, the Misamis Oriental pride Manto managed to climb to board two in the fifth round but lost in a seemingly equal position against Lawrence Earl Roy Gersalia of Bicolandia.

‎It was a heart-breaking loss for Manto as a win against Gersalia could pave the way for him to face Cua in the top board in the following round. He finished with 4.5 points.

‎Meanwhile, the Central Luzon Region team composed of Ulanday, Rodrigo Aquino Jr. and Gabrielle Kenth Hayashi, won the rapid team competition with an aggregate of 15 points after seven rounds, a full point ahead of the field.

*   ![Image 2: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)

‎The Central Luzon Region started strong in the early rounds with Bicolandia also holding its ground and even took the lead in the middle rounds.

‎Surprisingly, the Palawan Chapter —made up of Nazi Jester Erfe, Orlando Ba-alan and Jaquelene Ann Tambal —overtook Bicolandia in the last two rounds to claim the second spot with 14 points to show.

‎Eastern Visayas and Southern Luzon of Cua tied for third place with identical 13.5 points each, as Eastern Visayas secured solo third after superior tie-break points over Southern Luzon Region.

# 特朗普选举造势宣布台湾同意购买阿拉斯加30％天然气并投资44亿美元

美国总统特朗普13日在阿拉斯加州一场造势大会中，宣称台湾已同意在未来20年内采购阿拉斯加天然气管线开发计画中30%的天然气，并将额外投资44亿美元。台湾经济部表示，合作方向还包括开采后每年采购600万吨阿拉斯加液化天然气。

发表时间： 14/10/2026 - 10:36

 2026年10月13日，美国总统特朗普自安德鲁斯联合基地机场乘机，准备前往阿拉斯加参加中期选举造势活动。 REUTERS - Evan Vucci

 作者： [台北特约记者 陈筱涵](https://rfi.fr/cn/%E4%BD%9C%E8%80%85/%E5%8F%B0%E5%8C%97%E7%89%B9%E7%BA%A6%E8%AE%B0%E8%80%85-%E9%99%88%E7%AD%B1%E6%B6%B5/ "台北特约记者 陈筱涵")

继续浏览后续

根据《路透社》报导，美国总统特朗普13日在阿拉斯加州一场造势大会中，宣称台湾已同意在未来20年内，采购阿拉斯加天然气管线开发计画中30%的天然气，并将额外投资44亿美元。台湾的投资将建立在南韩承诺投入的500亿美元之上，是历来规模最大的承诺及交易之一。特朗普也赞扬这些承诺确保了计画的成功，不过外界对管线最终能否兴建仍有疑虑。

台湾中油在2025年3月曾与阿拉斯加瓦斯开发公司（Alaska Gasline Development Corp）签署不具法律约束力的意向书，计画采购液化天然气并投资该管线工程计画。并以此加强与特朗普政府的关系。当时赖清德总统表示，此举将能确保台湾的能源安全。

对此，台湾经济部回应，经过近一年半的密集协商及审慎评估，已与美国开发商取得重大进展。依目前规划，合作方向包括开采后每年采购600万吨阿拉斯加液化天然气，及参与专案开发，预估投资金额最高为44亿美元。

阿拉斯加液化天然气计画具备地理位置优势，可透过太平洋航线直达台湾，有助于分散天然气运输路线及地缘供应风险。若计画依规划期程顺利推进，预计最快可自2032年起进一步挹注台湾国内天然气供应，作为持续推动气源多元化的重要布局。

然而，对于如此大规模投资竟是透过特朗普造势活动宣布才得知，国民党立法院党团书记长许宇甄14日指责，赖政府对内喊能源安全，对外却连采购条件与风险都不清楚。 30％到底是指阿拉斯加天然气的产量还是台湾的进口需求？ 44亿美元的采购细节如何？国会到现在都不清楚。

许宇甄强调，赖政府不能对美方要求照单全收，把国家利益送上谈判桌却把帐单留给台湾人民，必须将完整评估报告送进国会严格审查。

行政院长卓荣泰14日则表示，政府一直努力在维持国内稳定供油、供电、供气，这条道路非常漫长，希望社会也能给油、气、电等相关国营单位多一点支持。

title: Lai calls for progress on unsigned Taiwan-Canada trade framework - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 黎智英呼吁未签署的台加贸易框架取得进展 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月14日电 赖清德总统14日表示，希望台湾与加拿大尚未签署的贸易合作框架能取得进展，并呼吁加强双边经济和产业合作。黎智英在台北总统府会见加拿大议员时表示，希望台加贸易合作框架安排（TCFA）能够在他们的支持下向前推进。代表团由自由党议员、加拿大-台湾议会友好小组和众议院主席朱迪·斯格罗（Judy Sgro）率领。
content:
中新社台北10月14日电 赖清德总统14日表示，希望台湾与加拿大尚未签署的贸易合作框架能取得进展，并呼吁加强双边经济和产业合作。

黎智英在台北总统府会见加拿大议员时表示，希望台加贸易合作框架安排（TCFA）能够在他们的支持下向前推进。

该代表团由自由党议员朱迪·斯格罗（Judy Sgro）率领，她也是加拿大-台湾议会友好小组和下议院国际贸易常设委员会的主席。

根据加拿大外交部全球事务部 9 月份对议会的回应，拟议的 TCFA 旨在加强双边贸易和经济合作，尽管其文本已于 2025 年 3 月最终确定，但仍未签署。

该部表示，该框架仍在考虑签署，但没有提供时间表。

赖表示，台湾在半导体、信息和通信技术方面的优势，加上加拿大在人工智能（AI）、能源和关键矿产方面的优势，使得两国经济在人工智能推动全球产业转型的过程中“高度互补”。
他表示，这些优势为“双边合作提供了广泛机遇”，并补充说，近年来双方在贸易、技术、供应链和海上安全等领域扩大了合作。

黎智英表示，台湾是加拿大在亚洲的第六大贸易伙伴，希望双方“发挥各自优势，推动更多实质性合作”，为两国产业和人民创造新机遇。

据台湾国际贸易管理局统计，2025年双边商品贸易额达48.9亿美元，同比增长5.6%。

在周三的会议上，黎智英还感谢加拿大立法者的支持，并引用了一项跨党派议会动议，反对他所说的中国歪曲联合国大会第2758号决议的行为，以及Sgro和下议院国际贸易常设委员会为推进TCFA所做的努力。

在黎智英之后发表讲话时，斯格罗表示，加拿大和台湾享有“强劲且不断发展的关系”，并列举了在贸易、投资、教育、科学、创新、文化和旅游方面的合作。

她说，牢固的关系“不仅通过正式协议建立，还通过持续对话、相互尊重和个人联系”建立。

不过，代表团团长在发言中并未具体提及TCFA。
第六次访问台湾的斯格罗表示，代表团的目的是加深议会对话并更好地了解印度-太平洋地区，她称该地区“对加拿大未来的繁荣与安全越来越重要”。

她说：“请知道，加拿大是朋友和伙伴，加拿大将与台湾站在一起。”

（赖阳光）

结局/AW

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) on Wednesday expressed hope for progress on a proposed trade cooperation framework between Taiwan and Canada that remains unsigned, as he called for closer bilateral economic and industrial cooperation.

During a meeting with Canadian lawmakers at the Presidential Office in Taipei, Lai said he hoped the Taiwan-Canada Trade Cooperation Framework Arrangement (TCFA) would move forward with their support.

The delegation was led by Judy Sgro, a Liberal Party lawmaker who is also chair of the Canada-Taiwan Parliamentary Friendship Group and the House of Commons Standing Committee on International Trade.

The proposed TCFA, aimed at strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation, remains unsigned despite its text having been finalized in March 2025, according to a September response to Parliament by Global Affairs Canada, the country's foreign ministry.

The ministry said the framework is still being considered for signature but provided no timetable.

Lai said Taiwan's strengths in semiconductors and information and communications technology, alongside Canada's advantages in artificial intelligence (AI), energy and critical minerals, make their economies "highly complementary" as AI drives global industrial transformation.

He said those strengths presented "extensive opportunities for bilateral cooperation," adding that the two sides had expanded cooperation in trade, technology, supply chains and maritime security in recent years.

Noting that Taiwan is Canada's sixth-largest trading partner in Asia, Lai said he hopes both sides would "build on their respective strengths and promote even more substantive cooperation" to create new opportunities for their industries and people.

According to Taiwan's International Trade Administration, bilateral merchandise trade totaled US$4.89 billion in 2025, up 5.6 percent from a year earlier.

During Wednesday's meeting, Lai also thanked Canadian lawmakers for their support, citing a cross-party parliamentary motion countering what he described as China's distortion of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758, as well as efforts by Sgro and the House of Commons Standing Committee on International Trade to advance the TCFA.

Speaking after Lai, Sgro said Canada and Taiwan enjoy "a robust and growing relationship," citing cooperation in trade, investment, education, science, innovation, culture and tourism.

She said strong relationships are built "not only through formal agreements, but also through sustained dialogue, mutual respect, and personal connections."

However, the delegation leader made no specific mention of the TCFA in her remarks.

Sgro, who is visiting Taiwan for the sixth time, said the delegation aimed to deepen parliamentary dialogue and better understand the Indo-Pacific, a region she described as "increasingly important to Canada's future prosperity and security."

"Please know that Canada is a friend and a partner," she said, adding that "Canada will be standing next to Taiwan."

(By Sunny Lai)

Enditem/AW

title: MAC accuses Beijing of election interference over Puma Shen family firm sanctions - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: MAC指责北京因对彪马沉氏家族实施严厉制裁而干涉选举 - 聚焦台湾
summary: 中新社台北10月14日电 中国大陆宣布制裁另一家与民进党台北市市长候选人沈伯洋之父有关联的公司后，大陆委员会周三指责北京试图干涉台湾选举。台湾负责中国事务的最高政府机构陆委会在一份声明中表示，北京在竞选期间利用有针对性的媒体叙事来“给某些政治阵营和候选人贴上标签，并施加经济压力”。 “这明显是恶意胁迫台湾社会、干涉台湾社会。”
content:
中新社台北10月14日电 中国大陆宣布制裁另一家与民进党台北市市长候选人沈伯洋之父有关联的公司后，大陆委员会周三指责北京试图干涉台湾选举。

台湾负责中国事务的最高政府机构陆委会在一份声明中表示，北京在竞选期间利用有针对性的媒体叙事来“给某些政治阵营和候选人贴上标签，并施加经济压力”。

马克说：“这显然是恶意胁迫台湾社会并干涉我们的民主选举。”

该委员会还指出，最新的制裁措施与去年对沈父的公司实施的制裁方式相同，在中国台湾事务办公室（TAO）宣布惩罚措施之前，香港媒体就出现了有针对性的报道。

MAC 做出回应之前，TAO 发言人陈斌华周三早些时候宣布，与沉的父亲沉土城有联系的 VWAY 有限公司已被禁止与中国的组织、公司和个人开展业务或合作。

陈在北京举行的例行新闻发布会上表示，尽管沉先生的另一家企业于 2025 年 6 月受到制裁，但沉先生的父亲仍然利用 VWAY 继续与中国公司进行贸易并创造利润。
在 TAO 宣布这一消息之前，亲北京的香港报纸《文汇报》周二发表了一篇报道，指控沉的父亲继续通过 VWAY 与中国公司开展业务。

在吹风会上，陈指责沉反华，阻碍两岸交流，同时与他的亲属一起寻找从中国市场获利的方法。

他补充说：“我们决不允许与顽固的台独分裂分子有联系的企业从大陆获利。”

2024年10月，北京将倾向台独的民进党无席立法委员沉定为“顽固台独分裂分子”，禁止他及其家人进入中国大陆、香港和澳门。

2025年6月5日，北京对其父亲的贸易公司Sicuens International Co., Ltd.实施制裁。

沉在当年6月13日的评论中表示，该公司只是从中国普通供应商订购产品，包括汽车零部件和自行车。

针对民政总署周三晚些时候的声明，沉的竞选办公室表示，台北居民正在选举市长，民政总署应该明白，这样的行为不会赢得台湾公众的信任。

竞选办公室补充说，相信正在寻求连任的国民党台北市市长蒋万安也持有同样的观点。

## TAO 在城市论坛上回绝沉
与此同时，TAO周三还驳回了沉表示如果当选市长，愿意参加一年一度的台北-上海双城论坛的说法。

沉在最近的一次采访中表示，他支持在今年晚些时候举办该论坛，如果当选，他将参加，前提是没有政治先决条件，并且该活动能带来实实在在的好处，包括对企业的好处。

陈在周三的吹风会上表示，过去16年来，该论坛促进了台北和上海在经济事务和城市管理方面的合作，但指责“顽固的台独分裂分子”“煽动两岸对抗”，并称他们“没有资格谈论台湾问题”。

【原文 English Original】
Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) The Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) on Wednesday accused Beijing of attempting to interfere in Taiwan's elections after China announced sanctions against another company linked to the father of Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋).

In a statement, MAC, Taiwan's top government agency for China affairs, said Beijing was using targeted media narratives to "label certain political camps and candidates and exert economic pressure" during the election campaign.

"This is clearly a malicious attempt to coerce Taiwanese society and interfere in our democratic elections," MAC said.

The council also noted that the latest sanctions followed the same pattern as those imposed on Shen's father's company last year, with targeted reports appearing in Hong Kong media before China's Taiwan Affairs Office (TAO) announced punitive measures.

MAC's response came after TAO spokesperson Chen Binhua (陳斌華) announced earlier Wednesday that VWAY Co., Ltd., a company linked to Shen's father, Shen Tu-cheng (沈土城), had been barred from conducting business or cooperating with organizations, companies and individuals in China.

At a regular news briefing in Beijing, Chen said that Shen's father had used VWAY to continue trading with Chinese firms and generating profits despite sanctions imposed on another of his businesses in June 2025.

The TAO announcement followed a report published Tuesday by the pro-Beijing Hong Kong newspaper Wen Wei Po alleging that Shen's father had continued doing business with Chinese companies through VWAY.

At the briefing, Chen accused Shen of opposing China and obstructing cross-strait exchanges while working with his relatives to find ways to profit from the Chinese market.

"We will never allow companies associated with diehard Taiwan independence separatists to profit from the mainland," he added.

Beijing designated Shen, a legislator-at-large from the independence-leaning DPP, a "diehard Taiwan independence separatist" in October 2024, barring him and his family members from entering China, Hong Kong and Macao.

On June 5, 2025, Beijing extended sanctions to his father's trading company, Sicuens International Co., Ltd.

In comments on June 13 that year, Shen said the company had merely ordered products, including automotive parts and bicycles from ordinary suppliers in China.

In response to the TAO's announcement later Wednesday, Shen's campaign office said Taipei residents were electing a mayor and that the TAO should understand that such actions would not win the trust of the Taiwanese public.

The campaign office added that it believed incumbent Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) of the Kuomintang (KMT), who is seeking reelection against Shen, held the same view.

## TAO rebuffs Shen on city forum

Meanwhile, the TAO on Wednesday also dismissed Shen's stated willingness to attend the annual Taipei-Shanghai Twin-City Forum if elected mayor.

Shen had said in a recent interview that he supported holding the forum later this year and would attend if elected, provided there were no political preconditions and the event offered tangible benefits, including for businesses.

At Wednesday's briefing, Chen said the forum had facilitated cooperation between Taipei and Shanghai in economic affairs and city management over the past 16 years, but accused "diehard Taiwan independence separatists" of "stoking cross-strait confrontation," saying they were "in no position to talk about cross-strait exchanges and cooperation."

(By Lu Chia-jung, Liu Chien-pang and Sunny Lai)

Enditem/AW

SEOUL, Oct. 14 (Yonhap) -- South Korea's central bank chief met with his counterparts from China and Japan in Thailand on Wednesday to exchange views on recent economic and financial developments, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said.

BOK Gov. Shin Hyun-song exchanged views on economic and financial conditions in the three countries with People's Bank of China Gov. Pan Gongsheng and Bank of Japan Gov. Ueda Kazuo during the 15th Tripartite Governors' meeting in Bangkok.

The meeting provided a platform for the three central bank chiefs to share assessments of economic conditions and financial market developments amid evolving global economic uncertainties.

The three Asian countries have been hosting the event on a rotation basis since 2009 to strengthen communication and cooperation. This year's annual gathering was hosted by the BOK.

content: 曼城主席 Khaldoon Al Mubarak（左）2019 年在埃蒂哈德球场与 Andy Burnham 交谈，当时他是大曼彻斯特市长。 据披露，曼彻斯特市长 Andy Burnham 在担任市长期间曾两次与曼城足球俱乐部主席共进商务晚宴。 总理曾在 2017 年和 2018 年的比赛中与 Khaldoon Al Mubarak 共进晚餐，但大曼彻斯特联合当局（GMCA）周一发布的关于他与该俱乐部会晤的声明中并未提及此事。 自俱乐部被裁定“系统性”违反英超规则（并将对此提起上诉）以来，Burnham 一直面临澄清此前与曼城讨论的压力。 这位前市长在上周表示，如果俱乐部所有者现在出售股份，他将“非常担忧”，这一言论引发了广泛争议。 周一，GMCA 发布了一份关于 Burnham 在担任该地区近十年市长期间与曼城会晤的声明。 声明称，他在 2021 年 10 月于英国政府全球投资峰会上与 Al Mubarak 举行了正式会晤，该峰会由国际贸易部组织；并在 2019 年为前球员文森特·孔帕尼举办的纪念赛中，在观众席上“非正式地”会见了俱乐部主席。 声明还称，“以市长身份，他曾在少数几次主场比赛中作为曼彻斯特城俱乐部的客人出席”。 但声明并未明确指出，这指的是他与曼城主席在两场不同比赛中共进的两次商务晚宴。 BBC 看到的一份 Burnham 之前的 GMCA 申报登记册显示，他于 2017 年 8 月与“时任曼彻斯特市议会领导人 Richard Leese 和曼城主席”共进晚餐，地点是埃蒂哈德球场的一场埃弗顿比赛，商务价值为 300 英镑。 另一条记录显示，2018 年 4 月他与“主席”在埃蒂哈德球场参加曼城/曼联德比比赛共进晚餐，价值约为 699 英镑。 Burnham 此前曾申报过这两次晚宴，以及 2018 年 5 月观看 Ed Sheeran 在球场演出的两张票，价值 150 英镑。 但申报登记册随后已从 GMCA 网站删除，据《太阳报》首次报道，但 BBC 了解到，该当局的政策是仅发布现任市长任期内的条目。 BBC News 已向 GMCA 询问了关于此政策的更多细节——尽管其网站上有追溯到 2022 年的条目，而现任市长任期始于 2024 年。 唐宁街为 Burnham 与曼城主席的两次晚宴进行了辩护，称这是他在主场比赛中收到的商务接待，已进行了申报，而非与俱乐部主席的单独会晤。 但 Burnham 此前与曼城任何过往讨论的透明度压力仍在持续增加。 保守党影子体育大臣 Louie French 表示：”Andy Burnham 曾承诺向国家和下议院完全透明地披露他与曼彻斯特城的往来。” “这在他对足球的不当干预之后至关重要。” 保守党领袖 Kemi Badenoch 要求第 10 号办公室（首相府）发布总理与俱乐部高层人物会晤的所有细节。 Burnham 上周在接受 Rest Is Politics 播客采访时说：“我已收到反对党领袖的要求，让我公布我的会晤细节，我很乐意这样做，并且我会这样做。” “我将非常清楚地公布我在担任大曼彻斯特市长期间与他们合作所做的一切。” “实际上，这些会晤都不是最近的。我实际上只有一次重要的会晤，那就是 2021 年。” 周一由 GMCA 发布的会晤清单并未包含讨论内容的细节。BBC 已向 GMCA 询问为何未具体提及这两次晚宴。 9 月，曼城——多年来一直统治着英格兰足球顶级联赛——被独立委员会裁定违反英超财务规定。 委员会发现，City 在 2009 年至 2018 年期间违反了九年的规则，通过与商业合作伙伴签订“虚假”合同，秘密将超过 8.3 亿美元注入其足球运营中。 制裁尚未公布，而否认任何不当行为的 City 已就裁决提起上诉。 本月早些时候，Richard Leese 爵士——2021 年之前担任曼彻斯特市议会主席长达 25 年——为市议会与曼城所有者阿布扎比联合集团（ADUG）之间的一项十年前的协议进行了辩护。 根据谢菲尔德大学的一份报告，在该当局与阿联酋王室相关企业之间的合作中，土地以“低于可比费率”租给了 ADUG。

title: Transport chief resists fines for transit rudeness, cites existing rules

香港交通局局长陈美宝以现有规则和执行情况为由，拒绝支持因公共交通滋扰而罚款。去年投诉增加了 50%，达到 66 起，其中包括噪音和不卫生行为。陈指出目前的处罚和教育活动，而不是遵循 S

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 18:09 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

运输及物流局局长陈美宝不支持对公共交通滋扰行为处以罚款，而是指出现有规则和执法措施。在回答立法者的提问时，陈强调了目前针对不同运输方式的不当乘客行为的规定。

立法会议员张浩峰询问，对大声播放视频或把脚放在座位上等无礼行为的投诉是否有所增加。陈表示，运输署和环境保护署去年共收到66宗投诉，较上年增加50%。其中涉及噪音的案件有 24 起，涉及不当或不卫生行为的案件有 42 起，而去年分别有 11 起和 33 起。
当被问及香港是否会效仿新加坡9月份的举措，对公共交通上的不文明行为处以最高500新元（约合3000港元）的罚款时，陈没有直接回应。相反，她指出，现有立法已经包含了对不同交通方式中乘客不当行为的处罚。

陈说，在专营巴士上，乘客须遵守告示，禁止大声播放电子设备或将脚放在座位上。前线员工在处理不当行为时遵循指引，包括发出提醒和采取跟进行动，并在必要时将案件移交执法机构。

陈补充，港铁工作人员在例行检查时，如发现乘客违反规定，会发出提醒并采取跟进行动。运输署亦一直与营办商合作开展宣传和教育活动，以促进乘客安全、顾及他人及尊重同行旅客。

关于试点“安静区”或“安静车厢”的可能性，陈表示，运营商需要考虑包括其运营模式、车厢空间和设计以及对整体客运能力的影响等因素。她表示，政府将继续监控乘客行为，并与运营商合作，推广良好的公共交通礼仪和舒适的出行环境。

Hong Kong's transport chief Mable Chan declined to back fines for public transport nuisances, citing existing rules and enforcement. Complaints rose 50 per cent last year to 66, including noise and unhygienic behaviour. Chan pointed to current penalties and education campaigns instead of following S

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 18:09 HKT · 2 min read

Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan has stopped short of backing fines for public transport nuisances, pointing instead to existing rules and enforcement measures. Responding to a lawmaker's question, Chan highlighted current provisions against improper passenger conduct across different modes of transport.

Lawmaker Chong Ho-fung had asked about a rise in complaints over discourteous behaviour, such as playing videos loudly or putting feet on seats. According to Chan, the Transport Department and Environmental Protection Department received 66 complaints last year, up 50 per cent from a year earlier. The cases included 24 involving noise and 42 involving improper or unhygienic behaviour, compared with 11 and 33 respectively in the previous year.

Asked whether Hong Kong would follow Singapore's September move to impose fines of up to S$500 (about HK$3,000) for uncivil behaviour on public transport, Chan did not respond directly. Instead, she noted existing legislation already contains penalties for improper passenger conduct across different transport modes.

On franchised buses, passenger notices prohibit playing electronic devices loudly or putting feet on seats, Chan said. Frontline staff follow guidelines when dealing with inappropriate behaviour, including issuing reminders and taking follow-up action, with cases referred to law enforcement agencies where necessary.

Chan added that MTR staff issue reminders and take follow-up action during routine inspections when passengers breach regulations. The Transport Department has also been working with operators on publicity and education campaigns promoting passenger safety, consideration for others and respect for fellow travellers.

On the possibility of pilot 'quiet zones' or 'quiet carriages', Chan said operators would need to consider factors including their operating models, carriage space and design, as well as the impact on overall passenger capacity. She said the government would continue to monitor passenger behaviour and work with operators to promote good public transport etiquette and a comfortable travel environment.

# Hong Kong moves to enact double tax treaties with six nations

Hong Kong will implement comprehensive double taxation avoidance agreements with Barbados, Jordan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Maldives, Norway and Rwanda, the government said. The pacts aim to promote bilateral trade and investment, bringing the city's total network to 60 jurisdictions.

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 14 Oct 2026 at 18:13 HKT · 1 min read

Hong Kong will move to implement comprehensive double taxation avoidance agreements with six countries, including Norway, as the city seeks to promote bilateral trade and investment, the government said in a statement on Wednesday.

The Chief Executive in Council made six orders on October 6 covering pacts signed with Barbados, Jordan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Maldives, Norway, and Rwanda, the government said. The orders will be gazetted on Friday and tabled at the Legislative Council on October 21 for negative vetting. The treaties will take effect once Hong Kong and the respective jurisdictions conclude their formal ratification processes.

The agreements ensure that residents of Hong Kong and the relevant tax jurisdictions will not be subject to double taxation on the same income, and enable investors to assess more effectively the potential tax burden arising from their cross-border economic activities, a spokesperson for the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau said.

Hong Kong inked the deals with the Maldives, Jordan, Rwanda, and Norway across 2025, followed by agreements with the Kyrgyz Republic and Barbados in March 2026.

The move brings Hong Kong's total network of comprehensive double taxation agreements to 60 jurisdictions, with 15 secured under the current government.

title: Residents in Saudi Arabia's capital say they have heard new explosions in Riyadh
summary: **CAIRO —**New explosions have been heard in the Saudi capital, residents said Wednesday, as blame again quickly fell on Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen. The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercept
content:
**CAIRO —**New explosions have been heard in the Saudi capital, residents said Wednesday, as blame again quickly fell on Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen. The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure in the latest front in the Iran war. Separately, the rebel-run Health Ministry reported two dead in attacks in Yemen on Tuesday and blamed the Saudis.

The Houthis, hardened by years of civil war, have emerged as Iran's most effective armed proxy of the moment, but experts say they also have their own agenda. Either way, they are applying increasing pressure on a key US ally.

*   [Saudi says Houthi attacks sparked Aramco fire, wounded 4 in Riyadh](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/world/americas-emea/saudi-says-houthi-attacks-sparked-aramco-fire-wounded-4-in-riyadh/2445161)

**Trump faces questions over possible US intervention**

The sight of smoke rising from some of Saudi Arabia’s most sensitive facilities has rattled the region and global markets, increasing questions for President Donald Trump, who has said he is evaluating whether the US should join the Saudi strikes on the Houthis.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The Riyadh residents spoke about the latest blasts on condition of anonymity for their safety. One lives in northern Riyadh, where King Khalid International Airport — targeted multiple times in the past week with strikes that have killed 17 people and hurt over 300 more — is located.

There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

[![Image 2: This photo shows a general view of Saudi oil giant Aramco's Riyadh refinery, south of Riyadh on October 3, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259175.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259175.jpg)
This photo shows a general view of Saudi oil giant Aramco's Riyadh refinery, south of Riyadh on October 3, 2026. AFP PHOTO

The Saudi civil defense reported air raid alerts in Riyadh and Kharj province southeast of the capital. Kharj is home to the state-owned Military Industries Corporation and Prince Sultan Air Base.

The Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks against King Khalid International Airport, oil facilities in the eastern city of Dhahran, which hosts the headquarters of Saudi giant Aramco, and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, calling them retaliation for “treacherous Saudi aggression” against the rebel-held Yemeni capital of Sanaa and other areas.

The Houthis have been warning in advance of attacks on both airports and oil facilities, and airlines have been suspending operations and pulling out planes. On Tuesday, a fire broke out in an administrative building at a facility operated by Aramco, one of the world’s largest oil companies.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

**Experts say Saudi Arabia can’t intercept everything**

The escalation has highlighted Saudi Arabia’s struggle to intercept Houthi missiles and drones, and the kingdom’s efforts to press allies like the United States for more military support. Regional officials say that Saudi Arabia, the world’s top purchaser of American weapons, is running low on interceptors.

The Saudis are trying to intercept daily attacks across a territory about three times the size of Texas. Experts have said trying to intercept all of the missiles and drones is impossible.

The Houthis have a large arsenal capable of striking targets well over 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers) away. Some warheads change direction during flight.

*   ![Image 4: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

Even interceptions are a danger. Overnight, Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense said debris from two intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles fell on residential areas in Riyadh, injuring four people including a child and damaging 15 homes.

Meanwhile, the Saudis have been carrying out airstrikes in rebel-held areas of Yemen in support of the country’s internationally recognized government. The fighting erupted this year when the rebels blamed the Saudis for a strike on the airport in rebel-held Sanaa. That attack revived anger over a Saudi blockade of the Houthis. The rebels in turn declared their own blockade against the kingdom.

A week and a half ago, the Saudi-led coalition responded with a major military offensive.

On Wednesday, the Houthi-run Health Ministry said two people were killed in an airstrike Tuesday in the Ras Isa port area in Hodeida province. The strike hit a facility of the state oil company and wounded two others, the ministry said, and blamed Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition also attacked an oil facility in Sanaa.

The targeting of fuel storage facilities in Houthi-controlled areas marks a new phase in the Saudi-led coalition's campaign, said Ahmed Nagi, senior Yemen analyst at the International Crisis Group, a think tank. He added that in a war of attrition, the rebels could risk losing much of their military capacity.

“The Houthis are betting on pressure, while the Saudis are betting on time. The Houthis are trying to strike critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia to raise the cost of continued military intervention and support for the Yemeni government,” Nagi added.

SEOUL, Oct. 14 (Yonhap) -- South Korea's central bank chief met with his counterparts from China and Japan in Thailand on Wednesday to exchange views on recent economic and financial developments, the Bank of Korea (BOK) said.

BOK Gov. Shin Hyun-song exchanged views on economic and financial conditions in the three countries with People's Bank of China Gov. Pan Gongsheng and Bank of Japan Gov. Ueda Kazuo during the 15th Tripartite Governors' meeting in Bangkok.

The meeting provided a platform for the three central bank chiefs to share assessments of economic conditions and financial market developments amid evolving global economic uncertainties.

The three Asian countries have been hosting the event on a rotation basis since 2009 to strengthen communication and cooperation. This year's annual gathering was hosted by the BOK.

title: Hong Kong leader marks Sun Yat-sen’s 160th birthday, touts patriotism education
zh_title: 香港特首庆祝孙中山诞辰160周年 宣扬爱国主义教育
summary: 香港 香港行政长官李家超于2026年10月14日在纪念孙中山先生诞辰160周年座谈会上致辞。李强调了孙与香港的关系，并概述了政府在香港第一个五年计划中深化爱国主义教育的计划。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日香港时间 16:36 · 10 月 14 日更新， 17:19 · 阅读2分钟 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/14/P202
content:
香港
香港行政长官李家超于2026年10月14日在纪念孙中山先生诞辰160周年座谈会上致辞。李强调了孙与香港的关系，并概述了政府在香港第一个五年计划中深化爱国主义教育的计划。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 16:36 香港时间 · 更新于 10 月 14 日 17:19 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/14/P2026101400585.htm)

香港行政长官李家超于2026年10月14日在纪念孙中山先生诞辰160周年座谈会上致辞，盛赞孙中山先生是“伟大的民族英雄、伟大的爱国者、中国民主革命的伟大先驱”。李在中国和平统一促进会（香港）举办的活动上发表讲话。
李回忆起孙在香港的时光，曾就读于拔萃男书院、中央书院和香港中文医学院（香港大学医学院的前身）。孙先生于1892年毕业，后来将香港描述为“我的革命思想的诞生地”。李指出，孙中山于1895年在中环成立兴中会香港分会，并于1905年在东京成立同盟会后，以香港为广州和惠州起义的基地，并在海外筹款。

行政长官表示，香港政府高度重视爱国主义教育，按照“一国两制”的原则，弘扬爱国爱城的价值观。他说，两年多前成立的“爱国主义教育工作组”一直在协调政府和非政府的努力，以加强国家历史和公民教育。

李引述了上个月发布的香港第一个五年计划，其中呼吁深化爱国、国家、国家安全和价值观教育。旨在培养“有德有才、爱国爱港、有文化自信、有正确价值观、有全球视野”的年轻一代。
李在2026年施政报告中建议将宪法和基本法学生大使计划扩展至所有政府资助的中小学，并举办交流和实习活动，让年轻人亲身体验国家发展。在中央政府支持下，陕西延安革命纪念馆将成为内地第二个香港青少年爱国主义教育基地。政府还将新建一座展示国家快速发展的博物馆，继续支持家乡协会，并在中国文化节期间制作高质量节目，“讲好中国故事”。

李家祥勉励大家学习孙中山先生的爱国主义精神和振兴中华的决心，把对国家、对香港的热爱化为实际行动，为实现中华民族伟大复兴的中国式现代化作出贡献。他感谢中国和平统一促进会（香港）主办此次活动。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

Hong Kong
Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee addressed a symposium on 14 October 2026 to commemorate the 160th birth anniversary of Dr Sun Yat-sen. Lee highlighted Sun’s ties to Hong Kong and outlined government plans to deepen patriotic education under the city’s first five-year plan.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 16:36 HKT · updated 14 Oct, 17:19 · 2 min read

 Image: [香港特區政府新聞公報](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/14/P2026101400585.htm)

Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee on 14 October 2026 addressed a symposium marking the 160th birth anniversary of Dr Sun Yat-sen, praising the revolutionary as a “great national hero, great patriot and great pioneer of China’s democratic revolution”. Lee spoke at the event organised by the China Council for the Promotion of Peaceful National Reunification (Hong Kong).

Lee recalled Sun’s time in Hong Kong, where he studied at Diocesan Boys’ School, Central School and the Hong Kong College of Medicine for Chinese, the predecessor of the University of Hong Kong’s medical faculty. Sun graduated in 1892 and later described Hong Kong as the “birthplace of my revolutionary ideas”. Lee noted that Sun founded the Hong Kong branch of the Xingzhonghui (Revive China Society) in Central in 1895 and used the city as a base for uprisings in Guangzhou and Huizhou, as well as for overseas fundraising after forming the Tongmenghui in Tokyo in 1905.

The chief executive said the Hong Kong government places high priority on patriotic education and is promoting values centred on love for the country and the city, in line with the “one country, two systems” principle. He said the “Patriotic Education Task Force”, established more than two years ago, has been coordinating government and non-government efforts to strengthen national history and civic education.

Lee cited the territory’s first five-year plan, released last month, which calls for deepening patriotic, national, national-security and values education. It aims to nurture a younger generation that is “virtuous and talented, loves the country and Hong Kong, has cultural confidence, correct values and a global perspective”.

In his 2026 policy address, Lee proposed expanding the Constitution and Basic Law student ambassador programme to all government-subsidised primary and secondary schools, and organising exchange and internship activities for young people to experience national development first-hand. With central government support, the Yan’an Revolution Memorial Hall in Shaanxi province will become the second mainland patriotic education base for Hong Kong youth. The government will also set up a new museum showcasing the nation’s rapid development, continue supporting hometown associations and produce high-quality programmes under the Chinese Culture Festival to “tell China’s story well”.

Lee urged the audience to learn from Sun’s patriotism and determination to rejuvenate China, turning love for the country and Hong Kong into concrete actions to contribute to national rejuvenation through Chinese-style modernisation. He thanked the China Council for the Promotion of Peaceful National Reunification (Hong Kong) for organising the event.

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Hong Kong's Digital Office has launched an "AI Assistant" feature in the iAM Smart mobile app to help residents access government services more easily. The tool uses artificial intelligence to search official sources for answers to users' questions and presents the information in a clear, organised format.

When residents ask about how to apply for an online government service, the AI Assistant will list the eligibility requirements, step-by-step procedures and provide direct links to the relevant online forms. It also supports the existing "Form Filler" function to help users complete applications seamlessly.

The latest version of the iAM Smart app (version 5.0) with the AI Assistant will be pushed to users gradually from 14 October through late October via official app stores. Users need to install the updated app and tap on the avatar of the app's mascot "A-Chi" on the home screen to activate the assistant.

The Digital Office said it will continue to improve the AI Assistant and plans to launch an enhanced version offering personalised services by the end of 2026, aiming to further improve the user experience.

title: Kelly Clarkson and Brooklyn store clash on social media
summary: **NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it. But just because we might all
content:
**NEW YORK —**It was something most people have likely done at one time or another: complain to others about feeling judged or dismissed during an interaction, maybe even take to social media to post about it.

But just because we might all have the same impulse, we all don’t have the same reach and impact. Exhibit A: a dispute between singer Kelly Clarkson and a small store in Brooklyn that's brought out angry fans and heated commentary.

The conflict from over the weekend, involving a high-priced mechanical bird, is raising more issues than just the quality of customer service. It's also a case study in power dynamics, and the differential that exists between someone with a high profile and those without.

*   [Marites Allen reveals fearless 2027 Fire Sheep forecast, pioneering ‘Destiny Is in Your Stars’ platform](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/entertainment-lifestyle/marites-allen-reveals-fearless-2027-fire-sheep-forecast-pioneering-destiny-is-in-your-stars-platform/2445260)

It started Saturday when Clarkson went to Art of Play, a store in Brooklyn that offers items like books, games and playing cards and also hosts magic shows. But the interaction turned negative, she said in a social media post, when she “was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it” and went on to say the store had “just lost a huge sale.” She named the store and gave it a thumbs down.

A back-and-forth ensued, with the store making its own posts saying initially that the item wasn't for sale and then adding that they had tried to find her an alternative. Clarkson said that wasn't true.

Since Clarkson's initial post, there's been a barrage of commentary online — and, the store owners say, in the real world. There have been hateful messages and reviews, and even someone showing up at the store, said Adam Rubin, one of the partners.

“I don’t understand why these people are willing to debase themselves on behalf of a celebrity they never met,” he said. Representatives for Clarkson did not respond to repeated attempts to get comment.

**The power of celebrity is potent**

Celebrities have power in different ways. They can influence what people feel as well as impact what they think or believe, said Alfred Archer, assistant professor at Tilburg University in the Netherlands, who has done research around the ethics and politics of fame.

In a situation like Clarkson's, the influence is heavily weighted in the celebrity's favor as a result, he said. That doesn't mean celebrities should be censored or barred from speaking, but they should be cognizant of that reality in determining what they say and how they say it.

“You can’t hold the celebrity responsible for everything that their followers do, of course,” Archer said, but those who have influence should remember that their words can resonate widely and “be careful about what they put on social media and what they communicate in public for that reason.”

That power can also have positive ripples — like when Ms. Rachel, the children's educator and YouTube star, asked people on social media for Black-owned businesses to support. She gave recognition to small businesses like a coffee shop in New Jersey, leading to a huge jump in sales and popularity.

“I think really the responsibility here is to use this power in a responsible way,” Archer said. “And of course, what that looks like in any individual case is going to be a decision for a particular celebrity to make. But they do have to think about it a bit more carefully than an ordinary member of the public does.”

*   ![Image 4: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

[![Image 5: A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259027.jpg)
A general view shows Art of Play, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, in the Brooklyn borough of New York. AP PHOTO

**Social media changed the equation**

While everyday people have always been fascinated by the famous, the explosion of social media and the glut of information — and the way we follow our family and friends right along with our favorite stars — means there's more of a likelihood that people can develop parasocial, or one-sided, unreciprocated relationships with celebrities. That can lead to the kind of harsh messages and bad reviews that the Brooklyn store says it has experienced.

That aspect of modern life is baffling to Franchesca Ramsey, a writer, podcaster, and content creator.

“I think social media itself has heightened people’s ability to feel a connection to a celebrity or a public person that they don’t know,” she said.

“Back in my day, you liked a musician, you put up a poster on the wall. You read the magazine articles about them. You maybe went to their concert. You watched their music videos. But beyond that, it didn’t feel like a two-way relationship. It felt like I’m the fan and this is the person that I really enjoy,” she said.

“Social media has... kind of created this false sense of reality where, I really think even the act of watching someone’s content on your phone and it looks like they’re talking directly to you," she said.

Asked what advice he would give another small-business owner facing this kind of situation, Rubin didn't have any. “This is not something that a small business owner has the capability to deal with,” he said. “This is something that happens on a level of fame and celebrity that I don’t have access to, (that) most normal people don’t have access to.”

Watching the crowd of reporters from his plumbing supply store next door to Art of Play, Daniel Graffeo couldn't believe the uproar was still going on several days after the initial encounter, but wasn't totally surprised. “Nowadays everybody's looking for something, you know, publicity,” he said.

He hoped it would never find him. “I would not want to be in that situation.”

Our top story.

The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte is questioning the Senate’s silence over the prosecution’s withdrawal of three of the four impeachment articles against the Vice President. Duterte’s spokesman Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. said the Senate majority should explain why it had not challenged the alleged waste of public funds caused by the withdrawal. He estimated Senate operating costs at about 25-million pesos per day. He claimed the expenditure on the abandoned articles was 500-million pesos, excluding congressional salaries, legal fees, consultants and other expenses. Panelo further claimed that the total public cost could exceed one-billion pesos when the House of Representatives’ proceedings on the withdrawn articles were included. He described the withdrawal as an admission that the allegations had no basis from the outset.

The prosecution at the International Criminal Court or ICC is asking the judges to admit previously recorded testimonies against former President Rodrigo Duterte. The testimonies involve allegations of extrajudicial killings in Central Luzon and an alleged police policy of killing suspected criminals. Prosecutors want the statements of the three unidentified witnesses admitted without requiring them to testify in person. The prosecution argued that this would expedite proceedings, save court time and resources, and avoid unnecessary appearances by the witnesses. Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity before the ICC over his administration’s anti-drug campaign.

title: Nigeria: NAFDAC Bursts Trade Fair Complex Den of Fake Energy Drinks, Wine, Whisky 'Manufacture'
summary: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State. The Agency
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State.

The Agency arrested two suspects allegedly involved in the illegal operation.

The suspects, identified as Okafor and John, were arrested during an enforcement operation in a two-storey building where equipment and materials allegedly used to repackage and produce counterfeit alcoholic and energy drinks where discovered.

The raid, according to NAFDAC, followed credible intelligence and surveillance on suspected counterfeiters operating within the Trade Fair International Market.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

Speaking during the operation, the Assistant Director of the Investigation and Enforcement Directorate of NAFDAC, Mr Kunle Ojo, said the agency caught some of the suspects in the act and recovered drums, filters, packaging materials, a heating device and other equipment allegedly used in the illicit production process.

"Gentlemen of the press, as you can see today, when we came, we caught some red-handed producing all kinds of alcoholic drinks," Ojo said.

"What we have discovered today is a lot, and it's mind-boggling. We are here to protect the lives of many Nigerians."

Ojo said the agency intensified its enforcement activities ahead of the festive season, when demand for alcoholic and other beverages typically rises.

He warned that the circulation of counterfeit drinks posed a serious public health concern, urging suspected manufacturers to abandon the illegal trade.

"You are killing Nigerians in order to make money, which is not good," he said, appealing to those involved to stop the activities.

The NAFDAC official disclosed that the agency would investigate the source of the products, the raw materials used and the individuals allegedly financing or directing the operation.

"Where are they getting the products from? Where are they getting their raw materials? Who is employing them to do this kind of dangerous activity?"

He added that the agency would evacuate the recovered materials and products to its warehouse for further action, including destruction in accordance with applicable procedures.

"Those people that we have arrested today will be dealt with administratively and definitely will face the law," Ojo said.

Ojo also appealed to Nigerians to support the agency by providing credible information about suspected counterfeit production facilities.

"If you see something, say something," he said, assuring informants that their identities would be protected.

**Confession**

One of the arrested suspects, Okafor, who identified himself as a drinks dealer in the market, in an interview with Vanguard at the scene said: "I deal on drinks. I change the bottle of the drink. It's not that the bottle is not good. It's the drink in there, because the other one is already damaged. So that's why we are putting it to the next bottle," he said.

Also speaking during the operation, Mrs. Christiana Obiazikwor, Deputy Director, NAFDAC Public Relations, said the agency routinely carried out surveillance, seizures, arrests and destruction of unregistered and counterfeit products, despite public criticism that it was not doing enough to tackle the menace.

"NAFDAC is still at work. We are on the streets. We are in the markets. We are everywhere," she said.

Obiazikwor explained that enforcement teams often conducted operations without publicity to avoid alerting suspected offenders or triggering confrontations.

She said the agency decided to take journalists along on the latest operation to demonstrate its activities and reassure Nigerians that it remained committed to protecting public health.

"Most of the things they do, we don't publicise them so that we don't raise alarm," she said, adding that enforcement officers continued to visit suspected production and distribution points.

She urged members of the public to report suspected counterfeit production and distribution directly to NAFDAC rather than merely posting allegations on social media.

"There's no point going to social media to create fear. Report to NAFDAC and we'll do the needful."

Obiazikwor assured informants that the agency would protect their identities, urging Nigerians to provide credible information that could assist investigations.

Speaking, the Assistant Director, Head Public Relation, Investigation & Enforcement, Mrs. Victoria Jennifer Akudu, explained that the raid was part of the agency's routine efforts to uncover illegal manufacturing activities and protect consumers.

"Every day, our people are in the field. Our enforcement department, they are on the field trying to uncover this. And they do a lot," Akudu said.

She explained that the agency routinely confiscated products, carried out seizures and destroyed offending goods, adding that the latest operation was intended to demonstrate the work being done by enforcement officers.

"This is just a routine activity of our enforcement directorate," she said.

Akudu further disclosed that the suspected operators had allegedly moved from an earlier location after enforcement action, prompting officials to continue tracking their activities.

"We have confiscated and sealed off the place. They moved to another place. This time around, we passed through the back door. And that is how we are able to get them," she said.

She urged Nigerians to report suspected counterfeit products directly to NAFDAC rather than allow rumours and unverified claims to create unnecessary public fear.

Akudu assured the public that the agency remained committed to its responsibilities, stressing that its enforcement teams were continuing operations against suspected manufacturers and distributors of illegal products.

"I will ask Nigerians not to fear. We are alert and we are alive. We are doing our statutory function the way it should be," she said.

NAFDAC officials said the operation formed part of continuing efforts to remove counterfeit, adulterated and unregistered products from the Nigerian market.

The agency reiterated that consumers could be exposed to serious health risks when drinks were repackaged under the labels of established brands without proper quality controls or verification of their contents.

title: Nigeria: Military Plane Crash - Traditional Ruler Cries Out As Decaying Bodies 'Pollute' Community's Source...
summary: _"This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water
content:
_"This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water that flows there, pumped to be treated for our drinking. So, it means whatever happens, pollution is already in the river, either as a result of decayed bodies or as oil that dropped into the river."_

A humanitarian crisis may hit Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, following the pollution of the source of water for the community by decaying bodies of the victims of the**[Nigeria Air Force](https://x.com/NigAirForce "https://x.com/NigAirForce")** (NAF) plane that crashed there last week.

The traditional ruler of the community, Afolabi Odidiomo, told PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday that the body of water has been polluted, leaving the people with contaminated water both for drinking and other domestic uses.

He also said the crash destroyed economic trees and fish, which are the community's source of livelihood.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

The NAF plane crashed into the swamp in the area on Monday, 5 October, killing the 25 people on board.

Efforts by divers and rescue teams to retrieve the wreckage of the plane and the bodies of the victims have been largely unsuccessful because of the terrain.

The search and rescue efforts deployed by a combined team of NAF, the Nigerian Navy, the police, the Igbokoda community and the state government about a week ago have only succeeded in retrieving pieces of human body parts as well as the broken parts of the airplane.

Officials confirmed that the main body of the airplane is yet to be located, as it is suspected to be deeply submerged in the underlay of the swamp where the crash occurred.

**Water pollution concern**

However, concerns have shifted from the initial shock following the crash to fresh fears of water pollution.

The body of water where the crash occurred is the same source of water for the Igbokoda community.

Rescuers have indicated that working on the site at the moment is hazardous as the area stinks badly of decayed human flesh littering the water.

The traditional ruler of Igbokoda, Mr Odidiomo, who spoke to PREMIUM TIMES at his palace on Tuesday, said the water has been polluted, leaving the people with contaminated water both for drinking and other domestic uses.

"The concern of everybody in this community today is that our government spent time, energy, money, and effort looking for people that had been chopped into pieces by the crash. The pieces that are floating everywhere in our rivers. The pieces that have decayed left so much stench that is unbelievable.

"Going close to the river is so scary now for children who usually go to swim when they return from school, because they see human flesh everywhere as they swim. Fish are also dying everywhere.

"So, the river that used to be friendly with children has become scary, as we wonder why the government cares so much for the dead rather than the living.

"This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water that flows there, pumped to be treated for our drinking.

"So, it means whatever happens, pollution is already in the river, either as a result of decayed bodies or as oil that dropped into the river, and any other pollution that went into the water thereof."

The traditional ruler called for immediate clean-up of the water in order to prevent a worse disaster in the form of an epidemic due to the polluted water.

He said the lack of a plan to protect the people from the inherent pollution was unfair to the people, as the government could have cordoned off the area so that the polluted water could be kept back from flowing into the main river.

Mr Odidiomo said that besides the pollution, the crash also destroyed economic trees and fish, which are the community's source of livelihood.

"We are asking the government for cleanup. We are asking the government for remediation, a kind of restoration of the environment. The restoration now does not mean that we want the trees planted back, but we want the government to still do something in memory of those that died just as we have in Lagos and Ogun states," he said.

He also said efforts should be made, in addition to cleaning up the water, to also provide an alternative source of clean drinking water.

Also speaking on the pollution, Benjamin Omoyele, a resident of Igbokoda and a 100 Level student of Civil Engineering at the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA), said the water pollution arising from the crash is a genuine concern that the people expect the government to look into urgently.

According to him, the body parts still left in the water are creating health concerns and contamination in the water, which might affect residents who depend largely on it.

However, Odunsola Dada, popularly called General at Igbokoda, said he believed that since the water is deep and keeps flowing down into the ocean, it would clean itself with time.

Mr Dada said the water would clean itself with time and that he did not see any present danger to the community.

"We are all humans, and what happened is a tragedy. We will all also die at our time. The water is deep and flowing steadily. It is not a well or a pool. It is a flowing river. In a short while everything will flow into the sea and people will be able to use it as before," he said.

Meanwhile, excavations are ongoing at the site with more machinery being deployed to assist in the removal of the remaining parts of the aircraft.

The search for the black box is the new focus of the operation as directed by the Chief of Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, during his visit to the site last week.

title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 14, 2026
summary: **Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila to Lead New Rebel Coalition** Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has been [named](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140066.html) leader of the newly formed Front for the R
content:
**Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila to Lead New Rebel Coalition**

Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has been [named](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140066.html) leader of the newly formed Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition seeking to remove President Félix Tshisekedi's government. Launched in Goma, the movement brings together former leaders of the AFC/M23 alliance, including M23 military leader Sultani Makenga, who was appointed one of Kabila's deputies. The coalition accuses Tshisekedi's administration of corruption, economic mismanagement, insecurity, and weakening democratic institutions. It is vowing to pursue change by all means, including force. Kabila, who ruled from 2001 to 2019, was sentenced to death in absentia for treason last year. The announcement comes amid continued fighting in eastern DR Congo and stalled peace negotiations.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

**Nigeria Plane Crash Raises Fears of Water Contamination**

Residents of Igbokoda in Nigeria's Ondo State are raising [concerns](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140088.html) about possible water contamination after a Nigerian Air Force plane crash that killed all 25 people on board on October 5. The aircraft crashed into a swamp connected to a river that supplies the community's drinking water. Difficult terrain has hampered efforts to recover the wreckage and victims' remains. Community leaders fear that decaying human remains, possible oil spills and reports of dying fish could threaten public health and local livelihoods. Traditional ruler Afolabi Odidiomo has called for an urgent environmental clean-up and the provision of alternative safe drinking water. Recovery teams are continuing their search, with locating the aircraft's black box among their priorities.

**Caine Prize Investigates Zimbabwean Writer Over AI Allegations**

The Caine Prize for African Writing is [investigating](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140062.html) Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza after allegations that he used artificial intelligence to produce his award-winning short story, The Blue Fighter. The controversy followed an article published by The Atlantic that criticised the story and raised questions about its authorship. The prize organisers confirmed they had begun an investigation, saying they have a responsibility to uphold trust within Africa's literary and publishing community. The story centres on Tinashe and his family, whose circumstances deteriorate after his father leaves his profession to pursue his ambition of building fish tanks. Kundizeza previously described winning the 2026 prize as an important recognition of years of writing. He could be stripped of the award if the allegations are proven.

**Somalia Sanctions 10 Individuals Over Alleged Al-Shabaab Links**

Somalia has added 10 individuals to its national financial [sanctions list](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140090.html) over alleged involvement in financing or supporting Al-Shabaab, the Al-Qaeda-linked militant group. The National Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Committee said the move aims to disrupt the group's funding networks and strengthen enforcement of counter-terrorism measures. Under the directive, financial institutions, businesses and individuals operating in Somalia are prohibited from conducting transactions with those listed. They must also freeze any assets belonging to the designated individuals and report related transactions to the Financial Reporting Center. The committee did not disclose detailed evidence supporting the designations but warned that violations could result in legal action. Al-Shabaab has waged an insurgency against Somalia's federal government for more than 15 years.

**Two Suspected Ebola Cases Test Negative in Kenya's Laikipia County**

Health authorities in Kenya's Laikipia County have [confirmed](https://allafrica.com/stories/202610140032.html) that two suspected Ebola cases in Nanyuki tested negative, urging residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information. Concern arose after a patient presented with symptoms resembling Ebola and was admitted to Nanyuki Teaching and Referral Hospital. Laboratory results ruled out the virus. The patient died while receiving treatment. A second suspected case reported by a private hospital also tested negative after samples were analysed at the National Public Health Laboratory. County Health Executive Albert Taiti said precautionary measures had been activated and healthcare workers had been sensitised on identifying and managing suspected infections. Authorities have urged residents to rely on official updates, report suspected cases promptly and continue observing recommended health precautions.

**Malawi High Court Blocks Extradition of Prophet Bushiri to South Africa**

Malawi's High Court in Lilongwe has issued a 175-page judgment explaining why it overturned the extradition order against Shepherd Bushiri and his wife, Mary. The court found serious procedural and legal flaws, including that the couple was not allowed to be heard before the order was granted in March 2025. Their lawyer, Wapona Kita, said they can no longer be extradited to South Africa under the quashed order. Kita said that the State would have to appeal the ruling to pursue the matter further. The decision deals a major setback to South Africa's efforts to bring the couple back to face legal proceedings after they returned to Malawi in 2020.

title: Rwanda: Five Key Things to Know About Rwanda's Formula One Grand Prix
summary: Rwanda is set to host a Formula One Grand Prix in the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement, bringing the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993. The agreement follows years of discussions around Formula One's return to t
content:
Rwanda is set to host a Formula One Grand Prix in the early 2030s under a 10-year agreement, bringing the championship back to Africa for the first time since 1993.

The agreement follows years of discussions around Formula One's return to the continent and marks a major step in Rwanda's growing ambitions to host major international sporting events.

Here are five key things to know about the planned Rwanda Grand Prix.

**1. Why Rwanda?**

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

The agreement follows years of discussions between Formula One and Rwanda over bringing the championship back to Africa. The continent last hosted a Formula One race in 1993, when the South African Grand Prix was held at Kyalami.

Formula One President and CEO Stefano Domenicali said the partnership is intended to deliver long-term economic and social benefits beyond the race itself.

**2. Where will the race take place?**

The circuit will be built in Bugesera District, Eastern Province, about 40 kilometres south of Kigali and near the new Kigali International Airport.

The project is being led by the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) as part of a broader initiative combining sport, tourism, infrastructure and commercial development.

**3. What will the circuit look like?**

The purpose-built circuit will meet FIA Grade 1 standards, the highest certification required for a track to host Formula One races.

Its design will make use of the area's natural terrain and elevation changes.

WurzDesign, headed by former Formula One driver Alex Wurz, and Tilke Engineers and Architects are working on the circuit layout.

Beyond Formula One, the venue is planned as a multi-purpose facility capable of hosting conferences, major events and other motorsport competitions throughout the year.

**4. What major international events has Rwanda hosted?**

Rwanda has increasingly positioned itself as a destination for major international sporting events.

The country has hosted the 2024 FIA Awards Ceremony, the UCI Road World Championships, the 2023 FIFA Congress, the ICC Women's Challenge Trophy and the Basketball Africa League.

The Formula One Grand Prix would add one of the world's biggest sporting events to Rwanda's growing international sports calendar.

**5. When will the race happen, and what do drivers think?**

The inaugural Rwanda Grand Prix is expected to take place in the early 2030s, following completion of the circuit. Formula One has not yet announced an exact race date or detailed construction timetable.

Several leading Formula One drivers have previously expressed support for the championship returning to Africa.

Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton has called for a Formula One race on the continent. Four-time world champion Max Verstappen has also welcomed the prospect, while Mercedes driver George Russell has expressed support for Formula One expanding into Africa.

Formula One says the sport has more than 100 million fans across Africa, with nearly 60 per cent of fans in key Sub-Saharan African markets aged under 35.

# Nissin noodle recall in Australia does not apply to Taiwan: TFDA

10/14/2026 04:02 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

Photo taken from nissin.com

Taipei, Oct. 14 (CNA) A Nissin Foods' instant noodle product recalled in Australia over an undeclared milk allergen does not raise the same concern in Taiwan, because the imported versions sold locally are properly labeled, the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) said Wednesday.

Food Standards Australia New Zealand issued a recall notice on Oct. 9 for "Nissin Salt and Sesame Oil Noodles Aburasoba 82g," distributed by Sweets & Beverages Australia Pty Ltd., because the product's label did not declare milk as an allergen.

The TFDA said the product, made by the Nissin Foods Group, a major Japanese instant noodle manufacturer, is imported into Taiwan, but the versions sold locally carry Chinese-language labels stating that they contain milk, so the problem that prompted the recall does not arise in Taiwan.

TFDA specialist Liao Tzu-ting (廖姿婷) told CNA that the product had import inspection records up to Oct. 11, and the agency had confirmed with the importer that all shipments to Taiwan carry the required allergen labeling.

The product has therefore been given a green-light designation, the lowest alert level, in the TFDA's overseas food alert system, she said.

The TFDA nonetheless advised Taiwanese traveling to Australia or New Zealand not to buy or eat the affected product while the recall remains in effect.

Liao also reminded travelers that food brought or mailed into Taiwan for personal use is exempt from import inspection if each shipment is valued at no more than US$1,000 and weighs no more than 6 kilograms, provided other exemption requirements are met.

However, products imported for sale, or personal-use imports that exceed the exemption limits, must undergo import inspection under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation, and violators face penalties, she said.

(By Shen Pei-yao and Evelyn Kao)

content: 对广大珀斯华人来说，很难把马蹄莲和“有害杂草”联系起来。 洁白的花，修长的茎，往花瓶里插上几枝，不用怎么搭配就很好看。婚礼花束里也常有它，讲究的是纯洁、优雅，寄托对爱情的美好祝愿。 所以，第一次在西澳各处的树林中看见成片的马蹄莲，不少华人可能都会愣一下：国内花店里卖的花，这里怎么长得到处都是？ 有些人甚至还会有点替它可惜——这么漂亮，怎么没人要？ 殊不知，当地园林、环保人员看见这片花海，非但不觉得美好，反而只会发愁…… 这片“花海”，霸气外露 据澳大利亚广播公司ABC报道，野生马蹄莲正在西澳西南部森林持续蔓延，已有超过3000名私人土地业主求助，希望清除自家地上的这种植株。 其中就包括很多珀斯人南下游玩熟悉的地方：马河以南的Boranup Forest，以及Busselton附近的Ludlow Tuart Forest。 林子里，高大的树还在，下面开满白花。乍一看，很难觉得哪里出了问题。 但森林不能只剩下马蹄莲。 参与环境治理的工作人员Obelia Walker解释，森林中大量的生物多样性藏在林下植被里。马蹄莲成片扩张，会挤掉原有植物，也破坏野生动物的栖息地。 Obelia Walker 原本长着不同植物的地方，慢慢变成几乎只剩马蹄莲的地盘。花是越开越整齐了，森林却越来越单调。 而且，这位看着文静的花店常客，实在不太好请走。 它既能靠种子繁殖，也能靠地下根茎扩张。鸟类、水流、被丢弃的园艺垃圾和夹带根茎的泥土，都可能帮它搬家。 地面上的叶子夏天枯了，也不代表清除成功，地下根茎还可能在秋天重新发芽。 养花时盼着植物皮实一点，轮到除草，才知道“生命力旺盛”这几个字有多难办。 农场主Glen Taylor的烦恼就很具体。 他已经把自家土地上的马蹄莲清得差不多了，可附近公共林地仍有大片植株，边界处不断受到侵扰。 你这边认真除草，它那边继续生长。围栏能拦牛，拦不住鸟带来的种子。 这也是当地土地业主和志愿者催促州政府加大治理力度的原因：私人土地在清，公共土地上的问题也得跟上。 州政府则回应，过去九年已向西南部马蹄莲治理项目提供超过260万澳元拨款。目前重点是保护优先区域；然而，考虑到它分布广、再生和传播能力强，现阶段要在整个区域彻底根除，并不现实。 事情已经发展到这一步：当初请进花园的客人，如今只能尽量控制它别再扩大地盘。 不过，局部治理仍然有用。当地的Arum Lily Blitz项目强调，持续几年防治，可以逐步压低数量，后续工作量也会减少，只是很难靠一次清理就收工。 真是我们认识的马蹄莲吗？ 是的，西澳的野生Arum lily，学名是Zantedeschia aethiopica。中国科学院植物研究所的“植物智”资料中，这个学名对应的中文名称，就是马蹄莲。 它也不是从中国“跑来”的，原产地在非洲南部。当年被作为观赏植物引入澳洲，后来从花园逸生，在适宜的环境里扎了根。 所以，并不存在一种在中国温柔、到了西澳突然“变异”的马蹄莲。花还是那种花，只是长在花盆里和铺满自然保护地，后果差得太远。 喜欢归喜欢，在西澳还能养吗？ 先说结论：野外看到这种马蹄莲，别挖回家，也别分株送朋友。 西澳早在2006年9月就实施了全州性的Arum lily活株禁售，官方公告同时禁止植株和种子的移动。农业部门后来的资料也明确提示，发现有人出售或赠送活株，可以向主管部门报告。 不过，盆栽活株和花瓶里的切花要分开看。上述禁售公告明确保留了切花销售，并没有把插瓶用的马蹄莲鲜花一并禁掉。 如果家里已经长着马蹄莲，先确认具体种类，再向当地Council或生物安全机构咨询适用的管理和处置要求。别自行挖出来扔进附近林地，地下根茎碎片也可能继续生长。 至于想买彩色园艺品种的朋友，购买前应核实标签上的学名及西澳规定。颜色不是通行证：当年的禁令也包括这一物种的若干命名栽培品种，其中就有Green Goddess和Pink Mist。 还有一件事，跟它是不是入侵植物无关：马蹄莲有毒。 昆士兰毒物信息中心指出，它的各个部分都有毒，包括白色的佛焰苞和中间黄色的花序。 误食马蹄莲的任何部分，都有可能造成舌头、喉咙肿胀，以及腹痛、呕吐等症状。 汁液接触也可能引起皮肤刺激，对猫狗和牲畜同样有风险。 家里摆放鲜花时，要让孩子和宠物够不着，处理植株时戴手套，也别因为名字里有个“马蹄”，就联想到能吃的荸荠。 若发生误食，可拨打澳洲毒物信息热线13 11 26；出现呼吸困难等严重症状，应立即拨打000。宠物误食则应联系兽医。 说到底，喜欢马蹄莲，和理解西澳为什么要治理它，并不矛盾。 花瓶里插几枝，确实漂亮。森林里铺天盖地都是它，其他植物就没多少位置了。 下次看见林间一片白花，可以拍张照片。至于“这么多，挖两棵回家应该没关系”这一步，咱们还是省了把。 花瓶里插几枝，确实漂亮。森林里铺天盖地都是它，其他植物就没多少位置了。 下次看见林间一片白花，可以拍张照片。至于“这么多，挖两棵回家应该没关系”这一步，咱们还是省了把。

# 辽宁舰航母编队赴西太平洋训练 解放军海军称不针对特定国家

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月14日 16:00

中国人民解放军海军10月14日组织辽宁舰航母编队赴西太平洋相关海域开展训练。海军说，这是根据年度计划组织的例行性训练，旨在检验提升部队实战化训练水平，符合相关国际法和国际实践，不针对特定国家和目标。官方通报没有公布编队的舰艇组成、训练科目和预计持续时间。

日本等周边国家一直派舰艇和飞机警戒监视这类训练。辽宁舰以往从青岛母港出发后，多沿东海南下，经冲绳本岛和宫古岛之间的宫古海峡进入西太平洋，或再往南经巴士海峡，进入后多在冲绳以东的菲律宾海活动；上一次训练期间，中方说日本的舰艇和飞机多次近距离跟踪监视。到14日下午，日本防卫省还没有公布这次行动的监测资料。

这次出海前，台湾总统赖清德10月10日在国庆大会上发表演说，说中国持续以军事与灰色地带行动施压，企图改变台海现状；他也说，台湾增加国防投资不是为了挑衅，而是为了吓阻战争。中国海事部门此前已宣布，10月12日至17日在渤海、黄海、东海和南海等海域进行实弹射击和军事训练。大陆军事评论员宋忠平分析说，台海如果爆发军事冲突，大陆周边都有可能形成战场，范围会很大，因此解放军需要重点防范周边全域。

辽宁舰上一次赴西太平洋训练是5月19日出发，正是赖清德就职两周年的前一天；那次训练到过南海和西太平洋，和两栖攻击舰编队进行过联合演练，6月22日返回青岛母港。日方监测到，5月26日至28日约有170架次起降，编队一度航行到距宫古岛约590公里的海域。

辽宁舰近年赴西太平洋训练的公开记录

1.   2016年12月至2017年1月 第一次经宫古海峡驶出第一岛链，进入西太平洋和南海
2.   2022年5月 编队一度有8艘舰艇，舰载机起降超过300架次
3.   2024年9月至10月 在菲律宾以东活动，舰载机和直升机起降约630架次
4.   2025年5月底至6月 和山东舰第一次同时在西太平洋活动，日方监测到辽宁舰起降约550架次
5.   2025年12月 经宫古海峡后北上，沿琉球东侧活动，起降约260架次
6.   2026年5月19日至6月22日 到过南海和西太平洋，一度距宫古岛约590公里
7.   2026年10月14日 海军宣布编队赴西太平洋相关海域开展训练

数据：台湾媒体整理的公开记录（含日方监测）和中国海军的通报

这次出海的辽宁舰是中国第一艘航母，2012年入列。中国第一艘自制航母山东舰1月中旬起在海南榆林基地的干坞维护升级，10月初的商业卫星图像显示它仍在坞内；2025年11月5日入列的福建舰，官方说它正处于从基本形成战斗力向完全形成战斗力过渡的关键阶段，还没有像辽宁舰那样常态化执行长时间的西太平洋远海训练。
