Japanese police arrested a US Marine stationed on Okinawa last week on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman at a hotel in the island’s capital Naha.

The US military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine’s arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a monthlong curfew from midnight.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Tuesday that “we began high-level, working-level consultations between Japan and the United States last week on what effective measures should be taken.”

“The Japanese government will continue to do everything in its power both to address this case and to ensure that it does not happen again,” she told a legislative committee session.

Motegi held a telephone call over the weekend with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who offered his “sincere condolences” over the alleged crime, pledging US cooperation in the investigation.

Crimes committed by US personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies.

Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a US Marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison.

title: Governor: Nueva Vizcaya prepared for El Niño
summary: BAYOMBONG, Nueva Vizcaya — Amid a possible super El Niño from late 2026 to early 2027, the provincial government of Nueva Vizcaya has calmed public anxiety, assuring residents that safe drinking water will remain available and that concerns
content:
BAYOMBONG, Nueva Vizcaya — Amid a possible super El Niño from late 2026 to early 2027, the provincial government of Nueva Vizcaya has calmed public anxiety, assuring residents that safe drinking water will remain available and that concerns linking the dry spell to mining operations are misplaced.

Gov. Jose Gambito has placed provincial agencies on monitoring mode following advisories from the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) and the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) that El Niño conditions may intensify from September to December 2026 and continue into 2027.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) has warned of below-normal rainfall, drought and extreme heat nationwide.

*   [Mayor’s cousin shot in police chase](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/regions/mayors-cousin-shot-in-police-chase/2444039)

In response to growing questions on social media and community meetings about water security, the Provincial Health Office issued a public assessment intended to prevent panic.

Provincial health officer Dr. Anthony Cortez said Nueva Vizcaya is in a better position than most low-lying provinces because its domestic supply comes from mountain-fed springs, rivers and community systems, not just from large dams that recede during prolonged dryness.

“Here in Nueva Vizcaya, we are [blessed] because we have mountains, and we have adequate water for human consumption,” said Cortez. “The bigger problem might be in the agricultural sector, not much on human consumption.”

**Cortez said the distinction is important. “Irrigation for farms may be affected if rainfall drops significantly, but household consumption is expected to be sustained,” he said.**

To reinforce safety, Cortez said the health office is ready to conduct bacteriological testing of drinking water sources if conditions worsen and noted that “purified water from refilling stations remains widely available, making panic buying of bottled water unlikely.”

*   ![Image 1: Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258343.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

**Alongside water assurances, the government released health advisories to reduce heat-related illness.**

Cortez advised pregnant women, senior citizens and persons with maintenance medication to avoid unnecessary exposure to extreme heat, wear light clothing, drink sufficient water and continue prescribed medicines.

Farmers were also advised to start fieldwork early, avoid working from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. when heat peaks, take frequent breaks in shaded areas and use protective clothing.

The provincial government also addressed the revival of claims that mining operations in the province are contributing to the dry conditions.

*   ![Image 2: Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258182.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/court-agrees-to-drop-3-charges-vs-vp-sara/2444853)

Officials cited the clarification from the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) that El Niño and super El Niño are global climate phenomena driven by warming of sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, not by local land use.

The MGB Region 2, headed by Director Mario Ancheta, said the two operating large-scale mining companies in the province — OceanaGold (Philippines) Inc. in Kasibu and FCF Minerals Corp. in Quezon — along with one exploration company, North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp., also in Kasibu, are not a factor in the occurrence or intensity of El Niño.

**The bureau said the weather pattern should not be conflated with local environmental issues that are regulated separately.**

Provincial officials used that clarification to refocus public attention on preparedness measures that address the actual risks: conserving water, protecting vulnerable groups from heat, monitoring water quality and planning support for farmers who may face reduced irrigation supply.

*   ![Image 3: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

According to the provincial government, coordination with DOST-Pagasa and the NDRRMC will continue for early warning updates, while health and agriculture offices remain on standby to adjust advisories as conditions develop.

The message from the provincial capitol here is that while El Niño is a serious climate event that requires precaution, particularly for agriculture, “there is no basis for fear of a drinking water shortage in Nueva Vizcaya and no scientific basis to link the forecast dry spell to mining activity in the province.”

title: The ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine
summary: _**Dear PAO,**_ _**I am a victim of “plastic surgery gone wrong.” After the surgery, my face became permanently asymmetrical and swollen. When I confronted the head plastic surgeon, he argued that his assistant made a mistake in administeri
content:
_**Dear PAO,**_

_**I am a victim of “plastic surgery gone wrong.” After the surgery, my face became permanently asymmetrical and swollen. When I confronted the head plastic surgeon, he argued that his assistant made a mistake in administering the proper dosage of the medicine required during the surgery. However, since I directly transacted and conferred with this head surgeon before, during, and after the surgery, I want to implead him in the lawsuit. Can I file a lawsuit against him?**_

_**Paula**_

*   [Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

Dear Paula,

Yes, a lawsuit against the head plastic surgeon may be meritorious, notwithstanding the fact that it was his assistant who was directly negligent during the surgery.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

In Dr. Milagros L. Cantre v. Sps. Go and Go, GR 160889, April 27, 2007, penned by Associate Justice Leonardo Quisumbing, the Supreme Court explained that the head surgeon or the surgeon in charge of an operation is liable for the negligence of his/her assistants, saying:

“In cases involving medical negligence, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows the mere existence of an injury to justify a presumption of negligence on the part of the person who controls the instrument causing the injury, provided that the following requisites concur:

“1. The accident is of a kind which ordinarily does not occur in the absence of someone’s negligence;

*   ![Image 1: Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258343.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

“2. It is caused by an instrumentality within the exclusive control of the defendant or defendants; and

“3. The possibility of contributing conduct which would make the plaintiff responsible is eliminated.

“As to the first requirement, the gaping wound on Nora’s arm is certainly not an ordinary occurrence in the act of delivering a baby, far removed as the arm is from the organs involved in the process of giving birth. Such injury could not have happened unless negligence had set in somewhere.

“Second, whether the injury was caused by the droplight or by the blood pressure cuff is of no moment. Both instruments are deemed within the exclusive control of the physician in charge under the ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine. This doctrine holds the surgeon in charge of an operation liable for the negligence of his assistants during the time when those assistants are under the surgeon’s control. In this particular case, it can be logically inferred that petitioner, the senior consultant in charge during the delivery of Nora’s baby, exercised control over the assistants assigned to both the use of the droplight and the taking of Nora’s blood pressure. Hence, the use of the droplight and the blood pressure cuff is also within petitioner’s exclusive control.”

*   ![Image 2: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

Thus, as the head surgeon, your doctor may be held liable not only for his own negligence, but also for the negligence of his assistants during the surgery or when such assistants were under his professional control. As the proverbial “captain of the ship,” the head surgeon may be impleaded and held directly liable for the medical malpractice or negligence committed by the assistants he is supervising.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice was solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

# ‘Pax Silica to be culturally sensitive’

[![Image 18: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/allen-limos "author image")

 October 14, 2026

 20

PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. assured the public that the government will be culturally sensitive to concerns of displacement caused by the Pax Silica initiative.

In a press briefing on Tuesday, The Manila Times asked Marcos about concerns of Capas, Mayor Boots Rodriguez, that local communities might be displaced because of the planned 4,000-hectare AI hub and concerns that ancestral burial grounds might be disturbed.

“We are very sensitive to that. That’s not something that people should worry about. We are very sensitive about such cultural concerns, and those are very much part of the discussions,” said Marcos.

*   [ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

When asked about livelihood concerns on the project, Marcos said that is the opposite of what the Pax Silica initiative is designed to do.

“I cannot see how such a development will endanger local livelihood. I’m not sure I understand the question simply because this is quite big; this is projected to create tens of thousands of jobs,” he said.

The chief executive is keen on positioning the country in the digital economy, as the artificial intelligence (AI) industry takes center stage.

“If you would look at what we did as chair of Asean, one of the things that we did as the chair of Asean was to define the roadmap for Asean for AI. But that was even before the whole idea of Pax Silica emerged,” he said.

“And so, it’s quite the opposite. It should have exactly the opposite effect on what you were asking about,” he added.

Malacañang earlier said that the Bases Conversion and Development Authority has submitted the legal framework for the proposed Pax Silica initiative to the Office of the President.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said negotiations are still being finalized about the specific provisions for the agreement.

title: Socmed ban for kids Okd
summary: THE House of Representatives has approved on third and final reading a bill that would prohibit children below 13 years old from creating or using social media accounts and restrict access for teenagers to online features that expose them t
content:
THE House of Representatives has approved on third and final reading a bill that would prohibit children below 13 years old from creating or using social media accounts and restrict access for teenagers to online features that expose them to harm or encourage excessive use.

Under House Bill (HB) 11566, or the proposed Safe and Friendly Environment for Kids in Digital Spaces (SAFE KIDS) Act, children below 13 would be prohibited from creating, registering, maintaining or using social media accounts, while those aged 13 to below 18 would be allowed restricted access to digital platforms.

The House approved the measure on Monday, Oct. 12, with 287 votes in favor, three against and none abstaining.

*   [Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

The bill seeks to address risks associated with children’s use of social media and online gaming platforms, including cyberbullying, online grooming, sexual exploitation and exposure to harmful content.

For teenage users, digital platforms would be required to prohibit certain harmful features, including unsafe communications and functions that may encourage excessive or compulsive use.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The measure also provides for the creation of a SAFE KIDS Office under the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), which would be primarily responsible for implementation. Digital platforms that fail to comply with the proposed safeguards would face penalties.

Pasig City Rep. Roman Romulo, who co-sponsored the measure and chaired its technical working group, said the bill seeks to ensure that children’s participation in the digital world is accompanied by safeguards for their welfare.

“The concern, therefore, is not whether children should have a place in the digital world. They already do,” Romulo said in a statement released Tuesday.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

“The question before us is whether the digital environment in which they grow up provides adequate safeguards for their safety, development, and well-being,” he added.

Romulo said the measure seeks to establish clear responsibilities for digital platforms and ensure that children’s rights and welfare remain central as technology evolves.

“The policy question is therefore not simply one of access versus prohibition. It is a question of how access should be structured, what safeguards must accompany it, and who should be accountable when those safeguards are absent,” he said.

The bill’s provisions would establish age-based restrictions on social media use, designate a government office to oversee implementation and impose penalties for noncompliance by digital platforms.

*   ![Image 2: Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258182.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/court-agrees-to-drop-3-charges-vs-vp-sara/2444853)

The Senate approved its version, Senate Bill (SB) 2424 titled the Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act.

Both chambers will need to undergo a bicameral conference to reconcile key differences before a final bill can be sent to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for signing into law.

SB 2424 sets a strict 18-and-under restriction while HB 11566 uses a tiered model starting at age 13, so lawmakers must resolve the disparity between the two age thresholds.

title: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires
summary: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. undertook the impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte to block the shoo-in for the presidency in 2028, so he could get somebody to his liking. If that was the strategy, the latest evidence suggests it has b
content:
PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. undertook the impeachment of Vice President Sara Duterte to block the shoo-in for the presidency in 2028, so he could get somebody to his liking. If that was the strategy, the latest evidence suggests it has backfired — not because Sara has been untouched by controversy, but because the proceedings have transformed her from an embattled vice president into the country’s most visible opposition figure. The persecution against her has only strengthened her charisma. That fits with philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche’s famous aphorism: “What doesn’t kill us makes us stronger.”

The more the administration has tried to claim Sara Duterte’s guilt, on trial, the more the public has placed Marcos Jr. and his government on trial. The impeachment was intended to test Sara’s fitness for office. Instead, it has intensified doubts about the administration’s motives, performance and morality.

Indeed, Marcos’ minions have become so desperate as to even accuse Sara, as Philippine Star columnist and former Estrada go-fer Ronaldo Llamas did, of being a “traitor” for being linked to a company that was exporting products to China.

*   [DA bungles core mandates; Tiu Laurel shifts to .... road construction](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/da-bungles-core-mandates-tiu-laurel-shifts-to-road-construction/2444865)

Does this idiot think that tycoons like Lucio Tan, the Sys of SM, Ramon Ang of San Miguel, the Gokongweis and Carlos Chan, who all have operations in China, as well as the 1,200 local companies that exported to China last year the equivalent of 11 percent of the country’s total exports, are traitors?

The other day, the prosecution presented a witness who claimed Sara had billions in unexplained wealth. His basis — “documents” that the prosecution supplied him that he pored over in only three weeks, without even trying to get Sara and her husband’s explanation — crucial in one-topic documents like tax returns and AMLC reports. While he claims to be a forensic accountant, he is not: he is not certified by the Philippine Institute of Certified Forensic Accountants. He is an anti-Sara Yellow activist, having been with groups that have been demanding her impeachment since last year, and had even met with Leni Robredo late last year, for reasons he did not disclose.

[![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258205.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258205.jpg)

The strongest evidence that Marcos’ impeachment project has backfired is the latest Pulse Asia presidential preference survey conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, 2026. Sara leads every hypothetical presidential contest presented. She receives 52 percent in a three-way race against former vice president Leni Robredo and Sen. Raffy Tulfo, 57 percent against Sen. Erwin Tulfo and Sen. Risa Hontiveros, 57 percent against Erwin Tulfo and Sen. Bam Aquino, 54 percent against Robredo in a two-way race, and 60 percent against Hontiveros.

*   ![Image 2: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

**Message**

The survey results offer a clear political message: The impeachment has not produced the collapse in Sara’s support that the Marcos camp wanted.

The most politically significant result is the 52 percent-30 percent-14 percent in a three-way contest involving Sara, Robredo and Raffy Tulfo. Sara leads Robredo by 22 percentage points and Tulfo by 38 points. More important, however, is the consistency of her advantage.

Sara does not lead in only one favorable matchup. She remains ahead when the names are changed, when the field expands and when she faces a rival one-on-one. In the two-way contest against Robredo, Sara leads 54 percent to 40 percent. Against Hontiveros, she leads 60 percent to 23 percent. That consistency points to a durable political base that has survived the impeachment campaign and has even been strengthened by it.

*   ![Image 3: Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258343.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

**Contrast**

The latest presidential preference figures also become more meaningful when placed beside earlier 2026 data.

A Pulse Asia survey conducted from Feb. 27 to March 2 presented Sara in a six-way field and gave her 43 percent, followed by Leni Robredo at 27 percent and Raffy Tulfo at 19 percent. In separate head-to-head matchups, Sara led Robredo 51 percent to 43 percent, while she and Tulfo were tied at 46 percent each.

The more recent September survey the shows Sara at 52 percent in the three-way Duterte-Robredo-Tulfo contest, compared with 43 percent in the earlier six-way field. That represents a nine-point increase.

*   ![Image 4: Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258182.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/court-agrees-to-drop-3-charges-vs-vp-sara/2444853)

The political direction is striking. In March, Sara was either slightly leading or tied with her principal potential rivals. By September, she was leading decisively in every candidate set shown.

**Lead**

Her lead over Robredo also widened. In the February-March survey, Sara led Robredo by eight points, 51 percent to 43 percent. In the September two-way contest, her advantage was 14 points, 54 percent to 40 percent. These figures show that the impeachment has not damaged Sara’s presidential prospects. Her position has even become more secure.

Sara’s Mindanao base is the foundation of her national lead. A 94-percent preference rating in the region is not merely a favorable result; it is an extraordinary territorial base. She also performed strongly among all socioeconomic groups, receiving 47 percent among Class ABC respondents, 50 percent among Class D and 70 percent among Class E.

It is her huge Mindanao base, and her corps of articulate believers in social media, which makes implausible the scenario claimed by Marcos minions that, as in the case of candidate Jojo Binay in 2016, the constant barrage of black propaganda will reduce her votes by election day. But Binay never had a solid base of support as Sara does with her Mindanao and social media followers. As important is the fact that Binay’s support eroded not just because of the Yellows’ black propaganda: it was because a charismatic figure, Rodrigo Duterte, emerged to claim his base.

The Marcos minions’ strategy was to bribe senator-judges enough so that there would be the required votes to convict Sara. This indeed worked in late chief justice Renato Corona’s impeachment trial, with President Benigno Aquino III giving the senator judges P100 to P150 million each in pork-barrel funding through the so-called Disbursement Acceleration Plan, getting 20 senators to vote Corona guilty.

But Marcos has run out of time for this strategy because the first impeachment move was delayed for a year as the case that there cannot be more than one such move per year was brought before the Supreme Court. Hence, the Marcos minions had to wait a year to file another impeachment case.

**Penultimate**

As a result, the Marcos-controlled House of Representatives got to undertake the impeachment process only this year, which is the penultimate year for Marcos’ presidency. This is in contrast to Corona’s impeachment which was undertaken at the middle of the Aquino presidency in 2012, and when his popularity was at its height.

This means that senators hoping to profit from Marcos’ largesse if they convict Sara will have only a very limited time, one fiscal year, to do so. Worse for them, the administration has been hit by the worst scandal ever in our history, the ghost flood control corruption scandal, which has, with a more vigilant citizenry, made pork-barrel type of bribes difficult. Because of that scandal, senators who would have been easily bribed during Marcos’ first years would be hesitant to follow his orders: Why should they when he is now a lame duck?

The Marcos minions also made a huge mistake in calling Sara’s brother Sebastian “Baste” to the witness stand. Baste proved to have such gravitas that he could replace Sara if she is found guilty and banned from running for the presidency in 2028. The winning Duterte brand could be easily be transferred to Baste. Think about it this way: If Sara accompanies Baste in each and every rally, and if his campaign materials all show his sister raising his hand, voters would not hesitate to check the “Duterte” box in the ballot.

Filipinos after all did not vote Benigno Aquino III because they believed that he was qualified just because he carried the Aquino brand. It will be the same phenomenon if it is Baste who runs for the presidency.

Marcos and his minions certainly deserve such karmic twist: They spent billions of pesos and expended so much energy to block Sara from being president, yet in the end, it is her brother who will run and win the presidency.

Marcos’ minions have actually been on a very wrong tack. About a year and a half to the May 2028 elections, Robredo is still stuck in Naga City in political limbo. No way for Erwin to be anything but senator in 2028. With the elections on the horizon, they find themselves with no viable candidate.

title: Court agrees to drop 3 charges vs VP Sara
summary: THE Senate impeachment court granted the prosecution panel’s request Tuesday to withdraw three of the four impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte, leaving Article II, which alleges unexplained wealth, statements of assets,
content:
THE Senate impeachment court granted the prosecution panel’s request Tuesday to withdraw three of the four impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte, leaving Article II, which alleges unexplained wealth, statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) violations and prohibited business interests as the sole remaining charge.

In withdrawing three of the four impeachment articles, the prosecution panel said evidence of P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth was sufficient to secure her conviction.

“Four articles of impeachment were filed against the respondent vice president. Today, the prosecution respectfully manifests that it will no longer pursue three of them. It will stand on one, and that is Article II on unexplained wealth,” lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said in her manifestation.

*   [Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/pangilinan-links-timing-of-41-m-carpio-withdrawals-to-dutertes-deped-exit-drug-charges/2444082)

Luistro said the decision would streamline the proceedings by reducing the number of witnesses and the volume of evidence the court would have to consider.

The prosecution had listed 10 witnesses for the article on grave threats but presented only three. For the article on confidential funds, it named 27 witnesses and presented 11. Of the 15 witnesses listed for the unexplained wealth article, 11 had testified, excluding individual bank and insurance witnesses.

The prosecution will no longer present the five witnesses listed for the bribery article. In all, about 32 witnesses will no longer be called to testify.

“We believe we have provided sufficient evidence on all these allegations,” Luistro said. “We believe that evidence is substantial and compelling, and warrants the respondent’s removal from office for culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust.”

Luistro described the decision to pursue only Article II as “the most judicious course consistent with the evidence and our duty to the nation.” She cited the impeachment trial of former chief justice Renato Corona, saying the prosecution in that case had also dropped certain articles and proceeded with the remaining charges.

*   ![Image 1: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/icc-prosecutor-removes-253-items-from-evidence-list-in-duterte-case/2444598)

“That precedent recognizes the prosecution’s privilege to determine which articles to pursue and which to drop,” Luistro said.

The withdrawn articles cover the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I, alleged bribery under Article III, and grave threats, including threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., under Article IV.

The prosecution’s decision followed the presentation of financial evidence by forensic financial analyst Alexander Cabrera, who estimated that Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, had P817,874,867 in alleged unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025.

Cabrera said the amount was a conservative estimate based on his examination of the couple’s financial records.

*   ![Image 2: Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258343.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte keeps 56% trust rating, Marcos remains at 36% – SWS survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/national/duterte-keeps-56-trust-rating-marcos-remains-at-36-sws-survey/2444939)

He told the court that the figure could reach as much as P1.5 billion under less conservative accounting methods.

The P817.87-million estimate covers allegedly undeclared cash, personal and real properties, computed undeclared income, and income attributed to several corporate entities.

The highest annual amount was recorded in 2024 at P264.22 million, followed by P195.69 million in 2025, P190.63 million in 2022 and P167.34 million in 2023.

Cabrera identified P207.70 million in allegedly undeclared cash over the four-year period, comprising P60.21 million in 2022, P80.70 million in 2023, P23.17 million in 2024 and P43.61 million in 2025.

*   ![Image 3: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

He also identified P143.50 million in allegedly undeclared personal and real properties, net of deductions. The annual figures were P76.15 million in 2022, P3.93 million in 2023, P52.02 million in 2024 and P11.40 million in 2025.

The analyst’s computation included P111.85 million in allegedly undeclared income attributed to the couple, broken down into P50.47 million in 2022, P12.20 million in 2023, P28.03 million in 2024 and P21.15 million in 2025.

For corporate entities Cale88 and Metro City Chow, Cabrera calculated P142.20 million in alleged undeclared income from 2022 to 2025. The annual amounts were P3.79 million in 2022, P14.79 million in 2023, P86.94 million in 2024 and P36.67 million in 2025.

For GenCorp Industries, the computed undeclared income reached P212.63 million over three years: P55.71 million in 2023, P74.06 million in 2024 and P82.86 million in 2025. No amount was recorded for 2022 under this category.

**Defense view**

Defense counsel Sheila Sison on Tuesday warned that the prosecution’s decision to drop three of the four impeachment articles could undermine due process and unfairly restrict the defense’s presentation of evidence.

Sison argued that while the prosecution has the prerogative to withdraw charges, it should not be allowed to dictate the scope of the defense’s case after the impeachment court had already spent considerable time and government resources hearing evidence on the accusations.

She warned that allowing the prosecution to determine which accusations the defense could answer would give it extraordinary power over both sides of the proceedings.

“The authority to streamline, to achieve speed in a trial is not the authority to diminish due process or to altogether disregard the fundamental rules of fairness,” she said.

“And the desire to reach a verdict expeditiously can never justify reaching it unfairly.” Sison pointed out that the impeachment court had already devoted substantial time and resources to hearing prosecution witnesses and examining evidence relating to the charges that the prosecution now intends to abandon.

She warned that the defense could be forced to limit its presentation to the remaining article, potentially preventing Duterte from responding fully to accusations that had already been litigated before the court.

“The prerogative to withdraw an accusation is not the power to suppress its rebuttal on the part of the respondent,” she said, warning that expediting the proceedings should not come at the expense of due process and fairness.

Senate Presiding Officer Francis Escudero said the prosecution could not unilaterally determine whether an impeachment article would be withdrawn once it had been filed before the court.

Sison clarified that the defense was not objecting to the withdrawal itself but maintained that Duterte and her lawyers should decide how to proceed with their presentation of evidence.

**Opportunity to respond**

The ruling drew concern from Senator-Judge Alan Peter Cayetano, who warned against rushing the trial at the expense of fairness.

Cayetano said the court should give the defense a fair opportunity to respond to allegations already aired during weeks of hearings.

He also said deliberations on the 2027 national budget should take priority over an arbitrary deadline to finish the trial.

Cayetano said the Constitution sets no deadline for completing an impeachment trial, arguing that the Senate could take a break from the proceedings to focus on the budget and resume the trial later.

He cited the looming Super El Niño, unfinished flood control projects and the country’s economic challenges as reasons for prioritizing the budget.

Cayetano also questioned the prosecution’s decision to withdraw Articles I, III and IV after presenting witnesses and evidence on some of the allegations, saying the defense should not be denied the opportunity to answer claims already presented in court.

He likened the situation to a boxing match in which one side had already landed punches before asking the other side not to retaliate in the interest of saving time.

“The prosecution could have started with the ill-gotten wealth and stopped there. But you chose to spend 38 days,” Cayetano said.

He raised concerns that the allegations could continue to affect Duterte’s reputation even if the withdrawn articles would no longer be considered in the court’s verdict.

“This is not purely a judicial process. As we all know, it’s a political process also,” he said, adding that the proceedings affect not only the possibility of conviction or acquittal but also public perceptions of the vice president’s guilt or innocence.

Cayetano said the situation differed from the Corona impeachment trial, which he cited as a precedent for withdrawing an article before evidence and witnesses had been presented in court.

Senator-Judge Francis Pangilinan moved to reconsider the decision allowing Duterte to publicly address allegations in the three withdrawn impeachment articles.

Pangilinan recalled that Senator-Judge Bam Aquino had raised the possibility of adjusting the trial procedure as early as July 15. Escudero had indicated that changes could be considered if both the prosecution and the defense agreed, Pangilinan said.

“Unfortunately, there was no agreement, and therefore we have to proceed as we have proceeded,” he said.

Senator-Judge Risa Hontiveros noted that the defense had yet to inform the court how it wanted to proceed following the withdrawal and that the court had yet to act on any such request.

Hontiveros said she wanted to hear Duterte’s response to the allegations raised by the prosecution.

Senator-Judge Pia Cayetano, meanwhile, said she was shocked by the prosecution’s decision to withdraw the three articles and said the defense should be given sufficient time to process the development, given that Duterte’s reputation was at stake.

Escudero said Pangilinan’s motion had been taken under advisement pending a possible notice from the defense, adding that he could rule on it during the court’s recess.

**Sub judice rule lifted**

The motion followed the court’s decision to lift Rule 18 restrictions, also known as the sub judice rule, on public comments concerning Articles I, III and IV.

Under Escudero’s ruling, Duterte may publicly respond to allegations involving confidential funds, bribery and grave threats. Restrictions on public comments about the remaining Article II, which concerns alleged unexplained wealth, remain in effect.

“In particular, the respondent, given that she will no longer have an opportunity or need to defend against those articles through the presentation of evidence before the court, may therefore answer them, present her account, defend her conduct or reputation in the course of public discourse,” Escudero said.

title: Hong Kong railway builds station off-site to avoid night-time closures
summary: 香港地铁正在屯马线上采用模块化施工方式建造新的洪水桥站，将重达 10,000 吨的车站两半在 30 米外组装，然后滑行就位。该方法避免了在有限的“黄金两小时”夜间窗口期间破坏性的现场工作。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 14 日香港时间 00:04 · 2 分钟阅读 Hong香港铁路运营商正在采用创新的场外施工方法来建造新的铁路
content:
香港
港铁正在屯马线上采用模块化建造方式建造新的洪水桥站，将重达1万吨的车站半部在30米外组装起来，然后滑行就位。该方法避免了在有限的“黄金两小时”夜间窗口期间破坏性的现场工作。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 14 日 00:04 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

一位资深工程师透露，香港铁路运营商正在采用创新的场外施工方法在屯马线建造新的洪水桥站，避免了直接在运营铁路上施工通常造成的干扰。

梁光浩在专栏中写道，该站的两部分长 210 米、宽 15 米、重 10,000 吨，主要由高强度钢制成。它们在距离最终位置约 30 米的地方进行组装，从而可以在正常工作时间内进行工作，而不是在受限制的夜间时段进行。

出于安全原因，带电铁路线上的传统施工只需要在所谓的“黄金两小时”（大约凌晨 2 点到 4 点之间）进行施工。传统方法还涉及混凝土浇筑、钢筋架设等繁杂的湿作业，会给附近设施带来安全隐患和不便。
梁说，模块化设计使得车站结构可以在场外制造并运输到现场，在那里组装好两半，然后滑入到位。他将这一过程描述为需要“全面的规划和完美的执行，以确保远远超出传统土木和建筑工程实践的卓越精度”。

工程师表示，滑移施工方法已广泛应用于世界各地的基建项目，香港专业人士也很快从中学习。他引用了之前粉岭公路高架桥的例子，该高架桥建在邻近空地上，并在临时转盘上旋转约90度就位，避免在拥挤地区进行长时间施工，以免中断铁路服务和供水。

梁振英表示，香港几十年前一直处于科技前沿，但后来慢慢落后于邻国。他对该市目前采用新的建设方法以保持竞争力和有效性表示满意。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
MTR is building the new Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line using modular construction, assembling 10,000-tonne station halves 30 metres away before skidding them into place. The method avoids disruptive in-situ work during the limited 'Golden Two Hours' night window.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

14 Oct 2026 at 00:04 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's railway operator is using an innovative off-site construction method to build the new Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line, avoiding the disruption normally caused by building directly on an operating railway, a veteran engineer has revealed.

Writing in his column, Edmund Leung Kwong-ho said the station's two halves, each predominantly of high tensile steel, measure 210 metres long and 15 metres wide and weigh 10,000 tonnes. They are being assembled about 30 metres away from their final position, allowing work to take place during normal working hours rather than in the restricted night-time window.

Conventional construction on a live railway line would require work to be done only during the so-called "Golden Two Hours", approximately between 2am and 4am, for safety reasons. Traditional methods also involve messy wet trades such as concrete pouring and the erection of reinforcement steel, which can pose safety risks and inconvenience to nearby facilities.

Leung said the modular design allows the station structure to be fabricated off-site and transported to the location, where the halves are assembled before being skidded into place. He described the process as requiring "comprehensive planning and flawless execution to ensure exceptional precision far beyond traditional civil and building work practices".

The engineer noted that skidding construction methods have been widely adopted in infrastructure projects around the world, and Hong Kong professionals have quickly learned from them. He cited a previous example of the Fanling Highway viaduct, which was built on an empty adjacent site and rotated about 90 degrees into position on a temporary turntable, avoiding prolonged construction in a congested area that could have interrupted railway services and water supplies.

Leung said Hong Kong had been at the forefront of technology decades ago but had slowly trailed behind its neighbours. He expressed satisfaction that the city is now adopting new construction methods to retain competitiveness and effectiveness.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

title: The café-fication of Binondo
summary: IT might be too soon to say, but Binondo’s face is changing one new café at a time. Certain parts of Binondo have always been pedestrian-friendly. Manila’s historic Chinatown has been long associated with trading houses, old-school eateries
content:
IT might be too soon to say, but Binondo’s face is changing one new café at a time. Certain parts of Binondo have always been pedestrian-friendly. Manila’s historic Chinatown has been long associated with trading houses, old-school eateries, gold shops and the business of commerce. Established in 1594, Binondo is widely recognized as the world’s oldest Chinatown. The Binondo now seems to be courting a new and different kind of energy with new cafes that stay open till past the Gen X bedtime.

Cafés such as Apologue Coffee, Still Café, Escolta Coffee Company and The Den are adding new stops to the neighborhood’s familiar food trail beyond dimsum. More people are walking, meeting friends over coffee, and lingering in places where the activity of the street becomes part of the experience. Apologue Coffee and Pastry was one of the first street-level cafes I experienced in the traditional Benavidez Street right across the historic noodle shop Masuki. It opened in 2023. I was immediately charmed by its vintage tiles, small modular furniture, and the vintage photos of old Chinatown. Though the stools and tables are tiny, one is encouraged to stay and linger because of the electric plugs. It reminds me of a place an old Tsinoy uncle would stop in after a long day at the office.

Escolta Coffee Company, a coffee roaster team has set up shop in the street level of the old Burke Building in Escolta. It is a cousin of The Den Manila, a coffee and creative cultural spot tucked in the back of the first floor of the First United Building. It took years for the urban and hip culture to move to the Burke Building. And now the roaster and all its coffee merchandise are visible behind glass from Burke Street.

*   [The strongman finally meets a stronger institution](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/the-strongman-finally-meets-a-stronger-institution/2444846)

I chanced upon Still Café on Jaboneros Street when it opened two weeks ago. Unlike the stealth and organic growth of the previously mentioned cafés, Still busted into the social media scene backed by what seems to be a concerted marketing effort. It is a Vietnamese-style coffee shop with a gazillion props of analog life — Singer sewing machines, books, typewriters, vinyl records, telephones, the whole caboodle. I asked the staff why sewing machines and books lined the walls, they didn’t have an answer. Story is everything. Binondo’s soul runs deep in its layers, there is no need to manufacture a new world “aesthetic” for a coffee shop. Apologue, Escolta Coffee and The Den get it and pay homage to the oldest Chinatown.

What I do appreciate with Still Café and the others I mentioned, is their boldness to invest in the streetscape and building façade in an area of Binondo lined with offices, trading houses and wholesalers. Most of them stay open until 11 p.m. Jaboneros is beyond my usual Binondo walking area. But now it gives people reason to visit and walk. It is a subtle but significant shift, one that says something important about our cities. When we make streets and public spaces better for people, we make neighborhoods better for business, too.

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The Binondo Riverside Esplanade adds another dimension. By opening up space along the river for people to walk and spend time outdoors, it offers an alternative to crowded streets and commercial interiors. The waterfront becomes more than a leftover space behind the city; it becomes a destination in its own right.

The Binondo-Intramuros Bridge over the Pasig River, completely funded through a grant from the Chinese government, is a very popular hangout or “tambayan.” I was there in March of this year and the bridge at night is lined by sightseers, food vendors, bikers, photographers, joggers and even mobile cafés. It was unplanned and uncontrolled, slightly dangerous but charming. The architecture of the bridge is a popular backdrop for photographers. People linger for the sunset views and Manila skyline. I gather the local police are beginning to discourage loitering to ensure safety and traffic are protected.

We often talk about revitalizing commercial districts in terms of investment, new buildings and major developments. But some of the most meaningful improvements happen at ground level. A better sidewalk, a safer crossing, good lighting, and trees and landscaping are details that determine whether people want to walk, linger, spend and return.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Our historic districts are not relics to be preserved behind the glass of nostalgia. They are living urban environments. Their future depends not only on saving old buildings but also on making the spaces between them useful, comfortable and alive. Even if I’m not a fan of certain café aesthetics, I am happy they are sprouting on street levels in what otherwise would be a dark street and closed to business by 6 p.m.

I am reminded of the great urbanist Jane Jacobs, who lived in my Toronto neighborhood, and her seminal 1961 book, The Death and Life of Great American Cities. Jacobs argued that safe, lively neighborhoods depend partly on what she called “eyes on the street” — the natural surveillance created by people using sidewalks and by buildings with active frontages. A café with windows facing the street, a restaurant with diners into the evening, or a shop that keeps its doors open creates a human presence that a blank wall or a deserted office lobby cannot. When people have reasons to occupy public space, streets become more visible, more sociable, and potentially safer.

The changing landscape of Binondo offers a glimpse of what that future could look like. The cafés are part of the story. The riverside esplanade is another. But the more important development is the growing possibility of experiencing the neighborhood on foot, discovering its history, supporting local businesses, spending time by the water, and seeing familiar streets in a new light.

title: From parking lots to people places
summary: WALK through any of the Makati CBD’s neighborhoods, and one begins to notice the abundance of open lots serving as parking space. Empty, heat-soaked, lifeless. They sit in front of malls, beside offices, apartment buildings, and even next t
content:
WALK through any of the Makati CBD’s neighborhoods, and one begins to notice the abundance of open lots serving as parking space. Empty, heat-soaked, lifeless.

They sit in front of malls, beside offices, apartment buildings, and even next to schools and hospitals. Prime urban land — often in the most accessible locations — reduced to storage for idle vehicles. This is not just bad design; it is bad economics and irresponsible land use.

**The hidden cost of asphalt**

*   [The strongman finally meets a stronger institution](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/the-strongman-finally-meets-a-stronger-institution/2444846)

A surface parking lot is one of the least productive uses of land in a city. It generates little economic activity, no social interaction, and contributes directly to urban heat, flooding and environmental degradation. And yet, we continue to plan cities as if cars, and not people, are the primary users of space.

In Metro Manila, land values are among the highest in Southeast Asia. Why, then, do we dedicate some of our most valuable parcels to something that produces no life, no culture, and no community? The answer is simple: We do not plan for people.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A city is meant to be a place where people meet, linger and interact. Parking lots do the opposite. They hinder mobility, break up urban fabric, and create dead zones between buildings.

Worse, they silently dictate urban form. Buildings are pushed farther apart. Streets widen. Sidewalks shrink. Trees disappear. The city becomes barren, not by accident, but by design. Land area does not grow, yet we act as if it were replenishable.

**A systemic issue**

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

When coming up with solutions, we must address the root of the problem. The deeper issue surrounding parking lots is not a lack of space, but a scarcity of mobility. In the field of urban transportation, there is a hierarchy of road users.

Pedestrians and cyclists sit at the top, for they are the most vulnerable. Automobiles and other motor vehicles sit below. Not only are they the biggest threat on the road, they also consume the most space. Parking is a problem because we prioritize the least efficient mode of transport.

This is most evident in many parts of the US. In a country where the majority travel by car, zoning laws have minimum parking requirements. Drive up to a Walmart, and you’ll easily see that the parking lot takes up as much space as the store itself. Stadiums are the ultimate example with the majority of land area allocated just for parking.

**Lessons from Boston**

*   ![Image 2: Academic freedom no alibi for enabling Sara Duterte](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256409.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Academic freedom no alibi for enabling Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/academic-freedom-no-alibi-for-enabling-sara-duterte/2443936)

I would like to reminisce on my time as a student at the Harvard GSD. One particular neighborhood in the Greater Boston Area that has become an exemplar in the management of parking space is the Fenway.

Because of the neighborhood’s integration with Fenway Park, the home of the Red Sox, it has no doubt become a hotbed for both foot traffic and vehicular traffic during game days in April to October of each year. In the early 2000s, the neighborhood surrounding the ballpark was composed almost entirely of parking lots.

Since the late 2000s and the early 2010s, up until the present day, the bulk of these parking lots have been turned into mixed-use and transit-oriented developments with retail, residential and office spaces.

Underground parking is still a component of these new projects. However, it was built to be mixed-use, accommodating vehicular traffic during game season in the Fenway and serving other purposes for the rest of the year.

*   ![Image 3: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

By shaping a neighborhood to be people-centric, repurposing parking lots creates value instead of taking up space. Property values gradually increase, local businesses thrive, and the streets become safer. It’s a classic play from the urbanist’s handbook: Always aim for the highest and best use of land.

**Local examples in tactical urbanism**

While we can’t get rid of parking lots completely overnight, they can be repurposed for more productive uses. The Mayflower Parking in Greenfield used to be your ordinary parking lot, but when the Food Truck Fest reopened in 2022, the space has never been more productive.

The lot is filled with small businesses serving all sorts of food and beverages to a diverse community, consisting of condo residents, bikers, joggers and office workers. It’s conveniently located near the MRT Shaw Station, and creates night life since it’s open from late afternoon until close to midnight.

Makati also shows how streets flourish when they are closed off to cars and opened for people, as seen with the weekend markets in Legazpi and Salcedo, Makati Street Meet along Paseo de Roxas, and Car-Free Sundays at Ayala Avenue.

These should not be limited to one-day events; their essence should be part of the daily lives of people living and working in Makati. That is why the De la Rosa 2 Carpark is being redeveloped from a parking building into a mixed-use space. This is also known as adaptive reuse.

**The Philippine opportunity**

The Philippines has a rare advantage: We are still building much of our urban future. That means we still have the chance to correct the course.

Only 12 percent of households in Metro Manila own cars. Catering to motorists while neglecting pedestrians, cyclists and commuters is transport injustice. As I said in my UP term paper in 1973, development is not worthy of its name unless it is spread evenly like butter on a piece of bread.

If we continue to allow vast surface parking lots to exist in prime commercial districts, we are effectively subsidizing underdevelopment. Every open asphalt lot has an opportunity cost. That land could house residents and shorten their commute. It could host schools that provide education, or offices that generate employment. It could provide pocket parks that cool the area and improve public health.

We would like to live in smart, resilient and sustainable cities. However, in order for our cities to be future-ready, we must integrate modern planning concepts such as mixed-use zoning, transit-oriented development, proximity-based planning and vertical urbanism, to address the demand for urbanization.

When these concepts are acted upon by city planners, LGUs, property developers and property owners, our cities have a better chance of maximizing our underutilized parking lots and hardscaped open spaces. When land has a multitude of uses, all of the city’s denizens will thrive.

title: China-linked hackers hit Fiji – US embassy
summary: **SYDNEY**, Australia — Hackers with links to China compromised a regional organization in Fiji, the Pacific nation’s United States embassy said on Tuesday, warning that governments and telecommunication networks in the region were also bei
content:
**SYDNEY**, Australia — Hackers with links to China compromised a regional organization in Fiji, the Pacific nation’s United States embassy said on Tuesday, warning that governments and telecommunication networks in the region were also being targeted.

Fiji is emerging as a major telecommunications hub in the Pacific Islands, as Google expands a network of subsea cables connecting the US military outpost of Guam, US defense ally Australia, French Polynesia and the mainland US via Fiji’s capital Suva.

Ioane Naivalurua, the island nation’s policing and communications minister, said he was reviewing the situation after the US embassy announced that a “regional organization in Suva” had its network hacked between July and August.

*   [Two vessels struck off Bulgarian coast – PM](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/two-vessels-struck-off-bulgarian-coast-pm/2444600)

“Hackers with links to China maintained access to the organization’s network over several days,” the embassy said in a statement posted on Facebook without identifying the organization.

US officials have previously urged cable host Fiji to boost cybersecurity to guard against data risks from China.

Naivalurua said police were investigating the reported attack and urged governments, organizations and the private sector to “take preventative action and harden the security of their respective digital systems.”

In Beijing, the Chinese foreign ministry said it was not aware of the case, but that it “firmly opposes hacking activities and cracks down on them in accordance with the law.”

“At the same time, we also oppose using cybersecurity issues to smear China,” spokesman Mao Ning told a regular briefing.

*   ![Image 1: Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Lacson asks Padilla to clarify ‘disregard for law’ comment on Duterte trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/lacson-asks-padilla-to-clarify-disregard-for-law-comment-on-duterte-trial/2444142)

Fiji’s government had asked the US last Friday to provide evidence for its claim last week that a Chinese state agency employee living in Fiji had paid bribes on behalf of Beijing.

The US State Department accused the man living in Suva of “significant corruption.”

The US embassy pointed on Tuesday to action taken by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in August to combat China-sponsored hackers targeting critical infrastructure in US.

The FBI action “matters directly for the Pacific,” the embassy said.

*   ![Image 2: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

A group of hackers called QTFY included former members of China’s military, working for a company paid by China’s Ministry of State Security, had targeted the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, the US Department of Energy, and power companies, an FBI affidavit said.

China-linked hackers were targeting foreign governments, organizations and telecommunications networks in the Pacific Islands, the embassy wrote on Facebook.

The region’s political bloc, the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF), said it was not the organization that had been hacked.

“While the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat is not affected, cybersecurity is increasingly important to the Pacific as the region’s digital security is closely linked to its economic resilience, national sovereignty, regional security, and wellbeing of Pacific communities,” a PIF spokesman told Agence France-Presse (AFP).

title: Visa gets approval to prepare for domestic business in China
summary: US payments firm Visa has received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world’s largest payment markets. The mo
content:
US payments firm Visa has received approval from China’s central bank to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution in the country, ending years of waiting to tap into one of the world’s largest payment markets.

The move marks a major step for Visa to join rivals American Express and Mastercard in operating bank card clearing services in China and represents a further opening up of the nation’s tightly controlled financial sector.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) issued an administrative approval to Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co. Ltd. permitting it to begin preparatory work, according to the central bank’s website.

*   [Prepare for El Niño, Marcos urges Filipinos](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/business/top-business/prepare-for-el-nio-marcos-urges-filipinos/2444065)

Visa Information Technology (Beijing) is a foreign-invested enterprise established in China by Visa.

“The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa’s long-standing commitment to China,” Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in a statement on Tuesday.

The approval comes after US President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier this year in China, which included more than a dozen CEOs of top US companies, including those of Mastercard and Visa.

“We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” McInerney said.

Visa must complete its preparations within one year, after which it can apply to open for business, the PBOC said.

The central bank, together with the nation’s top banking regulator, will review the application and, if it approves, issue a bank card clearing business license.

A goodwill gesture?

*   ![Image 3: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

Visa was hoping to break into the Chinese market, which is dominated by state-controlled China UnionPay, with an unprecedented 100-percent ownership stake in a future joint venture license, sources have told Reuters.

“This should be viewed as a goodwill gesture from Beijing toward Washington ahead of the next meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump,” said George Chen, partner and chairman of digital practice at The Asia Group. The two are expected to meet again on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen in November.

Greater market access in financial services has long been a priority for Washington, which has consistently urged Beijing to provide a more open and level playing field for foreign firms operating in China’s financial sector, said Chen.

Mastercard, partnering with local clearinghouse NetsUnion Clearing Corp., won approval to prepare to set up its bank card clearing business in China in 2020.

American Express’ joint venture in the country was cleared to start bank card clearing services later that year.

In China, bank cards processed 4.6 trillion transactions worth 963.60 trillion yuan ($143.92 trillion) in 2025, according to data from the central bank, highlighting the market’s enormous potential.

# Chinese court sentences scam operators to death

[![Image 22: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/102_1657587153.jpg)![Image 23: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/102_1657587153.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/agence-france-presse "author image")

[By Agence France-Presse](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/agence-france-presse "Agence France-Presse")

 October 14, 2026

**BEIJING**— A Chinese court sentenced three members of a criminal gang to death on Tuesday for operating a network of brutal scam centers in Myanmar’s Kokang region on the border with China, while jailing dozens more.

China has stepped up cooperation with Southeast Asian nations to crack down on a vast industry that has flourished in the region in recent years to fleece people out of billions of dollars.

Those conducting the online scams are sometimes willing con artists, and other times trafficked foreigners — many Chinese — tricked themselves into work and held in prison-like compounds.

*   [Two vessels struck off Bulgarian coast – PM](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/two-vessels-struck-off-bulgarian-coast-pm/2444600)

In a statement, the Quanzhou Intermediate People’s Court said on Tuesday it had sentenced Wei Huairen, Chen Dawei, and Liao Jingfang to death for their involvement in the “Wei family criminal gang.”

The gang was involved in crimes including drug trafficking, organizing prostitution, operating illegal casinos, telecommunications fraud, and the murder of at least two Chinese citizens, the court added.

Wei Huairen was identified as one of the group’s leaders and found guilty of several crimes including murder, the court said.

The gang’s operations netted more than 12.2 billion yuan ($1.8 billion).

Advertisement

Three more gang members were handed life sentences, while an additional 55 were given prison terms ranging from 24 years to three years and three months.

*   ![Image 28: ICC prosecutor removes 253 items from evidence list in Duterte case](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1257681.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

Analysts describe the Wei clan as one of the “four families” running crime syndicates in Kokang.

State-run broadcaster China Central Television (CCTV) on Tuesday called them the “most violent criminal force in northern Myanmar,” having created an “iron triangle of political, military, and business criminal activities.”

It described the gang as operating 14 “large-scale” scam compounds and luring “large numbers” of Chinese to Myanmar through fake promises of high wages.

Advertisement

Police had also discovered remains of victims bound with iron chains and with bullet holes in their skulls, CCTV said.

*   ![Image 29: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Members of the Wei family were first indicted in October 2025.

In January, China executed 11 people, including members of the “Ming family criminal gang.”

The following month, four members of the notorious Bai clan were executed for crimes including “fraud, intentional homicide, intentional injury, kidnapping, [and] extortion.”

## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AI[Subscribe](https://news.google.com/subscriptions)

A global slide in semiconductor stocks deepened, sending South Korea’s chip-heavy equity benchmark down more than 7% at one point, as concerns about AI overheating and Chinese competition intensified.

[Samsung Electronics Co.](https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/005930:KS) and [SK Hynix Inc.](https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/000660:KS) shares dropped about 7% and 10% each Tuesday, dragging the Kospi down 5.5% at the close. Taiwan’s Taiex and Japan’s Nikkei 225 both fell nearly 2% after US chipmakers slumped overnight.
