title: Chinese Loans Aimed at Influence
summary: The state-controlled Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) has invested millions of dollars in projects across Africa. A new report says the bank has made loans despite ignoring corruption among the countries receiving them while a
content:
The state-controlled Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) has invested millions of dollars in projects across Africa. A new report says the bank has made loans despite ignoring corruption among the countries receiving them while also aligning its investments with China’s political goals for the continent.

The report, “China Capital,” by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, reviewed nearly 5 million internal documents from 2005 to 2024 held at the bank’s London offices to identify the way the ICBC courted high-risk borrowers in Africa and elsewhere to secure resources and alliances for China.

Among the documents were instructions from ICBC’s Community Party committee, which pushes government policies. The investigation revealed that ICBC worked with clients that other lenders avoided because of corruption or sanctioned owners.

“Credit application forms and other confidential records sometimes included the phrase ‘China rationale’ to explain why ICBC London would want to pursue a deal, revealing the geopolitical nature of some loans,” investigator Scilla Alecci wrote in the report.

The ICBC does much of its work in Africa through the continent’s largest bank by assets, South Africa’s Standard Bank Group, which has affiliates in 21 African countries. The ICBC began its relations with Standard Bank Group in 2007 and renewed its investment in 2023. It currently holds a 19.7% stake in the South African bank.

Standard Bank told The Africa Report that, despite the ICBC’s stake, Standard Bank remains an independent institution that operates under its own guidelines for making loans.

“No individual shareholder is responsible for determining lending decisions,” the bank told The Africa Report.

An internal report written at the ICBC’s Beijing headquarters in 2024 warned that the bank’s overseas operations showed poor client screening, weak oversight of employees, and incomplete reporting on anti-money-laundering efforts. Some senior ICBC officials failed to act after receiving reports about the problems, according to the report.

“When convenient for Beijing, the records show, the bankers would willingly serve state companies — even those that were not transparent about their financial flows and controlled by governments that, in the words of one ICBC banker, were ‘clearly kleptocracies,’” Alecci wrote.

Angola’s state-owned Sonangol Group oil company was one of ICBC clients that received large loans despite a history of corruption. The company received $2.5 billion from ICBC when it was controlled by people with close ties to then-Angolan President José Eduardo dos Santos.

“Internal memos about a 2010 loan illustrate China’s leverage as Angola’s largest foreign creditor, requiring Sonangol to both sell its oil to China and use the loan proceeds to hire Chinese construction companies,” the ICIJ reported.

More than a decade later, the ICBC dismissed corruption allegations against the oil company’s former head, Isabel dos Santos, the former president’s daughter. She was charged in 2017 with costing $219 million in losses for the state during her Sonangol tenure.

An internal ICBC memo said, despite the suspected corruption, the bank should continue working with Sonangol Group because of its role in China’s Belt and Road Initiative.

ICBC supported Sierra Leone’s plans to upgrade Queen Elizabeth II Quay at the Port of Freetown in 2017. Despite reports of public corruption by the government, Chinese banks offered nearly $660 million in loans for the project.

“ICBC London made an exception to the bank’s compliance policies for the Sierra Leone borrower,” Alecci wrote. A year after signing the loan, reports of corruption by the developers caused bank officials to withhold the loan without actually cancelling it.

The ICIJ report quoted one ICBC banker: “If [head office] cancel it, it will hurt the relationship with the government of Sierra Leone.”

title: US And China Discuss Hosting Reciprocal Nuclear Site Visits To Build Trust Amid Growing Tensions
summary: In recent years, concerns surrounding nuclear weapons, military competition, and the possibility of a new arms race has led to tensions within the international community. To prevent these tensions from starting international conflict, it i
content:
In recent years, concerns surrounding nuclear weapons, military competition, and the possibility of a new arms race has led to tensions within the international community. To prevent these tensions from starting international conflict, it is important for countries to cooperate and communicate. Possible preliminary discussions between the United States and China about reciprocal visits to their nuclear facilities have offered an opportunity for the two countries to strengthen trust and prevent possible future conflicts.

These discussions come amid growing concerns about China’s rapidly expanding nuclear weapons program, although the United States currently has an estimated 5,000 nuclear warheads while China has approximately 600. However, China has been expanding its nuclear infrastructure and is projected to produce hundreds of warheads over the next decade, raising concerns that the world might be entering a new arms race. If one were to occur, it would threaten international peace and security by increasing mistrust, encouraging further military expansion, and raising the possibility of a dangerous confrontation between nuclear-armed states.

Efforts to establish a trilateral arms control agreement involving the United States, Russia, and China began during Trump’s first presidency. However, progress had been limited, with China and Russia largely ignoring U.S. outreach efforts. During that time, China argued that its nuclear arsenal was considerably smaller than that of the United States and Russia. As such, they were reluctant to participate in negotiations that would limit their nuclear buildup. These disagreements show just how difficult it can be to build trust and achieve cooperation when countries have different priorities and perceptions of military threats.

According to a report published by CNN on October 6th, the idea of reciprocal visits was raised by Chinese officials on the sidelines of gatherings by the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, known as the P5. They discussed visiting the U.S. Department of Energy’s national labs and China’s equivalent facilities. U.S. officials were open to discussing such visits. If these discussions come to fruition, the visits could serve as confidence-building measures for both countries, allowing them to gain a better understanding of the other’s nuclear activities and create opportunities for more significant discussions about nuclear risks.

Although formal negotiations have not yet taken place, discussion surrounding such visits represent an important step towards improving communication between China and the U.S. These discussions may not immediately lead to a formal arms control agreement, but they could establish a foundation for future negotiations. Fundamentally, maintaining peace requires that countries recognize their shared responsibility in preventing nuclear conflict. As tensions surrounding nuclear powers continue to grow, the United States and China must prioritize cooperation over competition.

title: 俄罗斯鼠疫疑云 呼伦贝尔发风险提示又撤回 香港澳门发布安全警报
summary: 俄罗斯西伯利亚一名防鼠疫研究机构工作人员因不明原因肺炎死亡后，内蒙古呼伦贝尔、香港和澳门相继发布公共卫生风险提示，加强口岸健康监测。不过，截至星期二(10月13日)，还没有证据显示中国启动了全国性边境管控，或对中俄边境实施新的人员往来限制。 这起事件之所以引起关注，不仅因为鼠疫是一种具有严重公共卫生风险的传染病，也因为前苏联历史上曾开展秘密的进攻性生物武器计划，其中包括对鼠疫等病原体的研究。 **俄罗斯事件尚未确认病因** 世界卫生组织(WHO)10月10日发布的[通报](h
content:
俄罗斯西伯利亚一名防鼠疫研究机构工作人员因不明原因肺炎死亡后，内蒙古呼伦贝尔、香港和澳门相继发布公共卫生风险提示，加强口岸健康监测。不过，截至星期二(10月13日)，还没有证据显示中国启动了全国性边境管控，或对中俄边境实施新的人员往来限制。

这起事件之所以引起关注，不仅因为鼠疫是一种具有严重公共卫生风险的传染病，也因为前苏联历史上曾开展秘密的进攻性生物武器计划，其中包括对鼠疫等病原体的研究。

**俄罗斯事件尚未确认病因**

世界卫生组织(WHO)10月10日发布的[通报](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON620)说，俄罗斯伊尔库茨克(Irkutsk)一名防鼠疫研究机构工作人员于9月29日因严重肺炎住院，并于10月2日死亡。由于死者在涉及高危病原体的研究机构工作，媒体曾猜测她可能感染了肺鼠疫。

世卫组织援引俄罗斯当局提供的信息说，死者及其接触者接受了多种病原体检测，包括鼠疫病原体和其他高危病原体，检测没有发现相关感染。俄罗斯方面还表示，调查没有发现实验室生物安全事故，也没有发现与该事件相关的其他严重肺炎病例。

不过，世卫组织指出，死者的确切病因仍未查明，因此目前仍存在不确定性。根据俄罗斯方面提供的信息，世卫组织没有发现与该事件相关的持续传播证据，也没有建议各国因此实施旅行或贸易限制。

**呼伦贝尔发布鼠疫风险提示后删除**

10月10日，内蒙古呼伦贝尔市融媒体中心官方微博发布了呼伦贝尔市疾控中心的鼠疫防控风险提示，提及俄罗斯伊尔库茨克研究机构工作人员死亡事件，并提醒曾到访俄罗斯远东鼠疫疫源地区的人员关注健康状况，出现疑似症状时及时就医。

提示同时指出，呼伦贝尔自1927年以来未再出现人间鼠疫病例，近年来常态化监测也未发现鼠间鼠疫疫情。当地疾控部门综合评估认为，呼伦贝尔发生鼠疫疫情的可能性较低。

不过，10月13日的媒体报道援引呼伦贝尔市卫生健康委员会工作人员的话说，当地目前并无鼠疫疫情，相关提示属于常规科普宣传，发布内容已被删除，以避免公众误解。

**香港加强机场筛查，澳门采取预防性措施**

香港政府卫生署卫生防护中心10月12日发布[公告](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/12/P2026101200212.htm)说，根据世卫组织提供的信息，目前没有证据显示俄罗斯事件涉及持续传播，事件对香港公共卫生构成的即时风险较低。

香港方面仍决定采取预防措施，包括加强俄罗斯来港航班的旅客体温监测、要求过去14天到访俄罗斯伊尔库茨克州的旅客主动申报旅行史，以及将出现肺炎症状的旅客转介公立医院接受进一步检查。卫生防护中心还将提醒本地医生和医院提高警觉，加强相关病例监测。

澳门也发布了针对俄罗斯相关事件的健康风险[提示](https://www.gov.mo/zh-hans/news/942985/)，并采取口岸防疫措施。相关报道提及加强旅客发热筛查，以及要求近期到访伊尔库茨克州的入境人士申报旅行史，旨在识别可能出现症状的旅客。

**鼠疫是什么？为何受到如此重视？**

鼠疫是由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起的一种人畜共患传染病，病原体通常存在于小型哺乳动物及其携带的跳蚤中。人类可能因被感染跳蚤叮咬、接触受感染动物的组织或体液而感染；肺鼠疫患者也可能通过呼吸道飞沫将疾病传染给他人。

鼠疫曾在历史上造成大规模疫情。14世纪席卷欧洲的黑死病是其中最著名的例子。现代医学已经能够通过抗生素有效治疗鼠疫，但及时诊断和治疗仍至关重要。

世卫组织指出，鼠疫目前仍在部分国家和地区存在。2019年至2025年间，向世卫组织报告的人类感染鼠疫病例主要来自刚果民主共和国和马达加斯加。

俄罗斯此次事件也使苏联时期的生物武器研究历史再次受到关注。

美国国会研究处(Congressional Research Service)2002年发布的一份[报告](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/RL31368.html)指出，前苏联的生物武器计划至少可以追溯到1928年，并在此后数十年持续扩大。报告列出鼠疫等病原体，称前苏联生物武器计划曾对这些病原体进行武器化研究。

title: Restored Taiwan film 'Osmanthus Alley' screens at Lumière Festival - Focus Taiwan
zh_title: 修复后的台湾电影《桂花巷》在卢米埃电影节放映 - 焦点台湾
summary: 中新社巴黎10月13日电 台湾剧情片《桂花巷》4K修复版入围卢米埃尔经典单元后，周一在法国里昂第十八届卢米埃尔电影节展映。该片于 1987 年上映，由陈坤厚执导，故事背景设定在 1900 年代初，陆小芬饰演一名孤女，她面对贫穷、守寡和社会束缚，坚强不屈。终其一生，她用自己的狡猾和美丽改变了自己的命运。台湾电影视听研究所（TFAI）已将影片修复为4K并恢复
content:
中新社巴黎10月13日电 台湾剧情片《桂花巷》4K修复版入围卢米埃尔经典单元后，周一在法国里昂第十八届卢米埃尔电影节展映。

该片于 1987 年上映，由陈坤厚执导，故事背景设定在 1900 年代初，陆小芬饰演一名孤女，她面对贫穷、守寡和社会束缚，坚强不屈。终其一生，她用自己的狡猾和美丽改变了自己的命运。

台湾电影视听研究所 (TFAI) 已以 4K 格式修复了该影片，并从国语版本中恢复了原始的台湾闽南语音频。

在文化部巴黎台湾文化中心的支持下，陈、陆与台湾文化协会主席褚明仁前往里昂，在百代白莱果电影院观看了放映活动。

戛纳电影节主席兼电影节主席蒂埃里·弗雷莫（Thierry Frémaux）在放映前介绍了该片，称赞台湾是电影制作大国，拥有相当多的创作人才，其中包括台湾导演杨德昌和侯孝贤。

他补充说，台湾充满活力的当代电影场景反映了深厚的电影遗产，得到了机构、电影节和经典电影修复工作的支持。
陈在接受中央社电话采访时表示，修复“桂花巷”可以让现代观众看到台湾早期的建筑和生活方式，了解台湾的过去。

陈还回忆起里昂卢米埃尔博物馆百年电影制作和放映设备的感动，反思了电影的进步，并表示这次经历再次坚定了他的职业选择。

与此同时，卢女士表示，她没想到在拍摄《桂花巷》时，电影有一天会带她去卢米埃尔电影节。

陆说，尽管上映已经39年了，但影片对坚韧的描绘仍然感动着观众。

朱说，这部电影最初是用台湾闽南语构思、编写和拍摄的，但后来以普通话向公众发行，这表明 TFAI 后来能够找到四份幸存的闽南语版本。

卢米埃尔经典部分成立于 17 年前，旨在表彰世界电影遗产的杰出修复。每年，电影节都会从世界各地的电影图书馆、工作室、档案馆、版权所有者和基金会提交的近 180 部提交的影片中挑选几部经过修复的电影，在活动期间进行独家放映。

卢米埃尔电影节将于今年 10 月 10 日至 18 日举行，通过修复版画、回顾和向过去的电影致敬来庆祝电影历史。该电影节以卢米埃尔兄弟的名字命名，他们于 1895 年发明了 Cinématographe 电影系统，由卢米埃尔研究所组织。
(By Tzeng Yi-shiuan and Ko Lin)

Enditem/ASG

【原文 English Original】
Paris, Oct. 13 (CNA) A 4K-restored version of the Taiwanese drama film "Osmanthus Alley" (桂花巷) was screened at the 18th Lumière Festival in Lyon, France on Monday, after being selected for the festival's Lumière Classics section.

Released in 1987 and directed by Chen Kun-hou (陳坤厚), the film is set in the early 1900s and stars Lu Hsiao-fen (陸小芬) as an orphaned girl who faces poverty, widowhood and social constraints with resilience. Throughout her life, she uses her cunning and beauty to change her fate.

The Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute (TFAI) has restored the film in 4K and recovered its original Taiwanese Hokkien audio from the Mandarin version.

With support from the Taiwan Cultural Center in Paris under the Ministry of Culture, Chen, Lu and TFAI Chairman Arthur Chu (褚明仁) traveled to Lyon and attended the screening at the Pathé Bellecour cinema.

Festival director Thierry Frémaux, who also heads the Cannes Film Festival and is familiar with Taiwanese cinema, introduced the film before its screening, praising Taiwan as a major filmmaking country with considerable creative talent, including Taiwanese directors Edward Yang (楊德昌) and Hou Hsiao-hsien (侯孝賢).

He added that Taiwan's vibrant contemporary film scene reflected a strong cinematic heritage, supported by institutions, film festivals and efforts to restore classic films.

Speaking to CNA by phone, Chen said restoring "Osmanthus Alley" allows modern audiences to see Taiwan's early architecture and way of life and learn about the island's past.

Chen also recalled being moved by the century-old filmmaking and projection equipment at the Musée Lumière in Lyon, reflecting on how far cinema had advanced and saying the experience reaffirmed his choice of career.

Meanwhile, Lu said she never imagined that when filming "Osmanthus Alley," the movie would one day take her to the Lumière Festival.

Despite being released 39 years ago, the film's portrayal of resilience continues to move audiences, Lu said.

The film was originally conceived, written and shot in Taiwanese Hokkien but later released to the public in Mandarin, Chu said, indicating that the TFAI was later able to find four surviving copies of the Hokkien version.

Established 17 years ago, the Lumière Classics section recognizes outstanding restorations of world cinema heritage. Each year, the festival selects several restored films from nearly 180 submissions from film libraries, studios, archives, rights holders and foundations worldwide for exclusive screenings during the event.

The Lumière Festival runs from Oct. 10-18 this year, celebrating cinema history through restored prints, retrospectives and tributes to films of the past. The festival is named after the Lumière brothers, who invented the Cinématographe motion picture system in 1895, and is organized by the Institut Lumière.

(By Tzeng Yi-shiuan and Ko Lin)

## 中共中央紀委：薄熙來前搭檔黃奇帆接受調查

圖像來源，China News Service

圖像加註文字，黃奇帆在薄熙來、王立軍系列醜聞爆發後留守重慶至2016年。

Published 2026年10月13日

閱讀時間: 4 分鐘

中共反貪腐機關宣佈，已離任多時的前重慶市市長黃奇帆被立案調查。

黃奇帆2001年起於重慶任職，2010年起出任市長兼中共市委副書記，不久後便爆發市委書記薄熙來與副市長兼公安局長王立軍系列醜聞。黃奇帆任職市長直到2016年底。

黃奇帆退任市長後仍不時作為經濟學家發表公開演說。來自香港的報導稱，他原定於兩週後在杭州的一場演講被突然取消。報導發表後不久，當局便公佈其被調查的消息。

[香港《明報》星期二報導](https://news.mingpao.com/p1791824909635)，這場由當地一家銀行主辦的論壇，原定於10月26日在杭州一間五星級酒店舉行，邀請黃奇帆擔任主講嘉賓。主辦方介紹黃奇帆為「復旦大學特聘教授、中國國際經濟交流中心副理事長」。

報導指出，黃奇帆所屬的這家交流中心，其理事長近期因受賄等原因被判刑。中紀委的通報並未說明黃奇帆被調查與此有否關連，但通報對其稱呼為「重慶市委原副書記、市政府原市長」。

## 從浦東到重慶：政壇「不倒翁」黃奇帆倒下了

圖像來源，Getty Images

圖像加註文字，黃奇帆（右）到重慶後在薄熙來（左）之下工作，在薄熙來因醜聞「落馬」後安然無恙。

黃奇帆祖籍浙江諸暨，1952年5月生。

黃奇帆的官場經歷頗為傳奇。[暫時仍可閱讀的官方媒體簡歷顯示](https://cpc.people.com.cn/BIG5/64162/123659/123804/7330846.html)，他在文化大革命爆發後的1968年，進入上海焦化廠擔任焦爐車間工人，一直升任至工程師。

他是在文革這段時間經推薦，以工農兵學員身份上了大學。官方履歷稱，黃奇帆擁有工商管理碩士學位，以及研究員資格。

黃奇帆日後在官場上卻展現出高超的財技，更歷經薄熙來、孫政才兩任重慶市委書記先後落馬，卻長期未受波及。

圖像來源，Reuters

圖像加註文字，1980年代後期的上海浦東，今天的摩天高樓全未興建。朱鎔基1990年任命黃奇帆領導浦東的開發工作。

黃奇帆的仕途，可以概括為上海和重慶兩個篇章。

改革開放實施後的1983，他進入上海市體制，開始從事經濟相關工作。

1990年4月22日，黃奇帆接到中共上海市委組織部通知：由[朱鎔基](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/cp839rnw40po/trad)提名，市委常委會審議通過，任命他到浦東開發辦擔任副主任，第二天就去報到。這是他事後的回憶，他本人在不同場合對日期的說法略有出入，有時也說是4月21日。

黃奇帆是朱鎔基開發浦東新區早期最重要的幕僚。1990年的浦東新區一無所有，只有政策，資金有限。黃奇帆籌建了外高橋、金橋、陸家嘴三家國有開發公司，政府把連片土地劃撥給這三家公司，土地折算成資本金後進行股權融資，再把融到的資金存入銀行，換取數倍的貸款。

這種做法，讓最初注入三家公司的不到1億元人民幣資金，膨脹到數十億元的規模。浦東開發才剛起步，就憑這套辦法取得了在當年看來不可思議的啟動資金。

1990年代中期，黃奇帆進一步主掌整個上海的國有企業改革。在上海的國企改革中，他對資產進行打包重組，並借助金融手段，讓上海眾多國有企業度過危機，形成幾個大型國企集團。

這使得，浦東開發與國企改革，朱鎔基時代兩項極為重要的經濟改革，他都參與其中。

這些經歷，讓黃奇帆在中國改革開放初期那個規則模糊和經驗不足的年代，屢屢創造出令人眼前一亮的成績。

圖像來源，Reuters

圖像加註文字，1998年的浦東，陸家嘴金融區此刻已具備相當規模。

2001年，他調任重慶，擔任副市長。當時中國地方政府仍在摸索運作模式，尤其在分稅制改革之後，地方政府的創收能力大幅下降。

剛到重慶的黃奇帆，先透過市政府旗下的城投公司改造爛尾樓項目，又接手有爭議的BOT大橋（民間以建設—經營—轉讓模式興建大橋）等項目，讓城投公司不斷壯大，也盤活了城裡一些爛尾項目。

接著，他以城投公司為平台，把政府資產注入其中，擴大城投公司的固定資產規模，以此向各大銀行高額舉債，使重慶市政府的可支配資金大幅攀升。他因此被稱為「重慶財神」。

此後，黃奇帆在重慶繼續擴大這套模式，組建了八大投資集團，全部隸屬市政府，為重慶市的建設帶來了大量的資金。這套城投債模式，逐步在中國各地方，遍地開花。

圖像來源，Reuters

圖像加註文字，薄熙來治下，他主力「唱紅打黑」，黃奇帆負責提振重慶經濟。

2009年底，[薄熙來](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/china/2013/07/130725_boxilai_profile)出任中共市委書記，主政重慶，與當時的市長王鴻舉矛盾尖銳，王鴻舉最後主動辭職下台，黃奇帆順利坐上市長的位置。黃奇帆曾形容與薄熙來的搭檔「如魚得水」。

黃奇帆繼續發揮他盤活地方資源的本事，薄熙來則專注於[「唱紅打黑」](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/china/2010/03/100306_npc_shirong_diary3)，兩人搭檔，形成了所謂的「重慶模式」。

但這一模式的神話，在重慶市公安局長王立軍2012年2月駕車駛入美國駐成都總領事館的那一刻，戛然而止。

當時中國輿論場對這起事件諱莫如深，海外和香港媒體卻流傳一種說法：薄熙來沒有第一時間親自出面，而是派黃奇帆市長率領70輛警車連夜趕赴成都要人。這一說法未經證實，黃奇帆本人公開否認。

[黃奇帆後來在接受鳳凰網採訪時說](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese_news/2012/03/120306_huang_interview_wanglijun)：「就你們說我帶了70輛警車去，那是子虛烏有、胡說八道！我是一輛車帶了我的一個秘書長去的。結果別人說有那麼多警車，那上面的牌照是川警，是四川的！」

圖像來源，Reuters

圖像加註文字，2015年11月，時任法國總統奧朗德（中）訪華，黃奇帆（左）接待其參訪重慶。

薄熙來去職後，副國級的[張德江](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese_news/2012/06/120622_chongqing_zhangdejiang_boxilai)在重慶過渡了八個月。官方的說法是，張德江在特殊時期領導重慶，穩定了大局；外界則普遍認為，他的任務之一是清理薄熙來的影響。黃奇帆在這場風波中留任，並在2012年11月張德江離任的大會上兩度落淚。

接著，年輕的孫政才接任重慶市委書記。孫政才當時被外界廣泛視為習近平之後的最高接班人人選，前途看漲，但2017年7月，中央將他調離重慶，並由中央紀委對他立案審查，[他其後被判處無期徒刑](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese-news-44035920)。

孫政才在重慶任職期間，黃奇帆與他共事約四年，依然未受波及。[黃奇帆2016年12月卸任市長](https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/chinese-news-38465447)，2017年任全國人大財經委員會副主任委員；2017年中共十九大後，他不再是中央委員。2018年卸任全國人大職務，至此退出政壇。

圖像來源，Reuters

圖像加註文字，直到被調查前，黃奇帆仍活躍於財金界活動上。

退休後，他轉以學者身分活動，成為中國各類經濟論壇的常客，也會在重要政策發布的時點撰文表態，成為經濟界一把極為響亮的聲音。

長期以來，黃奇帆被中國輿論視為重慶政壇的「不倒翁」。先後與薄熙來、孫政才這兩位極具爭議性的直屬上級搭檔，兩人相繼出事，他卻在薄案、孫案的風暴中都未受波及。退休之後，他反而在各類論壇上高調宣傳自己的經濟主張，獲得越來越多關注。

他當年引以為傲的城投公司和地方債模式，如今在中國受到反思與檢視。他留下的龐大地方債務，以及房地產模式退潮後的地方治理難題，在潮水退去之後逐漸浮現。

而他在政壇「不倒翁」的形象，卻在退休九年後，被立案調查，倒在了無人想得到之時。

title: Joburg pensioner wins billing dispute after seven-year battle
summary: For the first time in years, Johannesburg pensioner Umesh Daya can open his municipal bill without confronting a debt of hundreds of thousands of rands – and, he says, without the overwhelming, constant fear of disconnection that accompanie
content:
For the first time in years, Johannesburg pensioner Umesh Daya can open his municipal bill without confronting a debt of hundreds of thousands of rands – and, he says, without the overwhelming, constant fear of disconnection that accompanied it.

His seven-year billing dispute has involved repeated complaints, an appeal to the Johannesburg Ombudsman and, eventually, a desperate plea to Daily Maverick for help.

Daya says the mounting charges and repeated threats of disconnection caused enormous stress, affected his health and disrupted his employment. He says he repeatedly had to leave work and rush to his Crosby home when told officials had arrived to disconnect his services.

Now, his October 2026 municipal statement records an outstanding balance of R5,418, compared with a previous balance of R442,908. It lists sundry credits totalling R437,424.

Daya is relieved, although he continues to dispute the remaining amount.

The dramatic reduction follows questions from Daily Maverick to the City and City Power about the account.

City Power announced an “urgent investigation” and said appropriate account adjustments would be determined once it was completed.

### A confused account

According to City Power, electricity billing on Daya’s account began in May 2019 and was backdated by three years.

The City raised R276,244 in retrospective charges – R238,131 for electricity and R38,113 for water.

City Power told Daily Maverick that although Daya had bought his property in 1996, it was unclear why his water and electricity services remained linked to the previous owner’s account.

The retrospective electricity billing was based on estimated readings from a meter that was later removed. City Power acknowledged that the job card did not contain the meter reading at removal.

Daya also says a City Power official told him a meter installed at his home was stolen and belonged to another customer.

Correspondence from the Ombudsman records his allegation that, in April 2021, his conventional meter was damaged by a spark. When technicians investigated, he said, they told him it belonged to another address and advised him to apply for another meter.

The correspondence records the allegation that the meter belonged elsewhere; it does not establish that it was stolen.

But City Power’s subsequent analysis identified another apparent discrepancy: a customer number linked to Daya had been used to buy prepaid electricity since 2013.

“This suggests that the customer should not have been billed on a postpaid basis for electricity during the period 2019 to 2022, as electricity was being purchased through the prepaid meter,” City Power said.

### The Ombudsman intervenes

The Johannesburg Ombudsman took up Daya’s complaint in 2023, asking City Power to explain why he was being billed for conventional electricity while buying prepaid power, and when his electricity supply would be restored. The office requested a comprehensive response, but more than three years later, despite further meetings, the dispute remained unresolved.

In its September response to Daily Maverick, City Power said several reconciliation meetings had been held with Daya and the Ombudsman, but his account could not yet be confirmed as fully corrected.

### ‘You are my only hope’

By the time Daya approached Daily Maverick, he was desperate.

“I am exhausted, frustrated and completely overwhelmed by this situation. I have tried every avenue available to me, yet I am still no closer to a resolution.”

He pleaded for help: “You are my only hope now.”

Daya said the years-long dispute had devastated him financially.

“I have lost almost everything financially as a result of this ongoing ordeal. I don’t even know whether I will ever be able to recover all the money I have unnecessarily spent trying to resolve this matter with CoJ officials.”

He described the toll of the mounting debt: “It caused enormous stress every single month, opening these growing bills and worrying I would lose my house.”

Crosby resident Umesh Daya has been financially impacted by the City of Joburg’s inflated and inaccurate electricity bills. (Photo: Reitumetse Pilane)

### Threats and disconnections

Daya says he faced more than 80 threats of disconnection over the years and that his water and electricity were disconnected on several occasions. He also alleges that, on several occasions, people linked to the City offered to make his debt disappear in return for bribes.

“I was asked for a bribe many times to write the debt off, but I consistently refused,” he said.

City Power said its records showed two electricity disconnections, both in 2022, and none recorded between 2023 and 2026.

It did not say whether Daya’s specific bribery allegations had been investigated, but said customers were never required to pay employees or contractors to correct accounts or restore services, and urged them to report suspected corruption.

### Relief, with questions remaining

The October statement contains credits and adjustments across electricity, water, refuse and other categories.

These include a R243,424 City Power debt rehabilitation credit, a R73,195 water credit, and further credits and write-offs.

The description “debt rehabilitation” does not establish how much of the reduction represents the reversal of incorrect billing and how much reflects debt relief.

The statement now records prepaid electricity and no current electricity charge.

Daya still wants the remaining R5,418 investigated and removed if it relates to the disputed billing.

Although that dispute continues, the man who only weeks ago said he had exhausted every avenue available to him says the reduction has brought enormous relief.

“I am very thankful to Daily Maverick for intervening and getting this finally sorted out,” he said.

For Daya, however, reducing the figures on a municipal statement cannot restore what he says the seven-year battle has already cost him. **DM**

title: SA heads to COP17 with a practical plan to halt biodiversity loss
summary: With 2030 less than four years away, the sustainability target year marks the deadline for South Africa and other countries to fulfil 23 global targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss. The targets are outlined in the Kunming-Montreal
content:
With 2030 less than four years away, the sustainability target year marks the deadline for South Africa and other countries to fulfil 23 global targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss.

The targets are outlined in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), a landmark international agreement adopted in 2022 at the 15th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15).

The draft [Global Report on Collective Progress in the Implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework](https://www.cbd.int/globalreview) released in July has already painted a dire picture of the progress made towards implementing the GBF.

The draft report found that signatory countries are wildly off track to meet the 2030 deadline, with significant progress being made in only one of the 23 targets that were agreed on four years ago.

The UN report ultimately concluded that the global goal to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030 would not be achieved unless action by countries “accelerated rapidly”.

With the next instalment of the biodiversity COP starting on Monday, 19 October, and in light of the not-so-rosy picture painted by the progress report, South Africa said it was heading to COP17 with the goal of practical implementation in mind, not just reporting on progress.

“COP17 cannot be another conference that diagnoses the biodiversity crisis without equipping countries to act,” Deputy Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment Narend Singh said at a department briefing on Monday, 12 October, on the negotiating position South Africa would take at the biodiversity talks.

Singh will lead the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment’s (DFFE’s) COP17 negotiating team.

Deputy Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment Narend Singh delivers the keynote address at the International Day for Biological Diversity 2026 Global Flagship Event in Boksburg on 22 May, 2026. (Photo: Gallo Images / OJ Koloti)

He said that for COP17 to be productive, participating countries would have to agree on how to close the gap between global commitments and implementation.

“South Africa will call for a fair implementation package that matches global ambition with finance, technology and capacity, while ensuring that the benefits derived from our genetic resources are shared equitably,” Singh said.

### **State of SA biodiversity**

Even though South Africa is megadiverse, being among the top 10 countries for species richness, biodiversity loss remains a top concern for the nation.

During the briefing, the DFFE made a presentation on the country’s state of biodiversity, based on the South African National Biodiversity Institute’s (Sanbi’s) latest assessment.

The Olifantsfontein wetland next to Prime View Adventure & Leisure on 16 December 2025, where natural spring systems remain largely intact. (Photo: Gallo Images / Alet Pretorius)

According to the 2025 report, 986 ecosystem types assessed were under threat.

The report found that:

*   More than half of all assessed species are of concern, with the most fragile being freshwater and cartilaginous species.

*   Estuaries, rivers and wetlands are the most threatened and least protected, a critical concern for a water-scarce country.

*   Both ecosystem (terrestrial biomes) and species (species groups) Red List Indexes show declining trends, indicating increasing threat levels.

*   Climate change, unsustainable land use, pollution and invasive alien species were identified as major impacts.

Despite these challenges, Singh said that the DFFE would be finalising the revised National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) for 2026 to 2035 to help guide the country in effectively implementing the targets set in the Global Biodiversity Framework.

South Africa has developed its NBSAP by grouping the Kunming-Montreal targets into 12 thematic areas. This integrated, systems-based approach recognises the interconnectedness of biodiversity issues and aims for maximum benefits and impacts. However, to fully operationalise the NBSAP, Singh said South Africa and many other developing nations required support from the convention, which they would call for at COP.

Pincushion Protea (Leucospermum cordifolium) on 1 November 2020 in Overberg, Western Cape. Pincushion Protea grows in the Cape Floristic Region and has long-lasting flower heads with distinctive yellow, orange or red protruding spikes that make it a favourite for the cut flower industry. (Photo: Gallo Images / Jacques Stander)

### **What is SA negotiating for**

Singh emphasised that financial commitments had to translate into resources that developing countries could actually access and use, as “finance announced on paper is not the same as finance available for implementation”.

The GBF’s resource mobilisation target calls for at least $200-billion (R3.3-billion) a year for biodiversity from all sources by 2030. It also sets targets for international biodiversity finance to developing countries of at least $20-billion a year by 2025 and $30-billion a year by 2030.

As such, South Africa will advocate for biodiversity finance that is adequate, predictable, accessible and non-debt-creating, in line with developed countries’ obligations under Article 20 of the convention.

“Developing countries, we believe, should not be pushed further into debt to protect biodiversity that provides benefits well beyond their borders,” Singh said.

Responding to questions from Daily Maverick about challenges in implementing the GBF’s targets, the DFFE said that, as a megadiverse nation, SA noted that the goals and targets of the GBF were global in nature and, as such, each party contributed to attaining them in accordance with national circumstances, priorities and capabilities.

The department added that all the types of means of implementation, finance, capacity-building, technical and scientific cooperation, and technology transfer, had increased since the adoption of the GBF. However, they had not kept pace with the requirements to meet the targets.

“For SA, ambition cannot be considered in isolation from means of implementation. Ambition must be accompanied by commensurate, predictable, accessible and timely support for developing countries, including financial resources, capacity-building and development, technology transfer, technical and scientific cooperation and knowledge-sharing,” the department said.

South Africa’s message is straightforward: a global biodiversity deal cannot be considered realistic if the countries holding much of the world’s biodiversity lack the support to implement it. **DM**

title: Ten years of impunity that broke the West
summary: Two anniversaries confront us. The first is the 10th anniversary of November 2016, when Donald Trump’s first election – along with the Brexit referendum a few months earlier – marked a decisive rupture in the post-Cold War world order. The
content:
Two anniversaries confront us. The first is the 10th anniversary of November 2016, when Donald Trump’s first election – along with the Brexit referendum a few months earlier – marked a decisive rupture in the post-Cold War world order.

The second, which passed last week, was 7 October 2023. That date not only demonstrated humanity’s enduring capacity for barbarism, but something arguably more disturbing: Israel’s response to Hamas’ massacre has laid bare just how profoundly the supposedly “civilised” world order has broken down.

When historians look back on this post-Cold War period, they are likely to reflect that there were several discrete periods. The first was from 1989 and the fall of the Berlin Wall until the accession of China to the WTO.

This was a kind of neoliberal spring; the triumphant age of globalisation, liberal democracy and Francis Fukuyama’s End of History. The genocides and wars in Central Africa and the Balkans were inconvenient reminders that history had, indeed, not got the memorandum.

History returned with China’s emergence as the world’s manufacturing powerhouse and, increasingly, its creditor. An unsustainable economic imbalance emerged as Chinese savings financed Western consumption, particularly in America.

### Exotic debt instruments

The resulting capital glut was recycled through increasingly exotic instruments and into ever more dubious mortgages. It all collapsed with the fall of Lehman Brothers in 2008.

The response was, in hindsight, catastrophically short-sighted. Banks that had mispriced this risk and created the crisis were rescued, while the liabilities were shifted to taxpayers. Governments socialised the losses of capitalism while leaving the profits untouched.

In the US and in Britain, the consequence was years of economic insecurity, stagnant real wages and austerity. In Europe, the fiscal straitjacket of the Eurozone transformed a financial crisis into a sovereign debt crisis. Citizens were forced to bear the brunt of excesses they had neither been responsible for nor profited from.

Something had to give.

All exploded in 2016 when electorates spectacularly announced their disenchantment with the status quo, by voting for Brexit and then Donald Trump. This marked the end of the neoliberal honeymoon and the beginning of what might have been termed by historian Eric Hobsbawm as “the Age of Populism”.

The message was clear; voters in some of the world’s wealthiest democracies no longer cared about the rest of the world, and certainly not about exporting their much vaunted “universal values”. Increasingly they even seemed uninterested in protecting those values at home.

What mattered was protecting their own diminishing prosperity. If that required dismantling the institutions that had underpinned decades of stability and growth, then so be it.

### The enemy

The enemy was simultaneously the foreigner supposedly coming to steal one’s livelihood and the venal metropolitan “liberal” elite. The contradictions were irrelevant. Populism never requires intellectual coherence, only enemies.

This was relatively harmless until 2023. The tectonic fissure on which it was to shatter was inevitable. It was always going to be the fault line between Israel and Palestine; the very creation of the state of Israel was a consequence of the original sin of modern European civilisation.

The country simply would not exist had it not been for a genocide perpetrated in the heart of Europe. It is the crucible of Western guilt.

So bad for the unlucky Palestinians who were the eventual losers in this convenient expungement of collective remorse. And, after decades of occupation, dispossession and crimes against humanity, three years ago Hamas moved (with the Israeli’s prime minister being [forewarned](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/09/middleeast/avi-gil-benjamin-netanyahu-aide-october-7-intl)). And what a cataclysmic eruption it was.

How would Israel, the ultimate manifestation of postwar Western guilt and violence, react? If this had happened 30 years earlier, in the warm afterglow of the fall of the Berlin Wall and Nelson Mandela, it might have been very different.

### **The golden age**

Instead, we had entered the “f**k you” world, the Age of Impunity. Values, morals - such outdated concepts as consequences - were no longer relevant. Instead, the furious reaction was simple; all your eyes, all your teeth, all your children. As was repeatedly told to the world by Israeli politicians: no one is [innocent](https://www.yahoo.com/news/israeli-president-says-no-innocent-154330724.html) in Gaza. We are fighting human [animals](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/defense-minister-announces-complete-siege-of-gaza-no-power-food-or-fuel/).

Of course, the end effect was all too predictable. Yet another genocide, as so brilliantly and consummately shown by the now Nobel laureate Navi Pillay, of whom all South Africans should be so proud (despite what some former writers in this publication might [argue](https://www.timcohen.co.za/loose-canon-pillays-nobel-peace-prize-a-respectful-critique/?ref=tim-cohens-loose-canon-newsletter)).

The global order, which had been tested during the Cold War but held, and which had declined over the past 30 years but survived – had now officially collapsed. Geopolitically, the populists had savaged whatever was left of the multilateral system. Economically it was being disassembled piecemeal by a combination of desperate American protectionism, the tech robber barons with their [technofeudalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technofeudalism) empires, and the Chinese export machine that had torn the heart out of western manufacturing.

The irony is exquisite. Western politicians who promised national sovereignty are presiding over the ultimate vassalage of these countries to big tech, China and a US which has so departed from its so-called moral high ground it is now in the de facto Middle Ages, threatening to livestream executions.

### Two-speed economy

As to the economic effects, this is now becoming apparent. We increasingly inhabit a two-speed economy; there is big tech/AI, and then everyone else. Global equity markets are at all-time highs, but much of their performance is concentrated in half a dozen tech companies; stripping out the effects of AI, Bloomberg data show global stocks down almost 7% since August.

Sans AI-driven exuberance, the picture of corporate profitability, household purchasing power and economic dynamism is far less impressive.

Sovereign borrowing costs are rising as the debt-fuelled economies of the West start to exhaust their creditors; the generosity of Chinese and Japanese savers is no longer enough. As for the final straw? The Middle East, once again. The conflagration unleashed by 7 October, resulting in a rogue Israel starting forever wars and pulling the US into direct conflict with Iran, has now pushed energy prices to unsustainable levels. Ten years on from the beginning of the Age of Populism the entire economic system is poised to crack.

The global financial crisis destroyed confidence in the neoliberal economic order. Populism destroyed confidence in the political order. And Gaza has eviscerated any belief or confidence in a moral order.

The terrorists who stormed southern Israel three years ago understood this better than most. This was how to push the entire Western edifice over the edge.

Wherever they are now, they may yet have the last laugh. **DM**

title: Zimbabwe: Bikita Minerals Turns to Processing in U.S.$1bn Expansion Push
summary: Bikita Minerals is stepping up efforts to turn the country's lithium resources into higher-value products with planned investments expected to exceed US$1 billion by 2027 as the country seeks to build a domestic mineral processing industry.
content:
Bikita Minerals is stepping up efforts to turn the country's lithium resources into higher-value products with planned investments expected to exceed US$1 billion by 2027 as the country seeks to build a domestic mineral processing industry.

The expansion, led by Chinese-owned Sinomine, is expected to increase processing capacity, support industrial development and reduce reliance on exports of raw and semi-processed minerals.

Bikita Minerals assistant general manager Thomas Mufumi said the company had already invested more than US$380 million in completed beneficiation projects with further capital expenditure expected to take total investment beyond the US$1 billion mark.

"We have invested more than US$380 million in beneficiation projects, and by 2027, our total investment is expected to exceed US$1 billion," Mufumi said.

A major component of the expansion is a US$400 million lithium sulphate plant scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2027.

The facility is expected to produce 100 000 metric tonnes annually, strengthening the mine's capacity to process lithium into products used in downstream industries.

The company is also increasing the capacity of one of its spodumene processing circuits from two million tonnes to 3.3 million tonnes of ore a year while investing further in tantalum extraction.

The projects come as Zimbabwe seeks to retain a greater share of the economic benefits generated by its mineral resources through local processing, technology transfer and industrial development.

Minerals Marketing Corporation of Zimbabwe (MMCZ) general manager Dr. Nomusa Jane Moyo said the investment demonstrated how beneficiation could help transform mining from a predominantly extractive industry into a broader driver of economic growth.

"This is not only about producing minerals; it is about increasing mineral revenue, creating employment, and transferring technology into Zimbabwe. Every step towards beneficiation means more value is retained in the country," Dr. Moyo said

She said expanded processing capacity could stimulate economic activity beyond mining operations by creating opportunities for local suppliers, developing technical skills and supporting infrastructure investment.

However, the scale of the planned investment comes amid uncertainty in the global lithium market, with fluctuating prices and unpredictable demand putting pressure on producers.

Mufumi said the industry faced significant working capital requirements and called on the government to review taxes and allowable deductions affecting lithium producers.

"Lithium prices are volatile, demand is uncertain, and the working capital requirements are significant. A review of the tax obligations and deductions affecting the industry would help producers sustain operations and continue investing," he said

The appeal highlights the challenge facing Zimbabwe as it seeks to attract long-term investment in mineral processing while ensuring that mining companies remain financially sustainable during periods of weaker commodity prices.

Bikita Minerals employs about 1 400 people directly with the workforce exceeding 2 000 when contractors are included, according to Mufumi.

The company also supports community development programmes covering rural electrification, schools, clinics and road construction.

Moyo said investment in beneficiation could deliver wider economic benefits if it was accompanied by local supplier development, employment creation and the transfer of technical expertise.

"Bikita Minerals is showing what is possible when investment is linked to value addition. The opportunity is to ensure that Zimbabwe does not simply export its minerals but builds an industry around them." she said.

With the lithium sulphate plant and other processing projects expected to expand production capacity, Bikita Minerals has become a significant test of Zimbabwe's ambition to develop a more integrated mining industry.

title: 黄奇帆落马：退休八年的 「 不倒翁 」 为何此时倒下？
summary: 2026-10-13 明豪的博客 中共中央纪委国家监委 10 月 13 日宣布，重庆前市长黄奇帆涉嫌严重违纪违法，正接受纪律审查和监察调查 。 他曾先后与薄熙来 、 孙政才两任落马的市委书记搭档而未受波及，被称为政坛 「 不倒翁 」，如今在退休约八年后被查 。 图右为 2012 年 3 月全国人大会议期间的黄奇帆 。（照片：美国之音／公有领域；插画及后制：观 View） 【 中南海秘闻 】 重庆前市长黄奇帆传出 「 被带走 」 不到两天，消息就由官方证实了 。 中共中央纪委
content: 2026-10-13  明豪的博客 中共中央纪委国家监委 10 月 13 日宣布，重庆前市长黄奇帆涉嫌严重违纪违法，正接受纪律审查和监察调查 。 他曾先后与薄熙来 、 孙政才两任落马的市委书记搭档而未受波及，被称为政坛 「 不倒翁 」，如今在退休约八年后被查 。 图右为 2012 年 3 月全国人大会议期间的黄奇帆 。（照片：美国之音／公有领域；插画及后制：观 View） 【 中南海秘闻 】 重庆前市长黄奇帆传出 「 被带走 」 不到两天，消息就由官方证实了 。 中共中央纪委国家监委网站 10 月 13 日发布通报，称重庆市委原副书记 、 市政府原市长黄奇帆 「 涉嫌严重违纪违法，目前正接受中央纪委国家监委纪律审查和监察调查 」，新华社 、 央视隨后转发 。 通报照例只有一句话，没有说明具体涉案情节 。 黄奇帆今年 74 岁，是第十八届中央委员，曾先后与薄熙来 、 孙政才两名落马的市委书记搭档而毫髮无损，被称为政坛 「 不倒翁 」。 如今他在退休约八年后落马，距离中共二十届五中全会开幕（10 月 26 日）不到两週 。 从传闻到官宣：一天之內尘埃落定 这次事件的时间线相当紧凑 。10 月 12 日晚，旅美评论人蔡慎坤在 X 平台发文说 「 政坛不倒翁黄奇帆终于倒了 」。13 日上午，香港 《 信报 》 提到，聊天群组流传一位 「 老市长 」 原定在清华大学讲课，前一天被带走，由学者临时代讲；《 明报 》 则报导寧波银行杭州分行原定 10 月 26 日举办的论坛 「 因故取消 」，黄奇帆原本是主讲嘉宾 。 財新补充说，黄奇帆原定在那场论坛发表两小时的主旨演讲 。BBC 中文指出，《 明报 》 报导发出后不久，当局就公布了调查消息 。 黄奇帆直到最近都很活跃 。 据 《 联合早报 》 与財新报导，他 9 月 8 日还在福建厦门的第八届 「 丝路海运 」 国际合作论坛上做主旨演讲；今年 1 月 28 日，他出席重庆市两会开幕式，坐在主席台第二排 。 官方通报中的线索：为何用 「 重庆 」 头衔？ 多家媒体注意到，通报没有使用他退休后的智库或人大职务，而是称他为 「 重庆市委原副书记 、 市政府原市长 」。《 联合早报 》 引述分析说，这可能表示案情和他主持重庆市政府工作期间的事务有关 。 財新统计，中共二十大以来，重庆已有郑洪 、 熊雪 、 陆克华 、 段成刚 、 江敦涛 、 胡衡华 、 罗藺和黄奇帆等八名高官落马，另有李鉞锋 、 吴存荣也曾在重庆任职 。 德国之声指出，半年多內重庆有一名现任 、 一名前任市长相继被查 。 今年 3 月被查的胡衡华是重庆直辖以来第一位落马的市长，黄奇帆是第二位 。 分析一：重庆窝案延烧，「 红顶律师 」 彭静成关键节点？ 不少分析把黄奇帆案和今年春天以来的重庆反腐连在一起看 。 据財新今年 4 月报导，重庆静昇律师事务所主任 、 全国政协委员彭静 4 月 19 日被有关部门带走，疑涉以稳定幣受贿洗钱的案件，报导形容她可能是这一轮重庆反腐风暴的关键 「 交织点 」。《 联合早报 》 注意到一个细节：黄奇帆被查的当晚，財新把这篇 4 月的旧文重新推送，放上首页 。 根据財新与 《 海外媒体 》 整理的脉络，胡衡华 3 月 20 日被查，第二天三安光电实控人林秀成被留置，林的女婿林科闯隨后也被留置；据报林科闯曾以泰达幣（USDT）向胡衡华行贿，另有一笔资金据称流向罗藺，办案人员则在彭静家中找到冷钱包 。 彭静是重庆前副市长肖祖修的女儿，她的哥哥肖陵今年 3 月也已落马 。 X 平台评论人 「 艾地声 」 指出，彭静和静昇律所的成长期，和黄奇帆在重庆主管工业 、 財政 、 金融与国资的时期高度重叠 。 黄奇帆在政府工作报告中推动普遍建立法律顾问制度，静昇律所此后广泛进入重庆政府部门 、 开发区和国企的法律服务网络，参与过惠普落地 、 国企改制等项目 。 不过艾地声也强调，目前没有可靠证据证明黄奇帆和彭静有特殊私人关係，或曾直接指定该律所承接业务 。 网上流传的两人有私生子等说法，同样未经证实 。 分析二：国经中心整顿与 「 智库生財 」 问题 另一条线索是黄奇帆担任副理事长的中国国际经济交流中心 。 前理事长毕井泉去年 5 月落马，今年 9 月一审被判 14 年，罪状包括执掌国经中心期间受贿 。 今年 1 月，国经中心的主管单位由发改委改为中国社科院，並展开整顿 。 財新今年 2 月报导，国经中心多年透过承接地方政府课题 、 提供諮询服务筹集经费，存在可能不合规的爭议，一些在中心任职的退休中管干部已退回所得费用，有的数额巨大 。BBC 指出，通报没有说明黄案和此事是否有关 。 分析三：学者观点：旧帐重算，还是牵出新案？ 台湾学者的看法有分歧 。 淡江大学两岸关係研究中心主任洪耀南对 《 联合早报 》 说，黄奇帆落马 「 不是他现在说了什么，而是过去的旧帐 」，这也是在向其他老干部释放信号：「 过去的帐，隨时可以重算 。」 政治大学东亚研究所特聘教授寇健文则认为，黄奇帆经歷过薄 、 孙两件大案，又已退休多时，早年的问题应该已经查清楚了，现在出事应该是后来的案子，而且可能牵涉其他重要官员 。 BBC 则从政策遗產的角度切入：黄奇帆在上海浦东和重庆打造的 「 土地注资 、 城投融资 」 模式后来在全国推广，被称为 「 重庆財神 」 的成名手法，如今正因地方债问题受到反思与检视 。 分析四：自媒体的政治解读：上海帮 、 丁薛祥与栗战书 海外自媒体大多从高层政治角度解读 。 蔡慎坤认为， 五中全会是 「 残酷的清党会议 」；黄奇帆作为 「 上海帮 」 资深人物，在正国级后台吴邦国去世后 「 躲不过秋后算帐 」，风暴还可能波及政治局常委丁薛祥 。《 海外媒体》 则指出，丁 、 黄两人在上海的工作交集其实不长 。 澳洲评论人蒋罔正称，黄奇帆的儿子黄然非在深圳从事金融业务，並指栗战书的女儿相关的白手套曾和黄然非的企业在上市业务上频繁合作，还牵涉前证监会主席易会满的人脉 。X 帐号 「 政经鲁社长 」 形容，黄奇帆是重庆国资和金融领域的 「 皇帝 」，说他 「 这次还是没有扛过重庆的窝案 」。 评论人林保华则认为，黄的最大后台是江泽民 。 前 《 文匯报 》 记者姜维平早在 2016 年就曾在自由亚洲电台撰文，指黄的儿子在重庆国企进口铁矿石等业务中担任中间商 。 时评人邓聿文的看法比较保留：当前反腐不只看贪腐，也看是否 「 结党营私 」，而黄奇帆和党內开明派往来密切 。 以上说法都出自评论人或匿名爆料，没有提出可以查证的证据，官方通报也没有提及任何其他高层 。 为何是现在？ 综合各方报导，黄奇帆在这个时间点被查，可能和以下几条线索有关：第一，胡衡华 、 罗藺 、 彭静一路延伸的重庆窝案；第二，国经中心整顿和毕井泉案宣判后的后续清理；第三，《 海外媒体》 等媒体今年以来观察到的反腐趋势，即退休官员成为被查的 「 高危群体 」。 至于选在五中全会前官宣，是要震慑政坛，还是只是办案进度的巧合，目前没有定论 。 黄奇帆早已不是中央委员，不在全会需要处理的名单上 附：

content: Time Academy  时代学园   2026年10月12日 甲午海战的起因是什么？甲午战争给中国带来怎么样的影响？ - 甲午战争研究- 抗日战争纪念网 文：许知远 原载：经济观察报 当京城的绿营兵在１８９４年秋天奉调至山海关时，人们有理由为大清帝国的未来表示忧虑。一位目击者说，人与马都很瘦小，还没走出城南就已挥汗如雨，马鞍上挂着鸦片烟枪，一些士兵手里端着鸟笼，吐出嘴里的食物喂鸟，另一些人则显得又饥又渴，眉头紧锁。 创建于１９世纪初的绿营直属于兵部，创建者希望它能够替代战斗力曾强大一时，但彼时日显衰败的八旗兵，但仅仅几十年后，它就追随了前者的脚印，不管是面对外敌还是国内的叛乱，都不堪一击。长期掌管着清国海关的赫德曾在１８６５年的一份备忘录中写道：帝国的军队只有当叛乱者撤退后才敢前进，杀几个农民谎报胜利。而杭州一位粗通文墨的居民编出了这样的打油诗：贼至兵何在？兵来贼已空。可怜兵与贼，何日得相逢！大清帝国，这个以暴力建立合法性的政权失去了力量。 没人指望绿营兵能够击败日本。当大清国与日本的冲突在１８９４年７月爆发时，人们都把希望寄托在李鸿章指挥的军队上，他们大都出身于湖南与安徽，在曾国藩与李鸿章的训练下，士兵装备了现代武器而非长矛大刀，通过对个人与宗族的尊崇，这些地方武装拥有了令帝国嫡系部队黯然失色的战斗力。而李本人一手兴建的北洋海军经过２０年的经营，按照历史学家唐德刚后来的计算，它的装备已名列世界第八位，日本则排名第十三。它的指挥官们很多在英美受训，与日本那边的对手们曾是同学。１８９１年北洋舰队访问日本时，连日本的明治天皇也为舰队的实力而赞叹。那正是一个美国军事专家马汉所说的“海权”决定国家兴衰的年代。 ２００５年２月１２日，我坐在刘公岛上看着那些被打捞上的舰队残骸。整整１１０年前的今天，北洋水师最后残存的武装力量也投降了，海军提督丁汝昌在凌晨自杀。关于那场持续了７个月的战争，历史学家已尽可能挖掘出了尽量多的细节。但仅仅重温那段屈辱能给我们带来什么？历史早已过滤掉复杂的情感，只留下了时间、地点、人物、事件与数字，如果简单地重复它们当真就如黑格尔所说：“我们从历史中所学到的惟一东西是，没有人能够从中学到任何东西。” 这场战争中充斥着太多的荒谬性。我不能假装能够理解为什么叶志超在并未战败时就匆匆悬挂起白旗；不知道１８９５年２月６日大敌当前时，“来远”与“威远”的管带邱宝仁、林颖启为何仍能从容地上岸嫖妓；为什么大清国将领最赤胆忠心的作为不过就是吞食鸦片自杀。在紫禁城内，没有人真地在乎战争的输赢，比起外敌，内部人的权力斗争才更关键。在这场战争悲剧性的高潮到来之前，那位当时最有权势的女人决定挪用海军军款修建自己的后花园——宫廷内的个人喜好远比什么国家利益要重要得多；而对于绝大部分的中国人来说，战争根本就从未爆发，只要给一些钱，老百姓就会欢天喜地给敌人带路，他们头脑中根本没有国家这一概念，“中国”是外来者来称呼我们自己，我们只知道朝代的更替…… 这些看似互不相干的片段，最终都如磁场内的磁针一样指向了同一个方向——帝国的溃败。玛雅文明为什么消失？罗马帝国为何衰落？文明与国家就像个人一样，似乎逃避不了成长与衰亡的周期命运。即使到了现在，分析家们仍无法明晰这样的复杂问题。尽管历史的绵延感如此强大、充斥的变量又如此之多，但的确在某一时刻，我们会发现几乎所有的变量都在朝向更糟糕的方向，就像传染病在大规模爆发前的临界点。甲午战争最终变成了一个庞大的帝国崩溃的临界点，它无情地证明了之前那一代中国精英的努力不过是暂时延缓了它的寿命，而之后，这个国家的精英阶层尽管做出了更富变革意义的举措，却最终证明挽救的速度早已追不上衰败的速度。而帝国最后的捍卫者们也被迫承认，日渐全球化的历史已不能给予他们足够的时间进行有步骤，但过分缓慢的改变，他们的命运不再仅仅由自己主宰，而必须与外部世界共同分享，游戏规则改变了。 甲午战争提供了一块再好不过的切片，让我们能仔细观察一个曾经强有力的组织如何退化及最终死亡。一切历史最终都是思想史，单纯的历史事件不会重演，但是人们在应对挑战与挫折时的反应，却可能遵循类似的模式。自从１９世纪中叶以来，中国人在１５０年来的努力可以概括为三方面：消除外来的侮辱，建立现代的民族国家；在全球市场上获得匹配的地位；建构一个现代社会，它包括现代政治、现代经济、现代组织与现代文化。 没人比李鸿章的个人经历更能代表中国在１９世纪遭遇的挫折和尝试摆脱挫折的努力了。在他出生的１８２３年，至少在表面上，仍没有外来者公然怀疑中国是世界上最令人敬畏的帝国。１８世纪的几次征战，使得清帝国的疆土几乎扩大了一倍，它的势力深入到了亚洲腹地。它的人口在１００年中也增加了一倍，达到三亿多，比包括俄国在内的整个欧洲还要多。在这种情况下，中国人不可能消除自我中心的优越意识，在她所知的有限世界内，几乎所有地区都是中国在某种意义上的附庸——中亚大陆是它政治上的附庸，南亚部分是它礼仪上的附庸，日本则是文化上附庸，而朝鲜几乎在所有方面都在匆忙地追随中国的脚步。帝国对于海外的探险没有兴趣，当英国在印度的作为被传到北京时，清王朝开始实行海禁，陌生的东西总令人不安，那么就宣称它根本不存在。 在很多方面，中国理应获得这种充分的自信。按照前现代的标准，中国作为一个国家的存在已至少持续了２０００年，它拥有一套不庞大却行之有效的官僚系统，伏尔泰曾对此赞叹不已。中国拥有世界上最大的国内市场与国内贸易，以家庭与宗族为中心的社会组织形式非常稳定，她是行政官僚模式的先驱，而已延续了１０００多年的科举制度实在是个伟大的发明，它为社会提供了自下而上的流动机会，使杰出人士有机会管理这个国家，教育扮演着至关重要的角色，儒家经典为整个系统提供了一套意识形态，这套系统经历过朝代更替、蛮族入侵，却从未遭遇过根本性的挑战。 是因为外来者到来，还是它自身的弱点，造成了中国在１９世纪的悲剧性命运？按照哈佛大学的历史学家约瑟夫·弗莱彻的分析，中国命运的悲剧性已蕴涵在１８世纪，欧洲人的到来只是其中之一，另两个变化具有同样重大的意义，它们就是刚才提及的领土与人口的倍增。 越来越宽阔的疆域使得中央政府的控制难度明显增加，中央极权式微；在马尔萨斯为世界的未来担忧时，中国的人口在以前所未有的速度增长，在１８世纪末达到３亿之后，继续马不停蹄地增长到１８５０年前后的４.５亿，这既说明了传统体制的成功，刺激了消费与商业世界的生长，也说明它同时带来了资源的明显紧张感，更多的读书人期待获得官职，更多的农民需要耕地，更多的人要吃饭、穿衣。当这些通道没有同步拓展时，矛盾就开始积郁了，而无论是太平天国的领导人洪秀全，还是改革者康有为与孙中山，都是在传统的晋升之路被封死之后才去寻找新方向的。 在１８９５年前，帝国的大部分精英对自己的信心似乎仍未彻底崩溃。在一个像李鸿章这样的官员的成长过程中，他会目睹一连串帝国在外来者面前受到的屈辱：１８４０—１８４２年的鸦片战争；１８５７—１８６０年的第二次鸦片战争；１８７１年俄国侵占伊犁；１８７４年日本夺取琉球；１８８３年—１８８５年的中法战争，几乎每隔十年战事就会爆发。而帝国的基础在１８５０年代就曾显得脆弱不堪，欧洲的外来者不费多大气力就能够瓦解从沿海港口到北京的清军防线，一些最富洞察力的头脑很快就发现，他们是中华帝国几千年历史上未曾遭遇过的强力；而一支用变形的基督教统一了思想的太平军则占领了最富庶的长江流域，那里是帝国财政与粮食的供给中心。 但接下来却并非是帝国的崩溃，１８６０之后的３０年是中国社会一个复兴的时期，远非今日我们想当然的黑暗岁月。一代新的政治人物已经崛起，在中央他们以恭亲王与文详为代表，能用更熟练的技巧处理对外关系；在地方他们以曾国藩、左宗棠、李鸿章、胡林翼为代表，成功地镇压了太平天国等一系列的反叛。他们正直、勤奋、自我克制，重新树立了道德的榜样，他们大力挖掘人才，为官僚系统注入了生机；在外交上，总理衙门的引入让中国在处理对外事务上逐渐专业化，并赢得了某种尊敬；在军事上，更多的现代装备被引入湘军、淮军，包括机枪与克虏伯大炮；在１８６０年代，随着各路义军的逐个消亡，农业生产逐渐恢复，新开垦的土地带动了新的移民；洋务运动的倡导者开始着手建立现代工业，甚至中国商人在沿海贸易方面也开始赶上外国商人；新思想也开始被引入，更多的翻译作品受到了手握政权的地方改革者的重视；被腐败与战乱所摧毁的地方行政系统重新运行起来，士绅再一次发挥起作用；教授传统儒学的学校大批兴建，继续为帝国提供稳定的思想教育……在面对中国社会的老问题上，改革派们的成效卓著。比如，左宗棠完成了新疆的平叛，让帝国的光芒在西北地区重新闪耀；山东的丁宝祯治理了黄河及大运河的水患，加强了地方团练，改革了盐政；李鸿章则建立了还算现代化的军队，创造了江南制造局。一位驻中国的外交官在１８７２年写道，中国正在迅速地成为一个令人生畏的对手；整个官僚阶级都决心恢复中国的国际地位；兵工厂和造船厂的产量给人以深刻的印象；中国建造的军舰不久就将达到欧洲的最高水平…… 自１８６０年代开始的，被历史学家称之为“同治中兴”的改革，在很多方面，就像是日本人差不多同时开始的明治维新一样，似乎标志着一个古老文明面对现代挑战的应变。中国和日本同为专制政体，改革同样由精英阶层自上而下地推动，而在才智上，李鸿章一代也绝不逊色于伊滕博文一代。一直到１８９４年中日正式交战前，这两个国家谁的成功更显著，似乎仍未有定论，一位观察者在１８７０年代分别了考察了中国与日本之后，很确定地说，中国的前景更值得期待。但这两场变革的显著区别是，当面临挑战时，中国首先选择的是从历史中求诸答案，变革者们最主要的期待是恢复一个他们幻想中的朴实和稳定的农业社会。 在中国一代又一代人眼中，黄金时代总是存在于那个已经逝去的年代，他们采用的各种手段，不管是来自西方还是自身，都是为了保持原有的社会结构，原有的政治体制和原有的思维模式。所有近代化的努力，都像附着在内脏已经腐烂的身体上的光鲜皮毛，在任何一个考验面前，这种分离都如此明显，对于中国政治系统的官员来说，中日战场上的输赢，其重要性远比宫廷政治要小得多。改革虽然暂时扭转了内部传统部门的颓势，但不过是加固了那些本应被改变的体制，它使一个王朝延续了更多的时间，却没有向现代国家方向演变。向它所期待的康干盛世一样，王朝或许可以击败来自内部的叛乱和来自中亚腹地的挑衅，却对来自海洋那边的挑战无力抗拒。 当马关条约签署的消息传到北京后，对于那些受过教育的公众来说，它的刺激比之前所有对外战争的失败都要大，过去被他们看不起的学生日本，在仅仅一代人之后，就无情地击败了自己的老师。这一事件几乎彻底冲垮了中国人最后的信念上的优越感，而对于老一代官僚来说，他们终其一生的努力最终被证明不堪一击，伴随着他们相继退出历史舞台，官僚系统再次迅速地回落到无能、腐败、道德崩溃的地步，从地方开始的振兴活动，也促成了地方与中央的分离，并为后来的军阀时代的到来奠定了基础。甲午之战的惨败激发起了一场新的运动，以康有为、梁启超为代表的新型知识分子，希望能在政治体制、社会体制本身上进行一场变革。但很快，这群意气风发的年轻人发现，变革难度比他们想象的要大得多，他们需要得到来自最高权力的支持，他们在面对传统的官僚体制时需要更多的技巧，他们还发现广大人民需要被唤醒，因为他们对于自己生活的国家与世界茫然无知、麻木不仁。这些变革者甚至意识到，他们还要创造一个“中国”的概念，然后去拯救这个被创造出来的概念。然而他们或许不知道的是，一个他们心目中的现代政体需要一个全国性的经济环境与社会组织的支持。历史课本早已将１９世纪的中国描绘成半殖民地社会，但事实上，来自外部世界的改变仍旧很少，中国与外界最活跃的纺织贸易只影响到通商口岸的一小部分人，９７% 以上的中国人仍在穿着土布织的衣服，农业与手工业在经济中占据着绝对的主题；现代国家应该拥有的公共系统只露出很少的迹象，更何谈现代交通运输、通信和教育系统；现代意识更是少得可怜，那些北京的改革者们的声音最多能被几万名同道听懂，对于广阔的乡村世界来说，生活仍如几十年前一样，暗淡、迟钝地进行着，鸦片是对抗这种沉闷的最好方式…… 中国的历史太悠久了，幅员太辽阔了，它总能寻找到回避根本的变革的方式。当美国的“黑船”来到日本时，这个国家无处可躲，只能正面迎接变化；而在中国，即使八国联军攻占了北京，慈禧太后仍可以相对从容地逃到陕西。帝国的惰性总是不自觉地拒绝变革，而变革发生后，它传播的速度又过分缓慢。日本的历史学家屋太一发现，一个组织患有绝症的原因有三个：一，功能体的共同体化，功能体是为了达到组织的外在目标，共同体是为了满足成员自己的需求，晚清中国社会内部的不同利益集团，全部以追求自己狭隘的利益为出发点，而忘记整个组织的外在目标；二，对环境的过度适应；三，沉醉于成功的体验。超过２０００年的相对一致的历史，使得中国人极度适应了自己的生存环境，即使当一些新挑战到来时，他们也仍重复性地使用曾经有成效的老办法，比如“同治中兴”。 但所有的努力最终都没有收到渴望的成效，百日维新是一个无所不包的“休克疗法”，没有得到足够长的时间与足够强的权力支持。虽然在义和团运动之后１０年，清政府几乎采纳了百日维新的所有主张，但此刻，这个组织自我挽救的速度已落后于它腐烂的速度，而且它最终发现自己已无力面对层出不穷的危机。而且在２０世纪初，中国已不具备日本明治维新时期相对不受打扰的改革条件。更为彻底的国际竞争已经展开，国际环境的压力对于中国的压力更为显著，中国固有的政治、经济、文化与一个崭新的世界潮流的分歧越来越不可调和，不同背景、思维与利益的群体间越来越难以相处。越来越多的人相信，只有一场彻底的革命才能挽救她，而这场革命必须从一切方面洗刷旧传统……

By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- The Hanwha Eagles announced Tuesday they have re-signed their Taiwanese pitcher Wang Yan-Cheng for next year.

The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) club said Wang has agreed to a new one-year deal worth US$200,000 and that the left-hander also received a $100,000 signing bonus.

Wang was the Eagles' Asian quota player this year and served as a pillar in a rotation decimated by injuries and subpar performances, all the while making $100,000.

The 25-year-old went 11-6 with a 3.97 ERA in 133 2/3 innings while striking out 100. He was the only Hanwha pitcher to win more than 10 games. Wang finished second on the team in innings and strikeouts, both behind former major league pitcher Ryu Hyun-jin.

"I am happy to be back with the Hanwha Eagles for next season. I would like to thank the club for trusting in my potential and giving me another opportunity," Wang said. "I will try to address my shortcomings and keep getting better and better."

The Eagles reached the Korean Series last year but finished ninth in the 10-team league this year. They also ranked near the bottom in major pitching categories, such as ERA and strikeouts.

summary: 内容摘要：人工智能 (AI) 的经济后果在中华人民共和国 (PRC) 可能尤其明显，因为在一个已经出现过多供给冲击和负需求冲击的经济体中，人工智能 (AI) 将带来重大的正供给冲击和负需求冲击。 “十五五”规划将人工智能置于“现代工业生态系统”的核心地位，包括各种制造、技术、基础设施和对全球供应链的控制。为中国经济的工业方面提供动力的政策本身正在加剧结构性弱点和缺陷
content:
内容摘要：人工智能 (AI) 的经济后果在中华人民共和国 (PRC) 可能尤其明显，因为在一个已经出现过多供给冲击和负需求冲击的经济体中，人工智能 (AI) 将带来重大的正供给冲击和负需求冲击。 “十五五”规划将人工智能置于“现代工业生态系统”的核心地位，包括各种制造、技术、基础设施和对全球供应链的控制。为中国经济工业方面提供动力的政策正在加剧中国大部分经济领域的结构性弱点和缺陷，其中过度债务、低生产率、高失业率以及财政和金融失败正变得更加根深蒂固。习近平总书记和唐纳德·特朗普总统在 9 月份于华盛顿特区举行的峰会上讨论了人工智能 (AI)。中华人民共和国 (PRC) 和美国之间的观点分歧使得人们很难准确地看出这两个超级大国如何在人工智能安全和监管议程上成功合作。习近平尤其需要更多地关注人工智能相关的治理和经济问题，这些问题可能会加剧中国国内经济的结构性问题。政府已经明确表示人工智能可能对政治和社会安全构成风险。
中国国家安全部部长陈一新最近首次就此话题发出警告，习近平本人在7月上海世界人工智能大会开幕致辞中也谈到了人工智能治理（新华社，7月18日；南华早报，9月14日；中国简报，9月18日）。与此同时，人工智能的经济后果日益凸显。值得注意的是，多位中国经济学家在上海举行的2026外滩普惠大会（2026 Inclusion·外滩大会）上探讨了这一主题，主题是前沿与金融科技（财新国际，9月11日）。例如，中国工程院院士蒋昌俊将人工智能风险分为三重：幻觉、算法黑匣子、数据中毒；而清华大学五道口金融学院学者张健华则认为人工智能将放大“第三方依赖、网络风险、模型治理等现有弱点”（上观新闻，9月） 10）。人工智能争论的大部分内容都围绕着中国或美国是否会“赢得这场竞赛”，更好的描述是一场跨越和追赶的持续斗争。
然而，对中国来说，更重要的问题不是其技术能力，而是其经济模式是否足够强劲和可持续，足以实现中国共产党（CCP）雄心勃勃的工业和地缘政治议程。 政策将人工智能置于主导地位 今年早些时候公布的第十五个五年计划（2026-2030）将人工智能放在了重要位置。它被提及 52 次，而之前的计划仅提及 11 次（国家发展和改革委员会 [NDRC]，2026 年 3 月；南华早报，3 月 5 日）。它已经从电网转向了领先地位，有望在克服经济瓶颈、实现战略主动、自力更生和国家韧性方面发挥带头作用。人工智能已从指定的“战略”优先领域转向

Executive Summary: The economic consequences of artificial intelligence (AI) may be especially marked in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) because they will feature a major positive supply shock and negative demand shock in an economy that already presents too much of both. The 15th Five-Year Plan places AI in pole position of the “modern industrial eco-system,” comprising all manner of manufacturing, technology, infrastructure, and control over global supply chains. The very policies that are powering the industrial side of the PRC economy are exacerbating structural weaknesses and flaws in the much larger part of the economy where excessive debt, low productivity, high unemployment, and fiscal and financial failing are becoming more deeply entrenched. General Secretary Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump discussed artificial intelligence (AI) at their September summit in Washington, D.C. Divergence on views between the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and the United States make it hard to see precisely how the two superpowers might collaborate successfully on an AI security and regulatory agenda. Xi in particular needs to pay more attention to both governance and economic issues surrounding AI, which threaten to exacerbate structural issues within the PRC’s domestic economy. The government is already vocal about the risks AI could pose to political and social security. PRC Minister of State Security Chen Yixin (陈一新) recently sent out a warning for the first time on the topic, and Xi Jinping himself addressed AI governance in another “major changes unseen in a century” (百年变局) speech, when he delivered the opening address to the World AI Conference in Shanghai in July ( Xinhua , July 18; South China Morning Post , September 14; China Brief , September 18). The economic consequences of AI, meanwhile, loom ever larger. Notably, a number of Chinese economists took the theme up at the 2026 Inclusion Conference on the Bund (2026 Inclusion·外滩大会) on frontier and financial technology in Shanghai ( Caixin Global , September 11). For instance, Jiang Changjun (蒋昌俊), an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, discussed AI risk as being threefold—hallucination, algorithmic black boxes, and data poisoning—while Zhang Jianhua (张健华), an academic at the Tsinghua University PBC School of Finance argued that AI will amplify “the existing weaknesses of third-party reliance, Internet risks, and model governance” (放大第三方依赖、网络风险、模型治理等既有的脆弱性) ( Shangguan News , September 10). Much of the AI debate revolves around whether the PRC or the United States is going to “win the race” that is better described as a continuous struggle of leapfrog and catch up. Yet the far more relevant question for the PRC is not about its technology capacity but about whether its economic model is robust and sustainable enough to deliver the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) ambitious industrial and geopolitical agenda. Policy Puts AI in Pole Position The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), unveiled earlier this year, gives pride of place to AI. It is mentioned 52 times, compared with just 11 in the previous plan ( National Development and Reform Commission [NDRC] , March 2026; South China Morning Post , March 5). It has moved from the grid into pole position, and is expected to lead the charge in overcoming bottlenecks in the economy, and realizing strategic initiatives, self-reliance, and national resilience. AI has shifted from a priority sector among designated “strategic emerging industries” (战略性新兴产业) to the engine behind the CCP’s desire to create a “modern socialist nation” (社会主义现代化国家) by 2035 ( NDRC , March 2026). While the PRC has been the world’s factory and principal assembly platform in the past, the plan seeks to transform it into a designer of new industrial structures and supply chains that integrate industry with the help of AI. This new ecosystem will allow the PRC to become a world leader in modern and traditional manufacturing, smart and green technologies, infrastructure, and industrial services, and it will give the country unprecedented control over global supply chains. The AI transition is occurring at a highly sensitive time for the PRC, which the plan puts firmly in a geopolitical and industrial policy perspective, and underscores the importance it is expected to have as the country looks to dominate manufacturing and scientific research, military capability, and cybersecurity, and geopolitical power. As it states in its first chapter discussing the country’s development environment, “great changes unseen in a century are accelerating, international power dynamics are being restructured, and a new generation of technological revolution and industrial innovation is accelerating breakthroughs” (世界百年变局加速演进，国际力量对比深刻调整，新一轮科技革命和产业变革加速突破), demarcating the current moment as full of uncertainty but also opportunity for the PRC ( NDRC , March 2026). From an economic standpoint, the Party hopes that AI can be harnessed to produce a “revolutionary productivity leap” (生产力革命性跃迁) ( NDRC , March 2026). This is increasingly urgent, as productivity growth has ground to a halt under Xi, and has not risen in lockstep with commensurate advances in industry and technology. Approved commentary, such as that in the People’s Tribune , views AI as a possible compensation for likely labor and skill shortages and other demographic headwinds, acknowledging that it could have disruptive effects on jobs that will require government attention ( People’s Tribune , July 8, 2024). And the 15th Five-Year Plan rightly makes the point that, to be successful, diffusion of AI throughout the economy is everything, and must be rolled out successfully and widely—something it seeks to achieve under the rubric of the “AI+” initiative (China Brief, March 28, 2025 , September 21, 2025 )   From the crow’s nest, the plan’s focus on AI amounts to a massive technological bet to steer the PRC toward global economic superiority and domination of the so-called fourth industrial revolution. In other words, it is a doubling down on the Party’s long-standing and huge mobilization of resources that underlines existing industrial strategy. The pursuit of AI-led technological transformation, as currently envisaged, will very likely deliver further gains in industry and manufacturing. In so doing, however, it will also exacerbate the dichotomous nature of the PRC economy, or what might be better referred to as its two economies.  [1] One economy is the PRC’s “strategic emerging industries,” guided by Xi’s “new quality productive forces” (新质生产力). This accounts for about 13 per cent of GDP, featuring the dynamism of several world class brands ( NDRC , December 29, 2025). The other is the rest of the economy, which features problems that have become more evident since the bust in real estate started in 2021, but which have in fact been building steadily for many years. These include a rising burden of predominantly state debt, weak consumption and productivity, population decline and rising unemployment, misallocated capital, and monetary and fiscal policy tools that have lost traction. Any accomplishments that follow from the PRC’s pursuit of AI, therefore, will not constitute a macroeconomic cure for the phenomena that are chipping away at its economic resilience and adaptive capacity. AI will create winners and losers unevenly distributed across the economy, likely exacerbating the “problem of unbalanced and inadequate development” (发展不平衡不充分问题) identified in the 15th Five-Year Plan ( NDRC , March 2026). The PRC’s already lagging economic development model may be especially vulnerable to AI because it represents a major positive supply shock and negative demand shock in an economy that already features structural oversupply and inadequate demand as parts of a model which the government seems unwilling and unable to reform. Seeking Economic Truth from Reality Like other nations, the PRC cannot know the ubiquitous repercussions of AI on the economy, or how the shorter-term economic and labor market costs and longer-term, hoped-for productivity benefits will fall. Unlike other countries, though, there are few effective forums in which open and unrestrained discussion can occur about how to manage the transition, or institutions of constraint and consensus that can help to frame the agenda. This is especially significant given the dualistic nature of the PRC’s economy, itself largely the result of years of large-scale industrial policy. It is arguable that AI is already bringing some economic benefits. It is leading to higher capital spending at home and demand from overseas—reflected in buoyant exports—for AI supply chain-related goods. With residential and manufacturing investment weak, and infrastructure investment trending lower, AI has stimulated demand for semiconductors, servers, data centers, power equipment, industrial automation, electronics, and advanced machinery. The PRC is also uniquely positioned to harness AI economies of scale due to its massive domestic AI user-base of 700 million users. As a recent article from the Economic Daily notes, “user population is the foundational strategic resource in the AI industrial ecosystem” (用户规模是AI产业生态最基础的战略资产) ( Economic Daily , October 5). The AI boom has been bullish for stock market valuations, at least for the moment, which is helpful given that the privately funded part of the PRC’s AI sector is heavily dependent on the equity market (as opposed to the bond market). In the April–June quarter, for example, electronics and IT, which capture most AI activities, contributed over half of the 3.6 percent annualized economic growth compared to the first quarter, and a third of the reported 4.3 percent rise in growth, compared with a year ago ( Capital Economics , July 16). Commentary on Sina Finance summed up the effect of the AI boom as twofold: directly creating productivity increases due to automation, and speeding up the pace of innovation to “expand the industrial boundaries of what is possible” (拓展生产可能性边界) ( Sina , October 7). By substituting capital for labor and helping firms move up the value chain, the government hopes AI will boost productivity growth. There is no evidence to date, though, that this is happening, as the International Monetary Fund has explained ( IMF , August 2025). While some firms have almost certainly enjoyed an uptick in productivity, it has stalled at the macro level and has been sluggish for much of the last decade. This is largely a result of liberal economic and market reforms grinding to a halt. There might well be measurement issues, as often happens with new and significant technologies and, importantly, the pace of AI diffusion might still be slow or unaccounted for. It is also probable, however, that AI’s benefits at the firm level are being checked or choked in the wider economy by a number of economic drags. These include the effects of high debt and limited debt capacity, weak consumer demand, misdirected resources and capital allocation, the deadweight of overcapacity and over-indebtedness, the real estate bust, too many zombie firms even in modern industries such as electric vehicles and solar manufacturing, a monetary and financial sector that is too beholden to state enterprises and uncommercial lending, along with inadequate credit for small firms, and the broad prioritization of politics over regulation and efficiency ( Huxiu , August 12). A Mixed Picture for the Labor Market The Party envisions AI taking on many tasks normally performed by people. They hope mass AI adoption will offset the economic impact of contraction in the labor force and in skill availability brought about by rapid population aging. This is a credible position but it might not be straightforward. Workers with high and low levels of skill may well be less vulnerable to AI-induced job destruction—and the PRC is well endowed with both. Yet the crucial factors that might determine the rate and nature of job losses are likely to be the speed with which jobs are lost before new ones are created and the degree of routine. In this regard, the PRC remains vulnerable because of the preponderance of low skill and routine work in manufacturing, for example, but also higher skill levels in technical and technology services. In other ways, the PRC labor market may be particularly vulnerable to the AI shock. Professor Zhang Dandan (张丹丹) of Peking University has drawn attention to the predominance of gig or on-demand working ( Caixin , February 14, 2025). Li Daokui (李稻葵), Dean of Tsinghua University’s Academic Centre for Chinese Economic Practice and Thinking, has argued that the country’s unemployment is more than double the official rate ( Caixin , July 13). Youth unemployment alone is officially almost 19 percent, although possibly higher ( Caixin , September 18). Even the Vice Minister of Human Resource and Social Security, Wu Xiuzhang (吴秀章), has acknowledged that about 200 million people were engaged in “flexible employment”—essentially freelance, platform-based, gig economy jobs without social or employment benefits—equivalent to 27 percent of the employed, and 43 percent of the urban working population ( Caixin , March 2). These caveats matter because for all the economic benefits that AI might bring, it is not going to magically make the macro-economy healthy or address some of the important problems that even the National Development and Reform Commission unusually cited in its annual report to the National People’s Congress earlier this year. The normally self-congratulatory and well scripted celebration of the CCP’s accomplishments and objectives did not mince its words about the state of the Chinese economy in a brief section, stating: “The imbalance between strong supply and weak demand is acute; real-estate development investment continues to decline; infrastructure investment growth has turned from positive to negative; manufacturing investment growth has slowed further; overall investment faces mounting downward pressure; consumption growth lacks momentum; and the price level continues to run low” ( NDRC March 5). Nothing of substance has changed since then. Car sales are down 20 percent from a year ago, household consumption is sluggish, and the beleaguered real estate sector, now in its fifth year of decline, still reveals declining sales and transactions volumes ( China Brief , April 2; Caixin , July 8; Sina , October 7). Given the basic orientation of economic and industrial polices, the clouds over economic flexibility and adaptive capacity are liable to remain. The PRC could theoretically derive significant benefits from AI-adjacent sectors, including advanced chips. Fully harnessing such benefits, however, requires entrepreneurial incentives; successful diffusion; high-quality, shared, and transferable data and information; and a relatively well-balanced economy in which small firms get adequate and stable funding. These conditions, however, do not currently exist in the PRC. Conclusion The essential contradiction is really about the consequences of AI for an economy that possesses a highly sophisticated modern industrial sector but is struggling to adapt to the AI age. There is risk of a turbo-charged, AI-powered version of its wider growth imbalance in which remarkable technological and industrial capability, financed heavily by the government, sitting alongside an economy with too little market demand, inadequate private risk capital, low employment creation, and too much dependence on investment and potentially fragile foreign demand. To alleviate the basic supply and demand imbalances in the economy, the government needs to embrace extensive fiscal, monetary, and financial reforms designed to transfer resources from the state to the private sector and write down or write off losses in the state sector. To sustain open and mutually beneficial foreign trade, the government would have to reform the PRC’s economic model so the country’s massive trade surplus shrinks to a more acceptable size. This would allow imports from other countries to rise steadily, and Chinese exports would no longer threaten their industrialization plans and programs of not just richer nations but many in the Global South. AI, even in pole industrial position, is not the answer or solution to these trenchant challenges in the wider economy. And it might make them worse. Notes [1] A growing corpus of voices in the PRC have started to refer to the economy as exhibiting “K-shaped divergence” (K型分化) ( Caixin , June 22). Western analysts have picked up on the same phenomenon ( Substack/Yasheng Huang , July 29) The post AI Will Deepen Divide Between the PRC’s Two Economies appeared first on Jamestown .

content: 澳洲签证频频被取消！ 结果在中国机场被拦下！ 在悉尼机场小黑屋盘问2小时！ 澳洲签证大震荡！华人接连被取消签证！原因令人警惕！PR父母探亲签证有效期缩短至半年，移民政策开始全面收紧！ 澳洲签证恐迎“腥风血雨”！ 最近，一则则签证被取消的消息让不少华人胆战心惊！ 澳洲签证接连曝出重大变化！现在想来澳洲，真的越来越难了！ 近日，一名小红书网友发帖称，短短一周内，自己身边就连续发生了两起签证入境问题！ 其中一名租客此前持旅游签证来到澳洲，在澳洲停留85天后正常离境，原本计划6天后再次返回墨尔本。 谁知人还在中国机场，准备登机时就出了问题。 澳洲签证竟然已经被取消，连飞机都没能坐上！ 按照当事人的描述，问题就出在此前停留时间较长，短暂离境后又准备迅速返回。明明已经正常离开澳洲，没想到再回来时，手里的签证却不管用了！ 而另一名持商务访客签证的旅客，经历同样惊险！ 根据帖子，这名男子今年2月入境澳洲，待了接近三个月才离开；8月再次入境，又在澳洲停留了很长时间。 这一次，他仅仅离境9天，就因为有急事决定再次返回。结果在悉尼机场，他直接被澳洲边境执法人员带去盘问，前后接近两个小时！ 发帖人表示，当时工作人员一度提出可能取消他的签证。虽然帖子没有说这名旅客最终真的被取消签证，但近两个小时的边境问询，已经足以让频繁往返的访客重视起来。 更让在澳华人家庭关注的，是近期父母探亲签证的变化。 一名小红书网友晒出父母新获批的600家庭担保访客签证，表示这次的结果完全出乎自己预料！ 她说，她本人是PR永居，父母正在排队申请143父母移民签证，过去通常能拿到5年多次往返的访客签证。可这一次，等到的竟然是半年入境有效期！ 截图显示，这份签证于2026年9月7日获批，最晚入境日期为2027年3月7日，旅行条件则是Single entry。与过去的多年多次往返相比，这次获批的入境窗口只有半年。 类似担忧还在其他小红书帖子里出现。 有网友发文称，近期访客签证审核明显趋严，过去PR或澳洲公民父母常能拿到的3年、5年多次往返签证，如今似乎越来越难见到。 从离境6天签证被取消，到悉尼机场盘问两小时，再到PR父母只获得半年入境窗口，这些案例近期接连出现，足以说明澳洲对于移民的管控越来越严厉了！页让很多华人感到不安！ 而另一边，澳洲边境问题又曝出一宗大案，15人乘船偷渡登陆西澳，竟还有华裔母女策划跨州接应，最终连自己都被判刑！ 太疯狂了！华人母女为让伴侣进入澳洲，竟参与偷渡接应计划！最终3人获刑！ 就在华人讨论澳洲签证收紧和边境审查的时候，另一宗涉及中国籍人士的非法入境案件，也被澳媒曝光！ 一艘来自印尼的渔船，竟载着15人穿过海上边境，在西澳偏远海岸登陆。而更让人意外的是，澳洲境内还有一对华人母女，已经计划前往偏远地区接人，准备把其中两名男子一路带去悉尼！ 如今，这起发生于2024年的案件终于迎来判决，三名参与接应计划的人全部获刑！ 事情发生在2024年4月，一艘印尼渔船抵达西澳Kimberley偏远海岸，船上15人未经正常签证入境程序进入澳洲。 其中一名中国籍人士后来还与其他人走散，最终在Mungalalu-Truscott空军基地附近的一条土路上被当局找到。 偏远海岸突然出现非法入境者，边境执法部门随即展开行动！ 而在澳洲境内，56岁的Hong Shuyan和34岁的Zhang Zhongfang母女，早已准备前往西澳接应。 法庭披露，她们当时都是临时签证持有人，要接的两名男子分别是她们的伴侣，而且两名男子此前申请澳洲签证均遭拒绝。 为了把伴侣接进澳洲，两人竟然决定铤而走险，准备从偏远登陆地点把人接走，再送往悉尼。 她们还花钱找来一名29岁的中国籍男子Sun Shuai，让他驾驶租来的面包车，长途前往西澳偏远地区。目的地位于Broome和达尔文之间，距离悉尼非常遥远，整个计划需要跨越漫长的公路路程。 法庭获悉，Hong与Sun一同前往西澳，女儿Zhang则负责支付整趟行程的费用。三人一路通过微信保持联络，随时交换位置和行动安排！ 可计划还没有成功，事情就已经开始失控。当三人得知澳洲边境部队扣留了部分海上非法入境者时，立刻意识到情况不妙。 法庭披露的微信信息中，甚至出现了一句：“我们完了。”原本安排好的接应行动，最后连人都没能接到！ 虽然几人期间还曾多次通过电话联系，但最终还是空手离开了Broome。也就是说，这场跨州接应计划从头到尾都没有成功，原本准备接走的两名男子并没有被他们带往悉尼。 然而，接应没有成功，并不意味着已经实施的犯罪计划可以一笔勾销。随着案件进入司法程序，母女和受雇司机都必须为自己的行为承担责任！ 最终，三人分别被判处三年监禁，但刑期缓期执行，并须遵守保持良好行为的要求。这意味着他们被判有罪，却并没有立即入狱服刑。 澳媒还指出，根据澳洲严格的海上边境政策，没有有效签证、乘船非法抵达澳洲的人，将无法通过这种方式获得在澳永久定居的机会。相关人员可能被遣返回原籍国，或者被送往离岸处理中心。报道披露，过去四年，澳洲当局已经在海上拦截51艘船只，涉及700多人。面对海上非法入境问题，澳洲的边境管控一直采取严格措施。 小编想说，最近接连曝出的签证风波，确实值得在澳华人警惕！有人离境6天就被取消签证，连PR父母也遇到了签证有效期缩短的情况。另一边，竟还有人为了团聚铤而走险，参与偷渡接应，最终被判刑！澳洲边境审查绝不能掉以轻心，无论是来澳旅游、探亲还是长期往返，都要提前了解签证条件，千万别抱侥幸心理，否则可能付出沉重代价！
