Trump’s brief social media post Sunday offered few details but said the energy ceasefire took effect immediately, adding: “Do not break it!” On Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov wouldn’t say whether Russia had agreed to such a ceasefire, saying only: “Contacts are ongoing."

**Energy strikes have caused pain for both Ukraine and Russia**

Trump previously announced a similar agreement on ceasing energy strikes that did not come to fruition. In a social media post on Sept. 14, he said both countries had agreed “not to hit” each other’s energy infrastructure, but offered no details on that proposal either.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256649.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan links timing of ₱41-M Carpio withdrawals to Duterte’s DepEd exit, drug charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/pangilinan-links-timing-of-41-m-carpio-withdrawals-to-dutertes-deped-exit-drug-charges/2444082)

Russia has used attacks on energy facilities in order to deny Ukrainian civilians power, heat and running water during the war, hoping to wear down public support for Ukraine's response to Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Ukrainian officials describe the strategy as “weaponizing winter," and fear Russia could ramp up such attacks as cold weather approaches.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has launched strikes against Russian energy sites like oil refineries, sometimes deep within Russian territory. That's prompted Trump to blame Zelenskyy for record US diesel prices — rather than the US-led war in Iran — and to strike a deal with Putin on Friday to import diesel from Russia in an attempt to bring fuel prices down ahead of US midterm elections.

Speaking on Fox News on Monday, Zelenskyy pushed back on Trump's claims that Ukrainian strikes in Russia were driving up fuel prices, saying: “Everybody understands that the prices on diesel (don't) depend on our attacks on diesel in Russia. Everybody understands that it depends on the blocking (of the) Strait of Hormuz.”

**EU foreign policy chief skeptical of energy ceasefire**

*   ![Image 2: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

The European Union’s top diplomat on Monday welcomed the prospect of a pause in energy strikes on Ukraine, but said she sees no sign that Russia is willing to respect it.

“We haven’t yet seen that ... Russia will stick to it,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at a meeting of the bloc's foreign ministers in Luxembourg. “Personally, I would also welcome that the ceasefire would include people not being killed, not only energy.”

Trump's deal with Putin to purchase diesel from Russia dismayed officials in the US, Ukraine and around Europe. A bipartisan group of six US senators, including four Republicans, called Sunday on the Trump administration to “immediately reverse course” on the deal, saying the U.S. should “not provide Putin with a financial lifeline” while Russia is killing Ukrainian civilians.

Kallas also pushed back on Trump's comments Saturday that it was time for Ukraine to get a new president and that Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war. She said that now is not the time to hold elections in Ukraine, at least not without a ceasefire.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

On Monday, Zelenskyy said holding elections in Ukraine was impossible during war time, especially with new Russian tactics involving attacks day and night. He added, however, that he would be ready to work toward doing so if Ukraine secured a full ceasefire lasting at least 60 days.

In response, Kremlin spokesman Peskov said in a statement that in case of a Ukrainian election, Putin would be ready to halt strikes on Ukraine “specifically on election day,” and that Kyiv only wanted a 60-day ceasefire “to gather their strength, heal their wounds, and continue the war.”

**Russian attacks kill 5 and injure others, including children**

Meanwhile, Zelenskyy called for greater pressure on Russia to end the war after a Russian drone struck a high-rise apartment building in Kyiv on Monday evening, killing two people and injuring nine.

“This is further proof that Russia must face greater pressure. They are the ones continuing the brutal strikes. They are the ones prolonging the war,” he said in a post on X.

He called the attack a “response” to the U.S. proposal for an energy ceasefire.

“We count on the United States to recognize these signals from Russia and act with strength. Strength is needed to force Russia to end this war,” Zelenskyy said.

Monday's attack came a day after a Russian drone struck the village of Pisochyn in the Kharkiv district, killing three people and injuring nine others, including children, according to the Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office.

Ukrainian air defense forces shot down or suppressed 89 of 121 Russian drones overnight Monday, Ukraine’s Air Force said in a Telegram post. The attacks included one Kh-59 guided air-to-surface missile and 76 jet-powered Shahed-type drones, the statement said. Strikes were recorded at 15 locations in Ukraine, while debris from downed drones fell at four locations.

Meanwhile, the Russian Defense Ministry said Monday its air defenses overnight intercepted 151 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions as well as the illegally annexed Crimea and the waters of the Black Sea.

In a separate statement, the ministry said its forces carried out drone strikes overnight on Ukraine’s port infrastructure and a bulk carrier heading to Ukraine's port city of Odesa with military cargo on board.

title: Wage hike proposals met with mixed reactions
summary: **ILOILO CITY —**Calls for a wage increase comparable to those granted in other regions and for the deferment of an adjustment amid rising business costs emerged during a public hearing on minimum wage rates for private-sector workers in We
content:
**ILOILO CITY —**Calls for a wage increase comparable to those granted in other regions and for the deferment of an adjustment amid rising business costs emerged during a public hearing on minimum wage rates for private-sector workers in Western Visayas.

The Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-Western Visayas (RTWPB-6) conducted its third public hearing on the proposed wage adjustment on Oct. 9, with stakeholders from Iloilo City and the provinces of Iloilo, Antique and Guimaras.

Jessraf Palmares, president of the Iloilo Federation for Information Technology, Inc., supported a wage increase but urged the board to consider rates in neighboring regions rather than compete with wage boards granting substantially higher adjustments.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

“If possible, Iloilo should have the same minimum wage as Cebu,” he said.

He claimed that two BPO companies had planned to establish operations in Iloilo but eventually withdrew and redirected their plans to Cebu because of Iloilo’s higher minimum wage.

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A teacher from St. Anthony’s College in Antique also supported a wage increase but said a P200 daily adjustment would be too much for educational institutions to absorb.

She suggested an increase comparable to those granted in other regions, saying an additional P60 a day would provide some relief to workers without imposing an excessive burden on employers.

“Sixty pesos is more or less acceptable. It is not substantial but it could help,” she said.

*   ![Image 1: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

The teacher warned that a P200 increase could adversely affect private schools, particularly as they consider possible tuition adjustments.

In Central Visayas, private-sector workers are scheduled to receive a P42 daily minimum wage increase starting Oct. 14, 2026.

The minimum wage in expanded Metro Cebu and other Class A areas will rise from P540 to P582, while rates in covered Class B cities and municipalities will increase from P500 to P542.

In the National Capital Region, a P60 daily wage increase took effect on Sept. 26, raising the minimum wage to P755 for non-agricultural workers and P718 for agricultural workers and employees of certain small establishments. In Western Visayas, the current daily minimum wage rates are P550 for workers in non-agricultural, industrial and commercial establishments employing more than 10 workers; P525 for those in establishments employing 10 or fewer workers; and P520 for agricultural workers.

*   ![Image 2: Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255560.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/fast-times/aston-martin-dbx-gt-puts-luxury-first/2443744)

The Western Visayas rates were established under a wage order that took effect on Nov. 19, 2025.

**Businesses seek deferment**

Happy Mapua Abenir, president of the Iloilo Hotels, Restaurants, and Resorts Association, Inc., called for the deferment of the proposed wage increase until next year, citing economic uncertainties and mounting operating costs.

“The business sector is now experiencing an extraordinary event in 2026. It is very worrisome because we cannot seem to predict what will happen until the end of the year,” she argued.

*   ![Image 3: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

She described the current business environment as worse than the Covid-19 pandemic, saying businesses were struggling not only with rising prices but also with numerous expenses that had become increasingly difficult to sustain.

While acknowledging local governments’ efforts to help alleviate poverty, Abenir said providing loans is only a “band-aid” solution and would not address the underlying problems faced by businesses.

Instead, she called for relief from high taxes, rental costs, electricity bills and fuel expenses.

A resort owner in Guimaras likewise sought a deferment, explaining that the tourism business was seasonal and that establishments still had to retain employees during off-peak periods despite having little or no income.

“I hope the increase can be deferred for now because this is the off-season for resorts. We are just waiting for people to take their vacations at our resort,” she said.

Tiffany Ong of the Federation of Free Workers, who represented health workers during the hearing, called for government intervention through subsidies and temporary relief from mandatory deductions.

She proposed a moratorium on deductions for government-mandated contributions, including those for the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), Social Security System (SSS), and Pag-IBIG Fund.

“I hope these deductions can be temporarily suspended. We can hardly feel our salaries because of the mandatory deductions,” Ong said.

MSMEs need support

Palmares, who also operates a small business, said soaring electricity and rental costs had forced them to reduce their workforce and assign more responsibilities to their remaining employees.

He urged the government to provide subsidies and tax relief to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), including measures to ease their tax burden.

“What is the plan of the government to subsidize the MSMEs? I hope there will be a tax bracket under which value-added tax can be removed. MSME taxes should be reduced so we can still earn a profit,” Palmares said.

Elmer Forro, one of the lead convenors of the United Labor-Western Visayas Workers’ Alliance (ULWVA), which filed a petition seeking a P250 daily wage increase, said workers and small businesses had yet to benefit sufficiently from the region’s economic growth.

Western Visayas recorded a 6.4 percent growth rate in its Gross Regional Domestic Product in 2025, ranking as the fastest-growing regional economy among the Philippines’ 18 regions and outperforming the national average of 4.4 percent.

“But workers and MSMEs cannot feel this growth. Its benefits have not reached workers, and MSMEs but have also gone to big businesses investing here,” Forro said.

He acknowledged the difficulty of balancing workers’ demands for higher wages with the capacity of MSMEs to absorb additional labor costs.

“The big question in the debate between workers and MSMEs is the issue of wages. Higher wages are a burden for MSMEs, but workers also cannot survive if the minimum wage does not increase,” he said.

Forro questioned the government’s role in addressing the situation, saying one-time financial assistance was insufficient to address the underlying problems.

“We do not just need one-time, substantial financial assistance. The government needs to help MSMEs increase their capacity to provide fair wages to their workers,” he said.

He added that the government should provide greater assistance to MSMEs to help balance the interests of employers and workers.

“To our MSMEs and labor groups, it is high time for us to unite. We have a common problem. We are both victims. We should seek from the government what we deserve,” Forro said.

**Wage decision eyed before year-end**

Lawyer Sixto Rodriguez Jr., RTWPB-6 chairman and concurrently director of the Department of Labor and Employment in Region 6, said the board could decide before the end of the year whether to issue a new wage order.

“We will have to act within a reasonable time because you know the last wage order was Nov. 19. It might be after that; it should not be before that. Yes (before the year ends),” he said.

Rodriguez added that wage determination involved balancing workers’ right to fair compensation with employers’ interests in sustaining their businesses, taking into account prevailing economic conditions.

The RTWPB-6 received four petitions seeking a wage increase.

On April 30, ULWVA filed a petition seeking a P250 daily wage increase, which would raise the regional minimum wage from P550 to P800, along with a cost-of-living allowance.

The group cited global oil supply disruptions and their effects on the regional economy.

On June 5, the Iloilo Doctors Hospital Employees Union, also a member of ULWVA, filed a similar petition.

Following an evaluation, the board found that the petition substantially complied with legal requirements and issued a resolution recognizing its sufficiency.

The BPO Industry Employees Network filed another petition on June 26 seeking the same adjustment, citing concerns specific to BPO workers.

The fourth petition was filed on July 24 by the Iloilo Pepsi-Cola Workers Independent Union, which also sought a P250 daily wage increase.

“Our decision is always based on facts and based on evidence presented, as well as what constitutes a just and reasonable amount,” Rodriguez said.

title: Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ creates confusion
summary: **WASHINGTON**—US President Donald Trump sowed confusion on Sunday, announcing an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia that sparked astonishment in Kyiv, silence from Moscow and support from Ukraine’s Western allies. The ceasefire
content:
**WASHINGTON**—US President Donald Trump sowed confusion on Sunday, announcing an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia that sparked astonishment in Kyiv, silence from Moscow and support from Ukraine’s Western allies.

The ceasefire appeared shaky at best as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia struck multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday, including one in the capital and another in Kharkiv, leading to power outages and outrage.

Trump’s announcement came two days after he declared a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, prompting outrage by European allies and Kyiv, who said it would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

*   [NATO to warn Russia against any attack](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/nato-to-warn-russia-against-any-attack/2443624)

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said early Sunday on Truth Social. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!”

Zelenskyy appeared to express surprise at the announcement, saying he was seeking further details, but added that “Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well.”

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Russia has yet to confirm its agreement.

Zelenskyy later said that multiple Ukrainian power stations had been hit and that “Ukrainian skies have been infested with Russian ‘shaheds’ all day,” referring to a type of drone originally designed by Iran that is now used extensively by Russia.

## **‘Up to our people’**

The ceasefire appeared to garner support on Sunday from Ukraine’s key western allies, including the UK, France, Canada and the European Commission.

Several leaders called on Russia to uphold the deal.

That support was in contrast to broad criticism of the US-Russia diesel deal earlier in the week, which has led to mounting tensions between Trump and Zelenskyy.

Zelenskyy said the diesel deal was a “weak decision,” while several of Ukraine’s European allies expressed outrage and pledged to increase pressure on Moscow.

Seven US senators -- including four Republicans -- released a statement Sunday blasting the diesel deal with Russia, saying it was illegal.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney added to the chorus on Sunday after a call with Zelensky, saying the diesel deal “is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe.”

## **Support for Zelenskyy**

Germany’s foreign minister said Sunday that Berlin continued to “fully support” Zelenskyy.

“Europe needs stability and that means that we are very clearly continuing to stay by the side of Ukraine and its government,” Johann Wadephul said in Berlin.

[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen also backed the Ukrainian leader “as he leads the fight for his people’s freedom.”

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also said his country “strongly supports President Trump’s call today for a sustained energy ceasefire to start now.”

In Kyiv, several residents expressed concern about Trump’s call for Zelenskyy to be replaced.

“I believe our president is the best, and Americans should think about their own president,” said 40-year-old Olesia Goncharuk.

“We Ukrainians decide our own fate and our own freedom, and we are free people,” she told AFP.

title: Prepare for El Niño, Marcos urges Filipinos
summary: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged Filipinos to prepare for a super El Niño, including collecting rainwater and planting their own vegetables at home, to minimize the impact from the weather pattern. In a press briefing, Marcos stressed h
content:
PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged Filipinos to prepare for a super El Niño, including collecting rainwater and planting their own vegetables at home, to minimize the impact from the weather pattern.

In a press briefing, Marcos stressed how impactful El Niño was likely to be, citing government forecasts that indicate severe dry conditions lasting through the first quarter of next year.

He stressed that along with government programs, everyday households play a critical role in mitigating the severe impacts of the expected dry conditions.

*   [China's carmakers rely on overseas markets as monthly domestic sales decline continues](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/business/foreign-business/chinas-carmakers-rely-on-overseas-markets-as-monthly-domestic-sales-decline-continues/2443941)

“Part of that public service — and those public service messages — will be to gather or buy buckets now so that when it rains, you can collect all the water,” Marcos said.

He added that the government would be providing guidance and water-treatment tools to ensure home-collected rainwater is safe for domestic use.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“We will teach you... We’ll give you the filter, we’ll teach you how to do everything so you won’t get sick, and the water is treated properly.”

He also stressed that practicing strict household water conservation — such as reusing dishwashing water to tend to home vegetable plots — would help cushion families against rising food prices and supply constraints.

Marcos also highlighted the importance of keeping the momentum of the “green revolution,” or the movement to increase food production.

*   ![Image 1: Paper is not proof](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256393.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

“Get everybody to plant their own vegetables. That’s why if — that will help again. It won’t solve the entire problem, but it will help,” he said, encouraging a national revival of backyard farming and planting, similar to the time of the pandemic.

Beyond household-level measures, Marcos assured the public that Task Force El Niño, led by the Department of Science and Technology, had activated coordinated contingency plans.

The plans include ensuring medical facilities maintain standby generators, fuel reserves and water stores during potential heat waves and power outages.

The national government is also securing grain supplies through strategic imports while preparing cash-for-work and livelihood assistance.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Cloud-seeding operations will be done to boost reservoir levels before the onset of the peak summer months.

“It’s not just a regular El Niño. It’s going to be a Super El Niño... starting late October, beginning November, and continuing until March next year,” Marcos said.

“We should all prepare. We’re taking this very, very seriously.”

As this developed, the Department of Energy (DOE) on Monday also warned of rotating brownouts, particularly in the Visayas, where supply is already under pressure due to insufficient baseload capacity nationwide, with a super El Niño expected to put the power grid under severe strain.

*   ![Image 3: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

Energy Undersecretary Mario Marasigan said the department was closely watching.

He said the agency is doing various simulations with increased demand due to El Niño and noted that Visayas could again be hit with plenty of red alerts because of various plants’ possibility of going offline unscheduled due to the heat.

“Based on our simulations, and assuming we are under normal condition or there are no unannounced power interruptions, we are seeing a little amount of red alerts for Luzon, but will not necessarily translate to manual load dropping, or rotating brownouts,” Marasigan said in an online media briefing.

Marasigan continued that the DOE was closely monitoring the Visayas and working on the completion of immediate and interim energy generation solutions by the first quarter of 2027.

“If there are ancillary services that are available from these intermediate and immediate facilities, then we will be able to greatly reduce the potential of having red and yellow alerts in the island group,” he said.

Mindanao, meanwhile, will likely see limited yellow alerts, while Luzon could see a few red alerts but not rotational brownouts.

“I would say that we are still preparing for El Niño and that related programs are in place and already activated via the Task Force on Energy Resiliency,” Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said.

Malacañang, the DOE said, has been calling for meetings under a whole-of-government approach that will include an extensive education and information campaign on how the country is supposed to handle the situation for the coming months.

title: Mynt IPO oversubscribed
summary: INVESTOR demand for Mynt Inc.’s initial public offering (IPO) exceeded share allocations at several brokerages, with one firm reporting subscriptions more than four times its assigned quota, as investors bet on the growth prospects of GCash
content:
INVESTOR demand for Mynt Inc.’s initial public offering (IPO) exceeded share allocations at several brokerages, with one firm reporting subscriptions more than four times its assigned quota, as investors bet on the growth prospects of GCash’s parent company ahead of its stock market debut.

AB Capital Securities Inc., which handles subscriptions through GCash’s GStocks PH platform, reported that its allocated shares were 165.11 percent oversubscribed as of Friday. Regina Capital Development Corp. head of sales Luis Limlingan, meanwhile, said his firm’s allocation was oversubscribed four times.

Domestic trading participants and retail investors were allocated 2.41 billion shares, equivalent to 30 percent of the base offering of about 8.03 billion shares, according to the offering details.

*   [Trade dept welcomes Mitsubishi-Ayala deal](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/business/corporate-news/trade-dept-welcomes-mitsubishi-ayala-deal/2443998)

COL Financial Inc.’s head of research April Tan attributed the strong investor interest partly to the participation of about 22 cornerstone investors along with the attractive offer price.

“And the price is also good, not expensive,” she added.

 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

In a client memo issued Monday, COL Financial said Mynt retained significant growth potential through GCash, which had 41.5 million monthly active users, equivalent to 56 percent of the country’s adult population.

The brokerage noted that digital payment adoption in more developed markets typically reaches 70 percent to 80 percent of the adult population, suggesting room for GCash to expand its user base.

GCash also had 7.5 million active borrowers, representing about 18 percent of its monthly active users, indicating potential to expand its lending business, COL Financial said.

*   ![Image 1: Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256345.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

The platform could also grow through merchant acquisition and overseas remittance services for overseas Filipino workers.

SeA Focus Portfolio hedge fund manager Eric Jurado said the P6.60-per-share IPO price did not require Mynt to sustain its historical earnings growth rate to justify its valuation.

He said the offer price assumed annual growth of 15 percent from Mynt’s 2025 net income of P17.15 billion, or a 25.8 percent growth rate from 2026 to 2028, which he considered achievable based on the company’s historical performance.

“Given GCash’s market leadership, 41.5 million monthly active users, expanding financial ecosystem, and continued shift toward digital payments in the Philippines, I believe that is a realistic hurdle,” Jurado said.

*   ![Image 2: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1256531.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/news/unexplained-wealth-of-vp-could-hit-p15b/2443897)

He added that investors could benefit if Mynt’s earnings growth exceeded the rate implied by the offer price, potentially prompting the market to recognize greater earnings capacity.

COL Financial estimated that at P6.60 per share, Mynt would be trading at 21.7 times its projected 2026 earnings and 17.1 times its projected 2027 earnings, well below regional peer averages of 33.3 times and 24.2 times, respectively.

Mynt wrapped up its IPO on Monday and is scheduled to list on the Philippine Stock Exchange on Oct. 20 under the ticker symbol GCASH.

The base offering comprises 1.61 billion primary shares and 6.42 billion secondary shares for a total of about 8.03 billion shares, with an additional 1.2 billion secondary shares available through an over-allotment option.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

At P6.60 per share, the base offering could raise about P53 billion, with total proceeds reaching approximately P60.9 billion if the over-allotment option is fully exercised.

Mynt expects to receive P10.6 billion in gross proceeds from the primary share offering, of which it plans to allocate 60 percent to its credit technology business, 20 percent to product innovation, and the remaining 20 percent for general corporate purposes.

title: Remulla tags Subic as ‘smuggling capital’
summary: THE Port of Subic has come under fresh scrutiny after being branded the country’s “smuggling capital” by Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, as the Bureau of Customs (BOC) uncovered P29.17 million worth of cigarettes concealed in a shipment de
content:
THE Port of Subic has come under fresh scrutiny after being branded the country’s “smuggling capital” by Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, as the Bureau of Customs (BOC) uncovered P29.17 million worth of cigarettes concealed in a shipment declared as scrap metal.

The latest bust involved 320 boxes of Astro and Redwood cigarettes discovered during spot checks on two 20-foot containers shipped from Zamboanga at the Subport of North Harbor, with assistance from the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency’s K9 unit.

One container yielded the cigarettes, which did not match the shipment’s declaration, while the other contained boxes of white cigarette filters bearing Chinese markings, the BOC said.

*   [10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The seized cigarettes have an estimated import value of P9.6 million and a market value of P29.17 million.

The BOC did not disclose the consignee or importer or clarify whether the cigarette filters were also seized.

The discovery adds to a series of major smuggling-related enforcement actions involving Subic, including the destruction in August of three 40-foot containers containing about 3,000 cases of cigarettes worth P129.065 million.

The cigarettes were part of a 10-container batch of abandoned goods valued at P413 million, with the disposal of the remaining shipments still underway at the time of the report.

In September, customs and partner agencies also recovered an estimated P162.2 million worth of marijuana from a distressed yacht at the Subic Bay Yacht Club following an intelligence operation targeting the vessel’s suspected illicit cargo.

*   ![Image 1: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

Remulla earlier called Subic the country’s “smuggling capital,” citing apprehensions made in the area when he was still justice secretary.

He also pointed to the seizure of several containers of smuggled cigarettes in Cebu aboard a vessel owned by Gothong Lines.

The Ombudsman also criticized the BOC over what he described as repeated failures to provide complete documentation needed to investigate and prosecute smuggling cases.

“Lagi sa customs ayaw nila kumpletuhin ang documentation para ma-dismiss ang kaso,” Remulla said, alleging that requested documents often failed to reach investigators, undermining efforts to file cases and hold suspects accountable.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

He also lamented the lack of effective data sharing between agencies despite earlier discussions between the Department of Justice and the BOC on efforts to curb smuggling.

In response, BOC Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno reaffirmed the bureau’s commitment to improving interagency coordination, saying timely access to records and information is essential to effective enforcement and successful prosecution.

Nepomuceno said the BOC would continue cooperating with the Office of the Ombudsman, DOJ, and other partner agencies, adding that the bureau supports lawful requests for information and is strengthening its systems to improve data sharing.

“Smuggling is a challenge that requires a united government response,” Nepomuceno said, vowing continued cooperation and transparency to protect government revenues and prevent illicit goods from entering the market.

title: Homeware line designed for dormers, young couples, small families
summary: College students in dorms and young couples starting out often need a few items to make their spaces more comfortable. These often include basics like flatware, plates, beddings and maybe a lamp or two. While there are department stores and
content:
College students in dorms and young couples starting out often need a few items to make their spaces more comfortable. These often include basics like flatware, plates, beddings and maybe a lamp or two.

While there are department stores and home store chains that offer pretty much the same kind of mix, one of the newer entrants is the Metro Retail Stores Group. Last month, it launched its own brand of home basics, Metro Living in its four Metro Department Stores located in Alabang, Market Market, Ayala Center Cebu, and Super Metro Colon.

Arranged on open shelves and in compact displays, the merchandise is basic and designed to work together.

*   [Comedian Russell Brand appears in UK court for start of rape trial](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/entertainment-lifestyle/comedian-russell-brand-appears-in-uk-court-for-start-of-rape-trial/2443698)

“For Metro Living, we’ve shifted our entire retail philosophy from selling individual products to delivering fully integrated lifestyle solutions. Previously, customers had to navigate different aisles to assemble a look,” Joel Orense, Metro Retail President and COO told The Manila Times in an email interview.

“Through our dedicated shop-in-shop concept, we bring fully curated, pre-styled living spaces directly to the retail floor. It eliminates decision fatigue, offers immediate aesthetic inspiration, and maximizes customer convenience. We are elevating the overall shopping experience, and based on initial performance, we plan to scale this format to additional key stores next year,” he added.

Placing these household staples in a dedicated location inside their stores was only logical as it takes out the guesswork for shoppers.

Orense said that historically, people bought items for their homes from different stores. While this can actually be a fun exercise on a weekend or during sale season, it can also be a chore for people who might prefer to do something else with their time.

“By engineering a cross-category, cohesive product matrix, Metro Living bridges that gap — transforming single-item transactions into complete room solutions,” he said.

*   ![Image 1: The Getty Family and Koch Equity Development Commit to Equity Investment of up to $533 Million in Getty Images, Reflecting Confidence in Long-Term Growth Potential](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256496.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)

The current merchandise mix at the Metro stores includes beddings, pillow cases and cushion covers, kitchen linens, and window treatments. There also plates, cutlery and compact storage systems.

“Metro Living is tailored for the modern Filipino demographic — specifically first-time condo owners, growing families, young homeowners, and value-conscious style seekers,” Orense said. “These consumers want practical, elevated, and contemporary home aesthetics without compromising on affordability or functionality.”

title: PH to host 2026 East Asia Cup at RMBS
summary: THE crack of the bat will once again echo through the storied walls of the Rizal Memorial Baseball Stadium (RMBS) as Manila hosts the East Asia Cup 2026, presented by the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) from Dec. 7 to 13. For one week, s
content:
THE crack of the bat will once again echo through the storied walls of the Rizal Memorial Baseball Stadium (RMBS) as Manila hosts the East Asia Cup 2026, presented by the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) from Dec. 7 to 13.

For one week, six nations headlined by host Philippines, Singapore, Hong Kong, Thailand will converge on the capital, turning the historic venue into a hub of competition and sports tourism.

For the first time since its opening in 1934, the RMBS has undergone a major facelift, a transformation that promises to restore its past grandeur and elevate Philippine baseball to global standards.

*   [Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-suffers-worst-loss-of-2026-season-falls-to-world-no-217-shi/2443990)

“Our objective is to finish the facelift as soon as possible and bring the stadium to global standards,” said PSC Chairman Patrick Gregorio, noting that the grandstand will be retrofitted to seat 10,000, complemented by a digital scoreboard mounted on the historic outfield wall and an all-weather artificial turf built to international specifications.

“This is about giving Filipino baseball a true home worthy of its history and future,” Gregorio added.

Immediately after completion, the stadium will host the East Asia Cup organized by the Philippine Amateur Baseball Association (PABA), sanctioned by the Baseball Federation of Asia (BFA).

“This renovation is a turning point for Philippine baseball,” emphasized PABA Secretary General Mike Asuncion. “Hosting the East Asia Cup in a world-class stadium will inspire our athletes and show the region that we are serious about competing at the highest level.”

Asuncion added that the PSC-PABA partnership extends beyond RMBS, with plans to build additional baseball fields nationwide to nurture young talent and expand grassroots development.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

The RMBS is a shrine to baseball’s global heritage. In its inaugural exhibition game in December 1934, Lou Gehrig hit the stadium’s first-ever home run, followed by Babe Ruth with the second. Their feats remain etched on the stadium’s walls, reminders of Manila’s place in baseball lore.

Hataw Pilipinas, the official moniker of the 24-man Philippine national team that captured the Southeast Asian Games gold medal against host Thailand, enters the East Asia Cup with confidence.

Team captain and pitcher Romeo Jasmin, who will soon pass the baton to the next generation of Filipino baseball players, leads the charge, determined to prove that Filipino baseball is ready to step up its game.

Veterans such as Ferdinand “Bong” Liguayan Jr., catcher Mark Steven Manaig, leadoff hitter Jenald Pareja, and rising star Mark Beronilla likewise anchor the squad. TMT

title: <div bis_skin_checked='1'>European, Chinese automakers launch product blitz at Paris car show<div bis_skin_checked='1'>
summary: PARIS — European and Chinese automakers were expected to unveil as many as 60 new models at the Paris car show on Monday, as competition for buyers on the continent continues to intensify. The show comes days after the European Union (EU) a
content:
PARIS — European and Chinese automakers were expected to unveil as many as 60 new models at the Paris car show on Monday, as competition for buyers on the continent continues to intensify.

The show comes days after the European Union (EU) announced a deal with China to cut imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc, with a cap of 350,000 units a year, according to a European Commission official on Monday. It is still not clear how the agreement will be implemented, though it was welcomed by the region’s manufacturers.

The flood of hybrid imports into the EU is “not sustainable” for Europe, said Renault CEO Francois Provost, with the current deal “better than a trade war.”

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

Around 20 Chinese brands are attending the show, including BYD and Chery, double their presence at the last Paris car show in 2024 as they face a grueling EV price war and falling sales at home.

Chinese brands have gained share rapidly in Europe in the last three years, while total Chinese exports of hybrids to the EU’s 27-member states tripled to $7.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese customs.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The EU-China deal could hit BYD, Chery, and state-owned SAIC’s MG brand hardest, as between them they accounted for 90 percent of Chinese brand hybrid sales in the EU in the first eight months of 2026, said analysts at Jefferies on Sunday.

Speaking at an event on Sunday evening, Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume welcomed the progress in EU-China talks, adding: “Those who sell here should compete under comparable conditions and create jobs and value here in Europe too.”

The German carmaker’s deliveries fell 14.3 percent in the third quarter, the steepest quarterly drop in four years, dragged down by a further decline in demand in its top market, China, it said on Monday. Deliveries also fell in North America and Western Europe.

*   ![Image 1: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

As part of its bid to regain lost market share in Europe, world No. 4 automaker Stellantis is launching six new models across its European brands at the show and unveiling nine concept cars, a remarkable turnaround after years of maintaining a low-key presence at shows on the continent.

During a high-profile event on Sunday evening, Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa promised attendees they would “witness the reinvention of a European icon,” with an affordable retro electric version of the iconic Citroen 2CV aimed at fending off Chinese competition — which drew huge crowds as the show got underway.

“Our great brands never stand still,” Filosa said.

The company is also learning from the Chinese to go faster, Chief Technology Officer Ned Curic said, outlining plans to build small EVs in Pomigliano, Italy, based on the e-car platform being developed with China’s Leapmotor at Fiat’s plant in Mirafiori, Italy.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

**‘If they drop exports they die’**

Like other Western car shows, Paris had been in decline until Chinese automakers started showing up in Europe in force four years ago.

Alongside the likes of BYD and Chery, this year’s show will feature new Chinese brands like Aito, while state-owned automaker Changan will launch two new brands — Nevo and Avatr.

The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric vehicles in October 2024. The European Commission is also working on legislation that would include “Made in Europe” provisions, mandating minimum local content in EVs to gain access to large parts of the EU’s car market.

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Agreement between France and Germany on the provisions is “imminent,” French President Emmanuel Macron said at the show.

“Preserving this European sovereignty and our capacity to manufacture within Europe is crucial for us,” he said, adding that despite a “difficult” European market, companies on the continent were “innovating, advancing and accelerating.”

Major Chinese automakers have been looking for European production ahead of “Made in Europe,” often in partnership with legacy automakers.

**In July, China’s Geely Auto said it will produce electric SUVs at a Ford Motor factory in Spain.**

Speaking at an event on Sunday evening, Geely Auto CEO Alex Nan emphasized the automaker’s deepening partnership with French automaker Renault and the company’s “commitment to Europe.”

Car sales in China, the world’s largest car market, fell 20 percent in the first half of 2026, increasing the pressure on Chinese automakers to grow sales overseas.

As the US market is effectively closed to China’s auto industry, Europe is the top priority for its automakers.

“If they drop exports in Europe, they die because they can’t make the money elsewhere,” said Francois Roudier, secretary general of the International Organization of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers. REUTERS

title: TSMC to get 6th straight record profit quarter
summary: TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector. Analysts say de
content:
TAIPEI — TSMC, the world’s largest manufacturer of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, will likely report a sixth consecutive quarter of record earnings, driven by booming infrastructure spending in the tech sector.

Analysts say demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong.

That has catapulted Asia’s most valuable company, a key supplier to Nvidia and Apple, to new heights. Its market capitalization is almost double that of South Korean rival Samsung Electronics at around $2.1 trillion.

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

On Thursday, TSMC is expected to report a 65-percent surge in third-quarter net profit to ⁠NT$746.3 billion ($23.4 billion), according to an LSEG SmartEstimate compiled from 16 analysts. SmartEstimates place greater weight on forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate.

**An earnings call at which it will provide fourth-quarter and updated full-year guidance is scheduled for 0600 GMT.**

Any result above NT$706.56 billion would mark the company’s highest-ever quarterly net income, as well as its 11th consecutive quarter of profit growth.

Last Thursday, it posted a 50-percent year-on-year rise in third-quarter revenue, beating market forecasts and hitting a new record high.

In an Oct. 6 report, Morgan Stanley analyst Charlie Chan said he expected TSMC to raise its full-year revenue growth forecast to the low-to-mid 40-percent range from its current guidance of more than 40 percent, driven by strong demand for its 3-nanometer chips.

**Texas expansion prospects**

TSMC is investing $265 billion to ⁠build chip factories in the US state of Arizona, including an additional $100 billion that was unveiled in July.

In September, Reuters reported that TSMC was evaluating a potential investment in Texas. Tesla CEO Elon Musk also said last week that his companies would build and operate the Terafab AI chip complex, with TSMC potentially subleasing a part of it.

**Analysts expect TSMC to address questions about its potential expansion plans in Texas.**

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

In his report, Chan ⁠said an expansion in Texas could become necessary given growing customer demand and limited space at TSMC’s Arizona site in five years’ time.

Phelix Lee, senior equity analyst at Morningstar, however, saw limited urgency for TSMC to expand into Texas, given that some of its planned fabs in ⁠Arizona have yet to be built.

“Texas is a good location for a 2030s or 2040s expansion grand plan, given its long history of semiconductor ecosystem and talent pool,” Lee said. “It may be a dangling carrot to preempt potential US trade and other policies.”

On ⁠its July earnings call, the company raised its capex forecast for this year to between $60 billion and $64 billion from a previous prediction at the high end of $52 billion to $56 billion.

# France high school students plan new protests

[![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/102_1657587153.jpg)![Image 21: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/102_1657587153.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/agence-france-presse "author image")

[By Agence France-Presse](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/agence-france-presse "Agence France-Presse")

 October 13, 2026

 10

[Resize](https://manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/world/americas-emea/france-high-school-students-plan-new-protests/2443623)

*   ![Image 22: font icon small](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-small.svg)Small

**PARIS** —France’s high school students on Monday begin a new stage of their campaign for improved conditions, hoping to maintain the momentum with a fresh wave of demonstrations.

The new protests, scheduled for Tuesday, could be a turning point in the movement, launched in mid-September, which the government hopes is already winding down.

On Friday, the government noted a dramatic drop in the number of blockades and meetings outside the country’s lycées, where students -- most between 15 and 18 -- complete their high school education.

*   [Stolen Renoir paintings found behind wall in France](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/world/americas-emea/stolen-renoir-paintings-found-behind-wall-in-france/2443938)

More than 96 percent were opening Friday, said the education ministry.

The authorities are all the more keen to see the student protests end given that online activists have called for demonstrations next Saturday to protest the cost of living.

For President Emmanuel Macron’s administration, that brings back troubling memories of the grassroots Yellow Vest movement.

Their protests, launched in 2018 over a planned fuel tax rise, saw massive demonstrations and clashes between police and protesters that shook the presidency during Macron’s first term in office.

## **Concessions**

The government is still counting the cost of the high school protests.

A government source told journalists last week that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations was “at least 30 million euros”.

On Friday, the justice ministry said more than 6,800 people had been detained since the demonstrations started, 86 percent of them minors.

After clashes between some protesters and riot police left some students severely injured, sparking criticism of police tactics, the government suspended the use of stun grenades that cost one student his hand.

Police are investigating 18 alleged cases of misconduct within their ranks.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Sunday promised to make changes to the planned budget 2027 to respond to some demands set out in an online platform the government set up to gather students’ views.

## **‘Crumbs’**

The student organizations behind the protests are yet to be convinced.

title: The plight of our farmers and our food insecurity
summary: FILIPINOS consume 17 million to 18 million metric tons of rice annually. On the supply side, Filipino rice farmers produce only 12 million to 13 million metric tons of rice from a mere 6 percent of land area of the entire country devoted to
content:
FILIPINOS consume 17 million to 18 million metric tons of rice annually. On the supply side, Filipino rice farmers produce only 12 million to 13 million metric tons of rice from a mere 6 percent of land area of the entire country devoted to rice farming. We are one of the top rice-consuming countries in the world. This small percentage of land area for rice farming is under pressure to be reduced further to a smaller percentage as urbanization sprawls into the rural areas. The demand for land for renewable energy, particularly solar power plants, aggravates the shrinking of these rice fields.

Basic economics will tell us that this kind of shortage in supply and high demand in rice should translate to higher income for our rice farmers. However, our rice farmers continue to be the poorest among our citizens. Farming has become so discredited among the next generation that even farmers themselves would not encourage their children to be farmers. At present, the average age of a Filipino farmer is 56 years old. On the other hand, the median age of Filipinos is 27 years old. This puts the difference between the average age of Filipino farmer to the median of the population at 30 years old. The Philippines has one of the youngest populations in the world, albeit there are signs of aging. But it also has one of the oldest farmers’ populations. Policy makers are concerned about food security as less Filipinos engage in farming, particularly the back-breaking rice farming. The growing scarcity of farmers in the rural areas is felt not only with the increasing labor cost, but with the extreme difficulty of finding warm bodies to help till the land and retaining them. Data shows that our food security is going towards import dependency. This is not security at all as we depend on other countries to feed our population.

*   [Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

[![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256392.jpeg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256392.jpeg)

Who would like to be a farmer in the Philippines if over generations, farmers remained and continue to wallow in the miseries of penury and hard labor? Add to this the losses incurred in the damaging effects of climate change such as El Niño and La Niña, the vicious and merciless wrath of pestilence such as the African swine fever and avian flu that take away the other sources of farmers in tending livestock and animals. No wonder our farmers are being pushed to the edge of despair, a lot of whom has already fallen into.

Since I engaged in rice-farming and livestock farming myself, I experienced these losses firsthand. Fortunately, I have a stable source of income from my professional employment. This allows me to absorb the losses as they happen. But for most poor farmers, an occurrence of one of these disasters will mean terrible hunger and radical disruption of their family’s lives such that children will have to stop going to school and sick members of family will be left without medical care and tragically left to the mercies of benefactors without which a family will lose such precious life of a loved one.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

When I started rice farming in 2023, the cost of rice production was P15 per kilogram. When harvest time came, rice traders offered to buy it at a mere P9 per kg. As I had no storage facility nor drying and milling machines, I was thinking of selling at a loss so I could dispose of the palay grains to avoid the God-given bountiful harvest rotting unnecessarily. Thus, it was such welcome news to hear Sen. Kiko Pangilinan advocating fiercely for the implementation of the Sagip Saka Act, which he so painstakingly worked on to be passed into law in 2019. Upon returning to the Senate floor, he put to task the government agencies, specifically the Department of Agriculture (DA), on the law’s implementation. His efforts in compelling government agencies to buy locally produced rice raised the buying price of palay to between P20 to 23 per kg.

One major reason also for the ridiculous pricing of rice is the lack of storage, grain drying equipment and milling facilities for farmers. With these facilities inaccessible, the traders force the farmers to sell to them even at a loss whenever harvest time comes. This explains why palay was priced at an extremely low price of P9 per kg while milled rice is priced at a high price of P55 per kg. It would truly help the farmers if they could mill their harvest on their own and sell the milled rice directly to the market.

*   ![Image 2: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Our leaders in the Department of Agriculture can devote a substantial chunk of the budget to providing these agricultural equipment, storage and drying facilities to the farmers instead of allocating budget for more farm-to-market roads which since my childhood have been getting copious budget allocations. Yet most of these farm-to-market roads earned the moniker of being roads coming from the farm and not leading to the market but to the politician’s private resort, or the project funds going into the politicians’ pockets. This is just one of the many reforms that must be done, including better enforcement of laws against the illegal smuggling of rice into the country. Until then, our farmers remain poor and our country remains to be food-insecure.

title: The not so lost years
summary: **_First of two parts_** THERE is a dearth of detail on the life of the Brains of the Katipunan Emilio Jacinto after his leader, friend and mentor Andres Bonifacio’s death on May 10, 1897. But he left papers that give us an idea of the life
content:
**_First of two parts_**

THERE is a dearth of detail on the life of the Brains of the Katipunan Emilio Jacinto after his leader, friend and mentor Andres Bonifacio’s death on May 10, 1897. But he left papers that give us an idea of the life he led of continued service to the people while apparently pursuing personal happiness.

From his personal papers we found the he was eventually stationed in Santa Cruz, Laguna, where he produced two sets of rules in his own handwriting that may appear odd. One establishes a government in the “Hukuman ng Silangan” (Eastern Area) which places itself under the leadership of the Provisional Constitution of the Philippine Republic attested to at Biak-na-Bato on Nov. 1, 1897. Now this government was of course led by Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo, or Emiliong Matanda (Older Emilio, as opposed to Jacinto, Emiliong Bata or Younger Emilio), the one who approved the sentence of death on Bonifacio. How does this paper tell us that Jacinto submitted himself to Aguinaldo and formed a branch of the latter’s government?

*   [Paper is not proof](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/13/opinion/columns/paper-is-not-proof/2443919)

The other set of rules talked about establishing a People’s Association for Commerce in Santa Cruz, Laguna, where they could put forward agricultural, industrial and commercial interests that could sustain the needs of the people. In the early biographies, details and testimonies are scant about these two movements Jacinto was trying to build, but we may have some clues.

It can be said that he continued to have some fighting men under his command, but whether or not he was under the direct command of or in contact with Aguinaldo is something that cannot be proven in the present. What can be ascertained was that in mid-1897, not Feb. 27, 1898 as some secondary sources say, he was traveling on horseback at night with 20 of his men traversing the fields and the woods when members of the elite light infantry unit of the Spanish colonial army called Cazadores saw them. They clashed and because of the sound of gunfire the horses panicked. Jacinto fell from his horse, was hit by a bullet which shattered the bones of his foot.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

He hid in the mud until the morning when he decided to let himself be carried away by the river, and by the afternoon, tired, hungry and suffering pain because of his wounds, he began crying for help. An old man saw him and went to the town center to tell a Spanish lieutenant, who then went out to get him and took him to the convent of Magdalena. They preserved a corner near the stairs of the convent where he was supposedly placed when they arrived.

To avoid detection as he was being interrogated, he produced a cedula or a tax certificate of an undercover he previously killed, Florentino Reyes. He made up a story that he was an escaped captive of the “insurrectionists” as he called them. Because of this, a doctor was sent to him to check him. Fortunately, the initial plan to sever his foot was averted.

While recovering, according to the historian Jim Richardson, Jacinto was in prison in Santa Cruz, Laguna, in a Dec. 21, 1897 report by agent Tito David found in the spy documents of the Cuerpo de Vigilancia, “our forces treated him very well.” He was given a desk job and even lived at the prison. Despite this, he wrote two poems in Spanish “A la Patria,” where he wrote that his “soul’s vehement desire” was to see the land “without the Spanish yoke” (el yugo español). “To relieve, o Patria, your suffering, your sorrows,” he proclaims, “I would gladly give all the blood in my veins....” He signed it with one his pen names, Dimas Ilaw (he who cannot be blinded) followed by his real initials “E.J., 3 October 1897. Sta. Cruz – Laguna – (C.P.),” the C.P. meaning Cárcel Publica or Public Jail. In another poem, “A mi querida madre,” he wrote, “for in my chest a volcano blazed when I saw my Motherland wounded and enslaved, and when I saw her sorrow, I took up arms.” Talk about being careless.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

After some time, Jacinto left the jail house. And when he did, the Spaniards found out right away that they had been duped. He went into hiding in Manila but returned to Laguna after some time. As for the economic society, apparently he became a successful businessman in Laguna, a meat merchant and found time to marry someone. More on this next week. As we can see, Jacinto was an idealist, but when needed, we can also see some sense of practicality and pragmatism in his actions.

title: PH warned of repeated Chinese deployments
summary: THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and
content:
THE repeated deployment of a Chinese maritime militia vessel accompanied by dozens of small boats near Kota Island raises concerns over China's continuing efforts to assert its claims in the West Philippine Sea, national security expert and civil society leader Jose Antonio Goitia said.

The same Chinese Maritime Militia Vessel (CMMV) 9622 returned to the waters near the Philippine-held island on Oct. 9 with 22 sampans, just 11 days after it was reported in the area with 24 similar boats.

The latest incident involved an alleged attempt by the Chinese vessel to assert control over the area and order Filipino personnel to leave as Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel, supported by the Philippine Marine Corps and Philippine Navy, moved to address the Chinese presence.

*   [Sandiganbayan suspends Jinggoy anew over floor control mess](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/news/sandiganbayan-suspends-jinggoy-anew-over-floor-control-mess/2443890)

Goitia said Filipino defenders had the right to remain in Philippine waters and carry out their duties despite the Chinese vessel's reported demand.

“Our Coast Guard, Marines, and Navy have every right to perform their lawful duties in Philippine waters. No foreign vessel can simply order them to leave. They were there to protect our interests, and they had every reason to stay,” he said.

According to the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS), one of the 22 sampans approached within about 250 meters of Kota Island's shoreline.

The Chinese mothership maneuvered around and encircled Philippine boats, claimed the area as Chinese territory and directed the Filipino team to leave.

The PCG and NTF-WPS said the coordinated Philippine response resulted in all the Chinese vessels leaving the island's territorial sea.

The task force also accused the Chinese boats of engaging in unauthorized fishing and dumping waste at sea.

The return of CMMV 9622 so soon after its previous deployment highlights the recurring presence of Chinese maritime militia vessels and small boats near Philippine-held features in the disputed South China Sea.

Kota Island, also known as Loaita Island, is part of the Kalayaan Island Group in Palawan. Its territorial sea falls under Philippine sovereignty.

The NTF-WPS said the reported activities violated Philippine laws, including Republic Act 12064, or the Philippine Maritime Zones Act, and Republic Act 8550, or the Philippine Fisheries Code, as amended by Republic Act 10654.

China claims most of the South China Sea, including areas disputed by the Philippines.

A 2016 arbitral ruling under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea rejected the legal basis of China's expansive historic-rights claim insofar as it exceeds the maritime rights allowed under the convention. Beijing rejected the ruling.

title: Prosecutors to review NBI-flagged properties
summary: HOUSE prosecutors will review the National Bureau of Investigation’s (NBI) findings on properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family to determine whether the assets were included in the prosecution’s computation of P817.87
content:
HOUSE prosecutors will review the National Bureau of Investigation’s (NBI) findings on properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family to determine whether the assets were included in the prosecution’s computation of P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth.

Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo sought the review on Monday after the NBI presented its initial assessment of properties linked to Duterte and Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte, citing discrepancies between declared acquisition costs in their statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs) and the bureau’s preliminary estimates.

“Would you later look into this to counter-check whether the NBI’s investigation is correct?” Tulfo asked House prosecutor Chel Diokno during the 38th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial.

*   [Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

“Sure, we will do that, your honor,” Diokno replied.

Tulfo showed financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera materials from the NBI’s press briefing earlier that day and asked whether the properties had been included in his assessment of Duterte’s finances.

Cabrera said he could not confirm this without examining the relevant documents, including transfer certificates of title (TCTs), property addresses and land areas.

Tulfo specifically asked about an agricultural property in Barangay Santo Niño, Balac, on the Island Garden City of Samal (Igacos), reportedly declared at an acquisition cost of P200,000.

Asked whether two properties presented by the NBI were included in the approximately P817 million in alleged unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte, Cabrera said he was unsure.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

“I am not sure whether those are included,” he said, adding that the properties might already have been covered by Duterte’s declarations.

Cabrera also said that one property appeared valuable because it had two swimming pools, but stressed that its appearance alone was insufficient to determine whether it had been included in his computation.

Diokno told the impeachment court that the prosecution had copies of Duterte’s SALNs detailing her declared real properties but had not yet reviewed the NBI presentation.

Tulfo asked the prosecution to obtain the relevant documents and compare them with Cabrera’s findings.

*   ![Image 2: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

**‘Numbers don’t lie’**

Separately, Diokno defended the prosecution’s reliance on financial records, saying the unexplained wealth allegations ultimately concern transparency and accountability in public office.

Responding to Senator-Judge Lito Lapid, who asked what the public should take away from the witnesses and documents presented during the trial, Diokno said an honest public official should have nothing to hide.

“It is easy to pretend to be an ordinary person who eats at a neighborhood eatery, but under Article II on unexplained wealth, that’s where the truth comes out. The numbers do not lie,” Diokno said.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Lapid raised the question following testimony on the P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

Diokno said the central issue under Article II, which accuses Duterte of unexplained wealth, was straightforward.

“When we look at the heart of Article II, I think it comes down to this: an honest public official has nothing to hide,” he said.

He said the case hinged not on witness testimony alone but on financial records from banks, the Anti-Money Laundering Council, the Bureau of Internal Revenue and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

“What matters here is not the witnesses themselves, but the documents and the numbers,” Diokno said.

“These bank documents, for example, did not pass through the hands of the prosecution. The banks sent them directly to this court. So we can say that these are independent facts that anyone can verify,” he added.

Diokno said the proceedings were not simply about Duterte as a person but also about public trust, leadership and accountability.

“This case is really not about Vice President Sara Duterte as a person. To me, it is about the trust the people have placed in her,” Diokno said.

“It is not about her as a person, but about leadership — whether she has governed properly and, more importantly, whether a high-ranking public official has the integrity and fitness to continue serving in office,” he added.

Lapid’s questions followed testimony from Cabrera, who presented a computation of P817,874,867 in allegedly undeclared wealth involving Duterte and Carpio from 2022 to 2025.

The total covered allegedly undeclared cash, personal and real properties, income attributed to the couple, and amounts computed from several corporate entities.

The highest annual figure was recorded in 2024 at P264,217,123, followed by P195,692,505 in 2025, P190,628,012 in 2022 and P167,337,227 in 2023.

Cabrera identified P207,696,933 in allegedly undeclared cash over the four-year period: P60,214,776 in 2022, P80,701,151 in 2023, P23,169,077 in 2024 and P43,611,929 in 2025.

He also identified P143,497,177 in other allegedly undeclared personal and real properties, net of deductions. The annual figures were P76,147,730 in 2022, P3,934,560 in 2023, P52,016,994 in 2024 and P11,397,893 in 2025.

The analysis also calculated P111,852,349 in allegedly undeclared income attributed to the couple, broken down into P50,474,511 in 2022, P12,198,235 in 2023, P28,030,203 in 2024 and P21,149,400 in 2025.

For Cale88 Foods Corp. and Metro City Chow, Cabrera computed P142,198,690 in allegedly undeclared income. The annual figures were P3,790,995 in 2022, P14,788,989 in 2023, P86,944,369 in 2024 and P36,674,337 in 2025.

For GenCorp Industries Inc., the computed amount reached P212,629,718 from 2023 to 2025: P55,714,292 in 2023, P74,056,480 in 2024 and P82,858,946 in 2025. No amount was recorded for 2022 under this category.

Cabrera, a lawyer and certified public accountant with more than three decades of experience in accounting, taxation, law and financial forensics, has defended the computation before the impeachment court.

CATHERINE VALENTE

title: 3 Filipinos in ICU after Riyadh airport attack
summary: THREE of four Filipinos injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia remained in intensive care on Monday, with at least one in critical condition, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Monday. DM
content:
THREE of four Filipinos injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia remained in intensive care on Monday, with at least one in critical condition, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Monday.

DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said the fourth injured Filipino had been discharged from the hospital but would continue to receive assistance.

“He had some problems in his lumbar area, so this will be continually monitored,” Cacdac said during a briefing on Oct. 12. “He had some trauma burns, but again, he is healthy enough to be released from hospital.” Two of the injured Filipinos worked at the airport, while the other two were passengers. They were two men and two women.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

Cacdac said the government had reached out to the families of the injured Filipinos following the incident.

“We have also reached out per directive of the president to reach out to their families to help the families,” he said.
