Meanwhile, Philippine officials were assisting Filipinos affected by flight cancellations and the temporary closure of Riyadh airport.

Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) Administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan reported that 30 people, including overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) and dependents, were stranded in Riyadh.

Of the 30, 20 were staying in hotels sponsored by the DMW and OWWA, while seven had been picked up by relatives. Two seafarers in transit were staying at an airline-sponsored hotel, and one person had been picked up by an employer.

*   ![Image 1: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

Another 94 OFWs whose flights to Riyadh were diverted to Jeddah were receiving assistance from the Philippine labor office there while awaiting the resumption of flights.

“Currently, they are billeted and they’re being assisted in Jeddah awaiting for the resumption of flights,” Cacdac said.

The government was providing temporary accommodation, food, transportation assistance and help with flight rebooking.

In Manila, 37 OFWs sought assistance following flight cancellations, including temporary accommodation and transportation to their homes in Metro Manila and the provinces. Three remained in hotels as of the briefing.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

One other Filipino was reported stranded at Dammam International Airport in eastern Saudi Arabia after a flight cancellation. Officials said assistance was being provided.

Despite the attacks, the DMW said there is no deployment ban in place for Saudi Arabia as it monitors security developments and flight disruptions in the kingdom.

“At this stage, no deployment ban to Saudi,” Cacdac said on Monday.

Cacdac said the department was coordinating with the Department of Foreign Affairs and the Department of National Defense to assess the political and security situation.

*   ![Image 3: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

He noted that economic activity in Saudi Arabia continued despite the recent attacks and said that the government would remain in contact with its counterparts as developments unfolded.

**Tested**

Saudi Arabia’s energy minister acknowledged on Monday that the kingdom’s infrastructure and resilience had been tested, as he vowed a firm response following a wave of deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

The Houthi attacks over the weekend marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Saudi Arabia has long supported the internationally recognized government.

On Sunday, a strike hit Riyadh’s international airport, killing one person, just hours after another Houthi-claimed on the site killed 13 people and left hundreds of others wounded, forcing authorities to suspend operations there.

The attacks on Saudi Arabia, a regional powerhouse and the world’s top oil exporter which has poured billions of dollars into its military, were the deadliest to hit the kingdom in a decade.

“For Saudi Arabia, these circumstances have tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience. They have also tested decisions made long before present crises, because resilience is built before crises begin,” Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said.

“Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” he told a high-profile conference in Riyadh. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

The airport was not the only one in the country to be targeted: the civil aviation authority also reported another on Dammam airport in the east.

The Saudi-led coalition said Monday it had also “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.

title: Unexplained wealth of VP could hit P1.5B
summary: VICE President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, could have up to P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025, nearly double the prosecution’s conservative estimate of P817.87 million, financial forensic analyst
content:
VICE President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, could have up to P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025, nearly double the prosecution’s conservative estimate of P817.87 million, financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera told the Senate impeachment court on Monday.

Testifying on Day 38 of Duterte’s impeachment trial, Cabrera confirmed the maximum estimate after Senate President and Presiding Officer Francis Escudero sought clarification on the potential total, excluding double-counting of assets.

“I’ll be more specific, sir. P1.5 billion would be the maximum estimate of the undeclared wealth of the respondents from 2022 to 2025, without any double booking?” Escudero asked.

*   [Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

“Yes,” Cabrera replied.

“The amounts vary each year, and when you add them all up, that would be the ceiling,” Escudero said, explaining that the amounts varied by year and would reach that ceiling when added together.

“That’s correct,” Cabrera said.

Escudero then asked Cabrera how high the estimate could go if the prosecution’s financial analysis did not rely on conservative assumptions.

Cabrera explained that his team had deliberately used conservative figures in computing the couple’s alleged unexplained wealth.

*   ![Image 1: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Escudero also pointed out that deducting assets attributed to MetroChow, Cale88 and GenCorp from the P817-million total in undeclared assets would still leave P463.046 million in alleged unexplained wealth.

The deductions included P142.198 million attributed to Cale88 and P212 million in GenCorp assets, based on the figures cited during the proceedings.

The higher estimate could reach P1.5 billion if confidential funds, discrepancies reflected in Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) reports and less conservative figures for GenCorp were factored into the computation, Cabrera said.

The estimates cover the period from 2022 to 2025 and are based on the documents and assumptions discussed during the proceedings.

*   ![Image 2: Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1256500.png?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala suffers worst loss of 2026 season, falls to world No. 217 Shi](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-suffers-worst-loss-of-2026-season-falls-to-world-no-217-shi/2443990)

**Unexplained inflows**

A banana chip exporter linked to Vice President Duterte’s husband reported persistent losses despite substantial cash inflows, Cabrera testified.

Another company also linked to the vice president had P1 billion in alleged undeclared inflows, he said.

Cabrera flagged financial discrepancies involving the two companies, Cale88 Foods Corp. and GenCorp Industries Inc., as senators scrutinized their transactions, potential tax liabilities and ownership structures.

*   ![Image 3: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Cabrera also defended his estimate of P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband from 2022 to 2025, while acknowledging that P211 million of the total depended on an assumption about Duterte’s ownership stake in GenCorp.

During his interjection, Senator-Judge and Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian questioned Cabrera about P1 billion in alleged undeclared inflows recorded by GenCorp from 2022 to 2025.

Cabrera said the funds were not reflected in the company’s balance sheet, income statement or income tax returns, based on his analysis.

Asked whether the money could have come from loans, advances or pass-through transactions rather than sales, Cabrera said this was unlikely because such transactions should also have been recorded as payables.

Using a 25-percent tax rate, he estimated GenCorp’s potential tax liability at P250 million.

He agreed that the circumstances could warrant examining whether the corporate veil could be pierced, potentially extending liability to shareholders if the legal requirements were met.

Cabrera acknowledged that he had not prepared specific court rulings involving the piercing of the corporate veil in cases of unpaid taxes but promised to submit a relevant case reference to the Senate.

**Discrepancies noted**

He also questioned discrepancies between GenCorp’s general information sheet (GIS) and Duterte’s statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN). Duterte’s name was reportedly absent from the company’s GIS, although GenCorp appeared in her SALN.

Cabrera said he gave greater weight to the SALN because it is signed under oath. He also questioned whether GenCorp’s corporate disclosures adequately identified its ultimate beneficial owner under Securities and Exchange Commission rules.

He said his team used a 20-percent ownership stake for Duterte as a conservative assumption, based partly on her SALN declaration and previous business relationships.

He acknowledged that the actual percentage could be lower or higher and required verification.

Cabrera previously testified that GenCorp’s revenue rose from about P28 million in 2021 to more than P520 million in 2025, despite reported paid-in capital of only P1.25 million.

He said the company’s financial statements did not clearly explain the sources of funds supporting its growth and acquisitions.

Cale88 Foods Corp., a banana chip exporter linked to Carpio, also came under scrutiny over its financial statements and substantial cash movements.

Questioned by Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo, Cabrera said a comparison with five or six similarly sized export companies revealed differences in assets, inventories and profitability.

He pointed to the absence of recorded accounts payable, accounts receivable and raw-material or work-in-process inventories despite Cale88’s purported manufacturing and export operations.

“There are really many things that are not in the proper place in that financial statement,” Cabrera said.

He added that the company continued to report losses despite substantial amounts moving through its accounts.

Cabrera likened the transactions to a revolving door, with money flowing in and quickly going out without an apparent contribution to the company’s operations. He cautioned that this pattern warranted scrutiny but did not, by itself, establish wrongdoing.

Cale88 was also flagged for about P35 million in alleged undeclared inflows. Cabrera estimated a potential tax liability of P5 million to P6 million based on the documents his team reviewed.

The AMLC had reported about P1.25 billion in covered and suspicious transactions involving Cale88 from 2022 to 2025, including P319.33 million in remittances originating from China and Hong Kong, according to testimony presented during the proceedings.

Gatchalian separately questioned the discrepancy between an AMLC report indicating about P700 million in total inflows and Cabrera’s calculation of about P247 million in bank inflows.

Cabrera said the difference could partly reflect duplicate tagging when funds entered foreign-currency accounts and were subsequently converted into pesos or transferred elsewhere. He said his team attempted to eliminate duplicate transactions and adopted a conservative approach.

Senator-Judge Bam Aquino pressed Cabrera to distinguish findings based on documentary records from estimates dependent on assumptions about corporate ownership and the attribution of undeclared income.

The discussion centered on Table 39 of Cabrera’s report, which covered undeclared cash balances, personal properties and investments, unexplained outflows, and income attributed to companies.

Cabrera acknowledged that the 20-percent ownership interest attributed to Duterte in GenCorp was an assumption rather than a figure established by the corporate records he examined.

Aquino stressed that the actual ownership percentage could differ and that the final estimate should be determined by the evidence.

After excluding about P211 million associated with the GenCorp ownership assumption, Cabrera said the remaining estimate was about P606 million based on the records examined.

Aquino cautioned against introducing other allegations to offset reductions in the total, emphasizing that each component of the calculation should stand on its own evidentiary basis.

Cabrera said his analysis also considered whether undeclared corporate income could be attributed to beneficial owners under the legal doctrine of piercing the corporate veil. He acknowledged that the senator-judges would have to assess whether the doctrine applied.

During cross-examination, defense counsel Kristine Ferrer questioned Cabrera’s methodology, his access to corporate records and the absence of direct input from Duterte and Carpio.

Cabrera acknowledged that he had not received documents directly from the couple for his forensic accounting review.

He said his team examined materials submitted in connection with Duterte’s responses to the House of Representatives and the Senate but found no documents from the couple that could be used in the analysis.

“Had there been, I would have used [them],” Cabrera said.

Ferrer also questioned findings concerning alleged advances to Cale88, including P8.7 million attributed to Carpio in 2022, noting that Cabrera had not examined the company’s books of accounts.

Cabrera confirmed that his analysis attributed a 20-percent capital interest in Cale88 to Duterte based on documents examined by the prosecution.

He also acknowledged that time constraints prevented his team from reviewing all the bank documents provided and said the AMLC report was not used to determine Duterte’s net assets.

Meanwhile, Senator-Judge Francis Pangilinan questioned P41 million in cash withdrawals made by Carpio on Aug. 6, 2024, six days after drug-related charges were filed against him in connection with the alleged magnetic lifter incident.

Pangilinan said Duterte had resigned as Education secretary on July 19, 2024, while the charges against Carpio were filed on July 30.

According to Cabrera’s report, Carpio withdrew the money within about one hour and 13 minutes.

“I became curious about what happened on Aug. 6, or where they were at the time,” Pangilinan said.

Cabrera confirmed that the accounts belonged to Carpio and described the sequence of transactions as unusual, noting that withdrawals resumed immediately after a lunch break.

He cautioned, however, that the timing and amount of the withdrawals did not establish that the transactions were unlawful.

Pangilinan also questioned the reported transfer of Carpio’s shares in Cale88 to Pikimong Pikimong Philippines Corp. in 2025.

Cabrera said his team continued to attribute the shares to Carpio because it found no documentation establishing that the transfer had taken place.

title: Aston Martin DBX GT puts luxury first
summary: ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turb
content:
ASTON Martin has expanded its DBX lineup with the new DBX GT, a more comfort-focused version of its high-performance SUV that places greater emphasis on refinement, craftsmanship, and daily usability while retaining the same 727PS twin-turbo V8 used in the DBX S.

The DBX GT is aimed at buyers who want a quieter and more understated interpretation of the brand’s SUV. Aston Martin says the model combines improved ride comfort, lower cabin noise, and a more luxurious interior with the same performance capability expected from the DBX range.

“DBX GT is aimed at customers who prefer assured elegance over sporting aggression and demand a higher degree of luxury,” Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark said.

“By refining the visual drama and elevating the interior with new elements of craftsmanship, the DBX GT delivers a true ultra-luxury experience; one which comes with no sacrifice in performance,” he added.

Exterior changes are intended to give the DBX GT a more restrained appearance than the sportier DBX S. The most noticeable update is a new double-vane grille, offered in bright or dark finishes, with the split metal vanes extending toward the outer vents and daytime running lights.

The SUV also receives a new two-piece metal side strake with polished and satin finishes inspired by traditional watchmaking. The lower front bumper, side sills, and rear diffuser are painted in body color as standard, while new quad exhaust finishers are arranged horizontally at the rear.

*   ![Image 7: More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/12/1255130.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

A new 22-inch forged wheel with a Satin Titanium diamond-turned finish is standard, paired with all-season tires selected to improve ride comfort and reduce road noise. Buyers can also choose an optional 23-inch wheel and tire package.

Inside, Aston Martin has redesigned both the front and rear seats with additional cushioning, revised bolsters, and new comfort contours.

A 10-mm memory foam layer has been added to the seat cushions, while the rear cabin now features two individually sculpted seating positions designed to provide greater lateral support without sacrificing five-seat capacity.

The DBX GT also comes with a panoramic glass roof, semi-aniline leather, deep-pile floor mats, and GT-specific upholstery combinations. Aston Martin says each front seat uses 691 meters of thread, 3,297 perforation holes, and required more than four and a half hours of craftsmanship to complete.

*   ![Image 8: Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1255072.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Who should pay capital gains tax?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/legal-advice/who-should-pay-capital-gains-tax/2443313)

The cabin also receives anodized metal switchgear and a new drive-mode controller, while additional sound-deadening materials, improved body sealing, and acoustic laminated rear side glass have been used to reduce outside noise. Aston Martin claims a 13-percent improvement in its Articulation Index measure, which evaluates how easily occupants can hold a conversation while the vehicle is moving.

Performance

remains unchanged

Despite the stronger focus on refinement, performance remains unchanged from the DBX S.

*   ![Image 9: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

The 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 produces 727 PS and 900 Newton-meters (Nm) of torque, using turbocharger technology shared with the Valhalla supercar. Aston Martin claims a 0-60 mph time of 3.1 seconds and a top speed of 193 mph, or about 311 kph.

Stopping power comes from carbon-ceramic brakes measuring 420 mm at the front and 390 mm at the rear. The DBX GT also uses the faster steering ratio from the DBX S, while retaining a 12-meter turning circle.

The suspension receives its own GT-specific calibration, including revised damper settings and new internal damper valves designed to better filter small, high-frequency road imperfections. Spring behavior also changes according to the selected drive mode to balance ride comfort with body control and steering response.

Aston Martin has also recalibrated the throttle and nine-speed wet-clutch automatic transmission for smoother and more progressive responses in everyday driving. A revised transmission mount and additional longitudinal dampers between the body and rear subframe are intended to improve structural refinement over rough roads and large suspension movements.

The exhaust system also receives a dedicated GT tune. In GT mode, the system is calibrated for quieter progress, while Sport and Sport+ modes restore a more aggressive exhaust note.

“The challenge with DBX GT was achieving meaningful improvements in comfort and refinement in everyday use cases, but keeping the same class-leading reserves of performance and handling we have achieved with the DBX S,” Aston Martin Chief Technology Officer Ian Hoban said.

The DBX GT joins the DBX range as its most comfort-oriented and understated variant while retaining the same headline performance figures as the DBX S.

First deliveries are scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: U.S. restrictions on Chinese drones are hurting cash-strapped police departments
summary: For hours, bullets tore through the home, hitting neighboring houses and cars. Inside, a man wanted by police for allegedly killing his ex-girlfriend was holed up with his new girlfriend. As the SWAT team prepared to enter, Kevin Fennessy w
content:
For hours, bullets tore through the home, hitting neighboring houses and cars.

Inside, a man wanted by police for allegedly killing his ex-girlfriend was holed up with his new girlfriend.

As the SWAT team prepared to enter, Kevin Fennessy with the Ocean County Sheriff's Office tried something new first. He sent in a tiny assistant: a small drone equipped with a camera.

From a safe position outside, Fennessy slowly piloted the device through a blasted-in window, while he and other officers watched on a monitor. The video, viewed by NPR, showed hallway walls and furniture riddled with bullet holes.

As it entered a back bedroom where the couple had holed up, footage showed the man's body on the floor. He had killed himself. With the drone still hovering above the macabre scene, police deployed two flash bangs into the room. The woman rushed out and surrendered.

The incident, which happened about three years ago, sticks in Fennessy's mind when he considers the value of his department's drone program, which he heads.

"No one's hurt. Everyone's safe," Fennessy says. "Forty-one times they shot out the house at us. But at the end of the day, we were able to clear the house."

Chief Warrant Officer Kevin Fennessy lifts an Ocean County Sheriff's Office DJI Matrice 300 RTK drone out of the custom-built bed of a department SUV at Robert J. Miller Airpark on Sept. 4.  (Albert Yee for NPR)

New Jersey's Ocean County Sheriff's Office is one of an estimated 6,000 law enforcement agencies across the country that now have drones, used for search and rescue, fire and traffic crash investigations, and tactical response, according to the Law Enforcement Drone Association. It's an organization that advises, trains and certifies police across the country on their drone programs.

Ocean County's entire fleet is from DJI, a Chinese manufacturer of drones. LEDA estimates that about 80% to 90% of law enforcement agencies flying drones use DJI devices. China controls a vast majority of the global drone market, and it's the dominant source for the minerals and raw materials needed to build them, [researchers say.](https://cepa.org/article/reality-check-breaking-free-from-chinas-drone-ecosystem-is-harder-than-you-think/)

The Trump administration wants that to end. It's made several moves [to bolster U.S. drone makers](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/06/unleashing-american-drone-dominance/), including by banning many new foreign-made drones from entering the American market. Most recently, his administration [announced tariffs](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2026/08/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-bolsters-national-security-and-strengthens-u-s-supply-chains-by-imposing-tariffs-on-drones-and-their-parts-and-components/) of 15% to 100% on some foreign-made drones, making it much more expensive for agencies to buy these devices.

Critics of these moves say the American drone industry is not yet able to keep up with demand, nor can it match the high-quality and low-cost drones made in China. Law enforcement agencies that rely on these drones are getting caught up in the fight as the federal government pushes back on the dominance of Chinese technology.

"We're seeing lives being saved with the use of this technology," says Jon Beal, head of LEDA. He says the organization supports efforts to boost the American drone industry, but that reducing access to Chinese drones is not a good solution.

"What that's going to do is cancel out perfectly viable drone programs that are doing great work out there," he says. "We don't want to cut off our nose to spite our face."

### **How much does this cost?**

Agencies pay for drone programs in various ways, including with grants and fundraising. The Ocean County Sheriff's Office uses profits from asset forfeiture and through their municipal operating budget to cover their fleet of 25 drones.

"We have to be cost-effective. And to do that, get the best product that's available to us," Ocean County Sheriff Michael Mastronardy says.

A Seabob rescue vehicle inside the garage of the Seaside Heights Volunteer Fire Department Ocean Rescue office in Seaside Heights, N.J. This vehicle propels rescue swimmers during water rescues. The department is looking into aerial drones equipped with flotation devices and unmanned water drones like the ones the Ocean County Sheriff's Office uses to aid in water rescue.  (Albert Yee for NPR)

For them, that meant turning to DJI drones.

In the parking lot of the Ocean County Sheriff's Office in early August, Fennessy breaks down the costs of the equipment one of his deputies carries in his vehicle.

A DJI Matrice 300 RTK: $13,699

A set of two batteries: $1,400

A camera with infrared thermal imaging: $11,499

A (very fancy) remote controller: $1,600

A RESTUBE Automatic, a flotation device that can be dropped into water for rescues by the drone: $130.99

A payload release system: $1,099

That comes to a total of $29,427.99

Fennessy acknowledges this is a huge investment, but says the devices are well-used and well worth it — especially in the summertime, when Ocean County's population nearly doubles. Major events constantly pose a policing challenge for the department, and they've found that drones have helped keep an eye on big crowds.

In July, the department used a drone [to drop flotation devices](https://6abc.com/post/ocean-county-sheriffs-department-uses-drone-save-swimmers-distress/19553638/) to two swimmers in distress, and rescuers were able to bring them to shore.

Fennessy has become passionate about drones professionally and as a hobbyist. He's done a lot of research, including into the American drone market. "All their stuff is good," he says. "I've flown almost all of them. And I like them. I do. They make good products, but probably about three times the cost" of the DJI tools.

Beal, who says his organization is "agnostic" when it comes to what drones departments use, says he thinks Chinese-made drones are "light years ahead of what our American drones are able to do."

For instance, Beal says DJI offers a drone with an impressive, high-resolution thermal camera that costs less than $10,000 right now. He says American-made drones have worse flight-time capabilities, thermal imaging and zoom. And still they usually cost between $20,000 and $50,000, depending on the type and the model.

NPR compared the cost of two drones with similar features. The DJI Matrice 400 drone [retails for about](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1902987-REG/dji_cp_en_00000684_sp_matrice_400_sp_plus.html/?ap=y&ap=y&smp=y&smp=y&store=420&lsft=BI%3A6879&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=13531530366&gbraid=0AAAAAD7yMh03YNomD4OjPozDl-mrzp9Vq&gclid=Cj0KCQjwzsjVBhC3ARIsALnMv4lUwmWNBw6UtWvQCH7vVD7GrFqdYrMhCm3W2QG-KGrhfxERS2FRSx8aAtzIEALw_wcB) $10,500. The American-made Inspired Flight IF800 TOMCAT [is going for $21,000.](https://www.dronenerds.com/products/inspired-flight-if800-quadcopter-blue-herelink-ground-control-station-102830-dronenerds?variant=47809137901884&utm_term=&utm_campaign=Performance+Max+SS:+Enterprise+-+JF&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=5112913348&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_grp=&hsa_ver=3&hsa_kw=&hsa_tgt=&hsa_mt=&hsa_ad=&hsa_src=x&hsa_cam=23835978615&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23845832602&gbraid=0AAAAAC_1t-iPIHF2J7d-7hDbT2B0SxQqj&gclid=Cj0KCQjwzsjVBhC3ARIsALnMv4kmF10r_9e9NwHYV5CsvEYe9dxnv9a-W2aAeE046nGU-QmhRakLPaYaAoHhEALw_wcB)

### U.S. actions against DJI cite national security concerns

Ocean County is closely monitoring recent actions by the Trump administration that could limit options for updating its fleet in the future.

Agencies in other states like Florida, Texas, Mississippi and Tennessee have had to [terminate their drone programs](https://www.fox13news.com/news/lakeland-police-restart-drone-program-after-foreign-surveillance-concerns)or plans for one after state lawmakers[passed bans](https://www.axon.com/resources/new-drone-laws-take-effect) on agencies using foreign drones. Beal says some were left scrambling to find ways to pay for more expensive American alternatives when tight department budgets couldn't cover the additional costs.

And there are more federal actions in the works.

The Federal Communications Commission [is considering](https://www.fcc.gov/document/fcc-takes-action-secure-drone-supply-chain)a new rule that would reclassify drones that use tech like thermal imaging as "military grade" — effectively banning many Chinese-made drones that have this integrated technology. Ocean County and other law enforcement use thermal imaging to assist in finding lost people or pets.

An aerial view of an Ocean County Sheriff's Office DJI Matrice 300 RTK drone with a thermal-capable camera payload at the Ocean County Fairgrounds with the New Jersey Pinelands stretching into the distance. A propeller plane can be seen below and right of the drone.  (Albert Yee for NPR)

The FCC already bans the sale of some new models of foreign-made drones without the agency's approval. Federal agencies and contractors cannot use certain foreign-made drones.

The FCC said in response to NPR's questions, "Thanks to President Trump's leadership, America's drone industry is booming with new investment, manufacturing, and jobs. At the FCC, we're doing our part — working hand-in-glove across government and the private sector to make sure that U.S. drone and counter-drone supply chains are safe, secure, and reliable for all."

The administration says that Chinese-made drones, and DJI drones specifically, [pose a threat to national security](https://www.fcc.gov/sites/default/files/National-Security-Determination-for-UAS.pdf) — with, for instance, their potential for major attacks during large public gatherings, like the recent World Cup games, among other concerns.

DJI has pushed back against claims that its tech is shared with the Chinese government or that it accesses cameras and other footage collected by users, even hiring a U.S.-based cybersecurity firm [to test the company's products](https://www.dji.com/media-center/announcements/dji-drone-independent-security-assessment) for vulnerabilities.

Adam Welsh, head of global policy at DJI [said in a statement published](https://www.dji.com/media-center/announcements/dji-drone-independent-security-assessment) in May, "These findings confirm what DJI has consistently maintained: our products are secure, our data practices are transparent" and the concerns that led to the company being banned "are not supported by technical evidence."

There's also the allegation that DJI uses forced labor from Uyghurs, a primarily Muslim ethnic group facing human rights abuses under the Chinese government, to build its products. In 2024, the Customs and Border Protection blocked certain DJI drone imports under the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act. DJI [has strongly denied](https://viewpoints.dji.com/blog/navigating-u.s.-customs-demonstrating-djis-commitment-to-ethical-production-labor-practices) these allegations, too.

Fennessy says he understands these concerns. "But to be honest, right now," he says, "I want something that's capable to go out there and do the job. And I have it."

Beal says he's seen no hard evidence that China is using these drones or its technology to spy on communities that are using them. He says he can understand the argument to bring more of the drone supply chain stateside.

But that's a problem too, right now.

"We don't have a lot of the minerals. We can't produce the battery now. Even the American companies are using Chinese batteries," he says. "We're kind of limited to the resources that we have in-country or in an allied country, and sometimes that's just not there."

### Who's likely to absorb the costs? Taxpayers

The National Sheriffs' Association, which represents more than 3,000 sheriffs, has called for the FCC to reconsider the proposed reclassification of certain drones as military grade. In a recent letter, [the association w

content:
Sources: QS World University Rankings 2026 (published 19 June 2025, topuniversities.com); Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2026 (published 8 October 2025, timeshighereducation.com); Academic Ranking of World Universities, Shanghai Ranking 2025 (published 15 August 2025, shanghairanking.com).

Tsinghua University posted a perfect industry collaboration score (100/100) and a research quality score of 93.9 under Times Higher Education criteria. In computer science, Tsinghua and Shanghai Jiao Tong University tied for first place worldwide in CSRankings publications.

For UK, EU and Commonwealth students, the career proposition rests on two pillars. The first is direct exposure to a graduate market that recruits foreign talent into technology, green energy, supply chain finance and luxury management. The second is the increasing relevance of Mandarin and of working familiarity with Chinese regulatory environments for European multinationals operating under "China+1" supply chain strategies.

## Can foreigners study in China? Eligibility basics

Foreign nationals can enrol at any Chinese university authorised by the Ministry of Education to recruit international students, subject to three baseline requirements: a valid passport, a previous diploma at the corresponding academic level, and proof of language proficiency in the language of instruction.

*   **Bachelor's programmes**require a recognised secondary school diploma (UK A levels, French baccalauréat, equivalent foreign qualification) and, from 2026/2027, the new CSCA score.
*   **Master's programmes**require a recognised bachelor's degree in a related field, transcripts and a research-oriented study plan.
*   **Doctoral programmes** require a recognised master's degree, a detailed research proposal and the formal endorsement of a supervisor at the host institution.

Most universities require candidates to be aged between 18 and 30 at the start of the academic year for undergraduate intake, with the ceiling raised to 35 for master's and 40 for doctoral applicants. Scholarship-specific schemes apply tighter age limits (CSC undergraduate: 25 maximum; CSC master's: 35 maximum; CSC doctoral: 40 maximum).

## Choose the right Chinese university

The choice of institution should weigh four criteria: the academic reputation of the university in the field, the cost of living in the host city, the share of programmes taught in English, and the recognition of the diploma in the candidate's home country.

Public universities dominate the international student market. The "Double First-Class" initiative, launched by the Ministry of Education in 2017, designates approximately 140 universities and 460 disciplinary programmes as national priorities. The C9 League sits inside that perimeter, alongside flagship institutions such as Nanjing University, the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), Harbin Institute of Technology and Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU).

City choice has a measurable financial impact. Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen run as tier-1 megacities, with rents, transport and meals at the upper end of the national grid. Provincial centres such as Suzhou, Xi'an, Nanjing and Hangzhou cut the monthly student budget by 25% to 35% while remaining within 30 to 90 minutes of a tier-1 hub by high-speed rail. Suzhou specifically sits 25 minutes from Shanghai by train and concentrates a dense international academic and corporate ecosystem inside the Suzhou Industrial Park.

For UK applicants, academic recognition is handled by **UK ENIC**(Ecctis), which issues Statements of Comparability mapping Chinese bachelor's, master's and doctoral qualifications onto the UK qualifications framework [enic.org.uk]. For French and EU applicants, the equivalent service is **ENIC-NARIC France**, which charges a €20 filing fee and a €100 evaluation fee on admissibility [service-public.gouv.fr]. Mainland China is a signatory of the Asia-Pacific Regional Convention on the Recognition of Qualifications in Higher Education, which underpins those mutual recognition arrangements. Double-degree programmes registered under the French RNCP, such as the SKEMA Master in Management (RNCP n°41054), provide direct EHEA-wide recognition without a separate comparability procedure.

## Study in China in English or in Chinese?

The language of instruction shapes admission requirements, daily life on campus and post-graduation labour-market positioning. Both routes lead to nationally recognised degrees, but the operational implications differ.

**English-medium instruction (EMI) programmes**are taught entirely in English by Chinese and international faculty. They cover the most internationally exposed fields (business, management, finance, AI, international relations) and account for the majority of joint and dual-degree formats. Admission requires IELTS 6.0 or higher, or TOEFL 80 or higher, alongside academic transcripts.

**Chinese-medium programmes**require certified HSK proficiency, give access to a much wider catalogue of disciplines (humanities, law, medicine, traditional Chinese studies, large segments of STEM) and substantially raise the candidate's employability in domestic Chinese roles. Daily life on campus also changes: administrative procedures, off-campus housing contracts and most internships run in Mandarin.

Many candidates begin with a one-year Chinese Language Foundation programme (HSK preparation) before progressing to a Chinese-medium bachelor's or master's degree, particularly in fields such as Chinese medicine, law and Chinese studies where no equivalent EMI track exists.

## The new CSCA standardised test (mandatory from 2026/2027)

**The China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) is**a new standardised admissions test required of every international undergraduate applicant to a Chinese university from the 2026/2027 academic year onwards, scholarship-funded or self-funded. It is organised by the China Scholarship Council (CSC) and run on a dedicated digital platform [csca.cn, joint specifications published November 2025].

The test combines three modules:

*   **Specialised Chinese**(mandatory): adapted to the academic track chosen by the applicant.
*   **Mathematics**(mandatory): 60 minutes, 48 single-answer multiple-choice questions.
*   **Physics or Chemistry**(mandatory for STEM majors): one module out of the two, depending on the host university's specifications.

The CSCA runs five testing windows per year: January, March, April, June and December. Candidates take the test on a desktop computer using a dedicated software environment. The technical requirements are explicit: 64-bit Windows 7 SP1 or higher, 4GB of RAM minimum, and an internet connection of at least 20 Mbps. **macOS is not supported**, a practical detail that UK and EU candidates should anticipate when planning the test logistics.

Each university sets its own qualifying threshold per module and per field of study, and the score is mandatory at the application stage. Candidates planning a September 2027 intake should target the December 2026 or January 2027 windows to secure a result before the main application deadlines.

## How to apply to a Chinese university, step by step

Applications can be filed through one of two channels: directly with the university's international office, or via a centralised platform such as CUCAS (China's University and College Admission System) or China Admissions, which process documents across multiple host institutions in exchange for a service fee.

The application file is standardised across institutions and includes:

*   A valid passport with at least six months of remaining validity and two blank pages.
*   Notarised and translated diplomas and academic transcripts.
*   Language proficiency certificates (HSK and/or IELTS/TOEFL).
*   A study plan or research proposal: minimum 500 words at undergraduate level, 800 to 1,500 words at postgraduate level.
*   Two recommendation letters signed by professors or associate professors.
*   The Foreigner Physical Examination Form, completed by a licensed physician, mandatory for any stay exceeding six months.
*   A certificate of non-criminal record, officially translated and legalised.
*   The CSCA score (undergraduate applicants from 2026/2027 onwards).

Application fees vary by institution and route, typically between CNY 400 and CNY 800 per university. Interviews are common at postgraduate level and at top-tier institutions, usually conducted by video conference. Decisions are notified between four and twelve weeks after submission for self-funded applications and between two and four months for CSC-funded applications, which include an inter-institutional review.

## When to apply: timeline and deadlines

The Chinese academic year runs from September to July, with a smaller intake in March. Application windows align with that calendar, and missing a window pushes the start date back by one semester.

[Sources: cucas.cn 2026, csc.edu.cn 2026].

A defensible schedule for a September 2027 intake is therefore: CSCA registration and sitting between December 2026 and April 2027 (undergraduate applicants); CSC Type A submission between November 2026 and February 2027; CSC Type B and self-funded applications between February and June 2027; X1 visa filed at the CVASC between July and August 2027 once the admission notice and the JW201 or JW202 form are received.

## Scholarships to study in China

Chinese authorities operate one of the largest international scholarship systems in the world, with two national schemes at its core.

### Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)

The CSC, administered by the China Scholarship Council, is the flagship scheme. It is split into three application paths for the 2025-2026 cycle:

Full CSC packages cover tuition, on-campus dormitory accommodation, comprehensive medical insurance (CNY 800 per year), and a monthly stipend of **CNY 3,500 for doctoral candidates, CNY 3,000 for master's, and CNY 2,500 for bachelor's**[csc.edu.cn, 2026].

### Confucius Institute Scholarship (CIS)

Funded by the Chinese International Education Foundation, the CIS targets students of Chinese language, linguistics and literature. It covers tuition, shared on-campus housing, medical insurance and a monthly allowance: CNY 3,000 for MTCSOL (Master's in Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages) and CNY 2,500 for BTCSOL (Bachelor's) and short-term language students. An additional CNY 700 per month applies if off-campus living is approved.

CSC funding covers approximately 8% of the international student population. The remaining 92% are self-funded, and these figures should set realistic expectations for candidates without a pre-existing bilateral channel through their home-country embassy.

## Living costs

Monthly living costs vary substantially between tier-1 megacities (Beijing, Shanghai) and provincial centres (Suzhou, Xi'an, Nanjing).

Suzhou is explicitly classified as a provincial centre in this grid, with monthly costs around 30% below the Shanghai equivalent and a 25-minute high-speed rail connection to central Shanghai.

**Comprehensive medical insurance is**mandatory throughout the studies under Ministry of Education regulations. Universities arrange collective enrolment in the "Comprehensive Insurance and Protection Scheme for Foreigners Staying in China", typically underwritten by Ping An or PICC, at **CNY 800 per academic year (CNY 400 per semester)**. The plan covers in-patient treatment up to CNY 400,000 per year, outpatient and emergency care up to CNY 20,000 (with a CNY 650 cumulative deductible and 85% reimbursement), and accidental death or disability up to CNY 100,000. Dental, optical and mental health coverage are excluded and usually require a private top-up policy in the CNY 2,000 to 5,000 per year range.

title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 12, 2026
summary: Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will attend the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) held in Baku, Azerbaijan on
content:
Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will attend the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) held in Baku, Azerbaijan on October 15 as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, and visit Azerbaijan, Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria from October 14 to 20.

**Beijing Daily: Today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs put on its website the decision to take countermeasures against Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Emigdio Villate Samaniego and Belize Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca. Could you share more information on that?**

Mao Ning: The Taiwan question is a major issue of principle bearing on China’s sovereignty and national reunification. It is at the core of China’s core interests. Certain politicians in Paraguay and Belize willingly serve as chess pieces for the DPP authorities in their pursuit of independence by soliciting external support. Their visits to Taiwan and reception of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces in their countries constitute severe interference in China’s internal affairs. They also attacked and smeared China by spreading the “Chinese cyber attack” disinformation, causing egregious impact in the world.

In response to these moves and in accordance with the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law of the People’s Republic of China, China announced in the form of MFA decree countermeasures as an action of warning and deterrence.

**China News Service: Foreign Minister Wang Yi will attend the Seventh CICA Summit as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping and visit Azerbaijan. What’s China’s expectation of the visit?**

Mao Ning: CICA is an important mechanism for security dialogue and cooperation in Asia. Since its inception, CICA has been committed to enhancing interaction and confidence-building among countries and made important contribution to security, stability and development in the region.

With growing complexity and volatility in the international and regional landscapes, Asian countries are increasingly keen to ensure peace and tranquility and promote economic growth. At the upcoming summit, China will engage in extensive dialogue and consultation with various parties to practice multilateralism, actively implement the four global initiatives, and enhance Asian governance, so as to make new contribution to building an Asian community with a shared future.

China and Azerbaijan are comprehensive strategic partners. In recent years, under the strategic planning and guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Ilham Aliyev, China-Azerbaijan relations have maintained strong momentum of growth, with ever-deepening political mutual trust, steady progress in Belt and Road cooperation and fruitful collaboration on international affairs. This will be Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s first official visit to Azerbaijan in seven years. He will hold talks with Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov. We believe the visit will help fully implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state and deliver new outcomes for bilateral cooperation across various fields.

**AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia on Sunday. The ceasefire was met with surprise from Kiev and silence from Moscow and appeared shaky as Russia appeared to strike multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this “energy ceasefire”?**

Mao Ning: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis is consistent and clear. We believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out, and support all efforts conducive to peace.

**Reuters: The U.S. State Department last week said China’s maritime activities off Taiwan’s east coast are “deeply destabilizing.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment on that?**

Mao Ning: China has on multiple occasions made clear its position on this. China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. The party that instigates troubles and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side.

The Taiwan question is China’s internal affair that brooks no external interference. The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and take concrete actions to uphold the overall China-U.S. relations and peace and stability in the region.

**Xinhua News Agency: On October 10, leader of the Taiwan region Lai Ching-te made a speech in which he again solicited external support for “Taiwan independence,” and smeared Chinese mainland. What’s your comment?**

Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and the Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. To uphold the one-China principle, reject “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and support China’s reunification is where international public opinion trends.

Lai Ching-te’s so-called “democracy” cannot hide his “Taiwan independence” separatist nature. Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the outcome of WWII victory and the postwar international order. The real status quo across the Taiwan Strait is that both sides of the Strait belong to one and the same China. Whatever Lai Ching-te says or does, it does not change the fact backed by history and law that Taiwan belongs to China or the doomed failure of “Taiwan independence,” and will by no means stop China’s ultimate reunification.

**CGTN: Could you elaborate on the program and China’s expectation of Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria?**

Mao Ning: Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria are China’s important cooperation partners in Southeastern Europe. In recent years, China has maintained close exchanges with the three countries. Notable results have been achieved in cooperation on economy and trade, investment, tourism and infrastructure. There is extensive common ground on safeguarding multilateralism, tackling global challenges, growing China-Europe relations and other topics. During the visit, Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with the foreign ministers of the three countries and have in-depth exchange of views with their leaders.

Croatia is China’s important partner in the EU. The Chinese-built Pelješac Bridge is a landmark project of China-Croatia and China-EU cooperation. The two countries have enjoyed a more mature and stable partnership of comprehensive cooperation. Through the visit, China looks to better synergize development strategies and expand practical cooperation with Croatia, so as to promote the steady and sustained growth of bilateral ties.

This year marks the 20th anniversary of China’s diplomatic relations with Montenegro. Throughout those two decades, the two sides have always treated each other with respect and as equals. Together, the two countries have built a series of landmark projects, such as the South-North Expressway in Montenegro. China hopes that through the Chinese foreign minister’s first visit, the two sides will expand the breadth and depth of mutually beneficial cooperation, carry forward the traditional friendship, and inject new impetus into bilateral relations for the next 20 years.

Bulgaria is the second country in the entire world to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, China-Bulgaria strategic partnership has grown steadily, with close high-level exchanges and fruitful outcomes of practical cooperation. Through this visit, China looks to cement mutual trust, advance cooperation and deepen friendship with the new Bulgarian government, so as to further advance and deepen bilateral ties.

**Reuters: Regarding China’s sanctions on the Paraguay and Belize ministers, would this be first of such measures against ministers from countries that maintain ties with Taiwan?**

Mao Ning: For diehard supporters of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, China will take all necessary punitive measures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the very few countries left which still have so-called “diplomatic ties” with China’s Taiwan region to avoid being repeatedly manipulated and used by separatist forces for “Taiwan independence.” Betting on “Taiwan independence” has no future. It will only cost them opportunities for development and lead to international isolation.

**Global Times: Following his recent visit to China, former Japanese Foreign Minister and head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade Mr. Takeshi Iwaya said that the deterioration in China-Japan relations was caused by the Japanese side and that the Japanese government should seek ways to improve the bilateral ties. There are voices in Japan criticizing the evasion of historical responsibility for leading astray Japan’s policy toward China, and calling on the Japanese government to face up to and address the wrongdoings. What’s China’s comment?**

Mao Ning: China commends these remarks, which reflect reason and conscience among those with insight in Japan. As they have pointed out, the real issue lies in the distorted and erroneous views toward history and China held by those running the Japanese government, which has severely undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. The situation does not serve the two countries’ interests, and the responsibility rests fully with Japan. To bring China-Japan relations back to the right track, the ball is, apparently, in Japan’s court.

We urge those running the Japanese government to heed and take seriously the just voice at home, face up to the root causes of the problem, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and genuinely reflect on and correct wrongdoings on such issues as Taiwan, the history, and their China perception.

**AFP: A fresh Houthis strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others. This comes a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this?**

Mao Ning: China condemns the attacks, which caused significant casualties, and expresses grave concern over the escalating conflict. China opposes attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We urge the parties concerned to refrain from actions that could further escalate regional tensions, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiations, and work toward peace and stability in the region at an early date.

**Shenzhen TV: Today is the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Papua New Guinea. How does China see the development of bilateral ties over the past 50 years? What’s China’s expectation moving forward?**

Mao Ning: Today marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Papua New Guinea. President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have respectively exchanged congratulatory messages with Governor-General Bob Dadae and Prime Minister James Marape. As President Xi pointed out in his congratulatory message, over half a century since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, conducted fruitful cooperation for mutual benefit, and expanded people-to-people exchanges. The remarkable progress in bilateral relations has not only benefited the two peoples, but also injected strong momentum to building a community with a shared future between China and Pacific Island countries.

title: The US needs its own grey-zone tactics in the South China Sea
summary: Passive resistance to Beijing’s actions in the South China Sea is not working.If the United States wants to win in the region, it needs a grey-zone strategy of its own. Beijing has spent a decade refining a playbook that stays deliberately
content:
Passive resistance to Beijing’s actions in the South China Sea is not working.If the United States wants to win in the region, it needs a grey-zone strategy of its own.

Beijing has spent a decade refining a playbook that stays deliberately below the threshold of armed conflict.Chinese coast guard ships ram Philippine vessels, maritime militia swarm disputed reefs, and drones shadow foreign ships.Washington’s response – patrols, joint statements and expressions of concern – has imposed few costs and changed little.

This passivity means that China isn’t being deterred. Indeed, it’s being reassured that it can keep getting away with what it’s doing.

The US doesn’t need ships built for ramming to change that calculation.Rather, it should play to its strengths: a vast intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance network, powerful cyber and electromagnetic warfare capabilities and a web of regional partners.The US military’s F3EAD targeting cycle (find, fix, finish, exploit, analyse and disseminate) offers a template for response.For grey-zone competition, it can be adapted into F2RED: find, fix, respond, exploit and disseminate, with calibrated non-kinetic responses replacing the kinetic component (the ‘finish’).

The first two steps of the cycle that could be applied to the South China Sea are largely in place.Intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance assets across the region already track Chinese coast guard, navy, and maritime militia vessels, and coordination with partner forces can expand the network even further.But after that there’s a gap, because of Washington’s reticence to respond with any operation that may cause escalation.

One response below the threshold of armed conflict is to apply soft-kill effects – that is, nothing with kinetic impact, at least not on anything very costly or with people in it. When Chinese vessels launch uncrewed aircraft to harass or surveil ships of US partners, allied forces can jam or bring down the drones on the spot.Operations can be conducted against Chinese drones elsewhere to divert Beijing’s attention from the area of tension. The same tools become more potent against larger, more expensive ships and aircraft.Crucially, these effects must be paired with signalling, making it clear to Beijing that if its vessels don’t break contact with partners, costs will follow.

Cyber is a second channel for imposing costs. Beyond highlighting Chinese cyber actions against the US and its partners, the US can integrate offensive cyber capabilities into the ‘respond’ phase. By imposing proportionate costs on Chinese government, military or coast guard entities or networks, the US can signal that continued Chinese grey-zone actions will have consequences. For example, if a Chinese vessel rams a Philippine ship, the US could respond by disrupting critical systems associated with Chinese maritime operations. Because such capabilities can be employed from outside the immediate area of a dispute, they also provide strategic depth and another means of responding to Chinese coercion.

The US Coast Guard and Navy can work alongside partner coast guards to block, stop, and arrest militia or fishing crews caught operating illegally in partner waters.The principle is simple:partners enforce their own laws in their own waters, with US ships and intelligence backing them.This must stay strictly legal and be confined to those breaking international law and the law of US partners.Done properly, it turns Beijing’s favoured tactic, coercion dressed as law enforcement, back on itself, but from firmer legal ground.

Financial tools should be tied to response options.In 2022, the US Treasury[sanctioned Chinese distant-water fishing companies](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy1154), adding more than 150 vessels to the Specially Designated Nationals list over human rights abuses and illegal fishing.Extending that precedent to illegal fishing and militia activity within the region would mean freezing assets and persuading banks to cut their ties, further complicating militia and fishing operations and imposing additional costs.

The last two steps in the chain – exploiting and disseminating – are where the US holds its greatest advantage.It already operates extensively with regional partners, so the infrastructure for sharing information exists. It simply needs to be expanded to countries bullied by China.

That should include tracking data.If China can ram Philippine ships in Philippine waters, Manila should receive the information it needs to enforce its own rights, lawfully, in waters that Beijing claims.That should involve all of the aforementioned strategies supported by US capabilities – enforcing exclusive economic zones by arresting illegal fishing vessels, partnering with the US to jam Chinese drones within those areas, or using US intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance networks to identify and remove Chinese intelligence and surveillance sensors within partners’ territories.

A US–China hotline could accompany all of this, alerting Beijing before the response phase commences and giving it a chance to back down.

Critics will warn that all this would risk escalation, and in the short term some friction would be likely.But Beijing currently pays nothing for testing its neighbours, and it will keep testing them until it pays much more.Demonstrating resolve, rather than tacitly accepting Chinese sovereignty claims, is more likely to lead to de-escalation over time.

Additionally, many regional states dislike China’s bullying but lack the resources to resist it alone.Seeing Washington finally impose costs, lawfully and alongside partners, could stiffen the resolve of those fence-sitters.In grey-zone competition, passivity is a strategy that’s working in Beijing’s favour.

Author

**William Price** is a Major in the United States Marine Corps Reserve, has deployed to the Middle East and Africa as an intelligence officer, and has a master’s in International Service from American University.

title: Zille to ‘go into opposition’ if DA doesn’t win a workable coalition in Joburg
summary: [Helen Zille](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-13-zille-draws-coalition-red-lines-as-da-targets-joburg-majority/) believes that this is a make-or-break election for Johannesburg voters and is determined to either get the DA e
content:
[Helen Zille](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-13-zille-draws-coalition-red-lines-as-da-targets-joburg-majority/) believes that this is a make-or-break election for Johannesburg voters and is determined to either get the DA enough votes to lead the council or take the opposition benches.

What she is clear about is that should the party not get a majority, the DA will only consider a small number of coalition partners rather than get involved in a “chaotic coalition”.

“This is Joburg’s last-chance election and the people of Joburg must decide whether the city is worth saving or not.”

“I would not be here if it were not worth saving. I’ve put my whole life into this place.”

Zille has been campaigning in the city since September 2025, and by her own account, the party, and her as candidate, have pushed hard every single day of the year.

Zille’s campaign stunts drew the ire of Mayor Dada Morero several times as she focused on service delivery failures, the state of the city’s roads and shortcomings of the council.

The DA’s Joburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille says it’s the city’s ‘last-chance election’. (Photo: OUR CITY NEWS / James Oatway)

She told the story of a woman in Alex who sells chicken feet and gizzards, but has had no water at her home for 24 years.

“This woman is running a restaurant business and she needs water. No water comes out of her tap, and she needs to get it from neighbours or buy it.

“I got Johannesburg Water out, and they dug up something and discovered that the valve had not been opened. For 24 years, the valve was turned off. One turn of the valve gave her water. She had reported it to her councillor, but nothing happened. She was so impressed I fixed it, she kept saying ‘in one day’. It’s so tragic to see this happen.”

### Zille’s turnaround strategy

Zille said the City’s “massive liquidity crisis” meant there was no money to render services, but she believed the City’s dire financial situation could be turned around.

“Yes, it can be done, but this is the last time it can be done.”

“Joburg still has a very large revenue base, but it has been so badly mismanaged in the allocation of resources, and there has been so much corruption, that it has been squandered,” she said.

“So, we have a very good financial turnaround strategy and it’s implementable if we are determined to implement it. That’s obviously got to come first; we can’t do anything without money.”

“We have to stabilise the personnel and get the right people in the right places and then it’s going to be crucial to start on the most important service delivery issues which are water, electricity and roads, and of course refuse removal.”

The turnaround strategy, says Zille, is a six-month plan.

“If we can be very disciplined and turn it around, we will make big progress. When I was studying the figures for Joburg, it really struck me that if you add the non-revenue water and electricity cost, together with unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure, you hit 25% of the budget. It’s huge. If we just fix that, we make an enormous difference,” said Zille.

The City loses almost 50% of the water it buys from Rand Water, and electricity losses are at almost 30%. In the 2024/25 financial year alone, the City recorded R3.69-billion in irregular expenditure, R2.38-billion in unauthorised expenditure and R943-million in fruitless and wasteful expenditure.

She said: “I am not going to pretend it’s going to be easy to fix, but we have a plan. I can get real expertise into my office as mayor. There is a plan to ensure we hit the ground running and at least implement our financial turnaround strategy very quickly. We have to put together an adjustment budget and then implement our anti-corruption architecture, which we also planned very carefully”.

The first order of business for her as mayor would be to discuss the financial turnaround strategy with the National Treasury, the city’s chief financial officer and “crucially, with Operation Vulindlela”.

“We will have to set up some very tight public-private partnerships in order to deal with the trading services as quickly as we can; ringfence the finances (which has already started with Johannesburg Water), and we will find a way of getting our strategy locked and loaded and then move on to deal with corruption,” she said.

She is also worried about the targeting and assassination of whistleblowers.

“We will have to do all we possibly can to protect our whistleblowers.”

### **Coalition red lines**

Zille believes that voters have a choice between the status quo and the future they want to build for themselves.

“Vote for yourself. Think about the state of the city, think of the kind of city you want to live in in 10 years, then decide which party has the track record, the policies, the depth of leadership, the experience, to take Joburg there. And vote for that party,” she said.

Over the past five years, Johannesburg has been run by different coalition partners, all of which have proven to be difficult to manage.

Helen Zille says the DA will go into opposition if the party doesn’t win a workable coalition in Joburg. (Photo: OUR CITY NEWS / James Oatway)

Zille is not interested in having a nine-party coalition, because “someone will always pull in a different direction”.

With 82 parties and independents confirmed by the IEC as contesting the elections in Johannesburg, Zille is adamant that if the DA does not get an outright majority or a workable coalition, she will take the DA into opposition.

The latest [election polls](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-04-anc-and-da-in-dead-heat-across-key-metros-as-mk-dominates-ethekwini/) place the DA ahead of the ANC, but not by enough to win the council outright. The option then for the DA is to find an ideal coalition partner.

“To get Johannesburg working again will take at least 10 years. But in five years, we can make big changes. I am being very realistic; I know what it takes to turn a city around. We can make big progress if we don’t have unstable coalitions.

“And if there is a coalition, it needs to be with the smallest number of partners possible. I am not doing a nine-party coalition – been there, done that, and it is ungovernable. We will go into the opposition if that happens,” she said.

Besides turning around the financial fortunes of Johannesburg, Zille said she was equally concerned about the prevalence of substance abuse and its impact on society.

“The extent of substance abuse is the number one issue we have to deal with; no one knows how big it really is. It’s a vicious circle, and many kids are growing up in homes where substance abuse is rife.

“When I go to old-age homes, I find many grannies living with their grandchildren. Their own children are so high on drugs they can’t leave their grandchildren with them,” she said.

“The worst thing ever is knocking on doors of drug addicts and seeing the condition of their children. That is the worst thing ever,” she said. **DM**

_This interview is part of an ongoing series by Our City News featuring key mayoral candidates contesting the City of Johannesburg in the upcoming local government elections._
