title: UST activist suspensions: Testing the boundaries of academic freedom and student rights
summary: THE University of Santo Tomas suspended four student activists after they faced disciplinary complaints following a confrontation with military personnel at a Philippine Air Force (PAF) exhibit on campus on April 21, 2026. In addition to th
content:
THE University of Santo Tomas suspended four student activists after they faced disciplinary complaints following a confrontation with military personnel at a Philippine Air Force (PAF) exhibit on campus on April 21, 2026. In addition to the suspension, the university will withhold certificates of good moral character from the four students, effectively ousting one of them from a student council officer position.

The case stemmed from the confrontation at the PAF exhibit, held as part of UST’s 415th anniversary celebrations. The student activists heckled Air Force personnel about military equipment and operations, as well as alleged human rights abuses, two days after an armed encounter in Toboso, Negros Occidental, that left 19 people dead.

The UST Central Student Council criticized the university’s decision, saying the suspensions amounted to the “weaponization of the student handbook” and would prevent students from exercising dissent. The student council wrote an open letter to Pope Leo XIV, asking the pontiff to intervene against the alleged suppression of UST.

*   [Quo haec patria tendit?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/quo-haec-patria-tendit/2443321)

**UST’s academic freedom and students’ right to free speech**

In determining whether the UST suspension move was proper or violated students’ rights requires the application of two constitutional guarantees: students’ right to freedom of speech and expression, and the academic freedom of institutions of higher learning. In other words, was the sanction within UST’s valid exercise of academic freedom? Or did it violate students’ rights to freedom of speech and expression?

Get the latest news

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

While schools and universities are unique environments devoted to learning and discipline, they are not places where constitutional freedoms are completely left at the gate. Educational institutions like the University of Santo Tomas must balance their authority to maintain school peace and order with their duty to respect and protect students’ fundamental liberties while on campus.

**Jurisprudence on students’ free speech**

The landmark US case Tinker v. Des Moines firmly established that students and teachers do not shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech and expression upon entering the schoolhouse gate. Tinker introduced the now-classic standard that school authorities may regulate student expression only when it materially and substantially interferes with school activities or contradicts reasonable disciplinary policies. Note, however, that in Tinker, the students are participating in a public educational institution, not a private university like UST.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

Building on this principle, key Philippine Supreme Court decisions — Malabanan v. Ramento, Villar v. Technological Institute of the Philippines, and Non v. Dames — adapt and apply it in the Philippine context. These cases recognize that student assemblies, rallies and protests, even when critical of school policies, are generally protected forms of expression so long as they do not create a clear and present danger to the educational process. At the same time, they affirm that schools may regulate the time, place and manner of such activities and impose penalties, provided they are lawful, proportionate, and respect due process.

In the UST incident, did the students obtain prior permission from the university administration before they held protests against guests from the Armed Forces of the Philippines? Was the venue of such protest valid based on applicable university rules?

On the other hand, did UST observe administrative due process in the disciplinary case involving the students before imposing the suspensions and accessory penalties? Are these sanctions proportionate to the gravity of the offense committed, consistently imposed, and imposed in good faith?

A central theme running through these issues is the tension between the university’s academic freedom and students’ rights. Institutions of higher learning, such as UST, have the prerogative to set academic standards and to enforce discipline. This pertains specifically to the freedom of the university to determine “who shall be admitted to study.” However, this prerogative cannot be used as a pretext to silence dissent or discriminate against students for exercising their constitutional freedoms.

*   ![Image 2: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

On the other hand, the university’s obligation to respect students’ right to education, along with their rights to free speech and peaceful assembly, also implies students’ obligation to follow the institution’s established rules. They cannot simply hold lightning rallies without the proper permit or outside designated areas on campus. Students should also observe proper conduct even when protesting, as these policies still apply. They cannot disrespect persons in authority, such as the PAF personnel.

After all, educational institutions such as the University of Santo Tomas have a constitutional mandate to instill personal discipline and inculcate patriotism and nationalism, among other values. The university’s authority to promulgate its own rules governing student discipline aligns not only with the constitutional guarantee of academic freedom but also with its duty to shape the character of the youth.

Ultimately, while upholding students’ rights to freedom of speech and expression as vital, universities like the University of Santo Tomas must also exercise academic freedom to maintain discipline and order in the academic environment. The institution’s authority to set standards and enforce guidelines is essential to fostering a conducive atmosphere for learning and growth. Upholding academic integrity and ensuring respectful dialogue help prepare students for responsible citizenship. By navigating this delicate balance, UST can cultivate an environment where respectful discourse thrives while maintaining the discipline and order necessary in an academic setting.

title: Quo haec patria tendit?
summary: “WHERE is the country going” is the meaning of the above Latin sentence, Quo haec patria tendit. That seems to be the question of every Filipino citizen watching the gravely disconcerting political development unfolding in the country. It l
content:
“WHERE is the country going” is the meaning of the above Latin sentence, Quo haec patria tendit. That seems to be the question of every Filipino citizen watching the gravely disconcerting political development unfolding in the country.

It looks like the brains behind the ouster of Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte and her disqualification from the 2028 presidential elections are on track in their devious plan of convicting her in the impeachment trial.

The political bullet train carrying the judgment of conviction, if one is to believe the spokesman of the impeachment court, is arriving at its designated place on Dec. 16 of this year.

*   [Are Marcos’ minions in Congress plotting to amend the Constitution?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/opinion/columns/are-marcos-minions-in-congress-plotting-to-amend-the-constitution/2443331)

All the forced circumstances that will bring to fruition such devilish design have transpired, to wit: the arrest, detention and rendition of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, to the International Criminal Court (ICC) at The Hague; the overwhelming vote by the members of the House of Representatives to impeach VP Sara; the filing of nonbailable charges of plunder against identified allies of VP Sara and their incarceration; the service of an ICC warrant on Sen. Ronald “ Bato” de la Rosa that forced the embattled lawmaker to go into hiding to evade an unlawful arrest; the shake-up at the Senate that resulted in the ouster of Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano from the Senate leadership following the somersaulting of two senators who are facing capital offenses in connection with the flood-control project corruption, forcing them to abandon their colleagues in the majority resulting in the Cayetano bloc’s loss of control of the upper chamber; the threatened filing of criminal charges against a female senator and her lawmaker-son and the issuance of a warrant of arrest against the latter; and the filing of graft and corruption criminal complaints against sibling senators Camille and Mark Villar and their parents, former senator Manuel “Manny” Villar and former senator Cynthia Villar, as well as another member of the Villar family, that forced Senator Mark Villar to leave the minority and vote with the majority to unlawfully reduce the constitutional threshold of conviction in the Senate impeachment vote.

The scuttlebutt is that there are three more senators who are to join the majority to secure their liberty. If that probability happens, and the highest court of the land does not intervene to derail the unconstitutional amendment of reducing the required number of senators for conviction, then such circumstances will seal the political coffin of the impeached official.

The social media is abuzz with the bashing of Sen. Mark Villar for not only abandoning the minority but also voting to reduce the voting threshold for conviction. It is, however, easy to render rash judgment on him, to unmask him as a traitor to the cause of justice and truth, and for betraying his colleagues. But we must remember that a person under coercive and threatening circumstances where his or her liberty or life or both are at stake, especially when the members of his/her family are also at perilous risk, succumbing to a repulsive act against his will is inevitable.

Most of the members of both the majority and the minority are hostage to the power holders owing to their alleged involvement in some anomalies related to the release and use of the national budget. They have to toe the line, obey as ordered. Should they defy the command, the guillotine will swiftly fall on them. That will explain why, like dominoes, one by one of them is falling to the ground.

Rather than crucify them, the powers-that-be should be exposed and prosecuted to the fullest when the time of reckoning comes and they face the unforgiving wrath of the people and the law of retribution.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

For now, they appear to control the three branches of government, weaponizing the law against those whom they perceive to be roadblocks to their unquestionable lust for power and ill-gotten wealth.

They rule their fiefdom with absolute authority and impunity. They wallow in luxury, ransacking the natural resources and wealth of the nation as the people suffer in silence. Those who resist are subjected to black propaganda and dishonored, or worse, those who challenge their authority are thrown in jail.

The people are in despair even as they are disgusted and angry. They are waiting for the constitutionally designated protectors to fulfill their task, but they seem to be not forthcoming, waiting for a trigger that is either still in the making or has not taken shape. The last bulwark of democracy on Padre Faura appears to be vacillating or in a state of suspended animation.

The country is on the precipice. The seething outrage and desolation are percolating and near boiling point. There must be an end to this political insanity, but how and when?

[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

Que sera, sera; what will be, will be.

title: HEADLINES: Duterte’s lawyers to present evidence | October 12, 2026
summary: Good day. Here are the stories of The Manila Times for Monday, October 12, 2026. Today’s episode is brought to you by Wilcon Depot, The Philippines’ leading home improvement and construction supplies retailer — your Trusted Building Partner
content:
Good day. Here are the stories of The Manila Times for Monday, October 12, 2026.

Today’s episode is brought to you by Wilcon Depot, The Philippines’ leading home improvement and construction supplies retailer — your Trusted Building Partner.

**BANNER: Duterte’s lawyers to present evidence**

VICE President Sara Duterte’s defense team is preparing to present its witnesses and evidence before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel concluded its presentation of witnesses. The defense has indicated it will present a financial expert and other witnesses to challenge the prosecution’s findings, including its estimate of P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth involving Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio. On Friday, financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera testified that GenCorp Industries Inc., in which Duterte declared owning shares in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), underdeclared more than P1 billion in income over four years. Cabrera said GenCorp, which operates five Jollibee franchises, had P1.049 billion in undeclared income, representing an average annual underdeclaration of 87 percent.

**‘Lacson threatened contractors with plunder’**

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

SENATE Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has accused Sen. Panfilo Lacson of threatening to sue contractors for plunder to pressure them into signing affidavits concerning alleged irregularities in projects in the Laguna Lakeshore area in Taguig City. In a Facebook livestream on Saturday, Cayetano said four of the contractors implicated in the controversy refused to sign the affidavits, and two agreed to do so. He said Lacson warned the four holdouts they could face plunder charges if they refused to sign. He also alleged that Lacson, his staff and lawyers associated with them had prepared affidavits and were pressuring contractors to sign them. He did not identify the contractors or present copies of the affidavits during the livestream.

**Legarda may rejoin Senate majority – Pangilinan**

SEN. Francis Pangilinan has not ruled out Sen. Loren Legarda’s return to the Senate majority bloc, saying she was originally part of a group of five senators that included several members of the chamber’s current majority. Pangilinan said Legarda belonged to a group composed of Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III, Sen. Panfilo Lacson, Sen. Risa Hontiveros and Sen. Lito Lapid. Legarda joined the minority bloc led by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano amid changes in Senate leadership. Her return to the majority came under discussion after Sen. Mark Villar joined the bloc on Oct. 8, replacing Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri in the powerful Commission on Appointments and taking over the Senate Committee on Public Works.

**2 Filipinos among hundreds injured in Riyadh attack**

TWO Filipinos were among those wounded in the missile attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said Sunday. The attack, blamed on Houthi rebels, killed 12 people and injured 309 others. It was the deadliest strike on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac confirmed the two Filipino casualties but gave no further details, including their identities, the extent of their injuries and their current condition.

**BUSINESS: Global risks cloud remittance outlook**

REMITTANCES — a key pillar of the Philippine economy — will likely post slower growth as global uncertainties weigh on overseas employment and income prospects, a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) official said. BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Abenoja told The Manila Times that remittances are still expected to grow in the next two to three years, albeit at a slower pace amid global uncertainties. He added that the main risks to remittance growth are weaker labor demand in host economies and geopolitical tensions, particularly in the Middle East. The outlook carries significant implications for the Philippines, where remittances are equivalent to around eight percent of gross domestic product (GDP), helping sustain household spending and providing a steady source of foreign financing. Data from the BSP’s third-quarter 2026 Consumer Expectations Survey showed that food and other household expenses were the most common uses of remittances, with 98 percent of remittance-receiving households reporting that they used the money for these needs.

[**SPORTS: Eala on track for Alexandrova, Fernandez rematch**](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/sports/eala-on-track-for-alexandrova-fernandez-rematch/2443256)

FILIPINO sensation Alex Eala is on track for a rematch against Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova or a rubber match against Canadian Leylah Fernandez at the WTA 1000 Wuhan Open in China. World No. 18 Eala needs to get past a qualifier in her opening match likely on Monday before facing either No. 28 Alexandrova or No. 26 Fernandez who is of Filipino descent. Alexandrova and Fernandez were pitted against each other as the draw revealed on Saturday. Tournament No. 13 seed Eala battled Alexandrova at the Abu Dhabi Open quarterfinals where she fell to the latter, 3-6, 3-6, last February.

Rigoberto Tiglao and Fr. Ranhilio Callangan Aquino are today’s front page columnists. Tiglao’s column is about the alleged plot to amend the Constitution by allies of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in the lower house. Fr. Aquino’s column, meanwhile, talks about confidentiality in the impeachment court.

Today’s editorial is about the conflict between Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia.

title: Senate to probe rice smuggling – Pangilinan
summary: SEN. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan has called for the same level of public scrutiny and accountability for agricultural smuggling as for the flood control corruption scandal, saying both involve abuses that harm ordinary Filipinos. His call fol
content:
SEN. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan has called for the same level of public scrutiny and accountability for agricultural smuggling as for the flood control corruption scandal, saying both involve abuses that harm ordinary Filipinos. His call followed the interception of two vessels carrying nearly 20,000 metric tons of rice allegedly smuggled from Vietnam, with the shipments estimated to be worth about P700 million.

“Rice smugglers profit from farmers’ losses. Corrupt contractors profit while communities are submerged in floods,” Pangilinan said in an interview with DWIZ radio.

He said agricultural smuggling threatens food security, undermines local farmers and livestock raisers, and can leave consumers bearing the consequences.

*   [DOJ pushes through with obstruction complaint vs. Padilla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/doj-pushes-through-with-obstruction-complaint-vs-padilla/2443194)

“Rice smugglers and the government officials protecting them are like corrupt contractors involved in the flood control scam and the public officials enabling them. Both trade away the welfare of the people,” said Pangilinan, who chairs the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Food and Agrarian Reform.

He warned that officials from the Bureau of Customs (BOC), local government units, the Department of Agriculture (DA), the Department of Public Works and Highways, and other agencies should also be held accountable if found to have allowed or facilitated the illegal activities.

**“Even accomplices and enablers must be held accountable,” he said.**

Pangilinan requested that his committee investigate the rice smuggling cases, expecting the probe to begin before the end of October, possibly alongside the DA’s budget hearings scheduled for Oct. 20 and 21.

Authorities intercepted vessels MV Lucky Star and MV Tay Son 2 in separate operations in September in Limay, Bataan, and Davao, respectively. Pangilinan cited shipments of about 7,500 metric tons and roughly 12,000 metric tons of rice.

*   ![Image 1: WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254521.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[WTA is crazy, cruel for excluding Eala from finals](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/sports/wta-is-crazy-cruel-for-excluding-eala-from-finals/2443177)

He said the shipments had incomplete documentation and that he had asked the DA and BOC to reconcile discrepancies in their reported cargo volumes.

Pangilinan added that the Senate panel inquiry would examine the shipments’ consignees, the vessels’ captains, and any possible involvement of government personnel. He also said the Department of Justice should participate because it would handle the filing of criminal complaints.

Pangilinan stressed the importance of securing official documents and sufficient evidence to avoid court dismissal of the cases. He recalled that previous smuggling investigations had problems when cases were filed with incomplete records or photocopies instead of original official documents.

**“We will expose all of it and closely monitor the case,” he said, adding that government agencies had committed to cooperating with the investigation.**

*   ![Image 2: Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254827.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos names Lino Cayetano new PCO chief](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-names-lino-cayetano-new-pco-chief/2443262)

Pangilinan said the investigation would also test the enforcement of the law against agricultural economic sabotage, which he said provides authorities with stronger legal tools to prosecute large-scale agricultural smuggling.

He cited previous Senate investigations into smuggling, including a 2024 case involving imported pork worth about P100 million that was allegedly unfit for human consumption. Pangilinan said the Senate would revisit earlier cases and follow up on individuals who had failed to appear at hearings despite being subpoenaed.

The senator also raised concerns about the low number of cases filed in past smuggling investigations, saying seizures would have little deterrent effect if those responsible were not prosecuted.

“Especially with Super El Niño expected to further burden the agriculture and fisheries sectors, and with other threats to our food security, no one should be untouchable,” he said.

*   ![Image 3: Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254608.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Legarda may rejoin Senate majority — Pangilinan](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/legarda-may-rejoin-senate-majority-pangilinan/2443223)

Pangilinan said the Senate would also examine how the seized rice would be accounted for and disposed of, noting that discrepancies between initial announcements and records submitted during case filing had been a concern in previous cases.

**He said the government must show that agricultural smuggling demands meaningful accountability, not just mere seizure of shipments.**

He added that the looming Super El Niño makes protecting local food production more urgent, as farmers and fisherfolk face additional risks from adverse weather.

content:
BAYOMBONG, Nueva Vizcaya — A proposal by the Mines and Geosciences Bureau in Cagayan Valley (MGB-2) to substantially shrink a contested exploration permit in the upland town of Kasibu has become the focal point of efforts to ease tensions between the exploration firm and residents maintaining an anti-mining barricade.

The permit in question spans 4,456 hectares and has affected six barangay (villages), prompting protests, legal actions and a series of meetings involving national agencies, provincial and municipal officials, and community representatives.

MGB-2 regional director Mario Ancheta said the bureau intends to recommend that four villages be removed from the coverage of Exploration Permit EP-000029-II issued to North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp. (NLMRC), retaining only the villages of Pao and Kakidugen.

*   [Cebu ‘unhealthy’ air no longer from Indonesia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/regions/cebu-unhealthy-air-no-longer-from-indonesia/2442632)

The recommendation, he said, directly addresses the geographic scope that has fueled opposition.

Reducing the area to two villages is presented as a way to limit potential disturbance while keeping the exploration process within the existing regulatory framework, Ancheta said.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“The purpose of the current activity is to establish whether commercially viable mineral deposits exist,” he said.

Ancheta appealed to residents at the barricade to allow the firm to finish its technical work, noting that communities would still have a formal avenue to oppose any future mining development through free, prior and informed consent, and through the required concurrence of local legislative bodies.

That distinction is central to the regulatory sequence.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Exploration is treated as preliminary and technical, while any shift to development would require a separate, more stringent layer of social acceptability and clearances, he said.

Limits of local authority

Provincial officials, meanwhile, underscored the limits of local power over permits issued nationally.

Nueva Vizcaya Gov. Jose Gambito cautioned the company against any act that might place residents at the barricade at risk, saying it would be held accountable if harm occurs.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

At the same time, Gambito acknowledged that local officials do not have the power to unilaterally stop an operation backed by a national permit.

He expressed understanding for residents who oppose large-scale mining but said the authority to order a halt lies beyond the provincial and municipal levels.

Kasibu Mayor Romeo Tayaban shared that assessment, stating that the municipality cannot suspend exploration while a valid national permit remains in effect.

Gambito said he has elevated the concerns of protesters to Malacañang and noted that only President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. can order a halt to mining activities in the province.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

He added that past administrations in the province have faced similar challenges in stopping large-scale operations, and that he is pursuing all legal and administrative channels available with a clear conscience.

As a possible alternative, Gambito said that if the area is found to be more viable for small-scale operations, he would push for its declaration as a Minahang Bayan, or people’s small-scale mining area, a classification that allows residents to benefit from mineral resources under regulated conditions.

The model offers a different approach to resource use, centered on community participation rather than large corporate development.

Conflicting positions

Despite the proposed reduction in coverage, the barricade group continues to call for a complete withdrawal of the company.

Municipal councilor Anthony Glen Guingayan Sr., speaking for the protesters, said allowing the firm to leave the site would be the most direct way to avoid further confrontation, arguing that its exploration is already close to completion.

Guingayan said operations in Didipio are sufficient and that expansion to other barangay in Kasibu should not be allowed.

He also raised concern over criminal complaints filed against residents who joined the barricade to defend their lands, saying more than 20 individuals, including himself, have been charged and that more cases could be filed.

On the company side, lawyer Ulysses Ordoñez said the blockade has resulted in about P8 million in losses.

Ordoñez said the firm is considering applying for a preliminary injunction to remove the barricade and resume work, but would be willing not to pursue that legal remedy if protesters allow exploration to be completed.

Provincial board member Flodemonte Gerdan, who chairs the Committee on Peace and Order, reiterated the provincial board’s appeal for NLMRC to drop charges against protesters as a sign of good faith toward a peaceful settlement.

Bugkalot lawyer Efraim Osingat, meanwhile, urged those at the barricade to allow exploration to continue on their ancestral land, saying that for the first time a company willing to bring development to that land has come forward.

title: Chinese linked to POGOs in Bamban, Porac nabbed
summary: COMBINED elements of the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (Paocc) and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a Chinese citizen linked to human trafficking activities. The Chinese was identified as Huang M
content:
COMBINED elements of the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (Paocc) and the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a Chinese citizen linked to human trafficking activities.

The Chinese was identified as Huang Mingmin, who is wanted in connection with human trafficking activities linked to Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) operations.

The Paocc said Mingmin uses multiple aliases — including “Yang Bin,” “Sy Wang” and “A Bao” — to conceal his identity and evade detection by government authorities.

*   [Cebu ‘unhealthy’ air no longer from Indonesia](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/regions/cebu-unhealthy-air-no-longer-from-indonesia/2442632)

Mingmin was arrested at the K1 Center Building in Barangay Tambo, Parañaque City, on Friday.

The Paocc said Mingmin established a presence within the local business community and has already acquired real estate properties and fishing vessels on Jomalig Island in Quezon province.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The suspect also reportedly operates the Mother’s Wonderland and Sea Horizon Resort in Quezon province, where he was also identified as the owner.

The Paocc also alleged that Mingmin was among the foreigners who supported the broader operations of illegal POGO hubs such as the Baofu Hub in Bamban, Tarlac, and Lucky South 99 in Porac, Pampanga.

The Paocc also said initial investigations point to the subject’s alleged connection to individuals involved in the operations of these hubs, warranting further examination of his role and potential involvement in related activities.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

Based on court records, the Paocc said the arrested individual identified as alias “Yang Bin” is listed among the persons in control of the subject premises under Search Warrant 41M-M-2024, issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 81, Malolos City, Bulacan.

He is also one of the persons in control of the premises in connection with an alleged violation of Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code (serious illegal detention); and Search Warrant 42-M-2024 for the violation of Republic Act (RA) 9208, as amended by RA 10364, or the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012.

The suspect’s other known alias, “A Bao,” is listed among the individuals with arrest warrants in connection with the operations of Lucky South 99 and Whirlwind Corp. in Porac, Pampanga.

The case involves qualified trafficking in persons under Criminal Case R-PSG-25-01737-CR, pending before the Regional Trial Court Branch 157, Pasig City.

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Mingmin was brought to the CIDG-NCR for booking procedures and the completion of other necessary documentation.

Paocc said the agency, under the leadership of executive director Undersecretary Benjamin Acorda Jr., and law enforcement partners, remain steadfast in strengthening the government’s campaign against organized crime and human trafficking.

Former Paocc spokesman Winston Casio, meanwhile, said the POGOs “never left” the country and are still involve in guerrilla-like operations all over the Philippines.

Meanwhile, Ruperto Cruz, the former landowner, urged the government to clean the surroundings of the Lucky South 99 premises to prevent overgrown bushes from triggering fire. A golf club now operates near the Lucky South 99 property, which is now under the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Arrest warrants had been issue against key personalities in the Porac POGO such as Cassandra Li Ong and Ronelyn Baterna for qualified human trafficking charges, but the two had gone hiding.

The International Criminal Police Organization red notices were also issued against the two in October last year.

title: Taiwan ups defense spending to ‘deter war’
summary: TAIPEI— Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defense spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims. Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant thr
content:
TAIPEI— Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defense spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.

Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.

“Our aim by increasing investment in national defense is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” Leader Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.

*   [Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/candidate-named-hitler-mussolini-elected-mayor-in-peru/2443077)

Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion — and to show the United States it is serious about its own defense.

Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) in defense spending for 2027, which accounts for more than 3 percent of GDP.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.

“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting that China continued to “apply pressure through military and gray-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait.” Lai welcomed talks between the US and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist.” Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

[![Image 2: Taiwan�s President Lai Ching-te gives a speech during the National Day celebrations ceremony at the Presidential Palace in Taipei on October 10, 2026. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254374.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254374.jpg)
Taiwan�s President Lai Ching-te gives a speech during the National Day celebrations ceremony at the Presidential Palace in Taipei on October 10, 2026. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP)

‘US support important’

The US switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.

Trump’s suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on $14 billion worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defense system.

Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.

“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.

Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Lai’s speech was “relatively moderate” and unlikely to be met with “overt reaction from Beijing.” Saturday’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.

*   ![Image 4: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.

Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favors closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security,”but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.

“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event.

title: India deploys police forces ahead of huge protest
summary: NEW DELHI — India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief over alleged voter-roll irreg
content:
NEW DELHI — India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on Saturday demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

The protests, called by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilization following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision.

Demonstrations erupted across the country after a newspaper investigation last month alleged misconduct by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

*   [India crackdown on youth protesters provokes anger](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/india-crackdown-on-youth-protesters-provokes-anger/2443108)

The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety in the “special intensive revision”, saying it was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.

Opposition parties and critics say the exercise could disenfranchise voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Tens of thousands of police officers and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the capital, with multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocking roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the usual government-designated protest site.

[![Image 1: Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India�s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged ](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254362.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254362.jpg)
Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel stand guard ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India�s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged "special intensive revision� (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, in New Delhi on October 10, 2026. India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations on October 10 demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities. (Photo by Manan VATSYAYANA / AFP)

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

Police have not authorized rallies at the site this weekend.

The protests, called by the CJP, are widely seen as a reprise of its mass mobilization in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.

This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign.

‘Cannot detain the movement’

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.

Authorities have ordered the closure of dozens of metro stations, and cancelled several trains coming to New Delhi.

However, the Supreme Court on Friday said some trains must still run and that there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.

“The dictator would rather shut down the entire national capital and inconvenience millions of citizens than allow a peaceful protest at a designated protest site,” CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said on X.

*   ![Image 4: HEADLINES: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’ | Oct. 11, 2026](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254313.png?width=113&crop=113:85)
[HEADLINES: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’ | Oct. 11, 2026](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/podcasts/headlines-no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes-oct-11-2026/2443086)

“Imagine how many lives would be affected because of this shutdown by Modi.” The CJP, which emerged online as a satirical political movement in May, has accused authorities of intimidating its supporters ahead of the demonstration.

The party has said that “at least 10,000 people”, including protesters travelling to Delhi by train, have been detained across the country.

Some people detained in the central state of Madhya Pradesh were taken to hotels, The Hindu newspaper reported.

Police have not responded to the party’s broader allegations of mass detentions.

“You can detain the people -- you cannot detain the movement,” said Neha Bora, who has emerged as a leading face of the current protest.

The voter list overhaul, which began in 2025, has led to more than 133 million names being excluded from draft rolls.

The exclusions include duplicate entries and people found to have died.

The poll body said the exercise identifies fraudulently registered voters and aims to prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from casting ballots.

Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalized and minority communities.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

# India crackdown on youth protesters provokes anger

[![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/861_1632502576.jpg)![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/861_1632502576.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/associated-press "author image")

NEW DELHI— Indian authorities deployed a sweeping security crackdown across New Delhi and detained thousands of protesters on Saturday as India’s youth “Cockroach” movement sought to intensify a nationwide campaign against a contentious voter list revision that has fueled anger at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government and election authorities.

Police intercepted demonstrators before they could reach Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in the heart of India’s capital, chasing off some and detaining many others. Some were dragged away before being bundled into police vehicles and taken to temporary detention centers. Several “Cockroach” movement leaders were detained before arriving, effectively crippling the protest ahead of its start.

The crackdown extended beyond the protest venue, with police stopping buses, cars and other vehicles at checkpoints on routes into the capital and searching for demonstrators.

*   [India deploys police forces ahead of huge protest](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/world/asia-oceania/india-deploys-police-forces-ahead-of-huge-protest/2443114)

Jantar Mantar was barricaded, while anti-riot vehicles equipped with tear gas launchers were stationed along key routes. Restrictions on mobile internet and access to parts of the city added to the hurdles facing protesters.

Police said on Friday they had denied permission for the protest because the request was submitted late.

title: Filipino workers fear speaking up about mental health, Telus index finds
summary: SEVENTY-SEVEN percent of Filipino workers would worry about their career options if their workplace knew about a mental health issue, according to the latest Telus Mental Health Index for the Philippines, released by Telus Health in August.
content:
SEVENTY-SEVEN percent of Filipino workers would worry about their career options if their workplace knew about a mental health issue, according to the latest Telus Mental Health Index for the Philippines, released by Telus Health in August. That is up from 75 percent in 2022, while the share who would feel negatively about themselves rose from 57 to 63 percent.

More than half of workers have no emergency savings to cover basic needs, and half name personal finances as their top source of personal stress. A similar share say their mental health hurts their productivity, and nearly half often end the workday mentally or physically exhausted.

The overall index score is 61.6 out of 100, more than three points lower than in November 2022 and within the range the report labels “strained.”

*   [When security creates friction, employees find workarounds](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/business/sunday-business-it/when-security-creates-friction-employees-find-workarounds/2443042)

The online survey covered 2,000 people in the Philippines who are employed or had a job in the previous six months.

I asked Jamie MacLennan, region head for Asia-Pacific at Telus Health, what reason workers have to ask for help if they believe it could hurt their careers.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“If someone believes asking for help might cost them a promotion, silence can feel like the safer choice,” MacLennan wrote in an email interview. He traced this to Asia’s history of high stigma around mental health, and said the Philippines is similar to other parts of Asia but much worse than Western countries. Employees “look at how a manager responds, whether a conversation stays confidential, and whether someone who asks for help is still considered fairly for opportunities,” he wrote.

“Those experiences shape trust more than any campaign.”

Since 2020, employers in the formal private sector have been required to have a mental health workplace policy and program under Department Order 208 of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), which implements the Mental Health Act (Republic Act 11036). The order bars discrimination in hiring, promotion and other employment benefits because of a worker’s mental health condition, provided it does not interfere with their job performance or unduly affect their safety or that of coworkers, clients and the public. Yet nearly eight in 10 workers in the Telus survey still fear that disclosure could limit their career options.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

I also asked him about money. “When someone is wondering how to pay the next bill or what they would do if a family member became ill, that worry comes to work with them.”

Workers without emergency savings scored 55.5 on the index, against 69.0 for those with savings. Employers “should absolutely make financial well-being part of their mental health strategy,” MacLennan said, and salary alone does not cover it. He said the survey shows workers want financial consultation, education or resources from their employer. Across the region, Telus Health has seen confidential financial counseling and help with budgeting and debt work.

More than eight in 10 workers do their jobs while mentally or physically unwell at least once a week. “Many workers keep going because they feel they have to,” he said, since a day off can mean lost income, unfinished work or more pressure on colleagues.

According to the report, workers who never work while unwell lose 17.3 productivity days a year. Those who do it four or five days a week lose between 64 and 71 days. For employers who still count attendance and hours, MacLennan said “showing up is not the same as being well.”

*   ![Image 2: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

He told managers to watch for an engaged employee who turns withdrawn, has trouble concentrating or misses familiar deadlines. Those changes “should start a private, caring conversation,” he wrote. “People should not have to reach a breaking point before their employer notices.”

Workers under 40 are twice as likely as those over 50 to report constant stress, and 70 percent more likely to end the day exhausted. Younger workers score lower across Asia-Pacific, according to MacLennan, who listed the stressors that have piled up since the pandemic: cost of living, geopolitical risks, housing, job security “and now AI.”

Only six in 10 managers say they would know what to do if they suspected an employee was struggling. More than four in 10 workers say their manager has not told them what programs are available, and only about a third regularly receive clear information about them. More than half cite cost as a barrier to professional help. About a third do not know what type of care fits them, and nearly three in 10 do not know where to go.

MacLennan would start by training every manager. They should be able to tell employees whom to contact, what help exists, what it costs and what stays confidential, and then connect them to qualified support “without trying to be their counsellor.” Employers also need to keep explaining their programs and ask staff if they work.

*   ![Image 3: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

Many of us have worked beside someone who was struggling and never said a word about it. As MacLennan wrote: “The real test is whether an employee facing a difficult day knows where to turn and feels safe taking that first step.”

title: When persuasion begins to erode trust
summary: AT A RECENT marketing community event, I shared with a peer why I have become more selective about where I spend my time online. Facebook and LinkedIn increasingly feel like crowded marketplaces of expertise, with professionals competing fo
content:
AT A RECENT marketing community event, I shared with a peer why I have become more selective about where I spend my time online. Facebook and LinkedIn increasingly feel like crowded marketplaces of expertise, with professionals competing for attention through articles, commentary, advice and carefully produced content. Artificial intelligence (AI) has made it easier to participate in this competition. Still, I have begun questioning whether producing more content in already crowded feeds is necessarily the best way to build meaningful connections.

During our conversation, my peer raised another concern: the amount of manipulative content circulating on social media. Even the way some posts are scripted can make readers feel that their emotions or decisions are being deliberately influenced. The observation stayed with me because it pointed to a problem beyond content saturation. When people become suspicious of what they encounter online, even useful information may struggle to earn their confidence.

Marketing has always involved persuasion. Businesses communicate value, appeal to customer needs and encourage people to act. Storytelling is part of this process because decisions are influenced not only by facts but also by experiences, aspirations and emotions. The concern is not that businesses want to influence decisions. It is whether they do so in ways that respect the audience’s ability to make informed choices.

*   [When security creates friction, employees find workarounds](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/business/sunday-business-it/when-security-creates-friction-employees-find-workarounds/2443042)

**When polished content raises questions**

While preparing a digital storytelling session for tourism stakeholders in two provinces lately, I explored how a destination could be communicated through information, promotion and storytelling. Information helps travelers understand what is available. Promotion gives them reasons to consider a destination. Storytelling helps them imagine what an experience might mean to them.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

AI can now help transform a narrative into realistic images, videos and social media materials. This creates opportunities for smaller businesses that previously lacked the resources for professional content production. However, it also introduces questions about authenticity. An imagined visitor experience can look convincing even when no such visit occurred.

Fictional illustrations have legitimate uses in marketing and education, provided audiences are not misled about their nature. Problems arise when invented experiences resemble actual customer testimonials or when edited visuals create expectations that the business cannot fulfill.

There is also a less obvious consequence. As people become more familiar with AI-generated content, they may question genuine photographs and stories simply because they appear unusually polished. Businesses therefore face a communication challenge that cannot be solved by improving production quality alone.

*   ![Image 1: Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1253968.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Senate impeachment court to rule on dropped bribery charge next week](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/senate-impeachment-court-to-rule-on-dropped-bribery-charge-next-week/2442987)

**Difference between persuasion, manipulation**

Manipulation does not require AI. Misleading claims, selective information, manufactured urgency and exaggerated emotional appeals existed long before generative tools became widely available. AI can make producing and adapting such messages faster, but the responsibility remains with those deciding what to communicate.

A story can be emotional without being manipulative. A customer sharing a meaningful experience may help others appreciate a product or service. But when a business invents that experience, omits important limitations or creates pressure that prevents thoughtful evaluation, it risks crossing a different line.

This distinction matters because successful communication does not end when someone clicks, inquires or makes a purchase. The customer eventually encounters the actual product, service or experience. If reality falls short of the impression created, the attention gained through marketing may come at the expense of confidence in the business.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

**Why relationships matter again**

My growing preference for Viber communities and participation in professional associations reflects a different approach to communication. I still value Facebook and LinkedIn, but I increasingly prefer spaces where conversations can continue beyond a single post and where people have opportunities to get to know one another through shared activities and discussions.

These environments are not automatically more trustworthy. Misleading content and self-promotion can appear anywhere. What makes them useful to me is the additional context that relationships provide. When people have interacted with someone, asked questions and observed how that person responds, they have more information on which to form their judgments.

This also changes how I think about visibility. Reaching a large audience is useful, but it is not the only measure of meaningful communication. A smaller group of people who read, question, respond and remember may contribute more to a lasting professional relationship than a much larger audience that encounters a post briefly before moving on.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

For businesses, the implication is not to abandon social media or stop using AI. Both remain valuable for communication, discovery and customer engagement. The opportunity is to connect digital visibility with experiences and relationships that support the claims being made.

As creating persuasive content becomes easier, the challenge may increasingly shift from attracting attention to sustaining confidence. Businesses will still need compelling messages, but those messages must be supported by accurate information, credible behavior and experiences that justify customer expectations.

Perhaps the more useful question is no longer how to become more convincing online, but how to give people genuine reasons to believe us.

title: New logic of modern data center
summary: BUSINESS growth in Asia-Pacific is entering a new phase. The sustained increase in data, process automation, and the advancement of artificial intelligence are redefining the way enterprises compete and operate. In this scenario, computing
content:
BUSINESS growth in Asia-Pacific is entering a new phase. The sustained increase in data, process automation, and the advancement of artificial intelligence are redefining the way enterprises compete and operate.

In this scenario, computing has ceased to be a technical support function and has become a strategic factor, directly linked to productivity and growth capacity.

The growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. As models and workloads become more complex, organizations require platforms that can scale efficiently while maintaining performance and optimizing energy consumption. In this context, modern computing architectures are evolving toward models that enable greater processing capacity to be consolidated within a smaller physical infrastructure footprint. The typical result is a more efficient operation, with reduced space, power, and management requirements. In fact, comparing a solution powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors to a legacy solution to deliver the same workload showed that the EPYC solution could reduce the number of servers required by up to 86 percent, lower energy consumption by as much as 69 percent, and decrease total cost of ownership (TCO) by up to 41 percent over a three-year period.

*   [Accentuate professional development better at Accenture](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/accentuate-professional-development-better-at-accenture/2442156)

[![Image 1: TRANSFORMATIONAL SHIFT Growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254162.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254162.jpg)
TRANSFORMATIONAL SHIFT Growing adoption of artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and automation is increasing the demands placed on enterprise technology infrastructure. AI-GENERATED GRAPHICS

This shift is driving a transformation in data center architecture. The model based on physical expansion — more servers, more space, more consumption — is being replaced by schemes that prioritize efficiency, compute density and load consolidation. In practice, this means doing more with less: running more applications on fewer servers, reducing costs and operational complexity.

The approach can have a direct impact on total cost of ownership (TCO). By optimizing the use of existing infrastructure, companies can reduce energy consumption, reduce space requirements and simplify technology management. This approach is especially relevant in markets such as the Philippines, where operational efficiency has become a key factor in sustaining competitiveness.

At the same time, energy efficiency has become a priority. Electricity consumption represents one of the main costs in data centers, so improving performance per unit of energy not only has a financial impact but also affects the sustainability commitments that more and more companies are assuming.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

Another central element is scalability. Organizations require infrastructure capable of adapting to variations in demand, especially in environments where artificial intelligence demands real-time processing. Frictionless scaling allows you to accelerate service deployment and respond more quickly to market needs.

In the Philippines’ case, this change in focus offers potential benefits: greater processing capacity without the need for physical expansion, reduced operating costs and an infrastructure prepared to sustain future growth. In an environment where digital transformation is progressing unevenly, the adoption of more efficient models can make a significant difference in terms of competitiveness.

In this sense, recent technological evolution points toward more compact, efficient platforms designed for modern workloads. The focus is no longer on the volume of infrastructure but on its capacity for performance and optimization.

The breaking point is clear: the future of the data center is not necessarily about growing in size but about improving efficiency. Consolidating loads and optimizing resources has become a strategic decision to help reduce costs and sustain growth in the digital economy.

*   ![Image 3: Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253567.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Cayetano’s words, Cayetano’s shame](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/cayetanos-words-cayetanos-shame/2442752)

As a final reflection, the opportunity for companies in the Philippines is not only to adopt new technologies but to do so with a strategic approach. Organizations that understand that computing is the core of their growth, and not just a support function, will be better positioned to capture the value of artificial intelligence. Today, efficiency is not optional; it is the basis on which tomorrow’s competitiveness is built.

title: The next play
summary: For most of Gabe Norwood’s adult life, basketball dictated the rhythm of his world: practices, games, flights, seasons, championships, losses and the constant preparation that comes with being a professional athlete. For his wife, Lei, it m
content:
For most of Gabe Norwood’s adult life, basketball dictated the rhythm of his world: practices, games, flights, seasons, championships, losses and the constant preparation that comes with being a professional athlete. For his wife, Lei, it meant building a life around that rhythm too.

Now, with Gabe’s retirement from the Philippine Basketball Association (PBA), the Norwoods are entering a season unlike any they have had before. Their schedule is different, their priorities are shifting, and for the first time in years, they have more freedom to decide what comes next.

“It feels exciting, unfamiliar, and a little surreal all at once,” Lei says. “Basketball dictated so much of the rhythm of our lives for so many years. Now there’s a little more freedom to ask, ‘What do we want this next chapter to look like?’ Not just for Gabe, but for all of us.”

*   [Diplomats, public servants honored at Asia’s Modern Hero Awards 2026](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/the-sunday-times/filipino-champions/diplomats-public-servants-honored-at-asias-modern-hero-awards-2026/2443069)

For Gabe, the transition does not mean leaving basketball behind. The game has been part of his life for as long as he can remember, and his connection to it reaches beyond his years as a player.

“The playing part ended,” he says. “The relationships, the lessons, the love for the game, those don’t end.”
