Retirement has brought both a sense of finality and gratitude. Looking back, Gabe thinks about the teammates, coaches, fans, organizations and the national team that became part of his journey. There are things he misses, but above all, he feels fortunate to have experienced it all.

For Lei, watching him retire was equally emotional.

“It was truly a bittersweet ride,” she says. “I was beyond proud of him and all that he has accomplished. Full of gratitude for what has been and excited for what is to come.”

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The sadness of seeing an era end comes with an appreciation for everything basketball has given their family. And perhaps that is the best way to understand the Norwoods today. They are not leaving one life behind. They are carrying everything they learned from it into whatever comes next.

[![Image 2: Over the years, Gabe and Lei Norwood have navigated marriage, children, championships, losses, injuries, adventures, career changes, moves and all the ordinary complications that come with building a family. COVER AND INSIDE PHOTOS COURTESY OF GABE AND LEI NORWOOD](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254138.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254138.jpg)
Over the years, Gabe and Lei Norwood have navigated marriage, children, championships, losses, injuries, adventures, career changes, moves and all the ordinary complications that come with building a family. COVER AND INSIDE PHOTOS COURTESY OF GABE AND LEI NORWOOD

## **Growing together**

Gabe and Lei have evolved alongside his career. The couple they were at the beginning is very different from the couple they are today.Over the years, they have navigated marriage, children, championships, losses, injuries, adventures, career changes, moves and all the ordinary complications that come with building a family.

They have learned that marriage means making room for each other to change while continuing to grow together. Gabe says they understand each other better now: when to communicate, when to listen and when to give each other space. Through it all, they have learned to see themselves as teammates.

That mindset became especially important during the difficult stretches of a professional sports career. As the couple points out, people see the games, but they do not always know what it takes to get there. The physical work, the recovery, the travel and the pressure to perform year after year.

At home, Lei carried a different kind of responsibility.

*   ![Image 3: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

“When you’re traveling or focused on the season, somebody still has to make everything at home work,” Gabe says. “She gave me the ability to focus on my job because I knew our family was taken care of.”

It is a sacrifice he understands even more now.

There were certainly moments when basketball tested their marriage. Absences, fatigue, the uncertainty before the frustration after all came with the territory.

They worked through those moments by communicating and reminding themselves that basketball was Gabe’s job, not the foundation of their entire family.

“Basketball was my job, but my marriage and family were bigger than the job,” Gabe says.

For Lei, a lasting marriage depends on remembering what matters beyond the circumstances of any particular season. For Gabe, it has meant learning to process challenges without bringing them through the front door. Over time, they have become better at moving through difficult seasons together. Faith has also anchored them.

[![Image 4: Through many seasons, Gabe and Lei have committed to living a life that is authentic to who they are.](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254139.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254139.jpg)
Through many seasons, Gabe and Lei have committed to living a life that is authentic to who they are.

## **At home, he’s just Gabe**

Away from the cameras and arenas, Lei describes Gabe as very different from the competitive athlete people know. He is low-key, funny and extremely patient. He does not need to be the loudest person in the room.At home, he is simply Gabe.

There are the dad jokes, teasing the boys, lots of eating, sports on television and, inevitably, a reason to turn something into a competition. This is the version of Gabe his family knows best, and now they get to see more of him.

Retirement has changed the rhythm of their household, though it has not necessarily meant slowing down. The family moved, their boys entered new stages of their own lives, and everyone had to establish new routines. In some ways, they are still figuring out what normal looks like.

What excites them most are the ordinary things: family dinners without someone rushing off to practice, more weekends together, being present for school events and holidays without checking a basketball schedule first. There is also more room for travel and adventures.

“The little things you miss during a season become the things you appreciate the most,” Gabe says.

For their children, the transition has been surprisingly simple. They knew their father was a professional athlete, but they also knew him as Dad. Now, Dad is around more.

“I want them to see that your job can change without changing who you are,” Gabe says.

That lesson extends beyond basketball to the kind of home they want their boys to remember. Lei hopes they remember parents who showed up, made home a safe place and taught them kindness, discipline, resilience, humility, integrity and faith.

For Gabe, character matters most. He wants his sons to know that they can pursue their own paths without feeling pressured to become versions of their parents. He wants them to understand what it means to work hard, show respect and be a good teammate, whether in sports, work, marriage or life in general.

[![Image 5: Gabe during his last season of the PBA PHOTO FROM INSTAGRAM/GNORWOOD5](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254140.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254140.jpg)
Gabe during his last season of the PBA PHOTO FROM INSTAGRAM/GNORWOOD5

## **Beyond the jersey**

Retirement raises questions about identity as well as the future. It is not so much, "What will you do next?" as "Who are you now?"

For Gabe, the answer comes easily: he is a husband and a father first.

He remains competitive, curious and still deeply connected to basketball. But without the demands of preparing his body for the next game, he now has the opportunity to explore other sides of the sport.

He wants to continue mentoring younger players and learn more about basketball operations and the business side of the game. Coaching, player development, scouting, media or some combination of those paths could become part of his next chapter.

“The jersey was a big part of my life, but it was never all of me,” he says.

Lei is experiencing her own rediscovery. With more room to focus on her interests in food, marketing and storytelling, she is thinking about what she wants to build in this season of her life.

And for the first time, there is more opportunity to build side by side. The Norwoods do not have a perfectly mapped-out plan, but they have conversations, ideas and passions they are excited to pursue individually and together.

Their biggest shared dream may be less about one specific project and more about freedom.

The freedom to experience new places as a family and make decisions based on what feels right for them rather than what the season requires.

There is also the freedom to create and give back.

“Building something together that lasts beyond basketball would be pretty special,” Gabe says.

[![Image 6: Despite his many successes in the PBA, Gabe firmly believes the best is ahead.](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254141.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254141.jpg)
Despite his many successes in the PBA, Gabe firmly believes the best is ahead.

## **A different definition of success**

Ask Lei what she hopes life looks like five years from now, and her answer has little to do with status. She wants their family to feel rooted and their boys to thrive on whatever paths they choose. She wants Gabe doing meaningful work while she continues developing her own pursuits.

She imagines a home filled with family, friends, cooking and laughter, with people gathered around the table.

“Success for me at this point looks a lot like peace and purpose,” she says.

For Gabe, success means work with a sense of purpose, continued learning and the flexibility to enjoy life with his family. It is a striking evolution for someone whose career was once measured by points, wins and championships.

Now, legacy means something much more personal, too. Gabe hopes former teammates remember him as someone they could count on and that younger players remember he helped them.And no matter how busy and demanding the life on the hard court had become, he wants his family to remember he was still there for them.

As a family, Lei hopes they will be remembered for welcoming people, living out their faith and using whatever success they achieve to serve others and pay it forward.

Above all, she hopes people remember how much they love being a family.

title: COA flags Mandaue’s P55M Christmas expenditure
summary: MANDAUE CITY — The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned this city’s P55.525-million expenditure for its “Gugma sa Pasko (Love at Christmas)” food bundle program, saying the city failed to sufficiently establish how the assistance addres
content:
MANDAUE CITY — The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned this city’s P55.525-million expenditure for its “Gugma sa Pasko (Love at Christmas)” food bundle program, saying the city failed to sufficiently establish how the assistance addressed specific socioeconomic concerns and development gaps.

In its 2025 audit observations, COA said the city distributed 100,000 Christmas bundles worth P595.25 each in December 2025 to households registered and not registered under the Community-Based Monitoring System.

However, the audit team found that the program’s developmental purpose and contribution to defined objectives remained unclear.

*   [DENR pushes bamboo planting in Tarlac](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/regions/denr-pushes-bamboo-planting-in-tarlac/2443091)

“The developmental value and strategic relevance of the expenditure to the objectives of the 20-percent Development Fund could not be readily established,” the audit report stated.

COA recommended that the city prioritize programs addressing clearly identified social needs and development gaps to ensure public funds generate greater socioeconomic benefits.

In response, Mandaue City is seeking to revise the program’s guidelines and prioritize vulnerable sectors for its planned distribution in December 2026.

The city council approved on first reading an ordinance establishing the Gugma sa Pasko Mandaue Food Assistance Program, with a proposed P60-million allocation for an estimated 80,000 qualified beneficiaries.

City administrator Gonzalo Malig-on Jr. acknowledged the need to identify specific sectors that the program should serve.

*   ![Image 1: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

“Ang observations sa COA dapat naa gyud targeted nga sectors nga naa gyuy social program nga gi-address (COA’s observations emphasize that there should be targeted sectors served by specific social programs),” Malig-on said.

He explained that last year’s distribution covered around 100,000 households without restricting beneficiaries to specific vulnerable groups.

Mayor Thadeo Jovito Ouano has since asked the city council, through councilor Joel Seno, to establish the program through an ordinance setting clear guidelines and eligibility requirements.

The proposed measure identifies persons with disabilities, senior citizens, solo parents, low-income households and urban poor residents as priority sectors.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The City Social Welfare and Development Office will lead beneficiary screening and validation in coordination with concerned city offices and barangay leaders.

Malig-on said the number of beneficiaries would likely decrease from last year’s 100,000 households if the ordinance takes effect. He noted that Mandaue has more than 33,000 senior citizens and acknowledged that some previous recipients might no longer qualify under the revised guidelines.

“Wa man tay mahimo kay mutuman ra pod ang syudad sa gi-raise sa COA nga concern (There is nothing we can do because the city must comply with the concerns raised by COA),” he said.

Councilor Joel Seno, chairman of the Committee on Education, said the program would provide Christmas bundles to qualified residents across the city.

*   ![Image 3: Mayabang talaga!](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252273.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

The proposed P60-million appropriation would cover an estimated 80,000 beneficiaries, subject to validation, procurement results and fund availability.

“Murag Christmas gift ni Mayor ba para sa tanan, walay pili basta na-belong sa sector (It is like a Christmas gift from the mayor for everyone, as long as they belong to the identified sectors),” Seno said.

The Christmas bundles distributed in 2025 contained 10 items: fruit cocktail, cream, spaghetti noodles and sauce, Chinese luncheon meat, carne norte, sausage, beef loaf, pork and beans and cheese.

Seno clarified that the proposed ordinance would cover the December 2026 implementation only and would not automatically make Gugma sa Pasko an annual program. The city may consider continuing it in subsequent years depending on its implementation and the city administration’s direction.

Malig-on also disputed COA’s reported identification of the funding source, saying the P55.525-million expenditure came from the General Fund rather than the 20-percent Development Fund.

He said the city had already communicated with COA to correct the information in the report.

Despite the audit observation, Malig-on maintained that the program contributed to residents’ general well-being by allowing households to benefit directly from government assistance.

He also cited similar Christmas bundle distribution programs in Metro Manila, including those implemented by Pasig City and Quezon City.

COA said the money could have supported programs addressing identified development concerns, improving public services, strengthening economic productivity or promoting long-term social welfare.

Section 2 of Presidential Decree 1445, or the Government Auditing Code of the Philippines, requires government resources to be managed and used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, with safeguards against waste and improper disposition.

title: Cebu City landslide kills 3 family members; mother survives
summary: **CEBU CITY** — A landslide buried a family of four inside their home at Sitio Kandarong Riverside, Barangay Pulangbato, on Friday, killing two children and their 60-year-old grandmother while the mother survived. Rescue teams from the bara
content:
**CEBU CITY** — A landslide buried a family of four inside their home at Sitio Kandarong Riverside, Barangay Pulangbato, on Friday, killing two children and their 60-year-old grandmother while the mother survived.

Rescue teams from the barangay, the Cebu City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, and the Bureau of Fire Protection in Cebu City spent nearly six hours retrieving the victims as persistent rain and unstable soil hampered operations.

The fatalities were identified as Xian Caballero, 5; Kyden, 6; and their grandmother, Judith, 60. Their mother, Jolly Pearl Andamon, 38, survived and was rushed to a hospital for treatment.

*   [DENR pushes bamboo planting in Tarlac](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/regions/denr-pushes-bamboo-planting-in-tarlac/2443091)

Rescuers recovered Xian at around 1:45 p.m. and brought him to a hospital, where he later died despite emergency treatment.

They pulled Andamon out from the rubble alive shortly afterward. Rescuers then recovered Kyden at around 4:24 p.m. and Judith at 5:43 p.m. Both had died by the time rescuers retrieved them.

Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival expressed his condolences to the bereaved family.

“Our deepest prayers and sympathies are with the family during this painful time,” Archival said.

*   ![Image 1: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The landslide also forced 35 families, or 137 people, to leave their homes. The incident completely destroyed two houses and prompted residents of 29 other houses to evacuate.

The city government sheltered the evacuees at the Pulangbato Gym and pledged to provide relief goods and hot meals throughout their stay.

Archival also urged residents in landslide-prone areas to remain alert and take precautions amid the continuing rains.

He asked the public to stay away from the site and keep access roads clear for emergency vehicles and heavy equipment.

*   ![Image 2: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

The city government committed to giving P20,000 in financial assistance to the relatives of each deceased victim and another P20,000 to the owners of houses damaged by the landslide.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration in the Visayas attributed Friday’s rainfall to the intertropical convergence zone, which was expected to bring more rain until early next week.

**MANILA, Philippines —**The Department of Justice (DOJ) confirmed on Saturday that the preliminary investigation into the obstruction of justice complaint filed against Senator Robin Padilla proceeded last Friday, October 9.

Saying that the next hearing has been set on November 6, 2026, Justice spokesperson Polo Martinez said only the senator’s counsel was present during the initial investigation on the complaint.

The Philippine National Police-Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) on May 28, 2026 lodged an obstruction of justice complaint against Padilla and others before the justice department in connection with the escape of Senator Ronald "Bato" Dela Rosa from the Senate building.

*   [‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

A former PNP chief, dela Rosa has been the subject of an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court for "alleged criminal responsibility as an indirect co-perpetrator" in the crimes against humanity of murder during the Duterte administration's war on drugs.

He sought refuge at the Senate on May 11 after authorities attempted to serve the warrant. He slipped out of the Senate building in the early hours of May 14.

title: Hunger stalks Gazans, a year on from ceasefire
summary: KHAN YUNIS, Palestinian Territories — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family. It has been a year since a ceasefire between
content:
KHAN YUNIS, Palestinian Territories — Every day, Gazan mother Niyaha al-Masri spends six exhausting hours or more queueing at a community kitchen in the hope of getting some food for her family.

It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet widespread hunger persists there.

Masri has little choice. Without the kitchen run by humanitarian groups, she and her eight children would have “nothing at all”, the 35-year-old told AFP.

*   [Protests in New York as Trump admin defends ICE shooting](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/world/americas-emea/protests-in-new-york-as-trump-admin-defends-ice-shooting/2442976)

Each day she sets out early in the morning and returns in the afternoon, this time bringing four containers of rice, lentils and a little chicken, which the family throws itself at.

Among them is her husband, wounded in both legs by an airstrike, meaning he “cannot go and fight with the others” to get food.

This will be the only meal of the day for the family of 10, living in a tent in Khan Yunis. There was no breakfast and they will have no dinner.

What little flour they have, Masri explained, has to be rationed.

In August 2025, a United Nations-backed body, the IPC, declared a state of famine in Gaza, though Israel quickly denounced it as a lie.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos eyes nuclear energy to diversify PH power source](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254542.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos eyes nuclear energy to diversify PH power source](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/marcos-eyes-nuclear-energy-to-diversify-ph-power-source/2443184)

By December, the UN had lifted that declaration, saying that the ceasefire had allowed in enough supplies over the course of two months to ease conditions.

COGAT, the Israeli defense ministry organization responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, told AFP that the humanitarian situation in Gaza was stable.

[![Image 2: This photo taken on October 6, 2026 shows displaced Palestinians waiting to receive food at a charity kitchen in Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip. It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet the hunger crisis there persists. (Photo by Bashar Taleb / AFP) / To go with 'ISRAEL-PALESTINIANS-CONFLICT-GAZA-HUNGER, FOCUS](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254345.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/10/1254345.jpg)
This photo taken on October 6, 2026 shows displaced Palestinians waiting to receive food at a charity kitchen in Khan Yunis, in the southern Gaza Strip. It has been a year since a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel was supposed to allow food to flood into the ruined territory, yet the hunger crisis there persists. (Photo by Bashar Taleb / AFP) / To go with 'ISRAEL-PALESTINIANS-CONFLICT-GAZA-HUNGER, FOCUS" by AFP team in Gaza, with Anouk RIONDET in Jerusalem

*   ![Image 3: ‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254518.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

But Shaun Hughes, of the UN’s World Food Program, was less sanguine.

The food security situation, he said, “is still extremely serious”.

The most recent figures, from July, show that “1.4 million out of the population of about 2.1 million people are acutely food insecure”, he said, with 200,000 of them “just one step below famine”.

‘Shameful’

*   ![Image 4: Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/11/1254517.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Malacañang accepts Aguda resignation – Remulla](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/national/malacaang-accepts-aguda-resignation-remulla/2443171)

While some food is getting in, a lack of sufficient nutritional variety continues to pose a health threat.

“Dietary diversity is a major food security issue in Gaza,” said Hughes.

“You cannot survive on dry goods and wheat flour and bread alone. Particularly children, particularly pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, they need the micronutrients that come with high protein foods, fresh vegetables, fresh fruits,” he explained.

Masri said that her children, aged between three and 14, “dream of eating fruit” but the family doesn’t have the means to buy any.

She said one of her sons suffered from malnutrition during the 2025 famine, although “little by little, his condition is improving”.

Malnutrition isn’t only caused by a lack of food, but also essential nutrients. It weakens the immune system of children, making them vulnerable to illnesses and stunting their growth.

“Repeated bouts of acute malnutrition amongst children is something that human beings just don’t recover from,” said Hughes.

Cognitive and physical impairments “continue into later life”, he added.

At Khan Yunis’s Nasser hospital, the head of the malnutrition unit, Israa al-Najjar, told AFP she had “observed an increase in syndromes and conditions” linked to malnutrition that affect the immune system.

In a report published on Thursday, the day after the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack that sparked the Gaza war, Medecins du Monde published a study that found 93 percent of pregnant or breastfeeding women had symptoms of anaemia, which is closely linked to malnutrition.

Just 17 percent had a sufficiently varied diet to meet their nutritional needs, the group found.

All the while, Masri has kept visiting the community kitchen, despite asthma leaving her exhausted.

Her children spend their days collecting “pieces of nylon, bits of cardboard and chunks of foam” to try and reinforce their tent, which is in a poor state.

She said it was “shameful” that her children had to do so.

“I swear to God, this isn’t normal.”

# China denies obstructing PCG medical evacuation

[![Image 19: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)![Image 20: the author image](https://manilatimes.net/uploads/authors/4138_1768618327.jpg)](https://www.manilatimes.net/author/allen-limos "author image")

 October 11, 2026

 80

[Resize](https://manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/national/china-denies-obstructing-pcg-medical-evacuation/2443170)

*   ![Image 21: font icon small](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-small.svg)Small
*   ![Image 22: font icon medium](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-medium.svg)Medium
*   ![Image 23: font icon large](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/font-large.svg)Large

[![Image 24: Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google](https://manilatimes.net/theme_manilatimes/images/google-preferred-source.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=manilatimes.net "Add The Manila Times as a preferred source on Google")

CHINA denied allegations that the China Coast Guard (CCG) intentionally obstructed the medical evacuation conducted by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) in the Ayungin Shoal, accusing Manila of distorting facts.

On Oct. 8, the CCG vessel 5306 delayed a PCG medical evacuation at Ayungin Shoal by nearly 10 hours by using a water cannon on a PCG ship.

In a statement on Friday, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning asserted that it was the PCG that entered Beijing’s territory without permission.

*   [‘No simple living for the Dutertes’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/11/news/no-simple-living-for-the-dutertes/2443173)

Mao added that the CCG took “legitimate and reasonable measures” before ultimately allowing the evacuation to proceed on humanitarian grounds.

“After communication between the two sides, out of humanitarian considerations, China gave timely permission to the Philippine side to evacuate injured personnel by small boat and provided necessary facilitation,” Mao stated.

Mao also criticized Manila for raising concerns over the encounter, saying the PCG’s account was an attempt to misrepresent the situation.

“Instead of acknowledging China’s facilitation, individual Philippine officials have distorted facts and wrongfully accused China without showing the whole picture to the public,” Mao added.

Advertisement

“This once again reveals their intention of provoking China and staging publicity stunts, which is rather despicable. China will not waver in responding to any provocation and safeguarding territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests,” Mao concluded.

*   ![Image 25: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

The PCG has since urged China to respect humanitarian medical evacuations, emphasizing that life-saving sea missions should never face water cannon attacks, obstruction, or delays.

“When a life is at stake, there should be no water cannon, no obstruction, and no delay. Saving a sick or injured person at sea is a basic obligation that every coast guard in the world is expected to uphold. We call on the China Coast Guard to value and respect humanitarian missions moving forward, and to act in a manner consistent with international law and the professional standards expected of any coast guard,” said PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan.
